product_title: New Wayzon Mini Clip Metal Screen MP3 Music Media Player
review_headline: Great player for the money, just don't expect too much
review_body:
If you're looking for an exact replacement for a ipod shuffle you're going to be disappointed. The advantage it does have is that it's only $7. And if you're expecting more than $7 worth of music playing out of this you're fooling yourself. I will say that it does have its uses and if you work around a few of the problems with it it is a great little player.
For starters I didn't use the card reader. I tried and it didn't work for me right off, so I just used the one I already had. If I messed with it more I could have probably gotten it to work. I didn't use the earplugs either since they felt cheap and I already had some that I liked.
That being said, the usb charger cable worked fine using an iphone wall charger that I already had (it doesn't come with its own wall charger, just the usb to mini-usb cable). It is definitely awkward to charge. I managed to get it to charge by leaving the switch in the on position. Plugging it into the wall charger with the cable and then flipping the switch to the off position. The orange light flashes while it charges and the next morning the orange light was solid indicating it was fully charged. The charge lasts for about 4 hours I think is the most I've ever gotten out of it, and I noticed it takes just about that long to fully charge it.
It does not have a shuffle feature. From what I noticed it just plays the songs in the order in which they were added to the card. Also note, you have to buy your own micro SD card to use with it, it does not have its own memory or come with its own card. I formatted a card to FAT32 and uploaded just fine. After I realized the order it plays the song I changed my approach.
Round 2 I downloaded a program called "Random Copy" that you can download for free. I played around with it for a while and basically found out how to get it to upload songs from my computer to the mp3 player in a random order. This basically gave it the effect of playing in shuffle mode. With 8GB of music playing random songs in a fixed order, it was hard to tell it wasn't in shuffle mode.
Some annoying things with it are that it won't remember the volume setting (always starts roughly medium volume). There is some static at lower volumes and with the headphones I have (in ear) I had to play it at the lowest settings. So the static was annoying. It saves what song you were on last, but not where in the song you were. So, I wouldn't recommend this for audio books.
For me, this works great for what I needed it for. I have it hooked up to an FM transmitter to play on my work van stereo. It's always plugged into power so the battery life doesn't matter to me, nor how long it takes to charge. I drive a lot, so 8 GB of music was all that I needed. I've probably driven several hours with it playing and can't really tell that it's not shuffling with how I have it set up.
Like I said in the beginning. If you want all the bells and whistles of a ipod shuffle, you'll want to pay more money and get one. Otherwise, if you're willing to work a little extra to get this to do what you want, $7 is well worth it.

product_title: Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System
review_body:
I'm going to open this by saying that while I have a background in music, I'm not an audiophile. I'm normally not terribly choosy, speaker-wise. I can tell the difference between something amazing and a pair of cheap earbuds, but I enjoy music enough that I'm happy to experience it either way.

The trouble comes when you start talking about things like television, where complex sound mixing, made for high end movie theater speakers, gets horribly garbled and distorted with cheap TV speakers, like the ones that my ancient flatscreen has. In most modern TV shows and movies, the explosions and gunshots and intense background music are too loud, while the dialogue is so inaudible that I'd started to wonder if I was losing my hearing. I would have to use subtitles. It's gotten so bad that my husband was starting to talk about replacing the TV altogether.

The Bose Solo 15 Series has solved our problems. The dramatic stuff comes through crisp and clear, but more importantly, the softer moments and the dialogue also come through clearly, without having to hike the volume so much that the walls are rattling. It feels like the speaker is intelligent, the way that the sound fills my crowded TV room so perfectly without me having to go through the trouble of mounting speakers everywhere.

If you're having similar problems that I was with the way that sound in movies and TV are mixed now, this speaker will solve them.

The only complaint I have is that it's huge. I think that this speaker is meant to have the TV set on top of it, and that's fine if you have a TV that's the right size for that, or an entertainment center or something, but my TV is mounted on the wall in a room that's already pretty crowded with computers. The quality of the sound is worth going through the trouble of working out where to put it, but it would be a lot more convenient if Bose had made it smaller.

product_title: Generic 915B403001 Replacement Lamp with Housing for Mitsubishi Projectors
review_headline: Pretty much limps and sputters out of it's warranty period before dying.
review_body:
My father had a particular brand of projection television for several years before he needed to replace the lamp inside of it. So he had me buy this as a replacement for it. And over the course of about two years he had to buy two more replacements for it before giving up entirely and just buying a new television.

These things offer a five month warranty, and lasted about on average six to seven months each time. At what was $85 a pop, this was a pretty expensive thing to keep replacing every near half a year. The last time he bought one the price had went down to about $25, but again, the thing lasted about six months.

He was tired to of having to buy replacements, and moreover tired of having his television go down while he waited for a replacement bulb. The television he has now he couldn't be happier with.

The bulbs were fine when they actually worked. Problem is that wasn't for a very long time. And my father is not a power tv user. So it's not a matter of overworking the thing. These are just shoddy bulbs. But when they work they work. And it's currently going for about $18, which is a far cry better than the near $100 my father was paying each time the bulbs failed. So I guess if you still have this style of projection tv, this is probably your only option, unless you want to upgrade to something from this decade.

review_headline: Clear video. Wish I could get a little better range.
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:5e693daea1bcfee522144467cb849c4f]] This video includes info on a few parts for a fully built quad. Actual flight at 9:40 and all flight was done through this transmitter from your average 600 line boardcam.

The size of this transmitter is really incredible. I don't see how you could make them any smaller and still be able to not have it melt down from the heat generated. This one is perfect for flying in a small area and the 32 channels allow you to find one without interference.

My only complaint is that I wish I could get a little better range out of it. I was getting uncomfortable at about 200 yards. A couple things to not though are that I was receiving with a RC305 that I've never quite been sure what frequencies it hits(flip switches and see when you hit video), and the wiring on my quad is a mess. Unfiltered posed and interference from other components are probably strong factors.

Even with my range issues I was able to fly in a small space and because of that don't need anything else. If you're going for long range you'd be using a bigger quad and no be so worried about a few extra grams for something more powerful.If you can get a good receiver and wire up a little better than me there's no reason you couldn't use this for some aggressive flight. I received this product free in exchange for nothing more than my honest opinion.

You can see the iPhone Bluetooth marries the speaker because unlike other Bluetooth device with no connection name, this one explicitly say \\"Coosh\\" - so you'll never be in doubt. Alternatively, there is a 3.5 Aux MM input that you can connect to your phone. The command buttons are all self explanatory and very intuitive to use.

The sound quality is amazing! The calibration out of the speaker seems perfect to me - treble and bass are on point. I played the speaker in the backyard with my iPhone being away for about 10 yards and still had a good range. Whatever activities you're doing on your mobile device will project on the speaker - including calls. This speaker gets really loud - I love it! Definitely recommend this with 5-star rating.

product_title: AmazonBasics On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: No bells & whistles. Just solid design & performance.
review_body: Audiophile/Music Producer here. I needed a pair of knock-around headphones that wouldn't break the bank or cause me to worry about damage/theft 24-7, and have been a fan of the quality of many AmazonBasics products that I've bought so far so I gave these a try. I have to say, these were really impressive. The design was perfect. Simple and comfortable. These headphones are not heavy (which is usually a sign of quality) yet they delivered a great, balanced sound. The bass was clean and thick, the treble was precise without being tinny, and the mids were smooth and never became wonky as I increased the volume. None of the sounds bled into each other and nothing sounded muddy or fuzzy. I can actually say that these headphones brought out some of the more subtle elements in the music due to their clarity and balance. I listen to all kinds of music from bass heavy Hip-Hop to light and airy Folk and each genre sounded great. I tested these from low all the way to full volume and had no distortion or materials vibrating. I'm usually a skeptical buyer but I'm very satisfied with these. The only thing I wish was different was that one of the plugs on the auxiliary cord was a 90 degree angled plug. I much prefer the straight plugs like on Apple products. To sum these headphones up, I would say that they have no gimmicks, no bells and whistles, and are solid in design and performance. Well done Amazon.

review_body: These headphones were not good at all, so I returned them. I bought them for use in my work-outs, so I did not expect the same sound as I would get with much more expensive headphones. Even with all that in mind, they are unusable to me. I am not giving them one star, because they may work for you if you never listen to any music that includes even a tiny bit of guitar distortion. If you listen to Joni Mitchell's Blue, you would be just OK (nothing stellar but nothing too offensive either). But even if you try Dan Fogelberg (not exactly Led Zeppelin), things start to get little messy. And not to mention any hard rock or heavy metal. They sound very tinny, even if pressed with my hand against my ear, the treble is extremely harsh and piercing for songs with guitar distortion, and bass is not there, as others have mentioned. I could deal with the lack of bass if everything else were more balanced, but it is just not. I also tried these with two different players just to make sure that my player was not the problem, but results were the same. Finally, I tried using equalizers, and I was able to get them to work slightly better, but it was still not acceptable, because I would have to do a lot of messing around with settings to go from one album to another for marginal improvements. I just hope that I received a defective pair. I much prefer Koss Sportapro for my workouts as far as the sound quality, but they sadly lasted only four months. Maybe I will try another pair of Koss.

review_headline: Seems to burn fine, but avoid using Windows integrated burning software with these.
review_body:
I had some larger files that required archiving and these seemed like a logical low cost option from a reputable brand. I was able to successfully burn 7 discs until I reached a large 42 gb file that I wanted to archive to blu ray. I got the error unable to burn disc and got a coaster. I though it might have been a dud so I tried a second disc and now I have 2 coasters. It wast my Asus drive's fault because it was working until that point and could still read the freshly burned discs. I was reading online to her users experience similar issues with Windows burning blu ray discs with large files, due to a bug in Windows 7 burning software. review_headline: Cannot turn on after left off for a couple days at 100% charge! Bose said it's a shipping feature!
review_body: I love my Bose Soundlink Mini version 1, never had any problems with it. The version II finally has the features that was missing on the v1 - speaker phone and USB charging.  Everything was good until I left it off for a few days at 100% charge. It will not turn on. Had to plug in the charger cable for it to response and come back on. Battery is still at 100%  I called Bose and was told to try a reset and later on Bose told me that this is a "Shipping Feature".. come on? Bose said that it's to preserve battery life during shipping. Li-ion batteries looses about 20% / year. Unless Bose is looking to ship the speakers to Jupiter... no such feature is required. That never happens to my Bose Soundlink Mini version 1. Never had to plug it in to turn on.  Almost look like a defective charging circuit.  Edit:  In the Bose manual "When the system is unplugged and unused for three days with a remaining charge of less than 10 percent, it enters battery protection mode to preserve battery power. To reactivate the system, connect it to AC (mains) power (see page 10). "  My Bose Soundlink Mini II was at 100% and it should not have gone into battery protection mode.  Looks like the A/D function in the IC (To detect voltage level) is not working correctly or someone did not program it correctly.  To claim it's a shipping feature is ignorant from Boses's part and trying to deceive customers.  Looks like the A/D circuit cannot properly detect voltage thinking a 60%-100% charge is 10%.  I try to have Bose send me a replacement but the customer rep on the phone told me that because it's a known issue, Bose will not do any sort of warranty work (exchance, fix, replace) on it.  Bose SLM II has a factory A/D defect or a bug in the A/D routine, maybe hold (capacitor charge) time is not long enough etc.... but to say this is a "Shipping feature" is a LIE. Why will Bose agents and the supervisor on the tech support tell me a LIE? It looks like Bose don't want a recall or something... will cost them $. But to lie to a customer will probably cost more then this on their reputation.  I am not the first person with this issue, there are a few others with the issue on the Q&A and a couple other websites.

1. Sleep Timer. Remote doesn't have a dedicated button for setting the TV sleep timer. No problem, just follow the simple steps to have it learn that from my old remote and store it in one of the custom buttons. Super handy.

It was easy to make it so that volume/channel buttons always change TV volume (even if current selected device is AppleTV).

3. Power button macro. Similar to volume controls, AppleTV doesn't have a need for the power button. Made a quick macro so the power button always applies to the TV, then sets the remote to control the AppleTV.

product_title: Definitive Technology NECA-AW 6500 Outdoor Speaker
review_headline: Impressive outdoor sound at a reasonable price!
review_body:
After reading the many positive reviews here, I bought a pair of AW 6500s in white as open-box specials for $190 each and they arrived in perfect working order. I mounted them horizontally about 12 feet apart a few inches beneath the eaves overhanging our back deck so they have some protection from the weather. It was simple to paint them according to the instructions provided and mounting them with the included brackets was also a snap, the biggest installation challenge was snaking shielded 14-gauge speaker cables through our attic to connect them to an amp inside the house. I'm using an old (pre-HDMI) Sony STR-DE615 receiver rated at 100 watts RMS per channel into 8 ohms to drive the speakers. The input source is a Logitech Squeezebox Touch audio streaming device, which is connected wirelessly to our home media server and controlled by apps on our phones.

I'm pretty fussy about sound, but I really couldn't be happier with the performance of these speakers given their price and weather resistance. In particular, the bass output is pretty phenomenal considering the bass/mid drivers are only 6 1/2" and I have the cabinets mounted 7 feet up (the drivers are slanted downward toward the deck with the passive radiators pointing up toward the eaves). All genres of music I've played so far sound great throughout our back yard at modest volume levels, and paired with this receiver I can crank them up much louder than my neighbors would appreciate before hearing noticeable distortion.

I haven't auditioned any other outdoor speakers so I don't have a basis to compare these to competitors' offerings, but they're definitely a huge step up from the portable Apple stereo I was lugging outside for music and it's hard for me to imagine anything in this price range sounding better!

product_title: SMSL SA50 50Wx2 TDA7492 Class D  Amplifier + Power Adapter (Silver)
review_headline: Powerful and polished presentation, but no precision for percussion
review_body: I bought this amp to drive some outdoor speakers.  It will be perfect for that application.  The aluminum case, volume knob, and power button have a nice quality feel to them.  The bass and mids sound good, while the treble is decent yet lacking in clarity in comparison to my Tripath amplifier.  4 1/2 stars for presentation, and 3 1/2 for sound.  I bought this amp wanting to try the TDA7492 class D amplifier chip.  I had initially decided on the PartsExpress / Sure Electronics 2x50w amplifier board, but after considering the added cost of power supply, and lack of volume knob, I went with the SMSL for about the cost of the Sure amp board and power supply.  That's right, for a comparable price you gain the volume knob, power switch, and a nice looking case.  I have a Dayton DTA-1 (Tripath amplifier) driving some Infinity Primus 6.5" bookshelf speakers (P163s, fairly sensitive at 90dB @1W,1m) and had to compare the two amps.  For the SMSL, power-on was quiet, but right away I noticed an elevated noise floor in absence of source.  The noise continued into quiet portions of music, but was not distracting at moderate or strong program levels.  The SMSL is significantly more powerful than the Dayton (which is expected given its rating of 50W RMS vs 15 for the Dayton).  The bass was stronger and the midrange seemed a little "warmer" than the Dayton, but for percussion there was a lack of detail and clarity that I have become accustomed to hearing from these speakers.  My 2-way Yamaha outdoor speakers will appreciate the extra power of the SMSL, and won't miss the clarity of the Dayton since they don't exhibit the same clarity as my Infinity speakers when driven by the Dayton amp.  See my images for a peek at the internals.  As Adam says below, there are 3x2200uF filter capacitors = 6600uF.

product_title: Pro-Ject - Debut Carbon DC (Piano Black)
review_headline: The best fix is described here
review_body:
When I first received and set this turntable up, there was a very loud hum. I had done some research on this particular model, and there are lots of complaints about this, but there are also a number of fixes. The best fix is described here:

http://www.avsforum.com/forum/173-2-channel-audio/1513521-eliminating-hum-pro-ject-debut-carbon-turntable.html

With the neoprene washers in place, I tightened 1/4 turn on each of the two mount screws until the hum disappeared. And I do mean 'disappeared', as in dead silent. It has remained dead silent for a month, so I can definitely recommend this table now.

Some people have complained about the metal + felt base and pad, but I've had no issues. I figured I would go for the glass + cork combo eventually, but quickly changed my mind when I heard the stock base. It has no wobble; it is heavy enough to have no flutter, and the felt minimizes a lot of the warpage of some very old vinyl.

I did start with a cheap Behringer preamp, and was not overly thrilled with that, so I bought an Emotiva XSP-1

[[ASIN:B00PMCIYK4 Emotiva Audio XPS-1 Phono Preamp]]

This preamp did make a significant audible difference that I prefer. This is a good combo for a reasonably priced system.

The LCD display and a few of the sensors are not assembled. You'll need a soldering iron to use them with the enclosed breadboards. review_headline: I think for the price this is a pretty good buy
review_body:
I have been looking for a Bluetooth shower speaker for awhile, and when I saw the price of this one I decided to take a chance and go for it. I think for the price this is a pretty good buy. So far, here's what I like.

The sound quality is pretty good for something so small- in my shower or bathroom it sounds great. It's enough to listen to a few songs while I'm showering and getting dressed.

It's smaller, it doesn't take up a lot of room.

It's pink! It's really cute. I don't mind it on my shower or bathroom wall while people are over.

It was pretty easy to use, the directions are super small print, and I couldn't figure out why the light was flashing(I think it's because the battery was low) but overall it's fairly easy for me to connect to my iPhone 5c.

As for the negatives... The first time I stuck it to my shower wall, I could not get it off. I spent about 5 minutes trying to even move it. Now, it won't stick for long. I'm not sure why. It falls off the wall all the time.

It occasionally takes a second to switch songs. Not long enough to be upset about, but enough for me to wonder what's going on.

Overall I'm pretty happy with this, and I would recommend it to a friend

review_headline: Bring out your inner Celine in the shower
review_body:
**Update**
After using this product for a few months, I can no longer turn it off. So the battery just dies. Can't figure it out, but it stinks. But if you are looking for something that only works for a couple months, this is your gadget!!

**Original Post**
This is pretty good little speaker. Understandably the quality of the speaker isn't top of the line, but it gets the job done. I get to listen to music in the shower and bring out my inner Celine, okay so I probably don't sound like her, but that's beside the point. Setting this little guy up is fairly simple, just gotta charge it first. It would be awesome if the cord to charge actually came with the part to plug it in to an outlet, but for 14 bucks, that might be a lot to ask. I will say that syncing the blue tooth up for an android is far easier than on my iphone, but the quality you get is about that same. It does stream a lot better when you are listening to music from your music library vs. pandora. The phone button is pretty sweet, I called my boyfriend the other day and didn't realize he was in the shower and he answered the phone. Quality of the call wasn't too bad, obviously the shower was a little loud and kind of muffled his voice. But hey, it worked! I've seen some people complain about the suction cup and the speaker falling. I will say, we put it in the shower and not 5 minutes later it fell down. But, since we re-stuck it on the wall, it hasn't fallen in a week. For the money it is a good little speaker, and I would probably recommend it to others.

review_headline: I like to watch my shows when I'm in the kitchen ...
review_body:
I am about to pay almost $27 to send my REPLACEMENT ZVOX 420 in for a repair; I've only had it for about 4 months. The first ZVOX 420 had a problem right out of the box with receiving a signal from the remote control . The ZVOX tech determined that it was the box and not the remote; and since the remote worked my other ZVOX systems, I knew he was correct. The replacement ZVOX 420 came soon after I returned the first one. Within about 3 months after receiving it, the second has the sound cutting in and out when the volume reaches level 25. I like to watch my shows when I'm in the kitchen doing dishes, so I have to have the volume up rather loud so that I can hear the dialogue over my cleaning noise. Since the volume goes up to 30, I should have no sound problems up to 30.

I don't like that I have to pay to ship back a product that is still fairly new because it doesn't work properly. I noticed on the company's website that they don't have this product listed for sale, so I wonder if they are aware of the problems and have discontinued it. In the meantime, those of us who have purchased it already have to live with the problems.

I will say that customer service has been good. On the first return, I had no problems getting them to exchange it for a new one. (I'm trying to remember if they said it was refurbished.) I'm still rather annoyed, though, that I have to pay $27 to get it fixed.

review_headline: Awesome 60 ft. range after a quick mod (replace antenna)
review_body:
After modifying the antenna (replacing it with a longer one) the range was increased from about 6ft to about 60 feet! Sounds awesome. Lots of power for what it is and works flawlessly without any of that channel conflict tomfoolery others have described.

Simply replace the antenna with a longer one (I will try to post a link to one). One minor mod has to be made... as the antenna these guys use... have a male coupling... which is weird. Every other antenna you will buy will have a female coupling. Screwing in the new female antenna won't work because the center of the connector will not make contact. You have to get small paper clip, trim off about a 1/4 piece of paper clip... insert it into the antenna... then tighten the antenna. Message me if this does not make sense.

I know this seems like a lot of fooling around.. but even after the cost of the antenna... this is still the best solution for poolside audio for me.

product_title: Panasonic Best in Class Noise Cancelling
review_body:
I am very impressed with these. The packaging is sleek and classy and when I opened the box, I discovered they came with a carrying case which is super nice for storage and travel, to keep them clean and also protected inside luggage or while going through security. On opening the travel case, I found the headphones neatly stowed, and a zippered pouch containing a AAA battery, and two different connectors - one for a standard headphone jack for a device, and the other the 2-pronged connector more commonly seen on airplanes. They thought of everything!

The battery is placed inside a well-hidden compartment in one of the earpieces - so well hidden I had to search to find the button to open it. The button to turn on the noise-cancelling is similarly well built in and unobtrusive, though in a good location to easily reach up and turn it on/off - once you know where it is. Confession: I could not at first find it and had to pull out the instruction manual to figure it out - it is THAT small and unobtrusive.

The ear pieces appear small but when I placed the set over my head, they fit snugly and comfortably, and even without the noise cancelation turned on, they tuned out a lot of sound, meaning I can focus on the podcast I am listening to without distraction. Around the house I don't need them turned on, but also use these when mowing. It takes about 5 hours to mow my place and rather than have that time be empty, I like to listen to podcasts. I typically wear hearing protection, with ear buds in my ears, held on by the ear protector muffs. However I can use these instead, turn on the noise cancellation and they act as hearing protection while playing my podcast.

The head band expands easily and smoothly to adjust to different head sizes.

The only thing I have not yet tried is wearing these and sunglasses at the same time - essential most of the time when mowing. It was overcast when I tried them, so the sunglasses were not necessary. I have some concerns they might cause some ache when placed over the arms of the sunglasses on my head but I will update this review after the next time I mow and find out for sure. However at this point I can't find a single thing about them I don't like - and I don't impress easily.

product_title: Philips X2/27 Fidelio Premium Headphones, Black
review_headline: buy these if you want the best in music reproduction
review_body:
I have well over $15,000 invested in my home audio system. For a long time I have looked for a set of headphones that can provide the audiophile sound I expect from the rest of my system. I think I have found them in these Philips X2/27 Fidelio Premium Headphones.

The headphones arrive attractively packaged in a black box. They come with a detachable cable with standard 1/8" stereo plugs on both ends and a gold-plated adapter for use with conventional amplifiers and receivers that use a 1/4" plug. The cable is too long for listening with a portable mp3 player and too short for listening with a home audio system from across the room. I will be looking for a suitable extension cable to use with it since I plan to use these headphones solely for listening with my home audio system. Sadly, there is no bag or carry case included, which I think is a major oversight for headphones this expensive but not a deal-breaker.

The headphones are quite large, but very comfortable to wear. The head band is designed with comfort in mind, and the velour ear cups are very soft on my ears even with prolonged listening. I have been listening to a wide variety of music with them, music with deep bass, music with predominant midrange sound, and music with delicate high notes. These Fidelio headphones reproduce all of it with ease with no noise or artifact. Unlike other high-end headphones I own, there was no break-in period to hear music the way it was meant to be heard. There is no muddling of sound at all. Listening to music with these headphones I am hearing things that have for years gone unnoticed while listening with high-end tower speakers. It's like having all new recordings to explore.

If you love music and have the ear to appreciate quality sound reproduction you will find these Philips X2/27 Fidelio Premium Headphones to be well worth the expense. They are comfortable, versatile, and sound fantastic. I am extremely happy with this purchase.

product_title: 1byone Window Antenna 35 Miles Super Thin HDTV Antenna with 20ft Coaxial Cable, Extreme Soft Design and Lightweight
review_body: I love this antenna. After buying a heavy, metal monstrosity of a digital antenna at Best Buy for $80 (discounted from $120 last year) and having it not only be unsightly in my apartment, it would only pull in some channels when it was sitting on a table facing a window. I can't mount antennae outside because I live in an apartment that does not allow that, so I felt stuck. I saw this product and bought the black/white 50-mile version and couldn't be happier. I placed it at the very top on a large south-facing window hidden behind my black-out draperies and the first time I scanned for channels, I got 55 hits!! Since I live in San Diego and we are so close to the Mexican border, many of the channels were from stations in Mexico in Spanish, which I can't watch. I also got some channels that I did not care to watch (QVC, HSN, and others), which did some tiling as well. I also got some duplicate network channels from Los Angeles (KTLA and others), which I didn't need because the local network affiliates here in San Diego had more local news content. So after I deleted all the many channels I did not need or want, I pared it down to 12, and they are of the highest quality (10 of the 12 are 1080i and 2 are 720p.) I couldn't be happier and now I can truly become a cable-cutter. Please realize that these amazing results are certainly better than average because of the city I live in and the towers are all on mountain tops within 20-25 miles, so you may not get the amazing results that I did.

review_headline: Amazing Internet Radio and Tablet Device !!!
review_body:
I am totally impressed with this NexTune Internet Radio - it is totally amazing ! I liked it so much that after I had received my first radio, a few weeks later, I ordered a second one ! The sound is crisp and incredibly clear – and it has great volume as well ! I enjoy listening to internet radio stations, and podcasts, and apps such as Stitcher, RAD.IO, and IHeartRadio. I use both of my internet radios for several hours every day and night ! I love watching NETFLIX movies and YOUTUBE videos on these – the High Definition screen is so vivid, and like the sound – crisp, sharp, and clear – you cannot beat the picture quality ! The device is a very nice size and it fits very comfortably in your hand and you don’t get tired of holding it – which is important – as I listen all night long, or use various features on the device. You can also download various apps from Google Play Store – which I have done as well which is also fun ! The touch screen is very responsive and easy to use – you can move icons around, and zoom in and out on pictures and videos. The device looks great – it has a professional look and high quality (not cheap) feel to it – it is attractive as a clock radio on a bookshelf, dresser, or bed headboard shelf.
This is also a Tablet – so not only can you listen to radio, and watch movies and videos – you can also surf the internet – which I also do all the time ! It is so nice to be able to set multiple alarms (for the same or different days) – and wake up to a sound you enjoy (I use the Rooster – as I would have liked to have grown up on a farm !) – it is just another great feature. With the USB port – you can attach things like a USB flashdrive (which I also use) – to view recorded videos, songs, or pictures. You can also insert a mini-SD flash card (I also use this) to save and download things such as pictures, videos, or audio files from the internet ! The device also has a Camera which you can take pictures or videos with – and it is so fun to use that feature !
I had an issue with one of the devices after 1.5 years of using them, and I contacted customer support via email. The person who helped me (Brett) responded immediately and went out of his way to insure I was happy - you just do not find great customer service like this anywhere !
I am not easily impressed – but in my opinion – I could not ask for more out of this NexTune Internet Radio – the features, the high quality look and feel of the device, the sound – just cannot be beat !! I cannot recommend this device enough ! I am sure I have missed mentioning some of the features on this device - because of how many great features there are - so I would recommend buying one (no…make that buying two like I did) – I could not be any happier…and I honestly can’t think of any way to improve the device !

This speaker works, but has a few MAJOR flaws:

1. The instructions are blatantly wrong. I want the music louder, so I push the "+" button. Now I skipped to the next song and the volume remains the same. It is not intuitive at all to have to hold this button in excess of 3 seconds before the volume starts to rise, at which point it pauses the music to inform you that the maximum volume has been reached, then resumes the music...

For $50 (supposedly on sale from $100!!, never could I imagine it is worth anywhere near that) I expected more, and unfortunately for me, missed the return window by 2 days or I would definitely not be keeping this product. There are a lot of other speakers out there in this same price range, I suggest looking into those.

product_title: Sennheiser MM30 Headphones
review_headline: FANTASTIC PRODUCT!!!!!! Buy if you are looking for a longer lasting replacement to the Apple EarPods!
review_body:
This is a fantastic pair of headphones and I would recommend them to anyone!
Pros:
-Tangle proof: Don't worry about having to take 5 full minutes (or more) to untangle your apple earpods. These barely tangle at all, and if they do it doesn't take more than 30 seconds to untangle.
-Cord Durability: I personally sleep with head phones in and because of that my EarPod cord always ended up splitting or tearing, especially near the auxiliary jack end. Also the the rubber around the bottom of the part that goes in your ear always ended up ripping which allowed for more dirt to enter all the crevices. The Sennheiser cord has amazing durability and is really flexible. I haven't done any damage to it yet. One of the best things is that the auxiliary jack end rotates in the jack well because of the way it is shaped, which minimizes chances for ripping the cord.
-Sound quality: The quality of sound is fantastic for earphones. This goes hand in hand with the noise cancelling feature of these earphones. Also, when I use these with Spotify, or any other music app, the sound is amazing.
-Noise Cancelling!: YAY! These block out sound really well. I wouldn't say it does more than a pair of more expensive headphones that actually cover your ears (like Sennheiser's own headphones, which my friend has, so I have tested them before), but they do a good job for the price and I think they are comparable to Sennheiser's headphones' noice cancelling feature.
-Remote control: The buttons are very visible and easy to use. No hassle necessary and the mic is of good quality.
-The earbuds: Sennheiser gives you three different sizes of earbuds to fit the size of your ear. at first I thought the small one would be best for me because the earpods always seemed to be hurting my ears after long periods of time (which is not the case for these headphones). The medium size fit me best and the cool thing is that changing the earbuds is really easy and makes the earphone really easy to clean whenever you need to.

Overall: These headphones are fantastic and I will most likely hold on the them for a lot longer than a pair of EarPods (which are basically the same price).

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_headline: is very annoying and can make listening to any kind of music ...
review_body:
I had a problem right at the start with the earphones; only the right one worked, the left one dead; nothing I could do had any affect on it. I thought about looking through the reviews of other customers hoping to find someone else who had this same problem and how they fixed it, but there were just too many of them. Instead, I looked through the list of answered questions on the Amazon listing and found one that said make sure you get the cable connector securely into the earphone connector. I checked my connection and it seemed secure, but I pushed harder and it went in farther. I tried it out and the left earphone worked perfectly.

If you are having a problem of some kind that you can't solve, look through the answered questions list. You may find the solution there as I did.

My main problem is noise. I live in a small town that has a railroad track that runs right through the middle of it. The horn noise from trains, when they are approaching an intersection, is very annoying and can make listening to any kind of music or other programs very difficult. A second noise problem I have is that in the summer I always have a floor fan in the room about 15-16 feet from my main computer, so my music has been mainly in cooler weather. I like to listen to music while I'm using the computer, but the noise is such that I usually end up turning the music off. Buying these earphones was an attempt at solving my noise problems.

After I got the earphones working I put them to the test. With the noise cancelling off, the quality of the music was surprisingly good. The fan noise was lessened but still noticeable. After I flipped the noise-cancelling switch, the music quality sounded better, and the sound of the fan was barely audible. Voices on news and other programs were crisp and clear. I was amazed at the performance. I have a pretty good set of speakers on my computer but the earphone's sound quality was far superior.

The earphones have given me what I most wanted: noise suppression and good music quality. Are they worth the price? I think so. I doubt you can find better earphones for this price.

The one complaint I have is that I can't wear them more than thirty minutes or so. They aren't painful, just uncomfortable after a while. I can let my ears rest a few minutes and then go for another stint.

At the time of my purchase, others had given this product four-stars. I agree with that rating.

review_headline: I had about 30 people listening to it and they all loved it. I got a lot of questions like ...
review_body: I read several negative reviews on here and I just wanted to share my opinion because I disagree with a lot of what was said. I just bought this about a week and a half ago for an 80s party.  I had about 30 people listening to it and they all loved it.  I got a lot of questions like "where did you get that?"  "How much did it cost"?  I love this boombox. The Bluetooth works well and the sound quality is really good. To do this click the menu button several times until you get to the bass function. it starts at level 5 which isn't enough so kick it up to level 7 which is the highest. review_headline: Far better than my previous braided cable. Tangle-free, durable!
review_body:
I'd like to preface this review by stating that I did receive this item for review purposes from Sabrent, the manufacturer. I was not required nor given incentive for providing a 5-star review. I was asked to provide my critical opinion to inform customers of their new product. This review is written as if I paid full retail price for the item.

That being said, this is a definite 5-star item as most Sabrent products are. They have excellent quality control and, although they are always creating new products, they are always of a 5-star quality. This cable is no different.

I really like the design of most Sabrent products – This cable is designed to look sleek and discrete, yet, the ends of the cable are built very well and seem like they will hold up for a very long time. I have tried other brands and the cables usually give out where they enter the housing for the jack. There is a distinct difference in the quality of the ends in the Sabrent cable.

I have been using this cable in my car, where I prefer to use AUX rather than Bluetooth for playing Spotify from my phone. With my other cable, I had to adjust it every once in a while if moving my phone pulled the jack out of the port. I don’t have that issue with the Sabrent cable, so the audio always sounds crisp and perfect. I think the fit is just overall better – not too tight but tight enough to keep from wiggling out. The design of the cable also makes it nearly impossible to tangle or kink, which is awesome for the car as I can always keep the cable end in my cup holder when not in use – many cables will tangle up and become damaged.

Overall this is a cable – there isn’t a lot to say, but it does what it should very well and will definitely outlast my various other AUX cables.

review_headline: You Don't Know "JACK" Until You Read This! Helpful :) Xbox & Non
review_body:
The people who complain about this jack, don't know jack. Please see my uploaded photos for clarification.
When I see people whining and complaining about really good products, it really gets under my skin.
The reason why I felt compelled to start posting accurate and factual reviews about good items and good experiences.
For Xbox users, this adapter will most likely not work with your application. Please read further for advice.
For normal uses and common audio applications, this will work without any problems if you match your components properly.
Common things to look for and know when matching audio components like these are...
Tip, Ring and Barrel or Sleeve. Analog or Digital. Sticking with the basics for this application you can't go wrong.
See the tiny black strip on the metal shaft? That is important. Mono has 1 or 2 while Stereo has 2-3. Left, Right, Ground and Mic.
In most cases they are backwards compatible, but not always.
Xbox uses a mini-jack mono plug, but since it has 2 rings, it can be confused with a stereo jack. Also, it's a 2.5 mm (3/32") not a 3.5 mm (1/8").
One ring is used for listening and the other for voice. It is mono but with a microphone design. Left and Voice. Please research for more detail.
But overall, if you can see my photos, it's broken down visually to get a better understanding.
Connected to my laptop you can see the audio level is spiking and reading the audio clearly. Matched with a Cobra M29 BT EXT Microphone.
Overall from my experience alone, this jack works flawlessly and is an excellent deal for the price.
I did purchase the wrong jack but kept it, so I will be posting the same review for the other. Not much of a difference.
Hope this helps someone.

review_headline: Big Bewm, But Not Without Quirks
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:80a390e3695e460127acb3268e29785e]]Model: Atomick S202
Pairing name: iDea S202
Paired with Samsung Galaxy S6

The ability to play an SD card while still maintaining an active Bluetooth connection for phone answering is indeed unprecedented, and this most certainly has some incredible bewm bass, yet there are a couple issues:

a) The \\"crystal clear articulate high end\\" means the higher spectrum is emphasized as well, being slightly shrill to my ears (I do prefer a mellow audio tone) and the mid range suffers a bit for it.
b) The Power/Play/Pause/Phone Answer MFB (Multi-Function Button) has on a couple occasions simply turned off even with a brief press; it's supposed to be a three second long press to turn on/off.
c) The previous track function doesn't actually go to the previous track on my Samsung S6, just to the beginning of the current song no matter how much I fiddle with it. This remote previous track behavior is not uncommon on speakers and headphones, but nor is it the general rule. Forward track works fine.

Still, being the most boomy little 3W speaker I can recall in recent memory without causing crazy muddiness does bolster my liking. I do enjoy the BEWM. Just be aware there is a film on the bottom that you can peel off to help anchor the thing when on a tabletop... and be sure to take the carabineer off, too. It causes some serious bewm rattle otherwise.

- Discounted product provided for evaluation, yet my thinking here reflects all my personal purchasing decision processes, and hopefully may help clarify if this best meets your own needs and expectations.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade M-80 Vocal On-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_headline: Great sound, great build-quality. . .BELIEVE THE HYPE!
review_body: I have to say, all the hype about these appears to be true.  The build-quality is ABSURDLY sturdy. . .while I would never test it out purposefully, I get the feeling I could abuse these headphones in just about ANY way and they'd still work just fine.  And the sound-quality. . .well.  . .I must say, for a pair of headphones in this price-range, it's INCREDIBLE.  There are maybe a couple models of phones with the same level of sound in this price-range, but none of those have this kind of build-quality and so you could easily end up with one of the drivers going out in them after only a few hours of use, so they'd be a gamble.  As far as I'm concerned, these are the BEST sounding on-ear headphones in this price-range which also have this level of reliable build-quality.  The sound-signature is flat compared to most popular consumer headphones, lending itself well to equalization, but with somewhat of an emphasis on bass, which I would classify as fun rather than excessive.  The sound-stage is somewhere between what you typically hear with closed-back phones, and what you would find with open-back models.  I assume this is because of the V-Port technology. . .a nice touch, as far as I'm concerned.  The separation between different instruments and vocals is phenomenal, and the drum and cymbals and such hit hard and fast just the way I like them, with guitar sounding clear and, frankly, beautiful.  But, the treble manages to never reach the "painful" levels you sometimes hear with headphones with a good, flat frequency response.  I quite honestly never expected to get quite this level of sound from closed, on-ear phones. . .the sound-stage is WAY better than, say, the Sennheiser Momentum On-Ears which I have also used in the past, and the frequency-response is slightly better as well.  All that being said, there are a few things that others have noted in their reviews which, while not personally an issue for myself, I could certainly foresee a good portion of people having issues with.  First of all, if you have a very large head, these probably will not fit you!  And if you have large or even largish-medium sized ears, the earpads will not quite cover them completely and thus you'll have to deal with tweaking how they are centered on your ears in order to get good sound.  Finally, there's the isolation. . .I'd say  it's decent, but certainly not even close to enough for people who want to be able to listen to tunes while completely oblivious to their surroundings.  These don't leak a great deal of noise to the outside (although more than many closed-back phones), but they sure do let in a lot of sound.  From what I can tell the isolation in the upper-midrange frequences and above is quite good, but in the mid-midrange it starts to fall off, and in the low-midrange and below there seems to be no isolation whatsoever, and any sounds in that range will get in.  Personally I don't mind this, as I like to be aware of my surroundings. . .but this could be an issue for many people, I'm sure.  All that being said, personally, I love these headphones, and I'd recommend them to ANYONE who wants an excellent pair of over-ears that won't break the bank, as long as that person doesn't have a large head ;)

product_title: JBL Sub 100 Black 10-Inch Powered Subwoofer with High-Efficiency Class D Amplifier (Black)
review_headline: Excellent replacement for subs in smaller systems
review_body:
While this is not a very powerful subwoofer, it does a great job in the smaller system in my bedroom. The power rating is 100 watts, and that is enough for smaller setups, but it won't cut it for larger systems. The sound is fairly tight and punchy for a smaller sub, so I think that most people will find this to be a good sub for their needs. There is no XLR input, so you will not be able to connect balanced sources to the sub. Once again, this subwoofer is not meant for higher-end installations, so the standard RCA input is what most will want. The sub comes with a set of carpet spikes to help it couple with the floor under the carpet to keep it stable. The sound can be tailored with a variable crossover point, so you can roll your main speakers off in your processor and then overlap with the crossover point in the sub to cover the lower ranges, leaving your main speakers to worry with the ranges above your subwoofer crossover point.

The class-D amplifier in the sub is quite responsive and tracks fast, as digital switching amplifiers are known for in general. This helps bring the cone back quickly and allows for tighter control of extrusion. The power output of this amplifier is more than adequate for the system in my bedroom and a smaller system in the library. I find the sound of this sub to be superior to the pioneer sub that came with the inexpensive system in the library, so it will remain in place there instead of my bedroom.

My main listening system is comprised of the following:

Sunfire True Sub Signature (2700 watts) subwoofer.
Definitive Technology BP-3000TL main speakers (each with an 18" 1000-watt subwoofer).
Definitive Technology CLR-3000 center speaker (with a 150-watt subwoofer).
Definitive Technology BPVX/P surrounds (with 150-watt subs in each).
Emotiva XMC-1 Gen 2.
Enlightened Audio Designs PowerMaster 2000 amplifier (450 watts per channel).

I put the JBL sub in place to test it in my normal listening environment and it did okay at low volumes, but it bottomed out and didn't work well when approaching reference levels. I didn't find the sound to be bad at all at lower volumes, but it just cannot keep up with the other equipment in higher-volume applications.

Review system 2 (bedroom):

Pioneer VSX-1020-K (receiver)
Polk Audio RM705 (5.1 channel system)

I put the JBL sub in place and it sounded MUCH better than the Polk sub. The sound is far less boomy and just plain smoother. The power output of the JBL sub is greater than the Polk, and it does a far better job of reproducing the low end without becoming boomy. DEFINITELY recommended as a replacement in this type of system.

Review system 3 (library):

Pioneer HTP-072 (home theater in a box).

The JBL sub absolutely destroyed the Pioneer, and is going to replace this sub. My wife and kids are always watching movies and television downstairs in the library, so I think that it is only fair that they get the benefit. The sound is FAR better, smoother, less boomy, and powerful.

product_title: Bose Solo TV Sound System
review_headline: You will hear things you never heard before!!!!!!
review_body: I bought my Solo through Bose. Because I have bought Bose products before, they sent me information on this. You should take advantage of this "Today's Deals." I payed more, and it doesn't bother me. I have had it over a year. There is a huge difference, they aren't concerned with sound for a TV. And my Solo proves it. I wanted it for the bedroom. I have a LG, I measured diagonally-37". My husband had it going in minutes. WHAT A DIFFERENCE!  I can't tell you any specifications. What matters to me is how it sounds, what my almost 58 year old ears hear. We have no problems with the TV in the bedroom and the TV in the living room. My home is only 800 sq ft. I don't hear the TV in the next room and Husband doesn't hear the Solo, unless I turn it up for music, during a movie or rarely music video's. I do not listen to my music through the TV.  I have quite a few music listening devices, 2 stereo's, 5 MP3 players, iPOD, ROAR, Bose, Bose Wave etc... Headphones & in ear headphones (they are important too). I spend as much as I can afford for items for my music, it has to sound good and it has to sound good loud. My Magneplanar speakers, by Magnepan I got in the fall of 1981. The only thing I have done to them is recovered the fabric. They still raise the roof! They have fuses so I don't blow out my speakers. You may be annoyed at this review because I wrote more about music and my equipment. But my ears are the expert, and I think the Solo is worth every $$$$ I paid for it for the TV. I want to add, if you have favorite movies, I guarantee, I promise you will hear things you never heard before. There is one problem, some people just don't know when something sounds good. Is that called tone deaf? tin ear? My husband is kinda like that. He put in a stereo for his car from WM@rt. YIKES! He doesn't like music loud, (too bad)...I say "if it's too loud, you're to old".

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC33iS QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Great Value, Decent Sound, Small Package. Great Every Day Carry!
review_body:
These QuietPoint headphones aren't the absolute best out there, but they provide decent performance at a great price in a very small package.

SOUND QUALITY

The sound isn't the best I have heard from AudioTechnica. The bass is a bit overblown in some songs, the treble is lacking and overall these have a bit of a muddy sound signature. They aren't unpleasant and they will end up sounding better on an airplane than a pair without active cancellation.

NOISE CANCELLATION

These aren't as great at cancelling noise as the Bose QC25, but at the price I would say they do a pretty good job.

BUILD

The ATH-ANC33iS have a good build quality. There is proper strain relief, and the right angle plug is a nice touch. I would like to see a thicker cord, but it isn't by any means cheap. The included bag has a nice feel and will contain the headphones in travel. The inclusion of the comply tips is definitely a nice touch and adds extra value.

Overall, these would be a great choice for someone looking for an inexpensive solution to cutting some of the noise while traveling. If you don't absolutely need the active noise cancellation, there are many better sounding options for the price.

*REVISED RATING 11/5/2015

Forget about perfect sound quality or 100% noise cancellation. These things are unbelievably useful. Their size alone makes them way easier than my QC25s to carry. When I'm taking a trip to the city and don't want to carry a bag, I bring these. When I'm mowing the lawn, I use these. When I'm in a noisy area, I use these.

My only gripe at this point is the location of the battery pack. It gets in the way sometimes. But the battery life itself is FANTASTIC. Way longer than I expected. I have accidentally left these on overnight a few times, and they are still chugging away at the first set of batteries I put in.

The mic for phone calls also works extremely well. I have been on a phone call in a noisy train, and they had no problem hearing me even when talking quietly.

Bottom line, is when I leave the house, I grab these instead of my better sounding pairs of headphones, since they are easy to carry and do a great job at cancelling noise. I would definitely recommend these.ottom line, is when I leave the house, I grab these instead of my better sounding pairs of headphones, since they are easy to carry and do a great job at cancelling noise. product_title: Monoprice Ultra-Slim Wall Mount Bracket for 37"- 70" Flat Screen TV (LCD, Plasma, LED) - VESA Mount, UL Certified
review_headline: Serves it's purpose, but quality is far from perfect.
review_body:
Serves it's purpose, but quality is far from perfect. Of all the mounts available, I ended up choosing this mount because it seemed to meet my goal of allowing me to mount the television as close to the wall as possible. Surprisingly, there doesn’t seem to be many mounts available that do this well… I’m talking absolutely minimizing the space behind the tv.
The design is essentially a simplified version of the discontinued Sanus ML11-B1 which I have another television mounted to. In comparison to the Sanus, the Monoprice design is much simpler, utilizing only the top two VESA mounting points to hang the tv and leaving the lower mounting points simply for placing spacers (one with a kickstand). The downside to this simplicity is that it does not allow vertical adjustment of the tv independently of the wall bracket. So changing the height of the tv or adjusting level must be done by moving/adjusting the wall bracket.
As others have mentioned, the built in bubble level is not to be trusted. It was so bad that I could see with the naked eye that the level tube was skewed in relation to the bracket. So I used a 24” level when mounting the bracket. That’s when I noticed that the mount itself wasn’t straight. It had an arch to it! I ended up balancing the arch so that the gaps between the bracket and the level looked even at the ends. To give you an idea of how warped the bracket was, this came out to roughly 1/16” gaps at each end. With that said, once it’s mounted, it functions perfectly and these defects don’t really ever come into play again… so not a huge deal for me.
One more thing to note. Before I made the purchased, I was wondering how I would be able to reach the short pulls that operate the latch. From the product picture, they looked to me like they were hard plastic loops that were far too short, but they are actually velcro straps pictured looped back and attached to itself. I unlooped them completely so theycould be reached. Even then, they don’t reach the bottom of the tv, but there is some give where you can tilt the tv away from the wall enough get your hand behind there to reach the straps. Releasing the latch allows the bottom of the tv to swing out completely for accessing the back of the tv or taking it off the mount.

product_title: Cable Matters Gold Plated DVI-D Dual Link Cable with Ferrites
review_headline: They are good, but do not be fooled by the gold
review_body:
Do we really NEED gold plating on patch cords? Well, no, not really, nickel plating will do the same thing which is to protect the pins from corroding and causing either a short or become permanently fused to the socket they are married into. Ever thought about what happens the moment you slide the pins into the socket? Ever wonder how much plating will remain after a few disconnects? Well, do not trouble yourself with worry over it, but suffice it to say the plating is quite thin and does the job but is gold really necessary? It looks cool and it is conductive "like" copper.

If gold plated patch cables cost the same as brand X without gold plating, well heck, it is a no brainer... go for the gold! Just be assured that the plating is quite thin and the recycle value of the gold is significantly lower than the value of the copper wire inside.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_body:
I now have two of these remote hubs in my house, and they are fabulous. My first has been in use for well over a year, and I have had no problems associated with the Harmony Hub. My new hub was installed this past weekend, and it works flawlessly. There are a couple points to remember about this nifty device:

1) You need a smartphone or tablet with the Harmony app to set up a new hub. There is no way around this.
2) You need a solid internet connection to set up or change settings on the hub. My internet connection was acting up when I set up my new hub, and this added significant complication and delay.
3) The included remote does nothing but talk to the Hub. The Hub controls your devices. If you have devices in a cabinet, you may need separate IR transmitters. The package includes one. Others are available on Amazon.com or other stores. However, the Harmony hub uses 2.5mm jacks for the IR transmitters, and most non-Logitech transmitters use 3.5mm plugs. You may need an adapter for your non-Logitech IR transmitter, but this is also readily available.
4) While the buttons on the included remote can be programmed multiple ways (including different actions for short and long presses of the button), the number of buttons on the remote is limited. However, you get many more functions from the smartphone app.

Regarding the ability of the hub to control your devices, my original hub does have some issues because of how my devices are situated on my built-in cabinets. It isn't really a fault of the Harmony hub, but a result of multiple devices with IR sensors in diverse locations. My new hub is in an enclosed entertainment center and actually works flawlessly. I did put a different IR transmitter on for my TV, which is outside the enclosure, but the Hub and the included IR transmitter control everything else without difficulty!

If you don't mind taking the time to set up a Logitech remote system, then this is a great remote hub if you have multiple devices in your entertainment center. If you already have a Logitech remote which you configured on-line, you may be able to transfer the settings to this hub, which will save time on set-up. Either way, I strongly recommend this device!

product_title: Yamaha RX-V679 MC Bundle BL
review_body:
Have been using the RX-V567 for several years and was looking for an updated version supporting WiFi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, 4K + HDCP 2.2, and 2-zone output. I'll base this review on the upgrade effect rather than a full review on the sound (which was good with my old model too).

Pros:
- Great upgrade! It really makes a difference. Setup was quick and easy.
- User interface is simple, but good. Gone are the days where it was necessary to search the manual for the mystery mode that allowed bi-amping the front speakers.
- WiFi and Bluetooth worked out of the box. Plenty of options to find and connect to the access point. Haven't used the ethernet port yet.
- Audio streaming from my Synology server works great over the network.
- The feature to redirect the rear surround speakers to the second zone is great. Just what I need - in my setup the second zone is right next to the main zone and I'll probably use party mode mostly, so won't need the rear speakers then.
- Internet radio (although that wasn't one of my criteria) is a useful addition. It's a good list of free web radio stations, Yamaha chose the right vendor.
- Software update came in shortly after I turned the unit on for the first time. It's great to see that a product improves itself without user interaction (I hope Yamaha doesn't see the upgrade capability as a reason to dial down on QA - "we can fix it later!")
- New remote is more intuitive.
- At this point I haven't used the 4K streaming feature (my only 4K content is coming directly from the smart TV), and obviously there was no chance to try HDCP yet. That will probably prove useful at a later time.

Cons:
- AirPlay is limited to audio, no video playback or photo slideshows from the phone.
- Same seems to apply to media from network servers - I was unable to play movies from the network, just audio.
- Got AirPlay into a state where the meta data showed, the progress bar moved, but no audio was playing. Turning the unit off/on and rebooting the phone didn't help, had to unplug the receiver to get it back to working state.
- AirPlay also does some weird things like turning itself on on the phone (iOS issue?), thus moving away from the source that was selected earlier. At this point I disabled AirPlay as it needs some fixes to be enjoyable, either on the Yamaha side, iOS side, or both. A slight disappointment which can be compensated for by using Bluetooth for now - long term it would be nice if guests could play their music without having to BT pair the phone. Minor issue really.
- iOS app is ok, but is lacking a real design. It's seems to be made by hardware folks trying to do software. It works though and it's free, so alright.
- Renaming the zones has to be done in the app and on the receiver separately, and the new name doesn't show in the on-screen menu's top level. Not sure where it's even used.
- For some reason my subwoofer doesn't turn off automatically which it is supposed to do after 15 mins of no signal, so it's drawing power unnecessarily. I can't recall if that also was an issue on my old receiver, and I don't know if it's even the receiver's fault or the speaker's.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 20 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones, Samsung and Android Devices, Black
review_headline: Model 20 i for Apple, Model 20 for other devices.
review_body:
Note that the version 20i is for Apple devices and has four control buttons, version 20 is for all other devices and does not have the added features on the inline conrol, be careful of which one Amazon page is on when you order as they do not include the " i " in the title for some reason.

I'm used to hearing the words "noise cancelling" associated with earbuds, but that usually means the rubber pieces fit well in your ear canals and block outside sounds... The QC20 earbuds have the real deal electronic noise cancellation.
and it works well for me.

While you can press the button on the inline controls to cut it back to hear the outside world when you need to, you will certainly not be turning them off for listening to audio after you first hear the sounds you get from these... pretty fantastic in my opinion.

Also like that these do not fit way into your ear canals as that always causes me some pain after some time, these fit into the entry to your canal and have gone for some time without them giving me reason to remove them because they hurt.

Was happy to find you can use them to cancel noise even without music playing if desired, with the less tight fit they don't block the world fully, but sure do a decent job of it for most outside sounds.
Pretty good when used like this (without audio playing) when you also wear noise earmuffs over top while running motors and tools etc. But... music always helps the work go better anyway so why not use it as well.

Be sure to note that there are two versions,both with 3.5mm phono plug, but one for Apple devices (QC20i) and one for Android and other types (QC20) however, it seems they don't print the two different numbers on the packaging and Amazon does not even list two part numbers.
QC20i Apple version will work for other devices, but you will not get the extra button features to control it. Sound is still great however.
Was going to four star "like" them at first, but had to go with five start "love" them after another week of use.art "love" them after another week of use.

product_title: Victoria Tunewriter III 7-in-1 Stereo Entertainment Center
review_body: I gave it one star because I had to give it a star.  My advice is to save yourself a lot of disappointment and trouble--don't order it.  My only income is Social Security, so I've been waiting a couple years to be able to afford this machine. In the meantime I looked at, and read the reviews for, the available units of this type.  I have a number of LP records and cassette tapes that I really want to get digitized, and since this one seemed to have more good than bad reviews, I was happy when I was able to order it. . I'm no longer happy-- I got it on July 7 and and am returning it on July 8.  I set it up carefully, got the Audacity installed, decided to test it by listening to a tape.  It took a while to figure out the controls, as the manual isn't user friendly (I should know as I spent 7 years writing user manuals) and the markings on the unit itself are almost unreadable.  Anyway, I finally figured it out, and tried to put a cassette in.  Had a number of tries before the cassette finally settled in and I got the door to stay shut.  Pressed play and the music started.  And started was all it did-- for about 3 words of the song.  Then it began garbling.  I've heard that sound before, so I stopped it quickly.  When I opened the door and lifted the cassette out, there was a long, loose loop of tape that I had to  jiggle loose from something in the drive.  Fortunately I learned a long time ago to save all packaging until I'm sure something is going to work, so sadly I put the unit back into the box, printed out the return label, and tomorrow will be returning it.  Guess I'll have to figure some other way to get my LPs and cassettes from analog to digital.

review_headline: Lots of fun for a great price!
review_body: Awesome toy!  Well I wanted something that would receive VHF / UHF and this thing seems to cover them very well.  I found an adapter that goes to a BNC http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009G1T7BW?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o03_s00 which works great.  There is ton's of software out there for my PC and my Android phone.  So far I have used this with ADSB , Trunking police scanner, VHF, UHF aircraft frequencies, spectrum analyzer, FM radio, and some lower frequencies for VOR's that my handheld radios won't pick up.  I'm amazed at all the things you can do with this.  I suggest you search and read lots to find all the capabilities of this RTL.  The included software is useless in the USA, and don't install the included driver as it will not work with the SDR Sharp programs etc.  I'd suggest starting at the SDRSharp page and download and install those first.  I of course didn't do it that way and had to uninstall the driver and software a few times to get the other programs to work correctly.  I also have this working on my Android phone with a spectrum analyzer, ADSB, and tuner frequency scanner.  The included antenna is ok if your outside and works well for ADSB.  For VHF, I just use a magnet mounted car antenna which I have on my work car.  I also have lots of antenna's to use now with the BNC connector.

product_title: iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Ear Pads Cushion For Logitech G35 G930 G430 F450 Headphones (Blue Spare Pillow for G430 G930, Black Spare Pillow for G35)
review_body:
Bought these replacement earpads to go with my new Logitech G430 because I read bad things about the cloth material used on the original earpads, and I prefer the smooth faux leather. After seeing the reviews it was a no brainer to order, and was very disappointed.

To start with, they are about half as thick as the pads included with the headset, and made of a much less dense foam. They squish flat with just the pressure of the headband clamping the headset down on my head. Since I have average to large ears, this means my ears were rubbing against the inside of the earcup with a few minutes of putting it on.

The second critical failing was that these earpads are much smaller than the included pads. They were a major PITA to get on to the headset at all, and it resulted in them being stretched out of shape and not sitting nicely around the ears. the strip of faux leather that goes around the earcup was also strained to the max and would inevitably tear off. In my pictures, please note the blue plastic inside the earcups being visible with the black earpads on and completely covered by the blue ones.

I don't know how these pads got 5star because the ones I got in the mail are complete garbage. If you want leather earpads for the Logitech G230 or G430 headset, you're best bet is to contact Logitech directly and ask them for replacement earpads SPECIFICALLY for the Logitech G930 headset. They will be the same thickness and dense foam as the G230/430 earpads, just finished in faux leather.

review_body:
My son bought these for me for Father's Day, he did good! I listen to a wide range of music, classical, rock, country, new age, jazz...I have 4-12 inch woofers and 2- 1,000 watt amps on my home stereo, if that gives you an indication of how seriously I take music.
These are excellent headphones. They almost make the cymbals on an iPhone sound good...but then, that's impossible, headphones can only do so much. They do a great job with nearly every thing, you can hear the air in live acoustic recordings, the attack of a jazz trumpet, the bow on a cello solo, the subtlety of a fretless bass or the accuracy and transitions of a Jim Hall guitar passage, not to mention the ability to push hard on rock or full symphonic pieces.

It is possible to overdrive these 'phones, and lose the bottom end, but I blame that on the source, certain modern music simply has muddy crappy bass. They did a great job with Bach's Tocatta and Fugue in D Minor, which includes some serious loud bass.

There is some mechanical noise transmitted by touching or bumping the cable. I am going to try some other softer cables to see if that stops. Not an issue for me, but people that are active when using them might not like that.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: Great remote - 3rd generation for me!  They just keep getting better and more durable.
review_body:
My first universal remote was the Harmony 510 which was later replaced by the the Harmony 600. The 510 was decent enough but had significant design flaws like hard to press buttons and short batter life and terrible layout. The 600 was great. After about 2 years of abuse my Harmony 600 has become a little unresponsive at times so I replaced it with the Harmony 650. There is really no difference between these two except the 650 has a "colored" screen. The button layout is nice and very familiar to nearly every cable/satellite DVR remote. The buttons are soft and easy to press.

Pros: good design, long long battery life (9mo-1yr), easy to use after setup, lots and lots of features. If you have to replace or upgrade like I have, setup on your next remote is simple as re-syncing. Extremely durable!!! My wife dropped it the first few months and the plastic over the screen cracked. The remote has been dropped and abused many many times over the past 2 years and it still works great.

Cons: Setup is not the easiest if you are new. Luckily I have had 3 of these remotes and all of my TVs are Samsung so I have never really had to change my setup. Color screen is a scam. I have not hooked mine up to software in a long time, but when I first got it the database of icons is basically non-existent and there are no options(ie: make the screen a different color for different activities)
