product_title: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)
review_headline: With X5 Gen 2 FiiO has taken a winner and turned it into a champion
review_body: I bought the FiiO X5 Gen 1 when it first came out and have thoroughly enjoyed it over the past year. While I loved the Gen 1 there were a couple of things that I thought could be improved to make it a perfect hi-res player; which were -> size/weight, UI, startup time, and .ISO playback - all of which (and more) are addressed in FiiO X5 Gen 2.  I received my Gen 2 yesterday and after a day of use I am happy to report that FiiO has evolved the X5 nicely, making it better but without losing any of the things that made the original X5 such a wonderful player. Native DSD decoding with .ISO file support is extremely nice. While the Gen 1's DSD to PCM support was really good it did lose some of the "liquid" qualities of DSD, IMO native DSD decoding is a bit of an improvement in sound to the previous DSD to PCM conversion of the Gen 1 in the way that if you prefer the sound of a native DSD DAC such as the Schitt Loki you will appreciate the native decoding of the Gen 2. I think for most people it's a very small difference. The bigger thing for me is ability to play .ISO files. So I no longer need to extract the DSD streams from my SACD discs/ISOs which was a pain.  For common file types like 24bit flac's from HDTracks I'm not hearing any difference from the Gen 1 except for the levels which in FLAC (PCM) seem a slight bit lower, and in DSD are noticeably higher. But sounds quality, detail, sound stage, all seem the same to my ears from the Gen 1 - which is absolutely fine by me as I had no complaints with the Gen 1 in the sound quality department. I'm really happy that they didn't muck with the sound too much, and instead focused on DSD and usability/size. One of my minor complaints with the Gen 1 was the user interface which was a spinning UI that was quite confusing. For the entire year I owned it I thought I would get used to it, but I never did. I always overshot the icon I was trying to select or spun the wheel the wrong way. It was a neat idea but in practice was not intuitive to the brain, or at least my brain. I even loaded up the modded firmware to reverse the spin and rotate the UI, and it was a little improvement but was always a little weird. Fortunately in Gen 2 FiiO has booted out the spinning UI, and instead has a more traditional UI nav but still retains the circular "appearance". It's far more intuitive and simple and works like you think it should. My last wish with the X5 was size and weight, and while FiiO didn't shrink the X5 to nano levels it is a big improvement for me. The original Gen 1 X5 is as heavy as it is high quality. This never presented any problem for casual listening at home or on a plane, but on the go it's not a super portable device in the weight department. It reminded me a lot of the early iPods in size and weight and is very noticeable in your pocket. FiiO has cut the size and weight of the original by just enough to make it a more discrete and transparent device in your pocket - but surprisingly at the same time they've improved the build quality over the original which is some feat considering the original was already impressive in that department. It appears to me that they've cut tolerances and are using a little higher grade materials and parts in the Gen 2. The finish is a brushed aluminum vs the Gen 1's anodized surface is to me about the same quality as far as finish. The click buttons are now tighter and there is no longer any slop in the wheel. I also really like the fast startup time of the device. Both initial and wakeup from sleep times are dramatically faster making it more enjoyable to use and I appreciate FiiO moving the power button from the top to the side, it is more convenient there. Another nice touch is the little blue power LED in the button, a small but nice touch. All in all, I loved the Gen 1 and would still recommend it to anyone for great Hi-res audio listening, but with the gen2 FiiO has taken a real winner and made a series of small changes to make it a champion. And after all that it's still less expensive than my old iPod was. Amazing. Can't recommend this device enough.

product_title: TotalMount Apple TV Mounting Shelf (Compatible with 2nd and 3rd generation Apple TVs)
review_headline: Apple TV Mounting Shelf - Hide the clutter of cables
review_body:
Purchased this Apple TV Mount May 3, 2015 to hide our Apple TV from sight. Shipped via Prime and received on May 4, 2015, it's one-day shipping as of this writing. This does not come with a HDMI cord or an Apple TV

Pros: My goal was to eliminate all the cords going to from my TV and auxiliary devices. This did the trick and has worked wonderfully.
- No Tools Required. Took 5 mins to set up.
- Comes with all of the needed strong 3M tape, with 3 different mounting styles: above, below and behind. I do not expect the Apple TV to fall off with this tape. This could be a negative if wanting to move somewhere else.
- If mounting above or below, the mount has the ability to be expanded if needed. You can also mount flat against the back of the TV (like we did). I'd suggest for the best signal, mount it as close to the top as possible. (Pictures posted, close to top but can't see it from the front)
- Even with mounting directly against the back of the TV, we have no signal issues within the family room of the TV responding to the remote.

Cons:
- Sitting at our dinner table, ~ 15ft away and at a slight angle, we lose remote response. I can't speak for remote response from a top or bottom mounting, but would assume this would work better if you have a longer distance to the usual spot the remote is used for.
- Didn't like the look of the top or bottom mount, but this is more personal aesthetics

I'd suggest this to anyone looking to hide their Apple TV device and accompanying cords. Well worth the $15-20 for a cleaned up TV entertainment area, no wall holes from mounting the holder the Apple TV comes with and simple to install/setup.

product_title: Diver 4GB Waterproof MP3 Player with LCD Display and Earphones (Pink)
review_body:
- Out of the box: Packing is solid, device appears well-made and arrived with a partial charge, which is appreciated.

- Getting music onto the device: NOT Mac compatible. I didn’t look first and plugged it into my MacBook Air which caused the mac to instantly shut down. I guess I can’t be sure that’s what caused it, but as soon as I connected the USB cord to the device, the screen went black. However, it never was advertised as Mac compatible, so that’s my fault. Just don’t try it yourself.

On my PC, the device appeared as a mass storage drive quickly, as the directions indicated. It said to add music files to a folder in the drive, so I created a folder called “Music” since there weren’t any folders by default. I didn’t bother with subfolders, and just dumped a bunch of mp3 files in there.

- Turning on the device is easy (press and hold play) then press play to select Music and play again to start the first song. Sound quality is good (out of water) and volume is easy to adjust. Wish there was an option to shuffle songs, but there doesn’t appear to be.

- Swimming: I can’t comment on personal experience because I don’t have access to a pool at the moment, but I have no trouble believing this would work well in the pool. The clip is sturdy and the headphone cord is coiled like a spring so that it is short and won’t get in your way but still has room to stretch as you move around. The connection between the cord and the device is secure and I would expect the earbuds to pull out of my ears before the cord dislodges from the device if caught on something. The buttons are large and easy to learn what to press without looking, with raised markings so that you can feel that you’re pressing the right spot.

I’m not sure how well the pedometer or “swimometer” features work, but they’re nice to have. Overall, it feels like this device was designed to be used for swimming andother exercise—not from a tech/UX perspective like an Apple product would be. This is refreshing since, as a user while exercising, you care a lot more about the thing working while you’re sweating or swimming that you do about how many seconds the pretty interface saved you while uploading your songs.

Overall, this is a solid product that I would recommend for anyone (with a PC) looking for something more durable or exercised focused. It’s also a great price, especially if you consider you (maybe) won’t need to replace it if you accidentally put it through your washing machine.

review_body:
I can hardly believe how expensive these types of cameras are with other brands. I kinda get it, the two way audio feature is surprisingly useful for my business.

Now, because of how many other features are stuffed into this camera, I’d recommend that you thoroughly read the manual before you begin the operate it. This isn’t one of those things that a local tech wiz kid can figure out after fiddling with it for a few minutes.

There’s a video for it that I’ve found, actually. If you go on youtube and search ‘digihitech wi-fi’, there should be a video that explains this particular kind of camera. I referenced it after I read the manual, just to make sure I understood the order that I had to do things in.

With how everything has been dominated by smartphones these days, accessing the camera is easy for me and my employees. Once we get the app for this thing installed, we can see a live view of whatever is going on at the other end. There’s a lot of options with how to connect to the camera from your smartphone for the first time, so there isn’t an issue with any particular smartphone not being able to connect in one way, since it can just use one of the other methods.

The night vision is spectacular with this device. I can make out faces even without the colors. Combined with the motion detection and mobile alarm, I really don’t have to worry about intruders sneaking into the office at any point, or workers snooping later than they should be.

The camera itself is pretty complicated with how they managed to fit everything together in what amounts to an ear flap. That said, no issues whatsoever with moving this camera around. It’s one par with how you learn with bicycles, once you get the gist of it, the actual process if quick and straightforward.

Anyway, very happy with this little guy. Might see about putting up some pictures or footage down the line onto this review. Look forward toit!

product_title: Sonixx X-Fit Bluetooth Earbuds for Sport
review_body:
Why these work for me (and what doesn't):

1. The sound/price-point ratio is good. And by that I mean, I have no gripes. I liken earphones to referees, it's only when they do their job wrong that I notice. Isolation isn't what I thought it'd be, but it's still sufficient enough for plane rides.

2. In terms of connectivity it's pretty good. I connect it to three devices; and old iPhone 3Gs for running, a Samsung Galaxy SIII (my phone), and a Samsung Galaxy Tab 3. The Tab 3 has the best connectivity-- the two phones are about the same. Something I discovered that microwaves will interfere with the signal and cut off your audio, especially with the phones.

3. The ear hooks are pretty good. They aren't slip proof, but they do the job. The only time they fall off is when I'm running full speed and the wind blows them out. It also comes with inserts, which don't really work for me. I think it depends on the shape of your ear canal, since some people swear these things are slip proof.

All in all, I'd definitely buy this product again. I use it for running, or just around the house. The freedom from wires is something I never knew I wanted, but now, I don't think I'd buy another set of wired earphones.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home Touch Screen Remote for 15 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_body: I upgraded to the Harmony Ultimate Home from a four-year old Harmony One.  I like the fact that the Home Ultimate integrates with Smartthings very nicely and it also had a few additional features I wanted to have, such as the IR capability.  The Harmony remotes are truly wonderful in terms of being able to have one device that controls all my a/v equipment.  I would recommend them without hesitation.  I have been able to put eight other remote controls for separate devices in a drawer, hopefully never to be used again!  On top of it, with the Smartthings integration, I can now control room lighting, a ceiling fan, and even my media room fireplace from the Harmony remote.  So why not five stars?  The set-up was not easy.  I expected that already having a Harmony One that all of the devices and macro activities would transfer from one device to another.  Didn't happen.  The Home Ultimate uses different software to program it.  While the new software did find my devices from my Logitech account and load them into the Home Ultimate, all of the macro activities had to be reprogrammed.  In addition, the syncing process did not work at first, and the remote would not send any activity instructions.  After a couple hours of frustration, I finally tried the Microsoft trick of unplugging everything and then repowering. That caused the hub to reboot - and then everything worked.  I also want to note that when I was having set-up problems, I did email Logitech customer support, and they did get back to me within six hours (by that time I had already come up with the rebooting fix) which I thought was a pretty respectable response time.    One other quibble to mention: the Harmony One had physical number buttons which the Harmony Home Ultimate does not.  I miss those buttons.  It makes the remote more complex to use when trying to quickly change channels.  But, in spite of this, and in spite of the set-up hassles, I still think this is a great remote.  I notice some other reviewers have had problems with hub connectivity.  I have not.  The hub does have two IR blasters with instructions that one should be placed outside your a/v cabinet and the other inside the cabinet with the equipment to be controlled.  Perhaps the connectivity problems others have reported might be related to the IR blaster placement.  Logitech does recommend moving the blasters around if the user is having connectivity problems.

product_title: MartinRangers M200B 40 Watts Bookshelf Bluetooth Active Speaker
review_headline: Sound okay, but bluetooth and 1/4in connectivity is a joke
review_body:
Two stars is probably a generous rating for these. I like that they are powered (dont require a receiver) and therefore easy to connect to a tv as well as the fact that they are small enough to fit neatly on my tv stand.

Sound: These sound okay. Fairly balanced and provide a little bit of low end via the rear-facing bass ports. I have them connected to the audio out on my tv via rca. Unboxing and connecting them took all of 5mins. There's some ability to dial in the sound with Hi and Low EQ knobs on the side of the right speaker. I have these dialed in with a little more low-end and cut about 50% of the hi-end to act as a pseudo sub while my tv provides the hi-end. You wont get much below 50-80hz so dont expect these to provide any deep bass, but for my small apartment's TV area these provide a sufficient "umph" to round out the sound of shows like GoT pretty well. However, I bought these not only to connect to my tv but also for the bluetooth connectivity as a quick way to queue up some music when friends are over, and that's where these just dont work.

Bluetooth Connectivity: Does not work. plain and simple. I've tried both android and iOS devices and, at best, i can get the android device to connect briefly, but audio is very choppy and basically useless. My iPhone will recognize the speakers and indicate that it's connected, but when i queue up iTunes or anything else I cannot get the audio to play through the speakers. I was quite disappointed and after spending about an hour troubleshooting I gave up and opted to plug my phone into the 1/4in jack in the rear of the right speaker. Unfortunately, this is where it goes from bad to worse. Using the 1/4 jack limits the output to JUST the right speaker rather than both speakers. This obviously cuts the output in half, limits the quality of your music, and forces you to crank up the volume on your phone just to make it audible.

I took a flyer on these since they were relatively cheap and overall for $100 it's not the end of the world, but if i saved the box i would have returned them for something better.

The directions are sparse to the point of me having to figure out how to set the clock on my own as well as how to download songs and photos. The reason for getting an MP3 player is to get all the music taking up space on my phone and to have it more portable. This isn’t the device to do that. I loaded 165 songs, some of which were MP3s and some MP4s. Despite the product name, this player does not play MP4s. This is disappointing as MP4 is the standard download for music videos and even songs from my old CDs.

I downloaded various files to test the player – music, photos, videos, text documents and even a PDF. When I plug the player into my computer I can see the files yet only a few show up on the player itself. I’m not able to access anything but the MP3s and JPGs.

review_headline: Beyerdynamic T90 and A 20 Amp - Perfect Match.
review_body: To be honest, I feel terrible that I had bought so many headphones and returned them all. I've been listening to the T90 for a month now and the sound just gets better and better. I followed Beyerdynamic advice to pair these headphones with their A 20 amplifier. Not a cheap combination at all, but the crisp, cristal sound is phenomenal. They are a little bit on the warm side though. The treble is high and the bass is tight and punchy but it never feels artificial. It's fun to listen at them; any genre will make you feel young and happy, especially acoustic. The amp is connected to my iPhone 6+ and from that source seems to be the best option in my case. I don't know why the sound deteriorates a little bit when I connect to my 15" macbook pro retina (at some point, I'll try an external DAC). Similar sound headphones to the T90 are the Grado 325e and the Beyerdynamic T1 (surprise, surprise). Just for reference, I did not like the T5p (closed headphones do not sound that great), the boring Bowers & Wilkins P7 (all the money went to the fancy leather), Sennheiser HD650 (hurt my ears), Philips Fidelio X2 (really good for the price), Beyerdynamic DT770 80 ohms (a big, big step-down from the T90), and the Beats Studio Wireless (worst headphones ever at $379.00). So, I'll keep the T90 and the A 20 amp for a very very long time. Thank you Amazon for your patience and your amazing customer service.

product_title: QFX PBX-505100BT Portable Battery Powered Bluetooth Mini Party Speaker
review_headline: ) I liked the first one so much that I bought another ... 07/27/2017 UPDATE
review_body:
I read the reviews here before buying one on sale locally but decided to buy it anyway since bluetooth connectivity is not that important to me as I would either be using the AUX input or the built-in USB/micro SD slots. (I have tested it and BT seems to work OK... knock on wood!) I liked the first one so much that I bought another one to use in my car which has a 1988 AM/FM cassette player.

Perhaps the most impressive feature is the battery. There was a cover on the back secured with 3 screws which presumably held a replaceable battery. I opened it to get the numbers off it so I could see if a replacement battery was available here at Amazon or elsewhere. Wow! This has a sealed lead acid (SLA) just like the one in the portable jump starter for my car (only smaller, of course.) The number on it is 6FM2.6 with a rating listed as 12V 2.6AH and there are several sources at reasonable prices but none here at Amazon yet. I see that style battery used in wheelchairs and golf carts so you KNOW that it is dependable and should last a long time.

The sound is decent enough. BTW it also has a 1/4" jack for a microphone or guitar with seperate controls for volume and echo. For guitar you will to use a pedal or processor to shape the tone which brings us to one of the drawbacks: there are only 6 non-editable EQ settings (including OFF.) I would have liked to see a custom setting to adjust at least the bass and treble but it is what it is

Another drawback is that although it can play countless hours of music from a USB flash drive or micro SD card there are only 2 buttons for navigating- press them once for the next or previous track, hold down for rewind or fast forward at ~1/4 speed. Most players allow you to skip to the next or previous folder. I would have liked to use a card or drive packed with dozens (or hundreds!) of music folders and be able to skip back and forth between them. There is a workaround: if you cue in the track number asdisplayed on the display using the numeric keypad on the remote the player will jump to that track and continue from there.

There are some quirks, at least on the two players that I bought. If you plug in the charger the unit turns on but can't be turned off by the front panel switch (if you misplace the remote you are in big trouble!) And although the remote will turn off the player it will not turn it on. One minor quirk is that there is a button to allow you to repeat one song or all songs but there is no option for no repeat.

One feature or drawback depending on your needs is that the front panel volume control is a master volume which sets the maximum volume available. The volume buttons on the remote control set the relative level between 0 and 31. I like that because once I set the front panel control I don't have to worry about exceeding that volume. I have also noticed that some tracks sound better (or at least different) with the remote volume turned down a bit and the panel control turned up.

One definite drawback is the 1 year warranty from QFX. They will repair or replace it at no charge but you do need to include payment for return shipping. Although that charge is around $10 for most small items it is $75 for the PBX units. Yikes- that is almost as much as what I paid for 2 players! (The PDX line includes huge speakers rated at 2500 watts or more which might justify a $75 shipping charge but certainly not the PDX-505100BT.)

Verdict: It is what it is, and what it does it does well!

EDIT 07/27/2017:
I haven't used either one of my two players for a year and a half but I wanted to compare it to the discontinued and very affordable NYNE Bass Sport (highly recommended if you can find one at half the regular price.) As expected the batteries in each unit were dead but after charging both units overnight neither of them will turn on unless the AC adapter is plugged in. I just downloaded the manualwhich warned that the batteries could be permanently damaged if left without a charge.
So I am dropping rating from 4 stars to 2, at least until I can do further testing.

product_title: AMP Note Portable Bluetooth 4.0 Speaker with Stylish Magnetic Smart Lid for instant on/off and pairing
review_headline: Simple to Use and Great Sound
review_body:
I'm comparing the Antec Note Portable Bluetooth Stereo Speaker to the portable speaker I have been using up until now. I've been using a Cubot Bluetooth portable speaker for my outdoor listening pleasure. It's been a good speaker, but it's range is spotty and the battery life, supposedly four hours, has not lasted that long for me. I am lucky to get three hours from it. If I go onto my front deck and try to put it on the deck rail and don't bring my cell phone outside to be within six feet of it, sound cuts out.

Range

I put the Antec to the test, as I am sick of having to have my cell phone close to the speaker. If I'm outside, I don't want to have to have my phone out, too, I just want to stream music. With the Antec, it boasts a 30 foot range. I found that's pretty accurate as I could get half way to the mailbox before it cut out.

Sound

I am impressed with the sound. It's crystal clear, no static or interruptions. Just clean sound with plenty of volume.

Instructions

First, I am impressed with the box it comes it. This isn't paper or cardboard, it comes in a clear, solid plastic container that's built to last. Inside are two cables (one auxiliary and one USB/mini-USB), the year's warranty information, and the instructions. The instructions are simple to follow. There's the volume and skip functions, the Bluetooth connectivity button, the power switch, and then a button to connect your phone to the speaker. I rarely use my cell phone for calls if I'm home, so I haven't tested that function, but everything else works perfectly.

Bluetooth Connection

Here's the biggest plus in my book. The Cubot often takes a few tries to get it to pair up with my device. The Antec paired up immediately, no fuss. I love that!

One Downfall

There's no real indication on when the battery is about to die. I'll be outside playing music and suddenly it just quits. It would be nice to have a power bar or something to show me that it needs recharging prior to it just dying.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-MSR7 GM (Gun-Metal Grey) High Resolution Audio Over-Ear Headphone (Japan Import)
review_body:
Was looking for a portable headphone with good sound quality. Picked this over the Sennheiser momentum after a lot of research on the net.

Build Quality 4.5/5
First of all, I must say, I am really impressed by the build quality of this pair of headphones, especially at this consumer price bracket. Everything except the headband are of sturdy build. The brush metal finish is higher quality than the sony mdr-1a, and looks freakin amazing with the red accents. The stock cable is nothing good or bad. Does its job and nothing beyond.

Comfort 3/5
The headband pressure and the clamping force is a real pain (physical) to deal with. I had to bend and twist it to stop it from making a dent on my skull. The earcups are soft and comfortable. However, after an hour of listening or so, they can get a little warm. On a side note, the msr7 is by no means light. I consider it slightly heavy for a portable headphone (when compared with the momentum).

Sound Quality 5/5
The SQ is what really matters most after all, and this pair of cans surprised the heck out of me. The soundstage is very wide and deep for a closed-back headphone. Comparing to my home-use Q701, the soundstage is more defined, and when amped properly, more airy than the q701 although less wide. The Msr7 is definitely bass shy in every way, anyone who cannot live without a good amount of bass should stay away from it. Bass was amazing out of the box, too bad they disappeared after burn-in, but they are still very well textured. Sub-bass extension is mediocre, but mid to upper-mid bass are well done. Upper mids and highs are the real gems here. The clarity and shimmer don't lie to your ears. The amount of details is just absurd with amping. No wonder the high-res tag. Even without amping, with my cowon J3, it reveals decent amount of detail. Although sound isn't completely grain free and smooth like the much lower priced Fostex TH7, the MSR7 doesn't sound harsh to the ears either despite its highs focused signature. In general, I will recommend the MSR7 to female vocals lovers. Whoever listens to Pop and movie soundtracks will be very pleased with the purchase.

Isolation 3.5/5
Isolation is adequate for indoor usage. Just don't bother trying wearing it on the streets. It's not enough for outdoors. It's not a lightweight headphone either and not to mention it gets warm after a while. If sweaty ears isn't your thing, just don't. I guess its a bit of compromise made by ATH for the great soundstage and SQ.

Value 4.5/5
At this price point, I must say the MSR7 has a really high c/p value. You can only turn away from this headphone because of its ridiculous headband, or that bass4lyfe is your life motto. Did not regret my purchase at all.

review_body:

Maybe I'm not all together there but I didn't at first and only picked up one channel. Last, move the cord around. Moving the cord an inch or two also improved reception for some channels.

product_title: Sony CMTSBT100 Micro Music System with Bluetooth and NFC
review_body:
For the $200 asking price, this music system is an absolute steal for the amount of content that you get. I'm a huge fan of Sony audio products, so I decided to replace my desktop speakers with this system. This system now serves as my 1)output for my computer/laptop, 2)CD player, 3) bluetooth music player, 4)desktop radio, and 5)headphone amplifier.

NFC is a godsend for this device, as when I come back from work, I can just tap my phone with the NFC logo on this device and instantly play all of my music wirelessly. It also includes a remote control for added convenience. As for the sound quality, I could not ask for much more, as they are a vast improvement over my previous speakers. Great clarity and detail, and the system also has a built-in Bass Boost feature and equalizer for bass and treble to adjust to your liking. The system has an auto-standby mode, so it sleeps once you disconnect or put your input source to sleep. This also includes a headphone jack, which is handy so you don't have to keep switching plugs in and out of your computer. I use this as an amp for my Sony MDR-1A headphones and they sound much better coming through this system than from my laptop or phone.

All I can say is buy this product right now, it has so many uses and makes your music shine for an excellent price!

product_title: Photive Rain WaterProof Portable Bluetooth Shower speaker. Rugged Wireless Outdoor/Shower Speaker with Built in Microphone
review_body:
I wanted to write a review mainly because I saw some people on here disappointed with the battery life. I was able to get a full 8 hours of play from this during my first week of use (perhaps it's battery life will deteriorate over the next year?). I use it for podcasts mainly while working in vacant apartments since my phone's battery capacity is very poor. I'm able to clip this to my belt loop and it wills stay connected wherever I am in the apartment as long as my phone is plugged in at a central location. The unit can get very loud (uncomfortably loud for me listening by myself) so I often listen to it between 1/2 and 3/4 volume. There is very slight distortion in the sound when listening at full volume which I believe is resonance within the device and not a product of the driver being pushed too hard. The things is indeed water proof to splashes and jets and can take a downpour of rain. It also does just fine being thrown around and dropped and keeps on playing. I don't think I would throw it around on purpose, however if it falls of a table or gets sat on then it does just fine. I haven't tested the aux in. The unit does take a few hours to charge, but it can be used while charging. The charging flap is rubberized and connected to the device. The flap is very difficult for someone like me to remove as I have very short fingernails, but using a key to carefully pry it of easily does the trick.

In all I think this unit is extraordinary for what it is and for what it costs. I'll have to see how it does with time, but as of now I'm VERY happy with my purchase and could easily recommend this to anybody who needs a rugged, ultraportable, wireless speaker.

review_body:
My very first MP3 player cost me a small fortune for all of 16MB!! (There are 1000MB in one GB) Now for $20 I have a 16GB slim and sassy with for $20?!
I’m loving this sweet little MP4 player. It’s a beautiful light blue color. It’s easy to load and equally easy to play. This 16 GB little gem will hold 5000 songs. I have no-where near that many songs in my iTunes account, my computer and my iPad all combined. It will take me years to fill this up!
For our camping trip I loaded up several of the 3-year-old's favorite Jake And The Neverland Pirates episodes on this MP4 Player for her to watch. I must say, it was a brilliant move on my part. Alice loves watching NaNa’s tiny TV.
I love that I can not just listen to music, but watch a movie, view my photos, read eBooks and even store data!! Watching a movie or video is awesome because even though this is a small MP4 player the screen is great for holding in your hand and watching. Especially the kids!! The screen is 1.7″ of High Resolution, real color LCD viewing which is perfect for 3-year-old Alice to be entertained.
I think that one of the things I love the most is that with this price I’m not worried when the Grandkids want to play with it.
The battery life is excellent.
This little guy has great sound. The radio works fine, although where we live it doesn’t come in strong enough to really use.
On top of the MP4 player is the power on/off switch. The center round button gives you access to numerous applications on the menu: Music, Videos, Record, Voice, Radio, Photo, Setup, E-book, Games. MP4 even comes pre-loaded with some music, a short animated video and a couple of games too. Just enough to give you an idea of what this little guy is capable of. Hold the round center button down for a few seconds to return to the main menu.
My only whine is that pushing the control buttons is really loud. It’s a minor whine. Over all for $20 I’m impressed.

product_title: Philips FLEX Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
I received the blue/white speaker, but I believe that they are identical except for color. The color is a pleasant turquoise blue, very similar to the colors used with swimming pools.

With that aside, the speaker was rather disappointing for pairing with my Fire tablet. The sound was not as good, nor was it as loud as the onboard speakers the tablet has. I realize that not all devices have such good speakers, and sound quality may be better when compared with other devices, such as phones. This was not the only area that it fell short in, however.

There is an LED light on the speaker, which flashes when charging or fully charged. The directions are less-than-wonderful, pretty typical for a device made in China. It tells you to fully charge the speaker before use, but gives you no idea how long it takes to fully charge the speaker. The LED light is also not an indicator. So, you apparently are supposed to guess when it has fully charged.

The speaker pops up for "better bass". (I didn't notice any difference, to be honest.) However, the silicone sleeve is not easy to grip and pull open to the popped up position. It does pop down easily.

The pop up/down deficit could be ignored and tolerated. The crappy directions could also be tolerated. Even the less-than-wonderful sound quality could be ignored when used with some devices. The cardinal sin is that there is no way to know when the speaker is fully charged. Because of this, I would not use this speaker when I may not have access to a USB charger. (It doesn't even come with its own--it just has the cable.)

Overall, I'd say this speaker would be best suited to use by a child or teen, and certainly never by anyone even contemplating becoming an audiophile. It's also a poor choice for anyone who may have some hearing loss, due to the relatively low volume.

review_headline: Nice little amp, BUT did not work for my intended purpose.
review_body:
Amp is okay and would be rated a 5, but I could not use it for my intended purpose. For my office at work I wanted to plug in a samsung galaxy2 tablet from the audio out jack (headphone out) and run Pandora, but Amp 100 would not recognize the signal. I tried it in Input 1 and Input 2. Even called the Audio Source people and Engineer called back saying he'd never heard of that problem before. Amp 100 worked fine with my mp3 player though.

The tablet and Pandora actually works fine on my Onkyo home receiver and even on an older Sony home receiver I use in my bedroom. I have to turn the Onkyo volume up to 45 or 50 just to get moderate listening volume though. Other sources (e.g. CD or mp3 player) into the Onkyo and a volume of 50 would rock the house and alert the neighbors. Leads me to assume the output level of the tablet is very low, and actually below the threshold for the Amp 100 to recognize. So I use the old Sony to play Pandora from the tablet in my office and use the Amp 100 in my bedroom.

Lesson learned: Make sure your input device will be compatible with the Amp 100.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_body:
Generally, I like Audio-Technica equipment. These worked for a while, but ultimately failed and do have some drawbacks.

Noise Cancellation - These do a reasonably good job of canceling droning sounds like an aircraft. They are not perfect, but are a noticeable improvement over passive-only attenuation.

Battery Life - Reasonable. However, there is not an auto-shutoff feature. If you fail to turn off the cancelation, you will return to a dead set of batteries. Always keep a spare set in the carrying case.

Music Reproduction - Not bad. They are significantly better than cheaper headphones and earbuds. However, they are not at the top tier level.

Comfort - I found them to be reasonably comfortable for short periods of time (less than 1 hour.) Longer times tended to become uncomfortable due to the way the pressure exerts to keep the muffs in place.

Problem - A week after the warranty expired (one year), the left channel went out on these. I can tap the muff and it will sometimes come on, but overall, they are of little use in the current condition.

Overall - If the left channel had not died, I would recommend these without hesitation. However, since I don't know if mine was a fluke or indicative of larger QC problems, I suggest caution. A good pair will likely satisfy most people.

product_title: Philips Rich Bass Neckband Headphones
review_body:
These are the best workout headphones I have ever had. They sit very snuggly on the ears and will not fall off. They even help hold my glasses on!

They are very durable, and the little bungee that keeps tension of the signal wire really works well. I had an older version of these when I was young. I used them for years on my paper route until the foam padding wore off of the cans. I even wore them in the rain several times!

They sound pretty good considering there size and price. Out of the box I found the bass to be far too loud, and the highs were lacking in intensity. After a quick EQ they sound astounding. The open back design definitely gives them an open airy sound with plenty of bass response. In any event, they are leaps and bounds ahead of any ear buds you will ever encounter.

However they do leak a lot of sound due to their open back design. It's not enough to be a problem in a noisy environment like the gym, but at home or on an airplane it may be an issue.

I'm thinking it'd still trip at, say 16-18 amps, but it would need to be a constant load (current) over time to generate the heat required to trip the breaker; but that is what it's for to begin with, i.e., protect the wires (from heat build-up).

Pay careful attention to the alignment of the plug receptacles... look at the picture and make sure it works for you... the plugs sockets are in-line 90 degrees from what you may be expecting.

review_headline: These batteries work great, I've been using them for years at home ...
review_body:
These batteries work great, I've been using them for years at home and now started using them at work. I found that ALL Alkaline batteries will "OUTGAS", something the battery manufactures don't tell you and neither do the electronic device manufactures that used AA, AAA, C & D batteries. 9V & 6V's generally don't outgas into your devices because they are double sealed but the AA, AAA, C & D's will always outgas and destroy your devices. So you either have pull the batteries out after every use to prevent damage or hope the next time you us the device it's before the battery had died and before it has outgassed.

Outgassing of Alkaline batteries is a normal process after the battery has been completely drained for some period of time.

Using rechargeable batteries, you never have to worry about outgassing, only if you break it open but that would be a rare case

review_body: I highly recommend this antenna for the quality of the reception I got.  I live 46 miles from the closest broadcast tower. I was able to connect the unit to the existing cable from my old Dish receiver.  I did the appropriate hookups in the house, and voila, I now get 12 air channels FREE, 11 of which are in HD.  I immediately called to discontinue my Dish service, and the feeling was GREAT!  Naturally, Dish tried everything to get me to stay, but they charge extra for HD and channels I don't want.  I just want local service.  I would have given this unit 4 stars but for the rudimentary English on the directions (hire a native speaker, China) and the fact that I seemed to have paid a disproportionate amount for the j-mount kit compared to the antenna alone.  But I couldn't be more pleased with the reception.

review_headline: Great little speaker with good sound quality and incredible battery life.  A spectacular value for the price.
review_body:
I bought the OontZ on the recommendation of a friend when it went on sale for $19.99. Even at $27.99, you can't beat the price. The sound from the OontZ is pretty decent at most volume levels. It isn't really loud enough to, say, DJ a party, but it puts out plenty of sound for listening to music on the deck or while working on the house. The sound level ramps up a LOT if you simply place the OontZ in a corner (facing out).

If I were rating this thing on battery life, I'd give it fifteen stars. The battery is unreal. On a full charge, I've gotten 18 hours out of it, and it still wasn't dead. The manufacturer's rating of 10 hours is pretty conservative, at least in my experience.

The four-star rating is simply because the sound quality could stand to be a little better. It isn't terrible, but it isn't what I would have expected from a Cambridge Soundworks product. I recognize that the OontZ isn't a Bose Sounddock, but there is a little too much distortion at higher volumes to warrant a five-star rating. If the sound from a UE Boom is a 10 in this size class, the OontZ is a solid 8. Considering you could buy eight OontZs for the price of a Boom, it really is a hard deal to pass up.

product_title: SONOS CONNECT Wireless Receiver Component for Streaming Music
review_headline: Love it, hate it, like an old flame who makes your blood boil but your are better off without
review_body: This is a maddening piece of technology.  When it works, it is pure genius, an infinity of music at your finger tips.  When it doesn't, music withdrawal bites hard, and you will pull your hair out going around in circles with well-intentioned tech support.  My device randomly cuts out, skips, refuses to play anything at all, or goes rogue, ignoring the Sonos controller yet continuing to play music. It seems to have a particular hatred for Russian music. I often have to reset the controller or reconfigure the device from scratch.  Sonos's solution is that I should leave it wired to my router, but one of the key reasons I purchased the device is that it is wireless: I am not going to run an Ethernet cable across the middle of my living room.  When running wireless, your device will become erratic if neighbors' routers overpower yours, which will lead you to spend a lot of time trying different channels.  Performance is particularly bad at "WiFi intensive times of day."  Note:  I live in a large apartment building where many Amazon employees work.  I am losing the WiFi arms race.  I would rate the device 5+ stars when it works and 0 the other times.  There is a mishap almost every day, sometimes small, sometimes show-stoppingly severe.

review_body:
These really LOOK sharp. The go perfectly with a high grade wood grain furnished area. They are extremely comfortable and the sound is excellent. What you may not like is the cord that is included with the unit. If you use these headphones with an amp that is 10 feet away and has a 1/4" female jack then the cord is perfect. If however you use a phone, MP3 player or other portable electronic device with a 1/8" (3.5mm) standard smart phone headset jack then you may have problems. First the cord is very long {10 feet}. Second the adapter that comes with the cord to convert it from a 1/4" to 1/8" has a large diameter and if you have a phone case without an extremely large hole for the headset plug it won't fit. It wouldn't fit mine and I have a large hole. Fortunately I had purchased a short cord that works perfectly: http://amzn.com/B00KAKBHKM

The replacement cord above is rather expensive in my opinion but it is a braided cloth like material and it does feel expensive and elegant.

Also, if you buy a short cord, note that you must twist the existing cord about 1/4 turn and then pull it to remove it. I was tugging on it for awhile before I realized that I had to twist it to remove it. It is well constructed because I put a lot of pressure on it and the cord did not come out of the socket or break so you definitely shouldn't have to worry about normal use pulling the cord loose.

review_headline: Amazingly, does not bounce around on my head when exercising
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:eca08e925bff94015a5fec84da3c7bb0]] I'm not sure how they did it, but these earphones do not bounce around on my head no matter how much head or body movement that I have. If you can't use your arms, it will be almost impossible to get them off your head.

The fit in my ears seemed a little strange at first. This doesn't lodge deeply into the ear, like other headphones, but it rests at an angle on the ear. I realized that this makes it great if you still want to hear ambient noise while you're exercising.

Also, the phone works well, and you can make high quality calls with these headphones. I really didn't realize that the port on my phone would allow me to make outgoing calls. I thought that the headphone port was for outgoing voice only, but I tested this, and there's a high quality mic hidden somewhere inside these headphones. Really, the sound quality is great. I show these headphones with a Moto G 2nd Gen.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend these, but you might want to demo them in a store first or look at a friend's, to see if they're really for you.

Pros:
+Will not budge, once they're on your head
+Very lightweight, for headphones that are so secure
+Great sound quality
+Great for making calls with the mic in the headphones

Cons:
-Does not block out all of the outside noise
-The fit feels a little strange at first.

There is a nice hanging hook so you can hang the speaker from a post/tree or other structure. The light show and sound really are enhanced when the speaker is hanging where everyone can see the lights and hear the sound.

This is a really good speaker – I like the sound and the lights displays are awesome. You’ll have the most fun with this speaker using it at a party.

review_headline: Fine product marred by horrible ergonomics
review_body:
I haven't been using this product for long but so far it seems to work as advertised. I will assume all their impressive marketing claims are true.

The ergonomics of the charger are horrible, though. The batteries have to be inserted and removed at a pretty specific angle and with a pretty concerning amount of force. There are plastic lips on the sides of the charger that make it almost impossible to get a good grip on any of the batteries if the charger is full. There is no hole in the back for you to push the batteries out from behind, as you can with the Energizer charger.

The charger also ships with a piece of cardboard on top of the batteries to break the electrical circuit during storage and shipping. The cardboard is held in so tightly that it's literally impossible to slide out. You can only tear off corners of it. And it's holding the batteries in so tightly that you can't slide them out without some amount of cosmetic damage occurring to them. Now two out of my four batteries have torn plastic coatings on the bottom edges from the amount of force I had to use to pull them out.

Disappointing.

product_title: Sangean Table Top Wooden Radio
review_headline: Looks & sounds great, poor AM reception
review_body:
Overall, I really like the radio and it sounds great, but there are opportunities for improvement...

The Good
I found the WR-15BK to be aesthetically pleasing and the fit and finish on my unit appears to be perfect. FM reception is selective and no drift was experienced. The controls are solid and well-designed for their functions. I'm particularly fond of the geared tuning dial which is well-regulated and accurate to the display frequencies. To my ear, the sound is warm and full while providing plenty of volume. I am really impressed with the sound rendition for such a small form-factor device. The highs are crisp without sounding tinny and and the lows are pretty full - remarkably so for a single 3-inch speaker.

The In-between
I have not cracked the case to determine if the radio is using Superheterodyne or Digital Signal Processing, but I suspect that it is the latter. When tuning away from very strong FM stations, I can hear the unit briefly step off of the signal and reacquire. Once I dial a little further away, the signal totally drops as opposed to fading-out. My guess is that most listeners will simply find that there is no appreciable drift and that stations are easier to tune. However, individuals attempting to DX or catch weak signals in-between two strong stations would probably have a lot of difficulty.

The Bad
The AM reception leaves much to be desired. I compared Sangean's SR-35 pocket radio to the WR-15 since I was only catching a couple of decent signals on the AM band. The pocket radio easily pulled a half-dozen good stations. If you are planning on listening to much in the way of AM programming, I would look for a different tuner.

Since I'll be tuned to FM at the office when its on, the radio does not require much space, sounds great, and matches my desk accessories, I'm very pleased with the purchase.

product_title: iFi Audio Nano-iDSD USB DAC Portable Decoder PCM/DSD/DXD 32bit/384kHz HD dac
review_body:
This is my first foray into portable USB DACs for headphone use with my MacBook. I was originally looking into the LH Geek Out 1000 and the Meridian Explorer2, but decided to go with the iFi Nano iDSD for its support of a large array of high definition audio formats and sample rates, the touted seamless operation with the Mac and the cheaper price. I must say that I am impressed with the Nano iDSD since it exceeded my initial expectations. The Nano iDSD is powered from the host's USB 2.0 port and has an internal rechargeable battery for power when driven by a portable music source. Though its rated headphone output is only 130mW, it can drive my Sennheiser HD580's to levels loud enough to be uncomfortable and has more than enough power to drive my Etymotic ER-4S's.

For the features I have tried, the following is a summary to date (owned and used for 2 weeks)

What Works Well:

- Overall sound reproduction is very clean, accurate, almost analytical. It is a huge upgrade from the sound directly from the Mac which sounds muted and compressed by comparison. At the price, it is a serious value.
- Handle PCM audio from 16-bit/44.1kHz to 24-bit/192kHz without a problem. I used a sample album from HDTracks which has tracks with various sample rates and the Nano iDSD switches between them seamlessly.
- "It just works" with the Mac. Just connect to the USB of the Mac and turn the unit on and it is recognized in the "Audio Devices" by the Tidal streaming music player and the Audirvana player.

What Needs Improvement:

- I have detected what seems to be a glitch. When the Nano iDSD is connected to the Etymotic ER-4S and the volume control on the DAC is set to minimum, it drives the Etymotics at very loud levels. However, continuing to turn the volume control knob drops to the volume to expected low levels and the volume seems to operate normally from there. This only happens with the Etymotic's andnot with the Sennheiser's. By the way, I do not consider this an issue just an oddity.

There are other features I am looking forward to trying especially the support for DSD formats as well as use with my iPhone. Also, I plan to pair the Nano iDSD with an inexpensive headphone amp like the Schiit Audio Modi2 whenever I decide to upgrade from my Sennheiser's.

Overall, I am very pleased with this purchase. I do recommend the Nano iDSD for MAC users looking for an inexpensive way to upgrade their laptop sound.

product_title: Focal Electra 1028Be Floorstanding Speakers Champagne (Pair)
review_body:
I've had these speakers for a little over 6 months at this point and I am extremely pleased with their performance. My split is about 80% music and 20% home theatre, so the speakers are mostly run in 2 channel mode. They dig deep enough that you will not feel like you are missing any of the frequency range when listening to most genres of music. I listen to a lot of Jazz, Indie, Electronic, Acoustic, and Live music through these speakers, and they do every one of those genres justice. So much so, that any deficiencies in the recordings (or the rest of your signal chain for that matter) will be tough to miss. This is a serious consideration when purchasing speakers in the Electra range: they are unforgiving. I've paired mine with an Oppo BDP-105 and a Rogue Audio Cronus Magnum to tame the Berylium tweeters on some of the poorly recorded tracks in my library. The performance varies heavily based on the tube being used in the preamp section of the CM, but that's a story for another day.

Tight bass, crystal clear highs, and a mid-range that will perk your ears up when you catch that subtle cough in the background of that recording that you've listened to a hundred times but never heard before. Focal recommends that you sit dead center of the speakers for best performance, however, I've found the off axis response of these speakers to be wonderful. Placement will be important with these in regards to low frequency performance. My pair is not set up in an ideally shaped room bit they still sound amazing. Looking forward to a day where they have a room that's on par with some of the nicer ones I've been in at some of the local Hifi shops.

I've heard similarly priced speakers by Kef, B&W, Totem, Paradigm, Monitor Audio, etc, and you know what? They all sounded incredible. For my money, the Focals had the sound signature that was most pleasing to my ear, and for $7000, you sure as hell better get it right the first time. Barring a radical change to speaker technology (like some of the things Devialet is doing), I expect these to be the only pair of floor-standing speakers I ever own.ker technology (like some of the things Devialet is doing), I expect these to be the only pair of floor-standing speakers I ever own.

These are the third bluetooth speakers I've owned, having previously owned some speakers from bigger names (Jambox, Pill), but these are by far the best. For the size they put out good sound. Considering the many, many limitations faced by bluetooth speakers (including the downscaled music files, the limits of bluetooth, size, portability, battery-powered, etc.), these speakers are great (but realistically, they won't make you forget your large, wired speakers you used to have connected to your CD or phonograph.)

They hold a charge and feel very rugged. The speakers feature a screw on back so you can protect the ports from dust and water. They also have an "out" so you can charge your phone. I've been very happy with my purchase and recommend these speakers.

product_title: Panasonic ErgoFit In-Ear Earbud Headphone
review_headline: Great sounding headphones at any price.
review_body:
The construction feels a little cheap, but that is literally the only complaint. They are comfortable and have a beautiful depth of sound. The highs are crisp, the lows are present and appropriately not overpowered. I like strong bass, but not Detroit style shatter your back window bass. These are well balanced headphones. To get good bass you need to pick the rubber tip which fits your ear right. Try a size bigger than you think, you may be surprised. The microphone works very well and I am told it sounds clear.

These are not hip-hop headphones. If you listen to rap, go waste your money on beats. I rarely exceed half volume, they get quite loud for me.

There does not seem to be much sound bleed, good for those who are courteous to others around them, bad for those who like everyone to hear their music.

To the people saying they are not durable, I am not sure what you did to yours but I beat the heck out of mine and they work just as well as when I initially bought them. I accidentally put them through the wash, and after they dried out they worked perfectly fine. If you do this too, take the rubber tips off and blow them out. Then let them dry for a few days before plugging them in.

product_title: Status Audio HD One Headphones - Noise isolating. Matte finish. Foldable. 2 cables. Mic.
review_headline: Usually I'm in lock-step with such a high-rated product, but these just didn't come close for me...
review_body:
One of the main reasons I love Amazon is because of the product reviews. I've bought many products that I've really liked, sight unseen, all because of the % of people who really liked them (4-5 stars). That's why I bought these headphones.

Sadly, this was not such an item, for me!

A few years back I bought Audio Technica ATH-M50 headphones for use when playing my Roland electronic drums. Those are a fantastic piece of equipment - crystal clear highs, solid lows, and smooth throughout the entire range in between. This round I wanted to get my dad, who was an audiophile once upon a time and has become enamored of viewing YouTube clips on his smart phone, a really nice pair of headphones. My dad knows his hearing isn't what it used to be, especially in the highs, so I looked for a highly rated set that was less expensive. It looked like these would be a good choice.

In short, I did not like them and will be returning them. I am also a former (and still part-time) audiophile. The bass on these headphones was not as good - just didn't reach down as low as my Audio Technica's - and the mid-to-high mid's in these Status Audio phones had, for me, a bone-rattling resonance when I listened to them. It was nearly painful to the ears.

I decided to go back to the Audio Technica line and found that for $70 (only $20 more than these), I could get a pair of Audio Technica ATH-M30x's. Frankly, I can't tell any difference in the actual sound between the Audio Technica 30's, and the 50's I have been so happy with for almost 5 years now. And compared to these Status Audio phones, the Audio Technica bass is more solid, the highs still crystal "clear as a bell," and the mid's are far smoother and not irritating. Again, I'll return the Status Audio set and will be giving my dad the Audio Technica ATH-M30x's.

Sorry to other reviewers for going "against the grain." Normally my experience lines up well with other Amazon users. In this case it just didn't. For $20 more I highly recommend those Audio Technica ATH-M30x's, instead of these.

I received my switch yesterday and unfortunately have to join the latter category. The switch's blue LED comes on as soon as I connect the pigtail to my TV and plug in the DVD/Blueray player. The light blinks slowly. When I turn on the DVD, the light blinks faster but the TV's HDMI channel still says, "No signal."
What's the meaning of a fast- or slow-blinking light? It's a mystery. Nothing I've done so far has gotten a signal through the switch to the TV. One more try and it's outta here and on its way back to Amazon. Too bad. It seemed like a great product

review_body:
We tried this Bluetooth headset with my usual music track to see how it sounded, as well as how it fit.

Headset

Audio cable
USB charging cable

PLUS

+ We had no difficulty in understanding the control.
+ Paired with Bluetooth fine. Announcer says, "Ready for Bluetooth," and "Paired with bluetooth!"
+ Attractive design (I had the blue.)
+ On information card, there is an email address in case of difficulties. Excellent!
+ Device arrived charged sufficiently to use right away.
+ Liked the carry pouch - nice touch!
+ Earpieces fold inward to reduce to compact size.

CON:
- Uncomfortable. Each earpiece does not align with one's ear. I would not like to wear this more than a few minutes.
- User Guide is poorly written, although the printing is large enough, and I could sort-of understand what they are trying to say.
- User Guide is unclear about what the warranty length.

All in all, a so-so product. I cannot recommend; just too uncomfortable to wear.

product_title: iFox iF012 Bluetooth Shower Speaker - Certified Waterproof - Wireless It Pairs Easily To All Your Bluetooth Devices - Phones, Tablets, Computer, Radio
review_body:
The sound is surprisingly good for the speaker's size. The suction cup works well even if the surface is damp from condensation. Make sure you have a good grip on it when taking it down, but mine survived a 5' drop onto tile without any problem.

I wish there were a 4.5 rating, because the issues I have are extremely minor. I would prefer a standard connector for charging, since having a proprietary one means you have to keep it with you if you will need to charge the unit and if you lose it you're toast. However using the smaller plug probably helps keep the unit as water tight as possible. The controls on the unit are discernible by feel, but it would be nice if they were just a little more pronounced.

That leads me to the final kudos for the speaker, or more accurately the company behind it. The little user's guide is easy to lose on devices like this, but the company sends you a soft copy. That could be useful to anyone, but for someone who is blind, it's a very nice touch, since we can't read the printed manual at all without some form of assistance, be it human or an OCR solution. I will say sending it in 3 different email messages is overkill, but it's not exactly a huge file.

I would definitely buy this again, but I don't think I'll have to, at least until the battery gives out.

product_title: PWOW® USB 3.0 to 2.5"SATA HDD Converter Adapter Cable with Enclosure Case
review_body: First of all this is a very cool idea and I really wanted this device to work.  However, I could never get the device to work properly while connected to a USB 3.0 port.  The advertised product clearly states that USB 3.0 at 5 gbps is supported, but from my experience it doesn't.  Connected to a USB 3.0 port (which I know works fine with other USB 3.0 devices and hard drives), I tried both a 2.5 inch laptop spinning drive and an SSD drive.  Neither could keep a stable connection long enough to be formatted.  They would disconnect and reconnect over and over.  After several attempts, I did finally manage to get one of the drives formatted.  I then tried to copy a 5 GB file to it.  The speed was in the range of 10 MBs to 20 MBs and then the connection dropped after a couple of seconds.  I tried to copy the file several more times, but the same thing happened.  Then I plugged it into a an USB 2.0 port and was able to format and copy files with no problem.  The speed when copying the 5 GB file on the USB 2.0 port averaged around 23 MBs.  So, yes it works, but not as advertised and it is not stable when connected to a USB 3.0 port.  I would not recommend this device unless you are happy with USB 2.0 speeds.  I bought this hoping to be able to use it at USB 3.0 speeds and so that I wouldn't have to take drives in and out of my external hard drive enclosures all the time.  But this device isn't stable enough to do that.

product_title: Shure SRH840 Professional Monitoring Headphones (Black)
review_body:
I needed headphones with sound isolation to use in an air plane to a trip to Europe. I don't like noise canceling headphones, so those were not an option.

After reading all the positive reviews, I decided to order the Audio Technica ATH-M50x. In one word, "disappointed". I can see how teens may like this sound signature, but I really didn't like it. The bass is so pronounced that it bleeds into the mids. The mids are so recessed that some times it is really hard to understand song lyrics, or even worse to understand movie dialogues. What is is hard for me to understand is that these headphones are used by professionals, really??????

I decided to return the Audio Technica M50x and I ordered the Shure SRH840. The 840 WOW!, seriously WOW! They are about $30 more expensive than the M50x, but the moment you listen to them, you instantly forget you spent the extra $$$.

The sound coming out of the Shure SRH840 is more neutral than the M50x Lows, mids and highs are equally presented.

I listen to everything so please don't judge :) , let me explain. When you listen to an Adele song and the bass is so strong that it sounds like a rap song, that is not a good thing. And that is exactly what the M50x does.

I think a rap song should sound like rap, rock should sound like rock and a balad should sound like a balad. The 840 is so neutral that it does that. The bass is strong if a song has strong bass and it will sound softer if the song is softer. I don't really how some people can listen to headphones with emphasized bass. Believe me I know what I am talking about, a home I have the headphones with the best bass in the world, the Audeze LCD 3 and for $200 the 840 don't sound bad at all.

I know there are better headphones out there, but this is probably the best closed headphone under $200.

product_title: Diver DB-10 4GB Waterproof MP3 Player with Waterproof Earphones (Blue)
review_body: This was exactly what I needed for my monotonous laps in the pool. It helps me keep a better, more steady rhythm where I wasn't taking as many breaks in between and can keeping my heart rate up as well as helping me relax after a workday (or away from stressful toddlers!). Clips easily to my swimsuit. It sounded fine with the the earbuds out of the water but was like surround sound once submerged. You can't move super fast, but I'm not at that intensity yet anyway. My ears are small so the wraparound part slipped off if I jerk or move too fast, but I usually slip them over my goggle straps and they stay in, albeit a little awkwardly. review_body: Look, I don't know how this company produces and delivers so much value for so little money.  The mount is good, very good.  It is simple, well constructed and sits tight to the wall--which matters to me.  I want the TV to be as unobtrusive as possible.  The real difference is the thoughtfulness of the company with the installation and accessories.  I'm a commercial construction professional-- most of the fasteners and anchors provided by similar companies are junk.  Not so with Cheetah.  They provide very high quality load spreading toggle anchors-- these things are between 5-10$ each if purchased separately (it knocks me out that all their stuff is branded with their turquoise color).  They provide a very complete array of high quality bolts, screws, washers, spacers etc.  They really have thought this thing through.  What really surprised me, however, is the way they pre-assembled the splice hardware by loosely screwing on the bolt/washer/nuts into the splice brackets.  This helps people (especially those who don't like reading instructions) understand immediately how to assemble the unit.  They also provide a torpedo level AND a line-level vial (even though very few people know what to do with a line level).  It makes me chuckle with surprise though.  The instructions are clear, written by someone who understands the King's English (rare) and well illustrated.  The unit works dependably.  It is solid (I have a 65" screen hanging from it) and the quick release mechanism is simple and effective.  What more could you ask from a lowly TV mount?  I'm glad you asked;  they also give you a high quality ARC (Audio Reverse Channel) HDMI cable with braided cable cover (yes, in black and turquoise).  This thing is worth at least 10 bucks even on Amazon.  I don't know how they do this AND provide it all for one of the best prices I've ever seen for a non-articulating TV mount.  Well done guys.  I'd like to get to know your company.  I'll bet it's impressive behind the doors too.

product_title: Grado SR60e Headphones
review_headline: They feel great and sound amazing!
review_body:
It's sad to say, but most people today have never actually owned decent audio equipment or have really even been exposed to decent-sounding consumer audio equipment. As a result, the public has been suckered into thinking that Beats By Dr. Dre or Bose headphones, because they cost $$$, are the ultimate experience. Both of those are terrible excuses for "good sound." If you want more bass than your eardrums can handle, then yeah - Beats are probably your headphone. But if you truely want to hear what your music sounds like, but Grados!

Grados use an open back design, meaning the back of the driver radiates out into the air. They don't have lots of isolation (thus they're not good for riding the subway or monitoring live sound), but they're the perfect headphone for just about every other application. The foam cushion and bendable metal headband allow you to wear them for hours with very little fatigue.

Then there's the sound. To say that you'll rediscover your music is a bit of an understatement. Being open back, there's sound is complete of mud or boominess. This allows you to really hear into the mix. You'll hear the kick drum and bassline separate entities (not just a wall of bass noise). You'll hear an accurate rendering of the "soundstage" (the stereo placement of different instruments, reverberation, etc) along with things like tape spices and MP3 compression artifacts. In short, it sounds like you're hearing a real acoustic event taking place, not a wall of psudo-related noise like some headphones. They don't require a lot of volume level to be heard clearly and are un-fatiguing enough that you can listen for hours on end.
