product_title: Targus Driver Bluetooth Speaker, Black
review_headline: All undocumented beeping & LED status indicators explained. Complete review.
review_body:
Though branded Targus, this speaker is manufactured by Sakar … and it says so right on the external packaging as well as in the User's Manual. It bears reasonable similarity to the discontinued Altec Lansing-branded Soundblade Bluetooth Speaker, model iMW855-XL that sold for one Benjamin … that was also manufactured by Sakar. This Targus unit also currently retails for thirty smackers at Staples.

This speaker was manufactured in four color choices: white with gold trim, matte rubberized black, lipstick red … and a sort-of-Microsoft blue. The speaker's dimensions are 2.25" tall x 8.5" long x 2.5" deep.

This speaker DOES have a built-in microphone and so it DOES pair to smartphones to function as a speakerphone. It can also be paired to other audio devices to function solely as an external speaker. The speaker comes with a micro-USB-to-USB charging cable; no USB-to-wall charger unit is included.

The User's Manual seems very weak. For instance, it documents neither the meaning of any of the speaker's loud, aggravating beeps nor the speaker's un-pairing process. And barely documents anything regarding the meaning of the speaker's LED status indicators.

On top of the device there is (at left) a play/pause button at left, (at center) a rocker switch for (press-and-hold) up/down volume AND/OR (single-tap) last-track/next-track, and (at right) an answer/end phone call button. Speaker sound quality is very good, for the price, IMHO. The speaker's volume cannot exceed the volume on the paired device. Accordingly, I recommend just using the volume rocker switch on top to maximize the speaker's own volume … then actually controlling the volume using your paired device.

There are also three small holes on top. At left is a red/green LED, at center is the microphone hole and at right is a blue LED. The microphone hole would have been better placed on the front, of course. The top of the speaker slants slightly away from the front … and that only further inhibits the microphone. AND my ability to see the LED status indicators at desktop level. Sometimes I have to position the speaker so I am talking "down into" the top of the speaker. Fortunately I can report that this speaker, even though its microphone is so close to the speaker's audio output, does not exhibit any kind of "feedback loop" or "echo problem."

The speaker has a small "On/Off" switch, a micro-USB plug for charging the speaker and a 3.5mm mini-stereo aux plug for directly jacking in an audio device. This rear positioning of the "On/Off" switch makes using it very awkward; I have to catch it with the tip of my fingernail to flip it. The switch belongs in a more convenient position and should be of a type of switch (or button) easier to use/flip than this. And for that matter, the 3.5mm mini-stereo aux plug should have been up front or on the side as well.

The bottom of the speaker provides access to the battery compartment, containing a replaceable, rechargeable BL-5C 800mAh 3.7V battery. The battery is unbranded, but it is covered in a gray-and-black-with-semicircles pattern that mimics exactly an equivalent Nokia battery product that is widely available for a fiver. The compartment lid doesn't always pop off easily … and the sticker on the battery about positioning it correctly was, well, incorrect. And it appears that the compartment was designed so the battery is in there slightly crooked, even though that IS the correct position. The bottom of the speaker has four rubber feet to protect your furniture's finish. They tend to fall out but do snap back in easily enough. A drop of glue on each foot easily solved that problem.

When the speaker is turned on, it will be searching for its paired device, if it is already paired. If the speaker is unpaired, it will be in pairing mode, searching for a device with which to pair. No manipulation of the speaker itself need be done when it is in pairing mode, it will automatically send a pairing request to the first available device it finds (assuming your device is visible to non-paired devices, else your device will have to be told to "scan for devices.") Accepting that request at the device (and entering the 0000 pairing code, if requested) will complete pairing of the device with the speaker. Un-pairing the speaker is also entirely accomplished using the paired device. According to the User's Manual, the speaker cannot be paired with more than one device at a time; I have not tested it otherwise.

While the speaker Bluetooth-connects to its device automatically and promptly, it Bluetooth-DISconnects rather poorly. Even after switching the speaker's "On/Off" switch to the "Off" position, my phone sometimes still "thinks" it is connected to the speaker for quite some time thereafter. I have had to turn Bluetooth off my device, then turn it back on again, to resolve that problem when needed.

The User's Manual claims 4 hours of playback time at medium volume. The external packaging claims 8 hours of playback time (presumably at minimum volume). So I am guessing two hours at maximum volume. My actual experience is that, if the speaker is on "stand-by" (ie, on, but is not actually used as a speaker, paired or not) a full charge will last about 24 hours before the speaker begins to signal "low battery" with loud, nagging beeps. The Manual claims 4 hours to fully recharge the battery; I've fully drained it and seen it indicate full charge in just over 2 hours.

The User's Manual states that you cannot charge the speaker unless the "On/Off" switch is set to "Off." Despite what it says, I have no trouble charging the unit while it is on and/or leaving the micro-USB plugged in all the time. Except that I have to endure an occasional nagging beep telling me it's not charging … when it actually is.

Despite the aforementioned negatives, given the excellent sound quality and the low price, I can still recommend purchasing this speaker. I dinged it one star because of the useless, loud and aggravating beeps it seems to always be emitting to indicate its status.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Here's that list of what all the beeping and LED status indicators are signaling to the user:

* Single beep: Speaker has been successfully turned on.

* Two-step up-step beep: Speaker has just connected to its Bluetooth-paired device.

* Two-step down-step beep: Speaker has just disconnected from its Bluetooth-paired device.

* Two-step quick "bee-buh" beep: Toggle switch has reached minimum volume. Beep repeats once per second if toggle switch is continually held down.

* Two-step quick "buh-bee" beep: Toggle switch has reached maximum volume. Beep repeats once per second if toggle switch is continually held down.

* Two quick same-tone beeps (about every two minutes): Critically-low battery charge. If connected to its Bluetooth-paired device, the speaker will remain connected.

* Four quick, low-tone, same-tone beeps: Near-zero battery charge; shutdown imminent. If connected to its Bluetooth-paired device, the speaker disconnects (despite a constant-on Blue LED indicating otherwise). The speaker will no longer successfully connect to its Bluetooth-paired device.

* One short beep, followed by five longer beeps: This beep is a reminder that the speaker is attempting to charge while the "On/Off" switch is set to "On." The User's Manual states the speaker WILL NOT charge in this condition, but it actually WILL charge. This beep occurs only once, somewhere between 5-7 minutes after the On+charging condition is initiated. However, if you leave the charger constantly plugged in, every time you use the speaker it will shift into charging-mode and eventually emit this beep again. Even worse, sometimes when you are using the speaker with the charger plugged in, the speaker will cycle from full-charge to charging mode repeatedly, causing the beep to keep reoccurring. After a while that gets pretty durn aggravating!

* Red LED, constant-on: Speaker is charging. The charging cycle is complete when the Red LED goes dark. The Red LED will indicate independent of any Blue LED or Green LED indicating.

* Blue LED (but no Green LED), constant-on: Speaker is currently connected to its Bluetooth-paired device.

* Blue LED (but no Green LED), flashing (about once per second): Speaker has connected to its Bluetooth-paired device during the middle of a telephone call. When the telephone call ends, the Blue LED will revert to constant on.

* Green & Blue LEDs flash alternately (about once per second): Speaker is trying to connect to its Bluetooth-paired device -- but does not detect it. If the speaker is not paired to any device, the speaker is now in pairing-mode.

* Green & blue LEDs flash in synch rapidly (about three times per second): Critically-low battery charge. If connected to its Bluetooth-paired device, the speaker will remain connected.

* Green & Blue LEDs, both constant on: Near-zero battery charge; shutdown imminent. If connected to its Bluetooth-paired device, the speaker disconnects (despite any indication via a constant-on Blue LED). The speaker will no longer successfully connect to its Bluetooth-paired device.

* All LEDs dark: Either (1) the battery is dead OR (2) the speaker's "On/Off" switch is set to "Off" and battery-charging is not in-progress.not charging … when it actually is.

Despite the aforementioned negatives, given the excellent sound quality and the low price, I can still recommend purchasing this speaker. I dinged it one star because of the useless, loud and aggravating beeps it seems to always be emitting to indicate its status.

product_title: LUXA2 Bluetooth Speaker with Wireless Charging Station
review_headline: Great Sounding Stereo Surround Speakers, Very Well Balanced Sound Across Lows, Mid, and Highs.
review_body:
I have to say that these speakers surprised me, they sound great and are easy to setup. Simply power each one up and they bluetooth sync together. Then on one put it into discovery mode and on your source device find it in your bluetooth settings and pair up. This is your master speaker now. All audio will flow through this guy and in sync play in both speakers for a true stereo surround sound solution. You can place a left and right channel setup by just setting these apart. You can also use 3.5MM line in with an included 3 plug cable, and also charge these at the same time with a 3 plug micro usb cable included as well. So if you don't want to use bluetooth, thats good and this direct line approach works well.
Now for sound, these are very well balanced and sound crisp and clean, they have decent highs and low bass and good mid range. None of them are industry leaders in a specific area, but as I said, very well balanced across the board. So if you are looking for a Bass heavy speaker, not the ones for you. With up to 8 hours of battery life these will get the job done. I was surprised by the size that they sounded so good. They are very portable and come with a nice carry pouch as well. Well built, they have some weight and feel and look like a quality speaker. And the big win here of course is the true stereo sound you get with having two in step to your playing device. Pair one, get two. Great speaker solution.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V675
review_body:
I've been putting up with my Yamaha RX-V1065 for about 5 years now. Within the first year of ownership, the unit's power function (on/off button) started to fail. At first, like a normal person, I would turn the unit off at the end of the day--one day I turned the unit on, the display appeared for about 2 seconds, and then the unit promply shut itself off with a rebellious "click" sound. After waiting a few seconds, I pressed the power button again. Clicked on for 2 seconds, then shut down again. A third try, same power failure. At that point, after 3 tries, the unit simply went dead. What you do then is you unplug it, plug it back in to get another 3 chances for it to work. On average it would take about 20 tries--unplugging and plugging back in every 3 tries--to get the unit to power on and stay on. Yes, we use a high-tech power strip/surge protector, that's not the issue. Yes, the problem is with the quality of Yamaha's overpriced, defective product.

At this point, we decided to just leave the unit on all the time, 24/7, to avoid this obvious product defect (except when we left town for extended periods, then we would unplug it and go through the same ridiculous and infuriating process to get the unit to stay on again when we returned). Invariably, for 5 years, I played this game until finally, the unit went completely dead. Yeah, maybe I should have fought back more--returned it to the store, etc. etc. But honestly, since I could eventually get it to work, I avoided this inconvenience. But now that the unit has completely crapped out after never really working properly from the beginning, I feel compelled to write this review, and to warn others about Yamaha receivers.

Personally, I'll never buy another Yamaha receiver again in my life, based on the extremely low quality of the particular product I ended up with. I'm not a tech/electronics expert, but I am knowledgeable and experienced enough to appreciate and insiston quality technology and superior sound quality when it comes to home entertainment, especially when you pay more for it. I don't have much patience with expensive equipment that doesn't perform at a high level, let alone turn on when you press the power button! In fairness, I do have a Yamaha Blu Ray DVD player that I bought at the same time as the bogus crappy lemon receiver, and this has had absolutely no problems.

Just don't buy Yamaha receivers. In my experience, they are junk, and a frustrating waste of hard-earned money. I would love to hear someone tell me why I'm wrong about this. But my replacement receiver will be a Sony or some other higher quality yet affordable brand.

review_headline: Nothing fancy, but it does the job, as long as you don't overload it!
review_body: When you need a 12V outlet from a battery or other 12V source, this is a very handy little device. I am have lots of experience with this stuff , and I feel I should warn anyone considering this device that this is not designed for powering large loads. The wires are pretty light gauge and should not be overloaded. There is no fuse or other overcurrent protection, so you have to monitor it yourself (or put your own protection in place). If you're not sure whether your load is too much, keep a close watch on the wires when you start the load. If the wires start getting warm right away, the load is probably too big and you should probably find a similar device with heavier gauge wires. Like I said, this can be a handy little device, but should only be used if you know what you're doing.

product_title: Ortofon Ds-3 Cartridge Needle Gauge
review_headline: Even if I did get a bad one, you don't normally expect to see such ...
review_body:
Got one of these from a Japanese vendor. I was looking for Japanese made quality and did not want one of the myriad of Chinese made gauges out there.

I don't know if I got a defective one or not, but this gauge performed well below expectations. Accuracy is cited at .01g, but mine was all over the map. I used a small 5g calibration weight, and the unit read from 4.5 to 5.25g, depending on the position of the test weight on the tongue. There was only one location where the weight read exactly 5.00g. And unlike other scales, there is no marking on the tongue as to exactly where this "calibrated" location is. Unlike what some users publish, it does matter where the actual weight is located, particularly if you are talking .01 g accuracy.

I also had a lot of problems with the tare staying at 0.00. After a few measurements (adding/removing the weight), the tare values started drifting up to 0.15-0.20 g. Hitting the "TARE" button would not restore the reading to 0.00. Only cycling the power would bring back the zero.

I find this level of performance to be way under standards for a Japanese product. Even if I did get a bad one, you don't normally expect to see such a unit get through the Japanese QC.

product_title: Marantz SR6008 7.2-Channel 1080P and 4K Ultra HD Pass Through, Networking Home Theater Receiver with AirPlay (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I’ve owned many receivers in my 55 yrs. such as Kenwood, Pioneer, Yamaha RX-V series, Sony, & Outlaw. This is my first Marantz product of any kind. I use this unit as a pre-amp for now with an Outlaw 7-channel power amp.

The Good: Audyssey setup was surprisingly impressive. Audio Processing for movies is excellent. Great features such as XM radio, and other streaming services. It recognized music on my NAS, pass through video looks great, and the unit allows you to make picture adjustments. Love the phono input. Pretty easy to operate, and the setup wizard was simple to follow.

Cons: Remote pretty basic (I ordered the one that comes with the SR7008 which is a backlit learning remote) you can also download the app to use with your phone or access control via IP address on your PC. No built-in Bluetooth (again ordered the optional RX101 for bluetooth). No wireless network adaptor (guess I could buy one of those external ones or just run a network cable). No status display with Zone-2 out, component monitor out or composite monitor out. To be fair the SR7008 has some of these features, but wasn’t willing to pay the difference.

Conclusion: Receiver sounds better with movies than music. Had to do some manual tweaks to get the sound I like, but most of the multi-channel receivers are like that these days. Also you can’t make quick sound adjustments without the video monitor since most of the adjustments are menu driven. Overall I’m happy with my purchase. The features outweigh anything negative. The sound is smooth & not over bearing. Better high frequency response than any of my Yamaha receivers to the ear. The only small concern I have is that this unit runs a little warmer than any of my previous receivers except for the Sony (it got Hot), and I’m only using this as a pre-amp. I installed the unit in the same cabinet with an open back as my past units. Hopefully it won’t be a problem.

REVISED***

After (6) months in using this unit. The audio will drop about 15% for a few seconds and then go back to its set volume. This happens while using for about 30mins. The next thing it will go into auto-shut-off or auto protect after about 2hrs of use. Note that I'm only using this as a pre-amp. Fortunately it was still under warranty, and they replaced the digital board. product_title: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black/Blue)
review_body:
Okay, let me do a head to head for a couple of the more moderately priced Bluetooth speakers - [[ASIN:B00OUEO4BI RND Ripple Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with two front speakers subwoofer and microphone (Gun Metal Grey)]] and [[ASIN:B00I9ICXFA NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)]]. First off these are not the high end products like Bose, Sony or even Beats that can cost in excess of $200. These are more moderately priced items costing $30-$60. Your expectations should be appropriate for the price range.

Sound: first and foremost among what you probably want from a speaker. Both speakers offer good sound for the small size. The Ripple is a touch fuller on the bass, but both offer good sound across the volume range (better at higher volumes, a little tinny at lower volumes)

Portability: these are after all designed to accompany you mobile device. The NYNE is a bit bulkier, but is mountable on your bicycle (brackets and such included). Both units weigh in about the same when held, one in each hand, at less than a pound.

Charge: both are rechargeable, both come with a USB cable (you can use the plug adapter from you phone to connect the cable and charge), the Ripple is rated at 8-10 hours, I get about 6-8; the Cruiser does not seem to have an official rating on the Amazon product details and I have not run the battery enough to wear it down in the 4 hours of play time I've been using it.

Misc: the Cruiser is equipped with an internal microphone and can be used to answer calls, both are equipped with Aux input plugs so that you can play from non-Bluetooth sources, though that sort of defeats the purpose of buying a wireless speaker.

Pairing: both paired easily with my iPhone, nothing special here.

Overall, the Cruiser is nice as a casual bike mounted speaker for when you want to be 'mobile.' The Ripple is the less expensive of the two and a good solution for those times when you don't have your stereo with you and want to listen without a set of head phones. Neither measures up to our Bose, but then we expected that, these best use by giving them to the kids. P-)a set of head phones. Neither measures up to our Bose, but then we expected that, these best use by giving them to the kids. P-)

review_body:
Great idea in concept and practice. I have had back problems for a while and some days it is just too hard to actually get down to an outlet. This makes is so easy and I can see it being of great help to people who have any sort of mobility issue.

It looks great and suits your décor although the cords sticking out of the top do get a bit messy. I'd love to see a cap or concealment box that fits over the top of the cords as that would REALLY tidy it us in terms of the overall aesthetic when things are plugged into it as it feels a bit like picking up multi plug and raising a few feet in the air. That would however take away from the convenience of being able to plug things in and out and use the caddy so the design as is has its value.

I will be keeping it in my home though as I like the convenience it provides - it is most definitely an art piece of sorts and really solves a common problem an will be a god send on the days where my back play us badly. It feels pretty sturdy as well doesn't feel like it will tip with normal use although id still be careful with it if you have kids around especially when using the caddy / carry tray as a decent knock could tip it.

The outlets are we spaced so you have plenty of room for wall wart type plugs and the addition of the usb ports is brilliant especially if you are used to plugging these into the computer etc (although I have a plethora of USB multi chargers lying around it would be highly useful if like most normal people - you didn't)

Very nice product highly recommended!

Product provided for review - its just my opinion.

product_title: Powerbeats 2 Wireless In-Ear Headphone - White
review_headline: Very comfortable for long periods of use
review_body:
Though bulkier than regular headphones, the PowerBeats 2 are still lightweight and comfortable for wearing hours at a time. They fit my ears perfectly and can be worn over the neck, or under the chin like regular headphones. The latter position makes it easier to use the inline controls and mic, I find. I have noticed that occasionally, one side (usually the right, in my case), will feel unbalanced and very slowly work its way out of my ear. This is caused by the cord not being adjusted properly, with too much slack on one half. As a solution, I just make sure to rework the cord a bit every time I put these on. A minor adjustment is all it takes to get a perfect fit.

Pairing with my iPhone 6+ was simple and easy. I assume these work on Android, but I didn't have an Android device to test. But given that Beats is now owned by Apple, perhaps these are designed exclusively for iOS. I don't know. The battery inside the phones gives you about 6 hours of use. I do wish the battery lasted a bit longer, but they do charge very quickly as a compromise. I've found I usually only need to charge these for about 2-3 hours to fully replenish the battery. But for long trips, might want to pack a backup pair just in case. These are great for everyday usage, not just exercising. The cord, especially the white model, can get a bit dirty after a while, but a damp cloth or paper towel is all you need to clean them.

product_title: Brightech - BrightPlay Home
review_headline: Use this everyday, Ultra Long Range(1500 sq foot warehouse) and Great Sound Quality!
review_body:
Why have I waited this long to purchase this.
Plain and simple, it is a dependable Bluetooth Gadget that works this way:
1a)Plug your BrightPlay Home HD into any normal electrical socket(US)-might take up 2 slots
1b)Plug a pair of speakers to the auxiliary output slot(3.5mm)
I have my speakers connected to an amplifier and then the amplifier connected to this BrightPlay device.

2) Turn on your Bluetooth and connect to "Bright Play Home"

3) Press play on your music on your phone, play an audiobook, or watch a youtube video.

It works great.
There is nothing to download(no app, nothing).
You don't need the best equipment or the latest android or iPhone to use this product(but you must have Bluetooth enabled)

Multiple Phones can connect to this device(the instructions say 2) but I have had 4 connect to it without any issues so far.
I cannot confirm that the first two people can still connect(I am assuming that the "2" might entail that it remembers the last two to connect)

Re-connecting to this device if your phone is not recognized is as easy and unplugging this BrightPlay device from power in addition to the audio cable connected to it, and plugging it all back in.

Some food for thought, the Bluetooth signal is projected from the top of the product when it's plugged in. Do not cover this or place any metal objects directly in front. The signal is strong, impressively strong.

This has been tested in a large warehouse with lots of inventory and have been able to go to the opposite end of where the device is located and the sound is crystal clear(1500 sq ft warehouse).

It will not sound as crisp as plugging in directly but you will find it extremely difficult to tell the difference.
This device is worth every penny.

product_title: C Crane CC Skywave AM, FM, Shortwave, Weather and Airband Portable Travel Radio with Clock and Alarm
review_headline: Sensitive, convenient and low power consumption
review_body:
I've had my radio for less than a month, but that has shown to be sufficient for me to evaluate this on my own criteria other than durability. I understand I'm a dinosaur, but I like radio. It goes everywhere and works without consuming internet bandwidth.

•Battery life. This uses two AA cells. I'm using Eneloops (about 2000 maH). Playing at moderate volumes these rechargeable deliver around 50 hrs play time before needing recharge. [C. Crane states "30-100 mA DC (depending on headphone or speaker usage)".]

•Sound quality. Speech is very acceptable. Sounds like sound from larger radio.

•Easily recharged. I didn't buy an adapter. I simply plug in to USB and press/hold the recharge button for a few seconds until recharge begins. Fortunately I had USB cable which plugged in to radio.

•Sensitivity. I use this radio inside the metal shell of an RV. For moderate strength signals, every radio I own is picky about location. I assume I need to get the antenna (for FM) or internal antenna for AM lined up with a window. At any rate, I find this to be at least equal in sensitivity with my Sony 7600.

Portable radios, for me, are meant to be portable. In other words, I don't want to have to keep it plugged in and I don't want to feel like I'm wasting money on batteries. This radio receives the stations I want, delivers superb battery life and recharges without requiring changing out the cells.

product_title: Sennheiser On-Ear 926MHz Wireless RF Headphones with Charging Cradle
review_headline: Horrible experience--intermittent hiss, unforgiving static, mediocre range
review_body:
I was super excited for these, because I've heard nothing but good things about Sennheiser. I expected the audio quality to be top notch.

Unfortunately, these headphones were a significant disappointment. I have since returned them.

I will say that the audio WAS good--deep bass, full sound, etc--they felt like "studio" headphones.

However, the overall experience was terrible, due to several factors:

1. They have an awful "power saving" feature that forces the base (but not the headphones!) off, every five minutes. If you are watching a video and put it on pause, you had better remember to turn off the headphones, or you risk hurting your ears with the loud and obnoxious static that appears when the base is off.* Also, you had better make sure there is some audio playing BEFORE you turn the headset on, or you will be subjected to the same horrible static.

2. There is an intermittent "hiss", as if it is cycling through frequencies and continually hitting a noisy range. No amount of channel switching or playing with the slider can get rid of this.

3. The range is meager. Unlike the Logitech headset that I bought as a replacement, these have trouble reaching through a door. Depending on how I sit, the hissing can become worse.

4. The headset was heavy, and a little too tight, making them uncomfortable to wear for long periods.

product_title: Grado SR80e Prestige Series Headphones
review_headline: Not perfect, but still the best out there in this price range.
review_body:
This is what music really sounds like. I don't know if the higher end Grado's are any better than the SR80's but I'd find it hard to believe. The SR80's are a significant improvement over the SR60's though...

I've had mine for almost five years now and I use them on an almost daily basis. I can wear them for extended periods with no discomfort (I did bend them outward just a bit because out of the box, they were too tight). I can't stand to go back to my old Sennheiser PX100's because they sound so flat (yes, I realize this isn't exactly a fair comparison). Before purchasing the SR80's I tried the AKG K240's on the advice of the salesman, and they sounded fine in the store, but when I was able to do an A-B comparison, the SR80's just blew the K240's out of the water. The only edge that the 240's had was that they were better at reducing external noise and didn't let so much sound out.

I use the SR80's for everything from talk radio to Beethoven to Joe Satriani to Kenny Burrell to Dream Theater to Lee Morgan to Otis Rush to Big Bill Broonzy to Rush to Mark Knopfler etc... No matter the genre, music just sounds better on the SR80's than any other headphones I've tried. I hate the kind of artificial bass attenuation that so many headphone makers seem to think is necessary. The SR80's are capable of producing clean and deep bass without a hint of boomyness and the mids and highs are clean without being tinny.

The bottom line is if you want a reasonably affordable pair of headphones and care about sound, get these!

The only weakness in the SR80's is that they are VERY open. In fact it seems to me that the sound emitted out the back is actually louder than that which is directed toward your ears! So if privacy or disturbing others around you is a concern, you might want to grab something else, but you'll almost certainly be giving up sound quality unless you spend quite a bit more money.

EDIT Mar 24 2014:

There is one more weakness that is common to Grados. The sheathing from the "Y" to the earpieces gets stiff with time (I had mine for several years before it got bad) and I never really did like the "Y" into both earpieces configuration anyway. After doing some thinking and looking around at parts, I decided to re-engineer the cord. I cut the cord just below the "Y" and installed a male mini stereo jack on the cord. Then I installed a female mini stereo jack the right earpiece, and ran an extension up through the head band into the left earpiece. Now I have a detachable single connector set up which allows me to keep the cord out of my lap while working. The whole process only took me about an hour to accomplish once I'd figured out what I was going to do and assembled the materials. I highly recommend it!

Edit: Mar 2015

Once the above modifications were done, I took the next step and plugged in a bluetooth reciever into the mini-jack I installed. Purists may scoff at bluetooth anything, but for most of my listening going wireless is a beautiful thing. If I'm in the mood to the the most out of the headphones I still have the option of plugging in.

product_title: Pyle Home  Mini Power Amplifier with LED Display
review_body:
Great value for a small room. We have an older Pyle mini-amp downstairs which powers a pair of speakers in our kitchen. It has worked flawlessly for over 3 years, so I figured I'd give this little guy a shot. My daughter wanted a better sounding system for her bedroom, so I built her a pair of speakers using MarkAudio CHR-70A drivers. Paired with this amp, I think it is almost impossible to find a better sounding system for such a modest amount of money. As for the amp itself, she has had no problems with it. It has plenty of power for a bedroom system, even using the aforementioned drivers, which have a relatively low 85.4 db sensitivity. More sensitive drivers could go louder with the same amp. The sound is nice and clean, with no audible distortion until you really crank the volume up high, which she doesn't do anyway. Played at normal listening levels, the sound is great.

Love the fact that it takes a USB thumb drive. For those who may not be familiar with this feature, you simply copy MP3 or WMA files to a thumb drive, then plug the drive into this amp and it will decode and play them. Super convenient and it sounds great. We have not had any problems with any files not playing. It has worked great so far.

A note about the remote - it's a cheesy generic model, but it works. I don't think Pyle makes the remote - they probably buy it from some el cheapo Chinese manufacturer. Regardless, it works OK for basic functionality. You can punch in, for example, 14, and it will go to the 14th song on the USB stick, which is kinda nice. It works for volume too, but the volume knob on the amp itself is not motorized. So what this means is that the knob on the amp is sort of a MAXIMUM. The remote can reduce the volume below what the knob is set at, but it cannot increase it. Fair enough. She just sets the knob permanently at about the 12 o'clock position and then adjusts down with the remote.

The aux input works great with her iPod. So basically, this is the perfect little amp for a kid's bedroom, or for an office, den, or any other smaller room. Sounds great, loud enough for most people's tastes, and has been reliable so far. I did have some concerns about long term reliability, but noticed that Amazon is offering 3 years extended warranty for four bucks or something like that. Pocket change for 3 years peace of mind. product_title: Axiom Premium 3.5mm 1/8" Audio Aux Cable Lead Cord For Skullcandy Aviator Headphone
review_headline: Not perfect, but I feel like it's my only option...
review_body:
I purchased four of these in the past twelve months. The first one lasted a bit more than six months -- I received it from the manufacturer, and it seemed quality-made. I tend to play with cords as a bored/nervous habit, so my cords tend to fail eventually, even if they're quality-made (just to put the replacement time into perspective). Anyway, when I ordered a replacement, it wasn't from the manufacturer directly and the quality was noticeably different -- it was awful! Upon arrival, it was clear that there was something wrong with it -- the cord was a lot less stiff, and I had to adjust the end of it in my MP3 player, otherwise it was static-filled, or only in one ear. Within a day or two, it failed. I received a refund from Amazon, but it was very disappointing. When I looked back at my previous purchases, I noticed that the one that failed wasn't directly from the manufacturer, so I ordered my replacements from the manufacturer themselves. They seemed fine upon inspection, though I haven't used them yet.

Overall, I'd say these aren't the greatest cords -- lower mid-quality, at best. That said, they seem like one of the only options for the Skullcandy Aviator headphones I have, so that's why I purchase them. If there were another option, even if it were more expensive, if I knew it were higher quality for sure, I wouldn't hesitate to buy from them instead.

UPDATE: I tried using another brand stereo able (Sentey) which seemed like they were a higher quality, but it didn't stay in my Skullcandy Aviators as well as the Axiom cord did. The Sentey cord kept slipping out where it plugged into the headphones, and then audio would only be in one ear -- with just the slightest bit of pull on the cord (just moving around accomplished this). And yes, I tried both plugs to see if it was a problem with just one end, but it wasn't. So, while I'm not happy that the Axiom cords wear out so fast, at least they work! I added a star for this. There's a lot to be said for something just working. Great sound like with the Sentey cord, is a bonus, but only in one ear? No thank you. :)ng just working. product_title: Audio Technica QuietPoint Noise-Cancelling Headphones
review_headline: Audio Technica ANC9 vs M50X vs Bose QC25 - ANC9 is the best but the worst sound leakage ever
review_body:
I own M50X, they are fantastic and I absolutely love it. But I wanted noise canceling headphones that I can use it on the plane.

After reading and watching numerous reviews my two top picks for noise canceling headphones were Bose QC25 and Audio Technica ANC9.

My friend has the Bose QC25 and I compared it side by side with the M50X. The sound quality of M50X was clearly better than the QC25. M50X sound was clear and crispy whereas the QC25 was very muffled. This left me with my only other option ANC9.

I finally bought the ANC9. The sound quality just blew my mind away. Yes, all the reviewers were right. The ANC9 sound quality was even better than the M50X and M50X’s sound quality was better than Bose QC25. So you can imagine how much of a difference in sound quality you would get with the ANC9 when compared to Bose QC25.

ANC9 sound quality is much more crisp, clear and has punchy bass. There is so much more clarity with the sound and it sounds amazing. When compared to QC25 in terms of sound quality it is like day and night clearly. There is so much difference and the ANC9s are so much better.

The ANC9 is comfortable, no complaints. But QC25 is clearly more comfortable than ANC9 and I guarantee this does not make QC25 a better headphones because ANC9s are comfortable enough already. The noise canceling is on par with QC25, although QC25 may very slightly be better but that makes a very negligible difference, so don’t worry about that.

CONS:
After me bragging about the sound quality of ANC9s, Am I happy with these headphones? Not really. The sound leakage from the ANC9s are so very bad, they are unbelievable loud that it got me thinking these headphones have a set of speakers facing outwards. It is like playing music with your headphones around your neck. They are so loud that everyone is room can actually sing along with your music. These headphones have ridiculous amount of noise leakage andif that is going to be a problem for you then it is clearly a deal breaker. I really want to return these headphones because of the insane amount of noise leakage, but at the same time I do not know what other noise canceling headphones to buy and hence makes me think I should just settle for the ANC9s.

It seems to me as a such a waste of effort to make such great noise canceling headphones to have such a ridiculous amount of noise leakage. I had read several reviews mentioning these headphones having noise leakage, but I was like so what, big deal. But, its not. It is a very big issue for the amount of sound that leaks out of these headphones.

review_headline: Fantastic sound with tons of functionality = best clock radio ever?  Weakest part is documentation...
review_body:
Summary: Fantastic sound and versatility are limited by weak documentation. Note: free sample provided for evaluation

I've had a chance to review tons of bluetooth speakers, and I've just found my favorite in terms of sound quality. No doubt this being the largest one is part of the reason for the full, balanced sound. Still, I would argue that it's not fair to call this a bluetooth speaker since there's a lot more functionality

- Clock with alarm
- FM Radio
- Clock radio
- Built in MP3 player, plays from USB drives or from microSD cards

The weakest part is the limited documentation. Also, some of the controls are not what I would prefer. For example, in radio mode the up and down buttons tune station if pressed, then only change volume with a long press. Although this functionality carries over to playing music - a press skips an a long press changes volume, this is the opposite of most every set of bluetooth headphones or speakers I've seen, where a short press changes volume and the long press skips tracks or replays them.

The MP3 playback feature is good, but navigating is tricky. I would love a shuffle mode - it's very possible there is this feature built in, but the documentation is sparse.

The only thing that might limit using this as a clock radio on your nightstand is that the time readout is kind of bright - nothing that couldn't be fixed with a small dark rag, however. My wife already does this on her clock radio.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S3500 660 Watt 5.1-Channel Home Theater Speaker/Receiver Package
review_body: It was time to update my old 1998 Kenwood rack stereo system.  There was so much to look at and I knew almost nothing about the new stereo systems or surround sound.  This system made it easy:  5.1 surround means 5 speakers and 1 sub woofer; 7.1 surround is 7 speakers 1 sub woofer.  I just wanted something to play surround for my new Xbox One in a smaller room.  I had specific space requirements about where I could hang the surround speakers on the wall, because of that, I had to purchase 100ft of 16 gauge wire from Amazon Basics to run the wire around the edge of the room to reach the speakers where I needed them.  Don't use anything larger than 16 gauge because it won't fit in the speaker ports.  At the end of the day the system sounds great.  The speakers stand about 7 inches tall which surprised me.  The base is deep but won't blow your ears or distort terribly when cranked up, the system isn't meant for that.   I typically run the system at 37/90db and its enough to make people in this house think it's thundering outside when I cast lightning spells!  I turned on the hdmi passthrough which lets me just use the TV if I wanted.  After a week of having surround sound and then turning it off to just play with the TV's original sound was mind blowing.  I don't see how I used to be able to play games like this!  For what they are asking in price, this is a great investment.   There are some reviews here that state it gets really too hot.  If it was enclosed in a wood surround without fans I can see how this would be true.  However, I leave mine exposed on the stand without a wooden enclosure and it isn't too bad.  It would have been nice if they built a fan into the system for an extra 20$ to the price tag, but still this deal is good enough to warrant 5 stars.   One last very important thing, this particular model is the older model for this stereo system.  For typical users this will be just fine, it supports up to 1080p for all your HDMI stereo needs.  If you areinterested at all in getting a 4k (2160p) UHD TV at some point, this model stereo will not support HDMI 2.0.  You will want to get the never model Onkyo to future-proof your stereo surround.  Or you can be like me, and get this system for now then upgrade to the Dolby Axion 7.1 Onkyo receiver later after you get your 4k UHD TV to future proof your entertainment system.   This system is still worth the price you pay.  I'm happy with this system, and will gladly reuse all the speakers when I upgrade in a few years.  5 stars!

product_title: Audio-Technica Audiophile Closed-Back Dynamic Headphones
review_headline: My favorite soundstage on a closed back headphone!
review_body: Different speakers are for different purposes.  1) Speakers are meant to be felt.  Speakers push air.  Speakers hit you.  Unless you're paying thousands... you're probably not going to get the clarity, the separation, and the distinctness of each tone, instrument, & sound. 2) On the other hand, headphones don't push air into your chest.  Headphones gives you the imaging, the separation, the soundstage, the distinct instruments & tones.  Now there's the difference between Open-Back & Closed Back headphones 1) Open-Back let's sound in & it let's sound out.  I know for most people this doesn't make sense.  Open-back are for at home use.  Where they shine is when it comes to soundstage.  You feel like you're in the room where the musicians are playing.  You can hear all the separation.  It's phenomenal. 2) Closed-Back doesn't let sound in & doesn't let sound out.  I know this makes more sense.  Closed back cans are made for portable use.  You can listen to them commuting & in public areas... You aren't being bothered by outside noise & you're music isn't bothering anybody.  But, it's like putting your head next to a speaker.  It's punchy, but you don't experience the separation between the instruments.  Now, why can't you get the best of both worlds?  An open-back sound in a closed-back design.  Well, I introduce you to the Audio Technica ATH A900x.  I love love love these headphones.  These offer the greatest soundstage for a closed back headphone.  Things are far far apart from each other... It's awesome.  They aren't hard to drive.  They got punchy lows.  Beyerdynamic DT770's on the other hand are very difficult to drive & have kinda looser lows.  My issues with this headphone 1) The wings on top of your head aren't very firm.  It feels awkward honestly 2) The cups are gigantic.  The earpads are sitting at the base of my jaw.  It feel uncomfortable at times 3) It's hard to create a great seal with these cans.  But without the seal... you don't get the bass 4) The cable must be like 10 feet long... and it's not detachable.  If I compared this can to a girl... Imagine the hottest girl you could date.  She's beautiful.  She has great character & great depth.  The only knock is that she's a little gauche.  A lil socially awkward.  Would you date her or not date her?  Of course, you'd date her.  That's why despite the deficiencies... this is still 5 stars  I own about 30 headphones: ATH-m50x, Vmoda m100, Sony MDR 7506, Sennheiser HD 555, Sennheiser Urbanite XL, Sennheiser Momentum Over Ears, Sennheiser HD 25-1 ii, Samsung Level Over (a gift), Beyerdynamic DT770's, and more.  These cans have my favorite soundstage on a closed back headphone!

I own a lot of Creative products and have been very happy with them, this is one of the first Creative products that I feel sucks, just like the Muvo 20 (on which the bass sounds terrible and distorted).

No it's not, it sounds horribly offensive to me. This is my favorite album and I love this music, and it was hard to hear it sound so terrible. This is not how it's supposed to sound, listening on these Creative Auruvana Platinum headphones I thought to myself. Of course I tried many other kinds of music not just metal. Basically it all sounds terrible to me. Like I said I even tried plugging in the audio cable the headphones come with and listening on that instead of bluetooth, and it did not sound any better, still just as bad.

product_title: BRAVEN BRV-1 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker [12 Hours][Waterproof] Built-In 1400 mAh Power Bank Charger - Black / Black
review_headline: Died In Less Than a Week
review_body:
When this speaker first arrived, I was impressed with its overall presentation--the packaging was well done as was the included insert which featured a quick start guide of sorts (the full manual to be downloaded from the Braven website); the speaker was rather small, but hefty and felt solid in hand; and pairing it was incredibly simple with my smartphone.

What impressed me, though, was the sound quality, which is balanced beyond anything I expected for this class of portable speaker. I listened to classical, jazz, R&B/hip hop, rap, rock, alternative, and folk to get an idea of its range--and it has range. Typically, the highs would be drowned out by the mids and lows in other speakers, but this speaker allowed for nuances in the music to shine through and I especially appreciated this with the classical and jazz. That said, if you play a lot of rap, R&B, hip hop, rock where the mids and lows are dominant, it might come off a bit weak--though, not in a bad way, IMO.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to properly test any of the speaker's other features--namely the charger on the back, its battery life, the microphone, etc.--because it died in less than a week and in under seven uses. It died in stages, wherein while playing a song, the keys failed to respond to any input and it wouldn't even turn off. I had to disable the bluetooth on my smartphone which allowed the speaker to automatically shut itself off after 30 minutes. Once it did, it refused to turn itself back on. When I plugged in the charger, the indicator lights would illuminate. Now it doesn't even do that much.

The website had a troubleshooting section, which I tried without any success. I then sent an email to their support address asking for any additional troubleshooting tips, but after 36 hours with no response I sent another email. After another 8 hours with no response, I tried using the phone number they'd listed for support which sent me to a voicemail box. While I may have simply received a dud, I'm concerned about the customer support from a consumer standpoint. What should happen if this speaker had failed before the warranty period was up, but after Amazon's 30 day return policy expired?

review_body: I have used this set for a year for now and have found that it is very useful. Especially when we are busy in the morning, it actually has saved huge amounts of time several times. Now I am forty two years old and my memory is not as fresh as before, so I sometimes have a really hard time locating my key chain. However, since I used this finder, the annoying concern of finding my key chain every morning has permanently disappeared.  Pros: 1. It does its job right. It never fails in receiving signal from the transmitter and going off. 2. Manufacturers included some extra button cells so we do not have to wait until we buy another for replacement when the battery is unexpectedly dead. When it is dead, we can simply replace it with one of the extra ones that were included and we have time to buy another for the next replacement. 3. Manufacturer states that the battery needs to be replaced every 6 months, but I guess it lasts longer than that. It has been a year since I started using three receivers, but only one battery needs to be replaced.  Cons: There might be two things to improve. 1. Size: These days, we have more and more to hook in the key chain; key tag membership card, emergency led flashlight, little key ring tools, etc. So, if the receiver is smaller than the current size, it would be much better. 2. A tighter battery cover: This might be a serious issue: When a battery is newly installed, it beeps once, which means whenever the battery has new contact with the receiver unit, it beeps. When I was in class, it started beeping irregularly and I was very frustrated. I have taken a close look and found that the battery cover is getting loose as it gets older and this makes the contact between the button cell and the unit poor. Therefore, the contact between the two tends to be on and off at various and random moments and, in turn, it causes unexpected beeping. Or, maybe, it is randomly responding to a foreign signal, which is not supposed to happen. In spite ofthis defect, I still use it because the advantage of the receiver is much bigger than this random beeping disadvantage. If this problem is figured out, this product could be a perfect idea!

review_body: These are good earphones, but the Able Planet Company seems to use deceptive advertising and warranty practices. The strong clear sound could be heard while keeping the tiny plastic button depressed with a finger and it was good. product_title: Polk Audio T15 Bookshelf Speakers, Pair, Black
review_headline: Very good speakers for the price if you don't push them too hard.
review_body:
OK, there were already 57 reviews of these when I wrote this so I questioned if I could provide any information no one else had. Anyway, I LOVE these small bookshelf speakers. No, they won't blow out a large empty room (and no one in their right mind would expect them to do so). As near field monitors they work great. What does that mean? It means I have them in a small bedroom about 8' X 10' that I converted into a small office where my computers are on some furniture that has a bookshelf over the main monitor. My ears are about 3' to 5' from the speakers, hence the term "near field". They provide far more clarity and detail, with a nice soundstage for localization of instruments and voices than my older computer speakers. I have these hooked to an old VSX-D509S Pioneer A/V receiver that puts out 100 Watts per channel, and the source is an optical cable feed from my computer's sound card, so I use them for playing my iTunes library and for playing streaming audio and video while using my computers.

I subscribe to an audio streaming service, so I get higher quality sound (320 Kbps) than the free ones provide (128 to 160 Kbps), and I can easily tell the difference with these speakers.

I do have to have the bass turned up to get a nice balanced sound, and as many have noted, adding a subwoofer with these would possibly help, but I'm pretty satisfied as they are because I listen to mostly acoustic and normal rock music (not anything with artificial booming bass).

The only caveat I have found is that these should not be pushed too hard. One of the woofers makes some mechanical noise like it is hitting some stops when it is pushed to a very loud volume. Otherwise they work perfectly fine. [EDIT]: I bought another pair of these here in September 2015 and found they too will make some mechanical noise on the same source material when pushed hard. I now believe I am simply asking too much in loudness from them when the bass is turned up to +4 and now think that adding the PSW-100 Polk Audio Subwoofer would be the way to go, using a cross-over frequency of around 150 to 200 Hz. That way most of the really low bass would go to the sub and not overtax these otherwise very good quality speakers. I plan on using my 5 year old pair in an out building for when I am working on some hobbies, and may add that PSW-100 sub to my computer room soon, not that I play them overly loud most of the time.

Obviously, for more money you could get better sound, but the nearest competitors offering enough of a step up to justify the purchase, such as Boston Acoustics Classic II CS26 2-Way 6-1/2-Inch Bookshelf Speaker (sold EACH) would cost more than TWICE what the Polk Audio T15 does. Indeed, about once a year, Best Buy and perhaps Amazon will offer the T15 speakers for as low as $50 - $60 for the PAIR.

I do want to note that for any speakers it is very important that you connect the cables such that the positive and negative ends are the same from the receiver to the speaker, meaning they will play in phase. If that is not done, you will not have ANY bass at all, since the speakers will be cancelling each other out.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase of these Polk Audio T15 Bookshelf speakers. I would highly recommend them to anyone needing a similar application in a small room, and wanting more detailed sound than computer speakers can provide. If you have an old receiver in a closet gathering dust, this is a great way to get more bang out of your investment.

One final observation. When purchasing speakers always check out their size. Many other speakers are far deeper. My bookshelves were only 11" deep which limited my choice of speaker. I didn't want them overhanging the shelves nor did I want to wall mount them. Indeed, some bookshelf speakers have the tuned bass port (that hole you see in the T15 at the middle right) in the rear whichmeans you should have at least an extra inch space behind them, otherwise, you'll hear a "chuffing" sound on low bass when played loud due to air movement.rwise, you'll hear a "chuffing" sound on low bass when played loud due to air movement.

product_title: Fujifilm 100MB PC-Formatted Zip Disk (5-Pack) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
ZIP 100MB Disk

These ZIP 100MB disks are a high-capacity removable storage disk that is about the size of a standard 3.5" floppy disk. It can be read and written by an internal IDE drive (only one per system) or an external drive connected to a USB port or a parallel port (slowest in access). The IomegaWare Software provides utility functions designed for the ZIP disk, such as formatting or copying a disk. You should never use the Operating System disk copy function. Use the EJECT utility to remove a disk from a drive; this is required in Windows NT or Windows 2000. Remove the disk before turning a computer off. Normally, shutting down the computer causes the disk to eject.

The IomegaWare software tests for the presence of the ZIP drive. It should be used in Windows 2000 to format a ZIP disk in the FAT format. The data on a ZIP drive can be read and written by different versions of an Operating System (using the FAT format). Rewriting reuses space, it does not increase the used space. ZIP drives, like floppies, should not be exposed to magnetic fields or high heat (sunshine). The 100 MB ZIP disks can be read and written by a 250 MB disk drive. These disks use the FAT16 format so only 151 entries are allowed in its root directory. Files should be stored in folders to best use space. This also applies to memory sticks (unless they use the FAT32 format).

To test the status of a used ZIP disk. 1) Right click on the drive, select `Properties'. 2) Select the Iomega tab (after support was installed). 3) Select `Diagnostics', then `Close' after the green light. 4) Select `More Info' on the `Disk Type' Note the `Disk Life Status' and the `Format Life Status'. Percentages lower than about 85% are not good. 5) A `Long Format' can improve the Life Status statistics.
These are great for documents 5-50K but don't'have the capacity for digital photographs 3M to 7M.

product_title: Zeskit Braided Nylon Premium Audio Cable - 3.5mm
review_body:
I wear headphones daily and I have had difficulties with the cables either failing or getting twisted and kinked. I looked to this cable to help resolve those issues. So far, it has definitely exceeded my expectations and has worked much better than I expected. Though it’s “just a cable” there is a good bit that can be said for it.

This is a 4' stereo audio cable with 3.5mm plugs on either end. Even while still in the package it’s clear that this cable is a bit more substantial and rugged compared to most other audio cables available. It is a heavy-gauge cable with woven nylon casing that is actually very difficult to twist though I suspect if one tried hard enough to kink the cable it could be done. The jacks are gold-plated and rather than just molded plastic they have a metal cap that screws down to make the jack much more sturdy and give it a much more sophisticated look. This is not a run-of-the-mill plastic-coated audio cable with cheap jacks on the end but rather it is a quality cable that’s worth buying.

I replaced the cable on a pair of headphones with this one and plugged into a music player and noticed no difference in the sound quality. The primary difference between this cable and the one it replaced is an integrated microphone on the cable which is not something I need anyway.

I am happy with this cable and am pleased to recommend it. It is very well made and it works well. It is a little more expensive than other audio cables available but you get what you pay for with this cable.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

product_title: Nvidia 942-11431-0007-001 3D Vision2; Wireless Glasses Kit
review_body:
Not sure why all the bad reviews, perhaps there were issues with older version of the driver or installing the proper 3D driver? Either way, the 3D driver is already installed for nvidia graphics cards that are up to date nowadays. Installation was plug and play for me, with that said, games vary a lot in 3D quality. Some games, like BF4, are so good in 3D, I wont play it without it turned on. Others? Not so much unless you spend some time downloading 3D "fixes" that have been developed by other users.

As for the 3D (gaming), its pretty impressive, but not as "life altering" as some of the other reviews have made it out to be. Still, everyone should experience it and I think it depends on your personal preferences if 3D is worth it or not. It definitely makes the game more immersive. The edges of the screen seem to blur into your peripherals and make the monitor appear much larger than it is. Turn off the lights and the monitor takes up your entire field of view. IMO, this is DEFINITELY worth getting if you already have a nice Nvidia GC setup and you either already have the monitor, or are looking to upgrade your monitor anyways (as I was). I bought the "ASUS VG278HE 27-Inch Screen LED-lit Monitor 144hz 2ms" for your reference and absolutely love it so far.

Don't bother getting this unless you have a 120hz+ monitor that is (obviously) 3D ready. The graphics card should be up to snuff as well, though it doesn't need to be a world beater like some people have made the case out to be. I use an Nvidia 660 Ti EVGA SC, which is about 2 years old now. Maybe worth $150-200 tops nowadays and it needs to run 3 monitors. I can run Crysis 3/BF4 on almost max settings, in 3D, and keep a decent framerate going, though I will probably upgrade soon to future 'proof' my setup.

review_headline: Solid with a few minor inconveniences
review_body: Edit: So, it's been a while so I'm updating this review. Just recently these broke, under normal use and under very little strain. It broke off where the headphone connects to the head strap, once it breaks it's not really fixable. Believe me, I tried. Bought some gorilla glue and tried getting it back together and waited a full day for them to dry. It looked like the issue was resolved till it snapped again and smacked me in the head. The quality/build of these headphones could have been better I feel, not really much use to me now and now I'm having to shop around for another set. It's a shame, while it lasted I actually really liked these headphones. But because of this inconvenience, I'm dropping this from 4 stars to 2 stars and will not buy it again. Real shame!   This is a solid bluetooth headphone. I've now had it for a few months and have been able to move it around with me to get a good feel for them. So, I'll start with the obvious:  Pros - - Impressive sound for bluetooth - Bluetooth connection is stable even at a good distance of 30 feet, given there are no big obstructions, I've been able to go into another office and still hear my playlist from my macbook just fine - aux connectivity if you run out of juice for your batteries  Cons - - Not the most comfortable headphones, it's not terrible, but it comes with only two sizes (large and small), large fits me just fine, but it's a little tight around the ears. Not to the point of crushing or anything, it's just something I've gotten used to, the top leather brace is comfortable though - Can't really fold the ears on these things, so you can't easily pack them

product_title: MartinLogan Reference On-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I'm a headphone addict. I currently own 27 pairs of cans. They are priced from $ 20.00 to $600.00. With that said I would say that these are one of my favorite pairs of headphones for their sound. Only my Grado RS2E, 225i, Soundmagic hp150 and hp 200 sound better.
These cans have a very balanced sound. The bass is deep and well controlled. No exaggerated booming artificial bass. Mid's are well represented and natural. High's are clear without being sibulant or overly bright.
Out of the box they sound nice but really open up after burn in. These cans are built with high quality parts and should hold up well. Their build quality reminds me of V Moda. The cable seems fragile but the V Moda M80 cable works fine with them. Clamping force is strong but I eased it by grabbing the ends of the headband(not the ear pieces) and gently bending them till I got the right clamping force. At the current selling price they are a bargain at full retail I would chose some other brands.

product_title: Terk HDTVAZ Amplified Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body: Works great in my apt! I had owned an older cheapo type 20.00 antenna from Sears and that didn't pick up one single channel in my place. When I dropped cable a month ago I started researching OTA antennas and decided to try the TERK  first. Since I would be able to point an antenna out my window towards the broadcast towers, which are about 30 miles away, I decided to try a directional antenna instead of an Omni directional one like the Mohu Leaf.    It was a good decision! I was really surprised how many channels I get. I did a channel scan and got 110 channels off the bat and my tv and antenna aren't even by the window. I did temporarily move my tv & antenna next to the window where I can aim the antenna towards the broadcast towers for a quick test and got 128 channels - amazing!    I do have to adjust to get all the channels to come in but not much, for instance to get ABC I need to lower rabbit ears to horizontal and extend them out but I lose UPN. When I push the rabbit ears back in all the way, (but still down & horizontal) I get UPN but ABC gets a weak or no signal. It's not bad and I don't have to move the thing all over the place. I'll still experiment with different locations but I think I'm set for the most part. I do turn on the amplifier and it helps, I think because the antenna is not by the window. If I end up moving it to point out the window and towards the towers I may not need to use the amplifier.    OTA reception is so clear! It actually looks better than what I had through my cable so I'm real happy with this antenna.

product_title: Bluetooth Speaker, DKnight Magicbox Ultra-Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker Powerful Sound with build in Microphone, Works for Cellphone
review_headline: Nice sound but lots of room for improvement
review_body:
I am somewhat torn about this product. To give a better overview I will list the pros and cons:

Pros:
- beautiful sound quality: the sound is surprisingly full
- volume: it was really important for me to get something that can go really loud, and this thing definitely can!
- size: considering the nice full sound it produces, I am amazed by how small and light it is. This makes it super convenient to transport.
- price: the price for this speaker is great considering the quality you get.

Cons:
- cordless: I know this is supposed to be a pro, but I wish it came with a nice long cord, because the battery does not last very long if you intend to use this speaker through the entire night, like I do. As it is, if you leave it unplugged it will start making terrible beeping noises every few seconds when it runs low - not ideal when you're trying to sleep...
- bright light: In the front it has a small light that is incredibly bright and disruptive. This light is always on when the speaker is on and seriously seems like somebody is shining a flashlight into my face. I have to cover it with something so that I can sleep.
- no volume control: I wish there was a way to control the volume on the speaker itself. As it is I always have to find my phone and turn it up or down there.
- interruptions: This may very well be my phone's fault and have nothing to do with the speaker, but since I am not sure, I will add this part anyway. Every now and then the sound will cut out for a split second which is very disruptive if you are using this as a soothing sound machine where constant and consistent noise is essential. But again, this may not be the speaker's fault at all.

So, all in all, if you are using it as a speaker for a sound machine, you might want to keep looking unless you are not as terribly picky as I am.
If you are using it just as a speaker and mostly during the day, this seems like a fantastic little gadget and I would definitely recommend it.

review_headline: I did have a cheaper waterproof player that didn't have a display and it's was definity akward to use This one is a great player
review_body:
I've been using the Diver Waterproof MP3 for about 4 months,
I did have a cheaper waterproof player that didn't have a display and it's was definity akward to use
This one is a great player compared to it.

PROS:
- The sound volume is quiet good.
- Good quality FM radio reception
- simple to upload files from PC
- battery gives me at least 3 hours of playback without recharging
- the earphones are conformtable
- the clip to attach it to the goggles is great because you can detach it while you are in the pool with the earphones on, to change the track or select another radio.

CONS

- The podometer doesn't work as expected. In the pool it didn't work well. You should "very" fast so it counts your steps.
For example, the pool is usually 25 meters long, but it only measure 2, 3 o 4 meters once in a while. It seems to work better if you use it for running.

- The earphones have some sort of thin plastic disc membrane that separates the interior of the speaker from outer rubber part. I suppose that membrane is intended to prevent the water from going inside the speaker, That membrane wear off very easily after some months of use. I don't know if it will afect the speakers inside.

product_title: Poweradd™ 903A Universal 4-Bay AA/AAA Ni-MH Ni-CD LCD Quick Rechargeable Battery Charger Power Wall Adapter
review_headline: POWERADD 4-Slot Battery Charger for AA/AAA Rechargeables, LCD Progress Display, High Speed, Can Charge Single Batteries
review_body:
I go through a lot of AA and AAA rechargeable batteries in my various flashlights, headlamps, radios, hand tools etc.
I wanted a battery charger that was compact, had a folding plug for easy packing for travel, and also charged fast and had a LCD display to show battery charge status and progress.

This little 903A model charger from PowerAdd does all that, and more.
A very nice bonus to this model charger, as part of all the 'smart charging' features, is that you no longer have to charge batteries in pairs of 2 or 4 with this device.
That's right. You can charge just 1 battery, or 3, without having to charge in pairs. Very convenient, especially since most flashlights and headlamps use batteries in groups of three's.

The plastic body has a pleasant metallic Bronze finish, with beveled edges, very good looking.
The LCD display screen shows battery charge progress and signals when batteries are fully charged.
'Smart charging' features means no overcharging of batteries, even if you let them sit in the charger for days.

The charging wall AC plug folds up for easy packing. Lightweight and takes up little space in a travel bag, or a drawer.

Sample sent for testing and impartial review. Just a great little device, and I'm totally pleased. It works exactly as the listing describes.
Batteries fit snugly, contacts are good, and they've worked to recharge several different brands of rechargeables with no issues.

I hope this review is helpful as you comparison shop online. Happy charging, everybody.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S9400THX 7.1-Channel Network A/V Receiver/Speaker Package
review_headline: Amazing sound quality for 2 years 3 months - then no HDMI audio - FIXED
review_body: Love this system. I use the android app for remote control, use the Pandora network function, play from a USB connected iPhone, and play to the unit from networked computers (using Windows Media Player). All these functions give it superb functionality, and the sound quality is amazing.  That being said, this unit worked like a charm for over 2 years until it decided to quit 3 months after the warranty expired. Like others here, it seems that the HDMI board may have gone bad. One day I turned it on, no audio from any of the HDMI inputs, though video still worked flawlessly. I checked all HDMI ports from different sources, as well as component audio. Component audio worked, but the HDMI audio didn't. Turning the system off and back on seemed to intermittently fix the issue, but it kept getting worse.  To check for a similar issue, when viewing an HDMI input, press the "Home" button (under the down arrow) on the remote, go to "Info", and then look at the Audio detail. If the input says "Unknown" instead of something like "Dolby D 48kHz 2.0 ch" and it doesn't show an output, then you're in the same situation as I was. You should also be able to confirm by looking for the speaker glyphs on the left side of the receiver display. If you're seeing video but no speakers are shown, then you probably have a similar issue if this happened out of the blue.  Fortunately, thanks to another review, I found that Onkyo had extended its warranty for this issue (plus a network connectivity issue). Following the link below, I put in my serial number and it told me I was covered under the warranty. They're sending me some shipping supplies to return it for repair. We'll see how that goes.  https://repair.onkyousa.com/na/003_2012.php?country=USA  I'm writing this review because the info was buried in a comment on one of these reviews and I'm hoping this makes it easier to find.  EDIT: The return box they sent me had everything I needed to send it back - foam packing, ties, and even packing tape. I packed it up, sent it back with a prepaid return label (FedEx), and they turned it around in a little over a week (including shipping time). I got the receiver back, plugged everything back in, and bam. Good to go. They wipe the settings though so I had to do a little bit of setup to get it back to perfect. Looks like they updated the firmware and swapped out the old HDMI board to a new one. Here's to hoping this one lasts longer than 2 years. The Adcom seemed more powerful although its rated power was lower (no surprise), BUT the GFA 7000 was too cold and analytic in presentation. I have it paired with a B&K preamp, Klipsch KG4's and Audioquest cables. The 7025 is the right balance reminiscent of high end Yamaha amps. Very neutral, especially through the Klipsch horns. The amp is dead quiet. I never hear the fan. It is heavy and built well. The parts are of very high quality. I was very skeptical of D&M equipment due to many reported reliability issues. product_title: 66 AUDIO - BTS+ SPORT - Bluetooth Wireless Headphones - 25+ Hour Battery, Voice Call Noise Cancellation, Stereo Sound
review_headline: Would Buy Again Without A Second Thought
review_body:
I have had my 66 Audio BTS+ headphones for about 2 months, and I have no regrets for my purchase.
First the "down sides":
When I ordered my headphones, there was some trouble with package tracking. I was notified of it shipping, but no further tracking updates. I contacted customer service, and as you may have read in previous reviews, customer service is outstanding. They did arrive a few days later, but lets just say they had a more than acceptable back-up plan if they did not arrive. The other important thing is that they are not 100% comfortable. They do cause some discomfort to the tops of my ears after extended wearing. It is not unbearable, but if you need 100% comfort, please take it into account. (I have another pair of Bluetooth headphones who's ear canal design doesn't fit my ear canal, and they become unbearably painful after an hour or so of wearing.) The only other "negatives" I can see is that they may not be the best headphones for intense aerobic activity, and because of the shape of my head, I look like something out of Fritz Lang's Metropolis.
Now lets get down to the good part:
The sound is great! We are talking about a pair of headphones that are under $100, and have a sound that can beat many pairs of Bluetooth - and non-Bluetooth - headphones costing much more. Sound is important to me, and these get high marks, especially considering the price. The battery life is excellent. Call quality is also great. It has fooled people into believing I was not using a Bluetooth device. I have not had any connection problems. I have read some reviews where this was an issue, but my headphones connected easily, and maintain this connection at reasonable distances from whatever device. Things like walls can effect connection, but straight line connection is right around the 30 feet range. One nice quirk of the headphones I discovered ... I have them synchronized to my iPhone and Mac. Whenever I turn them on, they automatically connect to both devices. Didn't see that one coming.
Overall, I am very happy with my purchase, I would purchase them again, I would recommend them to a friend, and I would purchase them for friends and family members.

product_title: Outdoor Technology Chips Wireless Bluetooth Helmet Audio
review_body:
It is rare that I give a written review of anything I buy but I feel this product deserves one. I bought this based on other reviews from users on Amazon. I bought these to replace my Motorola S802 Bluetooth speakers. They were great in terms of sound and on the fly functionality but when it was cold they simply didn't work well. You couldn't get through a song without it cutting out 15 times or so a song. Barely doable on cold days.

Today was my first outing with these and not a single hiccup. It was -5 with windchills reaching -60 at the top. So they certainly can handle any cold conditions I throw at them. The functionality is great as well. As long as your helmets ear pieces have the ability to insert the speakers your fine. And since the entire speakers opposite side surface area is a button performing all available controls is very easy. The only caveat for me is that you have to press and hold the left side 6 seconds to advance a track and 3 to back up. I would prefer it the other way around since I rarely go back. But it's not enough of a negative to give it anything less than 5 Stars. I can't imagine anyone not loving these speakers. I see people with regular earbuds all the time. I was once one of them. I can't imaging resorting to that when products like this exist. Being able to have total control of your music on the fly effortlessly is a great thing.
