review_headline: This product nearly burned my house down - AND Belkin could not care less!
review_body: Belkin - you've really let me down here!  I am a huge Wemo fan and evangelist - eight wall switches, six lamps controlled through the outlet and have two sensors.  Then I bought three of these.  My wife just smelled a burning odor and found this plug smoking in our wall.  Please see photo below.  Please note that this product could have killed my children.  I just feel lucky my wife found this in time.  I have three of these that are now useless.  Wemo/Belkin - I do expect to hear from you with a plan for taking these back.  I do note additional burned plugs in other reviews and have also reported this item to the CPSC.  Sigh - do not buy this.  ***Update*** March 15, 2015  HOURS after I posted this review, Belkin contacted me telling me how critical it was for them to get in touch with me to rectify this.  I replied immediately.  Two weeks went by and I heard back from them on March 5th asking for my receipt and the photo taken of the burned Conserve Socket.  I sent these to them on the same day with a request for them to contact me immediately.  Amazingly, two weeks later I still have not heard back from Belkin about this.  I can only surmise that I received my initial email because Belkin only cares how my review affects their sales and could not care less about nearly burning my home down with my three children inside it.  For shame Belkin!!  You've officially converted this Wemo evangelist into a Wemo hater.

product_title: AUVIO® 2.4GHz Wireless Speaker Kit
review_headline: Works great for Surround Sound System
review_body:
Having read the prior reviews of this product I bought it with a little hesitancy, and have been pleasantly surprised and pleased with the performance. I have the unit hooked up to a simple Phillips home theater system in my family room and it has more than enough power for this unit. If you have a significantly higher end system, this unit is probably not for you. The dynamic range of the speakers has not been reduced and the volume adjusts well matching the wired speakers at all volume levels. When I first installed the unit I left it set at the default channel setting of 1 and did experience some of the issues that others have reported with interference with my WIFI network. Changing the unit to channel 3 and powering the transmitter and receiver units down and restarting them , this step is important, solved the problem immediately.

Installation was really quick and easy and the manual, which is very small, is really not needed if you have any experience with AV equipment, as the receiver and transmitter connections are well labeled and identified. The spring clip speaker wire connections are strong and secure, but are not designed for anything thicker than an 18 gauge wire.

This kit really is for the connection of the rear speakers of a home theatre system and not for powering remote speakers from a stereo in a remote location. When used for this purpose it does it's job well.

Cheap Price
Easy pairing
GIANT suction cup for wall mounting.

Cons:
Badly written instructions

USB port cover does not seal well, may cause issues later on.

product_title: Orei DA21X Bit Optical SPDIF and Coaxial Premium Digital to Analog Audio Converter
review_headline: Simple setup, Good audio Quality, No nonsense
review_body:
I bought this to connect the optical audio output of a Samsung UN60H7150 TV to my hi-fi stereo. Everything was working within 2 minutes. Connect the optical signal cable, RCA connectors and power. Set the TV to use the optical audio output instead of the internal speakers and there you go. Note that when you switch to a new input source or use one of the included apps (like Youtube or Netflix) for the first time, you will probably need to go into the advanced audio settings and set the audio format to be PCM (since it will default to DolbyDTS). This is probably the case for most or all new Samsung TVs as of 2014.

Also note that the optical audio output is a fixed-level output and you CANNOT control the volume through the TV. The output signal will be max-volume, and you will have to control the volume on your receiver or amplifier. Do not just hook it straight up to a fixed-gain amplifier or headphones because you might blow out your speakers or worse.

This DAC module only supports stereo audio output (left/right). Surround sound and that sort of thing is not what this is for.

The audio quality is great on this. There is no background hum or hiss, I do not hear pops or clicks when things turn on and off. So it performs well as an analog audio source. I use it to provide a signal to a Behringer stereo amplifier which drives some Scan-Speak floor-standers. Everything sounds fine, so the DAC quality is at least as good as my ears (I don't claim to have golden ears so take it for what it's worth!).

product_title: Panlong Optical Audio Switch with IR Remote Control
review_headline: Here's a 2-Port Switcher that Allowed us to Successfully Hook up an Amazon Fire Device!
review_body:
This product works as advertised, making it easy to switch the audio between two components (1. Cable TV and 2. Amazon Fire so that we can use Netflix). It would have been nice to have a USB-to-wall adapter but thankfully we didn't need that because there was an open USB slot on the back of our Cable box which sufficed and provided the needed power connection.

I'm happy that a remote came with this device because it makes it that much more convenient to use and not have to get up and go manually switch the channels on the device. However, it IS possible to switch the channels on the device manually if need be, like if you happened to lose your remote or something, so either way, you will be able to accomplish changing the channels.

This 2-port Optical Audio Switcher device made it possible for us to connect an Amazon Fire device to our widescreen TV setup which then, in turn, allowed us to use Netflix through that Amazon device which was our ultimate goal. Once I installed this 2-port Optical Audio Switcher, then everything worked perfectly (both the Cable TV feed as well as the Amazon Fire feed). All that has to be done is we use the accompanied remote to switch between the devices, depending on which device we are watching, and that's it!

Great product, thank you!

product_title: Sony STRDH550 5.2 Channel 4K AV Receiver
review_body:

I was disappointed with the HDMI passthrough. They don't tell you that you need compatible devices that support this feature (which is the main reason I bought this unit. I guess that should have been inferred by a technically astute audiophile, but I didn't figure it out until reading the friendly manual. So, in order to accomodate HDMI switching, you need to have the receive on. This brings up the next issue....

A month after installation, the unit started cycling between 'stand-by' mode and 'on' mode. So, the system would click on and off at 10 second intervals. And, it was one of those clicks that drives you crazy, like a beeping smoke alarm. Tried lots of things to troubleshoot--unplugging, turning off other devices, different cables, etc. It's just plain defective and will be returned for warranty repair.

This review has been updated. I have ordered this wire set at 2 different times. In fact, the most recent order was for 2 packages of these wire sets, giving me 3 of these wire sets. The two orders were several months apart and contained two different AWG wire sizes. I am less enthralled with the latest order.

Original post:
These are great for normal usage. Someone else pointed out that these have 18 AWG wire, which is on the very light end of your normal home extension cord sizes. Normal home extension cords are 14 or 16 AWG wire. Power equipment, heaters, items that use more than average power usually need 10 or 12 AWG wire. The smaller the number, the larger the wire and the more power it can handle. Battery wire in semi trucks is usually 4 AWG wire.

Enough on the wire. These are great for plugging in those 12 volt adapters used for charging just about everything any more. Those block chargers that use more then their share of space at an electrical outlet. Those block chargers usually don't pull much power. Their main goal it to reduce the electrical current to whatever is needed, which is normally less then 12 volts and low wattage. For that usage, these things are great.

For a larger power draw, you need heavier wire.

Update Feb. 22, 2015
I am revising my previous review from above and downgrading the number of stars that I gave this product.

I had just ordered these wires when I wrote the above information. My review was based on a previous order of these wires that I had received several months before. After receiving my most recent order of these wires, I did a comparison between the wire which I had received in these orders. I noticed that I had received 16 AWG wire in the previous order. Not the lighter 18 AWG gauge wire which the new order contained. I also noticed that the previous order which contained the 16 gauge wire also had a UL label, and the new order of these short extensions did not have the UL label.

The lighter wire can be used to power items that pull a small amount of current for a short period of time. But the thinner the wire, the faster it will heat up when used. (The larger the AWG wire size, the smaller the actual wire.)

There is a certain amount of heat anytime electricity passes down a wire. The larger the wire, the less heat that is produced for a given about of power. I'm not an electrical engineer, but I understand that the wire will start to melt (For lack of a better word) both itself and the coating around it once it exceeds the amount of power that it can safely transmit. Obviously, the coating around a wire will melt from heat before the wire reaches that point, and then you have a fire hazard. If you look around your home, you will find that most of your extension cords are 12, 14, or 16 gauge wire. And they all will have a UL label.

18 AWG wire is thin wire. As I said above, these wires should be fine for light duty and for short periods of time. But don't use these 18 AWG wire extensions for extended periods of time or with items that require more then a little power. These should be fine some of those big-block adapters which step the power down for a small device. I've noticed that I have several small devices where the current is stepped down to under 12 volts and pull only a few amps to recharge in a short period of time. These extensions should be fine for those devices. But don't plug anything into them that draws a lot of power or anything that is turned on a lot of the time.

Many laptops, tablets, and smartphones don’t put out a lot of volume, even when it is turned to the highest level. There are times when I need more volume or a better quality sound from these devices, and a Bluetooth speaker is just the thing.

The OREI Diamond Enhanced Bass NFC Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Speaker, Powerful Sound, Built in Mic, Aluminum Body, Touch Panel & Compact Size is a very nice option with a price point that doesn’t break the bank.

It’s small size and light weight make it easy to carry in a tote bag, but its blocky shape makes it less than ideal for a laptop case or similar style of bag.

All of the controls are touch controls, with the exception of the power button. The power button is a toggle switch on the back of the speaker. This is good because it means it won’t accidentally get turned on when in a bag, depleting the battery before you get a chance to use it. The touch controls are easy to use and very sleek and modern looking.

The speaker itself has a wonderful sound. I’ve been playing my music through it, and have really enjoyed it. I primarily use it with my laptop or smartphone, but have connected it to my iPod Classic using the speaker’s 3.5mm audio port.

OREI includes a micro USB cable in the package, and you can use this to charge the speaker via your computer’s USB port or a USB charger.

product_title: Maha Powerex Wizard One MH-C9000 Advanced Battery Charger and Analyzer - Deluxe Accessory Storage Case Included
review_headline: Fine for 15 days, then the microprocessor failed.
review_body:
I received my Maha on January 15, 2015, and put it into use immediately. I really like a number of aspects of the design. The display is large, bright, and readable. The functions, as documented elsewhere here, are outstanding. I own a lot of NIMH batteries, most of which are Eneloop. I found that the MH-C9000 did an excellent job of charging, and all the functions appeared to work.

A couple of days ago, I put 4 somewhat marginal nimh batteries into a "break-in" mode cycle. This evening, when the cycle had completed, I noticed some nonsensical results in positions 1 and 2. It claimed the capacity of the batteries was 20 MAH, when they had tested previously around 600. I tested the batteries on another charger, a LaCrosse Technologies unit, and found that they were ok. To further test the Maha, I put a brand new, fully charged eneloop battery into the unit. It shut completely off. I remove the battery, removed power from the unit, then plugged the cord back in. Now the unit lit up, apparently "thinking" there is a battery in position 1. But, there was no battery. When I put a battery in, and selected charge, it indicated a charging current of 125MA and a battery voltage of 0.00.

The microprocessor has obviously gone haywire after 15 days of use. Not good. I'll be seeking an exchange.

product_title: Zeimax Bluetooth4.0 Headphones Supports NFC Bluetooth, Revolutionary 8 Tracks 8 Driver Units Deep bass effect wireless Headphones On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: but I've had good luck with Creative products lately
review_body:
I haven't compared too many bluetooth headphones on the market, but I've had good luck with Creative products lately, so I didn't hesitate to get these. They are bypassing costly advertising campaigns with popular music artist as a salesperson and just selling solid quality products at great prices.

The good: Overall, good sound quality and pretty well balanced when bloated bass headphones are all the rage now days. I don't personally have the largest headphone collection. My main cans are Sennheiser 555s, so I can only compare to them. Granted the 555s are not the top end model, they are pretty good. The Creative Labs can't quite touch the quality of the 5554s wired cans, but one is over ear while the other is on ear. While they are balanced well, they do still seem to be just a little bass heavy. I'd imagine most people will like this and most of the time, its not a problem. I did listen to some Daft Punk and the bass was actually too heavy for that. The midrange was lacking during the heavy bass hits. Battery life seems just fine. I haven't actually tried to find its limits, but I only charge them once or twice a week. Sound quality reviews can be so subjective and its really hard to take other peoples reviews seriously. I will say this about them. For any shortcomings they might have in sound quality, they sound good enough and have a wide enough range to get lost in good music. They are very enjoyable.

The bad: Nothing too negative, but I don't think I'd want to wear them for more then an hour at a time. I generally don't and they are used at work most of the time. The on ear is not nearly as comfy as over ear. They feel ever so slightly tight.

Bottom line. I'm happy with them and I have no buyers remorse. I'd get them all over again.

product_title: Thorens TD 158 Fully Automatic Plug-and-Play Turntable - 33 or 45 rpm DN 251 S (Black)
review_body:
Amazon service was perfect. Five stars to Amazon.
However the product as delivered did not function - it was just defunct.
The original Thorens box was packed inside another very large box in which it was loose with a little crumpled brown paper and moved about side to side on any movement. The Thorens packing was however good and the turntable was intact.with all parts complete.
This model - TD 158 - is very easy to assemble. It has two red transport plugs of which one was missing ! The dust cover is easy to fit and nice to see. The turntable platter is easy to place. That is all. It is supposed to be plug and play model..
However when started the player kept switching off automatically within 5 seconds. The cuing lever to lift or lower the tone arm did not work. The tone arm did not rise fully, just made a slight movement and settled back. When I tried to place it manually it would stay on the same groove till machine switched off in next few seconds. When placed and stop applied the tone arm did not rise or return.
Within three or four minutes I knew I had been sent a dud machine.
I suspect that this player had not been adequately assembled or tested by Thorens before packing, or they were not careful when handling it. A transportation plug was missing. I do not know if the intermediate agency selling it to me over Amazon had checked it, or whether they had spoiled it. They may be just intermediaries moving the box on, I actually do not know. Personally my sense is that this piece should not have cleared the Thorens establishment in Germany. And so I cannot comment on the quality or lack of quality of the player as such.
Either way I have had a very sad experience and wasted so much time, energy, attention and effort in selecting this model all to no end.
Amazon has been perfect. They delivered on time and the return went through very well. Now I can look at something else.

product_title: OREI Enhanced Bass Bluetooth
review_headline: might be what you are looking for
review_body:
I own many different Bluetooth speakers and I am discovering that each one fits a different purpose and need. My favorite Bluetooth speaker is the Polk Camden square. The battery life is 24hours and the music it produces is bright brassy and fills the entire room. You can see my review of that product elsewhere. Unfortunately polks price point is much higher. This speAker by Orei comes out to provide a much lighter cheaper and attractive speaker.
Orei speaker is light for a Bluetooth speAker. I can easily toss it into my backpack without fear of weight to pack or damage of speaker.
Sound quality comes next. This speaker for its size really does pack a nice melodic punch. It doesn't fill the room very well but within the right conditions it sounds alright. Maybe a small bedroom or a kitchen counter. Definitely not a living room or a garage. I think you would be disappointed if you had grander purpose for this speaker. The sound quality is a little light without that Bose brassy punch, which is perfectly fine with me. I think the highs in this speaker really do alright.
So should you buy? If you need a light mobile Bluetooth yes. I think this competes with the Bose sound link. Sorry fan boys. The sound quality is much better still with the Sony nfc than the orei you are looking at. I would recommend this for your spare bedroom. I would recommend Polk for your living room or lady open space. I think this product fits a nice niche and you should check it out if you have the specific needs I mentioned.

product_title: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone
review_body: I decided on the 'Sennheiser Momentum - Over The Ear' headphone after days of research, my options being Sennheiser's own Urbanite, the Beats Solo and Studio, the NAD Viso HP, the Monster Ntune, a couple of Sony headhones, and V-Moda headphones.    The Momentum's are classy looking, and very unobtrusive. The sound is realistic, and clear. There is no booming overemphasized bass. If you want intense bass, you're better off with Beats and Monster. If you ever plan to watch movies on the go, this pair is quite well suited. Add to that the fact that it can be powered by a smart phone, makes its hassle free. The fit is comfortable, and even with extended use, its not a problem. The build is superb; its solid enough to feel substantial, while at the same time being light enough to be easy on the head. It does a decent job of cutting-out ambient sounds/noise. The best part is that though this is originally intended to be a 300 dollar headphone, there are some nice deals on Amazon which means it can be had for under 200 dollars. The packaging and carry case are wreak of quality.    This isn't my first pair of Sennhesier's; I have been using a wireless pair of theirs since 2006. When i decided to get myself a new one, I decided to check out the market and not just blindly go back to Sennheiser. But truth be told, after all the searching, and reading, Sennheiser was the obvious choice.    If you're looking for something that looks bling, and sounds intense, you're better off with Beats or Monster. The former looking more flashy, the later sounding similar to Beats but at a much lower price point. While its probably fun for music, for movies it'd be terrible. Also, be warned that with Beats parts cant be replaced or repaired. The only option is to replace the entire unit. Per the reviews the NAD Viso HP is supposed to be better, but I couldn't demo it anyplace, and the lowest price it was available for was 250 dollars.

review_headline: ... this little box in today and I am very pleased! This product works as described
review_body:
I just got this little box in today and I am very pleased! This product works as described. I have a 10+ year old Toshiba 40" flat screen in my bedroom with RCA jacks, and I been wanting to play my Sony Blue Ray on this TV. You maybe wondering why I don't get rid of the old TV and upgrade? This TV weighs 200 lb., and to get it in my bedroom I literally had to take the door off the hinges to get it in! Since the TV still works great, and it does have the simulated surround sound, I decided to get this converter after reading all the reviews.
The setup is really simple, and only takes 2 minutes. Plug your HDMI cable to the HDMI device, plug the other end to the converter, connect the USB power cord to a power source, plug in your RCA jacks, and you are ready to go.
There are 2 things you should watch out for. The power for this box is thru a USB style charger, so make sure you have a USB type charger, I just use my cell phone charger, or you can buy one locally or online they are very common. Some people in the reviews use their computer USB port. The other is the NTSC/PAL switch, if you are in the US make sure you switch it to NTSC. From what I've read online outside of most of north America and some south American countries uses NTSC, while everyone else uses the PAL setting. It's an encoding due to the type of electricity generated in the area (hertz). Mine was set to PAL when I receive my order, so I knew to set it to NTSC. Just messing around, I flipped the switched to PAL, and I get gray images. There was one or two reviews with this problem, and I can't blame them for leaving bad reviews. The instruction is terrible.
I hope this help someone.

review_headline: Good sound, but some design flaws
review_body: Update: changing the 1 star. I was sent a replacement set for the issue described in my initial review. Within a month the charging port cover fell off again. A few months later the left speaker stopped working completely. There's a reason they are cheap, because they are cheap. Avoid.   While the headphones have pretty good sound, I am a little upset over the build quality of these headphones. They come with a nice carrying case, and 5 different size ear buds so you can find one that fits your ears properly. The sound is quite good, with good bass reproduction.  The negative: - The track forward and track reverse buttons are the same as the volume up and down buttons, you simply hold one in longer (for example, press a button once to turn volume down, hold it in for 3 seconds and it changes the song instead). This is nice for not having a ton of buttons, but makes it impossible to go back to a previously played song. Reason being is how long you have to hold down the button for it to respond. For instance, I just finished song 1 and song 2 is now playing, but I want to go back to song 1. Hold down the track reverse button for 3 seconds, song 2 restarts. Hold down the track reverse button again for seconds and it should go back to track 1, correct? No, because now song 2 has already played for 3 seconds, so it simply starts track 2 over again. It is impossible to go back to a previous track with the buttons.  - The cover for the charging port fell off after about 10-15 uses. Since these are labeled as "Sport" headphones, you can assume they will be used around sweat. Well this cover is pretty integral to keeping sweat out of the charging port. I figure it is just a matter of time before the headphones no longer work due to sweat entering the charging port.

product_title: Satellite Speaker Stands
review_headline: Great choice for Yamaha NS-P40 Surround sound speakers
review_body:
These are good solid stands that I bought for my newly purchased Yamaha NS-P40 surround sound speakers. The front and rear speakers for this set are about the size of your silver cafeteria type napkin holder, to give you some perspective of what I'm using these stands for.

The stands are mainly the base that sits on the floor and the telescopic pole that screws into the base. These look to be cast iron and will be around forever. A small little metal \\"seat\\" screws on the top of the pole and is where the speaker is placed. A wire bracket slides into the seat and is used to secure the back of the speaker to the stand. There are also 4 screw holes in each seat if you wanted to screw the seat into the bottom of the speaker but I in no way see that necessary since these speakers are plastic and they aren't going anywhere, being secured by the wire bracket.

It would take a hard push to knock over these stands with these speakers on them, so I think they would hold somewhat larger speakers also.

2 different size of screws are provided to secure the speaker to the wire bracket, along with small rubber washers. One of the screws fit into the back of my speakers, so no problem there.

These stands are easy to adjust the height from below ear level at a sitting position to well above. The hand grip midway up the pole loosens and tightens and secures it well so it doesn't slide down. The hand grip is plastic, so I might think if it was tightened too hard it could possibly break over time, but I didn't need to tighten it much at all to get it to stay in place.

Before buying these I was concerned about getting the speaker wire through the pole, but I found that rather easy. I am using 16 gauge speaker wire and I easily got the wire through the stand in this sequence:

1) Don't strip the wire yet (if you do, I suppose you could tape a piece of paper around the end to keep it stiff)
2) Screw one of the poles into a base. The threads are a little tight, so it took just a little care to get the pole at the right angle to screw into the base. Keep the pole at its lowest position for now.
3) Take the end of the speaker wire that will connect to the speaker, turn the base and pole upside down and run that through the bottom of the base and pole until the end of the wire comes through the top end of the pole. Now take one of the little seats and put that around the speaker wire and screw the seat to the pole and then proceed to attaching the speaker wire to the speaker and securing the speaker to the pole with the supplied hardware.

It isn't that obvious until you have it in front of you, but it was quite easy.

I will say the end of the wire that attaches to the speaker should not have too much of it's insulation stripped (no more than about 3/4 in) as you may end up with bare wire touching the metal wire bracket of the stand. It is a minor issue but the bracket could have been designed a little better in that regard.

Overall these are a good choice for my speakers (I would think for many other similar type speakers also) and I have now bought 2 of these over the past week and have had no problems with either set of stands.so it took just a little care to get the pole at the right angle to screw into the base. review_headline: Poor sound, no bass and not for the gym or any physical activity.
review_body:
I did not buy these from Amazon, but made the mistake of buying them nonetheless. I will say that I go through ear buds quite often I need a good set for the gym and these were the only brand I had yet to buy. First of all, the package says "Unruly Bass." Ha! More like unruly treble! The sound quality is mediocre at best, and I have a top-of-the-line MP3 player.

Second, and I suppose this is only important if you plan on using these in the gym, the cable is made out of some stickier rubber compound. There is nothing smooth about the cable. Though long enough for tall people, the cable tends to tangle and stick to itself, even with the least amount of movement. This can be really annoying when you are exerting yourself with vigorous physical activity.

Third, the buds, designed to stay put in your ear with the help of rubber covers, constantly pop out of my ears. Under close scrutiny, I found that the rubber covers don't match in regards to size. Very poor quality and a total pain in the rear when trying to exercise. I learned the hard way to just spend the money and get some over-the-ear phones for my time at the gym. These are too much of a chore.

Finally, they lasted only about 3 weeks before one of the buds quit working.

You may as well give the $10 away if you are considering purchasing these inferior ear buds.

product_title: Boston Acoustics Speaker Foam Edge Repair Kit, 8" A60, A70, HD8, FSK-8
review_headline: Great speakers come back from the dead!
review_body:
I just re-foamed a pair of Boston Acoustics A-60s that I've loved since the late 80s. This kit is just the ticket. Speakers sound like they're brand-new.
A couple of cautions: Stop using and plan to re-foam your speaks as soon as, or before, they start to rattle. This is the sound of the voice coil rubbing on the magnet assembly, and will damage the voice coil. Also, a 1/8-inch bead of glue is too much for these little guys! It squeezed out and made a pretty nasty mess. Much to my delight, Gumout carb and choke cleaner will dissolve the fresh glue, for clean-up. Probably would hurt the foam, but is OK on the cone. On the second speaker, I used a much lighter application (maybe 1/16-inch) and all is good. They give you enough glue to do a couple dozen speakers! Don't even think you have to use it all! Plenty left over for hanging pictures, or gluing your teenage kids in their room. I was worried about the centering of the voice coil, but it was not a problem; just follow the instructions about gently pushing down on the center dust cap.
The YouTube video is a little anal on one hand, and incomplete on the other. Not hard to remember that the colored wire goes to the terminal closest to the label. No point in wasting 4 wire-ties... Putting the speaker gasket back in place using screws is kinda silly, IMHO. It also completely skipped the centering steps. I highly recommend this really inexpensive way to save these great speakers! Enjoy!

product_title: RCA Compact Outdoor Yagi HDTV Antenna with 70 Mile Range
review_body:
Goodbye Clearstream 2, hello ANT751. Firstly, it was my mistake for not knowing the difference between UHF and VHF. Second, my mistake for buying a UHF antenna and then wondering why I wasn't getting all the channels.

I had a Clearstream 2 mounted to the top of my chimney, well within range of the source towers. The UHF channels were perfect, no fault on the Clearstream there. The VHF channels would show up in a channel scan, but very rarely would we be able to get a picture. It was like this for over 2 years, we finally got tired of missing channels and I did more research. Fast forward to hooking up the ANT751. Connected but on the ground and not even pointing in the right direction, maybe 30 degrees away from where it should be aiming. It not only picked up all the missing channels on VHF, but it also seems that we are able to switch channels faster now. Possibly because of a better signal? I do have an inline amp, only the antennas were changed.

Let me restate that, Clearstream 2 mounted 35ft up and aimed properly versus ANT751 laying on the ground and pointing in the not optimal direction and behind a chainlink fence. ANT751 outperformed in both UHF and VHF.

Complaints, not many. Really the only thing I'd improve is the unfolding and alignment of the elements. I don't know how critical this is for reception, but I took a few minutes to make sure they were as level and uniform as I could make them.

On a side note, I'm 99% sure I received a returned product. The box was missing staples, it was packed with paper stuffed around it and airbags, more than half of which were broken. The accessories were in ziploc baggies. Lastly it was pretty clear that there was a UPS shipping sticker from Amazon to another person in Florida under mine, I peeled it off and could see their address info. Plus a packing slip on the box that showed it was ordered from Amazon, shipped to a person and how much they paid. All that said, the product works, I think I got everything, it's installed and working wonderfully.

Last note, I'm very disappointed with the Clearstream 2. When I took it down, it seemed heavier than I remembered. It wasn't until it had been sitting on the kitchen table for 20 minutes that I noticed it started dripping water everywhere. I swapped this antenna in the middle of January in Pennsylvania. Water had built up inside the plastic shell in the Clearstream, froze and was now melting on my table. I can only assume the water/ice being held inside would cause an early failure. I won't know because I won't be using the Clearstream.

product_title: Bluetooth Earphones, TaoTronics Bluetooth Wireless Earphones Sport Headphones Earbuds Headsets (Bluetooth 4.0, Delicate Sound, Build-in Mic, 6 Hours Playtime, CVC 6.0 Noise-Cancelling)
review_headline: A very good set of headphones
review_body:
Summary: The TaoTronics GoSport wireless headphones may not be the sleekest looking set of Bluetooth headphones available but they are very good in all of the other important aspects, including: Ease of Use, Connection, Sound Quality, Fit, Versatility and Battery Life. I also found the transmitting range to be comparable to typical Bluetooth standards (30 feet), however I used them mainly in short range situations. Not only good for working-out and listening to music or sports talk but works well in a hands-free phone situation as the control bar also contains a microphone. Overall I would rate these five star for functionality and quality of operation with a 3 star rating for aesthetics.

Ease of use: The control bar contains 3 buttons (2 for volume +/- and 1 Multifunction for power and phone control), the previously mentioned microphone, an LED indicator and the micro USB charging port. A quick read through the user guide and a quick charge and you’re ready to use the headphones.

Bluetooth Connection: The GoSport headphones proved easy to connect with a very simple process. Put it in discovery mode using the Multifunction button and select it in your devices Bluetooth settings. I used it with my iPhone, iPad, Windows PC and my TaoTronics TT-BA01 Bluetooth transmitter.

Quality of Sound: I’m not a sound expert but in my opinion the sound quality is very good (if not excellent) with a nice mix of base and treble to make for pleasing listening of music while working out, working around the house or listening to radio broadcasts of sporting events. DISCLOSURE: I received the TaoTronics GoSport headphones as a free sample for evaluation so I will not compare the sound quality to a specific price range, but the sound quality is real good.

Fit: I found the fit to be most comfortable using the “large” sized ear buds (small & large sizes are provided with the headphones). I use them for aerobic work outs (elliptical machine, fast walking and light jogging outdoors and on tread mills) as well as light yard work around the house with no real problems with falling out or issues related to perspiration. Best of all there are no wires to get in the way and yank the ear pieces out of my ears. The inter-connecting wire runs behind you neck and remains well out of your way.

Versatility: As mentioned I’ve used the GoSport with several different devices with no issues connecting. Make sure the GoSport is in “discovery mode” (LED blinking Blue and Red) and there should not problems.

Battery Life: The user guide states that working battery life is 6 hours. I’ve had mine last at least that long
.
Appearance: As I pointed out in the “Summary” above the design is a bit clunky – with small square black boxes for the ear piece electronics and the control bar. The square box design doesn’t present any technical or use problems – it’s more just an issue of aesthetics.

review_headline: Exhausted my disk space with virtual memory and may have accessed my email passwords
review_body:
I may be able to find a solution for it, but at the moment, when I hook this up to my MacBook and to my old tube TV, the picture is black and white, split in half, and flipping. The sound is crystal clear, though. However, within 2 minutes of it being hooked up to my Mac, I got an alert that my hard drive was full! SystemUIServer was exhausting 52 GB of virtual memory! I assume "UI" means "user interface" and that my Mac was trying in vain to resolve the picture issue, and in doing so used up the rest of my disk space for RAM. I unplugged and rebooted. Disk was back to normal. I checked Console for error messages. What I found was a bit disturbing.

Sure, there were bug warnings and statements that certain actions were corrupted or couldn't be completed, but there were also attempts to access my email accounts. The system denied it access, but the fact that something was attempting to access them and the fact that there were outgoing internet access messages, makes me very concerned for my privacy. I'm taking the MacBook to the Genius Bar for a system check up. I've read that others with Mac computers haven't had any issues, but I wonder what OS they're using. The email access requests may have nothing to do with this product, but I've never seen Console messages with so many error reports, especially at the exact same time my disk was being filled by virtual memory.

I will update this if and when I receive more information, but I caution MacBook users on Yosemite that the white mini model could be a very, very bad thing for your system. Regardless of whether I can resolve the errors, I'm returning this immediately.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Why I have to own both Bose headphones and Beats...
review_body:
Headphones are expensive, but I use them everyday for hours on end. Based on my music tastes, I own both these Bose QC15s and Beats by Dre Studio.
However, I understand that spending a lot money on one pair of headphones, nevertheless two pairs is quite the investment.

So in helping you decide on what to buy, here's a breakdown of when I listed to these:

Bose:
- When using for long periods of time, i.e. traveling, in bed, at work. They are extremely comfortable and you can almost forget that you have them on. As far as comfort goes, these are tough to beat. I even fell asleep in them and didn't wake up uncomfortable like other headphones.
- Traveling. Great for airplanes. I couldn't hear a thing around me and it felt as if I were in my own world. They certainly do drown out all of the surrounding noises.
- When listening to more mellow, acoustic music. These seems to have a more, balanced sound and sometimes you want that, but sometimes you don't

Beats:
- When listening to bass heavy music like hip hop, EDM, etc. Bose sound great, but lack a little on the bass side (if that's what you like). Sometimes (like when at the gym), you just want a loud, heavy bass thumping pair of headphones to get you through. These Bose wouldn't work as well for that.
- For looks. Yes, that's an expensive price to pay if you want to look good in a pair of headphones. Some call it vanity, but to others, it's important to also be in the mix of fashion.

As far as customer service goes, Bose wins hands down. I've had to return a pair after 10 months and Bose sent me a new pair rather quickly.

product_title: MEE audio Atlas Carbon IML Graphics On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: A Fine, Well Rounded Addition to Any Collection
review_body:
Nice build quality here. I read some reviews on tech websites which indicated that this would be a pretty good entry level pair of 'phones, and overall a good value - though not to expect miracles. On having these for about 3 weeks, I basically agree with that sentiment. I got them on sale for $35, which was a great deal for what I got.

What I wanted was a kind of hybrid of premium sound quality and functionality. My first priority was the sound, but a close second was comfort. I had curbed my expectations for the sound quality, given the price point, and I was satisfied with what I heard. I was not blown away by any means - and I really felt the mids were very weak - but what was coming through was crisp and clean. The biggest letdown was how the bass just dominated, and was an ever-present rumble, even with female vocals. However, there was a massive improvement after about 48-72 hours of heavy use, and the sound really tightened up over the first week. The bass had more "pop", and stopped bleeding into everything else, and the mids seemed to emerge, giving a much more even response. So if the sound is a little overwhelming, kind of "raw", or just all over the place, give it a few days and see how you like it.

The comfort level I was hoping for was there in spades. This pair lies really light on the head, has nice cushioning, and stays in place. I have no discomfort at all while wearing these for hours at a time, and they don't overheat my ears. Keep in mind that these are "on-ear" headphones. I thought they would cover my ears, but for my head/ear size they sit nicely. The cups are ear-shaped on the inside. While I don't really care that much how they look, these do have a nice form factor and are pretty sleek - you won't feel like you're wearing a space helmet. They feel solid, and having a detachable cord on them makes me far less anxious about wear and tear. I would be fine putting these into a backpack without a case. There's a vinyl bag included which may prevent scratches, which I think could be an issue, since the carbon shell picks up fingerprints easily. The one thing that would have made these completely perfect for me is if they were a little quieter for bystanders. If you keep the volume low for voice or audio books, there's no problem, but if you want to jam out to some tunes, it will be audible to people close to you(not super loud, but certainly not isolated).

So with the sound quality being good and the comfort level excellent - add on the convenience of the button and volume slider, plus the fact that they double as a headset for calls/video-chat/gaming, this is a product that is easy to recommend. If you want a pair of headphones with quality sound, comfort, and long-term durability - or a chat headset that looks and feels nice - this is definitely worth considering. I have been looking for headphones that kind of "do it all" for a very long time, and these work for me. At some point, I will invest in headphones that have a studio quality sound, but I expect that I will continue to use these even after that. I think these will see lots and lots of use over the next several years.

review_headline: Horrible tilt and instructions - do not buy
review_body: for the life of me, I can't figure out what the \\"patented\\" tilt mechanism is here. From what i can tell, and from reading the other reviews, it tilts by adjusting nuts and screws (4 PER SIDE) before mounting the tv. The hell?    I've mounted many tvs before so I knew what i was doing. But these instructions are a joke. For example, it tells you to use different drill bit sizes depending on whether you are installing on drywall or concrete. For drywall, it says to use a \\"2 [and then a weird symbol]\\" and for concrete, use a \\"4 [and the same weird symbol].\\"    There are no instructions on how to use the tilt mechanism. The instructions use a mix of words and pictures, but mostly awful pictures and non-descriptive words (such as \\"ok\\" and an arrow to the picture).    Save yourself the headache and do not buy this. I mistakenly thought the patented tilt mechanism would be something good, not freaking awful.    EDIT: So I figured out the tilt mechanism.  It isn't bad.  But it's locked in place and you may need to pry it out with a screwdriver the first time to get it to tilt (which is what I had to do).  When I mounted the TV to the mount, one of the drawstrings (used to lock the TV to the mount) fell off.  So getting the TV off was a pain (I had put it up for a test fit first).  Even though the tilt is pretty good, I'm leaving my review at 2 stars because of the awful instructions, and the drawstring that fell off.  Don't worry about the people who said that it's \\"flimsy\\" - they clearly have no idea how physics works.  The strength of your install comes from the mounting points to your wall (i.e. the screws into your stud or concrete/brick).  The \\"flimsy\\" mount isn't doing the heavy lifting.

product_title: SONOS CONNECT:AMP Wireless Amplifier for Streaming Music
review_body: I've been looking at this amp for a while and considering how much it costs, I vetted it out for a while.  My previous setup was 2 patio speakers in the backyard that I ran speaker wire to the back of my receiver into the second zone inside the house.  That second zone was analog output only, so options were limited.  Everytime I wanted to hear music in the back yard, I had to go inside, turn on the receiver, then connect a 3.5 line into my computer to play music out of the speakers.  It became annoying especially when I had dirty shoes or merely wanted to turn the volume up to go back inside and then out again.    Then I saw this amp.  Seemed to solve my problem of having to go in and out of the house since it does everything via the Sonos app.  I ended up buying it and in a matter of 15 minutes, disconnected the speaker wire from my receiver and plugged them into the plugs on the back of the amp, then went through the 4 minute process of setting up the sonos.  All in that time, I was outside blaring music from my speakers, controlling what music comes out of it and the volume straight from my phone.  The sound is just as good if not better than what it was coming from my receiver.  On top of that, there are times I want to listen to games streamed by ESPN or cable TV through my patio speakers (like a seahawks game), so I used the RCA inputs on the back of the amp along with a Y connector to plug into my laptop.  Using the ESPN app or my HDHomerun, I can listen to anything that's on TV or streaming on the web.  It's great.    One thing to note is I've seen a few challenges in the way the app works.  There are times I attempt to stream music from Pandora and it fails to recognize the stations on my account.  After about 10 minutes of opening and closing the app, they suddenly appeared again.  This may have been a wireless channel issue that I switched soon after and I haven't seen it since.  Also note that this thing is quite large (taller than an xbox, but 2/3 thewidth), so you'll need a decent place to put it.    Update 1/30/15:  I've been using this for a few weeks now and it's fantastic.  I've updated the rating from 4 to 5 stars.  One thing to keep in mind is that if the wireless connection fades, the volume will stay where it's at until you either get the wireless signal back or manually go to the device and adjust the volume there.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control for Control of 8 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_body:
One of the least intuitive electronics I have ever owned...
Although I have set up a few one touch controls that change my lights and dim them and switch all the inputs appropriately when I want to watch a movie or TV, the frustrations Im running into are aside from those items.
First of all, I accidentally added two 'one touch' settings with the same name. One works correctly, one does not, but I cannot figure out how to delete the setting that works incorrectly. I cant figure out how to delete an activity period. Im now searching the internet for a more robust manual for the remote that tells me how to delete an activity that you have created, because ive looked through all of the menus on the phone app several times and cannot find one that does what I need.
Additionally, there are buttons on the remote that just have a light bulb on them, and other buttons that have a + and - symbol next to those light bulb buttons. One would assume that those buttons would connect to a light preset with your Phillips Hue bulbs. However, I cant seem to figure out how to set the preset.
Additionally, the light selector for the bulbs themselves is a sample picker on a color spectrum. Good luck trying to get any of the bulbs in your presets to be exactly the same colors and brightnesses. Its nearly impossible. I dont know why a simple x/y coordinate cant be typed in to let you select the exact color and brightness you want your lights to be.
Also, there is a red button along with a green button, blue button and yellow button. What do they do? Who knows/. The remote doesnt come with a manual to explain that, just a brief booklet that tells you to download the set up app. Supposedly thats all you need. Im no bad with electronics either. I love messing with settings and tweaking things to be just right.
Although when it works correctly, the remote is fantastic, the set up has been less than intuitive for such a complicated device.
Final example of how little information is given about the remote. I see no where to replace the battery or charge the battery. There was a pull tab to activate the battery, but nothing else. Am I to believe that the battery never needs replacing or charging? If so, thats quite a selling point. If not, then maybe you should tell people how to change the battery......

Besides the T-111 plywood siding in my attic, I have no trees, hills or obstructions between my home and the transmission towers.
The description states this antenna can receive signals up to 40 miles, but according to the FCC web site, the transmitting towers are 56.4 miles away, and I receive them PERFECTLY.

review_body:
Whoa. How did I go so long commuting on a train without these? Looking forward my next flight now....

But then I plugged them into my iPod and didn't like the sound quality as much as my standard ear buds. I'm used to a nice rich bass and it just wasn't there. He is a musician, so he did all the research and found these and I liked the reviews...esp liked the richer bass people talked about, as well as the fact that these still work once the batteries run out. Wasn't sure if there would be a real difference with the three settings, but there really is.

As I write this review I have them on listening to my iPod shuffle and I swear, just got chills listening to an Emmylou Harris song b/c it was like she was singing right in my ear with her clear, bright voice. And now The Clash is on and it's ... just...great. Goodbye painful iPod ear buds and annoying train sounds.

Seriously, I'm so happy esp since these were $100 cheaper than the Bose. I do think the Bose were quieter with noise canceling on without the music, but music quality is more important to me.

product_title: Boston Acoustics TVee One TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I needed to improve and boost the sound from my bedroom television, but I live in a townhouse with shared walls. The Boston Acoustics TVee One met my needs perfectly! (Note: the Denon DHT-T110 is an identical product, with the Denon brand being aimed at consumers outside the United States. Denon and Boston Acoustics are owned by the same holding company, the D+M Group.)

The unit provides a much, much better sound experience than the tiny speakers in my TV. Newscasts are easier to understand, movies sound better, and the boosted bass gives the TV sound a richer, fuller dimension (without vibrating the walls and floors). It will NOT give you a surround sound experience, if you are looking for theater-like sound. A simple black box with a tiny nameplate on the front, it blends in with the television, to the extent the unit looks like part of the TV base. Setup couldn't have been more simple: it took longer to open the box and unpack the unit than it did to connect it to the television! Setting up my television remote to communicate with the unit was very simple, as well (one button push-and-hold). I didn't think I would use the Bluetooth function, but I've come to enjoy listening to music stored on my smartphone through the unit.

As for the unit's weaknesses: 1. junky remote (tiny and squishy); 2. rear-facing woofers prevent the unit from being used in an entertainment cabinet or shelf, since the bass would sound muffled; and 3. the optical cable included with the unit seems very cheap, about the thickness of a piece of vermicelli (works fine, but I may replace it, if it becomes a problem).

Overall, the Boston Acoustics TVee One met my needs perfectly, and I am pleased with the purchase.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 20 Headphones
review_headline: Good, compact noise cancelling choice for comfortable, portable, long term use.
review_body: The noise cancelling works very well, especially considering these sit lightly in the ear. That also means you can use them comfortably for as long as you like. The controls work as promised. The lead after the battery box is definitely too short. Worse, the several extensions I have purchased, including the official 20' Bose one do not pass on the volume and track commands which negates a major function bonus to the headphones. The aware button feature allows you to quickly defeat the noise suppression to be able to hear things like plane announcements works well which allows you to not have to remove the earbuds  from your ears or turn them off every time there is an announcement. The zippered case works, but it's barely large enough and the zipper is a bit of a hassle. I will probably switch to another case that has a magnetic flip closure that fits these headphones better if I can find one. The product comes with three different sizes of the "stay+ ear tips" to customize it to your ear size. The built in rechargeable battery lasts a long time. I have several other noise cancelling or suppressing headphones and earbuds and these are the best I have experienced for noise suppression without ear discomfort and excessive bulk. The phones will work for music or cellphone conversation with or without being turned on, but are way better on than off.

The music quality may be just a touch below true audiophile speakers, but the the music reproduction is very good, mid-range and highs are crisp and clear with muting across their frequency range.  Since I wall mounted them, I had no need for a sub-woofer, as the rear porting lets the walls be natural passive sub-woofers. product_title: C Crane CC Skywave AM, FM, Shortwave, Weather and Airband Portable Travel Radio with Clock and Alarm
review_headline: Not just a rebadged Chinese radio. Designed specifically for C. Crane using the Si 4736 DSP Chip.
review_body:
This radio has been reviewed on Radiojayallen, http://radiojayallen.com/c-crane-cc-skywave-radio/, and is being discussed extensively in the Yahoo Group Ultralight DX: https://groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/ultralightdx/info

There is also a number of photos showing the complete disassembly of the Skywave in the photos section of that group.

What set this little radio apart from the competition is that it is the first radio to use the new Silicon Labs Si 4736 DSP chip, which offers the best AM performance on a radio of this size to date. The FM tuner is clearly superior as is SW when measured against other radios this size. If you are into MW DXing, this is about the best radio for that in its size class I have ever seen, and even competes favorably against some larger portables.

While it does delete LW, it offers AM, FM, SW, Air Band, and NOAA Weather in the smallest handiest package available. It is easy to use, has great audio, and comes with a set of C. Crane earbuds which are among the best out there. The quality of the build is superior and solid as well. It is easy to use and has several features I really like such as being able to toggle the display between frequency and time, or, you can select frequency or time for the default display. While there is an optional AC Adapter, you can also recharge the radio (if you use NiMH batteries) through a USB port on a computer. It does not come with a USB cable for this purpose, however. AM,FM,Air, and Weather are not affected (at least as far as I can tell) when you are using the radio off of AC Adapter or Computer USB power. But, you will get some hash on shortwave, so it is best to use shortwave on batteries. The antenna is a wimpy 16" , but does an excellent job with FM, and surprisingly good on Shortwave.

This is not simply another Chinese radio which has been rebadged for sale in the USA. This radio was also specifically designed for C. Crane, as evidenced by the photos of the internal printed circuit boards showing the C. Crane logo. It is manufactured for C. Crane by Redsun, and there are no derivatives or copies out there.

There are a few things I did not like about the radio. First, the backlit display cannot be made to stay on full time. It has a ten second timer which allows the light to come on when you press a button or tune the tuning wheel, but it will always shut off after 10 seconds. Secondly, I had to press harder than I would like for all the key presses to register. Sometimes I would hear the key click, but the key function would not activate, so I had to press it again, harder. Lastly, at this price point the radio is literally twice the cost of some comparable Tecsun offerings. Is it worth the added cost? I would say that the performance enhancements coming from the SI4736 DSP Chip do make it worth the cost, but that is something everyone will have to decide for themselves.

If you are a fan of AM radio, this is about the best you are going to get in a travel radio in terms of reception quality, audio quality, and freedom from digital artificats.s of the internal printed circuit boards showing the C. product_title: Pyle-Pro PHA40 4-Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: Awesome deal with a few nit picks
review_body:
I am very satisfied with this amplifier, its size and price are definitely deceiving.
When I have my headphones plugged in wether I am listening to something or not there is no white noise created by the amp itself.
This amplifier is STEREO sound! many amps in this price range/size are mono, and I didnt want mono sound.
The sound is not diminished when another pair of headphones is plugged in and all the knobs work as intended (aka when one channel is turned up the other audio channels do not suffer in quality or volume).
The knobs themselves dont have any slack and are firmly attached.
At first I had a few issues with sound coming through one side only (as some other reviews had mentioned) but it was simply because I didnt have the jack firmly pressed in, once pressed in ALL the way the audio sounds even better coming out then going in.
There are a few things to note if you are buying this:
1. This does not come with an input cable, you will have to supply your own.
2. these are 1/4 jacks so if you have a standard pair of headphones or other accessories that have "small" (1/8) jacks you will want these (I got these as well). amazon.com/gp/product/B00PIWB2SO they are good quality, cheap and theres 5 of them so you have one for every port if need be.
3. The AC power cord is rather short, 3 foot, maybe 4 foot max. This made it rather inconvenient for me because my power source is just a bit farther than that.

Other than that this is a very well built amplifier that is worth the price you pay for it, I just wish it had a longer cord.

product_title: Yamaha R Stereo Receiver
review_body: I'm not a critical reviewer, but I'm very disappointed by the level of distortion this makes at high volume. I used it to power a pair of Definitive Technology StudioMonitor 350s, which are 8ohm and sensitive to 89db. Because they're reputed to prefer a more powerful amp, I went for this to replace a no-name 50w stereo amp I'd been using. Disappointingly, this seems to actually be worse at high volume than that one. Because I use this setup as computer speakers, they're much closer to me than they'd be in a typical home theater or stereo setup. Even medium volumes sees the treble start to go shrill, and turned up, the sound is too sloppy and harsh to enjoy even slightly. Even though I'd been using the 50w on my more sensitive Klipsch floorstanders, I may switch the two back in anticipation that I may have better sound at the computer. The Yamaha also has a somewhat unpleasant background hiss whenever it's on, which can be distracting for my computer speaker application. I'd given it two stars in the past, but the more I use it, the more I realize how much I really can't use it. I'd say that in this price range, you should spring for something with fewer features and better electronics. Or just something a bit pricier and a bit nicer!  Follow up: The Yamaha had been no better on the Klipschs, sounding exactly as awful, if not worse due to their horn-loaded tweeters. The speakers play very, very cleanly on the Adcom power amp/preamp I bought second-hand later on, so the bad sound was purely due to the Yamaha. It's the sort of "wall of noise" distortion that you at dive bars with awful PA systems and the like. I can't think of any kind of use, whether for casual or critical listening, where this receiver would be well-applied.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR636 7.2-Ch Dolby Atmos Ready Network A/V Receiver w/ HDMI 2.0
review_headline: Powerful receiver at at great price!
review_body:
I had this item on my Amazon wish list for over 6 months because I wanted to experience Dolby Atmos and was looking to upgrade from my old Pioneer 5.1 system. Finally, I received this unit as a Christmas gift from my wife with the Onkyo height speakers. This unit does not disappoint in delivering surround sound and by that I mean any of the old formats and the new. I had the opportunity to listen to Expendables 3 and Transformers Age of Extinction in Dolby Atmos and was totally blown away by the directional placement of the Atmos sound.

The only reason I did not give this receiver a 5 star rating was because the setup was not as easy as advertised. When I first turned the unit on, the initialization process did not go as smoothly as I liked. Once I had all my ducks in a row, I restarted the unit, hooked up the calibration microphone and everything proceeded without a hitch. Depending on your internet connection, the Dolby Atmos and any other updates took approximately 20 minutes.

Don't hesitate to buy this unit. It plays loud and will have your house rattling in glorious surround sound. I am not professional enough to tell you how well the 4K upscaling worked but the picture quality on my LG 4k TV was excellent. I don't know if that was a function of my new receiver, the TV, or both.

product_title: Mount-It! LCD Tilt Swivel Under Cabinet Mount
review_body:
This bracket is extremely sturdy and includes a catch which holds the folded TV in place. I installed a 20" TV under a kitchen cabinet using this bracket. The bracket was easy to install and the VESA bracket (for attachment of the TV) removes from the mounting bracket for easy installation. Then the VESA bracket and attached TV are attached to the main bracket by way of a hook and 2 screws (very easy). The VESA part of this bracket is able to be adjusted up or down so the TV is in the ideal place for watching TV then folding up and out of the way.

When the TV is folded under the cabinet, it latches and holds. To release and lower it, press upward on the TV and the catch releases --- although it has occasionally refused to release. In that instance, a flip of the catch easily releases the TV. All in all, this is a sturdy and reliable way to have your TV accessible and yet easy to stow away under a cabinet for more open space.

Note: the hanging bracket to which the TV attaches is 11+ inches long so one would have to be sure there was adequate room under cabinet to lower the TV and swing it back under the cabinet (H and D). My cabinet is 15" deep and 18" above the countertop and the depth of the TV is 11.3" so there was no problem. It seems it would work under a 12" D cabinet with careful measurement and placement.

product_title: Polk Audio Omni S2 Compact Wireless Wi-Fi Music Streaming Speaker with Play-Fi
review_body:
This review may sound a bit biased, but it is only because I have been a long-time fan of Polk speakers. Polk produces high quality speakers that all seem to have that certain "Polk sound" to them. I don't know how they do it, but you can always tell when you're listening to a Polk speaker system. Maybe it's the creamy mids, the crisp but not brittle highs, or the tight, yet not over-exaggerated bass response.

The Polk Omni S2 wireless speaker is all of the above when it comes to how it sounds. Even for a such a small speaker, the sound is full and room filling. This little speaker gets LOUD without distorting or sounding "woofy". No, it won't rattle the plates off the walls, but it will sound like a speaker system much larger than it is.

Setup was fast and easy. The speaker is controlled through a smartphone app, which is also is easy to navigate and use.

The interchangeable speaker grilles ares easy to snap on and off. The included white grille is a nice way to blend the speaker in with your surroundings if black is too intrusive looking.

This speaker can be oriented either vertically or horizontally. This makes finding the perfect place to set it so much easier.

There are a few ways this product could be improved though:

-- I would like to see Polk add a control program for PC control, instead of just smartphone control.

-- Add a 5 GHz band to the WiFi system. While most people can use 2.4 GHz without problem, some of us suffer from interference with nearby wireless devices such as wireless CCTV systems that disrupt or even completely block 2.4 GHz connectivity. Since nearly all modern routers include the 5 GHz band, it would be smart to have this as a connectivity option; even though 5 GHz has reduced range, it is better than no connectivity at all due to an overused and oftentimes abused 2.4 GHz spectrum.

The thunderbolt transfer speed is faster than USB 3.0 but USB 3.0 is still a lot faster than USB 2.0.  Transferring large files has become more bearable.  My MBA processor is fast enough for my needs.  The only bottleneck is the USB 2.0 ports and the price of thunderbolt.  I only wish it came with dual USB 3.0 ports.  This is a wonderful product for extending the life of our aging Macbook Airs.  I highly recommend the Kanex KTU20 to anyone who is looking to do the same thing.

product_title: Antennas Direct C2-V-CJM ClearStream 2-V Long Range UHF/VHF Indoor/Outdoor DTV Antenna with 20-Inch Mount
review_body:
I'm done with Cable TV. My cable bill this month jumped to $167 for cable, internet and (useless) phone service. Evidently, the super-duper special deal they gave me 2 years ago expired, so the bill went up $48. I expressed my displeasure with their sales people and tried to negotiate a lower price deal, but they turned me down flat.

After hanging up, I unplugged the Cable-DVR box, put it in the car and drove directly to the local service center and handed it to them. Enough! The Internet (and Roku) is my friend now. I'll save $90 per month off my bill.

Later, I thought, \\"hey, what about the Giants games and local news?\\" I knew that I needed an over-the-air (OTA) antenna. Indoor antennas work lousy, so I bought the Antennas Direct C2V outdoor (high reviews). Then, I got a bucket, some concrete, and PVC pipes and built a stand and mast for my patio. Total cost (including the antenna): $125.

Wahoo! I now get 31 HD digital channels (most in English) including ABC, CBS, NBC, PBS, FOX, etc. The picture quality is actually better than cable because the OTA signal is not compressed. The display looks more like a Blu-Ray movie playing than TV. Yep, I don't have 150 channels, but at least when there's nothing on the channels I have, it FREE!

TIP: Go to http://www.antennaweb.org/Address.aspx Plug in your zip code and you'll receive a detailed map of EXACTLY where your TV broadcast towers are located! For example, my towers are 32 miles away at a 203 degree compass heading from my location. Point your antenna at your towers, it's that simple to get great OTA reception.

product_title: Soundfreaq Pocket Kick Wireless Bluetooth Portable Speaker and Speakerphone
review_body:
I'm very happy with my purchase, but this isn't a great speaker for the sound quality vs price. There are very few speaker options out there that offer no compromises and the Soundfreaq Pocket Kick isn't one of them.

One of my go-to test tracks for any speaker or headset is Investigation from the Perfect Dark Original Soundtrack. This particular track has some intense lows and surprising bass. Its one of the standards I've come to use when testing a Bluetooth speaker and the Soundfreaq Pocket Kick fails that test with heavy distortion no matter what the source. Remember that the quality of Bluetooth transmitter you're using will drastically impact performance. You'll get different results from say like a $10 phone compared to a $400 one... That said, the speaker of this size deals out real impressive mids with little distortion on highs, but distortion is there when pushing the volume to the max.

The perfect volume is about 75% source (Laptop/Phone) and 80% sink (speaker). While its not the loudest it can get, most audio plays comfortably at this level without much distortion. If you use an equalizer, you can reduce the presence of the lowend of the spectrum to reduce distortion on bass-heavy/low music.

This sacrifice in sound quality brings out some pretty great qualities you'll really enjoy. What you may lack in low end or quality, you greatly make up in qualities like portability and battery life. The manufacturer-stated 10 hours is fantastic for a speaker this size, its metal grills feel great in the hand, and it's thin ice-cream sandwich-like design puts the "pocket" in Pocket Kick. Better speakers, comparable speakers, or even lesser speakers often take awkward, impractical, and large shapes that hinder portability. Shapes like cylinders and triangular prisms. Sure something like an Oontz Angle or Ultimate Ears Mini Boom might sound better, but they lack things like a wrist strap or fitting comfortably in a pocket thatwould make that "portable speaker" really portable.

My favorite part is able to slip this into my back pocket just like a wallet and forget that its there. Beats the pants off any cell phone speaker. There are many speakers that you can buy for $90 that are much better with sound quality, but few are this small, this portable, and still have fantastic battery life and bluetooth range. However the speaker isn't deserving of 5 stars on account that it's sound quality is only "okay" and that its a little on the expensive side when you consider quality of sound per the dollar.

review_headline: Great bass, OK mids and highs, a good overall value for the money.  My favorite in-ear headphones so far.
review_body:
I previously purchased the JVC HA-FX101B and was very happy with them, but lost them. These headphones are very similar, but have the inline controls (which I really like).

I've been frustrated in my search for a great headphone set. I prefer the sound and comfort of in-ear headphones, which you generally can't try in the store for hygiene reasons. The reviews online are difficult to interpret because tastes are so different. And even if you can find someone who likes the same kind of sound you do, unless they listen to the same kind of music their opinion may not apply. Sigh- I mention all this because I like a wide range of music, but mostly bass heavy music including R&B and hip hop. I seek an all around good sound, but if I have to sacrifice something, it won't be bass.

The bass in these is fantastic- substantially better than even the few much more expensive sets I have tried. I also went to best buy and bought the Sony MDRXB50AP for $60 to try them, figuring they were better because they were more expensive and had good reviews. The treble and mids were noticeably better, but the bass was nowhere near as good as either the HA-FX101B or the HAFR201B in my opinion. I returned the Sonys.

If I could find a in-ear headphone that had the bass of the HAFR201B with the mids at least as good as those on the Sony I tried, I'd buy them. It seems you have to settle in some regard. With that being said, the mids and treble on this HAFR201B aren't bad- they're just not as impressive as some other sets. When I listened to the soundtrack for the movie Interstellar, the mids and highs were noticeably muted from the cinema experience and compared to the sony set.

I use the inline controls with my android tablet and am satisfied- they work fine with google play music, for example.

Overall, for the money, you'll be hard pressed to beat the performance of this set. If you listen to bass heavy music, you'll reallylike this set. If you don't, you may not love them, but you'll probably still think they're pretty good for the money.

review_headline: An amazing little radio for the price.
review_body: This is an amazing little radio for the price.  You have to adjust your expectations for the price somewhat but even after that it greatly outperforms the much more expensive but now worn out Grundig Mini World 100 it is replacing. Sensitivity is good to great on both AM and SW.  I was able to tune very respectable AM DX sitting in my easy chair with just the internal antenna.  Selectivity is an issue but that is to be expected in a radio of this class.  The SW performance is equally good.  Using just the attached whip, I was able to get respectable results.  FM is a problem.  It overloads easily and takes some fiddling with the whip to separate out lower powered local stations.  The audio from the built in speaker is tinny but readable.  But, plug in a pair of earbuds and this little guy shines.  Bottom line, this little guy offers a lot of bang for the buck and has no annoying features or habits.  If you need something to throw in the suitcase or for that matter, a hot little AM pocket receiver to pull in news from the boondocks this is it.  You would have to spend a lot more money to get better performance.

product_title: Polk Audio RTI A3 Bookshelf Speakers
review_headline: Too bright, not ideal for music listening in smaller space
review_body:
Pros: Beautiful, nice materials, good bass extension for bookshelf speakers, a mostly accurate sound.

Cons: Overemphasized highs make these speakers suitable more for home theater setups than for listening to music.

I thought these beautiful Polk speakers would be that perfect first set of nice speakers that you invest in and use for years down the road. I decided to try these out due to Amazon's great return policy, and I am sad to say the listening experience confirms the negative reviews and existing frequency measurement data that I chose to ignore in order to give these speakers a chance. These are way too bright to be chosen over other speakers in its price range as far as listening to music goes. Starting at about 9khz and beyond, the volume measures at 3db to 5db more than the rest of the covered range. So if you are convinced you need to like these speakers, you will regard them as extremely clear and detailed, but objectively speaking the highs are just overemphasized if you are using these at a close or medium distance. There is just too much airiness and metallic buzz to everything. High hats take the front stage, and voices resonate with high pitched sounds in a distracting way. The midrange, while accurate sounding, sounds recessed and makes everything sound colder and less expressive than is ideal.

Unfortunately for audio equipment, people tend not to be very objective, and will give a 5 star rating to whatever they purchase as long as it doesn't have any glaring flaws or stop functioning correctly. I accidentally ordered two sets of speakers before this set: The Wharfedale Diamond 10.1 and the Monitor BX2. Between those two, the Wharfedale Diamond 10.1 sounded the most balanced, and very easy to listen to and enjoyable for music while not lacking treble extension, although they have less bass extension compared to the Monitors and Polks. Unlucky for me one side had a defect in the tweeter which caused buzz, so I hadto return them, and before I could order them again, I noticed these Polks were on sale for $308, and that's how I came to compare these 3 sets. I tried the Monster BX2 because I had read a review saying they were better than the Diamond 10.1, but I did not agree, as they sounded less warm and kind of on the bright side, although not as bright as the Polks.

There are lots of reasons why people may have a radically different opinion of these speakers, although I would say you cannot deny that the highs are very emphasized, since they can be objectively measured against the ideal of a flat frequency response curve. For example, perhaps someone might use these in a much larger room where the acoustics make it beneficial to have more highs. Or maybe some people really do prefer this bright sound. After all, as we get older our hearing range can whittle down all the way to 12khz at the high end, and audio perception is highly subjective in the first place. Though usually I think it's more just cognitive dissonance and not wanting to imagine they spent $400 on something that is not the best choice. I have asked on an audiophile forum whether my experience with these was unique, and other people have confirmed that these are indeed super bright speakers and that they are intended for home theater moreso than for music. I would urge everyone to take 5 star reviews of most audio products with a grain of salt, and pay more attention to the other reviews to see if there is some kind of common complaint.
