I tried to contact AKG by Harmon support through email to ask for a repair estimate, which I am willing to pay for because I spent a lot of money for this and I want to keep using it, but they have not yet replied.  I am disappointed that I purchased this product based on the name and reputation of their brand, and this product doesn't live up to its namesake.  For this much money, I expected that this product would have lasted longer, much longer than it did.  My recommendation is if you are going to spend a lot of money on a set of cans which you expect to own for at least a decade or two, buy a product made mostly of metal and leather. product_title: M-DISC 25GB Blu-ray Media, Inkjet Printable - 15 Disc Cake Box
review_body:
These discs work fine, but though there is 25GB capacity, you can't realistically get that unfortunately. I tried (and wasted) several recordings at and around 23-25GB and they all failed... I thought I had a bad drive or bad discs... then I noticed the actual capacity of a new and empty disc in explorer at 23.3GB. So I lowered my data to 21GB and it worked fine. Through several more recordings, I so far have not had a failure if I keep the data under 23GB. I haven't yet researched why this is, because there is only a small file on each new disc that is miniscule, so not sure why I can't get 25GB or closer to it, but that's my experience. I have an LG BE14NU40 burner. Otherwise the discs work great.

The inkjet writeable ones are best if you want to label... evidently writing on a regular disc could eventually leach ink on the reflective surface with time and render your disc corrupt. If you don't have the inkjet ones, you can write on the small "inside circle" where no data is if you need to label it with anything, but write small! : ) Otherwise get the inkjet writeable ones that have an extra layer for labeling.

I have lost 2 hard drives within a week before... losing my primary data and backup data... so backups with HDs is not the most dependable method of backup! Flash drives, Hard drives, they all will fail. And so will these... eventually. But it does provide a restoral point and keeping the important data on at least two seperate media at any point in time will allow a restoral if one fails. If interested in a reliable archival system, there are several articles on the net to get an idea of what works for you. Some ideas are too cumbersome to keep up with. I am now using a dual HDD system for immediate backups, and these discs for archiving long term. I store these at a different location, for extra security. This is for stuff I just absolutely don't want to lose, i.e. videos of the kids, pictures, etc... When technology changes, I can always move to it at any time.

For now, this is best for my purpose. They work great.

product_title: Sony SRSX5 Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Speaker System
review_headline: WOW. Packs a punch in the sound department.
review_body:
Wow. This little speaker packs a mighty sound. I'm very impressed with it. I wanted something that was bluetooth so I could listen to the music from my iphone 6 while at home, and to be able to keep the phone close to me at the same time. In other words, I didn't want to have to plug it in and then have to get it if the phone rang. Right now my phone and I are about 20 feet away from the speaker and it sounds great.
After I ordered this I went on to youtube and saw that someone posted a comparison between this unit and a Bose one. He played a jazz song to compare the sound of each unit. I was disappointed because the Sony sounded like it had too much treble, and the BOSE one sounded rich with much better sound. Please, please please, if you go to youtube and listen to that review, disregard it. It's so not accurate. This Sony SRSX5 sounds way better then the comparison on youtube.
First of all, it has a great balance of bass and treble. Neither one seems to be overbearing. It has an overall full sound. Also plays loud. I haven't even pushed the volume up all the way and it's plenty loud for my small one floor home. Earlier today, I just left the unit on, with the volume up a little high. A little while later, as I was sitting at my computer desk, I decided to listen to some music and just put my music on from my iphone. I didn't have to go across the room to turn the unit on because I had already left it on. I adjusted the volume from my iphone.
Some people say that if you unplug it you'll lose some volume, but I haven't tested that yet. I'm really not interested in using it without the plug. I just wanted a good sounding speaker to use at home that I could also pair with my phone via bluetooth.
It's also a very basic setup. I turned the bluetooth setting on my phone on, and in a few seconds it recognized the Sony SRSX5. Once it recognized it I was able to start playing music. Easy as that.
The AUX and USB is in the back next tothe power plug and easy enough to figure out how to use them if I ever need to.

If you want a small speaker system that has really good sound, then I highly recommend this.

review_headline: No Option to Use Own 3.5mm Cord, Yet Still a Fantastic, Easy Use Portable BT Receiver
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:2372b5b7ff0b7ef27baaf6a34a30a69e]]UPDATE INFORMATION - Thanks to a couple questions by a interested consumer, I shall add a few things:

a) Yes, it does auto-pair when turned on, and very quickly too.

b) No, it does not play while charging; however, most audio devices tend not to play while charging due to the audio feedback one gets from the charging electromagnetic field, especially on unshielded AUX ports (I had a 7\\" Y88X Tablet that was ear-rending while charging with 3.5mm headsets plugged in).

c) Empty Space White Noise/Hissing when no Audio signal is present - the noise itself is fairly inescapable with all budget gear. Also the AUX In jack/Receiving Speaker will have an impact. Zero \\"empty space\\" noise on an expensive Anker speaker using this, yet my water speakers (love them, but they are not faboo quality) hiss away like the good old analog days when no audio is being piped through. But then they do that with any audio, not just this receiver. :P

d) One last note to highlight - this does not have an AUX Out receptacle port. Only the AUX Out cord. For instance, I couldn't use this with a trio-set of computer speakers that don't have an AUX In receptacle, just the 3.5mm cord plugin itself.

---

I have a pair of 3.5mm Only speakers that I absolutely adore... and have wished they were indeed Bluetooth capable. I had given away the previous sets of receivers I had, never thinking I would be stuck in a situation where I would actually have non-Bluetooth speakers. :P

However, Veetop to the rescue, and I have to say, out of the prior sets I have examined, this one is the most self-contained and portable unit to date with it's excellent integrated 3.5mm cable. Now this does mean you can't use your own, possible far longer cord if needed, and this ought to be a consideration in your own potential application. However, if you are looking for a truly portable option with it's great playtime of 12 hours and auto-shutoff after 5 minutes, I wouldn't hesitate a moment in recommending VEETOP.

In fact, I have to chuckle. It has a relatively thick little instruction book, which isn't a bad thing... yet I didn't even glance at the book. I powered the unit on, it flashed red/blue, I paired it with my tablet, plugged in the unit into my water jet speakers, hit play, and BLAMMO! Total coolness.

product_title: Koss Pro4S Full Size Studio Headphones, Black with Silver Trim
review_body:
These Koss Pro4S Full-Size Studio Headphones really do the job! Although designed for studio use, I have been using them to listen to computer audio-and usually spoken word rather than music. That may be a waste of the quality that these things are built with but that's what I needed them for.

I have some hearing loss. Having used a variety of cheaper headsets for listening to computer audio, I've found most to be either cheaply made or to have unsatisfactory sound. Plus, many irritate my ears, especially ear buds. Now that I'm taking some online college courses, I've had real problems hearing much of the lecture audio and thought I'd try the Koss headset to see if it would work better. I was pleasantly surprised: the headset is sturdy and well-made. No more puny wires that break or uncomfortable earbuds . . these headphones are the real deal! I wish the coiled cable was a little longer, but it's adequate for most needs. Because the double-ended cord unplugs and plugs in with ease-and is the standard size, I suspect I can purchase a longer cord if I choose. It would be perfect if there were a separate volume control on the headphones themselves: instead, all sound control must come from the computer settings. The ear cups are very comfortable and the unit folds nicely to fit into the included hard case for travel. I almost feel guilty using them for what I do . . .they are designed for a more high-end use.

My suggestion would be that if you are using the Koss headphones simply for computer work, you are likely wasting money: other units might work as well and at a cheaper price. However, for music. these are excellent!! Koss has a great reputation for a reason . . they've provided excellence for years and have only gotten better!

review_headline: Not really getting what you pay for
review_body:
So I'm a bluetooth kind of person and I have a bunch of speakers and a few headsets I've used in the past.

The good thing about the headset is that its very comfortable over the head and you can lay back on your head without any hard pieces bothering you. It plays music pretty clearly too. Fits nicely in the ears and the controls are easy to reach. The controls are only 2 buttons for forwarding and rewinding and a switch type button to put volume up and down and press it in to pause/play or hold it to turn on/off or hold it longer to pair the device. The headset itself feels sturdy and well made. It also has a cool magnet to clip them together.

Now the things I don't like about this are mainly the call quality first and foremost. I used to have a very cheap $20 bluetooth headphones that had much better call quality through my network of MetroPCS with full bars but even better with Skype. With skype I literally felt like the person was in the room with how clear my old headset was. This headset falls very short of that with the skype quality almost as good as the network quality on my old headset. The network quality is barely understandable and you'll be saying "What?" to every other sentence. One more thing is that when you use the magnets to clip around your neck it feels weird because of the location of the cable connecting the headsets together. If you have a thick neck I don't recommend it.

Overall 3/5 stars. It does the job but for the price I would have thought it would have been better. Not really worth the price in my opinion.

product_title: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)
review_headline: Tough on the Outside but Soft and Gentle on the Inside
review_body: the following review can also be found here:http://www.head-fi.org/products/brainwavz-r3-dual-dynamic-driver-earphones/reviews/12069  a video review version can be found here:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=psUtd6mBQIE    Quick Summary: While these earphones have a really \\"unique\\" design to them, once you get over this, you will be rewarded with a beautifully balanced sound. I would put them on a similar tier as the very popular, and head-fi favorites Hifiman re400 and the Vsonic GR07. This is very high praise, let's find out below!    Accessories: The R3s come with a multiple ear tips of different sizes, shapes and even \\"bore/nozzle width\\"  3 pairs of Grey (medium bore) (in S,M,L)  3 pairs of black (narrower bore) (in S,M,L)  1 pair of Triple flange  1 pair of Double Flange  1 Pair of Medium Comply T400 eartips  1 ¼ adapter  1 hard carrying case (this is probably the nicest case I've ever seen, I'll probably getting a few for my other earphones)  Overall: 9/10    Design: These earphones look very interesting to say the least. They have almost a big water bottle shape to them. While they won't win any beauty contests, but in this case its more substance (sound) >style. The size of the housing is conducive to how big and spacious this earphone sounds.  Overall: 5/10 (I did get a few weird looks when walking around  the mall, and around town with them, they are quite big as well)    Build quality: These guys I feel have set the bar for build quality for even many full size headphones out there. It's certainly, the \\"Hummer\\" for earphones. The earpieces are fully made of metal, which makes me feel that they would win a war even against a hammer.  The cables is very thick and rugged, I think its on par or even exceeds some full size headphones in this category. Lastly, it has an big and overbuilt 45 degree jack, one that looks like the ones you see with TV cables. I feel headphone manufactures should really take a look at the Brainwavz R3 when building their cables.  These earphones will definitely last a while.  Overall: 10/10 (I feel the cable is a bit too thick and heavy at times for an earphone, however in this case I would say its better being overbuilt >underbuilt).    Comfort: These edges of the R3s are all rounded, but bottom line is that their still very large for earphones, affecting fit (I struggled at times to get a good fit). Brainwavz attempts compensated the size by having long nozzles, which would allow for better, deeper fit. However, the nozzle used are also very wide. My ear canals did feel a bit sore after about an hour or so, however the Comply's did help with the comfort. As a result, the issues listed above may affect those with small outer ears and smaller ear canals.  Overall: 6.5/10 (If the nozzles were narrower it would help improve the comfort)    Isolation:  There are a number of vents (I count 2).  As a result the isolation is just about average. Good enough for day to day use, though not my first recommendation for hardcore commuting.  Overall: 7/10    Cable noise: These were intended to be worn cable up, as a result, almost no cable noise.  Overall: 9/10 (when using these for physical exercises, the physical weight of the cable will cause some cable noise to come through)    Sound:  The sound I think Brainwavz have a done a fantastic job. It's a sound that is a \\"jack of all trades\\" it has the right balance of bass, midrange and treble. No single part of the sound spectrum screams out for your attention, instead it opts for a more neutral balanced presentation with some added warmth to prevent them from sounding cold or lean. I think in terms of musical preferences, I think these faired better for more acoustic and live pieces, I loved listening to OSTs, and ballads with them, because of its delicate nature and its wide soundstage. I felt it delivered the atmosphere and the emotions from those specific genres of music.    Bass: the bass here is rather linear from the midbass with a mild subbass rolloff. But the bass here is just a slightly emphasized (providing a soft impact) to allow for some added warmth. Its not anemic, but the bass here may not have the impact some are seeking. The bass here is very well integrated with good control with a smooth texture.    Midrange: I think the midrange, is rather neutral and natural sounding balancing male and female vocals very well. I feel that the midrange has enough richness, that give vocals a bit more body or thickness, though a bit diffuse. The tradeoff for the extra richness in the vocals, is a bit of clarity but it allow for both male and female vocals to have a smoother quality to them. However, as a whole its still a very clear earphone and I would put it just behind the Re400 and GR07BEs.    Treble: I think the treble as a whole is relatively clean, smooth, avoiding any siblance. I feel the treble hits a plateau in the mid treble and rolls off shortly after which makes the treble sound a bit just a bit \\"blunted\\" which makes the treble have bit of dullness, and a more laid back feel. Thus, the treble lacks a bit of the excitement and a bit air in treble, that I think would allow them to sound more open, and more engaging.  The complaints I listed above are very minor, I think the treble as whole executed very well.    Soundstage: Quite big, it's an out of the head experience with great placement and separation. It's a bit diffuse sounding and I felt it had better width than depth, making the presentation more flat  sounding.    Quick comparison : I think in comparison the Brainwavz R3 is warmer and smoother sounding (and less dry sounding) than the Hifiman RE400 and it has a much bigger soundstage. The bass is smoother sounding and both have that roll off in the subbass but its less noticeable on the R3s. The midrange has more thickness and more weight than the transparent and lean RE400s. The treble is more crisp on the RE400s, and more detailed and clearer as a result. But its so much better built, there isno contest, but the housing is bigger so it be challenge to get a fit for some.    Compared to the VSONIC Gr07 BE, its has a similar width size of the soundstage with a similar sort of diffuse characteristic (so more 2 dimensional).  The subbass on the Gr07BE is definitely more emphasized than it is on the R3, as well as the midbass, making it punchier as a whole. Its more midcentric and richer with male vocals. In terms of the treble  but its much smoother so those that felt GR07 was edgy and siblant in the treble would just love the smoothness of R3, while still sounding very balanced and detailed as a whole. Those looking for a more v shaped and more exciting sound should look towards the GR07BE.    *added note* I think the Brainwavz R3 is a good alternative (sonically speaking) to the Vsonic GR07(whichever version, i have the BE) and the Hifiman re400. Especially if you need something very rugged, i mean like strong enough to survive a war in your backpack and more.    Sound: 9/10 (the treble was just a bit blunt for me) but aside from that it was a very great take on a neutral, balanced sound signature with a bit of warmth.    In conclusion, while the R3s have this ridiculously robust build and the great sound of the R3s, I feel that the design and the long, wide nozzles would be an issue for others.  It's a good and durable option at this price range as long as you can get past the design and the potential comfort issues.  Overall: 55.5/70=79.3%

product_title: VideoSecu One Pair of Side Clamping Bookshelf Speaker Mounting Bracket with Swivel and Tilt for Large Surrounding Sound Speakers MS56B 3LH
review_body:
I'm using this to secure a couple of rather large speakers that weigh about 14lbs each. This mount can definitly hold them and allow them to be adjusted. the welds on the ones I got seem secure and I've had no incidents.

The one knock on these is that for larger speakers: it gan be ungainly to mount the flat plate before the speaker--if you try you'll need two people--at least, and when backed into a corner this can be troublesome to impossible. As such, you'll have to mount the flat plate to the speaker (straps or screws) before mounting the whole assembly to the wall part of the mount. the issue comes with the connection bolt. It has a square "key" that fits into the mounting plate's slot to allow it to be tilted and turned, and to hold the both from turning when tightened. The problem arises in that the "key" on the both is so small that the both can jump when tightened, making it very hard to secure the bolt. Making a larger square "key" on the bolt that would ensure that the key is engaged even if the both moves up when securing the bolt would solve this problem, which is why it loses a star.

I'd still recommed them, however, butyou'd have to take this into consideration before getting these. If your speakers are too ungainly to mount to the completed mountand you have to mount them to the plate first, you might have some headage getting the thing cinched down.

product_title: Bluetooth Speaker, Jelly Comb Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker W LED Lantern Lamp & Flashilight Feature for Outdoor Camping & Parties
review_body:
This little speaker functions as an mp3 player, a lantern, and a Bluetooth speaker. Notice I didn't say radio. I live where FM reception is good, but I rarely get a signal from this radio. Even when I do, I can't tell what channel (no display) I'm on and there's lots of static.

The mp3 player works with a micro SD card. It was a little scary inserting it because I didn't feel a spring, but there is a spring after all. Controls work as expected, except for volume. I tried to get the sound to turn way down low, but it doesn't turn as low as I'd like before muting. Oh well.

Bluetooth speaker is good for personal use. No one expects a lantern to have high end audio, but the sound is clear and the volume good enough to satisfy most casual users. On the other hand, phone call quality is extremely poor. The caller is far too soft, and they can't hear me, either.

Pairing is easy, reconnection is automatic, and the range is good. The stern female voice telling me Bluetooth is pairing is accented. I'm used to foreign accents on my devices. I usually find them pleasant, but this one is particularly strong and grating. If I didn't understand English, I'd think she was scolding me. It needs a sweeter voice.

The speaker unfolds into a lantern with two brightness settings. For its small size, it puts out a lot of light. My daughter actually complained about how bright it was when I brought it to her room at night, and that was on the low setting. I don't think it's as bright as she claimed, but it is bright enough for me to find my way in the dark. I could read by it if I had to.

This combination of lantern/mp3 player/Bluetooth speaker makes it ideal for camping and other outdoor activities.

This product was provided for review by Jelly Comb Corp.

The connectors, knobs, buttons and finish is of good quality and about average for speakers in this price point. I have the VM Audio in-wall speakers which are fantastic for the price in my living room 5.1 sound system. I’m installing more of them in my basement game room and now have these towers in my home office. review_body: Well, the leaf was too small. The card had been assigned to me from an early transaction during which I had agreed to TAKE THE CARD BUT NOT TO USE IT. Which I didn't on that occasion. I actually lashed the tiny 15 db preamp to a bigger winegard Flat Wave wall antenna exactly like the Mohu Leaf but bigger.  That antenna with the Mohu pre-amp produced far better results.  I bought the Winegard at Home Depot a few weeks earlier.  I railed at the reps at Amazon about mis-representing which card I was to use until it was too late to change it.  I considered stiffing the card company, which, incidentally, had an even worse, shrewish customer service rep by phone.  In the end I paid the half price figure to the card while privately vowing to not let this happen again. Amazon's Synchronicity card has nothing but bad will from me and I will remember.  I am using the 15 db preamp to power an old Radio Shack dish-shaped antenna that has its own pre-amp.  I added the Mohu preamp about ten feet of coax from the dish antenna itself and it brings in a lot. But u constantly have to adjust it when the weather changes.  I'm going to try removing the Radio Shack pre-amp and just go with the Mohu amp and see how that works.  Sometimes preamps cause more problems than they solve.

product_title: Universal Remote Control MX-450 Custom Programmable Remote Control with On-Screen Macro Editing.
review_body:
My unit was used, but like-new as described. Delivery was reasonably fast (4 business days).

The MX-450 remote is a tough item to program using the manual programming methods, but it does the job after you spend a lot of time researching and learning how to program it.
The manufacturer provides almost no useful detail on how to program this remote control.

RF control worked with my old $40 RF20, 6-output RF reciever!!

This RF reciever is a lot less expensive than buying the $200 special RF reciever! And you get a extra remote in the bargain (although the RF20 macro capability is a bit limited and its basic programming mode requires wasted time guessing through many possible codes from each munaufacturer, but the RF20 can learn from other remotes if you have a lot of spare time to program each key separately)

One great thing about this MX-450 controller was that the "basic programming mode" worked super. I just pointed at the devices in my cabinet (amplifier, cable box, Blueray with Netflix, CD player, and even a new 65" Samsung Smart TV) and it guessed the correct code for my device on the first try. No trying 10 different codes per device. This is nt learning fomr the remote, but identifying my devices!

This does not get you those valuable Macros, but it does get you a simgle remote that does almost everything 6 other remotes can do. The whole process took me less than 10 minutes for 5 devices.

There is little documentation for programming macors, so you need to spend a lot of time searching for programming assistance.
Universal will not provide the PC programming to end customers, only to their dealers.
Some of the Amazon prior reviews are very helpful.

I suppose the manufacturers dealers want customers to rely on them for programming, so they make DIY macro program as difficult as possible. Fortunately, the device is well designed, so you can still do a good job as a project after some research.

This is sad that this company provide so little support to this MX-450 product, since this could be a great consumer product if it had a freindly software package included.
It could be the best controller on the DIY consumer market with a good software package, even though it is a several year old design.

product_title: Brainwavz HM5 Velor Memory Foam Replacements Earpads for Over The Ear Headphones
review_headline: Replacement Pads to be Considered by All
review_body:
Pros: Comfort, Appreciable SQ Change
Cons: Nope
The HM5 Velours are quite simply, an uber-comfortable pad for HM5/Shure/Beyer/ATH/(most large circumaural headphones). I was offered a review sample from Brainwavz and have the following to say regarding these and their stock counterparts:

1. Comfort: Both the pleather and velour pads are exceptionally comfortable. The memory foam is quite soft and pliable and distributes weight very well. Even though the Brainwavz HM5 is a bit of a clamper, the lightweight and soft design of the pads alleviates most of the discomfort making these great for long listening sessions.

2. Sound:
Velours: Compared to the pleathers, the sound is a touch more neutral. This may be a weird statement as I consider the HM5 a pretty neutral can as is. Here's the reasoning: A little bass impact is lost coming from the stock pad, but that's to be expected as velour is gonna be more porous than pleather. On the Snarky Puppy and Amy Winehouse tunes, the kick drum loses a little slam, but certainly nothing drastic enough to cause any dislike or feeling of bass lack. It also bears mentioning in the same way, the velours can take a little more volume to achieve the same levels as the pleathers. Once again, a little more sound leak is the culprit.
Pleathers: As aforementioned, the most noticeable difference coming from velours to pleathers is bass quantity and sound leak. Pleathers seal a little better and therefore don't have to volume up as much, and retain a little more bass impact. Upon second listening, I also venture the idea that the pleathers have a slightly smaller soundstage than the velours. Maybe for the same reasons?

3. Adaptability: As you can see in these pads' review section title, they fit a ton of over-ear headphones. Even those that don't natively have the same cup shape as the HM5 (i.e. HE500, DT880, MDR V6, even Grados!) are being fitted all over head-fi with mixed results. The onlyvariation I'm able to try is on the Sony MDR 7506. The fit is a little unorthodox, but they will stay on. The velours don't play as nicely as the pleathers, which add a little bass impact and open the soundstage since the HM5 pads put more space between the ear and the driver. Maybe when I grow to be a bit more adventurous in my DIYing, I'll try adapting them to my HE500s.

review_body:
Great quality subwoofer, I was deciding between this and the Polk PSW10. I got lucky and was able to look and hear both of them at my local Bestbuy before I purchased. The main reasons I went with this unit over the Polk are below:

1. The Sony is smaller than the Polk, so it takes up less space in my living room. I also think it looks a little better.
2. The Sony has better specs on paper, 28-200hz, vs 35-200hz for the Polk. In theory, the bass should get 7hz lower on the Sony.
3. The quality of the materials is better on the Sony, the plastic and housing is much better made.
4. The actual subwoofer driver is made of a higher quality rubber on the Sony instead of foam on the Polk, it feels better quality and I would image it lasting longer and taking a heavier beating over time.
5. The Sony has 115w and the Polk has 100w. So the Sony is slightly more powerful.
6. The same Polk has been on the market for at least 8 years, most likely using the same technology from 8 years ago which is why they can sell it so cheap would be my guess. This Sony is a fairly new offering, I have to believe technology has come a long way in 8 years and the Sony probably is more up to date.

I have been very happy with my purchase so far, our living room is average size, maybe 300sqft. The subwoofer fills the room with bass very well.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR636 7.2-Ch Dolby Atmos Ready Network A/V Receiver w/ HDMI 2.0
review_body:
First off, I want to make it clear the reason I am giving this a one star rating is due to the lack of supported video that this unit claims to handle.

I purchased this AVR for the sole fact of being able to output a 4k @ 60hz signal with 4:4:4 Chroma, which can be handled with HDMI 2.0 -- yet this AVR can NOT do that, merely only 4k @ 30hz at 4:2:0. Why does that matter? Well when you buy a top end 4k TV and other electronics, you want your AVR to handle the video quality.

I contacted Onkyo support and they confirmed it would handle 4k @ 60hz, and I ensured that I asked "up-scaling or pass-through?" and I was told "both!" I then went to Best Buy (should have known better) and asked there, and was told the same thing. About 20 hours of messing around and posting online, I find that this does NOT upscale but merely pass-through the 4k @ 60hz signal.

Prior I had the 5007 model, which was their top of the line model a few years back, but is not obsolete because it can not handle anything past HDMI 1.3. Instead of buying the 3030 model, I opted for a less expensive solution that could fit my needs, but instead does not.

In the end, if you want to use this AVR, you are limited to 30hz, which looks good on movies, but fast action shows, sports, etc., looks horrible -- not to mention you will get signal failure when you try and watch movie channels through this AVR, such as HBO, it will say on your TV "can not find signal" if you have a 4k with up-scaling.

The rest of the features are meaningless to this review as the AVR has to be returned.

If you have a low-mid end 4k TV or nice 1080p and not looking to use the upscale to 60hz, this may be a good receiver, but otherwise stay away.

product_title: USBCELL MXAA02 AA Rechargable Battery - 2 Cell Pack
review_headline: Not so sure how safe these are for an older computer
review_body:
I dont know if the rumors are true, but the facts in my case... I have an ASUS M3N72-D with Phenom II 940 that has been happily overclocked to 3300MHz on air cooling for the past two years. Before that I ran it at factory 3.0gig speed with no issues. I know this computer is getting up there in age, but with an SSD, fast graphics card and an overclock has been and continues to be an excellent machine for what I do. Unless I plug one of these batteries in and try to do anything intensive.... Twice the computer has crashed hard enough to dump all bios settings back to factory thus destroying my overclock settings and both times, one of these was plugged in to it. I was able to duplicate this with prime95 running. Plug in one of these and less than 10 minutes later its locked up hardcore. Prime95 will run for days without this plugged in. So there is something to this. They get quite hot and I am sure these are drawing max current and my old motherboard is probably getting tired of supplying it.

ALSO, I have an older version of this same type of battery from a different supplier that oddly doesn't cause this. I for one wont use any more USB batteries in my computer, but will only plug them into external/phone USB chargers just to be safe.

No case or bag was included with the speaker.  This speaker works equally well on its feet and when lay back with speakers aiming up improving low response in some situations.    Sound is very competitive or better then the Bose SoundLink Mini Speaker, depending on the source music being played. review_headline: Great Product with some design issues
review_body:
The product is as described.

Pro: Great price and well built. Works well. More accessories included than expected (HDMI cable, torpedo level and level built into mount itself). Well packed.

Cons: Very heavy. The mount weighs at least twice the weight of the TV (40" LED). The locking mechanism for the vertical tilt isn't the most easy to use or accessible. review_headline: Nice to have if you want to install a new cartridge.
review_body:
Not much to say. It is a headshell that fits on certain Audio Technica turntables (and maybe some other brands).

The Audio-Technica turntables come with a cheap AT95 cartridge which you can buy for $35. So, that's a $35 cartridge on a turntable that costs between $250 and $350. You can upgrade the sound by simply replacing the needle with a higher quality needle like the ATN95S, which costs about $125.

But, if you are going to spend that much on a new needle, you might as well get a better cartridge. Unfortunately, Audio-Technica does not give you much info on how to install the new cartridge, such as what the position of the needle should be. So, my solution was to buy the new headshell, and install the new cartridge on it. I could then use the old headshell/cartridge that came with the turntable as a guide for correct placement.

I did this, and my turntable now sounds so much better, especially on the low end and with complex music.

But...I didn't really put on a new cartridge. I put on an old cartridge from my old Dual turntable that stopped working.

product_title: CyberPower EC350G Ecologic 350VA/255-Watts Energy Efficient Desktop UPS
review_headline: Great UPS. ECO outlets are particularly useful for some cases
review_body:
It works well as advertise. Solid construction, bright LED with useful information, supporting software you can download from web is well implemented and useful.

ECO outlets were especially useful to me. I have one particular LCD monitor which has an adapter that keeps making very annoying fade-buzzing sound when monitor is under stand-by mode (no buzzing when monitor is fully powered or adapter plug is off). Adapter itself works well, but this buzzing sound keeps getting on my nerve.

So instead of spending $35 for replacement adapter for the monitor (which I am not even sure it will resolve my issue), I decided to get this UPS with an assumption that if ECO outlets completely cuts power off when computer is off, then I don't have to keep plugging monitor power cable off every time I am done with my work - and yes it works!

You can configure ECO mode, so that if you don't need this functionality, you can change mode and use outlet as normal surge-protected outlets. Just keep in mind, in order to use ECO mode properly, you need to connect supplied USB cable from UPS to your PC so that when PC is powered, UPS will be notified and turn power on to ECO outlets.

I have been using multiple CyberPower UPS in my home, and none of them failed me so far (have 4 of them with all different max capacity)

review_headline: DirecTV charges $25 for this exact remote and it fixed my receiver
review_body:
I have an ancient model D12 DirecTV receiver that was starting to act up. I had to press the remote keys hard to make the receiver pay attention. Sometimes, the remote acted dead - the lights on the Mode switch wouldn't blink when the buttons were pressed - sometimes. The volume, however, directly controls the TV and it worked fine. Batteries were changed a couple of times.

In addition, the receiver acted like it was hanging. General weirdness.

I ordered this RC66 remote (exactly like the one that I already have) because the lights were not blinking on the old one. When I installed the two included batteries and tried it out, it worked fine with slight button push pressure. The receiver was still acting up so I just rebooted it - powered off/on. Now, everything is working fine.

The only thing I can figure, is that the old remote was stuttering and causing the receiver to get confused.

In any event, this remote works perfectly. You will want to search for the remote codes that your tv uses so that you can program the remote. The DirecTV site has the instructions for programming it.

Works fine. Price right. DirecTV charges $25 for this exact remote. You know that at this price, you really, really should have a spare - order two.

I gave it five stars even though the two included batteries failed after exactly two days.

product_title: FiiO X1 High Resolution Lossless Music Player
review_body:
Until my first experience with X5, a little over half a year ago, I used to refer to all dedicated audio players as "mp3" players. It wasn't my ignorance but rather a misunderstanding where I thought that I should focus more on higher bit rate songs and better headphones, and any "mp3" player or smartphone will play audio files just fine. Introduction to X5 changed all that and opened up my eyes to a world of music without being interrupted by emails, txt, or app updates, a world where audio player is not a cheap clip on gadget on my armband, a world where I ended up "rediscovering my headphones, all over again". X5 is great as a portable DAP, but in some cases I found it to be a little too bulky/heavy. In search for other quality audio players, I acquired some other DAPs, but nothing was able to replace the ease of navigation with a scrolling wheel. Now with introduction of X1, I can rejoice with a new pocket friendly super portable DAP that sounds as good as it looks, retains its scrolling wheel design, and cost a fraction of its big brother's price tag. But don't make a mistake thinking X1 is a cheaper replacement of X5. They can both coexist in a perfect harmony with their trade-offs in size versus sound quality. Others can think of X1 as a stepping stone for when you are ready to graduate from a basic mp3 player and want to get a taste of audiophile world - a taste that will whet your appetite for the next future upgrade when you are ready. Whatever your journey is, I think a lot of the people going to enjoy this little new gem from FiiO. Without further due, here is what I found while testing this fine little DAP.

My review unit arrived in a package similar to the latest E10k/E11k boxes resembling a size of double CD case. Inside, X1 was dressed in all black silicon skin with one screen protector already applied and two additional ones available for backup. USB to micro-usb cable also was included as part of accessory package. Since this is a review unit, I'm sure the final production package will probably going to have more accessories included. Silicon skin is definitely great for a basic scratch and minimal drop protection, but I wish it would have been gray like the one that comes with X5 since you can't see X1 charging light underneath of solid black. I'm sure with soon to be available bonus accessories, you will be able to get another skin color. But in a meantime, I took it out of the skin to enjoy a beauty of its brushed aluminum finish which I'm sure a lot of you will do to show off it's sexy curves!

Weighting only 108g with a measured dimensions of about 96mm x 56mm x 13mm, it gives a new definition to ultra-portable considering a very solid build and all metal front/sides with a silver finish hard plastic back. Having a size comparable to a deck of cards, the fitment in my hand was very comfortable with a great ergonomics of being able to reach every button/wheel control with a thumb. The aluminum finish and round buttons, especially power and volume on the side, makes it resemble a bit of an iPhone look. Buttons have a very nice tactile click response. At the top you have a single 3.5mm port, used as either HO or LO, selectable in Setting menu. On a right side at the bottom there is a slot for a single microSD card, keeping in mind that X1 by itself doesn't have any internal memory. MicroSD card is easy to access which is an improvement over X5 where it was a bit recessed. On a left side at the top you have a volume up/down buttons with an etched "+" and "-", a reset pinhole, and a power button. The volume buttons are slightly raised which makes it easy to distinguish them from power button by sliding your finger, and when you have silicone skin on - volume up has a raised dot bump on its cover. At the bottom you have a micro-usb port positioned in the center with two tiny hex screws symmetrically closer to the edges. This port is used for data transfer (no USB DAC support like X5) as well as charging up it's massive 1700 mAh battery which provides over 12hrs of playback time.

Top of the front panel is occupied by a display (2", 320x240 TFT), similar but not as bright as X5, which is a first indicator where they had to cut some corners stepping down from 2.4" IPS display in X5. Single microSD on X1 versus double in X5 is another change, though 128GB capacity still supported. For those familiar with X5, you will feel right at home with its scrolling wheel control and 5 control buttons with main Play/Pause/Select in the middle of the wheel, Return/Back in the upper right corner, Menu in the upper left corner, and Skip/Select next/prev buttons at the bottom. Otherwise, the wheel control is very intuitive and easy to get used to. Though the wheel looks and functions the same, it's updated from X5. When you turn it with a thumb - you can feel/hear micro-click action, and overall scrolling feels more solid and under a better control. I'm very pleased with this update, though would have been nice for a scrolling wheel to have a better texture, something I'm sure could be upgraded in the future with a textured sticker.

Once X1 is powered up, you are presented with a new updated interface. You still have icons arranged around the semi-circle but now at the top, and the scrolling logistics has changed from X5. Instead of 7 icons in X5, you now have 5 equally spaced icons with EQ and Favorite selections combined in other sub-menus in comparison to X5. Icons are placed at the top from left to right and instead of scrolling icons wheel, you have a scrolling glow pointer with a corresponding icon description text in the notification bar. Most of the Setting and Play Setting controls remained similar to X5 with one noticeable change being an option for Theme Color which helps to improve a contrast and to customize your DAP. I didn't notice any lag while scrolling through menu options or songs.The movement is fluid and as fast as with X5. Also, it really felt like a mature firmware release, and I'm sure FiiO team will fine tune it even further. Selecting to play a song displayed a name and ID tag info (if available), cover art (if available), and song format/encoding. Similarly to X5, at the top in notification bar you have volume with corresponding value, headphone/line out selection icon, EQ setting name (either built in highly usable presets or 7-band customizable one with a precise narrow band tuning), microSD card presence, and battery status.

So how would I describe the sound signature of X1? I found it to be warm and neutral. In comparison to X5, to me it sounded as neutral without any noticeable peaks or dips, just like you would expect a good source to be. Also in comparison to X5, X1 sounded a bit thicker and less detailed with narrower soundstage. That was expected and acceptable considering we are talking about scaled down version of X5 designed for a mainstream rather than audiophile audience. But don't get discouraged by this comment. Listening to X1, without driving yourself crazy with comparison to other DAPs, is actually very satisfying. You get plenty of details across entire frequency range, and X1 built-in amp was powerful enough to drive even some of my demanding headphones that typically require external amping. For example, I was able to drive B3 Pro I without a problem at 50% volume setting. It paired up well with anything I threw at it, either portable IEMs or full size cans, and even high sensitivity IEMs didn't exhibit too much background hissing. It looks like X1 has a single gain setting, and I noticed that it required volume level on average 10 ticks lower than with X5 in its default low gain setting.

Regarding HO sound quality in a comparison to X5, you can rest assure that X1 is not X5 killer. But at the same time, the difference is not really night'n'day. While X5 sound is more detailed and with a wider soundstage, X1 is not lagging behind by too much. This difference becomes even less apparent when you switch to LO with external amp. For example, while using E11k with X1 the sound gets more detailed, with a wider soundstage, and with a deeper and more detailed low end. The ability to switch between HO and LO, where internal amp is disabled, really sets X1 above other entry level DAPs with HO only output. Also, FiiO already announced a future accessory kit for X1 to stack up with other amps (similar to HS6 kit for X5). Plus, there was other mentioning about future accessories, such as armband holder, different cases, car mount, and even audio over micro-usb LO cable since X1 connector will accommodate a new docking amp in a near future.

Overall, testing X1 left me with a very positive impression about this new FiiO DAP. It feels very solid, it performs like a mature product, and it has a great sound quality for its price range. I liked all the improvements (over X5) with a new scrolling wheel mechanism, round physical buttons, and updated scrolling menu control. Sound quality is not equivalent to X5, but that is expected at a fraction of a price. At the same time, it's not too far off and when using external amp connected to LO, you are getting even closer to X5 or other quality DAPs. For $99 this DAP has an amazing value with a hard to beat price/performance ratio especially if you take into consideration everything from its build, design, sound, and firmware. The upcoming add on accessories will add more versatility to take this DAP anywhere with you on the go while keeping its bigger brother (X5) at home for a more serious listening. With such an impressive DAP line up (X3, X5, X1) one can only imagine what FiiO is going to come up with next to blow our mind with X7 release!

product_title: Bluetooth Receiver Car AUX Adapter with Hands-Free Calling Kit by GOgroove - SMARTmini AUX - Home & Auto Stereo Upgrade w/ 30-Foot Wireless A2DP Music Streaming for Smartphones & Tablets
review_headline: Unacceptable. Lack of Bluetooth automatic pairing with iPhone6 (maybe all iPhones? maybe all phones?)
review_body:
I bought this for only one reason, to answer the phone in my car, so that's where my review comes from --- I don't care how well it can play music on my phone or podcasts or whatever.

The good things are that it is small and the form factor easily plugs into and fits with my in-dash audio system. (But be aware, on my system it blocks the USB slot and the CD slot. This is not a catastrophe for me. I listen to MP3 audiobooks, so I only change the CD once every three weeks or so; and I don't use the USB slot, but for some other people it may matter.)
The audio is adequate for phone conversation --- I did not experience the echo's or other complaints that some people seem to have.

But these are outweighed by the bad issues, the primary one of which is the pairing story. I can pair it with my iPhone 6, but it's like a crappy Bluetooth peripheral from 2007, not what I expect from 2014. Specifically, EVERY TIME I want to use it I have to go through the following routine:
- power the device on by holding down the switch for 6 seconds (OK, I can live with that)
- open my iPhone and go to Settings/Bluetooth
- weight a few seconds
- click the SmartMiniAux line in the list of BT devices.
Point is --- it does NOT automatically connect to the iPhone 6 just by holding down the switch the way it is supposed to. OK, maybe one in ten times this might work, but the other nine times it doesn't, so the the only reliable usage model is what I described.

Compare this to the various other BT devices I use in my life, like my Pebble watch or my Automatic car engine monitor, or my friend's in car BT receiver, all of which JUST WORK. No pressing buttons, no dicking around with the iOS BT preferences pane; when I'm in arrange they magically just connect. I don't care if this is Apple's fault or not; regardless this device is not, by my standards of 2014, iPhone Bluetooth "compatible", and it's enough of a flaw that it takeswhat should be a 5 star device to 1 star.

There are other flaws which are less serious but still suck. Most prominently, the device needs to do a better job of indicating that it is connected to the phone. It flashes red and blue leds (according to a pattern whose significance I do not understand, and which is nowhere described in the manual) once powered up, but IMHO it should do something --- use a separate LED, or flash an obviously different pattern --- to indicate separately either "powered up but not connected to the phone" vs "powered up and BT connection is working". A device like this needs to be worry-free, and part of that is that (even after you begin to trust that the BT auto-connection always works) you can still look at the LEDs and be assured that you are connected. The whole POINT of this device is that I don't want to be surprised, while I am hurtling down the highway at 65 miles per hour, when my phone starts ringing and I discover that pressing the button I expect to answer it is not doing anything useful.

(BTW, yes I did what the manufacturer said to make it work with iPhone, namely reset my network settings. This cleared out my stack of accumulated WiFi passwords, which I then had to re-enter for every place I visit --- gee thanks, manufacturer --- but did fsckall to solve the auto-connectivity problem. The system auto-connected to the iPhone perhaps twice after this reset then never again --- once again I had to manually hold its hand and walk through the iPhone Settings/Bluetooth page to connect it every time I entered the car.)

product_title: Abco Tech Portable Water Resistant Wireless FM Radio Bluetooth Speaker with Hands-Free Speakerphone and Storage, Blue
review_body:
If you're in the market for a speaker for your bike, this is the one to get. It gets loud enough to hear over all the car traffic on the road, and it has a replaceable/rechargeable battery (awesome!). The buttons light up for easy access, and it has a compartment big enough for even the largest of phones, along with a clip for your keys on the outside. It straps very securely (and easily) to your handlebar and is just as easy to remove.

Also, this is definitely water resistant. I've left this out in extremely heavy fog overnight for over a month now as well as mild rain (for about an hour each time) and it hasn't suffered any loss of performance. Overall, this is extremely well designed and the execution is just as good; all stitching is good and the zippers seam very durable.

I use it on my commute to school and work, and I must say, I feel so much safer listening to music with this instead of headphones. It's also a great conversation starter and I've received a lot of compliments for it. I absolutely recommend this bike speaker, and for the price ($20.00 for the blue or red one) you are definitely getting your money's worth.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body: I wanted to leave a few comments for people who might be considering this.    1 - The bass is fine (for me). I love 80's rock, Trans Siberian Orchestra, Assemblege 23, Whitney Houston, Lindsey Stirling, etc. Bass is fine for me.    If you are bass heavy these won't be what you want but if you are fine with adequate bass you'll be fine.    2 - Sound quality is very dependent on DAC. I got the Fiio E07K Andes USB DAC - on some computers the headphones sound fine. On mine they sound TERRIBLE without the USB DAC. I would order one, try it with / without. If no difference send it back.    3 - Input source is important. I get most of my music from alltunes and the quality is pretty bad when compared with tidalhifi.com ($20 for high quality streaming).    Spotify high quality is also fine.  I did find tidal had many high quality remixes that sounded amazing but I wound up going with spotify for price + practicality.       4.  Vocals and acoustic is amazing on these.  The clarity of being able to hear what is happening on the strings of a violin or guitar is something you'll miss not having after these headphones.    Some of this quality is dependant on recording (comes thru in some music - doesn't others).  But for instance Handels Messiah album will leave you breathless even if that's not your type of music.     The detail range of mids and highs will leave you entranced with music you previously found boring (if you have the right source)    5 - Comfort on these can't really be over stated.  It doesn't feel like there is an air drum over my ears and it's easy to listen for several hours at a time with no discomfort at all.    Best way to describe it might be high quality speakers mounted on top of a phone cushion.     6 - They are sooooo ugly ... even for old man headohones.   I could care less.  But they still are.    If you go with Fiio + Headphones + tidalhifi you'll be in love.    EDIT: Update. There IS a difference between Pandora & PandoraOne quality. There's a much much smaller difference (for me) between Pandora high quality & tidalhifi.  However tidalhifi seems to have a lot of remasters that others like spotify don't.     After listening to some of them and talking to a few people my understanding is that the quality of original music capture on analog was great.  But with the move to digital that quality on converting is much better now than ten years ago.    I plan on maybe grabbing a pair of bassier headphones for some music types.  But these will make you WANT to listen to Classical, Jazz, Gregorian Chants, and everything else.

product_title: Sennheiser OCX 685i Adidas Sports In-Ear Headphones - Black
review_body:
I'm leaving my original review below. These worked as described below just fine for 3-4 months. But during a run in light rain they shorted and the volume kept going up; then the Siri voice command kept turning on. Basically, they shorted out.

Despite my hesitance to run with earbuds, I decided it was safe to use on trail runs (no cars). I tried a friend's bluetooth headphones, but found them to be heavy and they snapped in half after a few months worth of use.

For me, these headphones have worked as designed. I've had them for 3-4 months now and I haven't had any issues with them breaking or being degraded by sweat. The earbuds will come lose, but thanks to the loops they won't fall out of your ears like some earbuds. When inserted properly, they block out a lot of ambient noise (which admittedly is a safety concern) and music plays very nicely. It's not an expensive over the ears headphones so the music quality isn't amazing, and I cannot imagine using these outside of the context of work-outs.

The control piece lets you turn the volume up and down, skip, and pause songs. This is handy compared to having to dig out your iphone and change volume/song that way. It works for incoming calls too, but the quality isn't great and I can't imagine you'd want to use it other than if someone happens to call while you're working out.

These come with a handy shirt clip to help avoid wires getting in your way. They also come with larger and smaller inserts in case the medium ones are too large/small for your ears.

Overall, I've been pleased. They're not perfect earphones and the sound quality is just OK. Pretty good fit for why I bought them.

product_title: Koss Pro4S Full Size Studio Headphones, Black with Silver Trim
review_headline: So what is a STUDIO headphone? There is a difference with these...
review_body:
These Koss headphones arrived beautifully, yet simply, packaged and ready to sound off. While I realize that headphones need to be broken in--sort of like shoes!--and thus take a good 24-72 hours of use to get the drivers to smooth out, still I was puzzled when I first put this set on and turned on my music.

These headphones were significantly more tight, less bassy than most, and overall less indulgent in the music I was playing. I compared them to my Beats and also my JBL Synchros over and over, and the difference was shocking to me. These headphones, at first, seemed SO FLAT. Then I took a second look at the product, the description, and went over to the Koss website to do some investigating.

While it may be obvious to some audiophiles, allow me to help out those less experienced shoppers on these headphones: these are STUDIO HEADPHONES. These are not headphones that are made for those looking to kick back and do some leisurely listening to their favorite tunes. These are not indulgent headphones, they are purposefully flat because they are made for people who are creating and thus need unaltered sound.

From the Koss website itself: \\"The Pro4S Studio Headphone is specifically crafted for professionals who use headphones every day to create the world's greatest music. Featuring the all-new SLX40 element, tuned for reference, the Pro4S Studio Headphone delivers an incredibly accurate and unbiased sound, perfect for any studio or creative environment.\\"

So, I'm trying to point out here that these headphones are geared toward and created for sound engineers, not leisurely listeners. Just keep that in mind when you're shopping headphones! There is a difference when it comes to \\"studio headphones\\". Why? Because when they are creating music, sound engineers need to be able to hear what they are doing with the music, not the headphones. Does that make sense? They need pure, unadulterated sound--so they will purposely avoid headphones that emphasize one area over another. That's a great thing for the professionals!

Now, if you're into that sort of listening, please know I'm not saying you CAN'T enjoy these headphones. They are very high quality, in my opinion. Just realize, they are created specifically for studio use. With YouTube careers, self-publishing musicians, and all the opportunities to make something of yourself these days, a LOT of people can get great use from this sort of headphone! They definitely have their place in the market. IF you are searching for a great, immersive headphone that draws you into the music that has already been engineered to perfection in the studio, you might want to search elsewhere, not because these aren't good headphones--they're great--they just might not be geared toward your needs.

All that aside, here is what I love about these headphones:

- They're comfortable, over the ear headphones with plenty of cushion, great sound isolating
- They fold up quite nicely to be stored safely and flat in your backpack or briefcase, yet they are full size
- The headphone jack can be plugged into either side of the headphones, which also allows for a second listener to connect if that's what you need
- Comes with a carrying case
- Attractive! Call me vain, but I dislike chunky headphones that make me look like Princess Leia, these are slim and slick
- I like the coiled cord! When you have a lot of cords, a coiled one can help keep things tidy.
- Despite being geared toward studio use, once I got used to the difference in the sound, I have to agree that these are high quality headphones

review_headline: I've had great luck with these little key finders
review_body:
I've had great luck with these little key finders. We have a toddler at home and so times little hands like to hide things (keys, remotes especially). I attached one to my key ring and one to every remote. When they go missing, I just grab the fob hit the button and listen for the beep. They are a bit bulky and are definitely noticeable when stuck to items but that doesn't bother us. We have a pretty big house and I haven't noticed a range issue. Hitting the button and using a sweeping pattern usually does the trick. I don't think it works on line of sight but I find that method works best. Also, it's important to write down which color receiver you use on items you want to find or you're stuck pressing each color on the fob till you hear a beep.
All and all, I'm pleased. Good purchase.

product_title: 8GB Transcend MP870 Digital Music Player w/ FM Radio, Voice Recorder, microSD slot - black
review_headline: Bookmark add and retrieval function not working; back arrow button causes unit to power itself off
review_body:
Initially, when I first received this MP870 mp3 player - I thought that, at long last, I had found the perfect mp3 digital player. I was so impressed with the features that this player offered and after downloading and reading the owner's manual for it - before this 8GB player had even arrived, I decided to also order a 4gb version of the MP870 as well. The 4gb MP870 player was purchased from a different vendor and although I ordered it several days after I had ordered the 8GB model, it arrived almost two weeks before the 8gb player did.

I want to point that that my primary purpose for owning an mp3 player is to listen to web radio podcasts that I download from the web from various web radio networks that I have found and like. On my Windows PC, I create folder names for each of these web radio shows and when a new show is posted, I download the mp3 file for that show and deposit it in the appropriately named folder. On a 16gb microSD card, I have basically duplicated the folder naming scheme that I have on my PC - and then I use the drag and drop technique to place a copy of the mp3 file on my MP870 player's microSD card. As a rule, the vast majority of these mp3 podcasts are at least 60 minutes in length - and oftentimes almost 2 hours in duration. This means that I absolutely must have a bookmark feature that I can use to mark the spot in a podcast that I am listening to, but which I have to interrupt in order to conduct other business. I seldom can sit down and listen to a podcast that is 60 or more minutes long without interruption. Here is where I discovered a very serious problem on the 4GB MP870 player. I will explain how this problem was found shortly, but I want to state that as soon as my 8GB MP870 player arrived - I immediately tested it, to see if it had the same malfunction as did the 4gb MP870 - and it did.

Here is a description of the problem. When I turn the player on and navigate through the file management menu, selecting microSD card, and then moving forward to podcasts - when I browse my folder list, enter a folder, and select an mp3 podcast to
listen to - and then after listening to the mp3 for a period of time, decide to use the side button to access the Options-->Add Bookmark selection, this will set a bookmark at the point in the podcast where you are currently at. Powering off the MP870,
and then later, powering it back on - and following the same path to get back to the mp3 file in the folder that I had been listening to previously, selecting it again and pressing 'play' - starts the mp3 over at the beginning. At this point, pressing 'pause', and
according to the user manual instructions, pressing the back arrow button two times - is supposed to take you to the menu that allows you to 'View Bookmarks'. Once there, you can select View Bookmarks, and then scroll down to the last bookmark set, select it, and the mp3 file is supposed to resume at the point where that bookmark had been set. What happened on the 4GB
MP870, however, was that as soon as I pressed the back arrow button - the player powers itself off completely. This problem was repeatedly duplicated using the same sequence of button pushes. I then decided to update the firmware on the player to the latest and most recent version to see if that would resolve the issue. Firmware updated successfully. Once again, the problem with the back arrow causing the player to power itself off persisted. I then opened up a support case with Transcend and explained the problem to them. They advised that I send the unit back for repair, which I did within about 8 days of owning the 4gb player. This was sometime around October 27th. I have yet to receive the player or a replacement as of 11/20/14.

As I said, once the 8gb MP870 finally arrived - the first thing I did was to update the firmware, and then check to see if the 8Gb
model had the same problem as the 4Gb model did.The exact same malfunction existed. So, I opened up another case with Transcend Tech Support - and for the next 3 weeks, worked with the tech support people via email - explaining the problem in great detail and performing whatever tests that they asked me to perform, in hopes of helping them to troubleshoot the problem
and come up with a fix. I got exactly zero resolution for this problem, but during the course of the troubleshooting - I found that the 'View Bookmarks' function would sometimes work and sometimes, pressing the back arrow button in order to access the menu
that had the 'View Bookmarks' selection on it would cause the player to power itself off. At one point, I suspected that this failure might be related in some way to the level of charge that existed on the internal battery - but, additional testing on my part later seemed to discredit that theory. Transcend tech support was basically clueless and could not help me. In the end, I was forced to return the 8GB MP870 before my 30 day return for a full refund window expired.

And, I have yet to hear a word from the Transcend Tech Support people about the 4gb MP870 that I sent back for repair or replacement.

To conclude, I must say that I am greatly disappointed that these MP870 mp3 players (both 4GB and 8GB) have a defect that seems to exist right out of the box and which negatively impacts ones ability to use the bookmark feature the way it is supposed to work as per the owners manual. When using a player like this for web radio podcasts, or for audiobooks for that matter, having the ability to add a bookmark and then later be able to retrieve it and resume listening where you left off - is a CRITICAL issue. I loved every other feature of this MP870 player and would have very much liked to have kept it - but, I cannot do without a reliable bookmark add and retrieval capability. I am also very disappointed with Transcend technical support - since they had 3 weeks to troubleshoot this issue and could not come up with a fix during that time, after which I was forced to return the 8GB

review_headline: ... my 2nd Diver Waterproof MP3 Player and I absolutely love it. I exercise in the pool at my ...
review_body:
This is my 2nd Diver Waterproof MP3 Player and I absolutely love it. I exercise in the pool at my local YMCA 3-5 mornings a week, and my Diver Player keeps it interesting with my favorite music. It is easy to load songs onto the player by connecting to my laptop using the included USB cable. The instructions are concise and easy to follow. The player itself clips nicely onto the strap of my bathing suit, and it is easy to reach if I want to switch songs or adjust the volume.

As mentioned by another reviewer, I have had some trouble with the earbud plug pieces coming off in my ear when I take the earbuds off. After this happened twice, I learned to be extra careful and make sure the plug was still attached to the earbud itself. Not a major problem, but something to be careful about.

The quality of sound is very good, the unit charges quickly, and I've had many of my fellow swimmers/aqua exercisers inquire about the Diver. I always tell them it's great and worth every penny. I love the pink color which is not only cute, but makes it easy to find in my swim-equipment bag. I still have my first (black) Diver and will alternate using that one and the pink one for variety.

I've used other waterproof MP3 players in the past, and was frankly amazed at how much better the Diver is for ease of use, durability and sound. I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to listen to music or audio books or anything else in MP3 format while you are swimming or exercising in water.

FCC Disclosure: Diver gave me this product for free in exchange for a fair review. This in no way influenced my review, and I already had a Diver MP3 player which I truly love.

product_title: CyberPower Intelligent LCD Series UPS  Mini-Tower
review_headline: Excellent UPS Backup for My Home Theater Setup!
review_body:
I live in a rural area that has a co-op as our electricity provider. Basically, power in our area is quite unreliable. We get frequent dips in our power which are like blackouts that last only a few seconds.

I purchased this particular UPS for my entertainment center. This consists of a Vizio 47" LCD HDTV, a Pioneer receiver which powers my 5.2 surround sound audio setup, a PC with a 430 watt power supply (basically a home theater PC), an HD Homerun Prime cable receiver (also purchased from Amazon), a TP Link 5-port gigbit ethernet switch (for Internet access to various devices), and lastly my Xbox One (also purchased from Amazon).

I calculated that I needed 500 watts, at peak usage, to keep all of my devices powered. It didn't need to power them for more than a few minutes; just long enough to keep everything from resetting during a power dip. This UPS has fit that role perfectly! It has a USB interface which allows the PC to configure and monitor the UPS. It continually monitors my power usage (about 400 watts continuous with the Xbox powered off, and 450 - 500 watts continuous with the Xbox on and in use). At 400 watts, the UPS widget on the PC tells me that I've got about 7 minutes of backup power. At peak usage of 500 watts, that drops down to about 5 minutes.

Since I purchased this, I've had nearly half a dozen power dip events. The first time happened when I was playing an online game on my Xbox. I heard a click, and then a beeping from the unit, but my game continued and I wouldn't have even noticed if it weren't for the audio notifications (I should mention I have a bit smaller of a CyberPower UPS for my Internet cable modem, firewall, WiFi router, and 24-port gigabit switch in my network closet--the cable signal from Comcast appears to be unaffected by power outages). The widget showed a 4 second power outage during that event. Every subsequent power dip has been exactly the same--except for the audio notification, we didn't even notice the power had dropped.

This unit has done exactly what I wanted it to, and has performed to my complete satisfaction. I will definitely by CyberPower products again for any future UPS needs.

So this setup gives me about 13 channels in HD. Mostly without picture breakup (which used to be horrible with earlier antennas). review_body:
This thing will BLOW YOUR MIND if you've been watching cable and/or streaming Amazon.com offerings through Fire HD or Roku, but only using the TV speakers or a low-budget sound bar.

It took about 20-30 minutes to set this up. All the cables are included, so that was definitely a bonus and kudos to Bose for that. There are three major components that come with the system, namely a sound bar (with something like five speakers in it), the Acoustic mass module and the control unit (i.e. what you point the Bose remote and use to set everything up). You'll have to power, I believe, two of the components, with the third receiving power from connection with one of the powered components. The Acoustic mass module is wireless, so all you have to do is plug that in.

The first thing that's particularly impressive about this system is that it's smart. You plug an HDMI cable into your TV's ARC input, which on my TV is HDMI 2 and it actually says "HDMI 2 (ARC)." Stands for "Audio Return Channel." So, let's say you've got an Amazon Fire HD and a Blu-Ray player and a cable box plugged into your TV right now. Enter the Bose CineMate 120 Home Theater System. To set that up, you plug and HDMI cable from the CineMate's control unit into your TV's ARC input. You then take all the other HDMI plugs in your TV and plug them into corresponding connectors on the control unit. So, say I move my Fire HD from the TV's "HDMI 2 (ARC)" connector to the "AUX" connector on the CineMate's control unit. Now, to watch Fire HD, I just make sure my TV's on, push the CineMate remote's "AUX" button and the control unit box says "Loading" for a moment; then voila, I see Fire HD selections on the TV and when I hit play on the Fire HD controller, big booming sound comes out. (Same goes for cable and Blu-Ray [i.e. push Cable or Blu-Ray on the CineMate remote]). There's no more of that business of using the TV remote's "INPUT" button to toggle between cable, Blu-Ray, Game or streaming devices.

Now, I just set up the CineMate this past weekend, so there _may_ also be a way to make the CineMate remote work for changing cable channels or selecting shows on your chosen streaming device. That notwithstanding, it's way easier to switch from one device (cable, Blu-Ray, game, Fire HD/Roku) on the CineMate-connected TV than it is on the one with my Onkyo A/V receiver in my home office. Well done, Bose.

And the sound out of this thing is amazing for its size. TV, cable, streamed content all sound first rate. I was even able to communicate--over the telephone--to my tech-befuddled, semi-Luddite wife how to get it all going. That was easy!

product_title: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone
review_headline: Surprisingly good, and competitive BT headphones
review_body:
I never thought I'd own a pair of Beats headphones, let alone recommend them, but here goes: There are very good BT headphones, that with a few tweaks would be excellent. I won't dwell on the Beats reputation; if you care about it strongly (positive or negative), likely nothing I can write that will change your mind. That said, I have a hard time liking the glossy versions of these headphones, but I have the matte black version (but would have gone with the titanium color had it been the same price). I liked these well enough that I returned a pair of Bose SoundLink On-Ear BT headphones because these were much more comfortable and sounded noticeably better.

This is a "fun" headphone; it's not balanced by any means, but the bass is much more controlled compared to earlier generations of Beats headphones, and I was surprised by their clarity and dynamic punch. With the Bose and other BT headphones I've tried, you can tell at times that it was a wireless connection; I didn't get that sensation with these, which is a plus.

I had no issues using this with an iPhone 6 (running iOS 8.1). There is a very slight lag when watching video; you can tell if you are looking for it, but for the most part, it's not noticeable or annoying. The two (maybe three) things I wish were different: There is a NC "hiss" that is pretty prominent between tracks, which surprised me. If you want to use these just for NC, look elsewhere, as it is somewhat annoying. Oddly enough, the hiss seems to go away completely when playing music, so it's not an issue for me. (It'd be nice if you could just turn the NC off.) The other annoying thing is that you can't use Siri in wireless mode, other than activating it from your iPhone or iPad. Hopefully, this is a firmware fix, because the omission is puzzling. Finally, it would be really nice if the headphones could remember multiple BT connections and allow you to toggle between them, so you aren't having to disconnect and reconnect if you are switching source devices. The Bose headphones are great in that regard.

Finally, in terms of aesthetics, these (at least in the matte black version) are great looking headphones that seem well built and fold down and fit into a relatively small case given that they are over-ear cans. Even though I got these on sale, it'd be nice if these were closer to $250, not $370. At MSRP, these are a luxury/splurge, and if I had to spend only $250 on BT headphones, I'd probably get a pair of Sony MDR-1RBT, which are now being nicely discounted and sound great, but don't really fold down much.

All in all, I was surprised by how much I liked these headphones. Wireless is great, and you aren't giving up much with these compared to wired, if you can live with the sound signature and price.
