I have had some great Sylvania products in the past so I expected this to be a great product. It gets its extra star because: 1) the CD player works well 2) the radio works well, and 3) it has a nice clear sound, If it hadn't been for my intuition and a helpful post on a website, I would be calling Amazon Customer Service and this product would be going back to them. If I could get a message to the manufacturer, it would be this: "You seem to have a good product and your Marketing Department dida great job with its description on Amazon.But whoever compiles your User Manual needs to look at the one for SCR4975 and re-do it. review_headline: Good things do come in small packages!
review_body: Honestly, I was expecting more when I first opened the RE-400 package for the first time. They looked just like any run of the mill low budget type IEM. Nothing that screamed \\"hey, I'm special\\". In fact, the shells and cable looked wimpy compared to my Miles Davis Tribute (original) IEM's with relatively huge shells and thick cable.    HOWEVER,    After fitting the IEM's with the included large comply foam tips and then fitting them into my head, it got interesting. I use an iBasso DX90 DAP with lossless only audio files and when first plugging the phones in wasn't entirely impressed with what I was hearing. However, by letting the IEM's and my ears warm up for 10 minutes and making a few slight EQ tweaks, I was dumbfounded by how awesome the audio quality was. Gone was the over powering bass of the Miles. Present was a very well balanced sound across the entire spectrum. It didn't falter anywhere. Perfect reference quality audio.    How could that much audio information be possibly coming out of these miniscule pieces??? How could these possibly sound as good as my much larger driver, non-EQ'd AKG K712 Pro played through a Schiit Asgard 2 from a Pioneer optical SACD player with a set of very good DAC's.....over $800+ worth of gear..........while the DX90 and RE-400 weigh in at just a bit over half that amount.    Needless to say, the RE-400 are fantastic IEM's and when paired with a high end source such as an iBasso DX90 with dual Sabre DAC's can absolutely run right alongside the bigger dogs of the audio world.    I have quite a bit of mid grade gear at this point, amps and headphones. Some of my amps include Objective O2, a fleet of Little Dot Tubes, Schiit Lyr, Asgard 2, Valhalla 2, etc.........and phones.....Beyer T1, HE-500, K712 Pro, RS-1e, etc...    ......and now RE-400 which I feel are my best IEM's.....better than my TripleFi 10, Miles Davis, and Kilpsch X10    Great work Dr. Dangerous a.k.a. Brian Fang!

product_title: RCA TVPRAMP1Z Preamplifier for Outdoor Antenna
review_headline: Noticed a big boost in Signal Strength
review_body:
This preamplifier works great. I live in the Atlanta area and could receive most stations on a good day. Due to my distance from some of the broadcast antenna's, (I live 40 miles north of the city) the signal of many were weak and faded out if there was a storm or any interference. The preamp was just what I needed.

By itself, the exterior unit, which hooks directly to your digital antenna, boosts the signal significantly. On the closest TV to the antenna, the signal increase was significant. The weak stations now come in strong and no long longer fade out during storms. Love that.

I also have a second TV which was about 25 feet further down the cable. The external unit did not boost the signal enough on its own. HOWEVER, this unit also comes with an interior booster assembly which needs AC power. I connected the booster close to the 2nd TV and saw a much improved signal.

I now get 80 channels including several FM stations on my TV's. All of them clear!

This past weekend, we had some thunderstorms to move in. This usually kills the weak stations. But this time, all stations maintained a great picture - all except one very distant PBS station, but there was an identical station on another channel which was closer... worked for me!

So... this unit comes with 2 parts.
1. Exterior Preamp that fits on the Antenna
2. Interior AC powered Booster.

If the cable length between your antenna and TV is short enough, the exterior preamp may be all that you need.
Longer cable lengths may require the booster, which you want to plug in close to your TV.

BE SURE to read the directions and ensure the default settings are in place. Someone who had the amp before me had changed them. I just had to flip a couple of switches (very easy) to get things back. No big deal, but needed to read the directions to know this. The unit didn't work out the box. VERIFY DEFAULT SETTINGS!!!!!

review_body: These are the best earphones I have ever owned. I'm not an audiophile, but I notice that the sound is much more detailed than my $30 Skull Candy earphones, as one would expect.    After having read some of the negative reviews for these earphones, I suspect the other reviewers weren't wearing them above and around the ear (as recommended in the manual) but hanging straight down. My review below assumes wearing the earphones above and around the ear.    Pros:  + The three-button controller works perfectly and makes listening much more pleasant as you don't have to dig out your phone all the time.  + The flat cord doesn't tangle.  + The L-shaped connector that connects to your phone makes it fit better in your pocket and less likely to break. Why don't all headphone makers use L-shaped connectors?  + They are very comfortable, even after hours of use!    Cons (mostly minor, not enough to knock the product down to four stars):  + It took a little practice to get a good fit in my ears. Our maybe the silicone softened up after a few days?  + The downloadable app starts Google Music whenever I click the center button. Maybe there's a setting I didn't get right. Now I use the earphones without the app, which still gives me the play/pause and volume up/down that I need.  + There is noise when the cord brushes against my clothing. But I have yet to see a pair of earphones where that isn't the case.  + The bass is a little heavy, but that can be fixed in settings on the phone.

product_title: Package: Kicker 10CVT10-2 Ohm 800 Watt Shallow Mount Car Subwoofer + Rockville RSST10 Single 10" Shallow Mount 0.9 Cu. Ft. Subwoofer Encloure Box + Single Enclosure Wire Kit With 14 Gauge Speaker Wire + Screws + Spade Terminals
review_headline: Good enough, but be nice with screwing the subs in and do yourself a favor... order some replacement terminals.
review_body:
Be sure to order some 1 7/8" quality terminal cups to replace the crap quality ones included with these boxes. Springs are okay but lever for the positive terminal on one of the boxes came loose and had to put it back together with hope holding it more than anything, lol. Box seals are decent for the price, but not much around the terminal cups which is good since they're crap anyways. If you have the luxury of a power drill with torque selections set to 4 or 6 lbs. of torque AKA toddler strength torque because the MDF isn't too great. After pre-drilling the holes with 7/64" drill bit (a size smaller than technically needed for the 1 1/2" screws that come with it) and adjusting torque to 12 lbs. which I figured to be adequate, I quickly realized 6 lbs. was the only safe torque level. If you don't have a drill like this then just drill all the screws about 1/4" before head contact and finish with finger-tight pressure or just a tad more pressure but play nice so the screw doesn't strip the wood.

Also I don't believe for a second that these boxes are 0.8 cu. Ft. volume inside. That being said I haven't noticed any negative effects on the bass response despite being under the minimum compact sealed box vol. for these subs.

Here's my setup that works surprisingly well given my power constraint from my 105A Alternator:
2 Kicker 10CVT10-2 Ohm Subs (this item)
1 Boss BX55 Crossover (to cut out Freq. above 250 Hz and 18dB potential Bass Boost)
1 Boss Cap100cr 10 Farad Capacitor (which is probably overkill since the voltage hardly drops below 14 Volts)
1 Boss PH2.800 Phantom Amp with 1600W max

P.S. If you plan on pushing more than this you might need to seriously look into a 200 or 300 Amp Alternator and using 2 or 0 AWG power cable, otherwise just get a capacitor if you're worried about dimming headlights, but the Big 3 is the cheapest and most effective. Any thicker than 4 AWG power cable andyou'll have a tough time finding an amp with terminals big enough for 0 AWG terminal connectors if you can find the connectors themselves. Don't rely on RadioShack or AutoZone, etc. for your electrical stuff because most selection stops at 4 AWG mostly due to the fact that you'll never need 200 Amps (2000-2880 Watts) without needing a professional level alternator replacement to actually provide that power at RMS.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_headline: Comparison with ATH-M50 and AKG K240
review_body: I own Audio Technica M50's, AKG K240 Studio's and now Sennheiser HD598's. I am relatively new to the world of audiophile headphones, I bought my first pair of cans (ATH M50's) about 5 months ago. When I first got my M50's I was kind of disappointed, but I think my expectations were way too high. I thought they would make my music sound completely different and amazing, but obviously they did not. When I first got the M50's I was really disappointed, they did not sound any better than my Samsung ear buds that came with my GS4. I honestly preferred the earbuds and was questioning if I had received a fake pair. But I kept listening to them and they broke in sounded way better and then I couldn't go back to my ear buds. They just take a little time to get used to. Later on, I wanted to try a pair of more open cans so I got the AKG K240's and loved them. I could head individual instruments a lot easier with them vs the M50's. But I still wanted more.. So I researched and found that the HD598's were some of the most highly recommended open headphones for under $200. So I got them. When I first tried them on I noticed that the soundstage was a lot bigger than the akg's. I could hear more instrument separation. There are also significantly more detailed. I see people everywhere saying that they have a weak bass response. I don't find that to be true at all. I can feel the bass a lot more than in my AKG's. No where near as much as the M50's though. But those are closed cans, so I would figure that would be the case. They handle eq a lot better than the akg's too. So if you want more bass you can just turn it up. I wouldn't recommend using digital eq though, it just makes everything sound worse. I use an 80's stereo receiver called the Reference 240r by Quadraflex. They may not vacuum your ears out when listening to bass heavy rap or electronic music with the bass eq'd all the way up like the m50's do, but they are perfectly fine for rap music, in my opinion. I no longer have a use for my AKG's because they Sennheiser's are like a better version of them. I will use my M50's still however, because they are closed cans that i can use in a public place like an airplane. I will also use the M50's for rap and electronic music because when I listen to those genres I prefer to have more bass. I usually listen to progressive metal and rock like The Dear Hunter, Between the Buried and Me, Periphery and Animals As Leaders and these work great for those. I can finally hear the bass guitar in metal music. These headphones, along with my other headphones, are good for every genre. They are also the most comfortable of all 3. The velour pads aren't nearly as soft as the pads on the other two but the clamping pressure is a lot less and they are very light. My ears never get hot with these like they do with the other two. I think the M50's and HD598's are the perfect couple. One is better for rap and electronic and the other is great for everything else.

product_title: Winegard Outdoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: Really location dependent... do your research.
review_body:
Buying a digital antenna is very complicated. It's very location dependent so an antenna that works for one person may not work for another. To optimize the channels you get I would recommend finding a website that shows where your nearest broadcast towers are (antennaweb.org is one). If all the towers are in one direction, you may do better with a strong directional antenna.

These flat antennas are great, but I read that they tend to have problems picking up low power VHF. Where I live that includes NBC.

So for us, in a normal location we would get FOX, CBS, and CW. Sitting it on boxes near a window (we just moved) we also get CW and ABC. Nothing we do gives any signal from NBC. This was a little disappointing because we had a cheap $10 antenna. When I put foil on the rabbit ears and angled it a certain direction I got all the channels including NBC. You would think that an amplified antenna could do better, but again it's very location dependent and these flat antennas have trouble with the lower channels so just make sure that isn't a huge deal breaker.

product_title: Zipbuds Juiced 2.0 Earbuds
review_headline: Don't tangle and stay in your ear!
review_body:
I bought these earbuds for two reasons; I wanted to try the 'no tangle' promise and the 'stay in your ear claim.'

I usually can't wear this general type of earbuds because they won't stay in my ears. For years I've worn the iPod original type but those seem to be getting harder to obtain and most of the ones by other manufacturers, such as the Sony MDRE9LP earbuds, have an L-shaped plug-in to the iPod. I put my iPod in my pocket which seems to stress the connection, causing static and the phones to fail shortly after I buy them. So..these earbuds...

So far I'm very happy with these earbuds. They truly don't tangle which is on the plus side. On the down side, the wires are slightly heavier and more cumbersome than regular earbud wires but not so much that it matters (in my opinion). The wires plug straight into my iPod which eliminates the static and premature failure due to the wires breaking.

Most important of all, these earbuds stay in my ears. The reason these earbuds work where others haven't is two-fold. First, you are supplied with three sizes of cushion (versus two for most brands) which allows a better fit. Second, the slight cock in the angle of the buds as they fit into your ear also greatly aids in making them feel more secure. I find the sound quality excellent although since I'm listening to audiobooks, I can't speak to their musical qualities.

These earbuds cost significantly more than regular earbuds but are worth it to me because I can wear them. All the cost savings in the world don't matter if you can't use a product. The no tangle feature is excellent too, no more picking at tiny knots while swearing under my breath at how in the world two earphone wires can get so tangled when I just took them off for a couple of minutes.

Bottom line: probably not for everyone because of the price but worth it to those who hate tangled wires or can't get regular earbuds to stay in their ear.

About a month later: Just want to add an addendum to my review: although I still like the earbuds quite a bit, I have found that the earbud tips fall off with ridiculous ease. I listen in bed to audiobooks at night and in the morning, I can expect to find one or both of the earbud tips in the sheets. product_title: Audio Technica ATH-EQ300M BK Black | Ear-Fit Headphones (Japan Import)
review_headline: Not in love with these headphones.
review_body:
Even at a value price point, these headphones are disappointing.

Build-wise they are nice and light. However, the earclips are very thin and the way they are cut leaves kind of a sharp edge on your ear. Because of that, even with the light weight they get pretty uncomfortable after an hour or so. The cord is far too short. Wearing my previous pair of headphones (which finally died after 6 years) I could roll my chair about 3/4ths down the length of my desk, and freely spin my chair. With this pair, I can't roll my chair at all. I can turn my head, but if I spin the whole chair, pop goes the cord. Also, the cord into the right earpiece is several inches longer than for the left earpiece (by design, not a manufacturing defect). As a result, I'm always tugging on it accidentally as it gets caught between my arm and torso.

Sound-wise, I'd say they are slightly below average even at this price. There is a little bit of bass. Nothing earth-shattering, but it's nice to hear on cheap headphones, especially given the thin form factor. They get as loud as you'll ever want with very little distortion. On the other hand, there is no real separation between the mid and high ranges, so the music sounds very flat at any volume.

Long story short, even though I just got these a few weeks ago, I think I'll be replacing them very, very soon. I'll use these when I'm laying on the couch playing a 3DS game, but that's really all they're good for.

product_title: Bluedio Model R Revolution 8 Tracks Built in Mp3 Player Hi-Fi Rank Wireless & Bluetooth Headphones (Black)
review_body:
I've had these for just over 2 months and I'm not too thrilled. To try and keep it short:

1. I wear glasses and they hurt my ears after maybe 10 minutes. I bought these because other reviewers said they felt great with glasses but this is false for anyone who wears thick framed glasses.

2. They distort sound. I listen to a lot of chill/lounge/electronic at work and it seems as though they make certain parts of the song off tune. It's very weird and I don't know how to accurately describe it. It's almost as though it lags for a second? I don't know, it's not always noticeable but its enough to irritate me.

3/a The battery dies within 2 work days, even if I only use them for maybe 2-3 hours.
3/b There is no warning of a low battery. You just randomly find yourself sitting in silence and you're forced to plug in a different pair of headphones while you wait for these to charge for 3+ hours. Very annoying. Also, it no longer tells me when they're done charging. It did the first time but never again after that.

Overall, they're a decent pair for what I paid but I think I'd rather spend a bit extra to get something with better sound and better battery life.

product_title: Altec Lansing VS2921 30W 2.1 Speaker System with Subwoofer
review_headline: 1 audio set is a classic set of excellent style and sound fidelity
review_body:
This 2.1 audio set is a classic set of excellent style and sound fidelity. I looked at numerous styles and comparably-priced stereo sets for my PC, but kept coming back to this unit. First, I still own a Altec Lansing VS2321 speaker system that was purchased in 2006 and it still works flawlessly. This set my standard for judging 2.1 products. Next, I wanted to get a system that blended the contemporary colors and style exhibited by my new desktop PC. Of all the systems that I examined, the VS2921 met my needs.

My only complaint was the length of the speaker and subwoofer cables. They are only 4-foot long. The manufacturer suggested that you place the subwoofer on the floor to remain within this limited cable length configuration. However, after determining the excellent sound of the unit, I decided to use a different approach. Instead of returning the stereo unit, I decided to purchase three 3.5 mm (1/8 inch) cable extensions. This allowed me to set up the system in the configuration I wanted and I gained the quality of sound and reasonable price that I was looking for. Setting the subwoofer on the floor only exposes it to accumulation of dust and other materials that would reduce its sound output quality.

So far I am very pleased with the sound of this unit. The 30-watt RMS may seem limited to some audiophiles, but the output of this system is so rich that I have to reduce the volume to a comfortable level. In fact, the manufacturer advises that you begin at a low setting and then elevate the sound to meet your comfort level.

product_title: Auvio Element Earbuds White/black
review_headline: Mediocre, but good for the price.
review_body:
As a disclaimer, I am a mid-range audiophile that won't spend over $200 for anything, but most of my products hover around the $100 mark.

Just picked these up locally because i didn't bring my buds to work. I'm using a Fiio E7 with them and listening to lossless recordings on a macbook.

The build quality is simple and straightforward. It's not amazing and they are almost exclusively plastic, but the design is okay. The cord isn't great quality, but no worse than any earbuds that come included with any electronics.

They are between mediocre to terrible, but are good for the price. I did not break them in as I'm just using them to kill time. They are heavy on the bass and the bass is quite muddled. The mid range is lacking, but at this price it's expected. I have to admit that the highs are not bad and very clear but not tinny. I am also impressed by the soundstage, although it may be due to my DAC/amp.

Honestly for the price point, these are okay. These are some of the better buds I've picked up at this price.

product_title: Mount-It! MI-803 Floating Wall Mounted Shelf Bracket Stand for AV Receiver, Component, Cable Box, Playstation4, Xbox1, VCR Player, Blue Ray DVD Player, Projector, Load Capacity 66 lbs, Three Shelves, Tinted Tempered Glass
review_headline: Excellent.  READ this for some tips and notes before believing the negative comments
review_body:
Lots of negative complaints that I think (while may be true) don't matter in the end. I happen to really like these. Let address some of the complaints and provide some tips. I bought two and both came undamaged. I love the metal finish and the glass finish. It took me 45 mins to put the first one up. Only 15 mins the second one. The installation guide (with parts and diagrams only) is difficult to understand, but here are some tips:

MOUNTING
- First choice is how to mount. I chose a wood stud so it was as easy as drilling 4 small pilot holes, levelling and screwing in the screws. There are also drywall and concrete tools but I didn't use them.
- As others have mentioned, the bracket is different than in the guide. It's smaller with 6 holes. I used 4 of the 6 holes.

PUTTING IT TOGETHER
- On the back cover of the guide, you'll see two pictures. Only after trial and error did I see that the top diagram is upside down. The bottom diagram is right side up. The top diagram means that they want you to put this together upside down. I had better luck laying it (conduit side down) on a waist-high stool (though the floor could also work) and working on it vertically (from bottom to top).
- It is easiest to put the rubber plates on the conduit frame before inserting against the glass shelves.
- At the very end (top or right depending on putting it together), put the top allen screws into the top plate before place on the two rods as the rods won't stick out to thread them. This is the trickiest part if you are working solo: hold the left (or bottom) two rod caps with your finger while compressing the entire unit to keep the glass shelves from tipping, and then with your right hand use the allen wrench to tight and compress the shelf.

CABLES
- Everyone is complaining about the lack of size for wires. I am surprised as I got 12 cables for four different devices and the TV through there and still hadroom left.
- Tip: First take the shelf and turn it over horizontally on the floor or chair (glass side down with conduit side up). Take all the wires and bundle them together in your hands and lay them in the conduit. Then take each wire or plug connector individually, pull it up or down the conduit and insert into the hole for that shelf level (you don't need a lot exposed for most devices). Then at last make sure that the TV cords/connectors extend beyond the top enough to reach TV. I then used some throw-away old black ties and tied the cords into a bundle in the conduit (at bottom, middle, and top). You should be set to go at this point.

ATTACHING TO WALL
- Tip: have the two screws in your hand or handy before you try to attached.
- The best way to do this is to place your fingers on the cord bundle and palm on front of conduit (at top and bottom) and then lift and rest on the wall bracket screw prongs. By doing this all the cords stay in place and recessed against the conduit. Then with one hand pressing the shelf system against the wall thread both screws in so at least its anchored. Then finish with a phillips.

The finished product looks amazing! Highly recommended!

Hope this helps.

review_headline: One channel only problem - EASY FIX!
review_body:
Like many people here, my turntable suffered from the one-channel plague. Only one side was working, and when I switched audio cables, the other channel worked fine but no sound out of the other.

I thought I was done for, $250 gone! But--however--one trip to the Audio Technica website, and I found a comment thread that had a solution. One of the AT engineers said that one of the pins inside the tone arm sometimes get stuck, so all you have to do is take the headshell off of the tone arm, take something non-conductive, and push the pins in and out a little bit (they're spring-ey). I did that, put everything back together, and the unit worked totally fine!

It's not the highest quality product, but for what it's supposed to do it does reasonably well. At least when everything works. I hope this solution lasts.

This antenna is really great and I ditched cable. This is why I love it: 1. easy to assemble (5 minutes or less) 2. small, when I saw it I thought it was too small for the job but it is incredible how well it performs. 3. Great performance, I'll explain in my next paragraph.

The performance of this Antenna is just fantastic. I live 10 miles from the Washington DC towers and got great signal around 45 channels including the major 4 networks (NBC, FOX, ABC & CBS), spanish channels (Univision, VME, MundoFOX and other public networks in spanish) and pretty much all in HD . I installed it on the outside around 8 feet from the ground. In addition there were plenty of trees around (in August) . I'm no pro so I just tried to install it pointing to the towers. I added a pre-amplifier to this since I installed 4 TVs in it since after installing the additional TVs some channels fade away, but with the pre-amplifier more channels were captured, even some that were not available before (some in Baltimore and Telemundo as well). I strongly recommend this antenna. I just ditched cable and saving over $100 a month.

product_title: Universal Articulating Wall Arm for 32" to 52" Flat Panel Screens
review_headline: Perfect for built-in cabinets & entertainment centers
review_body:
Just bought my 2nd. This mount has the longest reach I could find. This thing is stout! (that's a good thing!) The kids could do pull ups on articulating arm. This mount weighs as much as most new TVs. I've used this arm on a 47\\" and a 55\\" thin LED LCD TV. Both were side cabinet mounts. The base was screwed into the side of a cabinet. Thus, the swivel is such that the TV is normally flat against the base plate and the articulating arm. The outside edge of the base is flush with the edge of the cabinet (just like a giant door hinge), giving you full use of the cabinet behind the TV, just swing the TV to open.

The 47\\" TV is mounted above my refrigerator, perfectly covering the cabinet, replacing the cabinet doors. The TV is basically a giant door and I can still use the cabinet; swings open to access the cabinet. This particular cabinet was next to an interior wall, so the base plate was screwed into 3/4\\" plywood behind the 1/2\\" cabinet interior. The arm has a dog leg in it that allows it to center perfectly like it was made for the cabinet, looks very professional/custom made.

The 47\\" was actually much harder to screw onto the mounting bar than the 55\\" because I had to take the mounting bar apart... the directions are totally confusing, not much help. The vertical bars that mount to the TV are covered by the solid back plate. Thus you have unscrew stuff and get it slide back and forth, then re-screwing and tightening. After unscrewing the two horizontal bars and fooling with it for an hour, I finally was able to screw the vertical members to the TV and get the horizontal bars back on. Sorry, it was 2 yrs ago, I can't give you a step by step.... and I can't fix Peerless's poor documentation here. I wish Peerless would post a video.

The 55\\" was a snap! I bought this one for my parents who have an early 90s built-in entertainment center made out of 3/4\\" Ash. The opening was 50 x 29\\", so perfect for a 55\\" LCD just like the 47\\" was for my kitchen. I was able to mount the back to the TV it straight away. For mounting the base, I decided not to use the wood screws that came with the mount, I didn't want to rely on the 3/4\\" plywood by itself so I took a small piece of 1\\" hard wood and used four 2-1/2\\" bolts with nuts and washers for the 4 base plate mounting bolts. I drilled both the cabinet and the hardwood. Luckily there's a side cabinet to the TV, so everything's hidden, you don't see the bolts and washers.

Like I said, this mounting arm has the longest reach I could find for a large TV.

One note for anyone doing a 55\\" TV, There's one tweak if you want it to fit perfectly, the reach needs an extra 1\\" if you want it to fit perfectly to cover a cabinet opening....

The Amazon product description says:
\\"Extending the flat panel screen up to 27.43\\" from the wall and allowing for a full 180 degrees
of side-to-side motion for perfect view positioning of screens up to 52\\". \\"

The Peerless website actually says 37\\" to 55\\" and 90 lbs. No modern 55\\" weights anywhere near 90 lbs,
even new plasmas are ~70 lbs, less for LCDs.

For my situation, a side cabinet mount, I thought 27.43\\" was perfect for a 55\\" TV in a 50\\" opening. as it turns out, the TV is ABOUT 1/2\\" off center. (Maybe because the base is actually 2\\" behind the cabinet face.) For my installation, it wasn't a big deal, because the TV need to tilted anyway (to keep glare from the windows from hitting the TV). To make it perfect, plan on using a spacer board under the base plate to give you that extra inch.

One of the most critical and difficult things to do (regardless of the type of mount) for precise cabinet mounts is placing the centerline of the base at the right vertical height. It's just math right?! .... After doing all the math on each TV, I was still an inch low in both cases. Luckily there's two jack screws on the TV connection and was able to raise the TV to the precise point.

People are totally impressed with both installations. My only criticism is the documentation, if you have a TV smaller than 55\\", there's a lot of screwing and unscrewing to do to get it mounted to the TV part. The base plate is easy, and hanging to TV to the arm is easy.pressed with both installations. review_headline: I would have given this product 4 stars if it had more mobility and better instructions. The extension is hard to pull out ...
review_body:
Overall, it works. The product instructions are simple, but sparse; and so I think that is why some have had issues with the product. Product is very strong, but also very heavy. I expected this based on the reviews. My application is above a gas fireplace, in between two walls (a built-in space that could hold an older tube TV). This mounting arm allowed me to remove the base from the 55-inch Samsung LED TV and make room for the surround sound receiver and other components in the space. It does that job well. The TV is also able to be tilted down toward the viewers, which is an improvement from the base mount. I would have given this product 4 stars if it had more mobility and better instructions. The extension is hard to pull out and push in but the pivoting of the TV works well.

Supplement to instructions (2 person job): Note: Like other owners of Samsungs, I had to go the store and buy 8mm x 30mm screws to work with my TV. I had to use the spacers provided. The back of my TV looks "flat", but if I would not have used the spacers the brackets would have stressed the TV. Use the spacers - don't risk damaging your TV even if it looks "flat" on the back. Also, I carefully measured to have enough clearance for my receiver (I needed 6.5 inches under the TV), but when it mounted and extended it was an inch too low. If you are doing something similar, give yourself an added inch or so of clearance to allow some sag when fully extended. For those that broke lag bolts, I did not have this issue. But, the instructions said to use a drill bit that is too small in diameter. Use one that is a couple sized larger than the instructions say to use. Hold the drill bit next to to the lag bolt and the bit should be about the size of the bolt minus the threads or just slightly smaller. This will give you the proper size pilot hole and reduce the driving force. Final tip: Noticed some viewers were complaining that even after leveling (yes - don't trust thebuilt in level - I had to use my own), that the TV was tilted. Again, the instructions are not super clear - but they do mention that you can adjust this by pivoting the front bracket plate (no need to loosen nuts). I was able to do this (don't try this by rotating directly on the TV -- apply the force to the brackets that attach to the back of your TV as it takes a bit of force to get it to turn. It is trial and error until you get it right).

product_title: ETON Mini GM400 Super Compact AM/FM Shortwave Radio with Digital Display
review_body:
The Pros:
-Comes with a nice case.
-Seems fairly sturdy in build.
-FM reception is remarkably good.
-Inexpensive.

The Cons:
-No Memory! Uses analogue tuning but will not go back to the previous station after changing bands? Really? Seems to have some sort of memory for shortwave bands but gives no instruction on how to use it.
-Shortwave reception is nearly non-existent. I've used it indoors and out, day and night, and have yet to tune more than three stations. Admittedly the reception in the area I live is lousy, but this is silly.
-Has a lockout function, which is good. The lockout function only affects the power button. So if you put the radio into the belt case you WILL affect the tuning and volume. Which makes the lockout useless.

If I was doing this over again I would save my money for a better unit. And I am doing just that.

Don't let the name fool you. It may say Grundig, but that doesn't mean what it used to.

EDIT: After carrying this radio (in the case, mind you) back and forth to work for a few weeks the buttons have started to fall off. It's about to go in the \\"drawer full of misfit electronics\\" and is being replaced by a Tecsun PL-360. I can't stress enough that this is JUST NOT WORTH PURCHASING!

review_headline: Decent design, substandard sound for piano (distortion)
review_body:
I have other Sangean products that I really like, including a table radio and a shower radio. Those units have great sound. This one has a nice overall design for a portable outdoor unit, but the sound quality is nowhere near as good as the others. I get good reception and live in a close suburb of Philadelphia. However, any music that has piano in it is horribly distorted. Voice only is ok, so it's fine for listening to talk. Most rock is fairly good. But something about the sonic signature of piano music causes trouble. So on NPR, the piano music leading in to All Things Considered sounds like absolute garbage.

And it isn't only because of radio reception. Using the AUX IN feature, the same distortion results. I piped through some Chopin nocturnes, and it sounds like a distorted mess. Go figure.

This is a durable radio and the ability to use (and charge) rechargeable C cells in it is wonderful. Just be forewarned that the audio quality is not up to Sangean's usual standards. Maybe I got a defective unit.

review_headline: Amazing amp for the price, but seriously, realize you are only paying $10... Know what you are getting.
review_body:
This amp is such a deal its unbelievable. It has so much functionality and decent power for a $10 amp if you're smart with it...

This amp features not only a volume knob but also a treble knob, and distortion knob (oops, i mean bass knob) OH I almost forgot it also features a SUPER DISTORTION button... oops again, i mean "super bass".. haha all jokes aside realize you are buying a $10 amp. All knobs actually do serve a purpose (yes even the super bass button does seem to take some power away from mids and add some bass). the sound quality from this amp is GREAT... until you try to push over 10watts of power out of it... any more than that and you enter distortion city. BE SMART ABOUT THIS PURCHASE. what do I mean by that you ask? DO NOT attempt to power 8 OHM speakers of any size, DO NOT attempt to power large 6.5 inch speakers with any expectations...

How do I use this amp? I have this amp hooked up to two 3-inch 4-ohm full range altec lansing drivers rated at 20W in a homemade box. and even such a low power speaker has more potential than with this amp. I deal with these exact drivers all day so I know what they are capable of. So understand that EVEN a 4-ohm 20 watt speaker is a bit underpowered by this amp. That means you WILL be disappointed if you attempt to hook up anything much bigger...

For MY application this amp works wonderfully, I spent $10 and it powers my speakers quite well. Not a whole lot of distortion till I try to push too much bass. They still get quite loud for the little boombox that is my project... MP3 input is a must for me and overall a GREAT unit for the price.

product_title: 3-Outlet Home Network UPS
review_headline: The APC BGE70 works as recommended, but I do recommend the APC BE550G which is the same price and gives you more!
review_body:
As a long time user of APC battery Back-UPS, I was quite amused with seeing the release of the BGE70 Home Network, a Back-UPS designed for low-power devices.

For one, it doesn't use a wall-wart, it's white, there are no basic surge protectors like other APC units but you get an extended 3 hours (on 10 Watts) while 24 minutes (via 75 watts) which is great to maintain a network when it goes down.

I use the BGE70 currently to maintain my router, modem and phone, while I use another APC Tower to maintain my main computer and harddrives and a two BE550G's to maintain my computers and other units.

But the BGE70 works perfectly for what it is made for but should it be $49.99 with only three Back-UPS outlets? Prior to testing out this unit, I thought to myself, why would you get this if the "APC BE550G Back-UPS ES 8 Outlet" is the same price?

For me, I would rather have four Back-UPS outlets versus three and the additional four additional surge protectors, which is a much better deal in my opinion. Sure it's slightly heavier and it's black but if this doesn't bother you...go for the BE550G!

But for aesthetics, no wall-wart and the fact that this device works as recommended, it's definitely worth considering. But truthfully, you can get the even better APC BE550G Back-UPS ES 8 Outlet for the same price, which adds more bang for your buck.

review_headline: Finally able to store > 1,200 Ripped CDs on an audio player.
review_body:
I suspect that I may have had different expectations of this product than many other users, so first let me discuss what I hoped to accomplish by buying this product.

I have a CD collection of about 1,200 CDs which I ripped to FLAC format using EAC. I have been converting them to MP3 files for mobile devices (Android phones, Android tablets, and a Sony mp3 player). For years I have wanted to store *all* of my music collection on a device, with SSD storage.

I am not an audiophile.

I have been using my DX50 for a few days, and so far it has performed well. I was able to access my entire music collection on the device (NOTE: I ordered a 128 gb microsdxc also (Sandisk SDSDQUA-128G-G46A).

The UI is very \\"basic\\" but functional.

I have to remember to never click the \\"all music\\" menu, because it takes multiple minutes to display each track in my over 1,200 albums. The software should be updated to simply NOT render a list of 13,000 items. No one is ever going to scroll through such a list.

Pros:

1) Good sound, at least to my non-audiophile ears
2) Ability to store > 1,200 ripped CDs!
3) The ProStudio Sound & Music seller was very responsive.
4) Uses standard micro usb cables and chargers.
5) Syncs flawlessly with MediaMonkey.
6) Touch screen is reasonably responsive to touch.
7) Solid build quality.
8) Good value (I paid $199 for mine).

Cons:

1) The power adapter made electrical, crackling noises when I first used it. I immediately stopped using it and notified ProStudio Sound & Music. They agreed to send a new one.
2) It is inefficient to scroll through a list of 1,200 albums to find one, especially if the title is towards the end of the alphabet. It is possible to do fast scrolling, but this is difficult to do when the device is in a leather case. It is hard to touch the screen on the far right in order to do this.
3) The power adapter was defective.
4) Battery life seems lower than the ~20 hours I was getting on my old mp3 player.
5) When I received my player, the manufacturer's website was down, so I had to get the firmware update from ProStudio Sound & Music. The website is now online.
6) Screen is small but good enough to find an album and play it.
7) It is awkward to play multiple album sets such as operas. After one ripped CD finishes, I have to go back and find the next CD. I really wish it would just go to the next album in the list and play it, as my Sony player does.

product_title: Elite Screens ezFrame Series, 84-inch Diagonal 4:3, Fixed Frame Home Theater Projection Projector Screen, Model: R84WV1
review_headline: Great Screen, Straight Forward Installation and Performed to Expectations
review_body:
After many reviews and hours of research I finally pulled the trigger on the Cinegrey 5D screen. I watched clips of other screens and am lucky enough to be close enough to Elite and the more expensive competitor, SI, to view this screen and the Black Diamond in person. There is clearly not $1700 dollars difference to justify the more expensive SI BD screen (IMO).

Installation: I was prepared for an exercise in futility after reading some of the other reviews here with regards to putting this together. I cleared an open space, laid down two bed sheets over the hardwood and followed the instructions to put it together. Bolting the frame together was a snap. The instructions were clear and being able to lay it all out made is a snap. The felt overlay has a few little shoddy spots (Black Sharpie fixed that) and doesn't perfectly align in one joint, but it's nothing anyone but me will notice. A cordless power drill had this thing together in about 10 minutes.

The screen, once laid out on the frame was fairly self explanatory. The nice little red arrows on the frame showing where the snaps lock in was a nice addition. The plastic tubes go in like a tent (Make sure to have the shorter ones on the horizontal and the two long ones on the vertical) and then I placed them in the grooved frame and went around the frame pulling it tight and pushing the screen into place and locking it in place with the snaps. I took my time here and stopped a for a beer, but in all it took no more than 15 minutes to get the screen in place. I was a little worried, because once I completed it there were some waves in the bottom of the screen. Not to fear, once the brace was locked into place it pulled everything very tight. I now had a perfectly smooth ready to hang screen. Piece of cake.

Viewing Experience: This section will have an update once my Benq W1070 arrives this week. I used my conference projector as an initial test case. It's an Epson. EX5220, super simple conference room projector and not intended for home theater. I fired it up with the HDMI output from my cable box with no lights and my initial impression was wow. I couldn't believe the picture from this no frills business projector. This thing usually looks washed out with no color pop at all. Then I turned all the lights on in the living room. There are no less than 6 LED lights on and the picture was unfazed. Once again, I was shocked at the picture. Little to no washout at all. Then came the next day. At 2 in the afternoon it's the brightest my living room gets. While there is no direct light, it's still full on daytime. The picture was once again fully watchable with very little washout at all. My wife couldn't tell the difference between the night with all the lights on and the day with the blinds open. I'll give a full review with video once the Benq is installed.

I would recommend this screen for anyone with ambient light issues. You're never going to get the same picture as a fully blacked out room, but IMO this is about as close as you are going to get with the lights on. Also, don't expect miracles if you have sunlight shining directly on your screen. Heck, even LCD and Plasmas have issues displaying properly with that problem. product_title: LABOR SAVING DEVICES 81-130 Creep-Zit" Green Fiberglass Wire Running Kit (LABOR SAVING DEVICES 81130)
review_headline: I was planning on only buying the 3' piece made by the same company and I'm so glad I didn't
review_body:
These things are expensive...... BUT WORTH IT! I was planning on only buying the 3' piece made by the same company and I'm so glad I didn't... at the bare minimum I needed 6' for a basic project and the most I used was 4 of the 5 pieces for a combined length of 24'. I thought I was only going to use these for one or two parts of my home surveillance camera install, but I ended up finding it made a LOT of the tasks easier. Instead of walking across the attic joists to search for the camera hole opening through the insulation, I just pushed a few rods toward the attic door opening. When I went up, they were easy to find and right next the attic door opening. I used electrical tape to tape the ethernet cord to it and pulled it back down.

I have a fishing tape reel that doesn't even compare to these. The fiberglass rods are kind of hard to describe, as they're stiff when you need them to be, but very flexible when you need them to be. In the back of my head, I have the mentality that when items that are stiff and you bend them (especially a significant bend), they will break in half or at least crack. But with the fiberglass rods, it doesn't break or crack and it won't... that's how they're designed.

product_title: 3-Outlet Home Network UPS
review_headline: Keep Connected to the Net When the Power Goes Off
review_body:
This is a really good idea. It's a back up power supply for lower powered devices and the purpose of it is to keep your network up and running. Given that my network is wireless and I have a number of battery powered devises that could connect to the internet even if the electricity is out I decided that this is perfect fit. Really, is there anything worse than sitting in the dark without anything to amuse yourself with?

As pictured there are three two prong sockets. The unit plugs directly into a wall, not into a surge protector or extension cord. I plugged my modem/wireless router for my DSL into one socket, my pogoplug into a second and an external drive into the third. It can support a load of under 75 Watts. The instructions state that when the unit is on battery power and the load is 75 Watts or higher it will automatically shut down. I didn't test that part, just took their word for it.

After I connected and let the battery charge for the required 16 hours, I pulled a circuit breaker and got out my Kindle Fire. I will admit that I went to another room on a different circuit because I still don't much like sitting in the dark. Worked perfectly. It lasted for a little under two hours but the instructions warn the user not to expect full battery capacity after the initial charge.

Of course in a real emergency situation you would want to use it more sparingly, but for those occasional power losses, this is quite handy.

There's a pretty good instruction sheet to walk you through set up and give you warnings about things you shouldn't try to do-- like use the back up outside. All in all a nice package.

ETA: Power did go off for two hours yesterday and this kept the internet ticking along nicely for my laptop, phone and Kindle Fire. It was still going when the power came back on in the office.

product_title: BRAVEN BRV-1 Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker [12 Hours][Waterproof] Built-In 1400 mAh Power Bank Charger - Black / Black
review_headline: (Could Have Been a) Super Little Speaker
review_body: I am heading off to the beach soon for our annual vacation.  Each year the family drags out this old, beaten radio and that's what we listen to; and each year I think \\"man I really need to get an outdoor Bluetooth speaker.\\"  This year I did.  I did my normal research, read reviews, etc.    I decided on the BRV-1.  It arrived in very nice packaging (similar to a GoPro if you are familiar with the way that's packaged).  The first thing I noticed is the size - it's much smaller than I expected.  I saw the measurements, and people saying \\"it's small\\" but I guess I didn't really appreciate that until I saw it in person.    I had no trouble syncing it up to Bluetooth on my iPad mini and S3, and it sounds surprisingly good for it's size.  It's very directional, though.  If the speakers are facing away from you then it would sound noticeably different.  This isn't really a bad thing; for the size and the fact that it's splash proof there must be some concessions, and directional sound is an acceptable one in my opinion.    I didn't turn it up to full volume but did play it pretty loud, the sound quality scales nicely with volume.  Perhaps at full volume it distorts a bit, but for my use the speaker will be fairly close by so I won't be cranking it full volume anyway.    The build quality of this guy is excellent, it looks very well put together and the finish is superb.  It does have some heft for it's size however this, in my opinion, lends more to the feeling of \\"quality\\" rather than \\"just heavy.\\"  The reality is that it is not heavy at all.  If I were going on an extended trek and had to be very conscious of the weight I was carrying, I might consider leaving this behind.  Then again, if a speaker is a consideration for that activity, then I wouldn't be put off by the weight.  The instructions provided get the job done - there's really not too much to it as the functions are straightforward and not at all complex.    I'm looking forward to using the speaker all day - thebattery is rated for 12 hours (assuming you aren't charging something off of it while it plays).  I haven't had a chance yet to see if it actually lasts this long but I do expect it to get pretty close.    There are only a couple things I would have preferred to be different:  1) The speaker does not come with a wall-wart.  It comes with a USB cable to charge it, but no plug that you can stick into a wall.  You must either go buy one or re-purpose another one from your phone or tablet (I used the one that came with my iPad mini).  Of course, you could always plug it into a computer.  For the price, though, I expected a wall-wart.    2) Regarding the charging - I think it's awesome that I can charge a device off of this battery.  And by device, I mean phone.  There's the rub.  I can't charge my tablet.  The amperage on the USB charge port is sufficient for a phone and that's it.  Ultimately, this is okay for me, as I have a dedicated battery for charging phones and tablets.  And the reality is that I will be using this as a speaker, and not a device charger.  So I don't really feel like I lost anything, but rather gained a \\"bonus\\" of also being able to charge a phone from this speaker.  But I sure wish I could also charge a tablet, and perhaps leave the battery behind when weight really is a concern...    Despite the above 2 items, I didn't feel that they were significant enough to warrant the removal of stars.    In summary, I'm really impressed by this speaker (but hey, maybe I'm easy :) ).  This is my first Bluetooth speaker and so far I couldn't be happier.  It looks fantastic, sounds almost as great as it looks, and I can take it pretty much anywhere.  What's not to like?    UPDATE: Well, I brought the speaker to the beach.  We used it the first day, for about 3 hours.  It worked great.  Charged it over night.  The next morning, it would not turn on.  It was completely dead.  I did rinse it lightly the night before to get beach sand off of it - but I didn't doanything stupid like leave the cap off, nor did I submerge it.  I just gave it a quick light rinse, something its IPX5 water-resistance should have no trouble with.  Dead the next morning.  I'm returning it as it must have been defective.  I also knocked it down 1 star - I had expected to use this much more and in more rugged situations before being concerned about it dying.  I was planning on getting another one but opted for a fully waterproof Bluetooth speaker instead.

product_title: SONOS CONNECT Wireless Receiver Component for Streaming Music
review_headline: Sonos Was Cutting Edge Five Years Ago
review_body:
Bought my Sonos system around five years ago and was highly satisfied for a long time. But while they added tons of streaming services (and took some of them away again, somewhat capriciously), software development fully fell by the wayside. Apart from UI polish, the software hasn't changed in 5 years. Same with hardware: it looks slicker and shinier, but it's years old under the hood. 24bit, for example, isn't supported (nor passed through), and there are no plans for a streaming component that would be able to handle it.

But the real howler---and you should be aware of this before you buy---is that you can't have more than 65,000 tracks in your personal Sonos library on your NAS, as their indexing system is infuriatingly old, outdated, and non-sufficient. While 65K looks a lot on the surface (not for all people, but for many), be aware that both long file names and meticulous tagging will take huges bites out of your 65K, so you'll end up with much less at the end of the day. (Therefore, classical music fans especially should be wary and think twice before putting money on the table.) Lots and lots of users at the Sonos forums have complained, suggested possible solutions, or invented convoluted workarounds over the years, but these threads are the very threads (and the only ones) where Sonos reps won't treat. Also, Sonos demoted the 65K limit from \\"problem\\" status to \\"idea\\" status some while ago, which is all you need to know.

To wrap it up: If you'll mostly be streaming from music and cloud services, Sonos is the best streaming solution around. If you have your own music collection on your NAS, and it's a large one, and maybe even full of well-tagged classical music, then you should think twice before investing into a proprietary system that's heavy on marketing and design, but light on technological development.

product_title: Stereo Integrated Tube Amplifier DIY Kit
review_body:
• As an introduction to that relaxing, tube sound, this is a great first amp. It sounds very good.
• As a first tube amp kit, this is a great kit. It is easy to build.

One great thing about this rather bare-bones tube amp kit though is that there are so many ways you can modify it and improve the sound and quality of the amp.

• You can of course try swapping tubes from different manufacturers. Or trying to find matched/balanced tubes. Keep in mind though that these tubes are no longer made and so you're going to have to look online for used tubes.

• Many "tweakers" go straight for higher quality capacitors, especially the so-called "coupling capacitors". For a little extra money you can find more exotic capacitors and replace the ones supplied with the kit.

• Replace the poor power switch.

• The output transformers are adequate but more expensive output transformers can do wonders to carry more of the low end of your sound. With that said however, know that tube amps notoriously underperform with low-frequencies. If you like a lot of bass in your music you'll probably want to pair this amp with a powered subwoofer.

Here are a couple of caveats, however.

• It leaves high voltages exposed. You can remedy this by building it inside of some sort of enclosure. (Search the web for "k12 tube amp" to see what others have done.)

• It gets hot. Such is the case for any tube amp of any significant wattage though. If you build a chassis (see above) and leave the tubes exposed, a metal cage can protect you from the hot tubes. If you don't have kids or keep it on a high enough shelf, you should be okay to just remember not to touch the tubes.

• The power switch is pretty poor.

Given all the above, this is a great place to start. Perhaps, like me, you'll find that years later you're deeper and deeper into vacuum tube amplifiers. This was my first and now, years later, I've perhaps built thirty or more various vacuum tube amplifiers.amplifiers. product_title: Sony Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Wi-Fi Speaker System
review_body:
Pros:
- Great Sound signature (music does not sound coloured)
- Gets fairly loud without crackling
- Small footprint (I expected it to be a little bigger)
- Decent amount of battery backup (approx 5.5 hours)
- Bluetooth connectivity

Cons
- Songpal app is ugly
- No Browser interface for eq settings

Compared to other premium bluetooth speakers:
1. Its nowhere near as bass heavy and artificial sounding as the Bose - When I was listening to a friends Bose Soundlink II I had to restrain myself from throwing that piece of junk out a window for how badly it was mangling some of my favourite songs.
2. The Jambox is more suited to being carried around in a picnic bag, however the sound quality on the Sony handily trumps the Jambox.

I would have loved to compare this to the polk camden square but wasn't able to get my hands on one. Comparing this to a Woodbourne or a B&W A7 would be kind of pointless as at that point you are jumping into a completely different level of speaker system.

I was looking for a bluetooth speaker that would primarily pair with my laptop and if need be could be paired with tablets and/or smartphones. Battery backup was a requirement but I didn't require hours and hours of battery backup - my use case is mostly for the home and for other environments where there are power outlets available. I also wanted something that would support a predominantly mobile lifestyle.

Sound quality was a critical consideration as this would be replacing a larger sound system with a semi-pro amp and high quality bookshelf speakers - Simply put when listening to Pink Floyd, Jethro Tull, Dire Straits and Coke Studio I wanted to be able to hear all the finer nuances of the music as well as pick up the microtones in Remember Shakti's Giriraj Sudha. For the moments when I wanted to listen to ES Posthumus or Beethoven or Sudha Raghunathan the speaker was still able to resolve therecording quite well.

The SRSX7 meets most of my requirements - it does not sound muffled (for a bluetooth speaker) and is able to put out an impressive amount of power while resolving sound quite well for a monopiece bluetooth speaker. It will let me watch a movie at a fairly decent volume as well as enjoy tunes while I continue to work. This has become my primary speaker.

Do not expect to bring the roof down with this speaker. Do not expect to pack a party of 20 people and more and pump tunes above the collective din. You will not be able to have the true stereo resolution from a dedicated 2.0/2.1 system but looking for that from a bluetooth speaker at this price point would be kind of ridiculous. If you want that you should have got a 2.0/2.1 system or spent on a good pair of headphones.

Bass output is more than sufficient unless you listen to r&b and hip hop. In which case buy a pair of beats. I have been able to squeeze up to 5.5 hours of music from the battery backup - however as has been noted in other reviews, there is a perceptible drop in power output when the power cord is unplugged. The ability to connect to Pandora and Sony Music is nice if a bit gimmicky.

The Songpal app works as advertised though i feel that it could have used a bit more polish which I would expect from Sony.

My only complaint is that this seems targeted squarely at smartphone and tablet users. I have a massive collection which is stored on my main computer and would appreciate having a browser interface to tap into the equalizer settings on the speaker.

Is it worth the price? That's a tough question - It delivers almost exactly what I wanted from a personal bluetooth speaker and so made me happy. If you prefer a very r&b/hip hop geared speaker this is not for you. If you like rock/classical (Western and Indian)/acoustic this speaker delivers quite well.

NOTE: I do not have an aptX source - so I cannot speak to sound quality over AptX.

product_title: Amplified HD Digital Outdoor HDTV Antenna 150 Miles Long Range with Motorized 360 Degree Rotation, UHF/VHF/FM Radio with Infrared Remote Control
review_body:
When putting together the antenna, the cable wires would not attach to the antenna. I replaced the cable wires with higher quality radio shack cable wires. Except for that part, the antenna was easy to put together.

I then proceeded to test by attaching the antenna to a USB TV Card to my computer using Windows Media player. My computer is located on the first floor. It pulled in about 10 local channels but would not pull in channel 13 -13.1, 13.2, etc. Still, much better than the paperclip I had attached to my TV Card, which only pulled in one channel.

I moved the antenna to the second floor bedroom and attached it hanging from ceiling pannels. Due to the way I have the antenna installed, it cannot rotate. Channel 13's came in briefly but then disappeared.

I purchased this mainly for the second floor tv local channels as I didn't want to pay for any additional fios or cable boxes. I also wanted something light weight and easy to work with to install indoors.

I wanted to provide some additional information. We live in Lincoln Place, Pittsburgh, PA 15207. We are close to Allegheny County airport. There are a lot of hills and valleys where we live. The two channels that seem to go out and come back in are KDKA (2.1) and Channel 13 (WQED). KDKA comes in most of the time but occassionally fades out. I'm not quite sure where Channel 13 is but I think it might be a lower elevation than ours and it might come in better if I could get the antenna outside and up higher. We don't intend to have this antenna replace our FIOS subscription as it was just purchased for an additional TV.

I am pulling in about 18 channels after moving it to the second floor bedroom. I am satisfied with the way it works.

product_title: SDMX22-004G-PAR
review_body:
This mp3 play is the best of the best! I have had tons of them in the past going back at least 15 years now. Technology has improved through the ensuing decades from when this type of devise was first introduced. One cannot do much better than the SanDisk Sansa Zip. it is tiny but can store tons and tons of books or music files. I clip mine onto my shirt pocket and use a unibud short cord earphone when I am gardening or doing projects which don't involve a lot of concentration. I also subscribe to audible hence have a large supply of downloaded books which fit very nicely on this devise. I prefer this product over the Sandisk Fuse, esp when driving - because the fuse has a "hair trigger" screen. Seems like you just think about touching the fuse and it reacts. The fuse is totally unsuitable for driving because you need to actually look at it to change tracts or pause or backspace or whatever. Not so with this devise. it is NOT touch screen (unlike the Fuze) so you have to physically click it to make it respond. In short order, you will memorize the location of the buttons and you can do so without looking at the devise - handy when driving. Also, it does not have a "hair trigger" so you can't change it by breathing on it (I exaggerate but you get the point). It is hard to say enough positive comments on this little devise. it is the best all around mp3 player I have ever owned - and I have had a ton of them. Several points which folks might find useful. When listening in the car or at home doing desk work - during times when one is likely to pause the devise to concentrate on something - keep it plugged in vs running on battery. Why you ask? Well if you run it on battery and you pause it, the devise will shut off in short order. Then when you are ready to resume listening - say after a tight spot in traffic wherein you shut your audiobook off - you have to restart the devise and it will need to reboot. If you keep it plugged in toyour cigarette lighter jack and you pause it, the devise will not shut down. Now when you hit the replay button, it will start up immediately where it left off without the need to turn on and reboot. Not a huge deal but it makes life simpler. Same with desk work. If you plug it in to an outlet vs running it on battery. Now - when plugged in and you need to pause it - say to answer the phone, or concentrate on something you are doing - it will start right up again after you hit the resume button. No need to wait for the thing to reboot. Other times you DO need to run it on battery - say when you are gardening or cleaning the house or whatever. Here, however, you are less likely to pause it. No need to concentrate much in these settings so you are less likely to shut it off.

Now the way you keep it plugged in is to also buy either a dc or an ac (depending on whether you are in your car or at your desk) charging devise. Here are links to both and a highly recommend you get one of each.
AC: http://www.amazon.com/Belkin-Micro-Charger-Charge-iPhone/dp/B004CLYIZG/ref=pd_bxgy_cps_img_y
DC: http://www.amazon.com/Belkin-F8Z446ttP-iPhone-Charger-ChargeSync/dp/B0047T79TU/ref=sr_1_cc_1?s=aps&ie=UTF8&qid=1404782931&sr=1-1-catcorr&keywords=belkin+micro+charger

The devise comes with the cable so you don't actually need to buy a usb cable to plug into these charger but one can never have too many usb cables. I personally like the colored ones so I have something akin to this item http://www.amazon.com/dp/B00KIBPOUC?psc=1. I like to use a different color for my various devises but that is just me. If your budget is limited, the cable with comes with the devise is enough.

One last thing. It is a very tiny devise and easy to get lost if you are not wearing a shirt with a top pocket. Accordingly, I have also purchased something akin to this item
http://www.amazon.com/Fuel-Card-Key-Ring-Specialist/dp/B004LU5SPW/ref=sr_1_19?ie=UTF8&qid=1404783298&sr=8-19&keywords=plastic+credit+card

I attach a lanyard to it and wear it around my neck when gardening, traveling on a plane, walking/hiking etc. The devise is small enough to fit inside along with a short unibud ear piece. The devise will not get lost and it is ever handy esp on a plane when one can simply pull it out and start listening. Audiobooks makes a 5 hour flight go buy much more quickly and saves the hassle of rummaging through the carry on bag looking for the devise. This devise is very tiny so it can easily slip out of a pocket. This system is esp useful when checking into a hotel after listening to it while driving for several hours. It keeps the devise safe and handy so you can pick right up where you left off when you arrive in your room and start to settle in. A small earbud will fit right into the plastic case as well so you will have both at your finger tips at all times. Handy when you are listening to a really good book. I also keep a charger and an extra cable in my toiletry kit so it is always handy once I arrive at my hotel room. These items are cheap enough that an extra can be stowed away and one need not worry about forgetting to pack the charger. There is nothing worse than being engrossed in a great book while traveling, having a dead battery on your mp3 player and then remembering that your charger is on your nightstand at home. Questions? email me at brennele@npceu.com

product_title: VIBE Sound VS-2006-MTS USB Mini Portable Turntable/Vinyl Archiver (Black) - Rip Your Old Vinyl to MP3!
review_body:
READ ME!
WARNING: This is not by ANY means a top quality product. It's so bad I felt the need to write my first review.

The price is good, its compact, but that's about where the pro's to this thing end.

Also note that I bought an almost new, still in the box, pre-owned one.

First off, there isn't a lever to lift and lower the needle to the record. Bad for your records.
While it says it can play 45s, it doesn't come with an adapter OR a way to change the speed from 33 to 45!
It doesn't play music out of your laptop speakers, you record it and then you can play it back. Or buy a speaker for it.
It skips. A lot. On my best, cleanest, almost spotless records, it skips some. On the old, scratchy, average record you shouldn't even bother trying to convert it. Could just be that the needle that comes with it is sh*tty. It probably is a crap needle, but that might not even be why it skips.
Seriously, it skips A LOT.
Also, it doesn't sit flat on any surface. Very important for a record player to be level.

So there you have it. I gave it 3 stars as a benefit of the doubt, on the off chance it skips SO much because...I don't know. I guess because it does record SOME of my records. Without skipping A LOT. I could get over it not actually playing the records, and not having the lever, and not sitting flat so the records are kinda 'wavy' but maaaaaaaan this thing skips like Alice on the yellow brick road.

Go buy a Stanton USB turntable. If you want one of these, I'll let you get it for $15. Plus shipping.

product_title: Royal WES5000 Wireless Stereo Speaker System
review_headline: TL;DR - Wanted these to work, but ultimately returned them.
review_body:
I live in a 600 square foot studio apartment and have a fairly old flat screen TV that is about 8 feet from my couch. I don't have any speakers attached to the TV, so the only sound comes from the bar speaker underneath the screen. Additionally, I use a portable air conditioner in my apartment that is extremely awesome, but somewhat loud. As such, I have found that it is difficult to hear my TV with the air conditioner running (which is pretty much constantly). Since I try to be a courteous neighbor, I don't want to have the TV blaring, so I looked around for some alternative speaker solutions. As my TV is about 10 years old, it doesn't have Bluetooth capabilities, so that limits my choices somewhat. Also, since I have cats, cords are a dangerous temptation and rarely last very long. As such, I arrived at this product. It was pretty reasonably priced and seemed that it would fulfill its purpose.

Unfortunately, after less than a month of use, I have returned them to Amazon for a refund. This is what my experience with this product was:

1 - Very easy to set up, no problem interfacing with my TV at all. The product came with all the cords needed and everything worked just fine out of the box. Set up in less than 10 minutes and working just fine.

2 - From the start the speakers would conk out intermittently. However, a small shake of the speaker and the sound came back. No idea why the sound would stop and start. It didn't seem to have anything to do with location or volume, they would just stop working. This happened every single time they were used. Annoying, but not insurmountable.

3 - These are incredibly awkward as far as shape and size goes. My husband has larger hands than mine and can palm them quite comfortably. The speakers are about the size of a large grapefruit and are just a bit too large for me to be able to grasp easily - I was constantly losing my grip on them and always needed two hands to pick them up and move them around. They are round with a small flat spot on the bottom. Unfortunately, the flat spot is REALLY small and they tend to tip over and roll if they get jostled or bumped. The entire surface is smooth and there is no traction on them at all. So, very tricky to handle and move around without dropping them. If you are using them around a hard-surfaced floor, be extremely careful.

4 - From the first use, there were continuous intermittent crackles and pops. These could be fairly minor or they could be loud enough to drown out the sound entirely.

5 - After about two weeks of use, the volume dropped to almost nothing. I have no idea why, but even with the volume at the maximum level on each speaker, you could barely hear anything at all. The last few days we were actually holding the speaker up to our ear in order to hear anything out of it. Initially, the volume level was great - it just seemed to deteriorate greatly over time, to the point that they are now useless.

6 - Possibly the most annoying factor of all - the base goes to "sleep" with any interruption. If you finish a show and pause for a moment before starting another, the base shuts off and the speakers no longer receive any signal from the TV. If you pause a movie to get some popcorn, the base shuts off. This isn't even a power-saving feature that I can see - the base is plugged into the power outlet and the speakers themselves run on a charge, but the speakers don't go to "sleep." Weird and inconvenient.

Overall, these seemed like a good solution to a minor problem. Ultimately, they just did not prove effective. To give some additional information about my entertainment center set-up - I have a single flat-screen TV, no DVR, no DVD player, no gaming consoles, no stereo equipment, no cable box, no satellite receiver. We don't have "live" TV, we only using streaming services routed through a wireless Roku. There is no internet connectivity directly to our TV at all. The TV has power to the wall and the Roku is hooked directly to the TV. That's it. I don't see that there was much chance of interference from other pieces of equipment.

Well, I hope this was helpful to anyone looking at these speakers. Good luck in your search!

product_title: OontZ Curve Bluetooth Speaker Ultra Portable Wireless Full 360 Degree Sound with Built in Speakerphone works with iPhone iPad tablet Samsung and smart phones - Platinum Silver Curve Platinum Silver
review_body:
I bought the Oontz Curve and three other highly portable bluetooth or wired speakers: the Roverbeats T3, the Kinivo ZX100, and the iHome iBT60 (the last from Walmart). This review concerns the Oontz curve. It is precisely the size indicated in the photo, and the model I received has a blue anodized finish. A voice informs you when it is connected, kind of a nice feature, especially vs. the bells and pops of the other three. I listened to it in four settings: my car with the sunroof open on the freeway; our kitchen (large with many reflective surfaces), our bedroom (many absorbing surfaces), and outdoors. I played Beethoven's Third (mid-range and base intensive), Jack Johnson's "The Horizon Has Been Defeated" (mid-range intensive) and Lady Gaga's "Born This Way" as extreme comparative cases. I also made dinner listening to tracks from Miles Davis's "Giant Steps".

In my car the Oontz fits exactly in a cupholder but because its speaker points straight up, this has no impact on its sound. The white noise in the car pretty well kills the treble part of any music unless it is really cranked up. The Oontz has very good midrange to base response, and so sounded very similar whether the ambient noise level was high or low. In my kitchen it sounds a bit flat because its treble response is not as bright as the other models I tested. In the bedroom and outside the audio performance was quite good, not like a pair of stereo speakers, but what the heck, this thing is the size of an apple and cost $30, so no complaints.

Beethoven and Jack Johnson both sound fine on this speaker, but Lady Gaga, other pop music, and Miles Davis sound a bit tinny: again, it was $30, fits in my hand, and if I need to move but am in the middle of listening to something, I just carry it with me. A bit of tinny sounds seems like a reasonable trade-off for so much convenience.

If you connect the Oontz to your phone, then you can take advantage of two very nice features. First, if you have audio reminders for your calendar, email, etc., it faithfully amplifies them, so you can walk away from the phone (and speaker) and still remain on top of your schedule. Second, it will ring when your phone rings, and if you press the blue LED button on the top of the unit, it will answer and work as a speaker phone. I hadn't paid attention to this feature when selecting it, but it is very handy if you are in the car or if your hands are a mess and you still want or need to take a call. I have a hands-off speaker in my car that has been a world of frustration to deal with, and the Oontz this officially replaced it. It also has buttons at the base that will stop or start a track, go back to the beginning, or advance to the next track. Since my phone goes to a log-in screen after 30 seconds of neglect, this is a great feature and minimizes my interaction with the phone while driving.

Finally, I have been using it more or continuously for 4 hours this morning and for another couple of hours yesterday (including my sound test) with no more than the original factory charge. This seems more than reasonable for battery life.

If your environment has absorbing surfaces or white noise, or you'd just like the convenience of being able to use a bluetooth speaker as a speaker phone, then look no further. Highly recommended.
