I finally decided upon and purchased this Denon AVR-X3000 home theatre receiver in April of 2014, and it is one of the best electrical/technological purchases I've made in 37 years of life on planet Earth. Having never owned or worked with home theatre systems & receivers, I found this complex-performing machine relatively easy to set-up (though time-consuming as I learned about such systems while installing it) with my various devices: Samsung LED 3D 55" TV, Xbox One, Blu-Ray 3D Player, and our Cox HD DVR box. The easy-to-follow on-screen instructions were very helpful and intuitive, as is the software in every regard. It's an easy plug-and-play piece of hardware. Likewise, the Denon Receiver Remote is extremely simple and functional. Every commercial, TV show, music video, and movie is like a miniature IMAX THX experience. The sound-quality is utterly mind-boggling. Immediately upon finishing up installation at 11:00 PM on a Wednesday night, I was captivated and unmovable for the following 3 hours as I watched "Man of Steel" and several other programs to experience and immerse myself in the system. I still need to finish up wiring the second zone, buy an ethernet to run from our Cox Modem to the Denon LAN to set up the various networks such as AirPlay, and do a few other things, but thus far I cannot fathom recommending anything other than this receiver. product_title: Eagle Aspen EASDTV2BUHF Directv Approved 2-Bay UHF Outdoor Antenna
review_headline: Works great in the attic, we had no need to mount outdoors
review_body:
Bought this antenna, expecting to be required to mount it on a pole outside.

However, before I went to all that work, I hung it on a nail in my attic, just to see what I could pick up. I live in Florida, which is pretty flat, so I was hopeful that it would pick up some stations.

To my delight, the antenna picks up ALL the UHF broadcasts in the area. According to AntennaPoint.com, we are up to 47 miles away from most of the stations' towers. Unlike our old UHF antenna (a cheap indoor model), this antenna gets them all.

To get the lone VHF station in the area (which broadcasts NBC), I also mounted a set of rabbit ears in the attic, and connected the rabbit ears and this antenna together into a 2-to-1 RF splitter. The single output of the splitter goes to a RF amplifier from Radio Shack. The RF amp pushes the signal into four cables, via a 1-to-4 splitter, with the 4 cables going to all the TV's in my house. All the TV's get all of the channels.

No need to mount this antenna outdoors, at least for us. We are very happy with our purchase, and will be recommending this antenna to everyone we know who chooses over-the-air TV broadcasts.

product_title: ZVOX 580 Low-Profile Single-Cabinet Surround Sound System with Optical and Coaxial Digital Inputs
review_body: While on sound quality alone, this unit would get five stars, I purchased two 580's both having the same intermittent problem. The signal from the center array of speakers would stop playing altogether. After unpacking the second one and discovering the same issue, we looked for a system with comparable sound quality but could not find anything. So I decided to crack open the 580. It turns out that a small plastic connector used to link the amp head to the speakers was loose, and the design placed this connector upside down when the unit is in use, causing gravity to pull the connector out of its position. For me is was an easy fix to permanently attach the speaker leads to the amp head by soldering the wires directly to the pins. Problem solved. We use the 580 in conjunction with a 50" plasma in the master bedroom, and sound quality is as high on my list as ease of use is on my wife's list. This unit meets both of our qualifications. While reading other reviews, this does seem to be a common issue. It maybe linked to one particular manufacturing batch, or just a design flaw waiting to manifest on every system. Either way since it was a simple fix for me, I left the review at four stars, for meeting our requirements.

product_title: Beyerdynamic Headphone Ear Pads Black
review_headline: Worth the price of admission (shoulda been OEM from the start)
review_body: I've owned my MDR-V6's since I first auditioned them in 1986 and blew all my birthday money on a pair.  Since then, they've been with me since the teenage years jacked into my Numark mixer, the college years keeping the noise down for my roommate, my first job in post production at Raleigh Studios, law school and then entertainment clients' editing bays and recording studios (every one has had at least one set of these cans).  They are still in great shape and are my go to headphones despite trying a myriad of noise cancelling, noise isolating in-ear, over the ear, behind the neck, wired, wireless, bluetooth, carved from wood, bullet shell casings and everything in between.  The sole complaint has always been the period deterioration of the ear pads.  After going through several pairs of Sony's replacements, which have never been improved but for the early change from acoustic foam to the current fabric cover in the middle, I switched to the Beyerdynamics.  At more than twice the price of the Sony replacement pads, they are definitely worth it.  The fit perfectly.  In fact, they move less than the OEM pads.  The velour does not get as hot as the OEM pleather which just gets nasty with sweat after a long listen, particularly if you are using them as DJ monitors in a hot club.  Sonically, they sound just as good and do not allow any more outside noise.  I know that Sony has long been at odds with keeping the MDR-V6s in production, but obviously the consumers are committed to these excellent headphones, and as the saying goes, "if it ain't broke..."  Then again, they could always try something radical and ditch the crappy pleather pads in favor of something exactly like these BeyerDs.  I'd love to be able to buy another set for my friends, nephew, clients or colleagues.  Until then, just don't wait 28 years to make the switch to the EDT 250s.

My biggest complaint would have to be the ear pads. You HAVE to buy vmoda's XL ear pads to be able to wear the headphones comfortably for long stretches of time. However, I've noticed that the XL ear pads, while they have a ton more comfort when you first get them, but over time, the pads start to flatten down. Heat is somewhat of an issues in the XL pads over the stock pads. In the stock pads, my ears sweat very easily. In the XL pads, it takes 3-4 hours of usage before i have an issues like so.

Though I love the sound quality, comfort is a very huge issue when purchasing \\"quality\\" items. How can you expect someone to listen to something great if they are physically uncomfortable?

If you guys are reading this, I would suggest a new type of ear pads.
If you notice some headphones have felt/cloth material on the outside of their headphones, have the inner chamber of the pad be pleather, and the majority of the ear pad that touched the head be cloth/felt. I would assume it would keep the sound stage similar, and not change the characterists of the m100 too much.
I would also HIGHLY suggest a new type of foam ear pad material for the XL pads. The stuff in the XL pad loses shape much too quickly, and I tempted to find another headset because I don't want to constantly keep buying new ear pads.

product_title: Sony NWZE38 Walkman MP3 Player
review_headline: Not the same as the older models.
review_body:
I have been a user of Walkman mp3 players since 2008, and have owned several. I loved the side volume and hold buttons, navigability that can be memorized, and overall easy to use. I would purchase one a year on average because I am very rough on them, and they really took beatings, so a few years ago I bought a few and my last recently broke of a cracked screen. I was reluctant to purchase a newer model; they seem smaller, I was very used to the built in stereo of previous models (even if they didn't last long from dirt build-up), and honestly I don't care for the design pattern on the outside... but upgrading to a newer model was a lot cheaper than finding used old models I was bound to break immediately.
Upon receiving the mp3- I was confused on where the volume or hold buttons are. The volume button can only be accessed from the "now playing" screen, and always defaults back to a middle volume. The hold button is consolidated into the Power and option button- Which doesn't seem logical to me at all, considering the Hold button is used to lock the buttons- not turn off the mp3. product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_body:
Harmony remotes have always been a step ahead of other remotes because they can be programmed using an intuitive program on your computer instead of flipping through countless code books and punching in sequences of numbers and watching flashing lights. You answer questions like: "What kind of TV do you own?" and "When you watch TV, which devices need to be on?" Then, when you are done, you plug in a USB (included) and let it download the instructions to the remote.
The setup does take a while the first time but the questions are easy to understand and the categories are very simple. If you need to make an adjustment, you simply open the program and change the way a button works or what happens when you hit "Watch Movie" button.
I like some extras in the programming department, as well. The first is the ability to tell the Harmony about a unique button that your remote has but the Harmony for some reason does not have an option for. For example, I had 'mapped' all the buttons to their proper new buttons on the Harmony but I was missing the option for 'video source.' I simply told the program to learn a new command, plugged it into my computer, then pointed the old remote at the new remote and pressed the button I needed. In a couple seconds, it had learned the new command and then I was able to map that command to a certain button. Very nice to be able to add literally countless numbers of commands particular to your remote.
I used to have a Harmony H659 (bought it 10 years ago and loved it) which I would still be using if I hadn't dropped it one too many times (more like 1 million too many times) before the screen stopped working. To say that moving to the new remote was easy does not give it justice. Opened the Logitech program, told it I bought a new remote, and all my previous commands and devices were moved to the new remote. I did have to program the contextual buttons again, though but only because the new remote only has 4 such buttons instead of the 6 on the old remote. Everything else switched over perfectly- even the delay my TV needs to switch between inputs after it initially turns on. Easy, easy, easy.
The only comment I might make on this new remote is it feels a bit less ergonomic than the one I'm replacing. There is one big, rounded area at the bottom that fits nicely into your hand but the rest of the remote is totally flat. I found my hands missing the 'notches' on the back where my index finger and middle finger would naturally rest and balance the remote in my hand. My family commented that the new remote looks more 'stylish' and 'modern' but I still can't get used to how bottom-heavy the remote is and how it feels like it might slip out of my hand. I suppose I will adapt eventually.
There are a few new additions, however that help make this more modern. The first is the inclusion of the Red, Blue, Yellow, Green buttons found on many DVD, Blu-Ray, and Cable remotes. These are the blank buttons that depending on what is needed, the device will ask you to 'press yellow to accept' or 'press blue to search.' Having them right on the remote saves having to add them to the programmable screen at the top.
Not mentioned in most descriptions of this remote, there is a backlight to the buttons. I have not used it in a dark room yet, but I was concerned that the remote didn't have it so I'm pleasantly surprised to see it included.
Also nice is the separate up/down button just below the screen. I mapped that to be "page up" and "page down" so when I am scrolling through a long list I can quickly navigate. The play-pause-FF-RR buttons have all moved up to the middle of the remote instead of being all the way at the bottom on my old one. Your thumb is naturally right on top of them and between my DVR and Netflix instant, I use those a lot more than I ever used to 10 years ago.
In addition, I am a fan of the haptic response you get when you press the buttons. You know the signal was sent because you feel the 'click' under your thumb and that is a huge improvement over my previous Harmony.
And the designers have included a really nice feature where the remote's screen and backlight turn on when you pick it up or tilt it in your hand. It turns off after a programmable amount of time to save battery.
You need to spend a little time setting this up but once you do, you'll be able to put away the other remotes and just use this. You'll be able to switch between watching TV to watching a movie to listening to the radio to whatever else you want to do in a snap and with only one remote. No more "Turn on TV, pick up other remote, turn on home theater, switch input to DVD player, pick up another remote and turn on DVD player, etc., etc., etc.," From now on, you just need one remote.
Do yourself a favor and get this or any other Logitech Harmony remote.

review_headline: IR receiver and Logitech Harmony Remotes including 520
review_body:
I can confirm that the Harmony 520, and probably many other Harmony remotes that are purported to not work with this IR receiver, does in fact work. However, there's a bit of a trick to it: along with setting up the Harmony remote to use the ChinaVasion CVSB-983 profile as has been covered in earlier comments, with some Harmony remotes there is an extra step one must take before it will work: you have to assign the buttons in the Harmony remote software manually. There are two totally separate areas in the Harmony desktop software to assign buttons. One is in the Devices manager and one is in the Activities, themselves. While you can use the Device manager to change buttons, these changes will not be carried over on some Harmony remotes, because the button layout in the Activities remain unchanged. Instead, on the page where your activities are listed, click the button marked "Customize Buttons" under each activity that you want to use the ChinaVasion profile on and manually assign the buttons and update the remote. You will now be able to use the Harmony 520, and probably all others, with this IR receiver.

Good luck.

Now let me say that both are very well made and regardless of your decision you will be buying a premium equipment. When it comes to the final results I have to say with regrets that the Bose Mini got beaten by quite a margin by the Marshall Stanmore speaker ! It was almost shocking ! I expected a hard fought battle but had to stop the experiment after only 5 mns!

The Bose renders the sound well but there is no real ooomph factor to it, the bass is artificially boosted and lacks of real depth, the rest seem accurate. In contrast the Marshall, really benefits from its bigger size; it renders an incredible sound with a very deep, warm and punchy bass - which is extremely attractive to any audio purist !

The blind tests done with relatives confirmed my first impressions. Almost all the members said that it was no contest and that the first speaker (MARSHALL STANMORE) was clearly superior. I tried a few adjustments on the Bose to make the comparison fair but in vain, I simply couldn't make them sound equal. For illustration, I had to adjust the volume of the Bose Soundlink mini to almost 100% to make it stand up to the Marshall which was merely set at 30% !

I have retained the Marshall with its retro look and unique appeal. Hope this review will help someone in the future ! There is more than BOSE in the music world !

product_title: Cowon iAUDIO 9 16 GB Mp3 Player
review_body:
This is (or should I say was) my second iAudio9. The first I9's battery overheated, expanded and cracked the entire i9 housing after a few years of use. I regretfully replaced it with another i9 which lasted just over two years. First , a note about the accessories. In that time, I've replaced the proprietary USB cable 4 times and the optional mini USB jack twice. Both the cable and the jack tend to become loose which makes maintaining a link to your PC or other devices nearly impossible. Given that COWON uses a proprietary port and not your standard mini/micro USB, means I've spent nearly $50 on cables alone, which is frankly ridiculous.

When working, the player is great. Jeteffect 3.0 and BBE were extremely useful when it came to tweaking the overall sound of the i9 to suit my tastes. I've gone through a bunch of IEMS while using the I9 and I was able to adjust the EQ to suit each of their sound signatures. The UI, while slightly odd, is easy to learn while the capacitive touch screen,for me, was responsive. The battery life is phenomenal and recharged quite quickly via my computer's USB ports. I was also able to easily connect to my car's audio system using the car's USB port. The I9 is also quite slim and was great as a workout DAP. Some might find 16gb to be lacking but it worked well with my listening habits. I have quite a bit of music (couple hundred physical albums and a couple hundred digital albums) but I would regularly wipe my I9 to avoid listening to the same albums.

The problem with my second I9 began when the USB port would not make a secure connection with the USB cables. Some how, the USB port became warped as neither my USB cable nor my mini jack would insert all the way. This lead to connection issues: if you were to look at the I9 wrong, the device would disconnect/reconnect. It was only an hour or two after I discovered the USB port issue that the I9 no longer powers on.

Pros:
+Portable
+ Easy UI ( not a steep learning curve)
+ Audio
+ Battery Life
+ microphone (recorded a lot of lectures with it)

Cons:
- BUILD QUALITY
- plays videos.. but why?
- proprietary cables

I'm done with COWON. For all the good things the I9 can do, the fact that it's built like a Happy Meal toy is frustrating. From here I'm moving on to a Fiio X3 and hoping they build something that can last longer than 2 years.

product_title: 25 Taiyo Yuden Bluray Discs 4x Speed 50 Gb Bd-r Dl Original No Logo for Professional Use Blueray
review_body:
Similar to the known quality of Verbatim. I did not know that Taiyo Yuden is under the name, That's. "That is quality." Whatever. These burn very well in an external Buffalo BDXL drive. Unfortunately, my DigiStor external drive failed quite recently and had to be pitched.

As far as the difference of this brand versus Verbatim, the near inner edge of the That's discs do not appear to have the protective coating on the read/write side, either because it is not present, or covers the entire disc. Still, CDs and DVDs scratch easily compared to Blu-Ray ones. It somehow resembles the CD-RW slightly more scratch-resistant than CD-R.

Good luck trying to find BDXL for under $40, or more than 1 disc. 128 GB BDXL do not even exist. I have searched the Internet, no such product. Maybe the Blu-ray industry does not tell you that they learned the same lesson trying to get CD-R at 99 minutes to burn and read without problems in your CD player. 50 GB is more affordable, and takes up less space than 25 GB BD-R. Cost per gigabyte may be better on single-layer 25 GB ones, but compared to Double Layer DVD blanks, the Blu-ray are a lot more reliable. Also note that in my experience, internal writers that cannot seem to read a disc written a year or two ago can be read in an external drive. Laptop computers with internal writers often do not burn a disc correctly, rendering the disc unreadable.

That said, I highly recommend this brand, and for Verbatim (Mitsubishi Chemical) as well. The burned image on the That's may be a little better, but this is a visual thing. Burn these at 2X speed to avoid reading problems in the future. Take my advice, I have burned a lot of discs and know things that many people would not consider. Good luck, and be coaster-free. If you do have a coaster, shred the disc if it contains personal information.

I haven't tried it with any other players to test the integrated function, but this is the one I prefer to use when doing activities anyways. I bought these to replace some beloved Sennheiser PMX 680's that I seem to have lost somewhere =(

Oh yeah, and they sound wonderful, have no listener fatigue (like the pathetic toys that seem to proliferate the marketplace these days), are super light and comfortable, and don't fall out or pull annoyingly downward like other gravity-suffering earbuds!!

These easily clear most bike helmets and hats too, a definite bonus!!! I also love the little clip to reduce cord weight and bounce. I wish I could buy extras though, that is my next mission, since they are easily lost.

Thumbs up all the way Sennheiser!!!!!

product_title: Channel Master UHF and HDTV Antenna
review_headline: May be a cheap "clone" re-branded as "Channel Master"
review_body:
Pros: Brand name (questionable - see comments); Compact Size (not 100% clear what that is - see comments); Good reputation; 90 days warranty (which is a "Con" as much as it is a "Pro").

Cons: Poor documentation; Support - very polite, yet not very helpful; Short warranty when compared to other manufacturers; Is this a discontinued product ?!?

Comments:
I have a very diverse (and difficult to deal with) mix of local and distant stations, so before ordering I needed some relevant technical information. I know enough about RF to be aware that "Antenna range" is irrelevant. The manufacturer's web site shows "technical data" on 3 different pages, but that data is incomplete and inconsistent, as if someone mixed up, randomly, specs taken from at least 2 different antennas.
Called Channel Master technical support and asked for a gain/frequency chart and radiation patterns (these are basic antenna parameters, just like asking about engine capacity, horse power and torque when talking about a car). After checking with managers and engineering, the support representative told me that the company does not have such data for this antenna. That can only mean that CM did not design this antenna; and neither did any quality control testing on it. Asked if this antenna was re-designed recently, and the self-contradicting specs on the web site is a transition thing. The answer was that this antenna design is at least 5 years old.
So, for 5 years (or more), CM is selling an antenna that they did not design or test, and they never took the time to even document it consistently on their own web site. There are a lot of un-documented "clones" out there, that sell for up to $30. Could it be that Channel Master took one of those, put their name on it, and are trying to sell it for twice the money (or more)?
In the end, the CM-4221HD may be better, worse or the same as other antennas. In my opinion, it isthe manufacturer's job to test and prove their product's performance; I am not going to do this job for them, and pay them while I'm doing it, too.
If you think this antenna is worth the price, go for it.

product_title: Optical Quantum OQBDR04LT 4X 25 GB BD-R Single Layer Blu-Ray Recordable Logo Top
review_headline: Great Media - Burns well consistently using the FREE program Imgburn!!
review_body:
Pros: I've purchased numerous 50pks of these OQ discs and they have burned flawlessly for me on my 3 LG burners (WH14NS40, WH14LS38, WH12LS30)! . These discs can really be a great buy especially when on Sale! I recommended these discs to a neighbor and he is very happy with them as well! I have also used OQ 6X media as well as their BD-R DL media with great results too!
By the way, the maximum available space that can be used on 25GB media is: 23.3GB and for 50GB (dual-layer), it is 46.6GB. That is because Windows sees media the same way that is sees Hard Disc Drive capacity, do a google search if you need more info about that.

For those reviews that mentioned having playback problems on a Sony set-top Blu-Ray player, TRY updating the FIRMWARE of the player (Internet connection is needed) and see if that doesn't solve playback problems. I have a Sony player and have NOT had ANY problems playing this or other BD-R media.

In case anyone is interested, the LT in the description of this media means Logo Top - NOT LTH as I have seen some others post on a different website (Newegg) LTH Blu-Ray media writes differently and is very finicky with the burners that it will write with, so I wouldn't recommend them (LTH Media). Logo Top simply means there is the Optical Quantum name printed on the top side of the media - hence Logo Top. Also, if anyone is curious, the Media ID for these discs is: Philip R04-000 --- Imgburn will also give you the REAL manufacturer of any brand media regardless of what the Media name is; by that I mean Verbatim, Sony, Memorex, OQ, etc. are not necessarily/usually made by the name branding of the media. That is normal for any media.

Other Thoughts: As I've mentioned, this are a great buy. While these discs can burn much faster than 4X, I use ImgBurn to set the WRITE speed to 4X/6X just to make sure I have good quality burns. Imgburn is a FREE burning program that can be used to set the burning (writing) speed of DVD/Blu-Ray media so that you will get good quality, consistent burns - you can find it easily by doing a Google search. Imgburn will also find any Firmware updates that are available for any brand of Blu-Ray burner that you are using - this is a very valuable tool to have to find Firmware updates!!

Just because you can burn this Media at a faster speed than what it is rated for DOESN'T mean that you should - that is what causes burning/playback errors ----- that is why I recommend using Imgburn to set the burning speed. The lower burning speed may take a few minutes longer in the process, but it is well worth it to make sure that you have Quality burned media - why be in such a hurry and have problems!!

I tend to listen to music during my commute to and from work, and having used headphones previously that I could simply wrap around my phone and use whenever I wanted, I found the Monster Turbines to be extremely difficult to whip out and put in my ears. The large button half-way up the wire prevents does not allow the now useless (and hard-to-move) wire clip to reach the top of the wire, so that more often than not I have to untangle the earphones before using them. Even this proves more difficult than usual as the wires are rather heavy and resistant to being bent this way and that.

Most notable however is the inability to disable the large button that switches tracks and changes volume. If you are one to keep your earphones plugged into your audio device so that you can use them at any time with minimal effort, then do not buy the Monster Turbine Pearl. The button is more likely to be pressed inadvertently and you might find your device playing loud music out of your pocket without your realizing it. Your only choice is to keep the earphones unplugged before using it, and at this point I am more willing to buy earphones that do not have the stupid large button.

I can only imagine one use case for these earphones, and that is when you have the space and the 45 seconds to actually take these out, and plug them in before listening to music. To me, this contradicts the primary motivation behind earphones, which is their portability.

product_title: Photive BTH3 Over-The-Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Built-in Mic and 12 Hour Battery. Includes Hard Travel Case.
review_body:
Bought these to replace a pair of Jabra Halo Bluetooth headphones that keep falling off my head now. Actually they were 1 of 3 I bought at the same time. The other 2 went back because 1 slid off my head if I so much as looked down at the ground, and the other moved around a lot (though didn't fall right off). The BTH3's are by far the most stable; even vigorously shaking my head couldn't dislodge them. If you plan to exercise with your headphones, or want them to stay on when you reach down for something, these are the Bluetooth headphones you're looking for.

Sound quality is excellent. They're not noise cancelling or isolating, but I wear them on my daily commute, and I want to hear the announcements on my train and traffic around me on my walk. So these are perfect.

The battery life is also very good. My Halo's are a few years old and even though I only wear them for my 1 hour commute twice a day, I have to charge then daily now. The BTH3's last all week!!

A couple minor cons: it sends a battery life signal to my iPhone 5, which shows up beside the Bluetooth icon. But it always reads full charge, for some reason. And it doesn't do multipoint, so only 1 device at a time. May not be a big deal for most, but multipoint means I could connect to my iPod Classic (with Bluetooth adapter) and iPhone, and it'll pause the iPod music and switch to the iPhone when a call comes in.

Overall, I want to give these a 4.5, but I can't, and given how long it's taken to find Bluetooth headphones I can be active in, docking a full star seems harsh. So 5 stars it is.

review_body:
These Monster headphones claim to offer superior sound quality because they contain no \\"live electronics\\" or batteries. The sound quality is pretty good. In the past I've found that Koss headphones offer great sound. I can't say that these Monster headphones sound superior to Koss, but they're easily as good.

I currently use an [[ASIN:B002HWJT1A Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint]] headphone, because it offers noise cancellation. (They were the cheapest noise cancellation headphones I could find.) Naturally, Audio-Technica contains \\"live electronics\\" and requires a single AAA battery. Despite that, it sounds as good as the Monster, at least to my ears. So I'm not convinced that the tradeoff -- no \\"noise cancellation\\" on the Monster so as to avoid \\"live electronics\\" -- is worth it.

The Monster headphones do a fine job on sound quality, but if there's an air conditioner running, I'll opt for the Audio-Technica. Monster claims that its foam padding around the ears does a great job blocking outside sound. They are good, but no better than the foam padding around the Audio-Technica.

The Monster headphones fit comfortably.

Neither Monster or Audio-Technica have volume control knobs.

The Audio-Technica must be turned on. Monster, having no \\"live electronics,\\" naturally does not need to be turned on.

The Monster headphones' packaging refers to something called the Monster Power Card, which can be recharged through a USB port. I'm not sure what this Power Card is, but no Power Card came with my Monster headphones.

Monster headphones derive their power from the source (e.g., a laptop, TV, CD player), so I'm guessing the Power Card is used if the source doesn't have enough power to run the headphones. But I've found that my laptop, TV, and CD player are more than capable of supplying the Monster headphone with all the power it needs.

review_headline: Perfect for getting AppleTV Analog Audio
review_body:
My one use for this product was to split the Hdmi signal from my AppleTV(3rd gen) to 1) an Hdmi input on my Yamaha receiver and 2) an analog audio input on the same receiver. Because Zone 2 on the amplifier will process only the unit's analog inputs, this is the only way to run audio from the AppleTV to Zone 2 (patio speakers in my case.) After reading many reviews for many similar products I chose the Premium Quality Hdmi To Hdmi + 3.5mm Stereo Audio Extractor Converter for my project.

The factors I read in the reviews and bore true in final usage were these:
1) Both the Hdmi passthrough signal and the analog RCA output remain active at all times -- no switching required.
2) The passed through Hdmi signal seems to be as strong as the original. (No picture loss on anything I've watched so far including a 1920x1080 H.264 23551 kbps video streamed from my iTunes on the Home Sharing computer.)

The unit is powered by a 5V USB power supply with the cable included. The one thing I would wish for on this unit would be a USB power supply. It clearly stated in the description that it was not included so I can't ding the product for not including it. It would be nice if they even sold one as an add-on for $3-5. As is I had an extra one that I use on trips. I'll now have to "steal one" for my next trip.

All in all this purchase has been everything I hoped for. I now can watch movies from my AppleTV inside and step outside and listen to my playlists out on the patio. Thanks J-Tech!

review_headline: Great cans for your average young adult
review_body:
Alright. I picked these up for $100 at Best Buy. I went around testing all the available models they had and these stood out with the price point and sound. (They easily beat all of the Beat's in sound quality, AND comfort)

Comfort was a big deal to me, I spend a lot of time studying and playing games with my friends, so lasting comfort was a must, especially with me wearing glasses. These feel great. I can get into a study/game session for 6 or more hours and sometimes forget they're even on. They don't seal great, which is fine with me because I want to be able to hear how loud I'm talking while gaming or if someone calls me.
One small problem is that the headband isn't the softest and can begin to make the top of your head sore. Simply elongate the headphones, and move the pads to have your ears support them more, taking some weight off of the band. Problem solved!

Comfort - 9.5/10 even with my glasses on

Admittedly I'm somewhat of a basshead. I love electronic music and alternative rock. These things are super versatile. I usually keep the bass adjuster around 25%, and that works great for subtle rumbling and great sounding bass. Whenever I'm in the mood, I can turn the bass all the way up and enjoy my music for a bit. Also sounds great for movies and games, being around or inside a tank in Battlefield is an experience not like any other headphone has offered me

Sound - 9/10, pair these up with an EQ and they will sound great.

While they don't feel too expensive, I'm not worried because Skullcandy headphones come with a lifetime warranty, so I'm covered! Definitely stylish enough for me to wear around college and get compliments!

I didn't really have a lot of respect for Skullcandy years ago around 2009, but I was Wowed by the new Crushers, completely blew away the old trashy Skullcrushers.
Skullcandy is stepping their game up, and I'm quite impressed with them.

product_title: Antennas direct, inc
review_body:
Apparently those who say they can't get reception with this antenna don't understand the basics of setting up an antenna and reprograming after each adjustment. I bought the DB4E as my first step in cutting the cord. Sick of paying eighty dollars plus per month for 150 channels and watching only three consistently. Two of which are local. I had a small problem with assembly due to a manufacturing error. Customer service was rapid in offering three solutions for the problem and explaining the situation. Human error is an occasional factor and has to be expected. This was an error in bolt and sleeve hole size and I doubt quality control would have noticed without having assembled an antenna. Point being...an error was made...it was corrected rapidly and with apologies.
'nuff said about that.
Now about the reception. I live 40 mile south of the primary transmitter farm in Knoxville TN with some terrain issues. (foot hills of the smokies). I tried attic mounting but really didn't expect it to work with the log walls. It didn't so I went to an outdoor gable end mount. Using one inch electrical conduit I created my own very sturdy mast at a fraction of the cost of buying an actual mast. Took no time at all. I spent more time trying to find where my grandson left the hacksaw than I did actual setting up the antenna. Once set up went to the tv and on first program picked up seven channels. This surprised me as I thought there were only five in Knoxville. Too many years attached to direct TV. Couldn't pick up channel eight so made an adjustment to antenna direction and picked up 15 channels (one from Bristol VA.) Spent three hours trying to pick up channels eight and PBS fifteen. Finally turned on another set still connected to Direct only to discover both these channels were off the air due to a bad wind storm earlier in the day. Went out this morning with directions from antenna point. Made another adjustment, back to reprograming and discovered that I now pick up twenty one, you read that correctly, 21 channels. Every one was crystal clear. And for all these years I thought we only had five and I've spent thousands of dollars receiving what I could have had free of charge. Easy assembly, easy installation, great customer service. If you take the time to set it correctly you're going to love this Antenna. Buy one and cut the cord.

product_title: Ceptics Grounded Universal Plug Adapter
review_headline: Light & compact. Holds securely in the socket. (3) pack for charging laptop tablet & phone
review_body:
These adapters will make your life simpler the next time you travel to Germany (or France...I have only tested them in Germany).

If you have ever used a universal plug adapter, you know the drill: it fits loosely, sometimes falls out of the socket, and occasionally makes scary sparks and burning sounds. Often, contact is lost and you wake up at your hotel with a discharged phone. Plus, if you only travel with one big clunky USD $30 adapter, you can only plug in one thing at a time. In the age of laptops, tablets, and phones...this just doesn't cut it.

Well, this economical yet high-quality three-pack of special-purpose adapters is the answer. Specifically designed to fit the power outlets in Germany, they come in a little white cardboard box that is surprisingly light and easy to pack. And yes, this is a genuine \\"Schutzkontakt\\" German-specification \\"Schuko\\" adapter. It is very safe, with no chance of accidentally touching 230 VAC pins. It holds securely in the socket, thanks to the presence of guide rails on each side that engage mating rails inside the socket.

In short, these are well-made and well-designed. I doubt you could find better, especially at this price. I have used them all week here in Germany and I can say this with confidence: I am NOT going back to universal adapters!

product_title: Yamaha R Stereo Receiver
review_headline: The Yamaha R- S201BL Receiver: It Is Plenty Good
review_body:
Not everyone wants or needs an elaborate sound system that carries six loud speakers plus a center speaker and a subwoofer. That is the setup I have in my standard size condominium apartment's living room. The Yamaha R-S201BL receiver is an entry level receiver that takes me back decades to my youth. It is a two channel stereo receiver with terminals to accept a maximum of four loud speakers. And it is going into my large bedroom for use with my TV plus two medium size speakers.

I tested the R-S201BL receiver using two large speakers, a tape deck and a CD player. I also tested its reception of radio broadcasts. All departments performed very satisfactorily. All of the radio stations I receive on my Sony STR-DE897 receiver are equally well received by the Yamaha. When playing compact disks and cassette tapes I see that I have to turn the volume up to about 50 on the indicator to equal what a 30 gives me on the Sony. But there is no distortion in the audio; it is crisp.

The Yamaha has buttons on the front panel to push and boost bass and treble when desired. I prefer this to what you find on some receivers (the Sony for example) where one has to always try and remember how this is done in a number of steps. Bass can be boosted adequately on the Yamaha.

Simple is often good and that is the R-S201BL. Just remember that to use headphones without audio in the large (A and B) speakers you must first disengage the speakers.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: Finicky and pricey, but solves a lot of problems...
review_body:
I suspect my experience is not unlike that of many others - I've accumulated remotes for TV, blu-ray player, cable STB, Apple TV, etc, and it's a true headache to keep track of all of them and ensure that they all play nicely with each other. I had tried several other "consolidated" remote control devices, and always found them very balky - looking up the codes for each device from the lists provided was always a huge PITA; sometimes it worked, and more often than not it didn't.

The Harmony 650 remote fixes all of that by gathering codes from the manufacturers directly (?) when you plug the remote into an internet-connected computer and establish a Logitech account. You enter the make/model of the electronic equipment you want to use the remote with, and the Logitech system finds the correct codes and loads them into the remote.

I would have hoped that once this process was complete, the Logitech Harmony remote would work perfectly, but this wasn't the case. There's still quite a bit of button programming / assignment that has to be done once the codes are gathered, and even this isn't pefect - it probably took me 2-3 weeks to really nail down all of the functions to work the way I wanted them to. In addition, once that was done, there's still a bit of a lag in starting up all of the right devices once you hit the button for what you want to do (e.g., "watch a movie" starts the TV, the HDMI splitter, and the Blu-ray player, and it takes time for the TV to start up and go through its menus to get to the right configuration. So you have to have a little patience with this device.

Despite the complexity, in the end, it works, and the ability to control all of one's devices with a single remote is truly an invaluable thing. So I give it 5 stars, even given its glitches.

review_headline: Not worth it,  not at all
review_body: I was so excited to get these headphones today.  I unboxed them and was thrilled with the quality of the build and the softness of the leather ear cups.  They even smell wonderful.  (yes Im that person who smells stuff)  I stuck in the provided AAA battery,  turned them on,  placed them on my head and expected to me amazed.  First though there is one thing I noticed as I went to my audio device...each time I took a step,  there was a rattling in the right ear.  I thought oh well,  I guess I could look past this if they sound awesome and the music covers it up...after all my in-the-ear buds have a thumping sound every time I take a step.  So I plugged them in and cranked up the music.  Now the rattling is coming from the right ear when the music is on and that simply is not acceptable.  Before you stop reading though,  please bear with me while I explain to you how I would have reviewed them had they not had this defect.  First off the comfort is amazing. Much better than the Sennheiser HD 202's that I already own.  The cord is thick and rugged and the headphones themselves seem to be made of very durable plastic.  While some complained of their size I don't really see an issue here.  Unfortunately,  this is where the positives end for this set of phones.  The sound quality is \\"decent\\" but not \\"amazing\\" like so many reviewers here claim.  I guess if you had only listened to $5 earbuds through your phone,  then yes,  these would sound amazing to you.  However to us folks a little more acquainted with quality audio headphones you will be disappointed. Even the noise cancelling feature leaves a lot to be desired.  It was noticeable, yes,  it didn't even eliminate the sound of my central air conditioning in my house so its certainly going to frustrate you in a more demanding noisy environment.  Overall they were built great,  they are super comfortable,  but at the end of the day you just want to hear amazing sounding music,  and this set of phones just aren't going to do it for you.  I have a set of Klipsch Image S4's that blow this out of the water in terms of sound quality.  the only thing about those is,  they have a stethoscope effect so you can hear all of the  talking,  chewing, swallowing, walking, etc that you do.  That is why I was looking for an over the ear headphone in the first place.  Unfortunately these are a huge let down for me.  I know I'm in the minority on the sound quality issue,  but trust me,  if you are an audiophile you are going to hate these. A good euphemism would be that Its like I was eating Texas Roadhouse steaks expecting Ruth's Chris and ended up with Outback.

The problem is this, depending on the orientation of your cables and jacks, you might find that the weight of the cable going into the S-Video end of the adapter pulls down on the adapter. Notwithstanding this, contact appears tight enough, and I am using it successfully in my system.

Form: Designed with travel in mind. They come with a groovy carrying case and a number of optional cables (a long ribbon cable and a short braided cable). Fold up small and tight with metal hinges.

Function: It Just Works! The three words all consumer electronics should abide by. Connected via BT to my older Android phone with no fuss. I am an amateur musician, so I need a speaker loud enough for me to play a regular piano or acoustic guitar with when I'm just wanting to play around for fun. It doesn't offer an EQ control on the unit to control lows, mids, and highs, but I just selected the best audio mix on my iPhone or Mac for the sound I prefer -- that's why I didn't give 5 stars. The setup and pairing was simple and had no difficulty right out of the box.

I checked out Best Buy's speaker displays in this category and nothing they carried came close to this one in sound and price. The Beats Beatbox Portable Speaker was the closest, but was $400, and isn't nearly as nice looking.

review_headline: Prepare to be disappointed if you are a previous Fuze/Sandisk owner
review_body:
I bought this player to replace a Sansa Fuze+ that got destroyed by going through the wash. Took a risk on this one buying it right when it came out and had no reviews, really wish I wouldn't have done that.

I have been a fan of Sandisk since the Fuze, which was really an awesome player. When that one died, I got a Fuze+, which seemed like more of a downgrade, but still acceptable. I gave this one a real chance, but unfortunately, it is the worst one I have had yet.

The player starts up faster and navigating is fairly quick and has an micro sd card expansion slot, but that is pretty much all it has going. It doesn't store numbering for songs, so everything is out of order and sorted alphabetically (which drives me crazy). Shuffle is terrible, it doesn't keep track of what has already been played (much like the Fuze+) so you will hear repeats before it has gone through everything. You can't just play all albums from an artist, a workaround is to play on shuffle, then go to the menu and turn shuffle on and back off and it will play in order, but still all songs are sorted alphabetically so kind of pointless unless you just don't want to be hearing repeats before the list has completed.

The buttons can sometimes be unresponsive and delayed, so you might have to click more than once or wait a second or two to wait to see if the click processed. If you keep this in your pocket like I do, get ready for your songs to switch all the time when you don't want to from accidentally pushing the buttons, there is no lock feature on this one.

This thing is bigger than the clip Zip that my wife has (I am not sure if that one functions as bad as this one), but it is still microscopic. I don't know who is telling the mp3 player companies that people want smaller and smaller mp3 players, with less functionality, I much preferred when they were at least a 2 to 3 inches in size.

The real deal breaker for me is just the lack of functionality, the only thing that is left for me that I like is the fact that it can play mp3s. So I will be returning this product to Amazon. It is a shame, they had the opportunity to create a better product but instead just removed more features and functionality. I know the mp3 player industry is struggling because of smartphones that now take the place of it, but making terrible mp3 players can't be helping that fact either. Otherwise, if you are using other things like apps or moving around on the screen it is basically a big mouse. There is a little "magic" in that. It is better than the remote that comes with the LG LN5700.

If you don't mind 2-3 remotes then the Magic Remote is nice. The Magic Remote does "eat" batteries so be ready for that as well. In alot of cases you may not need one because once you create lists of things you like to see, navigation is not that bad with the box remote that came with the TV.

product_title: BeoPlay H6
review_headline: The right mix of sound quality, style and comfort
review_body:
UPDATE:
I highly recommend using a headphone amp to take these headphones to the next level. For just $60 you can get a cMoyBB amp from JDS labs [...] (and they'll even customize the amp to match your specified headphones). Now my BeoPlay H6 headphones sound incredible!

Overview:
I imagine the BeoPlay H6 would be the headphone recommended in a music appreciation class, as long as heavy metal and hardcore hip hop weren't on the agenda.

Sound:
The highs and mids in this headset are sublime, and the lows can hit heavy enough as long as you crank the volume. But these aren't exactly the headphones to listen to while getting pumped for a sports game or blasting out the last rep at the gym (would anyone wear a $400 headset to the gym?). The H6 is a headphone for the naturalist. It stands nearly - and happily - isolated in a circus of overbearing bass-laden chaos (for those unaware, heavy bass is usually a compensation for poor sound quality).

The Competition:
I personally tested the following 10 headphones via my iPod classic (NOTE: All headphones are over-ear and either noise canceling or noise isolating [I was looking for headphones for the office] and range in price from $199 to 399): Bose QuietComfort 15, Parrot Zik, Monster DNA, Bowers & Wilkins P7, Sennheiser Momentum, Beats by Dre Studio, Beats by Dre Executive, Bang and Olufsen Beoplay h6, Marshall Monitor, Sol Republic Master Tracks.

Final Verdict:
The BeoPlay H6 had the right mix of sound quality, style and comfort to earn my 400 bucks. Next to the Bose QuietComfort 15, the BeoPlay is the most comfortable headphone (by far) of all the ones mentioned above. I thought the B&W P7 slightly edged out the BeoPlay in sound quality, due to the P7's heavier hitting low end with equally impressive highs and mids. But the B&W P7 was the least comfortable of all the headphones I tried on. The Sennheiser Momentum is a great deal, but it will only fit over-ear if you have small to average size ears (I don't). And its sound quality isn't quite as good as the B&W P7 or the BeoPlay. So if you're seeking exceptional comfort and quality sound - the BeoPlay H6 is your answer.

product_title: Koss Porta Pro On Ear Headphones with Case
review_body: Like everyone else who has purchased these headphones, I love them - they are comfortable for long periods of time, because of their design they work well with eyeglasses, they stay in place (I can work out and run in them), and they sound amazing out of the box.  I also own and use Sennheiser HD 558 and AT-50 - I like them all, but I will go to the PortaPros most of the time.  Like alot of reviewers, when I first used them I felt the bass was alittle too strong and affected mids and highs somewhat.  Here is the cool secret about these headphones: remember that they are designed to sit ON your ear (and not around it).  The closer the headphone's driver is to your ear canal the greater the bass.  If you (1) set the comfort zone to LIGHT, and (2) move the center of the drivers slightly higher on your ear (by adjusting the metal band), you will reduce the bass to near perfect and open up the mids and highs (it even widens the soundstage IMHO).  For those of you who have backed off these headphones because of reviews of excessive bass, buy these headphones and try the tweak!

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_body:
I had previously purchased this years ago from a different company. I liked it so much I decided to get another one. Between all the devices we have and all the remotes that take up space, it just makes sense to have one remote. I don't need something high tech like the things that look like tablets....to me that's just silly.

This is pretty easy to use and set up. You write down all your model numbers from your devices. In my set up I have a DVD player, sound system, TV, cable box, and Roku. Sit down at the computer, plug it in, go to the website and start setting things up.

product_title: Audiovox Corporation ANT700F RCA Indoor/Outdoor Amplified Antenna
review_headline: Didn't work 40 miles from broadcasters, extremely fragile construction.
review_body:
It was remarkably sensitive to the location, and I was unable to position it to receive more than one or two channels (at best). The only location that received ANY channels was way too far away from the preferred location for our TV. I had to string two wires across the house to test the device. That's where the real trouble began.

It started receiving only ONE channel when it was dropped less than two feet. While stringing the coaxial cable through a window across the house, the feather weight device was tugged off of a low platform bed onto a lushly carpeted floor and we only received a single channel, despite locating the antenna outside in the direction of the broadcasting towers in the next county. The device is VERY light, and the fall made NO sound whatsoever, not even a "clunk." It was no louder than the sound of an empty cereal box falling onto carpeting. The TV without an antenna received the same channel, so it seemed that the device may have stopped functioning entirely. It's impossible to test.

This apparent fragility made it seem pointless to pursue an outdoor mounting, as it seemed it would not survive the jostling required to mount it on the side of a house or on pole and unlikely to survive outdoors in the sun in our area that hits over 100 routinely in the summer.

While the inability of this antenna to receive any channels may have been more of a factor of geography and geometry than its design, the poor durability forced me to give it a low rating.

product_title: Klipsch Image S4i-II
review_headline: Fit is amazing, sound is great. High quality and tangle free!  Cord noise prevented 5th star
review_body:
Let me start by saying that I bought these after returning a certain red colored more highly-rated, less-expensive set of tangle-free ear buds with a microphone. They were junk, and those reviews were inflated by customers who received the product for free, so beware!

Onto these: I love them. The first thing you notice is the build quality. These are well-made ear buds. The cord is solid, there is no play or wiggle in the connections, nothing about them is chintzy. It doesn't hurt that they've got a great clean, modern look as well.

The next thing I noticed was the fit. In a word: phenomenal. This is what sets these buds apart from others. They are angled in such a way that they seal easily to block out ambient noise and transmit sound directly to you without having to crank them up. Like most earbuds, they come with gels in different sizes to customize the fit. The gels are much different than what I'm used to seeing, however. They're more of an oval shape than round. I suspect the reason that these fit so well is that our ear canals aren't really round (but are more oval), just as ear canals are not angled straight into our heads as normal ear buds would have you believe.

Comfort is incredible. I've worn them all day basically every day since I bought them. There's no discomfort even after 8-10 hours, much different than any other buds I've owned. This includes expensive offerings from Sennheiser, Beats, Skull Candy, etc.

Sound quality is top notch. I'm not sure if it's the quality of the speakers or just the amazing fit, but either way, these things sound awesome. Bass is solid, mids and highs are clear and don't get "tingy" or muffled. No complaints whatsoever.

The cord is clearly marked with L and R which is helpful, but I've found that with the unique shape, I can tell right away which ear each bud belongs in. No need to even look closely to determine whether you're putting the bud in the correct ear. While it seems minor, this actually makes a big difference.

The microphone and remote work well. The volume controls are intuitive and easy to find and press, even while wearing gloves. They work perfectly with both my iPhone and iPod. The middle button moves to the next song, and will answer and hang up calls when appropriate. Sound quality through the microphone is good, as well. Certainly no complaints there. Placement of the microphone is a little off. It's down at the "split" in the cord instead of further up. This makes it necessary to adjust the cord a little so someone can hear you easily. Not a huge deal.

The flat cord is absolutely tangle free. It doesn't have memory, so it doesn't come out kinked up. Even after being wadded in a pocket it straightens nicely. It also doesn't get stiff in the cold, a problem that plagues many other ear bud cords. Since I commute via public transit in Minnesota, this has always been a huge problem for me for a significant portion of the year. It's nice not to have to worry with it with these!

One problem that the cord does have, and this is what prevented the fifth star, is that it transmits bumps and brushes pretty badly. This is a problem with all ear buds, but it's an annoyance nevertheless. I feel that these buds may transmit thuds a little worse than others, possibly due to increased surface area on a flat cord. This isn't a huge problem while commuting, but I wouldn't recommend these for exercise. It would get annoying quickly.

Overall, if you are using these for anything other than exercise, I can't recommend them enough. Great, great product, especially for the money. The fit, comfort, and performance are all well above the price range.

product_title: RCA Compact Outdoor Yagi HDTV Antenna with 70 Mile Range
review_headline: Easy mount to old satalite dish stand / 40+ mile reach (with pre-amp)
review_body:
I first tried a cheap set of RCA indoor rabbit ears to see what I could get first out of Manhattan, KS. I didn't expect much given I was down at the bottom of a river valley. I got two 7 digital channels (ABC, CBS, CW) along site one snowy analog (FOX) but a couple of them were duplicates.

I mounted this antenna using the old satellite dish stand on the roof. I re-positioned it to point towards Topeka, KS using tvfool.com position and a compass app on my smartphone. I simply re-used RG6 cables from the dish and was in business within minutes.

With this antenna, reception jumped to to 11 channels (added PBS and NBC). I then got a RCA pre-amp to help with the analog station and also picked up 3 more digital channels (including a digital FOX) including one that was 44 miles away.

Overall, I've been pretty impressed. I want to see how it handle in bad weather as that is something I despised about satellite. This is really reminds me of when I grew up in rural KS but the quality with digital is so much better. I already cut the cord before this for several months before but wanted to watch a few live sports events. All in all, I still spent the equivalent of 1 month of satellite fees and I and my wife couldn't be happier.

product_title: FRiEQ 3.5mm Male To Male Car and Home Stereo Cloth Jacketed Audio Cable (4 Feet/1.2M) for iPhone, iPad, iPod, Smartphones and mp3 players (Plug will be Fully Seated with Phone Case On) Blue/Yellow
review_body:
As a music junkie, it is very important for me to be able to connect my iPod to my car stereo. I have tried other cords in the past, but the abuse that they endure as they are moved around in my car, sat on, and readjusted so that it isn't tangled around my floor shifter eventually wears down the wires and the signal becomes degraded. As with most people, I want a cord that is both durable and functions well, that doesn't have horrible sound quality and can withstand both the extreme heat and cold that cars sit through. That is where the FRiEQ® Male-to-Male 3.5mm Audio Cable (F M2M for short) comes in.

Appearance/Features

While at its heart, the F M2M is a simple audio cable, enabling you to plug in your desired audio device to the jack connection in your car, your personal stereo, or other speaker unit. What separates this cable from others is the design considerations to not only provide great sound quality, but to withstand the day-to-day usage that many people could subject it to.

As shown in the product images, the jack end (the male adapters) is nice, shiny, and what you cannot see, heavy. It feels well-built and, frankly, would hurt if you swung it over your head and whapped someone with it. There is a “step” on the adapter to allow you to plug it in to a device with a case, so when inserted it will stick out ever-so-slightly.

In terms of use, there was a little bit of play between the port on my car stereo and the male adapter; I switched ends and it remained. I tried the cable in my boyfriend’s truck with no issues, so I am going on a limb and saying that it has something to do with my vehicle. All of that being said, I noticed no difference in the terms of the sound quality; it was great! With the exception of it being a smidgen “loose” in the port on my car, I had no issues.

Overall

This is a great, durable cord to get for hooking your iPod/MP3 player/phone up to a stereo. The cord itself is encased in paracord, so gripping it is not an issue, and if you have a case on your device the male adapter ends are beveled so that you do not have to take the case off to use the cable. The sound quality is excellent, and while my car had a bit of play in the connection to my stereo, the cable is more than capable of channeling some excellent tunes.

product_title: Audioengine D1 24-bit Digital-to-Analog Converter
review_body:
The first one I got had channel imbalance (tad to the right), and some problems with clicking.
Ordered another one, and this one doesn't have those problems.

Build is solid, thought both came with a layer of dust from the factory. Everything feels firm and I trust that it'll survive a good throw.

Sound is good. I don't believe DACs improve sound quality (unless you have a really bad on-board DAC in your computer). This just doesn't color the sound, doesn't distort, and will (it has to) bypass your on-board sound card. I don't detect any new detail, or any massive improvement in quality.

I bought this mainly because it has a very low impedance so there's no hiss for any headphone I feel like listening to. IEMs and some more sensative headphones have the tendency to pick up any noise and random hiss; this has a dead-silent noise floor, making it all almost dead silent.

A few problems though:
It's got a finicky power supply that needs a good, clean USB to run from. Some of the USB outputs on my computer caused this to have hiss.
And, you need to set your sound output to it's highest to get rid of some hiss (sometimes).
While also, if your cables aren't grounded or touching something they shouldn't, you'll get hiss.

It's a finicky, small, and ultimately great DAC/amp. I think anyone would be happy having one of these, and I'll probably never spend more on a DAC/amp after this (unless this one dies).

product_title: Tenqa Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds for Running / Sports Handsfree Wireless Headset for Smartphones
review_headline: All around Excellent. Best for the $
review_body:
Great sound, very impressive rumblings of bass. They're large but they're light and don't look silly in the ears. No slip, comfortable.
They work with phone calls and speech recognition and voice commands and Siri. One mic is for noise cancelation and wind cancelation, the other mic is for speaking. Callers say I sound a little muffled but still loud and easy to understand. They repeat a tone if you have an incoming phone call. Hit the little volume up or down button to answer, hold down the volume up or down button to hang up. They even tone if you receive a text message. If music is playing it pauses for the call and resumes after the call. If you have an iPhone or other iOS device the remaining battery life is shown right next to the iPhone's/iPad's/iPod's battery icon. Good for 5 .5 hours of use or 300 hours standby time. It says charge time is 90 minutes but I'm getting full charge after 40 minutes (and I've verified that I'm getting 5.5 hours of continuous use).

On my iPhone holding down the power button for a second pauses the music as long as the iPhone screen is off. Holding down the power button when no music is playing starts Siri when the screen is off. It's a fine line between pausing music/starting Siri and powering down the earbuds. And you have to take the earbud out of your right ear to get to the power button.

Hold the volume up button to skip to the next track, hold the volume down button to go back. It lacks a play/pause button but, if the music is paused, using the next/previous track commands start playing the next/previous song.

The manual says to charge for 1.5 hours before using them the first time. Plug them in to USB until the LED light is on steady blue and they're ready. Took me five minutes until LED went from red to blue so you can probably skip this step. Been using these for days and a full 5 to 5.5 hours use only takes me 40 minutes to charge.

Very easy to pair with Windows 7 and iPhone. For Windows you may need to restart the computer and device after pairing for the first time to get the audio to stream. Most Bluetooth transmitters will download the driver automatically, which allows pairing keyboards and mice and such, but go to the manufacturer's site and download the most up to date driver to get stereo audio devices to pair, too.

These are a third of the price of others like Jaybirds Bluebuds or the Yurbuds (and they may be better than the Yurbuds). Great value, all around impressive little things. review_headline: They do their job very well, but...
review_body:
First off, for 4 pairs of 3D glasses, this is a great deal. If want to up the quantity of glasses on hand for when you have guests over on movie night, then this is a great way to go.
They do they job remarkably well and they are easy to operate. We've already watched about 15 hours of movies on them and only now has the first one needed recharge. We have the BenQ W1070 and the match makes for some awesome 3D.
I took off one star for comfort because, at least for me, I find them uncomfortable. There are two semi-hard rubber nose pads that just pinch my nose. Everyone's head is different I'm sure, but these seem to me to have a flawed design. My wife can wear them over her eyeglasses without issue, however.
Then I had to take off another star for durability. I fell asleep in the couch watching a movie and when I woke up and got up to go to bed, my glasses where broken. I think I had taken them off and put them on my stomach and from there they ended up under me. One earpiece snapped off right through the screw hole and the other one is bent in the same place. If I bend it back it will snap for sure. Okay. Its my fault for falling asleep without taking the glasses off and putting them away properly, but I'm disappointed that they could not withstand that level of wear and tear. If you have children, then do not expect these to last long.

I think I'm going to try their big brothers, the XLs

Bottom line: I would buy them again and I would recommend these to a friend, but not for everyday use.

product_title: Reactiv Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (With Mic and 8 Hour Battery)
review_headline: Some key features set this apart
review_body:
When my review sample of this speaker arrived I initially thought it was yet another generic bluetooth speaker in impressive packaging. How wrong I was. At a glance this looks like a plethora of other speakers that have flooded the market. However, there are some key differences - some subtle and some not so - that truly set this one apart.

The most impressive feature in my opinion is the battery protection mode that will take effect if the unit has been in standby mode for a long period. Since the battery is sealed, this is a nice feature that protects your investment in this speaker.

Sound quality is absolutely superb. Better than most of the speakers that I have tested (and I have tested dozens of them.) This one is loud, but has sufficient headroom so the sound does not start breaking up or distorting at higher volumes. More importantly, it reproduces low, mid and high range frequencies with clarity and fidelity. I have a suite of albums that I use to test speakers and this one passed all with flying colors. The primary album I use is Miles Davis' Kind Of Blue, which exercises the frequency spectrum and that album played through this speaker such that I could hear every note and nuance.

A more subtle feature that I appreciate is the raised buttons on top. This may seem trite, but I have other speakers with the same embossed octagonal design and the buttons on those are flush and nearly impossible to feel. At sixty-five my eyesight isn't what it use to be, so not only is this feature important to me, but shows the attention to detail the engineers and designers paid to this speaker.

I'll refrain from repeating the features in the product description, but will say that I tested each of them and all work as described. If there is one wish I would love it had this speaker automatically broadcast itself via bluetooth when I powered it up. Some of the newer speakers do this and it makes pairing and connecting much easier for folks who are new to using bluetooth devices.

One final note: if you purchase this speaker do charge it for two to three hours before trying to pair it with your phone, tablet or other device. It seems to want a full(er) charge before initially pairing it. Other than that, this is one of the best speakers I have tested and one that I would not hesitate to recommend to friends and musician colleagues.folks who are new to using bluetooth devices.

product_title: Grado GR10 In-ear Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Grado GR10, near RS1 sound quality on the go...
review_body:
First up, I am a longtime unashamed admirer of \\"the Grado sound\\". My first encounter with Grado was when I was buying headphones and came across great reviews for the moderately priced SR80s. Having used Bose quiet comfort 15 headphones (that cost 3-fold that of the SR80s) for some time I was immediately impressed by the clarity of the SR80s. I was hearing things in my favorite music that I simply hadn't heard before. I found that I wanted to hear all of my music through the SR80s to find out what else I had been missing. Compared to the Bose, the SR80s brought what I can only describe as an exciting presence to the music. Gone was the Bose woofy bass and dull compressed midrange. Some say the SR80s don't have enough bass for their tastes, but this might be because people expect a lot of bass, but rarely get the tight realistic bass characteristic of Grado. A couple of years later I bought a pair of the expensive Grado RS1s. These are just amazing in sound. They have all of the presence of the SR80s, with more detail in the mids and highs, and unlimited tight low ends. THe sound stage or openness is greatly increased relative to the SR80s. However, while the traditional over the ear Grado headphones provide clear realistic exciting sound, they have two disadvantages, first they have an open design that leak a tinny sound into the room that can be annoying to those you share space with, second, they aren't designed for, nor work well for listening on the move.
Enter the GR10s. I purchased a pair and have been using them for about six months now. I run them from a Fiio X3 and use WAV FLAC or other lossless formats. The pairing of an excellent source and the GR10s provides superb sound. The GR10s have the excitement of the RS1s, however their soundstage is very slightly reduced, and the bass, doesn't have that feeling of total authority that the RS1 projects. Having said that, the sound from these IEMs is phenomenal, providing a very close rendition of the RS1 listening experience that is available on the go.
I want to reiterate something other reviewers have commented on. These in ear monitors need to be positioned just right in your ear canal to get the full rich sound, particularly the full bass. They come with instruction to this effect. I find it easiest if i place the cords diagonally upwards facing forward and when you push the IEM into the ear canal, they just rotate and \\"pop\\" into just the right position. It only takes a few times to get this down, and once you do you get rewarded by the amazing sound quality.
In short, these IEMs will allow you to experience concert hall quality sound anywhere. To fully take advantage of their quality, MP3 owners should consider upgrading to the relatively inexpensive Fiio X3 music player (around $200) with its excellent DAC and amp for rendering lossless music files. A little eq adjustment may be necessary (sliders) to bring more bass out if that's what you prefer.

Perfectly fine for mostly quiet places, however around noise you'll hear all of the outside stuff through them. I still use in ear, ear buds that seal well at work or around noisy areas.

Comfort: Ohhhhhhhh yeah.ahhhhhhhhh...so lightweight, plush and comfortable. No fatigue, you forget they are even on(can wear for hours), supersoft ear cushioning.

Design: Again ultra lightweight, Great design, mostly plastic but feel durable. (cord) jack on the left side that is detachable(but proprietary however, but only 7 bucks to replace if necessary) The cord is thin and a tad long but I haven't had the tangling issues some have mentioned. The 3.5 mm jack is angled to reduce angular stress on the cable when your phone or mp3 device is in your pocket. They rotate/fold flat but do not collapse or fold inward like some sets do. Not the most aesthetic set of headphones but nice looking enough. Fairly understated, not for show.

The soft draw string pouch doesn't provide much protection if you travel so I'd recommend an aftermarket hardshell case. I picked one up on Amazon for 13 dollars.

review_headline: Used to be good, but now it's a paperweight. Don't buy one.

The internet radio streamer plays nothing but silence. Slacker or Pandora will work ONCE, but then you need to unplug the device and let everything clear before you can use it again. Netflix plays 5-10 seconds at a time before stopping to buffer (not my network causing the issue, my galaxy s3 can be sitting right next to it and play netflix in HD with no buffering). The support forum is a joke, nobody from Sony comes in to address your problems. And since this is a thin-client and all processing is done at Sony's end, it is Sony that is causing these issues.

It's also missing some very basic features. You can listen to music from a USB stick, but you can't set any of those songs as an alarm. You used to be able to set a slacker or pandora channel as you alarm, but not anymore (the option was removed).

In short, If you'd bought this soon after it came out, you would have gotten some use out of it prior to it becoming useless. If you buy it now, you'll be nothing but disappointed.

product_title: Zipbuds FRESH Earphones with Mic and Remote
review_headline: Close, but no cigar.  Heavy, stiff, microphone placement stupid
review_body:
I wanted to love these, so so much. The idea is brilliant, and ZipBuds seems to be the only company capitalizing on the idea. The zipper has the ability to finally create truly tangle free earbuds! I ordered these with high hopes, and the sound is good enough, but the problems were just too much. I had to send them back.

1. The zipper is too heavy. No matter which size fitting I used, the earbuds still easily fell out of my ear. I use my headphones on public transit with lots of shuffling around and wearing bulky clothing in the Minnesota winter. They fall out too easily because of the weight.

2. The cord is way too stiff. The zipper is just not manageable. It's like having the headphones attached to a solid rod such that any time you move, one big piece sways around in a unified response to your movement. This adds to the earbuds' propensity to pull out of your ears. This effect seems to be compounded in the cold.

3. The microphone placement is just dumb. It's about an inch and a half below the right earpiece. I'm not sure it would pick up sound dangling directly down, but the booklet depicts wrapping the cord above the zipper and below the earpiece around the back of your ear. This would undoubtedly cause the earpieces to stay in place better, but then the microphone is BEHIND YOUR EAR. How can it work then? I absolutely need a microphone, and this one might as well not be there.

All in all, the idea is great. I'm more than willing to give these another shot if the company finds a way to make the zipper more limber and to place the microphone in a position where it can be useful. I don't think the weight issue will ever be solved with the zipper design,, but greater flexibility of the 'cord' and ability to use the earbuds as designed without them falling out would make them great. I'd be glad to try out any future improvements, as the tangle free factor of the zipper can't be ignored.

If only, if only...
