product_title: S390G Smartphone - Wi-Fi - 3G - Bar - Black
review_headline: Potentially good hardware ruined by awful software! Call 911 from pocket every time!
review_body:
For the first day I was pleased with this phone. Solid feel, nice keyboard, lots of features.
But the very first evening I took it out of my pocket and it was asking "Call SOS?". Luckily(?) I had no service there, so it didn't complete the call. I looked online and it turned out that lots of people have this problem with the phone. Pressing "911" does it, even if the phone is locked. So does "000" and "112", thus covering their bases. The FCC apparently has a requirement that any idiot be able to pick the phone up off the road at the scene of an accident and make an emergency call even if the phone is locked, but the result for this phone is a disaster. It is not an exaggeration to say that EVERY time I put it in my pocket even briefly, it gets to the "Call SOS Y/N" stage or worse, I hear the 911 operator from my pocket. (Perhaps my pocket is very scary, so the phone calls 911?) In desperation I started carrying it around in a plastic Chinese takeout container, which was safe but not very convenient. Then I accidentally ran over it with a car, and although the container was utterly destroyed, the phone had no apparent damage at all! Very solid!

The 911 pocket dialing is the worst, but with the possible exception of the e-mail, everything else about the software is terrible also. Did the developers not try this thing out for even a day before they put it on the market? Here are a few of the other problems:

1) Doesn't tell you who the text messages are from until you read them. So I have to click on them to see that they are spam. Worse, there doesn't seem to be any way to block text messages from spam numbers. They have slowed a bit now, but for a while I was getting 5 or 10 a day.

2) The browser button is on the front screen, right where you can click it every time you unlock the screen. That way you can click it as you put it away, and it can suck down hundreds of minutes while in your pocket or purse. Some of the stuff on this phone is just stupid, but this "bug" is clearly malicious. My LG 800g did something similar. I can't say I ever tried out the browser, but if it's like the 800g's version it's completely useless - it's only purpose was to drain your minutes while you weren't watching.

3) It occasionally forgets my contacts, and just shows the numbers.

4) It plays music nicely over bluetooth, but then the phone crashes. After some messing around it would restart, but the battery would be totally dead. (When working properly, the battery life is actually very good, up to two weeks.)

5) The calculator wants you to use the mini touch pad to select operations, thus rendering it useless.

6) The mini-touchpad built into the center button is barely usable, and the scrolling software for it is abysmal. Trying to find a particular message in my inbox was impossible if there were more than a couple, so I had to empty it out all the time.

7) Taking a picture requires several menus, button clicks, etc., so by the time you have it ready your subject is gone.

8) Another stupid feature: pressing the center of the space bar gives you a space, period, and capital letter. Pressing one or the other sides gives you the normal space. Even once I figured this out, I still had to backspace dozens of times to clean it up when I hit the button wrong.

9) A smaller annoyance, but the T9 touchpad doesn't show the associated letters (ABC = 1, etc.) They could easily have set it up so pushing the letters while dialing gave the proper numbers, but they didn't. So it's hard to dial a phone number given as letters.

10) Rings when the battery gets low. This should be an adjustable option. I don't want to hear about it when I'm trying to sleep.

11) How to dismiss the voicemail/missed calls/text message notification without checking them is not clear. They keep popping upwhen I'm trying to do something else.

12) The on-screen labels for the buttons are lined up over the wrong ones. Until you figure it out, it looks like you're supposed to push the outer pair of buttons, but actually the labels refer to the more central pair.

13) Even aside from the emergency dialing problem, the screen locking is inadequate. You can add a security code, but it only requests it on startup and a few other things like some multiple deletes. And of course you don't have to enter the security code for 911, or the screen unlock sequence.

So this is the last TracFone for me, what awful phones. I'm getting a Republic phone next week.

product_title: SONOS BRIDGE for Sonos Wireless Network (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Check out capabilities before you buy!
review_body:
Bought this in great hopes it would bring sound to my whole house like my old clunky 900mhz wireless speakers do. However it couldn't connect to my wifi (first device ever to have a problem). Then once I got the speaker and bridge connected with old-school ethernet I discovered there was no bluetooth or aux input ability at all! You have to use their app/widget to do everything. With a house full with their own libraries and individual Pandora accounts this quickly became a paper weight.

Amazing that in 2013 a high-end audio maker wants to lock you into their music providers and a single PC library. Thought I would be bragging to the neighbors about how cool this system was. Instead I had to explain my defeat.

Most bookshelf speakers that have 10 and bigger woofers...well just cant produce mid bass like these do! These speakers have great binding post connectors

Pros
Heavy (super durable)

Loud(give it at least 75 watts)

Great mid and high range

Cons

Heavy (can still be a pro. Just not to the light weight small speaker people)

Finish is ...well not the best (for under $80 its amazing just comparing it to all level speaker finishes)

Hit its max excursion alittle to fast for me (i play heavy bass boosted songs) even though i got a subwoofer and nice crossover

Overall

This is a great entry to intermediate to price conscious audiophile . Although, if you just dont want to get theses .try looking around for some good deals on the pionneer andrew designed book shelf speakers

product_title: Wi-Fi Music Player with 3.5-Inch Color Display
review_body:
My wife runs on the treadmill every day and likes to listen to Pandora Radio on her phone. I thought perhaps this would be nice upgrade vs. using the phone - big display, easy controls, and access to a lot more content. She is not a huge techie so I was worried that she might just look at me sideways wondering why I purchased this for her.

However, she was really excited about the radio - we plugged it in just after opening the box on Christmas morning and she kept it playing all day. I think she really loves it! It's very simple to operate and understand (key feature for non-geek).

Setup for Pandora requires registration (free) to another web site to join the radio to your Pandora account. Other than that, setup was a piece of cake.

My only complaints are:

1) Does not come with a battery (another $35) - As much as my wife is enjoying the radio I know she'll want to bring it from room to room sometimes
2) Line output is to RCA jacks rather than a standard headphone style jack. We will connect the unit to a larger stereo system for running (to get the volume cranked up). RCA jacks may provide better sound quality but it is much less convenient for frequently connecting and disconnecting. Also, the internal speaker does not automatically turn off when connected via RCA jacks (unlike most devices with a headphone jack), so you have to turn the speaker on/off if you don't want it to play also. There is a headphone jack on the side of the unit but it is in "mono" mode unless you change some settings, which you then need to change back to use the internal speaker.

These are not major issues but things I would change if I could.

product_title: Onkyo C-7030 Compact Disc Player (Black)
review_body:
Finally, smart CD reviews! I just want to thank all of you who reviewed the Onkyo 7030. It is such a relief to read reviews written by people still purchasing both CD's and single disc CD players. I cannot tell you how much time I've wasted reading reviews of either carousel changers or players that play a gazillion formats in addition to CD. Most of the reviews I've read are useless, foolish, or vapid - at least to listeners who want to listen to a CD from beginning to end. Granted, some cannot make up their minds what they want to hear and prefer to listen in ways that resemble the random order of a radio set list. Don't they realize that most artists and producers put together an "album" (yes, I still think of them that way) in a certain sequence to be heard a certain way? They still medicate for schizoprenia, don't they? Others prefer to listen to music on speakers smaller than the average soup can and using a format resembling the human thumb or existing only in cyberspace. They tell me that their PC speakers are as good as their stereo speakers. Hey, buy a new stereo (oh, excuse me, a new 3, 5, 7 . . . n speaker home entertainment, surround sound system). But I digress. The Onkyo C 7030 is by far the best I've heard compared to the Sony, Marantz, and NAD I tested before deciding which one to buy.
I've owned Onkyo components in the past and have heard friends' Onkyo CD players - one of which is the C 7030. Although I own a NAD T 514, I've decided to switch to Onkyo after hearing how a borrowed C 7030 sounds thru NAD Amps and Pre-Amps powering a pair of Cabasse speakers. I tried a significantly more expensive Marantz ($1000 +), a mid-priced Sony (around $500) and a slightly higher NAD (around $800) and was extremely impressed with the Onkyo. My decision to buy the Onkyo was not based on the price but only on sound reproduction quality. Although I'm a firm believer that we are limited to a large extent by the production quality ofthe CD we choose to listen to, I was very surprised by how well the Onkyo performed next to my other three choices. I used the same CD's, at the same volume, and at the same neutral bass and treble settings. It sounds cliche', but I found the Onkyo produced much warmer bass responses and very smooth treble responses when compared to the others.
For those shopping at Amazon who are flustered by encountering useless reviews by no more than casual listerners, give the Onkyo C 7030 a shot. Read what the other reviewers have to say about it or find an audio dealer that carries Onkyo and give it a listen.

You have to slide off the shiny plastic piece on the left side of the headset to put the batteries in. Do not try to slide off the side with the on/off switch and indicator, the dial and indicators should be on your right ear facing back.

Turn on the receiver with the red light facing you then turn on the switch on the headset. I usually pick up a radio station right away, but after pushing the scan button 2 times the sound from the cable box comes in right away. If I leave the room I usually pick up a radio station but I don't care because I usually pause the station that I am watching anyway when I leave the room. review_headline: Great product, easy install, but weak rubber gasket inserts
review_body:

I'm always looking at the bright side.

As other reviewers have mentioned, this is a great solution to be able to surge protect an outlet as well as conceal wires for an extremely clean installation. I now know that I am up to code, surge protected, and lookin' good to boot.

The one complaint (and the reason for 4 stars) is that the plastic is not the most rugged, and the rubber inserts for the cable pass-through are somewhat flimsy. Unfortunately, after passing cables through and pulling them the rest of the way through, the friction was enough to start a tear in the rubber of the top unit. With that bit of a break in the rubber, some of the tension is gone in the way it is seated in the panel opening, and it now pops out whenever the cables are shifted or adjusted. It's not the end of the world, since it's behind the TV, but a little bit of a more rugged rubber or a different design would have helped.

product_title: APC BE550MC Battery Back-UPS with Green Feature (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Dead On Arrival. Connected the battery, then the mains, went straight to battery power with the alarm sounding, no matter what outlet I tried. Made sure the fuse was reset etc. No visible physical damage. Faulty wiring despite QC? Transport damage? Have previously set up half a dozen of these (non-\\"Green Feature\\" though), never had this issue.

First time I ordered one online instead of a local store (where I could just bring it back the next day), and of course now I have to do the RMA dance, find a new fitting box (since it originally was part of a larger delivery). Meh.

UPDATE: Actually found out it's not returnable... things are going to get more interesting. Either way never again online, at least for this type of item.

UPDATE 2: After calling support, first I was given the option to have a replacement sent, with an estimated arrival the following week. And still dispose of the non-functional one responsibly (electronics recycling) due to shipping constraints, same as the website's paragraph on this matter. But then the package was rescheduled to be delivered within a couple of days, and suddenly I also received a return label anyway, by email. Luckily, I hadn't recycled the UPS yet, and found another box to ship it in.

The replacement has arrived, and works as expected of an APC product. I increased the rating to reflect a finally functional product. But I could have done without the extra hassle, and while, as always, Amazon customer service has been prompt & courteous, it would be nice if they (and the website) were on the same page regarding the handling of this type of item in case of failure (i.e. recycle or return after all?)

In short, it works great, takes some time to program but then operates multiple pieces of equipment completely and flawlessly. No doubt. I've used it for TV, Directv, Apple TV, Xbox and DVD. Perfect. The Harmony software is a little clunky and it takes some time to get it set up just how you want, but then after that? Junk all your old remotes, at least put them in a junk drawer because you will need them when this one breaks. And it will.

All 3 of mine worked for a while, maybe even several months, then suddenly when I push a button, it lights up, starts the activity and then restarts. Every time I push a button it does that. New batteries don't help, reprogramming it doesn't help. This remote has some flaw in the power system or power connections that causes it to lose power and restart. Take my advice and don't buy this.

product_title: Mohu Leaf 30 TV Antenna, Indoor, 30 Mile Range, Original Paper-thin, Reversible, Paintable, 4K-Ready HDTV, 10 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, USA Made, MH-110583
review_body:
I don't normally like leaving negative reviews, but in this case I at least want to let other buyers know that this won't necessarily be a solution to their reception problem.

To begin, installation is easy. You simply connect one end to the antenna, one end to the TV, and then either push-pin or velcro your antenna to the wall (or window). A benefit to the Leaf Paper antenna is the ease and flexibility with which you can move it around. It has a long high-grade coaxial cable that will allow you to try many different points to try and maximize your reception.

For a lot of people in areas with already decent reception, this antenna might work great. It slightly improved my reception but honestly wasn't that different from what I was getting with a cheap set of amplified rabbit ears. I still have regular disruptions in my signal, and was unable to pick up any extra channels in my metro area than I was before.

The results with this product will obviously vary depending on many factors. I want to make clear that I am not saying this won't improve your reception, just that it DID NOT improve mine and was in my case not worth spending $40.

*update*

I moved to a new place and have noticed much better results with this antenna.

product_title: Denon AVR-4520CI Networking Home Theater AV Receiver with AirPlay (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Denon has gone steadily down hill from the old days...
review_body:
Pros: Good Price Point for amount of features. Audyssey XT32, Ample HDMI inputs. 4k support. HD Radio. 4ohm compatability. Network hub. Network apps. Network upgradeability. Simple Audyssey setup. Setup mic included.

Cons: No THX certification. 4ohm setting / support. Average sound quality. Sound bleed from other interfaces. Always seems to be doing something quirky. Too simple Audyssey setup.

I am a long time Denon fan since the AVP-8000 days (early 90s), but feel this may be my last. Since the 8000 series, I have owned a 3000 series and a previous 4000 series. I now own the AVR-4520CI, and I am terribly disappointed where Denon has ended up. I actually did a thread on AVS Forums asking for input / alternate suggestions prior to purchase, but you know how those threads go. ;]

I am using the AVR-4520CI in a 7.1 configuration with Miller & Kreisel (M&K) 4ohm S-150THX / SS-150THX Ultra setup in an about 6000 cu ft dedicated home theater. This setup has worked flawlessly with previous Denon configurations. (even ones not rated for 4ohm)

First I immedialy performed a software upgrade. Then I went through Audyssey setup and started watching movies. Something was missing. Movies did not have that "explosive" impact and music seemed to be underpowered compared to my previous 4308CI even though this had more power. After digging, I noticed that channel volumes were limited by default. I had to unlimit for each input, but still didnt seem to have the volume the old less powered model had. Music, radio & HD radio also seemed to not have the volume my old amp had. Removing the limiter helped, but did not resolve all.

Secondly when turning on the reciever, I would intermitently hear "radio" playing with no source materials playing. It would be on a Game input, and my game console on, but I was hearing music at VERY low levels. (so low I had to walk up to a speaker saying whet the heck is that.) I could never tell if this was a Radio, HD radio, or intenet radio source playing. It eventually goes away on that source, but wierd bleed right?

I have done several microprocessor resets thinking the unit is not performing correctly only to come back where I was originally.

review_headline: TrippLite is my most trusted surge brand

They are usually built like tanks, although I know they make plastic models, but give me the big metal tanks any day. This thing is definitely in the metal tank category, feeling plenty heavy. I know heft does not translate into protection, but it sure feels sturdy.

Anyway, no complaints after several years of use. I do not use the RJ45, since the network gear is already behind the TrippLite, but I do use the cable inputs to isolate cable modem and satellite feeds for an adjacent TV. That this unit has three banks of cable inputs gives one plenty of options. Having 10 outlets gave me plenty of options for all the devices attached to it. The color coding is a nice option, although I usually just label each cord with a flexible label printer just to satisfy my OCD (really is a plus to not have to guess all the cables). The color portion on the TrippLite did partially delaminate, but since I do not poke at that often, it really did not matter with my own labels. The black construction is a dust magnet, but since it is hidden away, I do not really care (we do vacuum it every so often).

We get plenty of storms in our area, and the suppressor has weathered them all without issue. No direct lightning strikes, as obviously this would not survive, but otherwise OK so far.

Recommended.

product_title: Beats Executive Over-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Nice headphones, but not good enough to keep.
review_body: I bought these for my wife originally, but she found them to be uncomfortable and too tight. Never one to waste an opportunity, I took possession and began using them for travel immediately. I'm on a plane about a quarter of my time in any given week. First, they were comfortable for me - they adjust, extend, twist, and are well padded on the top and on the ears. Second, they are clearly high quality builds. The workmanship is great from the flexible joints to the high quality cords that come with them. So, those were the high points. What I really wanted them for, though, was sound isolation and noise cancellation while sounding very good. These would replace my Klipsch earbuds if they met my needs. Unfortunately they did not. They cancelled a significant amount of jet engine noise, and air vent noise, but they didn't cancel all of it, and, frankly at their price they needed to do that. They also were not as sound isolating as I wanted them to be. (Probably good to hear that there is an announcement being made while awake, not while asleep.) They didn't do a great job blocking the baby two rows back. All of this I could have lived with, though, if they had also had great sound. But, they had very good sound, not great sound, and so they are going back to Amazon with some regrets. Loved the look and feel, but ultimately the function wasn't quite sufficient to justify a price 5 times higher than my earbuds. I'll keep looking.

product_title: URC WR7 Universal Remote Control for up to 7 A/V Components with 4 Favorite Channel Buttons
review_body:
PROS: I had 4 devices set up in a matter of minutes.
Much cheaper than a Harmony 650
Punch-through works well
Light-up

CONS: Keys are hard to read
Keyboard layout is clunky
Doesn't feel solid.
Created in a world where DVRs don't exist.

My URC 6131n has been controlling all my gear for yours but it didn't have codes for my new LG TV or Sony BluRay player (if you know how to make that happen let me know!) I went remote shopping and landed on the Logitech Harmony 650. I did not care for it all. It's window-centric: it wants to put all the extra commands from a device in that window. Like the skip forward/backward buttons on a DVR - the window is an inconvenient place for them. And It doesn't have volume punchthrough! People in forums make a lot of noise about how you're working with Activities and Devices and in an activity you can control it with macros, or it means you're doing something wrong -- the bottom line, you have to work the way Harmony wants you to. I just want a remote that I can push my buttons.

So I give the WR7. I was able to find 3 digit codes for 3 of my items (LG TV, Sony BluRAY and Motorola Cable Box). The first is my old ReplayTV DVR (yeah, yeah. HD DVR. One of these days). I looked through the instructions, and I don't think the word DVR or PVR is mentioned - as if the remote was built in 1995. Since the WR7 is also a learning remote I quickly mapped the AUX button to handle my DVR.

I have some fine tuning to do. Some device buttons turn the device on while others do nothing but allow you to use the POWER button. But generally speaking, it's doing everything I wanted it to do - replicate all the buttons from my four remotes.

Oh, and twice in a week I woke up and found my Harmony 650 dead. Apparently, if you don't set it down exactly right it will drain its batteries.

product_title: Marantz PM6005 Hi-Fi Integrated Amplifier with Digital Inputs
review_headline: Excellent Phono Stage and seemingly acurate sound
review_body: I bought this for my home office to utilize with Vinyl records and a Apple Airport Express/AppleTV for Airplay streaming digitally to the optical DAC.  I also needed to drive my Bookshelf B&W 686's which are not super efficient.  PROS:  I have utilized the Phono Stage with a ProJect Carbon Debut, MusicHall MMF7.1, and my trusty Technics 1210M5G.  Cartridges used:  AT440mla, Ortofon Red & Black, MusicHall Mojo (aka Ortofon 540mkII).  All I can say is this phone stage with the Marantz in "Source Direct" mode really gets the job done.  If you don't want to mess with extra/external boxes acting as the Phono Stage- look no further. [UPDATE 3/4/14] - Found the perfect combo.  I am running a Denon DL-110 (High Output Moving Coil) Cartridge with the Marantz phono stage.  WORKS PERFECT, and is the best sounding in my use case.  The DAC - works perfect with Airplay on (Apple Airport Express or Apple TV) to stream from Apple devices and iTunes.  (FYI:  You can utilize BOTH an Optical & CoAxial Digital input.  Think of it as 2 Digital inputs not as one-or-the-other.) [UPDATE 3/4/14] Added a NuForce U192S to my Macbook Pro to send over 192/24 HDTracks to the Marantz DAC capable of 192/24. WORKS PEFECT!  Source Direct Mode is nice, in addition to an old school Loudness button for low volume listening as I do in my Office.  CONS: (Why it loses 1 star)  -Volume Knob.  First of all this thing has a blue LED for just about every thing-- EXCEPT on the volume knob!  I am sitting 5' away from it and I can BARLEY discern it is currently at 9 o'clock.  -or- If using the (touchy) remote to control the volume you can't see it's movement/position.  -Source Selector Knob.  I like this concept, but it is too vague.  I always feel like I am between inputs or otherwise doing harm by not accurately hitting the spot for the input I want.  I suppose if you use the remote for selection this is moot, however, in my use case I reach over from my desk and manually use the controls on the face.-Stickers.  As mentioned by another reviewer.  Please Marantz, put the darn FCC/Warning stickers on the BACK.  Mine has one on the side that does not want to peel off, and one on the top presumably to warn you about heat.  WOULD BE NICE:  ~Midrange Adjustment Knob~.  Although I listen to this in Source Direct mode the majority of the time or in Loudness with the Bass/Treble at 0.  There are a few times on my Progressive Rock records that I would love some MID control like on my Vintage Marantz 2270!!!  Now if only the PM'8'005 had a DAC and was available in the USA, that would BE the ONE!

review_headline: Great headphones, even without the batteries
review_body:
These headphones are well worth the purchase. I bought these because a while back my beloved Sony headphones got stepped on and broke. So in the market for some new headphones I had some criteria. First, they had to be over-the-ear headphones because I had heard that they were very comfortable and because they provide more noise cancelation than on-ear. Second, I wanted them to have noise cancelation for use on busses. With these parameters I set out to find my next pair of headphones and I found these Panasonic's. These are a great price and they sound great! Some of the best features are not the ones advertised about.

Things I love about these headphones
-Once burned in these headphones are Amazing! The rich bass and piercing treble balance out wonderfully
-They are the most comfortable headphones I have used. I have used 20+ pairs of headphones
-The noise isolation of the over-the-ear design is really good and gives very astonishing native noise cancelation

Things I was disappointed about
-First and the most disappointing thing is that the noise cancelation function absolutely does not work. If anything it just hurts your ears with the low frequency sound waves that are supposedly supposed to make your listening experience more comfortable.
-The wretched squeak every time you want to turn the ear-cups to put them on your head.

Overall, they are fantastic headphones with unrivaled quality for this price point that are perfect for everyday use.

9.5/10 - fantastic overall quality if you don't mind not using the noise canceling function

Happily, that wasn't what I wanted - I had no interest in setting up five speakers, a subwoofer, and running wires along the walls. I wanted something simple to install that would make my movie watching and game playing more enjoyable.

The PBAR met and exceeded my expectations. For the price, its a a great bargain and a simple solution for someone looking to improve their listening experience.

product_title: MartinLogan Reference On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Great value at current selling price.
review_body:
At the current selling price, these represent a good value. At the original retail price of $300, there are likely better choices when it comes to sound quality. Interesting style and design that will appeal to some. They certainly look distinctive and are well made.

Sound quality:
In general, I find the sound quality to be enjoyable. Some have complained about the bass. I find the bass adequate. Many headphones these days have exaggerated bass. Detail is good. Mids and highs are good. I don't have a lot to complain about the sound. No part of the frequency spectrum jumps out to me as wrong or distracting. I like all genres of music, but it's unforgivable if the voice is not reproduced well. The Mikros 90 does a respectable job with voice. I do not like the scooped mids and exaggerated bass and treble that a lot of headphones have these days. The Mikros 90 thankfully does not have a U shaped frequency response.

Fit:
I can see how some people might find these a little on the tight side. If you have a big head, then they may exert too much pressure. I find them comfortable, but these are not all day wearing headphones.

Build quality:
Solid. Nicely packaged. I can see they were trying to go for the $300 price point. So at their current selling price of under $100, these represent better build and aesthetics than your typical $100 headphone.

Summary:
I like these headphones. I can understand why some are more critical, but when current price is factored in, I don't think there's a whole lot to complain about. Not the reference quality ML may have been aiming for, but still a good set of headphones that doesn't do a whole lot wrong. If you like full, emphasized bass, these are probably not for you. I find the bass just fine, with good articulation and pace.

(I am a long time audiophile. Have owned HD650, AKG K1000, ER4S, Westone 3 for headphones and Apogee minidac, Benchmark DAC, Grace m902, Cary300SEI for headphone amps.)

review_body: I've been smiling from ear to ear since I first booted this beast on. If you can live with the rough edges you won't find a better sounding dap in this price range. The sound is detailed and expansive with great dynamics, it's in a different  league than any other stand alone player I've owned - that includes Cowons, top end Sony's with the digital amp, Irivers, Zune, Mpio, Creative, Samsung, Sharp, Rio and others I can't think of ATM.  The build quality is very good , but the UI and navigation may put some people off.  Another thing is it runs a bit  warm and has froze a couple of times, I'm going to update the firmware and see what improvements Fiio has made. I've owned other Fiio products and have complete cofidence in them, they are not a fly by night company and build nice gear for great prices.    If you are looking for amazing sound from a stand alone dap and don't mind simplified browsing and UI and know a bit about computers and daps don't hesitate to grab this gem, your ears will thank you. :)    Of course I should add that with the high end Wolfson dac anything encoded with a lower bit rate is going to reveal lots of audio artifacts, especially with high end iems. I personally wouldn't use anything less than 256 kbs.    Edit : I should maybe explain a bit more on the sound qualities on the X3- by detail I mean the separation of the instruments is more pronounced and the tones more rich and complex. By dynamics I mean there is a proper difference between soft and loud passages. And lastly expansive refers to the sound stage in general, it sounds bigger and fuller not thin. In other words if you listen to the X3 a while and listen to the identical track say on your iPod it's going to sound constricted, lifeless and weak in comparison.    Edit 2, just to let folks know beta 3.2 is out and fixes album art and adds an 'all songs' option to the artist tab along with some fixes. Just do a search for Fiio x3 firmware and you will find the headfi link for downloading 3.2 beta. It works a charm, cheers! Firmware instructions: unzip firmware and place file in the root (base) folder of your micro SD card, turn off unit then hit the back and power button simultaneously and your unit will start updating- let it do its thing and you're golden. Select language, update database and boom-audio bliss.    Also to maybe help cut down on the one and two star reviews ..... THIS is not like an iPod in any way shape or form..if you're expecting to hook it up and have it populate your music on the device it isn't going to happen. My advice is if you haven't messed with an older mp3 player like a Rio, creative, cowon (iaudio) I would simply not buy this. I gave it 5 stars because I knew exactly what I was getting into- drag and drop simplicity with simple folder or tag browsing with awesome sound. Things have gotten a little better with firmware upgrades, but that's not going to help if you can't upgrade the firmware in the first place.

review_headline: One of the best sounding bar with minor inconveniences
review_body:
At current price, this sound bar is one of the best sounding bar in the $250 - $400 range. The sound is full, rich, well balanced and a pleasure to listen to. I haven't A/B compared with brands like Klipsch, B&W, Yamaha or Onkyo sound bars but in comparison with other electronics manufacturers' brands such as Sony, Samsung, LG, Panasonic or Sharp's sound bars in similar price range, Pioneer trumps them all in sonic quality. It doesn't matter what feature the sound bar claims to have (like 3D sound processing, multi-channel virtual surround, sound enhancing processing gimmicks) unless the speaker actually has good drivers to begin with. Listening to music with this sound bar was the closest thing to listening to a regular pair of speaker - wide, balanced and full. The small subwoofer that comes with the sound bar delivers clean and powerful bass without distorting or muddying mid/high tones. If you are shopping to get the best sound as the top priority, this should do the job. If connectivity and DSP gimmicks are more important, you should look elsewhere.

What I like:
- Sound quality (5/5). It is closest thing to real speakers that is pleasing to listen for both music or watching movies and TV programs. Most sound bars that I tested amplified voice/mid frequency too much to a point that made it annoying when listening to music or sounded tinny/boxy.
- Wireless compact subwoofer delivers clean and tight bass
- Bluetooth is now fixed but the range is short and sensitive to blockage (iphone sync performed better than macbook pro -12+ft vs. 3-4ft.)
- Remote learning capability
- Enough power to fill an apartment living room or small to medium sized living room
- The power adapter (the square plastic box on power cord found on most laptops/monitors/sound bars) is inside the sound bar so less clutter

What I wish Pioneer had or what's missing:
- LCD screen to show current volume, source, EQ setting
- Auto Volume Leveler (Since current volume cannot be seen due to lack of a display, different sources with varying volume can either be too loud or too weak)
- Dialogue mode turns off the subwoofer. Instead, it should change the EQ to increase mid frequency.
- Manual subwoofer turn on/off option. The only way is to unplug it or use the dialogue mode which would also modify the sound EQ.
- I wish they included a Night mode that lowers the subwoofer volume without turning it off.
- Lower profile design dimensions. For current TVs using stands (not wall mounted), 4.1\\" height blocks the IR port or part of the screen.
- HDMI with ARC capability
- No wired connection option to the sub-woofer or no sub-out option in the back of the sound bar for those of us looking to upgrade the subwoofer.
- Better quality remote control that doesn't use those annoying flat circular batteries. Standard AA or AAA would make life easier.

I think most people would shop to add a sound bar to enhance the overall sound quality more than the looks or artificial sound processing. product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: First portable speaker I would consider owning
review_body:
I've been perpetually disappointed with small/portable speakers, until I listened to this one.
A Lotus Exige S gives you 90% of the thrill of a Supercar with a 1.8L 4 cylinder engine. 0-60 in 4 seconds. Handling like a go-kart. It does this not thought brute force, but through better engineering. I feel this is also the case with the Bose Mini. How can such a small volume resonate with so much clean bass? Not the muddy, dirty kind that gets loud only at a certain frequency (the resonant frequency of the enclosure) but clean, flat frequency response way way down, way below what should be possible from such a small device. And yet, there is its.
I'm not saying it is perfect, but if they do perfect it in the next version, I'd have to give it six stars.
For one, the extreme highs are a bit attenuated. we're talking about above 12kHz or so. They are still there, but not as crisp or clean. But wait, compared to other speakers of this size, with no separate driver for the high frequencies, I don't think you could do better.
Second, I would love to see the ability to optionally run TWO of these speakers, one for each channel, to get stereo sound when you're, say, at home. You can still opt for mono when on the road and carry just one of them. From a marketing perspective, this should be a no-brainer, why not tempt the buyer with two units instead of just one?

product_title: Belkin 6-Outlet Home and Office Power Strip Surge Protector with 4-Foot Power Cord, 720 Joules (BE106000-04)
review_headline: Good For What It Is - Basic Protection Only
review_body:
You don't have a lot of time, so here's the short form. As a general rule, any surge protector your buying for less than $20 and probably less than $30 is not providing you with a lot of protection. The really cheap ones can sometimes provide so little protection you might as well not be using anything. This strip is quite good for what it is. While still basic, it's at least a step above those worthless ones; just don't expect it to do more than the bare minimum.

You are probably familiar with a lightning strike frying electronics, but there are other reasons for a protector. The power in your area may not always be \\"clean\\". There can be highs and lows to the normal output that comes from your wall and those changes can damage sensitive electronics over time. This unit provides at least a minimum level of filtering and good spike protection, for the price point. The design is quite good in my opinion, though it could have used some side ones for bigger power blocks. The outlets are suitably wide to handle a big cord, but if you have a power brick it's still going to cover up other outlets.

Construction is good and the model I'm using, the 7' one, has a great reach. The plug into the wall is small enough to not get in the way too much. It also has the on/off button on the back of the strip, which while I usually prefer on the top, is not a big deal. It's got the warning lights on it to tell when it's not grounded and when it's not protecting any longer. However, I have read reports that many strips still have the light even after their effectiveness is at an end, still Belkin is a good brand so I lean towards trusting what they tell me. Personally, I've never had a reason not to yet.

If you want something to protect your expensive hardware, you really ought to be looking at a [[ASIN:B0019804U8 UPS]] (Uninterruptible Power Supply) or in other words a backup battery. If you get a good one it will protect you from voltage spikes by suppressing high voltages and supplementing low voltages. There's also the added benefit your computer/tv/etc. will run for a brief time on battery power if you have an outage. However, this should really be saved for expensive hardware since they're quite a bit more expensive than a basic power strip. It's all a matter of what your needs are. For a baseline protection, you can't go wrong with one of these.spikes by suppressing high voltages and supplementing low voltages. product_title: Kinivo 501BN Premium 5 port High speed HDMI switch with IR wireless remote and AC Power adapter - supports 3D, 1080p
review_headline: Great switcher for 1.3a and 1.4 HDMI input
review_body:
I bought this product along with a Kinivo HDMI 1.4 splitter to replace an older HDMI switch after purchasing a new 3D projector. I have an older receiver and was hoping this combination of 3D capable products would allow me to avoid buying a new receiver. Unfortunately, with HDMI 1.4, all products have to be compliant. If it sees even one 1.3 HDMI device in the path it will drop both outputs to the lower res (non 3D) that all devices can handle. So I am having to return the splitter since it would not pass the 3D signal on to the Projector and also pass along the DTS Master Audio/Dolby HD audio to the receiver. My only option is to use a digital optical out from the playstation to pass audio to the receiver and pass the video direct to the projector via HDMI.

However, I can still use the Kinivo Switch so I am going to keep it. I currently have too many sources for my (pre 3D) Pioneer Elite receiver to handle. It has three in and one out. So I use a switch to take several sources and automatically select the active one and pass it to one input in the receiver. For this application, even though it is not switching a 3D signal, it works great for all non-3D sources I have.

As far as ease of use, as I select a different source, the switch automatically detects and selects it. It came with a remote but I won't need it. For switching between three non-3D sources at this time this thing works flawlessly. The price is right and it looks to be very durable. Based on how well it switches non-3D signals, I am confident it should work great for 3D applications as well.

product_title: Kaito T-1 Radio antenna
review_body:
This makes a great accessory to any radio's built-in antenna. Of all the somewhat \\"negative\\" reviews that say it doesn't work well, or it's just another piece of wire...really doesn't understand radio wave propagation & how the atmosphere & the time of day really affects those incoming radio waves. I won't get into detail on how those work because it's a technical process to explain, but any Amateur Radio operator knows the point I wanted to make here.

Clipping this onto the Kaito Voyager Pro while camping out in the middle of \\"nowhere\\" really helps pull in the radio stations. It's mostly used for shortwave, longwave & \\"worldband\\" frequencies, not for everyday \\"insert your favorite FM station here\\" kind of music station. It will help a bit, but not much. It's not designed for those bands.

As far as getting it back into it's case...it's not a problem. Think of this scenario: when reeling up your garden hose, it reels up nicely if you use the whole reel, not just one side. In other words, reel it up while \\"tilting\\" it to the left then to the right, just like a garden hose or an extension cord onto a cord wheel. Use the whole wheel inside. It rolls up nicely with room to spare if done like this. Don't use the finger indentions to roll it up. Put your finger somewhere on the same side & spin. Don't use two fingers...it'll drive you crazy!

I say it's a good buy for less than ten bucks. And it really helps pick up the atomic clock time server in Boulder Colorado on 20 MHz (or 20,000 KHz) at night. It's the strongest signal of the 5, 10, 15 & 20 MHz bands. Well, at least here on the East coast!

product_title: Klipsch Image S4i Premium Noise-Isolating Headset with 3-Button Apple Control
review_body:
I bought these IEM's in 2012 for ~$60. A good bargain considering the S4 II's sell for $99.99 (officially). To start, these IEM's are an awesome first purchase for those who have never experienced IEM's before; it was truly remarkable how much better these sounded than the Apple Earphones - and honestly, it should since we're dealing with a completely different product category.

While they sound excellent, what really ruins this experience is the terrible cabling that plagues this model. After a few months, you'll start to notice the protective rubber where the cable meets the monitor begins to peel, exposing the wire to the elements (and lots of bending). Naturally, the wire wears down faster, and as a result, I've had to get two replacement models (on my 3rd with this exact problem) from Klipsch. Not only do I now have the above problem, but the wire is beginning to fray near the headphone jack. It's also worth mentioning that the cable produces a lot of noise, just walking around - not to mention running. If you're a runner, you should check out the [[ASIN:B009X845N8 Klipsch Image A5i Sport In-Ear Headphones]] - the cable is much better and meant for hard use. Note: Steer clear of the iPhone rugged models - their cabling hasn't been updated yet.

It's important to note that you do get a two-year warranty with Klipsch, provided that you buy directly from Amazon. Both times I requested replacements, I got them promptly, and somehow, without a request for me to ship the old ones back (this is probably due to the discontinuation of the S4i (I) ). Supposedly, some don't like Klipsch's support, but I've never had a problem with them for both these headphones and the [[ASIN:B000062VUO Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 THX Certified Computer Speaker System (Black)]] speakers I own.

Overall, Klipsch is a great brand and has a great support staff behind them. Unfortunately, I can't recommend this model whatsoever. Check out their revision, the [[ASIN:B008X8HZZO Klipsch S4i-II]]. The cable seems a lot better, but I'm unsure if it alleviates the problems this model has.

product_title: August MR100 Bluetooth Audio Receiver Adapter - iPod Dock to Bluetooth Docking Station Convertor – Enable Bluetooth on Any iPod/iPad Speaker System
review_headline: My new favorite bluetooth adapter for the price.
review_body:
I currently have a CoolStream and wanted a cheaper solution. I bought this to put on my Logitech Sound dock with 30pin adapter at work. I wanted a cheap adapter, in the event it got stolen, I wouldn't be out too much money. I was hesitant to buy this one due to a small number of reviews, but I decided to take the gamble because it had such great reviews.

It comes inside a small box without directions. To those who NEED instructions, here you go:
Place MR100 bluetooth adapter on 30-pin connector and turn on sound dock.
The lights on MR100 start to flash quickly blue/red telling you it is searching for your device.
I went into my iPhone 4s bluetooth settings and found the device "mr100" and connected.
That was it. Nothing else needed. Took only a few seconds.
Once connected, the blue led flashes 4 times every 4 seconds when connected.

* If you pull the MR100 off its dock, or power is turned off your sound dock, you will have to re-connect to your device. Not a big deal.

I did buy this product partly because a reviewer said it works on DC power too.
I haven't been able to get it to work on my Logitech sound docks. (S715i & Pure-Fi Anywhere 2)
The CoolStream doesn't work on DC power either with those devices.

In my opinion the only difference between this and the CoolStream:

Dimensions are different, the coolstream is wider/bigger/different shape and color.
The CoolStream has a pair/power button, the August MR100 does not have any buttons.
Range is about the same, no scientific tests done but it works throughout my small home.
Sound quality is the same in my opinion.

product_title: FiiO E6 Portable Audio Headphone Amplifier
review_body:
<I am not an audiophile, nor can I give educational info about frequency numbers and/or audio terms and definitions. I do know that amplifiers (or amps) are used to get the full benefit of most high-end headphones or speakers>

This is a great, and cheap solution to increasing sound levels for my Zune HD, but can be used for any audio device that uses a standard 3.5mm headphone port. By default, the Zune HD outputs some low level volumes, especially when used on external speakers (such as my car audio and mobile AUX capable speakers). I decided to get the FiiO E6 because it's at the sweet spot between the older E5 (that only has I think 1 available EQ setting) and the newer E10 (that's just way too much for what I really need it for).

The E6 has three EQ settings: a bass boost option (red led), bass/treble boost (blue led), and a lower level EQ for a quieter listening experience (not positive about this, but the third option does sound like it lowers all sound level frequencies).

The unit comes with a mini-usb to usb cable for charging and use while charging. It also has a clip (x2 in case one breaks) that you can use to clip the device to a pant pocket or shirt or tie. It also includes two 3.5mm male-to-male audio cable; one that has two straight plugs, and one that has two 90-degree angled plugs. I like that they include these two options for versatile usage.

The E6 after a full discharge, takes about 30-45 minutes to charge via USB 2.0 port. If you have a wall outlet power adapter, it can take a shorter time. The led light on the clear corner turns from red to off when fully charged. After a full charge you get up to 10 hours of play before you'll need to recharge.

Overall, I've found so much use in this little device. I've owned the E6 for about a month and a half now and I love it.

(UPDATE: March 2016) This things still kicking. Even after accidentally washing it... Twice... Same amped volume output. Hoping the next Fiio I get can be so lucky.lume output. Hoping the next Fiio I get can be so lucky.

product_title: Panasonic ErgoFit In-Ear Earbud Headphone
review_body:
I just wanted the cheapest earbuds I could get that weren't the horrible plastic iPod ones. I used to like Skullcandy earbuds, but I became disillusioned with them when all three pairs I had purchased for myself and others had failed in less than a year. I tried these Panasonics because they were inexpensive and had a large sample size of reviews.

There are three sizes of rubber earbuds so that you can get a good fit. When I put these in, they do an amazing job of blocking out external noises; I wish I'd had these the last time I had to take a long flight. I can wear these while gaming and be comfortable for hours at a time (versus over-the-ear headphones, which make my ears ache after about 90 minutes). I was satisfied with the sound quality. However, my significant other (who is a big music buff and has bought LOTS of different headphones, including expensive Grado ones) liked these so much that he ended up appropriating them for himself. (I can remember him telling me how much he liked the bass on these, and they were on par with $20-$30 earbuds he's owned in the past.) We also agreed that these were much superior to Skullcandy earbuds in terms of sound quality and comfort. These obviously wouldn't take the place of quality over-the-ear headphones, but they are a fantastic buy for the money, and I will definitely be recommending these to others.

As an owner of Pioneer Elite (1500 dollar) receiver and a great set of Martin Logan speakers (over 3500 dollars) and considering myself an audiophile (but not a sound scientist or sound doctor) I must admit I was impressed by this little 16 bucks monster. Since I like singing while I take showers -yes I do!, haha- I decided to search online, looking to buy some nice iphone dock or some sort of sound system I can keep in my bathroom to either listen to music or the news...

So here is my appreciation to this little black box:

PROS:
-Value and price : 16 bucks! come on!!!
-GETS REALLY LOUD! this is great!!!! Great Bass!
-Sound quality is NOT CHEAP, and DO NOT GET DISCOURAGE BY PRICE. costs $16, but sounds $70-$200. Lows and highs work impressive from 0 to 60-70% volume.
-ITS WIRELESS and RE_CHARGEABLE!
-USB connectable! Charge it on the wall, laptop, or in your car.

-Ideal little speaker for small areas, like bathroom, office, store, etc. I would say a 10 x 10 or less. Now, I am confident you can produce great sound in larger areas, but I personally wouldn't do that. Its price makes it so accessible to keep one at the workplace, one on each bathroom, construction site, or wherever you want to take it.
-ALMOST RISK FREE.- because of the price, I don't have to worry about the humidity in my bathroom, dropping it or having my kids destroying it. I actually think it may be some sort of "kids resistant"...

CONS:
-Anything over 70% volume gets lightly to decently distorted. I wouldn't take 1 star out for this reason, due to the fact that the price makes out for it and that most people may need need to go that high, and that is my case.

So for all this reasons get, this little guy!

I like to wear my headphones while I am cooking or cleaning the house or moving or cleaning the car etc, and these are CONSTANTLY coming out.  Or just pulling out a little so that the seal is broken, and then you have to put them back in and adjust them again.  I really quite hated them.  I had just about talked myself into getting another set of Bose when my wife found my old set!  I was so happy to have them back, it was like Christmas.  The Bose stay in your ear no matter what and you can't even feel them.  And the sound quality is....well they are Bose.  It's simply the best.  I wear my headphones quite a lot, so having a bad set is a thorn in my side.  If you do not wear them often, or you don't move much, maybe these will work for you.  But if you are buying headphones to wear while you aren't moving, why get in-ear?  I have the Bose MIE2i's and I highly recommend them.  i got mine on sale at Target for 80 something.

product_title: Sound by Boho Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Hands Free + MP3 Playerand Now Bluetooth Receiver
review_body:
Ignore the negative reviews from people who haven't tried it I understand the skeptical reviews; they list some good reasons for being suspicious - but they are wrong. And they are wrong to pan a product they haven't used.

This little speaker sounds as good or better than my [[ASIN:B0094S354W Logitech UE 984-000298 Mobile Boombox Bluetooth Speaker and Speakerphone (Black Grill/Black)]].In addition to excellent sound the Boho has an TF card slot, and costs FAR less.

This little Boho speaker is very good, but it's not perfect:
-On an iPad 2 and an iPad mini, both running iOS 7 the "pause" button works but not the "back" or "forward" buttons. Another review here implies they do work when playing from the TF card.
-The volume buttons control only the volume on the speaker and have no effect on the volume of the iPad - so you have to manipulate both to get the full volume. My Bluetooth earphones control the iPad volume directly - simpler and easier.
-The Boho speaker is loud enough to listen to it in my car, but it's difficult (dangerously so?) to adjust the volume while driving. The Logitech UE Mobile Boombox volume controls are large and easily accessible on top - much easier.
-The instructions are inadequate; they don't explain why the status light blinks all the time, for instance.
-In an informal battery test I was able to listen for several hours multiple times over two days - good enough for me. The BohoSound website claims 3 to 8 hours of battery life.

NB: Neither the package insert nor the Boho website mention a warranty.

1st Followup: When I wrote my original review this speaker cost $30, About 11/11/13 the price was $50. Today (11/15/13) it's $100. I still recommend Boho, but I would have to say that at the current price it's no longer head-and-shoulders above the competition. Factor in the price change when you read some of the other reviews, too.

2nd Update:
I've used this speaker almost every day since I bought it almost a year ago. It's working as well today as the first day. I changed my rating from 4 stars to 5 because I'm very happy with my purchase. Also, the price is now (8/14/14) $10 less than I paid ($20 vs $30) so it's even a better deal than before. I haven't comparison shopped for Bluetooth speakers in a while so I don't know what the alternatives are - I just know this speaker sounds excellent, has lasted in daily use, and is inexpensive enough that I wouldn't worry that there's a slightly cheaper deal somewhere.

review_headline: Excellent entry level sub FOR THE PRICE!!!
review_body:
Excellent entry level SUB FOR THE PRICE!!!

Ok...here goes. I like good sound. I LOVE good sound for a bargain price! In my quest to find a decent 2.1 stereo setup for music and occasional movies I stumbled on this sub for it's unheard of price for $69. My review is based on when this sub is on sale for $89 or less...if it's at the normal price of $129 I would look elsewhere.

I paired this sub with [[ASIN:B004R929AY Teac LS H265 2 Way Speaker System]] (Seriously, google these and their review in Cnet...I found them cheaper at accesories4less for $90/pair shipped) and [[ASIN:B006U1VH2S Sony STRDH130 Channel Stereo Receiver]] (I purchased this refurbished for $70 through Newegg).

I like the Teac bookshelf speakers a lot but as with any smaller speaker, found the bass to be a little lacking. The receiver I purchased is a Stereo 2 channel receiver (if you want 5.1 or 7.1 you will have to buy something else) altough it is able to run a total of 4 speakers. I used the \\"A\\" speaker outputs to run my Teacs and the \\"B\\" speaker outputs to connect to the Polk PSW10 with 14 guage speaker wire (I bought on Amazon way cheaper than they have at Best Buy etc).

The Polk sub was the missing link I was looking for! The Teacs do a fantastic job on the mid and upper range with the Polk filling in the bass. For a total of $230 shipped, I challenge you to find a system that sounds this good! If you do, I would like to buy it also lol. When looking at bookshelf speakers I wanted an accurate sounding speaker with fairly good sensitivity. I own the Klipsch Synergy B-20s (these are really good speakers also when they are on sale at less than $150 a pair, the Polk Audio T15s (which are currently on sale for $50 at Best Buy right now!), and the above mentioned Teacs. I like all of them but the Teacs are my favorites, if budget is an issue buy the Polks while they're $50 a pair.

If a quality sounding system at a good price is what you are going for, buy this while it is on sale. If you need more (my experience says most people probably won't) step up to the Dayton Audio 12\\" sub on here for $110-$125. If you really want quality and budget isn't a big concern, I would go with one of the internet direct companies for subs: HSU, Outlaw, Lava, etc but it's going to cost you!

product_title: Micca Reference Series R-6C 6.5-Inch Rimless In-Ceiling Speaker (Each, White)
review_body:
I purchased the R-6C, M-6C, and C-6C and did some back-to-back listening between the three. All three were tested in 0.8cu ft MDF enclosures packed about 50% with polyfil. My ceiling is open to the attic space so I needed to close in the space behind the speakers. Of the three, I thought the R-6C outperformed the other two and was worth extra money. For this review, I'll focus on the R-6C.

I was disappointed that the R-6C comes with an aluminum tweeter as I find that metal cone tweeters usually have a strong, in your face sound, and this was no different. For a speaker that I want to sit down and pay attention to that's OK, but for something that will be playing in the background I would prefer a smoother sound that doesn't grab your attention. The speaker in general pulled a lot of detail out of the music, much more than the other two Micca examples, and did a much better job in the lower frequencies. In fact, I'm quite happy with the way it represents male vocals and music with larger string instruments. No sub in the room, and don't feel the need for it. Because the R-6C had an up-front sound I had initially set the tweeter switch to -3DB and the woofer to +3DB hoping to tame the somewhat harsh sounding tweeter. But after some experimentation I discovered that those switches weren't simply cutting the level of each of the drivers' entire frequency range, but were actually changing the tone of each driver. Those both went back to 0 and I turned my attention to the limited bass and treble adjustments on my receiver. Again after some listening and dialing in I was able to get these sounding pretty close to what I'd like. Installing the grill (with the included cloth lining) also softens them a bit. The other two do not have the cloth lining in the grill so I suspect Micca added it to the R-6C to tame that tweeter a bit. Overall I'm pretty happy with them, and not just for the price. Will be buying more for the rest of the house.

product_title: BESTEK 200W Converter
review_headline: Nice unit for 220-110 conversion when overseas.
review_body:
For the US consumer this is a unit that is primarily intended for overseas travel. You can take your 110V-only devices (e.g., the charger of my electric toothbrush) and use them in Europe or elsewhere. The primary benefit is the 220 to 110 transformer that is embedded inside. It would not make much sense to use this unit in the US exclusively, though you could.

- I didn't get an opportunity to test this unit overseas yet. I will update the review if I encounter something negative. I thought I should write a short review since some of the other reviews here are confusing and misrepresent the device. Other reviews here mention successful use overseas.

- The unit has a fan that makes a little noise. This fan must be cooling down the transformer which may generate some heat under heavy load. Again you should not buy this unit if you don't need the 220 to 110 conversion and if you do need the conversion light noise is something one can put up with for the benefit of charging your 110-only devices. Alternative is to get heavy step-down transformers which are difficult to carry. (I am not aware of any competing devices in Amazon that offer similar functionality with similar number of outputs.)

- My unit has a ground at the input and outputs. I will check later if they are actually connected but no reason to think they are not. Other reviews about ground leads missing are not accurate for the device I was shipped. That said, in most places overseas a ground lead will be hard to come by.

- The spec mentions protection. There are no user replaceable fuses, etc. So a fuse is hopefully inside the unit, again, no reason to think it is not.

- There is a functional on/off switch which can be used to turn the unit (and the fan noise) off when not in use. The switch by itself is a little unreliable (one star off) but there is a light which assures you of the status.

- The unit looks very nice.

Overall I really like the device and I look forward to giving it extended use.

To the manufacturer: Most people will be concerned about the safety of using the device under load. Assuring specific current/voltage protection and adding a user replaceable fuse will improve the device. Please use a better on/off switch in future iterations.

product_title: Teac Receiver with Integrated Amplifier and High Quality DAC's
review_headline: Finally a quality integrated amp with a DAC in a small footprint
review_body: I purchase tons of stuff from Amazon but this product wasn't available a month ago so I bought it new from a stereo store on eBay.  Too bad, it is $120 cheaper here at this reduced price.  Anyway, I have been looking for an integrated amp with a DAC and this one has all the features I wanted.  The NAD's are larger and their USB module only supports 96kHz.  The Onkyo has some poor reviews, some sort of amp buzzing.  Others are so ridiculously expensive I was getting a little disappointed that nothing was in my sweet spot for purchase.  I use this unit in my office going bit direct from my computer.  The TEAC WASAPI driver is solid.  Their software player is really lean, you would probably want to use Foobar 2000 or JRiver MC.  However, the player is a really quick way to test if you are truly going bit direct and avoiding the Windows mixer as it is really easy and straight forward to set up so it makes for a nice diagnostic utility if you will.  The sound of the amp is excellent.  Not for a huge space, of course at 30-40W, but for an office, bedroom or small apartment, you are going to be very happy.  The other important thing to realize with this or any DAC for this matter is that when your computer sleeps, or when you switch input sources, etc..., sometimes these units can lock, especially when switching to and from the streaming USB input.  My Cambridge DAC would lose link even with the TosLink input.  But there is only an electronic on/off button on the Cambridge and many other similar units so when it would lock up you could not reset the unit w/o unplugging it.  This TEAC unit has a hard on/off switch so you can \\"reset\\" the unit if need be.  I've had to do this only twice as the driver is solid, and it is really convenient to just power down and then back up from the front panel.  The small footprint is great for a desk setup.  Super quiet operation, no amp buzz or anything.  When connected to the optical input or the USB, volume at 100%, with music paused, absolutely no amp hiss or noise through the speakers, a very low noise floor.  I just think TEAC really got it right here, in fact, check out the whole new reference line from them, some really interesting and innovative quality stuff at good price points.  I know Sony is also getting into the whole high res audio space with some new equipment but the TEAC stuff just seems more practical to me for a computer based digital setup.  I've been buying stereo equipment for many years and this is the first time in a while I've really been excited for a new unit.  Finally, sound quality is excellent, again at super loud volumes you are going to press the amp but at moderate to even somewhat loud levels, it is super clean.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
My office is located in a building that used to be a factory or a beer brewery at some point. Very high ceilings, festooned with two industrial-size air conditioners and adorned in large pipe work, produce never ending hum, which reflects from the walls and concrete. Whoooooo is what I hear all day. The noise level is high enough to drown out conversations two cubicles away from me. This hum is most irritating especially when you try to concentrate on programming software.

The UPS Man arrived with my package from Amazon and I promptly extracted these headphones from the box. Popped the battery in put it on my head and flipped the switch. The silence is deafening. All hum is simply cancelled out. Just like that with a flip of a switch it was off and staid off all day. Interestingly enough I could still hear people talking near by, but all the hum and ambient noise simply went away. When at the end of my working day I took the headphones off my head I was surprised how loud the normal ambient noise is at the office.

Listening to music in these headphone is also a joy. I do not have to crank it up loud to drown the ambient out. And the sound quality is very very good.

The headphones are comfortable and soft, but perhaps not so comfortable if used in a room with 75F temperature because the ear pieces are closed of course.

These headphones will not do you much good at a rifle range or if you work next to a pumping diesel engine, but they work well to cancel ambient sound. You can still hear normal conversation though it is muffled.

This product does exactly what it say on the box.

product_title: SoundMAGIC E30 Noise Isolating In-Ear Monitor Earphones (Black)
review_headline: Finally the right earbuds for me.
review_body:
I went through several earbuds at this price point including Skullcandy Titans, Sony XBA-1s, and Sennheiser CX300-IIs. The Titans were the worst of the lot, with muddy mids and overpowering bass. The Senns had a nice tight bass and good midrange but way too much sizzle. The Sony's had the best midrange detail of all of them, but lacked bass altogether and the high end detail was muted. The SoundMAGICs however, are right in the sweet spot, a real Goldilocks item. Still not nearly as good as my Grado over ear cans, but good enough for walking around and working out.
As far as build quality goes, they seem very good. The wires are a little stiffer and less prone to tangling than any of the others, and I like the metal used on the plug and where the wires split. The wires also don't seem to have problems with microphonics. The over the ear style is a personal preference issue, and I happen to be OK with them. The only downside is the various tips it comes with seem cheap. There are enough of them that I did find a couple of pairs with a decent fit, which is the key for this style of earbud to sound right.

product_title: RCA TVPRAMP1Z Preamplifier for Outdoor Antenna
review_body:
I have to state right now, I love this little gadget. I have a roof mounted antenna that I bought and installed so I could "cut the cable". We ditched satellite and cable TV in favor of Internet, Netflix, and an antenna to get local channels. The antenna was good by itself but had some trouble with periodic fade or momentary signal loss on the 2 channels I wanted most. If I split the signal to go to 2 TVs it was even worse. I got this to fix that problem and not only did it do that most superbly, I picked up about 8 or 10 new channels! I was very impressed to say the least. You really have to pay attention to the instructions because they are a bit confusing, and I'm a tech nerd too, but once you get the connections right, the results are excellent. I also mounted this inside the house right at the point where I split my signal, instead of on the antenna pole like it says to do. Either way works but I prefer it inside. I think one of the biggest things to ensure though is you also have a good, high quality cable running from the antenna to the TV (with whatever devices in between). The better the cable the better the signal is going to be. Don't go buy those overpriced hundred dollar cables you can find, just a good quality cable with nice, properly constructed ends. If it looks cheap, it probably performs that way too. I got mine at Menards or Lowes, can't remember, and I think the 100 footer I had to use only cost me abouot $15 or $20.

Anyway, can't say enough good about this. If you are on the edge of reception and really need to boost the signal to clear it up, this works very well and the price is very reasonable.

product_title: SENNHEISER Headphones
review_body:
I'm ancient, have OK hearing and am no trained audiophile. That said, these are great headphones, make no mistake! Lemme gas on a bit, regarding these and comments made thereupon:

Construction:
These are no better or worse than anything at this price point. Sure, everything's plastic, but well-made as I have found with Sennheiser products since 1975. I bought mine at a local store so I had an immediate, In Your Face return option if anything went wrong. Some online stores like Crutchfield or Guitar Center are also good for damaged goods return. Once one gets these in their hot hands in good condition, there shouldn't be problems. You don't want to yank them off your head or pull the plug by the cord or leave them in a hot/freezing car for a month, or wear them in the rain. Other than that, anyone having mechanical problems is, IMHO a nit of the first order.

The cord is quite long on these--probably a good six feet. To my mind, this immediately renders them a non-starter for portable use; I would have nightmares trying to use them rolling down the street on my ol' Schwinn. Remember how Isadora Duncan ended up..?

Sound:
Some call these low volume phones and I think they are not using the right tool for the job. Portable audio devices don't have the Oomph to drive serious headphones, folks. They are fine for small earbuds which require tiny amounts of current, but regular headphones will always need more juice to operate properly; get over it. You want good portable sound, find some earbuds you like, friends.

Aside from these headphones alleged inefficiency, there have been comments regarding their overall sound. Now that's going to be very subjective, so I'll be as OBjective as possible so the potential sheller-outer can form a reasoned opinion:

Frequency Range--Strong trebles, decent bass. I'd aver that if you hear music on a truly flat set of speakers, like KEF Reference series, they sound \\"bright\\"--but aren't. It's just we're used to mid-fi which is voiced for particular purposes. As for the bass output on these, it's detailed and natural. Again, the iPod/Walkman crowd may be opting for jaw-dropping lows, but that's not natural--nor desirable in headphones designed for normal listening, especially to natural voice/acoustic material. These are terrific for those applications and again, the wrong tool for the Techno/Pop/Dance addict. Plug these into your computer or radio, turn on a Jazz station and you WILL NOT be disappointed!

Sound Stage--Nicely balanced and natural, instruments accurately placed when no sound adjustments are made, other than volume. My computer can create digital reverb effects I don't really care for, but are well reproduced.

Detail/Presence--Superb detail, instruments very live. Presence is OK, rather flat not warm as you get from a pair of JBL, Polk or Infinity speakers. Again, a pretty flat frequency response.

Noise Isolation--Some, but not a design issue. These are around the ear phones for home listening, not noise isolation or cancelling. If someone comes in and asks a question, I can easily hear them through the music, with normal incidental house noises blocked well. These phones are lightweight, nothing like the KOSS Pro-4AAs of the past. Those blocked sound OK, but after a half hour or so were unwearable.

The bottom line is that Sennheiser makes great headphones at nearly any price point and the majority of users who choose them for the right reasons will not be disappointed. This pair is for listening at home to acoustic music and maybe pop that isn't all bass-heavy like Death Metal or Dance. They are a poor choice for portable use, not due to design flaws, just the wrong application. I mean, you wouldn't take a Volkswagen Beetle to a construction site for heavy hauling, right?

You won't find a better pair of twenty-five buck (or so) headphones for casual listening at home anywhere. In my own experience, you'd need to go over $100 to get truly worthwhile performance improvement over these. In other words, A Best Buy Under Fifty Bucks!

product_title: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with 2.1A USB Charging (Black)
review_headline: A great charger and plug strip with a few design flaws
review_body:
I love that this surge protector and plug strip has two USB ports for charging my Kindle and cell phone, but the placement of the USB ports, which is a major selling point for this unit, is hindered by the position of the cord wrap feature as well as the areas to plug in your larger electronics that have the big boxy plug. The USB ports are tucked right in between the cord wrap spot and the place to plug in larger plugs, so if one isn't blocking your USB ports, the other is.

In addition, I kind of wish that the majority of the plugs were spaced farther apart. I have a few electronics that have very small boxy plugs, and those don't fit right next to one another on the main area of the plug strip. The only thing that will fit on those plugs without overlapping are the traditional small plugs that are on lamps and other uncomplicated items. I don't have too many of those, and I'm guessing that most people buy plug strips because they have a bunch of electronics, almost all of which would have those bigger boxy plugs.

That said, the surge protector feature is absolutely effective, and I know this because we had PG&E replacing some poles in our neighborhood recently and we had many incidences of brownouts, surges, and spotty power, and this unit kept any harm from coming to any of my electronics that were plugged into it.

And while it is easy to make design suggestions, I have to say that I haven't found the perfect plug strip yet. Almost all of them seem to have some design characteristics that make them not quite ideal. While this unit is not perfectly designed with regards to the placement of the USB ports and the spacing of the regular plugs, it is certainly a high-quality, very functional unit that does what it says it does, and I trust the Belkin brand that it's going to function for some time. This plug strip is also nice in that it has a space so that you can mount it on the wall or on the back of your desk if you so desire.

review_body: On the advice of a friend, we purchased this TV mount for mounting our first flat panel TV. The cost was MUCH cheaper than in the big box stores and that had me worried. We placed the TV in front of a window, so I mounted the mount on a piece of  2X12 which was cut to span the opening to the stud one each side of the window. I mounted it using: thick standard (SAE) bolts, fender washers, stop washers and nuts all found at my local home improvement store. Once mounted, I mounted the board holding the TV mount over/in front of the window securing it with four anchor screws into each stud; 2 studs to the right and two to the left (the window framing studs and then one more stud out from that). The installation of the TV side of the mount was EASY as could be. I actually followed the TV's instructions on this part, just sued the appropriate screws from the TV mount kit. At this point, I called my friend who had installed several TV's of his own and suggested this mount to come help me mount this, and when he looked at how the mount was made, and installed (up to this point) he said it would take a hurricane or tornado to pull the TV off the wall. All in all, I am VERY happy with this TV mount and will certainly buy another if the time comes (if we move from this house, I am leaving the mount as mounted because of the work it took & will buy another one of these).
