product_title: Onkyo ES-FC300 On-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I have a pair of 280 HD sennheisers I've had for about 8 years now.
They go for $80-90 most of the time.
Given these ones were almost twice as much, I was expecting something better.

I was sorely disappointed when they didn't measure up. The sound is not terrible, but overall I'd take the sennheisers hands down.

Here is the breakdown.

Pros:
- Sound is very good
- Design is nice and stylish
- The color is a deep violet that both men and women can wear (I was afraid it would be a lighter violet)
- The chord is decent length
- Plastic quality is very good

Cons:
- The are \\"on ear\\" as opposed to cupping the ear. Which means that sound leaks a lot more than the sennheisers.
- The 280HD sennheisers for half the price have a better sound (I am not an audiophile and could tell the difference)
- presses on ear, more uncomfortable than ear cup style headphones

While in a vacuum these could be 4 start headphones, given the much higher costs than a product I own, and the fact that it didn't quite measure up, makes it very hard to recommend. If you care more about the look, these might be a better choice. The HD 280 look more professional, serious, boring black. These are stylish with a little more flare.

product_title: ARCTIC P531 Gaming Stereo USB Headphones
review_body:
Like a lot of people, I don't always have a lot of money. That's why I look for \\"bargains\\" or \\"cheap\\" versions of nice things. My gaming computer is Frankenstein living off of used and cheap parts, with the exception of the CPU. My favorite gaming headset, the Turtle Beach P51, has had the right side stop working, unless I endlessly jiggle the wire and hope it comes back on. Not ideal, to say the least. I had to resort to wearing two pairs of headphones, on with the mic, the other without, just to hear and talk at the same time. It was pretty bad.

I looked all over for a nice replacement, and this time I wanted to go a step further. If possible, I wanted to go for surround sound. And thank whatever religious deity you believe in, I found these.

First off, not only are they 5.1 surround sound, they are TRUE 5.1 surround sound, meaning they actually have all the speaker in each side that make up the surround sound experience, rather than simulating it like other cheaper headsets. Now, I've never used surround sound headsets before, but I have used nice quality stereo headsets, and these can compete very well. The bass is rich, and sounds like it's really all there. The surround is also very nice. Again, while I haven't used other surround headsets before this, I have used surround sound speakers, 7.1, and these sounds very close, and crisper since it's right by your ears.

I'm using Windows 8, and while the box doesn't have Windows 8 support on it, these do work with it. The reason is, these came out before Windows 8, but if you go to the Arctic website, you will find Windows 8 drivers, which are a MUST download. I mean it. These won't work like you expect them to without them.

The software is very helpful. You can tweak the EQ to your preference, configure where you want the speaker sound and how much of it, and even toggle 7.1 virtual surround sound, which is a bit hit or miss in quality. (In games that don't support 7.1, you won't hear some sound effects. I recommend just keeping it on 5.1 unless you're for sure the game or movie you're using supports 7.1)

After some tweaking, you'll be impressed with the sound. Again, rich, deep bass, great speaker quality, and great surround sound. The mic is also good. Not great, but good. I've recorded myself, and used the Skype playback feature, and it sounds clear and picks up your voice very well without picking up the popping sound when you use Ts or Ps in words like my Turtle Beach mic did. There is also noise cancellation and voice modulations in the software that you can configure.

These headphones do have some weight to them. Personally, they are the heaviest I've ever used, however it's not too much that they are uncomfortable, it's just a bit off-putting when you're not used to it. They also have very nice cushions for your ears, and grab onto your head snuggly. Some people may not be able to wear these for very long periods of time though. Either the weight, or the way it fits may cause a little strain to people who aren't used to it after some time of use.

Music sounds beautiful. Games sound realistic, and the headset even vibrates in times of explosions (though I only notice it on the right side. not sure if that was on purpose, or if my left side isn't working correctly)

I honestly didn't expect such great quality out of these for its price, especially since it used True 5.1 surround rather than virtual. I'll update after I give them more use in case I notice they don't last very long, or any complications arise later on. For now, I certainly recommend them, like many others on here have.

EDIT: It's February of 2014, about 4 months later, and they still work just fine. To be fair, I've tried to be delicate with them, but I have dropped them a few times (since they are heavy, they have fallen off my head when I've had to sneeze), but so far that doesn't seem to have caused any damage. They still sound just as good as when I first got them, and the mic still works. I even got my younger brother a pair since I've liked them so much, and he does as well. The vibration feedback in games like Battlefield 4 is pretty amazing. If I ever need to replace these in the future, I know I'll miss having that. Overall, I still have no real complaints other than its weight. The cord however has started to show signs of use, as it tangles up and bunches like many standard cables do. Also, I've really come to hate the control box on the wire...it tends to get in the way a lot, and can add some extra tension to your head if you don't have it laying on a surface.

EDIT 2: 5/20/2014 So in November, my brother got a pair of these for his birthday. Well, about a month ago, they stopped working. The one side slowly faded out, and the mic no longer worked. As for mine, that I got two months before his, are still working just fine. It all depends on how you treat them. My brother wasn't exactly delicate with the cord, so that could be what the problem was. product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_headline: Logitech finally got it with this one!
review_body:
I own two of the older generation Harmony remotes (an 890 which this just replaced downstairs, and an 760 upstairs, which is next on the chopping block after this huge success). After the last two, I nearly didn't buy this one, it was a giant leap of faith on my part. This new remote is by far the best one yet. It works as I always wanted the old remotes to function, but they never really did meet my needs and expectations. They always had some shortcomings, causing the others in the house to not use what they lovingly called, \\"that stupid useless remote\\". I'd change functions and have to spend a few minutes clicking through the help menu to reset items that didn't change correctly.

Well this new remote is pretty dang slick, and it works like it should. Setup took a while, as with any of these it does, but once it's done, it's really pretty beautiful. The new programming interface is much easier to use, navigate, and is leaps and bounds ahead of what the previous were. You can even change functionality from the smart phone app if needed, so no need to plug back into the PC and reprogram it over and over like I did before. The real big items for me was the bluetooth integration, wifi, and smartphone compatibility. Now I don't need the remote if I have my phone nearby. Another big plus is the ability to pair with the Playstation 3 and the Nintendo Wii, so I no longer have to manually turn them on or off.

Well done logitech, keep it up, this thing rocks and i'll be buying a 2nd one to replace my other old Harmony 760 in the very near future.

review_headline: Once overcoming hook up problems, it works
review_body: This product requires a headphone level output to generate a signal strong enough to activate the transmitter.  Simply hooking up to an audio line feed out from your amplifier will not work.  This unit is advertised as being compatible with your AV receiver/amp, but keep in mind that if you hook up to the headphone output on your amp, you will get no feed to your speakers (headphone connection usually mutes the speakers).  This is a problem unless you are able to tap some other headphone output with volume control within your system.  This I was able to do.  This is primarily designed for IPhones or some other portable with an earphone/headphone jack output.  This system needs to more fully address the customers who want to use this unit as an external wireless speaker connected to a home AV audio/video system, specifically allow connection to audio RCA outputs.  Once I got the proper audio feed to the transmitter, it worked fine.  But, it was not at all straightforward.

review_body:
Let me start with why I bought these to begin with. I normally never spend much on anything that plays music because for the most part I never really got into listening to music....until I got a free pair of griffin wood tones (the ear buds at a marketing convention)and I'm not going to lie, they were amazing and made me see music in a whole new light. After about 3 months they broke (I was very rough with them) and I went and bought new griffen wood tone earbuds which made me as just as happy as my previous pair. So much so I decided that it would be a worthy investment to get the headphone version.

As you can see above I gave the headphones a 4 star review, which still means that in my book they are a good pair of headphones, and I would still recommend them to anyone looking for headphones. But these headphones just don't give off the same quality of sound that their earbud counterpart do. In comparison the bass is significantly weaker, there is a more idle noise, and it distorts very high notes, and for that I sadly have to mark it down a star.

So in review, if you haven't bought the earbuds DO SO...NOW! and if you are in the market for a headset, keep this one in consideration.

product_title: JBL Speaker Foam Edge Repair Kit, 10" JBL 125A, 127A, 127H, 410G, 4410, FSK-10A
review_headline: Bringing Back My Speaker From the Dead
review_body: A few weeks ago, one of my JBL LXE990 loudspeakers started making strange clicking sounds.  When I removed the front grill, I discovered that the foam surround on its 10 inch woofer had completely disintegrated.  What to do?  I searched online for a suitable  pair of replacement speakers, but could not find anything comparable with larg woofers.  Apparently, speakers like this just aren't made anymore, because  manufacturers have  decided that small bookshelf speakers with a separate powered subwoofer are now the way to go.  I did some more searching and came across this JBL sspeaker repair kit from Simply Speakers for $25.  I ordered it from Amazon, and it was delivered by USPS just three days later.  The box contained two rubber woofer surrounds, one for each woofer in the pair, plus a tube of special adhesive to glue them onto the woofer cones.  The online instructions, available on the Simply Speakers web site recommends removing the woofer from the cabinet before starting the repair job, but this isn't really necessary to get good results.  I just laid the speaker cabinet flat on the floor face up with the drivers exposed.  First I carefully removed the gasket from the woofer frame and scraped away  traces of leftover foam using a screwdriver and some cotton puffs doused in rubbing alcohol.  I applied a thin bead of glue to the circumference of the woofer cone and attached the inner lip of the surround, making certain that it was centered properly.  I then pressed all around the lip to  make sure that it adhered securely to the woofer cone and let it dry for an hour.  Then I glued the outer lip of the surround to the woofer frame and let it dry for another hour.  Finally, I glued the gasket back over the outer lip of the surround and let it dry for yet another hour.  When I reconnected the speaker to my receiver, I was amazed to hear that it sounded as good as  new.  The bass was deep and powerful once again with no clicks or rattles.  So for only $25, I rejuvenated my speaker and saved the cost of buying a new pair.  And I have another surround on hand in case the surround on the other speaker's woofer rots away.  If you have a JBL speaker whose woofer surround is showing signs of rot or deterioration, do yourself a favor, buy this repair kit and fix it yourself.  You'll be able to enjoy your speaker again for many more years to come and save a bundle of money on new speakers.  I'm not much of a do-it-yourselfer, so if I can do it, anyone can do it.

product_title: Soul Combat+ Ultimate Active Performance Over-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I purchased the SL150s back when they were first introduced and I still have them today, still works great, and still a very satisfied customer. So when Soul introduced their new sports line, I was obviously intrigued.
It's like they read my mind. The only thing that I wish I could do with the SL150s was to wear them during my workout. While I technically could, it just didn't feel right. The band gets all sweaty and I worry that it would break the speakers. So I never really did. But now, I think they have solved my problem!
I went with the combats because they look like a pair that is more durable than the Transform and they simply look amazing. I mean, they just look sweet and it just looks like it fits perfectly. I didn't get a chance to try these on since I bought them online. But given the good track record from the SL150s, I had faith. And of course, it didn't disappoint. Here is a quick summary of how it feels and how it sounds, since I am casual user and not an expert, but hopefully this will give you an idea of what these headphones are like.
They are super light. When I put them on, I can barely feel them. Not only because of the light weight, but also because it fits so close to your head. Usually, if something fits so tightly, sweat becomes a problem, especially when you are being active. But the dual band design allows more ventilation. Sound is comparable to the SL150s, great mid range, plenty loud, and not a whole lot of sound leakage. The bass is not as strong but I expected that with a slimmer headphone. Overall, the headphone is clearly designed for you to move around actively. I've ran with these, I've lifted with these, and even shot around the basketball with them. Not once did they slip or felt loose. So they are meant for all athletes.
I say give these a try if you are an active person. If not, go with the SL150s. Otherwise, these are just perfect and I am glad someone finally decide to make something that targets towards athletes and that are not just the basic in-ear. Soul clearly cares about sound quality, but with the combats, they really hit a home run with both sound and feel.

product_title: Sony MDRZX100 Headphones
review_body:
Ever since the days of the original Sony Walkman (cassette), no matter where in the world I've travelled, if I needed a replacement pair of headsets/earbuds, the one brand I could always count on to deliver satifactory sound was Sony.

So..... when I recently needed another pair of closed headsets, I ordered these without so much as a second thought.

The (white) colour is clean and appealing, and the red, plastic-ring right-ear "indicator" very helpful.
The fit is comfortable, even over extended periods.

The sound quality, however, is another matter...

With the model number of MDR-ZX100, I knew this was an "entry level" product, but that was all I required for the particular application in mind.

However, upon receipt and use of this product was I ever surprised.... rather unpleasantly so, I'm sorry to say.

As a fan of Sony's trademark "Bass Boost", I expected the usual "big bottom" sound found in that frequency range. Unfortunately it just isn't there with these earphones.

Also lacking is the usual "punchiness" normally heard in the mid and high frequencies.
Vox lack definition and depth.
There is an overall "mushy" sound quality.

Additionally, there appears to be a type of AVL (volume limiter) built into this product.
This may be fine for younger/unsupervised children who may inadvertently blow-out their eardrums, but as an adult I prefer the freedom to adjust the volume to my liking.

While acceptable for general usage/spoken word, overall I found the MDR-ZX100 disappointing for a Sony product.

I intend to continue to use them, but cannot recommend them for those with discriminating audio expectations... even for a basic, entry-level headphone.

- C.C. Amazon Prime Member-Reviewer

product_title: Nxg 12 500w Powered Subwoofer 24hz-200hz Black Pebble Finish
review_body:
First off I wanted to give a big thumbs up too AVS house for their great customer service!. I want to compare this sub-woofer too 3 others I tried: BIC F12, Energy 10.3 and the Klipsch RW-12d. I used my receiver to control the crossover and set my speakers(polk rti8, csi5) at 70 hz so everything lower was going to the subwoofer. When I first started using the subwoofer I set the volume too full, the sub was clear but it didnt quite have the same umph as the Klipsch, or Energy 10.3. Second I couldn't feel the low low vibration I could with the Klipsch. I wasn't to happy with it, I actually contacted AVS house about a return, they promptly responded with a return authorization. But during this time the sub started to break in, I also moved the sub too a different position(Corner), it seemed to react differently than the Klipsch, F12 or Energy. Now I can feel the subwoofer, but the volume was way to high, currently I have my level on the receiver set to -1 and the volume on the sub set to half, its more than adequate umph for my 2000 cubic feet room(scares the dog).

NX-BAS-500 vs BIC F12: I've had the BIC F12 for about 3 months, it was a mistake too buy I was being too cheap. The F12 can rattle the floor and get loud, but not as loud or as low as the BAS 500. The F12 is ok in Movies, but absolutely horrible in Music the Bas-500 integrates in music perfectly. Additionally the NXG is a smaller sub.

NX-BAS-500 vs Energy 10.3: The energy is a friends sub, I only used it to test for a direct comparison, its a good sub, but when the Energy is cranked up to a comparable volume as the BAS-500 it sounds very distorted and muffled.

NX-BAS-500 vs Klipsch RW12d: I bought the RW12d on a sale, the same time as the NX-BAS-500, the loser would get returned. First off the Klipsch has a control panel on the front top of the subwoofer, this is pretty convenient, the Klipsch is about 25% larger than the NXG. In music the Klipsch was good, hit very hard without getting muffled but didnt rattle the floors unless turned up, whereas the NXG even listening to low volumes, you can feel it, plus the NXG is a smoother sound. In movies during explosions I liked the Klipsch more, but in everything else I prefer the NXG, I think its a better sub. Secondly I think the NXG aesthetically looks great, of all the sub-woofers I've used its the clear winner.

product_title: Philips SHS8105A/28 Ear-Hook Headset for Android
review_headline: Great headphones but they didn't last for me
review_body:
These headphones were generally great for me. I needed an over-the-ear style to keep earbuds in, and this was one of the few options including a mic and remote. I used them almost daily for about four months and was happy as a clam. Until one day the remote suddenly stopped working. None of the buttons would do anything. Then about three days later the headphones themselves stopped working and they never came back on again. The weird part is that I've had headphones like this fail before, but usually you see something physically wrong, like the headphone comes apart or the wire gets worn at the connector, but these just stopped working even though they appear to be in good condition. While I did wear them a lot, I wouldn't say I wore them out. I would give these a five star review if they had continued to work. That said, I couldn't in good faith give it only one or two stars because frankly I'm about to order another pair (!!). I see now that they have some sort of one-year warranty and I might have been able to get them replaced by Philips, but I threw them away a few days ago when they stopped working. There still aren't many choices like this in this category so I'm about to buy this product again, hope for better luck, and pay more attention to the warranty.

[UPDATE] I see now that this isn't the exact same model that I bought last time. There's another pair just like this but with a different remote and packaged as an iPhone headset. For some reason that one is $5 cheaper even though it has volume buttons on the remote, not just the play/pause button on this model. Also this \\"Android\\" version has a small red detail on the headphone; everything else is identical. I would have deleted this review and moved it over to the other model but honestly I can't figure out how to delete a review. That said, I still think the above review is valid for this model because now I have this one and I can say they are identical other than the remote and the red part.Even though this model works fine with iPhone and I'm sure the other model works fine with Android, I would now go with the other model since it has volume controls. Search for \\"Philips headset iPhone\\".

review_headline: Best speakers so far - let me compare quickly...

I love these speakers the most of all the systems I've ever had...

These - HTCT150 - best because of the 3 HDMI inputs and 1 HDMI output - makes working with a universal remote a dream come true...

HTCT260 - I also have these, bought because of the bluetooth... but forget having any good selection of HDMI inputs, and you really don't need bluetooth anymore, at all, if you buy the $35 google chromecast dongle, which works better than anything in the world... love it.

Yamaha DSP Soundbar - at $1500, it sounds almost no different than the HTCT150, and lacks any user-friendly inputs... it's a mess.

Creative ZiiSound D3X - my favorite, but more for a bedroom application - actually, for the bedroom it's the best system ever... and I loved it when I had it in the living room, it's just that the inputs are really limited to a headphone cable. It's much more expensive, but for sound quality it's my overall favorite... especially with the subwoofer and two speakers... all wireless too.

To my ears the Bose Soundlink Mini was the clear winner by far and I ended-up impressed enough to buy it even though I really wasn't looking for this style speaker. I thought it even sounded better than the (higher priced and larger) Bose Soundlink II. The mini has a very high quality appearance and robust feel, from its weight vs. size to the layout and feel of the controls. The sound is remarkable - lows, highs and mids. I suppose a drawback for some may be that it doesn't have a microphone for speaker calls but that's not important to me. I'm not sure how anyone could be disappointed with this speaker for what it's built to do. "Best of Class" might be the most accurate overview. I definitely recommend it and if you do get one, enjoy the surprise at how good it sounds for being so small!

I'm able to hear the difference with my 320KPS MP3s but your quality Flacs really are bright and will make you cry. product_title: Polk Audio OWM3 On-Wall Speaker (Black)
review_headline: Awesome Speakers For Desktop Computer Sound System
review_body:
I purchased the OWM3's during a sale through Polk Audio to use as main speakers for a desktop computer sound system. The speakers are being powered by a Lepai LP-2020A+ mini amp. The cost of the setup was $100; the same price as a Bose Companion 2 Series III system. The sound quality and power output from the Lepai/Polk OWM3 combo completely BLOWS the Bose Companion system away! The OWM3's have a deeper fuller sound, more clarity, and get much, much louder! I have a feeling the Lepai/Polk OWM3 combo would blow away any multimedia speaker setup anywhere near the $100 price point. The OWM3's are only marginally larger than the Bose Companion 2 speakers and the amp is only 4.7 x 5.8 x 1.7 inches so the overall footprint isn't that much bigger.

The OWM3's are wonderful, versatile speakers! They are only 4.1" thick so they can easily be placed on a desktop for a computer sound system as I have done. With the Lepai/Polk OWM3 combo you can have a great sounding setup to play MP3's that is small enough to place almost anywhere! The sound is even loud enough to fill a 2 car garage! The shallow depth of the OWM3's also make them ideal to use if mounting on a wall for surround speakers which is why most people have purchased them. Even though the OWM3's have a small footprint they produce a surprisingly full sound. This is due to the 4.5" woofer which can produce sounds down to 80Hz. By no means are they going to thump your chest. However, 80Hz is lower than other compact desktop speakers I've looked at in their price range. If you need deeper sound just add a subwoofer. My only regret now is not having ordered more OWM3's during the sale!

product_title: Bose SoundLink Bluetooth Mobile Speaker II
review_body: I own the Soundlink II and the Soundlink mini.  If you are wondering which one to buy, the answer is, it depends.  Both have amazing sound - yes, both sound better than the UE Boom, the Braven, the Soundmatters speakers and pretty much anything else on the portable bluetooth speaker market.  There is no hype or bells and whistles with these speakers - they just simply look great and have rich powerful sound.  The Soundlink II plays louder and bit clearer than the Soundlink mini.  But the mini holds its own with the Soundlink and amazes with its warmth and volume.  The Soundlink II is of course larger than the mini, but not by as much as you might think.  Hold them in your left and right hands, and you you will be struck that either could go in your carry on luggage or accompany you to the beach.  We have found that the Soundlink II is actually shaped better to slip in and out in a carry on bag.  Both are sturdy and impeccably built.  Both have good battery life.  Both connect easily to your phone or computer.  The Soundlink II costs $100 more than the mini.  But even there, the comparison is closer than you think.  If you buy the neoprene cover and travel case for the mini (both recommended), you are up to within $20-$30 of the Soundlink II cost.  In balance, I recommend the mini if you must have your speaker as small and light as possible.  For example, you are hiking with it or a frequent business traveller.  On the other hand, if you using the speaker at home - on your deck for example - or travel now and then, well the Soundlink II shines.  Either speaker can excel in all of these situations, but we find ourself using and travelling with the Soundlink II because it sounds just a bit better.  If these were cars, the Bose mini is the BMW 3 series and the Soundlink II is the BMW series 7.  Both are luxury rides and very capable.  They share many similarities.  But the additional money you spend on the Soundlink buys you just a it more of what makes these the best bluetooth speakers on the market.

product_title: Supersonic SC-2020 Portable CD Player with Cassette Recorder & AM/FM Radio
review_headline: Know what you are ordering - this is model SC-2020U
review_body:
Product review update January 2015: Quite recently I began to use the CD player a lot when I am practicing dance. The CD player has stopped working properly. After I select the track I want it sometimes starts in the middle of the track. The fix I discovered is to shut the unit off and turn it back on. I am still reasonably happy with this item because it is for personal use only and I will put up with some glitches. But I wouldn't try to use it to provide music for a dance class, for example, because the CD player seems to have become unreliable.

First let me say that at the time I ordered there were at least three different pages offering this product. All three pages had different details and different prices. I thought there were two different models: an SC-2020 and an SC-2020U. The reason I thought so is because there were reviews on two of the three pages AND one page titled the product as the SC-2020U and the other titled the product as the SC-2020. As far as I know there is only one model - the SC-2020U. Had I scrolled down and read two of the pages a little more thoroughly, or better yet, had I printed out the information and perused it carefully, I might have noticed that the item model number was the same on two of the pages. On the third page I've mentioned above there is very little info and the only place the model number shows is in the page title and, of course, the page titles the product as the SC-2020. I pretty much ignored the third page because of the lack of info. In any event, I figured this all out after I had ordered and received the product and it turns out I paid $10 more because I chose to order from the SC-2020 page instead of the SC-2020U page. Caveat emptor.

Due to the conflicting reviews on both pages, I deliberated with myself for quite a while before taking the plunge and ordering. I needed to replace an AudioPhase dual cassette/cd recorder & AM/FM Radio that I bought back in 2001. The Supersonic was the only product I found that came anywhere close. My AudioPhase had a 3 disc turntable while the Supersonic plays only one CD. Still, the Supersonic had the overall features I was wanting to replace - notably recording from CD to cassette, recording from radio to cassette, and recording from cassette to cassette.

I received the product very quickly and I have checked it out pretty thoroughly. It is meant to be portable and can be battery operated so expect it to be small and lightweight. I measured my unit and came up with 23\\" wide, 7\\" deep, and 9\\" tall with the speakers attached. The shipping weight on the label said 13 pounds. So far I have recorded from cassette to cassette and from CD to cassette. I have also used the radio and I have played CDs. The only thing I noticed is that when I play a cassette on Deck A the sound quality is not as good as on Deck B. But the recording ability worked fine in both cases and I have been very pleased with the radio reception and the overall sound quality. The unit comes with a remote that you must use in order to record from CD to cassette. The remote will not turn the unit off nor will it adjust the volume. I don't find this to be an issue because I use this unit primarily to provide music when I am working out. When reading the instructions I noticed mention of a \\"Bass Boost Switch\\" which I have not yet located.

Unless this product suddenly stops working properly as some reviewers have mentioned, I must say that I am very happy with it, I believe it is a decent product at a reasonable price, and I believe it merits a four star rating.

review_body:
PCT hasn't made new variable gain amps for several years now (at least 3), so people are selling from stock. This is not a problem. The product is rugged and should last decades while it sits on the shelf. When I get rich, I'm going to get another couple to sit on my parts shelf for friends or for my next house.

The beauty of this box is the variable gain.

At some point, especially with HDTV, more amplification makes reception worse. This is because the noise is also amplified, and the noise will reach a point where it overwhelms the good information in the signal. In short, a stronger signal isn't necessarily better.

But, you can add small amounts of amplification, stay below the point where you boost the noise too much, and get some improvement. In my configuration, I've adjusted the PCT to add about 3 or 3.5 dB. Things are noticeably better with this small amount of increase. Other amplifiers added large amounts of gain (10 dB, 13 dB), which was too much.

The adjustable PCT lets me pick amount I need. The adjustment screw turns around 5 or 6 times from minimum to full gain, so its easy to ramp up in small increments until you reach the best setting.

(If you care, the industry generally gets small amounts of amplification by using a big amp followed by an attenuator to reduce the strength of the amplified signal. I think that avoiding the over amplification by using a variable amp is a cleaner way to do things.)

product_title: GOgroove DynaMIX Noise Isolating Earbuds Earphones with Microphone and Control for Handsfree Calling & Music Playback - Includes Flat No-Tangle Cord & 3 Sizes of Noise Isolating Silicone Ear Gels
review_headline: One of the BEST earphones I've EVER owned!
review_body:
So, my beloved Beats earphones that came along with my HTC Rezound finally died out on me recently (specifically, the left earbud started crackling and, then, stopped working entirely). I was upset at this since I loved those earphones so much. Fortunately, I owned another pair of $100 Klipsch earphones that I saved as a back-up pair, and was looking forward to enjoying those since they were my second favorite. Unfortunately, I couldn't - and still can't - find them anywhere. Enter my search for new earphones...

I had recently bought a friend a pair of Beats Tour in-ear phones as a gift, and couldn't see myself spending yet another $100 on another pair of earphones for myself. (I've already owned a pair of Bose in-ear phones, in addition to countless other ones by Sony, JVC, Blackberry, Apple, etc.). I did my research on CNet and other review sites for the best earphones and was undecided UNTIL I ran across a COMMENT from a POSTER on one of these reviews who absolutely loved and gushed about these GOgroove DynaMIX earphones. The poster even provided the link to buy these earphones here on Amazon. So, I took a look, read even more positive reviews on them and, when I saw that they were only $16.99, I thought: \\"Hey, what's there to lose? If I buy them and don't like them, they were only $17.\\" So, I got 'em and was excited to test them out when they arrived, and wasn't expecting much...

BOY, WAS I WRONG! As SOON as I popped them in my ear, I realized just how comfortable they are. And, as SOON as the music started playing, I was IMMEDIATELY BLOWN AWAY by their sound. These GOgroove DynaMIX earphones are better than ANY other in-ear phones I've owned and are JUST AS GOOD as my old Beats earphones, if not better! I ran an extensive test comparing these to the Beats ones that I bought my friend. Honestly, for SOME songs the Beats sounded better and for other songs the GOgrooves sounded better. At best, they sound BETTER than the beats.And, at worst, they sound almost as good as the Beats. But, factoring in their ridiculously low price completely changes the game and helped me declare the GOgroove earphones as the undisputed winner! For 17 bucks, how could you go wrong?!?

TRUST ME, GET-THESE-EARPHONES! They're amazing, ESPECIALLY considering their price. They are straight-up BETTER than my old Bose earphones; they're slightly better than my Klipsch in-ear phones (their style of sound is so different, so it's hard to compare); and they're just as good as - or even better than - my old Beats earphones (depending on song). BUT, difference is, they're not 100 bucks, or more, like the other ones! They're 17 bucks! I can't get over it! But, these GOgroove DynaMIX in-ear phones sure sound like they should cost a helluva lot more!

To be a little technical: They are bass-y - which I like and got accustomed to because of my Beats - but the bass is punchy without feeling muddled, and adds depth to everything you play. Their highs are crisp WITHOUT any shrillness or annoying - even painful - hissing, even at high volumes (like others). In fact, they sound even better at high volumes! And, very surprisingly, their mids are warm and clear and don't get lost in the abundant bass. Also, the microphone works very well - callers sound clear, and they report that I sound very clear to them. The cord doesn't get tangled, the ear buds are very comfortable and, most importantly, they don't slip out.

Now, are they the BEST-sounding in-ear phones I've ever HEARD? No...but they're damned close. The honor for best in-ear phones I've ever heard goes to the Monster Turbine Pros (Copper). (I ain't spending $150 to get them, though!) BUT, these GOgroove DynaMIX earphones are, however, the best in-ear phones I've ever OWNED - especially considering the price! I couldn't be happier with this purchase. I've already recommended them to friends and even got my picky-as-hell audiophile friend and his wife to buy two pairs - one for each of them. And, soon, I will be buying more pairs for me and my wife, since I feel that they're going to \\"catch-on,\\" and their price will increase. ;)

product_title: Coby Micro MP3 Player with LCD Flash Memory MP301 (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great except for the clicking noise...
review_body:
***UPDATE: I just learned that Coby has recently gone out of business. So this is more of a gamble than before. I don't know if the company that bought them will continue to sell under the Coby name or if you will be able to get the great customer service I speak of in my following review, which is unedited from my previous post***

So I own another Coby MP3 player, the MPC885, which is perfect except it only has 1GB of memory, and as far as I know there is no higher memory version of it. So I got this one: same brand, different model, more memory. And it was AWESOME, for the first month or so, then it stopped connecting to the PC. So I could no longer add music to it. Called Coby's customer service--which I highly recommend; they are friendly and helpful--and they could not figure it out. Sent it in to them and they finally just replaced it with a new one. Okay. Problem is the new one had the click others have complained about. What it is, is a clicking sound you hear in the headphones, which is independent of the volume of the player. If you have the volume all the way down you will still hear it, and as you turn it up you can actually drown it out. But I don't like to play music that loud in my headphones. So I constantly hear this clicking sound during the music (it clicks about once a second or so). So I called support again, and they had me send it back. They replaced it, and the next one also had the click. Well, it has now been a couple years since I bought it (meant to do this review back then but am not really online all that much), so I forget exactly how many of these I went through, but I think I was on my 5th one before I finally gave up. The shipping & handling was starting to add up, negating the whole purpose of buying a low-priced player to begin with. So now what I do is use this one in the car, since I turn the volume all the way up for the car stereo adapter (all the way up on the player, not the car stereo!), and theclicking sound is completely inaudible in the car. And I use my 1GB Coby for personal listening. Not what I was aiming for, but it works.

(Oh, and yes I tested different headphones in the player, and the same headphones on different players, etc. So it is definitely in the player and not the headphones.)

So there you have it: quite honestly if you get one with no defects this is a 5-star product--low priced, plenty of memory, easy to use. It's just there seem to be a high number of defective ones, so be aware you will be taking a bit of a gamble. But again, their customer service is very helpful, so you've got help there if you have any trouble. Honestly, nowadays there aren't that many good choices for low priced players that run on AAA batteries (one AAA battery, great battery life, and I use rechargeables), so if that's what you're looking for I highly recommend this at this time. Just wanted to share my own experience so you know what you may run in to.

review_headline: Great product, quick shipping.  Works great.
review_body:
I bought the three-way to hide our cable box, DVD and Audio. First off, the product arrived quickly and everything was in the package. They also included well written documentation. Extra adhesive pads were included as well.

Here are a few suggestions that I tried after reading other reviews. Once you have found the original position of the IR receiver on the front panel of the media device, clean it with a bit of glass cleaner or rubbing alcohol. Not a lot, just enough to clean the area where you will be placing the transmitter. Use a couple of pieces of transparent tape to secure the wire on the front and top of the device. (hint: fold over a tab so it is easier to get off later).

Transmitter placement is a tough one. If your not sure where the original IR receiver is on your media device, find a friend and do a bit of trial an error before removing the adhesive backing. You can slide the transmitter over the face of your media device until it works. Keep trying, when it starts working, take flashlight and shine it through the panel. You should see a small square with a dot in the middle, mine were about 2mm square. Don't forget to clean the panel before removing the adhesive backing.

product_title: OREI 2 in 1 USA to India Adapter Plug
review_body:
I picked these up for a trip to Scotland and Wales from the US. These adapters were exactly what we needed. They allowed us to run all of our electronics while overseas. They fit firmly into UK outlets. Though they become chunky and rather heavy with something plugged into them, they stayed tight and secure.

Plugging a US cord into one of these adapters for the first time is a bit tight and stiff, but they loosen up with just a few uses. As other reviewers have stated, these adapters don't change voltage, they simply change over the shape of the plug. The typical voltage used in the US is 120 volts. In the UK it is 230 volts. Most pieces of electronics can run on a range of something like 110-240 volts. So you would be able to use those devices in virtually any country. However, there are some products that run on no more than 120 volts. So without some type of converter, you will be unable to use them in the UK. Check all of the items you wish to use overseas before you leave. (Nintendo's products are rather well known for having this problem).

It's just that I'm not sure it was worth the few extra bucks for use in my camper. Read some of the other reviews up here. Plugging the amplifier directly into the TV's USB slot also allows me to save precious DC power when not using hook-ups. The amp only turns on when the TV turns on, perfect!

product_title: CyberPower PFC Compatible Pure Sine Wave Tower UPS
review_headline: Does everything I need and more
review_body:
I've been using the 1000VA 600W UPS with my main desktop computer for about 5 months now, and already it came useful during a power outage. The lights and all the appliances went out, but the computer and monitor kept on running as if nothing happened. Now that doesn't mean I'll be playing the latest Call of Duty while the power is out, but it provides ample time to wrap up my work, do some last minute tasks, and safely shut down the machine.

There are many things to like about this unit. Firstly, the software is easy to set up and use, and is deliciously free of bloatware and useless junk. The unit itself has tasteful, low-key styling, makes no audible noise, and is compact enough to sit under my desk and let me forget it's there. The LCD has several useful readouts such as power consumption, battery charge level, and estimated minutes of battery power remaining. product_title: Onkyo TX-NR616 7.2- Channel Network A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I bought a new receiver grudgingly to replace my 20-year-old Sony, which I loved, but it was time to switch everything over to HDMI around here. I figured that I'd get some cool features, like direct streaming of Pandora, but otherwise, it would be just a new black box that linked A/V devices to the speakers. I was wrong. The surround sound on this Onkyo has noticeably and remarkably better imaging and clarity than the Sony it replaced. The surround modes serve my needs better, especially the All Channel Stereo mode for background music, which is an obvious feature the Sony didn't have at all.

It was a real pain having to upgrade the firmware immediately out of the box. It's a scary kind of thing to do, where you cross your fingers and hope it doesn't just go permanently dead. But it worked out okay. The automatic calibration with the little microphone more than made up for it. I think that's why this unit sounds so much better than the Sony.

Also, I don't know who decided not to put phono inputs on receivers, but I found a little box for $14.95 to solve the problem (but now there's yet another #$@*$ power cube behind there). The menus are a little clunky and weird to navigate. The Sony had better feedback on the front panel -- why don't receivers have full-color high resolution front panels? My $18.95 pocket MP3 player has that. There are a bunch of tiny buttons on the front panel, but you need a magnifying glass and a flashlight to read the markings. Most of them aren't necessary, and are functions the remote does better. The OSD display of volume, source, etc. is cool. I'm glad somebody realized that connecting your PC to your audio system is a normal expectable thing to do -- in the past I had to pretend my computer was a DVD player.

The one feature I miss from the old Sony is the ability to cross-assign the audio and video inputs. For instance, I had two sources assigned to my cable box, one that said Watch TV and the other thatsaid Soundscapes, and the two had different surround modes and other settings. I also had the TV video on screen whenever you were listening to a source that didn't have video. Can't do that now.

I didn't have any of the troubles other people have mentioned in the reviews here, but it has only been a few days.

All in all, a lot of solid functionality for the price. Recommended!

product_title: Snap-N-Store Stylish Storage File Box (SNS01913)
review_headline: Great box but Amazon rations how many you can get!
review_body:
I have a large CD collection that is overflowing my CD bookshelves. Since I have imported all my discs into iTunes I decided that most of them do not need to be out. I found this storage box while doing a search and it looked perfect and had a great price. I debated between the single-row and double-row box and decided on the single-row since it seemed to me a little more stable with less flex which would help the snaps stay in place, a common problem on the double-wide boxes according to the reviews. At $4.88 a piece, for the single box option ($12.99 for the two box option) I thought I would take a chance and buy 5 boxes, the maximum allowed for the order I thought. They arrived and were very easy to put together, the lid is pre-assembled, and I was impressed with the quality. The snaps were tight, and the boxes hold together well when fully loaded. Many of my CD's are Japanese with obi strips, which I like to keep with the CD, so I have those in poly bags for extra protection. The CD's fit in the box nicely, even in the poly bags, and the lid just rests on the top of the CD's, which is fine as it is good for stacking.

I was so impressed I wanted to buy another 5. I put together another order with those as my \\"add-ons\\", but at checkout I was informed that Amazon will not sell me any more. I guess there is no limit on the 2-packs for $12.99. I went over to Staples which sells them for $5.99, with free shipping and you can buy as many as you want, I bought 10. It may not be much of a savings over the 2-pack, but I think that is a better way to do business. For as much as I buy from Amazon, this was not a positive experience.

Update: I ordered 10 more from Staples, for roughly the same price as 5 two-packs. The quality was fairly consistent, except for one which didn't have tight snaps on one side. It would unsnap on its own after a while, so I followed the recommendation of another reviewer and used Gorilla Glue on the snaps. That worked fine.

Another reviewer mentioned receiving a box that was missing a side. I noticed on many of mine the sides were stuck to the bottom panel and I had to use a little effort to peal them off. They are a fine product, but just be aware of a few minor issues.

product_title: Runtastic Bike Case for iPhone 4, 4S, 5 (White)
review_headline: Nice idea for iPhone bike mounting but several annoying flaws
review_body:
I got the runtastic Bike Case for iPhone hoping to incorporate my
iPhone 5 as part of my bicycle training. It's a plastic case that has a
clamshell design and will hold iPhone models 4, 4S, and 5. The case
comes with a piece of mounting hardware which is designed to be mounted
on either the bike handlebar or stem. I chose the stem mounting for my
road bike, using the enclosed zip ties and rubber protective backing.

I also downloaded the runtastic Road Bike app from the App Store and
registered on the runtastic web site using the enclosed activation code
that converted the free Road Bike app to the PRO version. The sign-up
and activation process went smoothly. Please note I am rating only the
Bike Case and not the runtastic Road Bike app for the rest of this review.

Unfortunately, three flaws came out when I actually used the Case when
riding. First, despite tightening down the zip ties as snugly as
possible, either the mount or the connection between the mount and the
Case rattled when riding on bumpy asphalt roads. Second, I had to use
the Case in landscape position (the mount allows both portrait and
landscape positions) but the Road Bike app doesn't appear to support
landscape orientation. This meant I had to view all the stats sideways
while riding. Third, the size of the Case was just too big for my taste:
it wasn't too much bigger than the iPhone but the overall size is
distracting to my eye. Unfortunately, due to the way the drop handle
bars on my road bike are wrapped, it was inconvenient to use the Case in
portrait mode on the handle bars. Perhaps if I was able to use the Case
in that manner, the last two flaws might not bother me as much.

If you are able to mount the Case differently than I did and you ride on
rather smooth roads, this product might work well for you.

review_headline: Not the best headphone, but has many perks

Like a lot of people, I first saw these headphones at Best Buy, and after trying it out and comparing it to other headphones, this one was clearly the best out of all of them imo. After buying a used one that was in perfect condition, I trying it on for a few days, this is what i noticed.

Positives:
-Has great bass and mids
-most COMFORTABLE set of cans I have tried on, earpads are extremely well made and soft
-absolutely great and comfortable for anyone who wears glasses
-flat chord means less tangling, and there is a three button control for those who use Apple products
-doesnt clamp too hard or too lightly (of course, depends on your headsize, but I would say i have a mid sized head)
-looks stylish/ not too plasticky

Negatives:
-If you are an audiophile, you might consider it muddy due to some weakness in the highs
-if you have a large head, it might clamp down too tightly
-could feel a bit uncomfortable and ears might sweat after 30 minutes or so, but this would definitely be more apparent for those with larger heads
-case is small, but it is very inconvenient to put the headphone in (gotta shorten headband all the way and face earcups downwards)
-swivels are a bit loose, so if you are usually rough about your headphones, that may not be a good idea.

Overall, if you are fan of superior comfort, this headphone is definitely one of those you should check out. On the other hand, if you could care less about comfort and just want the best sound possible, you may want to consider something else.
You should definitely try these out at a store first, but realize that the sound is probably not as good as what you heard in the store, but still quite pleasant. Buying a used one is a great option, as they can be in pristine condition and less than 50 dollars, which will make these headphones all the more appealing.

review_headline: Solves problems and provides good sound

The Yamaha's speakers are front facing - problem gone. It got better. Pushing a button resulted in the voices of the characters or newscasters becoming more distinct. It got even better. My wife watches a program Sunday sponsored by the loudest commercial in our viewing experience. Push another button and the sound is normalized - the commercial volume is reduced to blend in with the volume of the program.

Advice: read the suggestions of the other reviewers. My summary comments (again read the other reviews):
1. Once you hook up the sound bar, you'll need to turn off the TV speakers through a systems setting on the TV.
2. I found the instructions on how to set up the sound bar to respond to the TV remove hard to understand. Standing inches from the bar and reading the instructions aloud, I was able to configure the sound. If I had it to do over, I would have forgone the struggle and just justed the simple sound remote. My recommendation - plug the sound bar into the TV, turn the TV volume off, plug the sound bar into the TV and try just using the remote. Your total box to TV time will be single minutes. Once you've played with the sound bar, then configure it.

Finally, if you've followed my suggestion of skipping the synchronization of TV remote and sound bar control, then sign up for Pandora and select a station. The sound you'll hear will justify your purchase to your wife, neighbors, and yourself.

Overall, these are great headphones but they do have shortcomings. When I first received these I plugged them up to my iPad and my current ones (Skull candy noise canceling which were about $40) to my iPhone and played the exact song together one in each ear and then switched them and played again to review the sound quality. At first I didn't notice anything so I played a classical song since its a better genre to judge sound quality in my opinion. Bose beats them out as far as sound quality is concerned. You could hear the horns, percussion, and the subtle cymbal hits that bring out the feel of the music which I couldn't hear on the skull candies. Another good thing was after about 2 minutes I didn't even feel that they were in my ear, they were that comfortable. I was skeptical that they weren't going to stay in my ear during exercise, so I ran a mile just to be sure on rocky terrain and they never moved, so these are great for exercise as well.

There is a negative though and that is there is no noise cancellation. However, These CLEARLY state these on the packaging and the description so that is not why I gave it 4 stars but I believe that for the ordinary user this could be a deal breaker. I have a fan on high in my room and I had to turn up the earphones quite a bit to not be able to hear it anymore so if you are on a plane or a busy subway station you may not be able to cancel out all of that noise and that's it gets 4 out of 5 stars. With the Skull Candies and others alike, they are cheaper and have decent sound quality and also include noise cancellation. I will say this though, if you are going on a long trip go with these Bose because you won't be able to feel them, others I've tried are very uncomfortable after awhile.

All in all I would definitely recommend these earphones, by far have the best sound quality of all the ones that I have tested and by far the most comfortable.

I downloaded the app and found it to be just OK. I don't know that I'll use it and actually favor the software for my Phillips Dock over this, although that one is far from perfect as well. Otherwise the unit top controls worked fine to control the docked iPod. The build materials seem pretty solid. A couple of disappointments, there is no remote and the connector is too short to work with most cases. Neither my sons iPod, nor my iPhone will connect to the dock without removing our cases first which is a little annoying. I have not had this issue with my older docks with the wider connection, although I guess I've never had such thick cases as we have now.

Pros
+ Good Sound
+ Completely Plug and Play (although you can add an app if you want)

Cons
- Connector not long enough to work with iPod or iPhone Cases on.
- App for the dock is just OK, there is room for improvement.

All in all, it is a decent dock for the price. My son is very happy with it, other than the fact the connector does not work with our cases.

review_headline: Lightweight, and comfortable with my glasses.  Worth the price, which is still cheap compared to many.
review_body:
These have been great. It took me forever to find some headphones that fit my nitpicky criteria, in order of importance.
1) Will not crush my glasses between my ears and skull.
2) Comfortable for wearing a long time while to my head and ears, hopefully some padding around the top.
3) Lightweight.

Any one of those was easy, all three were surprisingly difficult to find. After a long time searching, these came up. some further research showed them to be good, and while the first day or so out of the package they clamped a bit, now they fit perfectly. I can wear them for ages with no discomfort, but they do not fall off or jostle around from leaning down to grab stuff from a desk drawer, eat food, or (gently) headbang.

Now if only I could find a USB headset that fit my three requirements. The closest thing I have so far leaves a dent in the top of my head from the lack of top padding/edges in the plastic, if still gentle on my ears and not too heavy. I'd throw money at Sennheiser if they made a headset that was basically \\"This one, with A USB connection and Mike\\", but not seeing one for all three hopeful requirements yet.

It was a pleasant bonus that these are in a good price range as well. A bit less than $100 full price unlike so many 200-300 monstrosities, and I got it here for a wonderful $52 and change. I'm no audiophile so any deep sound purity issues compared to other options just fly right over my head, but for my own single player gaming, music, and videos it sounds just fine along with feeling fine.

Also, there is often a severe problem with the adapter blocking access to other sockets on the PC which are too close to the HDMI. This product solves both problems very effectively.

In case you can't tell from the description and picture, the small connector fits right into the HDMI socket on the PC, and the DVI-to-DVI cable from the monitor fits right into the large connector on this gadget. product_title: Microlab MD312 Bluetooth Wireless Portable Speaker
review_headline: This speaker is one of the best Bluetooth speakers I have tested and ever heard!
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3GGKS3OYS5YQ2]]This is a beautifully designed and powerful Bluetooth speaker that has a rechargeable Lithium-Ion battery inside of it to make it portable. The first thing you want to do is install the battery and charge it for 4 hours. The manual states that you should have the speaker off when charging it. It also advises you to only charge the speaker with the supplied charger and do not use your computer or any other USB style of power source. The charging plug is a Mini USB so make sure to use only the supplied power supply. When charging the battery the LED on the front of the speaker is bright red and when charging is complete the LED is still red but very dim. There is an ON/OFF switch on the back of the speaker.

I have included a video to show how to install the battery and pair the speaker with your smart device. Pairing the Bluetooth was fast and easy with my iPhone and my iPad. I always suggest that when you are pairing a Bluetooth device to your smart device that you have them within 3 feet of each other. There is a carrying handle built into the speaker's back.

The speaker's sound output is marvelous. Its bass is booming and the treble is clear. The speaker has a 5 watt Woofer and a 2 watt Tweeter powered by an internal amplifier. product_title: Duronic HDS3 Mini 3 Port Gold HDMI Auto Switch PIANO BLACK 3x1 (3 way input 1 output HDMI Switcher)
review_body:
The price is high for what it is. Cheap plastic. I am okay with it as long as the price was right.

Here is the low down, it did not work for me because the darn thing only checks devices with power.

I connected by cable box, Xbox 360 and media streamer.

Problem is, this thing does not work for devices in standby mode. It only checks if there is ANY electric current in the HDMI wire. Most of the new devices with remote are in standby mode when you power them off. This makes the auto switching on this thing useless. It does not check for level of electric current. It is in binary mode, either on or off.

So the cable box would always be on for this device. Unless I manually get up and click the utton on this thing or unhook the HDMI wire (hotswapping is NOT recommended for HDMI).

It worked when I tried the XboX as xbox seems to be fully off with no electric current to HDMI output. But then, I have to get up, push a button to turn it off.

Same case with PS3 as xbox, it works. What did not work with PS3 was Simplink using LG TV (Where you use commands to TV through TV's remote and they are routed to PS3 as PS3 commands).

It did not work with my netgear media streaming device either. Same case, most devices with remote will keep some power running to anticipate signals from the remote making this device useless.

The display from the device works with 1080p and 3D.

The auto-switching,(when working), takes a good 5 seconds to recognize where to go next. The wait is to the point where you wonder if it is working right now or not!

I am going to use it as an extender to my 4 HDMI input TV where I will only use it when I have to connect my laptop, cell phone etc to TV and I HAVE to plug in cables for those anyway. If you want auto-switching, forget it.

product_title: LOFTEK® HDfuryproTwo Input HDMI to RGB Component YPbPr / VGA 2x1 Switch Converter Support 5.1CH Surround Sound.
review_body:
I was hesitant about ordering this product due to the mixed reviews, but fortunately it worked for me in the end. Here's my siutation:

I have a whole house audio / video system in my home. The video is run using component video cables which are in wall and not easily replaceable. I have a TV which has HDMI and component inputs in my office, but I need to use component video to hook this up to my whole house audio/video system. I first tried using the HDFuryPro directly plugged into my LG BD550 blu-ray player. I remotely turned on the blu-ray player and saw the boot sequence on the tv, so far so good. But then all of a sudden the picture would disappear before it got to the home page. I was worried that maybe the HDCP wasn't working properly but decided to spend some time troubleshooting. After going through the menus on my dvd player (directly hooked up via HDMI) i changed the video output setting from auto to 1080i. Then I tried hooking up the HDFuryPro again using component video. This time when I started my Blu-Ray player it made it past the boot sequence to the home page. Playing a Blu-Ray worked fine. Netflix worked fine too. I left it on for an hour and had no issues. I then tried hooking up the HDFuryPro to the output of my receiver, Denon AVR-2313. All of the video sources worked without any issues.

The reason I am giving this product a 4 instead of 5 is because of the video quality. I hooked up my Scientific Atlanta DVR to my TV using component video only and it looks good. However, when I run HDMI to HDFuryPro to the same TV I notice that the picture is much softer. Looks washed out a little. By playing with my TV picture settings I am able to get it to look better but that may not be true for everyone.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_headline: Spend the extra money and get the Ultimate!!
review_body:
Despite the fact that I always have my iPhone in my pocket or right at my side, using it as a TV remote is unfortunately not as great as I had hoped. As other reviewers have discussed in great detail, the iPhone app is designed great and works great, as does the included hardware which communicates between the iPhone and the TV. The problem is sometimes old fashioned is just plain easier and better. If you want to turn up the volume one click, it is much easier to pick up the remote and make one click rather than reaching in your pocket, digging out the iPhone, unlocking it, opening the Logitech app, waiting for connection, and then making the click. Logitech does include a basic remote here, so my point is kind of void, but overall I do stand by my thought that using the iPhone as a remote is not as useful as expected. My TiVO has an iPhone app with similar functionality, and I've never used it more than twice, so I guess this should have been expected.

Where this does excel is when there is typing needed... Typing on a remote is dreadful, so being able to use your iPhone keyboard rocks. Overall though, I would say spend the extra money and get the Logitech Ultimate version, which includes a full fledged remote. You'll be happier with the convenience of a physical remote despite the extra cost. Note that the ultimate also includes the ability to use your iPhone, so if the remote is on the other side of the room you can always pull out the lazy card and whip out the phone if really needed :)

Feel free to comment if you have any specific questions about this remote (or the Ultimate, since I have both), and I'll get back to you as quickly as possible!

product_title: Gefen Digital Audio Decoder (GTV-DD-2-AA)
review_headline: So Far So Good - For Analog Audio Stereo Headphones
review_body:
This digital audio decoder is working so far.
It runs a little warm as other people indicate.

I have this presently hooked directly to the digital optical output of my Panasonic L55DT50 HDTV.

It is powered by a power adapter and not a USB cable so it does not switch on and off with my TV as I had hoped.

When receiving PCM signals and switching channels, the analog audio signal is generated quite quickly for the headset.
When changing channels to a Dolby Digital encoded signal, the decoder takes a moment to recognize and decode the signal as one might expect. Accordingly, there is a slight delay before the audio signal is generated for my headphones.
For those complaining about the delay, this is probably normal for most AV receivers as well when decoding digital dolby signals.

I have to add a splitter in front of this decoder in the future which will cut the optical power in half. I will try and update to let you know how that goes. Splitting the optical signal will allow me to split up the optical signal between my old AV receiver and this decoder/headphones. I also have high and low quality optical TOSLINK cables. I am curious if the quality of the TOSLINK cable effects how this decoder operates.

There are a few headphone systems that directly receive a digital optical input and have this decoder built in.
However, they are very expensive. This decoder will allow me to use my older analog headphone systems for a longer period of time.

I must say, this decoder does seem to be rather expensive given whats there. The reason for four stars. There is probably one chip. They could make this less expensive if they eliminated the digital COAX input and made an optical only decoder. If they accepted power from a USB port, they could eliminate the adapter as well. I have seen other makes that receive power over a USB port but can't say how well they work.

Update:
I finally received the Optical Splitter that I had on order. I was able to split 50% of the optical power up to send to an AV receiver and to this Gefen Decoder.
The Gefen Decoder continued to work after doing so.
In comparison with a Sony AV Receiver, the Gefen decoder took a little longer to decode the Dolby Digital signals after a channel change.
I don't know the long term effects of providing half the optical power to the decoder.

I would add a photo showing this, but Amazon seems to have disabled that option.

product_title: Subjekt T.N.T. Headphones with Mic Rogue Status
review_headline: Big things come in small packages
review_body:
The Subjekt T.N.T is one of those fashionable headphones that attract people with its design more than heritage. However, those who are interested will be happy to find out that these cans actually sound good.
I was dubious about the sound quality even though many youtube reviews have confirmed that they are good mid-range headphones. The sound is quite exceptional, even comparable to my V-Moda LP2's.
That beings said, the seal is not quite good enough, and the build quality is very questionable; I doubt these will last me years with regular use.
The light weight makes them very comfortable, although the material on the earpads could be much better. Also, the cable is non-removable. If you dislike that feature, you should go buy other cans.

Pros:
Sound (Good bass but doesn't bleed into the mids or the highs)
Comfort
Design (personal taste)

Cons:
Build Quality
Bad seal (also leaks quite a bit if they're not placed right)
non-removable cable

Conclusion:
These headphones deliver more than I had hoped for, and for 20~30 dollars on amazon, they are far superior to the competition in this price range. If you're interested in a very portable headphone, these or the Urbanears (they fold up for better portability), these are a good buy.
If you need something with good build quality and sound seal, you should invest more and move up to the 100 dollar price range.

A little Info on how I made the choice.
(Note: I have put a Quick specs list at bottom)

I have had many cd players starting back in the late 80's to newer with the last ones having digital outputs

I had a old SONY 300cd changer that found it liked to hang and destroy my cd's. Good thing I killed its power, only 5 needed to be replaced.

SO, How do I play all my cd's? I looked into media players. I dont want a computer running my home audio system. I don't want to have to update firmware.

I make my own VERY high res MP3's from cds (not looking to save space that much) for my Sandisk SansaClip8GB with 32GB card.

For the test it is connected to a HI-FI audio system with old (made in the 60's with a perfect flat sound curve and can be set to match the room they are in, The good days of audio) 5way speakers.

The Mp3's sounded MUCH BETTER than the cd's played on the older players I have. When I played a CD in the unit, It was the best I have ever heard. The left and right seperation, and how clear everything was amazing. You may have to change your settings on your AMP/(home audio unit) if you have a older or less expensive player now.

I have used many types of HiFi devices, 8-track, Adjustable weight phonographs (record players), Reel to Reel, you name it.
so I know each device has its own color it adds to the sound and take that into my judgment.

To get the best out of this unit, use a good AMP/AudioSystem so the range of the unit is not lost or compressed witch makes any device loose the clear highs and powerfull lows.

Another tip. When you make your mp3's or what ever format you want to use with this or any digital system, Lay out the songs in a logical way. Don't lump them all in one folder or skip on typing in info the fields in the software you use. You will find it helps if for example in the most simple way,,,,, Name the file the name of the song. Put the song into a folder named after the album it was made from. If your software allows, fill in the artist and other things.

I don't have a I-pod so that I can't say much on that, What it works with in the manual and in the PDF manual you can find on-line.

Well, I like it, Others have thought the Mp3 I was playing was a CD. I am very happy with it and for what I needed it was perfect.
If I were to do it over, I would buy it again.
I will have to keep a eye out for more from Marantz. Seems to be well built and worked right out of the box.

For more info, Look for the manual online from Marantz or where you like. Compaire the features with other units. Judge if its right for you. Hope this helps.

product_title: Logitech Ultimate Ears 600 Noise-Isolating - Dark Silver
review_body:
I purchased these from Amazon due to the high-quality brand and the 26dB noise isolation promise which is comparable to the best active noise-cancelling sets out there and I couldn't justify the cost of a Shure pair.

On the noise isolation front, they do an solid job all around when using the comply foam tips at the expense of some ease of use and comfort. It takes a few seconds to insert them and get a good seal, removing them can also be a bit uncomfortable and I've generally found a tip shape to be less comfortable than the Klipsh S4s.

I've flown hundreds of hours with these and the comply foam tips provide similar isolation to ear plugs on a plane, although they are not as durable as the silicone tips. The audio quality is clean and well-balanced, notably better than cheaper in-ears although I do find the bass lacking and I often struggled to maintain a good seal (especially with the silicone tips) which quickly degrades the audio experience.

Finally, the UE 600 wiring turned out to be very fragile, especially at the flex/jack connector points. I had exposed wire and sound problems after about 10 months of use, completely lost sound in R-channel after 12 months. Granted, I did not store those in the plastic box, but they were used very lightly and I was expecting to get a bit more life out of them.

Verdict: one star off for comfort, two stars off for durability = 2/5 stars. Works as advertised otherwise. review_body:
Warning, this is a 110 V AC powered clock (Not a battery powered one - although it has a small back up battery). Before you buy this make sure you have the same AC characteristic as the power sources in the U.S. If not you should buy most probably a step down transformer.

This is a good clock and provide a beam of red digital readouts on your wall or ceiling. It has two alarms and you could set one for the weekend and another for the workweek.

Overall the clock part is good and does its job well. I love that I do not need to wake and take the clock

I believe the radio part have some room for improvement

1. Needs auto channel detect and preset. This is old technology and should be standard. I would rather have buttons to select my favorite station.
2. Audio may need quality upgrade and be made into stereo.
3. Should be battery powered. There are a lot of advances in battery technology lately.

I understand that this may be asking too much for a clock but unfortunately, there are a lot of products out there that have these features and more. While good, this product may soon lose to its rivals.

Overall, I think this would be what I would expect as a great clock for hotels.

review_body:
I live in Eau Claire, WI, where CBS (8) is extremely difficult to receive since it transmits from 50+ miles away to the south. To make matters worse, the southern line of sight from our house consists of a low hill and thick trees. With our old rooftop antenna, CBS would not come in at all, so I bought this antenna hoping (but doubting) that we would receive an okay signal.

After receiving this antenna and slapping it together (be prepared...this beast is bigger than you might expect), I put it up on our roof, assuming CBS would likely still not come in. Thankfully, I was wrong. With a little shift in direction after my first installation, we now receive CBS very well. It breaks up a bit once in a while, but at 50+ miles, that's to be expected. Still, we have had storms since I installed the antenna, and CBS does come in throughout the wind and rain.

Overall, I've been pleasantly surprised by the effectiveness of this antenna and would recommend it to anyone. If it can pull in a good signal from 50+ miles away over hills and through trees, it's a darn good antenna in my book!
