product_title: Noontec ZORO HD Stereo Headphones with Inline Mic and Answer/End Button
review_headline: These headphones sound so clear and balanced
review_body:
These headphones look like Beats Solo HDs, but sound much much better in my opinion. Beats Solo HD headphones sound boomy and muddy to my ears, but the Zoro HD's sound like high fidelity phones. I took these headphones to a Fourth of July parade, I had my relatives try them out, and two of them said \\"Oh my goodness, these sound so clear!\\"

That's the way I would characterize the sound of these headphones, crystal clear, clean, and balanced. The treble is pristine without being sharp or piercing, the mids are forward but not intrusive, and the bass is potent and clear and extends down deep.

When I say that the Zoro HDs sound balanced, I mean that no part of the sound spectrum dominates the other. Bass, mids, and highs can all be heard equally. The headphones are portable and can be folded up and placed in the accompanying pouch.

The negatives: The build quality is not quite as premium as with the Beats by Dre line, and when you crank the volume on your MP3 player all the way loud (which you will not need to do with these headphones because they are efficient), it sounds a tad scratchy. If you wear glasses, you might not like the pressure that the ear cup places on your right ear. Also, if you like DJ music where the bass rattles the fillings in your mouth and You hear and feel the beat, but it overwhelms the other instruments and the song, you won't be satisfied with the Zoros.

But if you like hearing beautiful pristine music that sounds exactly the way the artist intended, you will be very happy with the Zoros.

The sound is a detailed stereo sound, meaning that you will hear bass in one ear, vocals over your head, piano or guitar in another ear, etc. It sounds like you are in a auditorium, and you can almost pinpoint where on the stage the different instruments are being played.

These are sealed headphones, they will not leak sound if you have them properly placed directly on your ears (I suppose if you have the volume turned all the way up, which is not advised, they might leak a little...)

At the $100 price point, these headphones are hard to beat. They have a clearer sound than the similarly priced Sennheiser HD 438, They do not sound congested and insular like the ATH M50s, And they do not sound harsh like the Grado SR 60 or the Grado SR 125.

But in my view, they are one step below $350 sealed headphones like the Sennheiser Momentum, which are even clearer with a more luxurious build quality.

But these headphones get a lot of time on my ears, because they are portable, affordable, easy to tote around, and they look awesome :)

By the way, do not confuse these with the Zoro professional headphones, which are priced $40 cheaper. They are good, but they leak sound, and these are a big step up.

Highly recommended, and they do not need a headphone amplifier, though they benefit slightly from a portable amp like the Fiio E11.u have the volume turned all the way up, which is not advised, they might leak a little...)

review_headline: This speaker did fairly well in my stress test. Comparison with XBOOM Mini speaker

[[VIDEOID:mo1CAU1W6VW0T47]]XBOOM CERAMIC Mini speaker is 3.5\\" tall when extended, and can be collapsed into a 2\\" ball when not in use. It weighs in at 3.5 oz. Its small size makes a perfect companion.

I am attaching a video which has several short snippets of music to demonstrate the speaker's sound. As one of the top reviewers I get asked to test and review a fairly large number of speakers. This allows me to compare a large number of speakers to each other. To help me make this comparison I always use the same two pieces of music, so I can compare speakers using \\"apples-to-apples\\" comparison. As a stress test for the bass I use Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor. The second piece of music (Tchaikovsky) does not have a lot bass and allows me to test the mid-range. XBOOM CERAMIC speaker did well on the mid-tone test, it did break up a bit in a bass range, but it did better than a number of other small speaker which could not handle Toccata's bass at all.

In the video I switch between the tablet's built-in speaker and XBOOM CERAMIC speaker so you can compare the sound. You can hear that the speaker produce the sound that is richer, fuller, and louder sound the the built-in speaker.

The speaker comes with split cable - one part of it is a charging cable (6.5 inches long) the other part is an audio cable (23.5 inches). The charging cable is quite short, but it does not have to be attached when the speaker is playing. This speaker can be daisy changed to another speaker, it has a built in audio cable to connect multiple speakers to each other.

The package also includes is a cloth pouch we can be used the keep the speaker in its cable together so they don't get separated.

I received XBOOM speaker and XBOOM CERAMIC speaker from the manufacture for testing. I found that the XBOOM speaker performed somewhat better than XBOOM CERAMIC speaker at the bass range. I am posting reviews for both of these speakers so you can compare the audio clips I posted if you are trying to decide between these two speakers. I hope the video will give you a good idea of what to expect.

Based on other speakers of similar size/price I rated this speaker as good (4 stars). The XBOOM CERAMIC speaker performed well with music without strong base as well as when I listened to spoken human voice (e.g. news), bass did not sound as well but not too terrible.

product_title: Yamaha T-S500BL AM/FM Tuner (Black)
review_headline: Sound is good , but nothing extra
review_body:
The sound for this unit could get a 4-5 . I have done A-B comparisons with a number of other FM tuners , those that are new , And those from the 1970's and 1980's . The dynamic sound of this turner was surprising in that is was better in the following areas . Pulling in stations . only the SONY XDR-F1HD , a digital tuner may have been better . other wise
the quality of picking up signals is very impressive . The musical quality was better than any stand alone turner that I had . This was a surprise to me . The stereo separation and dynamic quality of the sound was great .It was very musical . You would have to spend a lot more to perhaps get a better FM radio . The AM radio works , that is about all I can say . There seems not to be too much effort by anyone to build a good AM radio . Overall this is a disappointing omission in the industry . I had a 1970's Techniques , that had the best AM radio. This isn't difficult or new technology . The over all ease of use is excellent too . 40 station memory that is remembered when the unit is unplugged . So I am in most points happy I purchased this tuner . AS a radio that sounds GREAT this gets a 5 . That is the point after all , isn't it . But it has some major and very disappointing features .

First there is no remote . It is assumed that one will purchase the amplifier , which has the remote for this unit. This is very shallow corporate thinking . I have purchased mini amps from China for ~ $30 , and these had great credit card remotes . No remote codes given , nor is there a APP that you can use with this radio . Today this is unbelievable . Every electronic device has a app that you can use to control the units , but not this . This case is 90 % air , and is made from very thin and cheap steel , The size of the tuner could be much smaller . It is of course the size to match the amp that goes with it . The above ad says 2 line screen . this may be true , but in reality only one is used .Why are these screens overall size so small , they are hard to see .there is lots of room to have been made much larger. There is no RDS , why not ? This isn't rocket science . A stereo light comes on , but no tuning meter or antenna strength , I find these important in setting up my unit . The lack of these items is just another indication of just how cheaply this unit is made . There is nothing extra . Even the tuners of the 1970's have more features that were important . Of course it isn't a HD radio . I do not know why the stereo companies do not make HD radios.The SONY HD radio was under $ 100 . Of course for some reason SONY stopped making these , and are hundreds $$$$ in the used market . This unit is $250 while not being digital . I can tell you this , if it were a HD unit with the quality of the FM radio , Yamaha could not make enough to keep them in stock . There is a major void in this area of the market for a product like this . This is just another area of not doing anything innovative .

I opened the unit and the main board is of course very small . It is probably the same board used in their stereo receivers . The compactors' look good , but are really small .
the transformer is as cheap as possible . Disappointed there is not a toroidal transformer .Another corner cut . it is very interesting that just about every connection has a sealing paint on it. If you did a mod , it would be very easy to see . But this isn't a turner that lends itself to mods .

So bottom line , It has a great and wonderful sound , great tuning quality . There are not many AM/FM turners anymore on the market . review_headline: Alarm:  you can't shut it off.
review_body:
So you purchased an APC UPS to manage power surges and outages to protect your computer system and other delicate electronics. The APC unit includes software with some weird cord to connect to one of the precious USB ports on your computer. It has software to be installed that will gently shut down your computer if the power goes out, in the event that you're writing your dissertation and you've got the autosave function disabled on your word processor or something.

You're setting everything up, trying to hide wires and get on with your life.You plug the APC into the wall, the computer to the APC, everything seems to work, you're done. You ignore the CD Rom and pitch the cord.

Fast forward a few month or years. You have a power failure. You know you had a power failure because the AC went off, all the clocks are blinking and you've got to reset the damn coffee maker. To make matters worse, your APC UPS has a continuous loud, annoying beeping sound. Why is it beeping? According to APC, to tell you there was a power failure. What kind of caveman walks into his house and doesn't know immediately that there was a power failure? Can you imagine the cacophony if all your appliances had a buzzer like this? Anyway, the alarm is driving you insane. There's no switch to turn off the alarm. You can turn the entire APC off, but when you turn it back on, the alarm is back on. You can unplug it but when you plug it back in, the alarm is back on. You can remove the battery, wait an hour but when you put it back in, the alarm is back on. You can't turn it off.

Try opening up the case to destroy the alarm. It unscrews easily enough. Unless you're an electrical engineer (or perhaps spent a few years in some Hong Kong electronics sweatshop), you won't be able to identify the alarm buzzer.....or reassemble the case. Kudos to APC for figuring out exactly the minimum amount of wire and space it takes to hold one of these together. Hope you're good at puzzles.

So you're going to have to be legit about disabling the alarm. Because you pitched the CD Rom you'll have to download the software (http://www.apc.com/products/family/index.cfm?id=129&ISOCountryCode=US&tsk=g413v). Now you have to connect the computer to your APC UPS, no worries. Your computer has an RJ45 (ethernet port) and so does the APC. You've got a ton of ethernet patch cables laying around, just make the connection and you're good, right? Nope. Not going to work. You need that funky cable that's RJ45 on on end and USB on the other. Don't remember where you put it? You're screwed.

If you're the type of soulless individual that relishes pouring over instructions and filling out warranty cards AND doesn't mind a USB port being occupied by a device you'll rarely utilize (unless you count the NSA monitoring your internet activities), then you'll really enjoy the APS UPS feature that requires computer input to disable an annoying alarm. product_title: Kaito KA321 Pocket-size 10-Band AM/FM Shortwave Radio with DSP (Digital Signal Processing), Black
review_body:
This little radio is a great, small, hand-held radio. I am very impressed with the signal pick-up strength. I live outside of Denver, CO, in Aurora. I travel all over the city on busses. This little radio does a great job with FM signals and antenna is a boost to clarity when needed. I rarely ever need the antenna extended. The antenna is NOT used for the AM stations, as expected. I find that AM doesn't come in a well as FM when I am on the bus. And, of course again, the AM stations sound best when radio as a whole is rotated to a certain position. I use a suction cup on busses to hang radio on window, when I want to listen to AM stations. FM comes in great on the bus. The headphone port works as expected, with nice stereo output and PLENTY of volume.

The mono speaker quality is what one might expect from a small speaker (no deep bass, but decent enough for general listening.) I listen to talk radio (850 KOA) when I water the flowers and the grass from my deck. The sound coming out of this Kaito is crystal clear and my wife laughs because the radio is so small, yet decent sound. It is a little bigger than a deck of cards, but not as thick. Oh, I enjoy the little piece on the back side that flips outward to make a prop for the radio. It looks kinda cool sitting on the handrail of my porch.

I have found a couple shortwave radio conversations and that was fun, but mostly I listen to AM and FM.

The red light is hard to see unless you look orthogonal to the face of the light. This is a slight drawback as the light greatly assists in finding the best tuning spot on the analog dial.

I guess another drawback for me, personally, is when this radio hangs from my wheelchair's under-the-seat hook, the opposite side of the radio rests on my sandals; often times the tuning dial or the volume dial rub on my sandals and the results are quite unexpected when this happens. I tried shortening the string (which is a fine length for general purposes), but the dials still manage to rub somewhere. So, I wish the the handy tie strap attached to the opposite corner of the radio. :) Not a big deal.

I highly recommend this little Kaito radio. (Oh, and after 20 hours of listening, the batteries are still strong.) I don't know the battery life, as of yet.

product_title: Emotiva UPA-200 2-Channel Amplifier
review_headline: A little taste of "high end audio" for short money ...
review_body:
I purchased the Emotiva UPA-200 solely based on internet research. In the old days, I would never have purchased an audio component without hearing it first in some audio system, ideally, in my own audio system. My circa 1995 NAD 214 power amplifier was on the fritz and I decided to replace it rather than try to get it repaired. A large part of the reason I settled on the Emotiva was that I could try it in my system and return it if I didn't like it. Also, Emotiva's 5 year transferable warranty gave me confidence that, at the very least, I could expect to use the stereo power amp for 5 years. I used to be part owner of a high end audio company, Expressive Technologies; we made some of the best moving coil step-up transformers, preamplifiers and interconnects, so I've heard a lot of gear, albeit many years ago. Anyway, I wasn't looking for a state of the art or ultimate solution, just a way to play Pandora and CDs for background music.

When I received the Emotiva UPA-200, I was immediately impressed by the build quality and modularity of the small, simple circuit boards inside. From my design experience, it struck me as very well thought out and executed. One nice touch is the cloth bag that the amp is shipped in to keep it clean and scratch free. The only faults I noticed were that the metal case's top bowed slightly in a convex manner, something that would not affect the performance one iota but was visually less than ideal. The other fault was that there was no instruction manual or warranty card in the box. I notified the company via email and they cheerfully send out a printed manual and warranty right away via US Priority Mail.

I use the Emotiva UPA-200 with a Grace Internet radio, an Audio Research SP-9 preamp and Celestian SL6 loudspeakers. Interconnects have shields grounded to the preamp's ground post and speaker wires are relatively short. To date, and I've used it every day for a month, the amplifier has functioned without a single glitch.

So how does it sound? Very darn good for a $350 power amp. The first thing that impressed me was a relatively solid, articulate bass. Most amps in this price range don't have nearly the control of the Emotiva in the lower registers. Now, the Celestians don't really produce any deep bass, so I don't know what is going on at subwoofer frequencies, but the mid bass is pleasingly and solidly reproduced. Bass is one of the key distinctions between mediocre and better audio components and the UPA-200 passes in this regard. It is also a part of the frequency spectrum that, in theory, won't suffer too much from less than ideal, digitally compressed, sources. The rest of the spectrum is also well reproduced to a point. At low to mid listening levels the amp is pleasant and clear. Voices, guitars and so forth are well reproduced though lacking the ultimate detail of the best class A power amps. Where the UPA-200 shows its sonic flaws is when the volume begins to rise, even well before what I believe is distortion due to clipping. When pushed, the amp loses its composure. At even moderately high levels, the thing starts to sound noisy and strained. That said, as far as I can remember, the Emotiva UPA-200 sounds much better than my old NAD 214 ever did with the little, reserved Celestians. It drives them better, so they sound more dynamic and lively. For background music, I'm enjoying the system immensely, and a number of people, who know nothing about high-end audio, and have not been made aware of the audio system per say, have commented on how good the music sounds. This small, inexpensive power amp really does provide a little taste of high end audio for very short money.

product_title: Nyrius NY-GS3200 5.8GHz 6 Channel Wireless Audio/Video Sender Transmitter & Receiver System with IR Remote Extender
review_headline: The Nyrius NY-GS3200 exactly fit my needs...
review_body:
I bought the Nyrius video transmitter/receiver system to be used with an upstairs 30-inch television for my wife's sewing room. I am remote connecting a standard-definition FIOS cable-box using SD video to a second floor room about 25 feet diagonally from the transmitter. No direct line-of-sight exists between the transmitter and receiver, and the Nyrius works well in spite of the walls, ceiling, and furniture in the way. Yes, there's interference if you walk between the transmitter and receiver, or if you put large metal objects in between the two. (Like the television... It doesn't like transmitting through the television.) But once you pick locations for the transmitter and receiver that work well, and aim the antennas appropriately, it's a perfectly good (and almost unnoticable) viewing solution. In my case I'm fortunate that nobody can walk between my antennas (I'm transmitting through the ceiling), and while the picture is not HD quality, it does not have any disturbing video or audio defects on my 30-inch LCD remote TV. No interference with phones or microwaves either. Overall this is exactly what I was looking for to do this task. It's a well constructed product that works well, sold at a good price, and assuming it lasts well I would definitely buy this product again.
*** Update ***
The system has been in service daily for about a month, and once the antennas were adjusted it hasn't been touched again. Everything just works with no fuss or bother. Due to local thunderstorms we've had the power flicker on and off about a half-dozen times on different days, plus go totally out twice with the units giving us no issues at all. This was a great purchase, and I can highly recommend this unit.

review_headline: Great receiver, but not at the current $450 tag. Shop around.
review_body:
This receiver sounds very clean with nice highs, not a lot of bass when compared to a Denon or Pioneer. I find it matches very well with smaller satellites. I have it powering a set of Kef 3005's. The Yamaha goes great with Kefs ,b&w and most brighter sounding speakers. The power is sufficient and the user interface is very easy to figure out.

One issue I had when buying this was figuring out how to hook up 7 speakers all play the same sound. The 2nd zone will have a audio delay, so if your second zone is kitchen speakers and your 5 others are in the next room you will have a delay. After wasting time on different options one including a speaker line slitter I decided to get ride of the second zone all together. Hooked up 7.2 in my tv room (using front highs) and hooked up my out door speakers on the 6/7 channels. When I watch tv I shut off rear speakers and turn on front highs, when I have a party or want to listen to music out side I switch it to rear surrounds. The rear surrounds you can change the hertz and speaker size, this is not a option for the front highs. The next model up 763 can play the second zone without a lag its called \\"party mode\\" a marketing plan by yamaha. I cant use individual volumes with all 7 speakers playing in the same zone like I could if it was broken into 2 zones but to save a $200 I didnt think it was needed. The current price of 450 for the 653 is a horrible deal. I got mine from amazon for $357. I would wait until the price goes down, the new version 675 is about the $450 price tag, might as well get the new one.

I owned a onkyo Tx nr-616 before I got this and returned it due to it not working properly. I would stay away from Onkyo as their receivers all seem to have quality issues. I also tried a pioneer sc-1522 and returned that because it had video input problems. The yamaha has been perfect, it runs pretty cool has great features and is easy to configure (unlike the pioneer).

Airplay is awesome and I feel its leaps and bounds better than connecting via blueTooth. Next receiver I get for my upstairs system will need more guts and better room correction so I most likely will get a Denon or Marantz. I am using klipsch speakers and dont think the Yamaha will sound as nice with the due to the klipsch having horn tweeters. It might be a bit TOO bright. Also, when you get into the higher end recievers I think Yamaha falls short on power and options when compared to the Denons. The yamaha 1020 vs a 3313 is more money, has the same power and less options with not as good room correction. don't get me wrong both will sound great. I feel it might not be the best bang for the buck. But in regards to the under $500 price tag I wouldn't get anything but a yamaha. All the bells and whistles on the Onkyo are meaningless if it doesnt last more than 6months.

I'm a sucker for powerbanks. Don't know why - I must be paranoid about not being able to read my Kindle on the plane or something. Or play sudoku on my phone.

I need to get a life...

Anyway, this is OK for an extra battery pack, but there are better ones out there. I've been able to charge my Kindle Paperwhite and my phone (Samsung Galaxy S3) from a little less than half way to the top on a single charge. I think I should have been able to get more than that, but I get the feeling that this doesn't stop charging things when the things are full, so it runs out of juice when it doesn't have to.

This feels like it's about the same weight as my phone in its case, so it's not super heavy - probably 50% heavier than my naked phone. It comes with a 5 inch cord for charging (micro USB to USB) that I actually like a lot - I've been trying to find super short USB cords for traveling - so I might get more use out of the cord than the actual battery. :) It's just nice for having when I charge my phone in my purse - no long cord to get tangled.

So for the price (~$45 as I write this) and the performance, it gets 3 stars. It works OK, but not spectacularly so, but it's inexpensive. I don't trust the lights on the front. I like being able to charge 2 things, but so many powerbanks do that now.

It will charge my [[ASIN:B007P4VOWC Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (7-Inch, Wi-Fi)]], and not every powerbank will do that.

product_title: VideoSecu Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket for 26"-55" LCD LED Plasma 3D TV with VESA up to 400x400, Full Motion Tilt Swivel Dual Arms BD4
review_headline: Wall mounting plate is too narrow
review_body:
This mounting bracket is pretty good and the price is right, but there are a couple things that made me reduce its rating by 2 stars.

The first thing you should consider for this or any TV wall mount is the width of the mounting plate vs. the spacing of the wall studs where you want to hang it. This mount allows for a maximum 16 inches between the lag bolts. I found that the wall where I wanted to hang my TV had 24 inches between studs. So what I thought was going to be a couple hour project had an extra day added to it because I had to go buy a 2x10 plank, cut it, sand it, paint it, drill the pilot holes, then mount IT to the wall before I could mount the bracket to it. The instructions only assumed the wall stud spacing was no wider than the mounting plate and gave no hint as to what to do otherwise.

The other ding against this product is because it didn't come with all the right bits and pieces to attach the TV to the bracket. It had 2 sizes of screws and in 2 lengths to put the TV on the bracket. The 2 lengths of the larger screws were too short or too long, and no washers supplies for the larger screws per the instructions. I had to hunt around in my garage for 2 sets of extra washers: one to put on the screws as instructed, and another to fill the space because the screws were just a bit too long.

Also check all of the bolts on the bracket before hanging the TV, a few on the one I got were a bit loose.

product_title: X10 Powermid PM5900 Remote Control Extender Kit - Includes a Transmitter and Receiver
review_body:
I don't usually write product reviews and when I do it is to complain about something. However, I felt that I just had to report my experience with this product. It worked exactly as advertised!

I placed the transmitter on a bookshelf in my home theater and the receiver on an equipment shelf inside a closed small room when all of my components reside. There were three aspects of the performance of the Powermid that surprised me.

First, it is extremely responsive. There is no apparent time lag between pushing a button on the remote and the component response.

Second, it was incredibly easy and fast to setup. It took less than five minutes.

Third, I didn't have to do anything special in terms of aiming or placement of the receiver. I just placed it on a shelf in the room and all of my components respond. This is probably because my components are in a small room where the IR signal reflects off of the walls and bounces around.

If I had to offer any criticism at all it is that you must aim the remote directly at the transmitter. Its reception of the IR signal seems quite narrow. However, this is nit-picking.

I really admire the simplicity of this product. The transmitter converts the IR signal into a radio frequency, which can pass through walls, and then the receiver converts it back to IR and sends it to the components. This all happens in a fraction of a second. Compared to some other products I tried and/or investigated, this one is superior by a whole order of magnitude.

review_headline: Three out of four failed within 45 days of light, intermittent use.
review_body:
I have owned four of these within the past four months. All but one stopped working. Two of the three stopped working within the first 30 days and were therefore eligible for exchange, which I did. The third one stopped working exactly 39 days after I received it. Although the return policy is limited to 30 days, the truly wonderful folks at Amazon were still right there for me. This time, I accepted a refund rather than a replacement. Basically, I'm giving up on the earbuds.

So what went wrong, specifically? Two of the four started cutting-out at the base, where the cord emerges from the little plastic thingy just above the plug. The third failed at the control pod - the buttons became non-functional. The fourth one, by the way, I managed to lose within three weeks of its arrival and so that one's entirely on me. I'd feel bad about it except that, based upon my experience with the other three, I have to believe that it, too, would have stopped working - sooner rather than later. Allow me to say at this point that these most definitely are are not the first earbuds I've owned in my life. Of the 30 or more others (that's not an exaggeration by any means) I've owned over the years, only a couple of them ever gave me problems. Basically, what I'm saying is that I'm not hard on earbuds. And yet, three of the four of this particular brand which I've owned (and I really had high hopes for them) failed within a month and a half. I'm not certain that it rises to the level of statistical significance but I have to believe I'm detecting a trend here.

By the way, I also purchased a fifth pair (the pink and white version) for my wife. She hasn't used hers yet but I think I can safely predict the outcome once she does put them into service. So here's my assessment of these earbuds: They're great! They're wonderful in every respect except for the minor drawback that they become absolutely useless within the first month and a half of use.If you're okay with that, by all means go for it. Meanwhile, although I can't recommend these particular earbuds, I can, without hesitation, recommend Amazon 100%. It's a great company.

All in all it works great, especially if you live far from your nearest stations. I am hoping that when I get it on the 20 foot pole and a clear place to put it that I might get in more channels. But on the 10 foot pole it works better than my old one on a thirty foot pole. And my old one was working fine until it got some damage, more from old age than weather.
I gave it 4 stars because of the rotating motor doesn't work properly and missing the one bolt and nut. Other wise it is a great buy for the price and works really good for you that live out in the middle of no where like me.

product_title: HDMI Splitter
review_headline: Laptop to Monitors -- Have to reset sound
review_body:
Maybe I'm doing something wrong. Hooked this up to HDMI port of Laptop and output to two LCD computer monitors (not full TV's). Works great, get good picture on both monitors, except sound on laptop does not work. Can see pictures fine, but get no audio. I think this device assumes you are using this with a full TV and not with just a monitor. As soon as you plug the splitter HDMI cable into the laptop, there is no sound. The speakers attached to the laptop stop making sound. When you unplug it the sound comes back. If this was laptop to two televisions, probably no problem since TV's have their own audio player. Monitors rely on laptop for audio, but this appears to disable laptop audio.

Anyway, I need to see if there is a fix for this or return it.

OK, now I fixed it. I went into the laptop/windows control panel and selected sound. When I opened sound I saw that either this product or a new monitor I purchased to use with it had installed a new sound speaker which the laptop defaulted to whenever the HDMI cable was plugged in. I fixed this by clicking on the new sound speaker and under properties disabling it. Then the sound came back on. So my problem is solved.

Actually, I do not know whether my problem was caused by a new HDMI computer monitor I purchased to use with the splitter or by the splitter. The new HDMI computer monitor was plugged into an output jack of the splitter. All I know is that when I plugged the input cable of the splitter into the laptop, the sound stopped working. The above of going in to the laptop control panel and disabling the new speaker is the fix.

So I give this 4 stars because with the above fix everything is working perfectly - sound, picture, everything.

I've always heard that the quality of sound transmitted via BT is of inferior quality compared to wired speakers. I play streaming movies and TV from both my iPad and Samsung S4 phone, and the sound is rich, full-spectrum and virtually distortion-free on this speaker. You can really \\"feel\\" the base. The choice of three equalizer settings, although limited, does help the sound quality for the environment in which the speaker rests. It lasts for many hours on a single charge. I already owned an X-mini speaker, X-Mini II XAM4-B Mono Portable Capsule Speaker, Black, when I saw this newer model. I got this newer one in part because I like the metallic color and because I have so far been extremely satisfied with the old speaker.

The X-Mini is a light, compact speaker that goes everywhere with you and comes with a nice carrying pouch. I have used it with my ipods, Kindle Fire, lap top and desk top. One of the things to note is that though it gives amazing volume, it tends to get \\"shaky\\" and the sound gets \\"blurry\\" when you get close to the maximum volume. With all my aforementioned devices but the desk top, it is noticeable but not as jarring as with the desktop. I assume this because the desktop is capable of higher volume limits that the other devices.

But all in all, I do really like the speaker and would recommend it to anyone looking for something in this price range and at this size. Also, my older X-Mini is still working perfectly fine a year later so I would assume this one will also stand the test of time.

review_body:
I absolutely love these headphones. I have been buying Philips' In-Ear headphones for years. I upgraded to these because I lost my last pair and I am really glad that I did.

These are the first earbuds I have owned that do not get tangled. I repeat - they do not get tangled! The fabric wrapped lower portion of the cord is great and keeps knots from getting twisted into the cable. The clips that Philips has added to the upper portion of the cord is by far the best part. You simply slide the clip up towards the earbuds and the two sections of the cord are held together. The far end of the cord can then be folded up and clipped in place as well. I have never seen such an elegant solution to such a frustrating problem!

Simple conveniences aside, these are also great headphones. They are extremely comfortable and stay securely in your ear. They are so comfortable that I have fallen asleep with them in and woken up the next morning with them still in my ears and no soreness or discomfort after wearing them for 8 hours.

The sound in these is fantastic! The bass is robust and I have enjoyed these headphones for both listening to music and podcasts/audiobooks. The snug fit of the earbuds also passively cancels noise. With both of them in, I can easily hear my music in a crowded room with the volume turned all the way down.

Considering the low price and many advantages, I think these headphones are absolutely worth it!

product_title: Koss SportaPro Stereo Headphones
review_headline: The Sportapro has a dirty little secret.
review_body:
The SportaPro has a dirty little secret.

The Sportaro literally uses the same exact drivers and housing as the KSC35, but instead of attaching the KSC35's clips, they attached the SportaPro headband. Here's my head-fi review 'snippet' of the KSC-35 which IS the same as the Sportapro:

KSC-35, the more mature Koss clip-on that was discontinued and then brought back (only on the Koss website), for a pretty hefty $45. I'd say it's hefty because it honestly should cost just slightly above the KSC75 range, not 3x as much. They sound very similar to the KSC75. However, they are fuller sounding, with fuller bass approaching full-sized type bass, and the mids/vocals are very rich and forward. Treble is also quite neutral for me, not being too smooth, and not too sparkly. I actually am quite fond of their treble. The KSC75's treble is harsher, grainier, and more fatiguing. The mids on the KSC75 are slightly laid back, while the KSC35 presents them up front and more fleshed out. In all honesty, you can say the difference between the KSC75 and KSC35 is like the difference between the K701 and Q701. One is brighter, drier, and thinner sounding, while the other is more natural, and fleshed out.

All in all, it's a solid sounding headphone, that does work very well. Bass was strong but quick due to the open nature of the headphones, but slower than the KSC75. Based on sound alone, I'd say the KSC35 is a headphone you could use for hours without fatigue. Kind of like a smaller, more bassy HD650. Nice tonal balance that I don't think anyone would dislike.

The Koss Sportapro houses the same drivers as the KSC35, for less than half the price. You can literally buy the Sportapro, snap off the drivers, and snap the KSC75/35 clips on to the Sportapro drivers, and you have a cheaper KSC35. Ideal solution is getting the Sportapro and KSC75, putting the KSC75 clips onto the Sportapro drivers. This will save you $10, give you BOTH the KSC35 and KSC75 as a spare, and give the most comfort, IMHO. Just make sure to bend the KSC75 clips to place the drivers closer to the ears, as stock form may place the drivers too far, losing bass and overall sound quality.

The more popular alternative, is to buy the cheap Parts express headphone (http://www.amazon.com/Mini-Stereo-Lightweight-Headphones-feet/dp/B0002KQZJS/ref=sr_1_1?s=electronics&ie=UTF8&qid=1371458925&sr=1-1&keywords=parts+express+headphones), taking off the crappy drivers, and using the headband for the Koss drivers. I prefer the Koss clips rather than the Parts Express headband, but I'm in the minority.5 as a spare, and give the most comfort, IMHO. product_title: Yurbuds Ironman Inspire PRO Performance Fit Sport Earphones with 3-Button Control and Mic, Black/ Red
review_headline: Best fit 'active' earbuds I've ever had
review_body:
I've now spent probably more than the cost of my iPhone on various headphones for when I go running. That said, I originally had tried the Jabra and the Jaybird Freedom wireless Bluetooth models prior to this one. When they worked, the wireless ones were very convenient. However, the fit was never as 'secure' as they advertised (despite trying all the different ear fittings, etc...but granted, my ears are probably odd-shaped). The worst part of about wireless (for me) has been that they stop charging after only a few cycles...on both types I've had.

So...I went with Yurbud Ironman Inspire Pro earbuds. They're wired...so not as convenient...but the ample amount of cord length allows me to wear them with the cord running along my back so I don't accidentally get tangled up with my arms when I run.

More importantly...the simple insert & twist of earbuds gives a GREAT fit that felt comfortable and didn't slip/fall out at all during my first run with them (for about 4.5 miles or so). The earbuds sound really good for sport headphones and they let in all the ambient noise in traffic, etc so you can hear enough of what's going on around you.

I may try some different options to do something with the cord, but I'm very satisfied due to the fit and comfort.

review_headline: Like it, but don't love it.
review_body:
I have had this system in my wish list for over 7 months,and now that the price is at half off ($298). I'm not thrilled. Here's the thing that has me wondering what is going on with Sony. I have a Samsung Galaxy S2, granted its a apple docking station but I only wanted to play music through Bluetooth and my TV. Does it do it, it does, do I like it, I do. But one of the only things that I would love to do with it is control the volume while watching TV without the use of the cheap remote that comes with it. You would think you could just download an app, there isn't one, and there won't be as far as Sony is concerned, I emailed customer service about this. The product suits my needs, but the difference between having it docked with an Ipad and D-sappli app is the only way you can get the true sound out of it. Disappointing. Even docked, I wouldn't want to be without an Ipad having to use the cheap remote 20 feet away having to get up to change music folders, or Itunes. If you can live with 20% of the sound quality stripped as I am, its still good for the money ($298).

The Pos: Looks good. Not as good as the Samsung DA-E750, Also in my wish list.
Connects to bluetooth and airplay effortlessly. The process took me 30 seconds.
Inputs, optical, and what looks like a head phones jack plug in.

Cons: Zero android support.
An awful remote control that has a hard time turning the volume up or down and feels cheap, like an hp remote that use to come with some laptops Pavilion DV5 and 6 series.
The sound doesn't live up to the price of the original $500 and up price point when I first added it to my wish list. The Bass or equalizer is not adjustable unless you have it docked with an apple product. But when docked, it sounds great.

product_title: Samsung 3.6-Inch Galaxy Player
review_headline: I got what I was hoping for from the Samsung Galaxy
review_body:
I purchased this MP3 player as an alternative to my Android Phone. I was looking for a lot of storage, WIFI and a decent play back that would run my indispensable Audible app. The Samsung Galaxy delivered on all of these specifications and more.

Pros:
-WIFI enabled
-Android, so I can utilize my favorite apps, mainly Audible and Amazon MP3.
-Clean display that utilizes every bit of its 3.6 inches. I like reading my emails and RSS reader posts on this device more than my phone.
-Responsive touch screen
-Affordable with 8 GBs of memory and an upgradeable micro SD slot. 32 GBs holds a lot of books! I also got a refurbished model for half price and it shipped in regular packaging with no discernible issues.
-Clear sound even using the cheap ear phones it comes with. The speakers without a speaker doc or earphones do leave something to be desired, but I thankfully I know how to accessorize.
-Doesn't freeze (I've been using this for 3 months now). And it hasn't frozen or prompted me to shut down an application yet.

Cons:
-Glare makes it impossible to navigate, even in indirect and low sunlight. You can't even tell if it's on. It makes listening outdoors more difficult.
-Good for only a day or so of battery life after a single charge.
-The camera app delivers blurry photos.

product_title: Apple iPod touch (5th Generation) NEWEST MODEL
review_body: Received this as a gift to replace 3rd gen ipod touch.  I am a holdout for a smartphone.  Would love iphone or android phone but can't get over ridiculous cost of phones and plans.  I currently use $30 Tracphone and $6 month family plan, so I balk when I see what the cell carriers want.  That said I love what I can do with the ipod touch.  It is much better at working independently without using iTunes on my PC (slow clumsy software).  With iOS6 I can set ipod to automatically download podcasts that I subscribe to.  I do a lot of driving and love podcasts.  Screen is very crisp and battery life is excellent.  Two things keep me from giving a 5 start rating.  One is the slightly narrower screen size.  It makes typing in portrait mode a bit tougher because the keys are narrower. Perhaps I will get used to it over time.  I am torn because I think a slightly bigger screen would be nice, but like the size of the device in  that it can slip easily into a pocket, unlike the new 5+ inch android devices.  The other thing is the lightning connector, and the fact that if you want your legacy charger/speaker to work (charge and play audio) you have no choice but to buy Apples $30-$40 adapter.  That said I am quite satisfied, and hope Apple continues to make the ipod touch until smartphones and plans become reasonable.

product_title: JBL Ultra-Portable Speaker with Built-In Bass Port and Wireless Bluetooth Connectivity
review_headline: The Best Bluetooth Speaker I've Yet Found
review_body:
This is the 4th Bluetooth Speaker I've bought, and it buries the competition by a significant margin. One of the earlier Bluetooth speakers I bought was the Cambridge Soundworks Oontz, which by comparison, falls way behind the JBL. The Oontz almost completely lacks in any of the lower frequencies, and doesn't greatly impress me in the rest of the sound spectrum. On the other hand the JBL Micro Wireless Bluetooth speaker has better bass, and overall, a much more realistic sound spectrum. Almost all smaller speakers, one buys, are going to be a compromise in some area. To have the desired portability, obviously you can't put a 12" woofer in such a speaker, but what you can do is maximize the frequencies that a portable speaker system can produce. JBL has done the best job so far. No, it isn't stereo, but how much stereo affect can you expect from a speaker you can hold in the palm of your hand? I read that one reviewer found that this speaker distorts. Well, any speaker, driven too hard, will distort. If you are driving a speaker that hard, you are in danger of blowing it's voice coil. Obviously, it's unrealistic to expect a speaker, the cone of which is around 2", to produce the level of sound of a bigger speaker. Physics can tell you why that is, but common sense should also. Within the reasonable realm of use, this speaker is, for now, the clear winner out of what I've experienced. The battery charge life is very nice also. JBL understates the expected duration of the battery charge life. I got probably more than 7 hours at a very respectable sound level. I also like the loop at the top of the speaker. With the loop, I can put a carbiner on the speaker, and suspend it from a belt loop. That enables me to carry it with me at work. Lastly, pairing with my I-phone was a breeze. Should I have trouble with any of my other Bluetooth devices, I'll amend my review. If you are looking for a great little Bluetooth speaker, with a long charge life, this is a wise choice. I can comfortably recommend it to anyone looking for a portable, Bluetooth speaker for their phone, or any other Bluetooth enabled audio device. Don't waste your time, nor money on the competition; this is the one to get.

***UPDATE***

After owning my JBL Bluetooth speaker for more than a month, I'd be prepared to give it an even higher rating, were one available. I'm still amazed, and was even fooled into believing someone was in an adjoining room, where I'd left it a few minutes before. I'd forgotten that I'd left the speaker on, and thought someone was having a conversation on his phone. That is the quality of sound that the JBL produces. I also have to say that the charge capacity is even better than I initially reported. With the volume turned all the way up, the speaker continued through the entire work day with charge left over If someone knows of a Bluetooth speaker with greater quality sound, given it's size and cost, I'd very seriously ask that they send me a comment to that effect. Finally,in my belief, the JBL Micro Wireless Bluetooth speaker is, if not the best of it's kind, I have yet to find a better one. You can buy this one, and know that it would be hard to do better.

***Second Update*** After more than 2 months my enthusiasm for this speaker remains as high as ever. I never cease to be amazed at it's charge life. Used at full volume for nearly 8 continuous hours, the speaker's battery still has charge left. I also have to agree with the others who praise the sound of the JBL Micro. While the bass isn't going to blow you out of your seat, for a very small speaker I still want to know if someone finds one that is better, especially at a non-astronomical price point. I'm sure there is one out there that sounds better, but is it as small, and is it's price as reasonable? I'll believe it only if I see it. Yes, IT IS THAT GOOD!

***Third Update**** My enthusiasm, forthis speaker, just continues to grow. Last night, at work, my mp3's battery died on me causing me to have to plug it in to a charger. I wanted to continue to listen, and thought I'd give the speaker an opportunity to show how far I could go without losing the pairing between it and the mp3 player. At one point I was probably at least 75 feet away from the player, and the the speaker was locked on solid. Mind you this was line of sight, but at the same time, the building I was in was a crazy source of Radio Frequency noise. The range of a signal is a product of signal strength, distance, and other RF noise. AS the distance increases the signal strength drops, and eventually it drops beneath the background noise. The signal will keep on traveling infinitely, but will be of such a low strength that it will be completely overwhelmed by noise. I digress. The JBL Micro seems to have a robust bluetooth receiver in it, and is well capable of receiving a very respectable distance from the source. This is just another reason to put it on the top of your list of possible choices for a bluetooth speaker.
****Fourth Update****** It has now been more than a year since I bought my JBL, and it still keeps pleasing me. Since buying it, I have purchased 2 other bluetooth speakers, neither of which will fulfill the role the JBL Micro does. I'd say that the 2 biggest positives with the JBL Micro are the battery charge, and the overall sound. Again, it doesn't have the most powerful base, but the overall sound spectrum is well balanced, and voices come out sounding very natural. The only downside I can see with the JBL Micro is one common to all Bluetooth speakers I have so far seen, and that is that there is no provision for changing out the battery once it will no longer accept a charge. That won't stop me from changing it, though, it will just make it harder. Still, in the final analysis, even over the Bose Soundlink II Mini, I'll take the JBL Micro for most purposes. Definitely, it is vastly more portable than the Bose, and far less likely to bother others around me than the Bose speaker. I still recommend the JBL Micro to anyone wanting a great quality, affordable Bluetooth speaker. Definitely it has been worth the money.
*****Fifth Update***** Today is the 1st of September 2014 and my JBL Micro, though looking a little worse for the wear (to be expected when I have it with me all day long at work every day) keeps delivering. On at least a few occasions my time at work has approached 12 hours, and though I might not have the speaker going every single minute of the day, most of the time it is on. The only time I've had it run out of juice is the day I forgot to recharge it. Other than that, it is as reliable as sunrise. And it still sounds great. If there are any more updates it will have to do with letting you know when/if the battery finally refuses to charge. There really is nothing else left to say. Great, great product, get one and hear for yourself.
******Heads Up********** More than a year ago I bought what I thought was another JBL Micro, but in retrospect I believe it may have been a knockoff. It didn't occur to me, at the time, that that was the likelihood, so I did nothing about it. Since that time I bought yet another one, and it is the equal of the first. The second speaker I bought was beyond inferior in sound. One clue should you get one of the bad ones, is that it has a microphone in if for telephone conversation. I don't know if JBL actually has such a speaker, but just know that if the speaker you get sounds crappy, with no bass whatever, you may have gotten one you may want to consider returning. The 3rd speaker I bought is just as good as the first, so I'm suggesting that if you buy one of these speakers, and it sounds like crap, it might not actually be a JBL, and you might not want to keep it. product_title: NYNE 30-pin Home Audio iPad/iPhone/iPod Speaker Dock with Wireless Bluetooth
review_headline: Great Versatile Speaker System For Home
review_body:
I've been looking for a new speaker system to use in my living room - mostly for when I'm entertaining guests. Given all the new technology available, I included \\"docking and charging capabilities\\" on my list, as well as \\"remote control\\" and Bluetooth connectivity. When I had the chance to try out NYNE's NH-5500, I took it, because it meets all of my criteria.

The NH-5500 comes in a big box! I wouldn't consider this speaker \\"portable\\" by today's standards, but it can be moved from one room to another without having to call on a weight lifter. The speaker is best suited for a large room, both because of its size and because its formidable sound requires distance from the unit.

Inside the box was everything I needed to set up the speaker and start using it. My devices are all Apple and blue-tooth enabled, so I had no need for the 3.5 mm audio cable. The shipping cover for the speaker is thick and cloth-like, which gives it a high-end feel. The styling is sleek and low-key, fitting well with my recent campaign to simplify my surroundings.

I plugged in the speaker and set the power button on the back of the unit to \\"on.\\" After that you can permanently control the power with either the touch controls on the top of the speaker, or with the remote. When I popped my iPhone 4s into the docking connector it instantly activated the phone. A few finger slides later, music from my playlist was pouring out of the speaker, filling my office with sound. A little loud at first - but that was easily solved with a finger swipe on the volume controls on top of the speaker.

I next tried out the remote control unit, immediately discovering the controls work best if you have the unit pointed directly at the small red/blue light glowing in the lower right side of the speaker. Otherwise, the controls can be persnickety. You also must choose the correct source setting on the controls: iPod, Bluetooth, RCA or Aux. The volume controls area little sticky until you become accustomed to the buttons. Mute and pause buttons came in very handy when I had numerous interruptions.

NYNE has included 4 selectable sound effects (Movie, POP, Classic, Rock) with the NH-5500 speaker system. I played around with all four of them, using various music genres from my playlists. I mainly noticed changes in the bass and treble from one setting to another. The \\"Movie\\" mode worked best for me - providing what I perceived as the most well-rounded sound experience, regardless of music genre. Ultimately, these effects are probably of limited function for someone like me who is not an audiophile but enjoys good music.

Having experienced difficulties in Bluetooth pairing with my partner's BOSE SoundLink, I was prepared for battle with the NH-5500. I'm happy to report that Bluetooth pairing with my iPhone and my MacBook Air was seamless. I was able to switch back and forth between the two devices with no difficulties or permanent disconnection or lost signal. The NH-5500 maintained its ability to recognize and distinguish device signals even after shutting down units for the night and starting them up again in the morning. Kudos for that!

I also paired this speaker with my MacBook Air for watching videos streamed via internet. The sound quality is much better than my old portable computer speakers. This gave me the idea to try the speaker as an audio source for our giant wide-screen TV. TVs are notorious for bad sound quality, and ours is no exception. The NH-5000 easily out-performed the built-ins, serving, in essence, as a respectable sound bar for the TV.

How about the sound quality? It's very good, overall. I did not notice any distortion at high or mid ranges. If you want booming bass, the \\"Rock\\" setting will help out. My music tastes are eclectic, and I think this speaker will do equally well with rock, classical, and jazz.

My conclusion: The NH-5500is a worthy alternative to the two dinosaur age speakers that used to occupy space in our apartment living room. It's a great all-round entertainment device that I can use for docking my iPhone, charging, listening to music, and watching TV. Bluetooth connectivity is excellent, and the included remote is a necessary addition for those times when I'm not standing right next to the speaker unit.

The price is right and it is immediately recognized on any computer into which you plug it...no set up, no nothing. On the downside, they are hinky and frequently become temperamental for no apparent reason and under varying conditions, so it's impossible to pinpoint a specific action that the Sansa finds annoying, but when it does get annoyed it freezes, or loses files, or renames them with numbers, or places them in odd locations. Sometimes a file will show on the player, but not on the MicroSD; sometimes you'll get random \\"renew your subscription\\" messages when you have deactivated your subscription to Rhapsody; sometimes you just don't know what will happen. The biggest issue of all is the failure of the AUX port where you plug in either your headphones or the AUX cable for use in the car or with speakers...the port's connection becomes loose and then you get mono- instead of stereo.

Sansa actually downgraded features from the original Clip...the clip is no longer replaceable so once it's broken, it stays broken. The old one used to have a slide-in replacement piece so if it broke you could get a part and fix it, and frankly, since the Clip part is the most salient and useful feature, once it's broken, it's much less convenient to use this player unless you stick it in your pocket or buy an armband.

I now have three. The first was only 2GB, so I needed a new one. The second one has the MicroSD slot, but has the random renaming issue (it matters whether you use MSC or MTP as your USB mode ) and the clip broke and the AUXport is loose and crackles, the third one is exactly like the second one, but I'll be more careful with the clip this time.

product_title: Micca MB42 Bookshelf Speakers With 4-Inch Carbon Fiber Woofer and Silk Dome Tweeter
review_headline: Outstanding Value in this Price Range
review_body:
I collect high-end vintage "Hi-Fi" equipment from the 70s & 80s, including many sets of loudspeakers. When I read the reviews on the MB42s, I thought I'd get a pair and hear what all of the fuss was about. If you line these up with the best speakers in this price-range (50 bucks), these win top-prize, hands down.
Paired with a cheap, small subwoofer - like the Polk PSW10, you've got yourself a pretty good speaker system. Pair it with a cheap T-Amplifier, like a Lepai LP 2020A+ (20 bucks) modified with a larger power adapter (10 bucks), and an mp3 source; you've just built the best audiophile set-up available on earth for under $150 (all available from amazon).
But have no illusions... a small speaker set for fifty dollars is a small speaker set for fifty dollars. A 4 inch driver is not capable of delivering loud, deep bass- even in a small bedroom. The silk-dome tweeters provide good imaging as expected, and the physical appearance of the speakers is excellent. Adding a subwoofer is a good 1st step to getting the most out of these speakers.

review_headline: It works once you can plug it in
review_body:
I bought it so I could use my high-end scanner with my laptop. It does what I was hoping it would: I am now scanning to the laptop. It was shipped promptly by first class for free, and arrived in just two days.

I would have given it five stars if not for two serious nuisances. First, the four-pin end is extremely difficult to insert into the S400 port of my Sony Vaio. Not just the first time, every time (well, all five times I have used it so far). So much so that for now I have decided to keep it plugged in my computer and just connect and disconnect the 6-pin cable as needed (the 6-pin cable is easy to insert and remove). Naturally, I will have to pull it out whenever I need to take the laptop outside of my house, so it makes me nervous that eventually I will not be able to use this adapter.

Secondly, the picture is deceiving. The six-pin female end is not encased in plastic but is sticking out, so you have to be careful not to short your cable accidentally.

This is sold by several Amazon vendors. I got mine from CablesOnline, so it is possible the one sold as an add-on directly by Amazon does not have these issues. At any rate, Amazon lists them as the same product. And the packing slip also said it was a C2G / Cable to Go - 27028 Firewire 6-Pin Female 4-Pin Male Adapter.

Still, once it is plugged in, it works. Not bad for the price.

review_headline: Off button is too small, the method of setting the time on the alarms is idiotic
review_body:
When I get up, my husband is still asleep. I don't want to have to turn on the light to find an itty bitty tiny off button to be able to turn off the alarm clock. The point of turning off the alarm is to not wake him up, but then I wake him up by turning on the light so I can find the tiny off button.

The method for actually setting the time for the alarms is the most ridiculous I've ever seen. In fact, I've NEVER seen this method. It is a dial that you pull forward to go forward in time, and push backward to go backward in time. The rate at which you change time with this method is extremely unpredictable as you try to figure out how hard you are pressing the dial forward or backward, especially if you just want to go one minute at a time.

The idiot was me. I assumed that with it being a Sony, it would be a good, so I didn't keep anything needed to return the item, not that it would be worth the hassle. Just don't bother purchasing in the first place. I'll donate it to some organization and hopefully someone can get some use out of it that doesn't need the functionality of being able to USE AN ALARM CLOCK!!!

It has become impossible to find decent alarm clocks with two alarms these days. My husband has the giant Bose system, and I didn't want that because it is such a space hog, but now I wish I'd have just gotten it. At least it is functional and useful.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Remote with Customizable Touch Screen and Closed Cabinet RF Control
review_body:
This is a terrific remote. Gone are the 8 remotes laying around and now everything can be controlled with one remote, even PS3. Set-up is fairly quick and easy and if you have a previous Harmony you can import most of devices, activities, commands. You will need to add your favorites which is easy to do after picking your cable/satellite company and then organize them as you wish by dragging icons into the order you want. Settings can also be changed directly on remote.

Placing hub and receivers is shown in quick set-up guide. I was amazed how this worked in the closed cabinets and how I am now able to control my PS3. I have 8 devices, 9 activities and this remote controls them all, picking tv on correct input, changing sound receiver to correct channel and turning on or off the devices as programed. Even controls the ROKU making streaming easy.

Touchscreen works great and the gestures screen can be pulled up from bottom of screen in any actiivity, if you wish to use it. You can customize buttons to suit yourself very easily if you need to do so. Also has a lock on the device so kids can't accidently change settings or mess with icons or channels. Once you have everything set up how you like it you can lock the settings. Ths might not be something everyone will use, but for families with younger kids, this can be a life saver.

I would recommend the new Logitech Harmony Ultimate. It does everything you would want it to do and even stuff you never thought you would have a remote do !

product_title: Monster EA SPORTS MVP Carbon On-Ear Headphones (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Monster Mobile Talk Headphones Provide Balanced Sound, No Noise Isolation
review_body:
I own a good number of in-ear monitors (IEMs) at various price points, including the more expensive Monster Turbine Pro Gold, so I was happy to have an opportunity to use and review the Monster Mobile Talk In-Ear Headphones.

I look for three things in in-ear monitors: sound, fit, and sound isolation. The ability to block external noise is important to me, as I primarily use IEMs while commuting on trains. While Monster does provide three sets of ear tips with these headphones, I was unable to get any kind of sound isolation with the small, medium, or large ear tips provided. It's important to note that a big part of achieving sound isolation is fit, so while I may not be able to get the right fit, others with different ear canal sizes will experience different results.

From a sound perspective, the Monster Mobile Talk Headphones provide a very balanced soundstage. Bass heads will be disappointed, but those who want their music balanced will be satisfied. I used these headphones with my Droid phone, an iPod, and a Samsung MP3 player, and found that I got better results with the phone and Samsung, most likely because those devices have better equalizers. Still, the sound was very balanced and true to the source, so if you are using these headphones in a quiet setting, you will hear highs, mids, and lows that are pretty even. Because I could not get a real tight fit, the lows are not very pronounced.

I do like the flat cord, which does not tangle easily, and the mic/cell phone features worked well on my phone. The headphones are also magnetized, which is useful since Monster does not provide a small bag or carrying case.

Overall, I like these headphones. Sound isolation is important to me, so since I could not achieve a tight fit I will not be using these in noisy situations. But these headphones do produce balanced sound, and seem pretty durable, especially with the flat cord. Monster also has a pretty generous return policy, which is a nice plus in case these ever break.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-the-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Good music and gaming headphones (NOT completely noise-canceling/noise-proof)
review_body:
This V-MODA headphone in general is a good headphone but it is not completely noise canceling. It has awesome sound quality and sturdy construction. I have used this headphone over a year and it is still playing my music daily.

CONSTRUCTION:
*The headphone feels sturdy and well-balanced. The metal pieces that connect the two ear pieces might feel flimsy but it has held up suprisingly well considering it has been tossed and handled.
*The width of the headphone is adjusted by sliding the ear buds into the band.
*Depending on your comfortable level, adjust the headphone well before a long listening session because headphones can exert uncomfortable/slightly painful pressure to the sides of your head.
*The sturdiness of the Kevlar(TM) coated headphone cable is great because for some reason it doesn't tangle as much as regular plastic cables and better resist the general wear and tear that might fray regular cables.
*Packaging and headphone case seems high quality.

SOUND QUALITY:
*Excellent bass quality. I know some reviews for this headphone says the bass is too heavy but it all depends on your preference. For me, the bass was just enough that for listening to Beethoven's Symphony No. 5 felt like being in the concert hall. Higher tones and pitches are also clear and distinct. For someone who is not an audiophile, I can say going back to cheap earphones is impossible once you hear music from this headphone.
*Gaming headphones: This headphone makes immersive games like Mass Effect, Skyrim, and etc. feel alive. You can hear distinct small sounds like creatures calling and distant conversations but also grand sound effects like cinematic battles. This adds another layer of enjoyment and immersion to games.
*Noise-Canceling: This headphone does not completely block out noise. It can overwhelm small sounds like people talking. But DO NOT wear these if you work in an extrememly noise environment and have to turn your volume to the highest level to hear. You still receive all the noise around you in addition to the loud music from your headphones. This combined noise can actually damage your ear and your hearing.

These headphones are great to listen to in a low noise environment such as walking around the neighborhood. They are clear, distinct, and well designed.

product_title: Pyle PT798SBA 7.1 Channel Home Theater System with Satellite Speakers, Center Channel, Subwoofer and Bluetooth
review_headline: Not the best, but for that price & 7.1, I can't complain.
review_body:
Well, I was honest to myself from the beginning: I wasn't going to purchase anything fancy (simply because I don't have the money). I was going purchase the cheapest 7.1 set I can get from a relatively known brand. So, here we go...
When I purchased this HT system back in January 2013, there were no reviews at all in Amazon. Besides Pyle webpage, info/reviews around the web were very scarce. But I liked the looks (and the price) and after checking all the specs over and over, I ordered it.
After a week, I got a BIG box (oops!?). The first thing I noticed was how large the satellite speakers were. I was expecting something smaller. I went back to Amazon.com to confirm the dimensions and yea, the size is correct. They ARE big (duh!). Then I pulled out the main unit. It is also bigger than thought, but it includes the subwoofer, doesn't look cheap and the minimalist face looks really nice showing only the VFD display and a volume knob.
It came with all the cables, antenna, remote, etc. nicely packaged. Nevertheless, 3 of the satellite speakers had subtle scuff marks on the glossy finish (UPS bumpy ride?). I had to put those on the back of the room.
The speaker wire was enough in length (small room) but too thin for my needs (22 AWG?). I just went ahead and purchased real-copper 16 AWG wire.
So, I installed the thing. My setup includes a 50\\" LCD TV and a HTPC running Windows 8 (see customer images). I really like how the whole system looks now.
The MOBO on the PC has 7.1 HD audio included so the Pyle receiver is directly connected to the computer. There's no digital input on the Pyle so I used stereo 3.5mm to stereo RCA Y cable connectors (analog).
Then I downloaded a 7.1 sound test WAV from Microsoft to check each channel. Each speaker responded correctly (whew!). Initial overall sound from the PC was disappointing though. Then I tested the Bluetooth music playback from my Galaxy Note and it sounded beautifully. Good sound balance with nice bass with very little tweaking on the Poweramp app. I even was able to jump to the next song on my phone using the Pyle remote. Cool.
So I knew this Pyle was able to do much better from the PC. I went back to Windows, Control Panel, Realtek HD Audio Manager, Room Correction and entered values for distance and decibels. Way better. Surround sound effects in Avatar (BluRay, 5.1) were really good. But bass was still lacking. I pumped up the SW volume on the Pyle remote and I got some good bass, but not great (I eventually added a second subwoofer to fill the void).
I noticed the speakers make a tiny hissing noise even after the unit is turned off. Not a problem for me because I'm using some remote controlled AC outlets to entirely disconnect my system from the grid.
Now, after 3 months, many movies, music and fine-tunning, I can say I'm satisfied with this Pyle. For this -low- price you get real 7.1 sound (with some bass). But you will need to play with the settings on the unit and your source (in my case, Windows) to get the real deal.
Music over Bluetooth sounds great out of the box (with great bass). Haven't tested aux or mp3 inputs.
Would I recommend it to a friend?... If in a tight budget, yea.h nice bass with very little tweaking on the Poweramp app. I even was able to jump to the next song on my phone using the Pyle remote. Cool.

review_body:
I am a retired 25-year computer professional and still builds custom PC's for high-end clients. I have yet to see a cable of this quality, for a consumer product, and rarely for even data centers. But the cable is not so stiff and thick as not to bend easily for routing purposes (you know to keep those high-tech cables from being ugly).

This is now my preferred cable. I use it, will always buy for my computer/Multimedia installations (I do Home Theater, HDTV stuff too), and will recommend to my friends.

product_title: Sangean RCR-22 AM/FM Tuning Clock Radio (White)
review_body:
I, too like the Sangean RCR-22 for it's great reception and features. And like many, I found it's Electric Blue display to be either way too bright (when I want darkness in the room) or, if adjusted to be dim enough, it is difficult to see the numerals.

The FIX - put a deep red colored lighting gel over the display. I bought a strobist filter gel kit, such as are available on Amazon and elsewhere, and tried the different colors until I found one that blocks the blue light, and lets the white light of the numerals through. I affixed it with good quality Scotch tape.

It looks really neat now. The filter gel from the strobist kit is big enough to cover the whole part of the display that emits light, and could even be trimmed a bit shorter if I cared to. And, the display is red with an eerie light blue surround. Sort of an Alien Control Pod effect. I think it is rather cool! The red color is easy on the eyes, and when I'm looking at it when the alarm goes off, even though it goes to full brightness, it is easy to see but not nasty on the retinas.

I've extended the FM antenna wire up the side of my dresser, and don't mind the coiled wire from the radio to the Signal Sensor antenna. The radio works great, even in my electically noisy bedroom, and the time adjusts automagically too!

Cons - I wish I could adjust the Snooze time to be longer than 5 minutes, and when tuning sometimes the up/down button switches the band from FM to AM. Minor annoyance, I just slow down and it is OK. With 7 presets, I don't manually tune often anyway.

review_headline: Good sound, good price, and very portable
review_body:
I purchased these headphones after reading an in depth review of them from a Hi-Fi experts web site. They had very good things to say about these headphones comparing them to others in its price range and some above. After I received them and have had a chance to listen to music, podcasts, and other spoken word material I have to agree with the review I read.

These headphones sound very good for music and voice. The bass is strong, but not over bearing. The treble (highs) are clean and crisp without hiss. Sound wise I am happy with them so far.

**Used primarily with a Samsung Galaxy Nexus phone (hiking) and Nexus 10 tablet**

Feel and comfort: I have bought many portable headphones over the last 3 years or so and most have sounded fine, but I have trouble keeping ear buds and in-ear headphones in my ear without falling out every few minutes while hiking (my main use for headphones). After getting tired of constantly pushing in the ear buds after falling out I tried the \\"behind the head\\" style which worked well but only lasted about 6 months and one side quit working. The same thing with a pair that loops around the back of the ear. I finally got tired of this and bought this pair that rests on the ear. Since they provide very little pressure (this is also adjustable for even lighter pressure if needed via a switch on each side) they are very comfortable and no more falling out! I was happy that after my 2 hour hike my ears didn't hurt a bit and no constant adjustments.

Looks/Style: They are a bit bulky compared to ear buds or in-ear models, but still quite lightweight and portable. review_headline: Solid hardware, expandable memory, terrible OS

The tablet is mostly used for games and movies for the kids, which both work quite well with the Nook now. Infact I would rank the Nook with the AFN modification as a better overall tablet then the Kindle since it provides for addition storage (up to 32gb) and is very easy to root. My biggest complaint left (same as the Kindle) is a lack of camera, gps, and bluetooth.

In stock form, this tablet is a 2 star product because of the crapware Nook OS. But when rooted with Android, this is a solid all around tablet worthy of a 4 star rating.

product_title: LG Electronics AG-F310DP Cinema 3D Dual Play Gaming Glasses (2 Pair) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: You don't need these if you have a couple extra pairs of regular 3d glasses
review_body:
So these are at a good price and are pretty nice glasses for gaming (thus the 4 star), but if you have bought a LG 3d tv and want to play games splitscreen but don't want to shell out the cash, here's how.

Simply pry open the regular glasses that came with your TV from the top. There is a lining you can probably see. Once you pop out the edges by the hinges, then you can pull out the flimsy lens part. Just do this to a left eye and then a right on another pair. Switch those 2 lenses you just removed to the other glasses and snap the plastic back together. Done. You now have 2 pairs of Gaming glasses.

Lots of companies will try to get you to pay $10-30 for a pair or 2 or 4 of these when you can make them if you have a couple extra pairs you aren't using. Mine came with 4 pairs, so I have 2 pairs for 3D viewing and 2 pairs for gaming. Just use fingernail polish or a permanent marker to mark the Gaming ones so you don't get them mixed up.

That said, these are a pretty decent deal and if I could not have done the above fix (or if I just didn't have more than 2 pairs) then I would have bought these.

Hope this review helps people.

product_title: uxcell Computer PC Fan Noise Speed Reduce 4 Pins Resistor Cable Adapter 5 Pcs
review_headline: They work good, but they could be improved...
review_body:
Functionally, these work good, but they aren't very "user friendly" when it comes to keeping your cables/wires neat. The reason I say that is because these are very stiff. This is partly due the the solid leads of the resistor, but primarily because they use standard heat shrink tubing as a "sleeve". You can bend it a little bit but not by much, and if you try to force it you could easily break the resistor leads.

I think this product could be made better if they made it a bit longer and soldered [short] stranded wires to the resistor leads (as opposed to crimping the leads themselves directly to each connector). This would allow for better wire arrangement in the computer case, as well as allow more flexibility in the product itself (so it would be so easy to break). Also, using a shirt piece of nylon sleeving instead of heat shrink would not only look nicer, but would make it much more flexible as well.

That being said, they do what they are supposed to do, and they will work fine as long as you are careful with them.
