review_body:
I've purchased a good number of headphones along the line--wired and bluetooth. As expected, the bluetooth don't sound as good as the wired cans. I an inexpensive Sony bluetooth model, replacing it the the Beats wireless cans. I found the Beats too bass heavy for my likes and rarely put them on. I read a good review of the MEElectronics Runaways on CNET and figured for the price, I could afford to try them out. They arrived earlier today (the shipping and delivery were prompt) and I've tried them out for an hour or so. I have some fatigue from the pressure on my ears (I've always found on-ear to be more of a comfort challenge than over-ear phones), but the pressure was really minimal, and it wasn't any worse (and in some cases better) than other on-ear headphones I'd auditioned.
As for the music, I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of the Runaway sound. For the most part, treble/mid/bass were well balanced, with the mids only occasionally overpowering the higher and lower frequencies. I listened to electric and acoustic pop and rock, solo female voice, classical, klezmer, jazz, and droning speech in a podcast--all sounded quite good. If I were to pick a weakness, it would be heavy rock; the response isn't as full as I'd like, but overall, I am quite happy with these headphones thus far.
Construction seems good. Hinges appear solid. MEElectronics couldn't have cheaped out with a worse carrying case (it's really just a felt bag), but I don't buy headphones based on their packaging. Additionally, the phone will also work wired to the iPod or other source; while I haven't listened this way yet, the CNET review said the headphones sound even better this way.
No problem recommending these so far.

review_headline: Great gadget for limited outlet space
review_body:
This outlet adapter is outstanding for several reasons. The first is that its pronged outlets allow most bulky plugs to fit. Currently I have an extension phone charger plugged in, a rechargeable radio with a bulky plug and my camera charger. All fit fine, and because I have this outlet in the top plug of my double wall socket, I also have my Dyson cordless vac charger with its bulky plug in the bottom. I've used both USB sockets as well, one with my phone and one with my Kindle and both work fine.

A green light shows in the small hole in the middle of the adapter to tell you it's getting power and best of all, the prongs on the back (all three) fold away in case you want to travel with it to expand your options away from home. The prongs are toward the bottom of the unit on the back so if you plug it into the top outlet, it's less likely to conflict with the lower outlet which allows some bulky chargers to fit there as well as standard plugs such as for a lamp. Many products these days have oversized plugs or large bulky chargers, but because of the outlet placements on this unit, more options are available to accommodate them. I have only the one receptacle handy in my home office for temporary use. My other outlets are under and behind furniture where a power strip works for things that are permanently plugged in, but for those items that need to be easily accessible this gadget has really helped me.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-920-K 7.1 Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Well, add me to the growing list of people with HDMI problems!
review_body:
Had this receiver for roughly 1 year, and over the course of the last week, I have had intermittent problems with HDMI output to my TV. I have a DirecTv tuner, PS3 and XBox 360 all hooked up to the receiver, outputting HDMI up to the TV. This setup has worked fine in the past.

The intermittent problems are increasing to the point where a normal TV show is unwatchable. Forget playing a game or watching a movie. This happens on all sources with all devices, and the issue goes away when the source is hooked up directly to the TV over HDMI (isolating the receiver as the cause).

It is too bad, I liked the receiver and the price I paid for it (got it on super clearance at a big box store, I suspect I now know why). Money down the drain! I would have thought that a major name brand like Pioneer would not fail me like this, but here we are. Reading other reviews here, I can see it is time to cross Pioneer off my list.

FWIW, I bought this to replace an old Sony STR-K840P I ran for about 10 years with absolutely no problems. The only reason I stepped up to this receiver was because I added the Xbox 360 and ran out of HDMI inputs on my TV (was running all HDMIs to TV then optical out to receiver), so decided to \\"upgrade\\" to all HDMI. I wish I would have read the reviews here first!

EDIT: Not even 15 mins after I posted this review, I went to my receiver to hook back up the HDMI cables and just \\"live\\" with the problem until I return it to the Big Box store. I must have hurt the receiver's feelings with my review, because the receiver had completely given up the will to live. It was dead, and will not even power up. Dead. Deceased. An Ex-Receiver. No longer pining for the fjords. Bereft of life. 'e rests in peace.

I took the time to find my receipt... Nov-2011 to May-2013. 18 months. RIP

product_title: eStoreimport @ USB 2.0 Hd Video Audio Tv DVD VHS Capture Adapter
review_body:
I bought this product wanting to capture video from old VHS tapes and from programs recorded on my DVD recorder's hard drive. I discovered after a lot of trial and error that it will easily capture any video you play through the device but that any videos that are in widescreen format (16x9) will not be captured in widescreen but will display with black bars on the sides of the videos. So if you're looking for a device that can capture in widescreen format, look elsewhere. Having said that, if you set the video quality to the highest setting, the quality of the recorded video that it does capture is excellent. It will also take up a lot of space on your hard drive (about 2.6 GB for an hour long program). The device has the capability to connect standard composite video (yellow connector), S-video or even component video (red, green & blue connectors) if the device your recording from has any of those outputs.

The biggest downside to this product is that it is a generic product. That is, it does not have a company name or brand or web site that you can go to for support. Also, the software bundled with it, DVR 2.5, by Honestech, is an older product (2009) and is not even listed on the Honestech web site. When I contacted Honestech about the software, they responded that I would need to contact the device manufacturer for support because it was created for this device! So, to sum up, you have no support with this product. You're on your own! If all you want to do is copy VHS tapes to your hard drive it will do that. You'll need another program to edit and burn to DVD and if you need technical support, you're out of luck. I'm returning it to the seller for a refund.

review_body: I ordered this item to install in my 2005 Honda Accord EXL V6.  I have absolutely no background in any type of car installation like this, so all of this was new to me.  I bought this product, this trim removal tool - [[ASIN:B002LE8CPS Pro.Fit International DM-40-22 Dash Trim Removal Tool]], and a premium monoprice RCA cable - [[ASIN:B0094A1F3S Monoprice 3ft Premium 3.5mm Male Stereo TRS Plug to Two RCA Male Plug Cable - Black]].  I wanted a tough cord that would last me the lifetime of my car, and I believe this will work perfectly.    This video was perfect for helping me take out the inside dash trim and compartment:  [...]    The bad part about my car was that the factory radio pin connections were facing away from me.  I had to take out the initial XM radio pin connection, which was fairly difficult with barely any room to pull away from yourself.  After that was done, putting the correct PIE HON03 connection in the now empty port was fairly difficult too.  Mainly again - there wasn't really any room to spare turning the cable around to connect to the now empty port.  After some frustration and cut up fingers, everything was in the right place.  Remember the other end of the Y connection needs to connect to your old XM radio pins to maintain your XM.  I then just lodged the PIE HON03 in the back left corner of open area, drilled a hole in my compartment to put the RCA cord through, and put all paneling and screws back.  Now everything works great and the sound is much better than any FM transmitter!  You can connect any type of audio source with a 3.5mm jack.    So far I love this product and I hope it lasts!

product_title: Sony Bluetooth Wireless Speaker system
review_body:
This is a pretty cool device for a lot of reasons. The wireless streaming from your Bluetooth device allows you to use a powerful 20 watt speaker system to blast out music or have a powerful augment to your phone's speaker capacity. You can also plug your music device directly into it provided you have a male/male plug to use. It also has USB capability for charging your device, which is kind of cool, but also probably creates issues of draining the speaker's battery while charging the device sending info to it.

The design is simple; a latch slides over to release the kickstand, behind which hides the power and input buttons. There is a button for two varying speaker sound qualities (kind of a bass boost, if you will) so you can chose the best sound for your liking. It is a bit heavy at roughly 5 lbs., but it's pretty well balanced once you find a place for it. It comes with a storage case that would be even better if it had a handle or strap. It also comes with the charger and it seems to hold a charge for a while (the specs say 8 hours), although I don't use it continuously...which is part of my logic below.

This novel device has good potential for a group phone chat, as a music source during a social gathering, or simply to play your music through in your home (or car, or boat, or...). However, I can't say that it's worth the price because it doesn't really add much of value to my life. The price tag simply seems too high to me and there are other, cheaper methods to provide speakers to one's mp3 player or smart phone. It's clever and cool, and sounds good, but the price makes it a luxury I could do without.

product_title: Razer Goliathus Control  (Fragged)
review_headline: Cloning and stretching, yes. Dual desktop, no.
review_body:
From the product description:

\\"The SP122DP2DVI DisplayPort(r) to Dual DVI(r) Multi Monitor Spanner Cloner is an innovative, external multi-display adapter that allows you to add 2 DVI displays to your desktop or laptop from a single DisplayPort source. The DisplayPort to 2x DVI expansion module lets you combine 2 DVI monitors as one display, at a maximum resolution of 3840x1200, to make the ultimate wide screen desktop. The DP to dual DVI can also clone your primary display and functions as a DisplayPort to dual DVI Video Splitter.\\"

\\"The operating system will automatically detect the expansion module and either clone/mirror a single image on both displays, or span the image across both displays. To change the display setting/mode, change the display resolution via the operating system's display properties. To use Clone/Mirror mode, set the display resolution to equal or less than the maximum resolution of the smallest connected display. Set the display resolution higher to use Span Mode.\\"

REVIEW: For best experience, I would strongly suggest using two monitors of the same size. The OS will detect a single monitor that is twice as wide as the connected devices. Both monitors must use the same orientation. Maximizing a window will cause it to span both monitors. You should be adept at docking windows to half screen width before considering this purchase. (On Window 7, press the Win+Left Arrow, or Win+Right Arrow to dock windows side by side.)

product_title: FiiO E6 Portable Audio Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: Nothing fancy and it works great for my needs
review_body:
Simple and compact device that does the job.

I live in an apartment and have thin walls so this allows me to listen to movies at a good volume at night while in bed. My bedroom shares a common wall with a neighbor so I have to watch my noise levels.

I use my FiiO E6 to boost the signal from my Roku 2 up to line level (note, the new Roku 3 has a built in headphone jack in their newly redesigned remote controllers- so this usage I'm describing is no longer necessary). This allows me to listen to movies at louder volumes without disrupting other people.

It is nothing fancy and works easily straight out of the packaging. Plug it in with the USB cable to your computer to fully charge it and then use it to bring a signal up to line level.

Sound quality is decent to my ears. Certain bassy sounds can get distorted at times. I have not messed with the settings at all so I don't know if this can be corrected or not. It was only a couple times so far so it doesn't seem like a big enough reason to tweak the stock settings.

Charge lasts for several hours. I haven't actually had it die on me yet except for when I've fallen asleep and left it on. So I'm not sure how long it truly lasts. I've watch several hours of movies/tv on a single charge.

I've read about one of the suppliers here selling cheap dangerous (potential fire hazard) knockoffs of this model. There is information around here and on the internet about what to look for. I believe that mine is real based upon the information on the web and I've had no problems with my unit.

Balanced Sound

Long Battery Life

Questionable Build

A Bit Too Tight

Poor Packaging

Hold the power button for a few seconds: Turns on (blinking blue light)
Continue holding the power button after it turns on: Pairing mode (flickering light that alternates between blue and red)

product_title: Midland HH50 Pocket Weather Radio
review_body:
I went to Minnesota's Boundary Waters in June 2012 and took this radio with lithium batteries in it.
My group of 4 was able to be ready for the three very bad storms as they came through during our trip.
The radio worked well \\"remember to extend the antenna\\" and our signal was good everywhere we went.
Having the reports at hand we knew when to move and when to stay (hunker down) in regards to our camps.
The Boundary Waters storm are as wild as the environment so having knowledge of what weather is coming is helpful.
The radio report told us that an extremely strong system was coming so we decided to get out of the \\"waters\\" 2 days early before we became stranded.
We left camp and got off the water as it started to rain and get dark.
The next day, Duluth was flooding and lightning and winds were heavy, had we been in the Boundary Waters during that three days, I don't know how we would have survived.
I gave the radio to my friend who will be returning and purchased a new radio for my use and another for my 83 year old Aunt who loves it's simplicity.
Our story and lots of pictures are on the outdoorsmichigan.com website.
If you are healthy, you must put this trip on your bucket list to visit this beautiful and wild wilderness at least once in your life....

product_title: Micca Slim-HD 1080p Full-HD Portable Digital Media Player w/ 2.5-Inch HDD Drive Bay
review_headline: It's no XBMC, but it works.
review_body:
Let me just say it up front: I wish this thing were running XBMC rather than the built-in, barebones GUI it has. While the Micca Slim-HD does indeed play every file I throw at it, and I can't complain about the size, shape, weight, or playback efficiency, I have to say the GUI is just plain ugly. Bland. Lifeless. It can't even support thumbnails properly.

If this thing had the ability to run XBMC it would be awesome. Five stars-- No, Six stars! It would rock. As it is, though, it just stands at \\"very good\\" and not \\"amazing\\".

I know. If wishes were horses then school lunches would have meat. Or something like that. Either way, I'm not going to give this thing a bad review because of what it isn't. I just wanted to say: It's SO close to awesome that it kind of hurts.

So here's the basic rundown: The Micca Slim-HD plays your media files. It does it well. It does it in HD if they're HD to begin with. It has a remote control, can hold a hard drive of your choosing, can use external storage via USB, and has a card slot. It really does handle every media type I've tried thus far. And it's small.

The Good: Plays everything. Lets you use your own hard drive. Supports many types of storage media. Simple to use.

The Bad: Crummy remote control. Boring, bland user interface.

The Ugly: Nothing ugly to report, thankfully. The remote gets close to being \\"ugly\\", but it's passable enough to be classified as just \\"bad\\" for this review. The user interface is functional, so I can't lump it here, either... But it is still \\"bad\\" in my book.

The Final Verdict: If all you want to do is play your media files, the Micca Slim-HD is a great choice. The no-frills interface might be a bit of a bummer, but it makes up for that somewhat in versatility and compact size.

I give the Micca Slim-HD Four Stars. I docked it one star because of the bland interface and mushy, tiny, not-very-sensitive remote control, but the fact that it doesn't flinch no matter what files I throw at it makes it a solid four-star device.the fact that it doesn't flinch no matter what files I throw at it makes it a solid four-star device.

product_title: Toshiba DR430 1080p Upconversion Progressive Scan DVD±RW Recorder w/USB & HDMI (Black)
review_body:
I'm pleased with the DR430 after a couple months of recording programs from satellite broadcasts, especially movies. It is replacing a Sony RDR-GX355. One drawback of the DR430 compared to the Sony is the limited number of recording speeds if you are recording movies and maximizing disc space with quality. The Sony has 8 speeds and the DR430 has only 4. However the Sony takes only a standard RCA-jack input from my satellite receiver which limits picture quality.

product_title: Xmi UNO XAM14 Capsule Speaker
review_headline: Small in Sound and Size, Nice Looking
review_body:
X-mini UNO XAM14-GM Mono Capsule Speaker - Gun Metal

There are a lot of things to like about this capsule speaker. First all the Gun Metal color is a lot sleeker to look at than the pictures show. It's darker and works pretty well with black. The size is pretty amazing. The only thing that keeps this from being a really portable device, aside from the nano speakers, is the USB and audo cord attachment. Fortunately, the little cloth bag helps with this regard. It looks really nice an travels well. The battery life seems pretty amazing too. I played this thing off and on all day and it never ran out of juice.

The not so good:

When I hold it in the palm of my hand, you can certainly feel the bass, but even just sitting with it on a surface nearby, I can barely hear it. I played around with the Altec and my Soulmate speaker to see if I could get a good comparison. Over time, the Soulmate has grown on me, the rich bass from that system blows this one out of the water. The problem is... the price points are not even close where the two should really be compared. For the price, this does really well, I was just expecting more based on the overview and the description.

I do want to note that the guide is pretty bad. I mean it's tiny, and some of it has very little words so much as pictures with a slash through it indicating you can power through the USB port but not play sound via the port alone, you must also plug in the cord into the audio port. I understand companies want to save on printed material... but come on, a mini guide for a mini-speaker... they could have gone a little extra.

I must say I am intrigued with the idea of daisy chaining these things to get more sound. I don't have multiple devices right now, but perhaps in the future I will get a chance to see if a few of these might make a nice little set-up in a small space.

Audio is not a hobby or passion of mine, and even I was disappointed. If music is really your thing, I think you're going to want to pony up the money for something like the Soulmate over this. Now if your primary goal is to have something portable with a stronger sound than the tiny speakers on your notebook, tablet or mp3 player that looks modern, this is your thing. Visually, this thing is pretty cool; I have to say that one more time at least.

product_title: Sanyo NEW 1500 eneloop AA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries
review_headline: So far, better than expected! 4 pack AA with Charger.
review_body:
I have had these batteries for a couple weeks now. I wanted to test them a little bit before reviewing and am very happy with the results I am receiving thus far. I also have read all negative reviews and most positive reviews for these batteries and for several other brands.

I will start when I first received the batteries. I know they come "pre-charged" however I wanted to be sure they were full and were not partially discharged from storage times. So I charged them immediately after opening the package. I do not have a separate smart charger I only have, and only use the Sanyo charger that came with these batteries. The charger is simple, when you plug it in, it displayed a green blinking light while charging the batteries, then when it was finished it showed solid green lights. I charged it no more than an hour or two after receiving before they were completely full. I then tested with my digital voltmeter and to my surprise they all showed 1.5 volts, not the listed 1.2 volts on the package and what other reviewers have mentioned.

I then put them in the Xbox360 controllers, as that's what I purchased them for. They worked just fine and did not show the "low battery circles" on the controller as other reviewers have stated. The xbox guide shows the full battery icon. I have now been using it a few days a week for a few hours at a time. My alkaline batteries that I was using prior to this, would typically need replacing after about a week, maybe 2 weeks if I was really lucky. These still indicate a full battery on the xbox guide after 2 weeks of use under the same circumstances and use as the alkaline batteries.

I am highly impressed with these batteries and am planning on slowly collecting enough of these rechargeable batteries to no longer have to use any alkaline batteries an solely use these rechargeable batteries (and have enough on hand to have a few extra charged, waiting to be traded out per device that may need the freshly charged ones). Overall I highly recommend these for most any situation, especially game controllers such as the Wii-motes, Xbox 360 controller or any battery operated controller.

product_title: Logitech UE 900 Noise-Isolating Earphones
review_body:
My audiophile journey started with a cheap pair of Koss in-ears (poor fit and boomy bass), followed by Etymotic ER6i's (accurate but anemic bass, boring sound signature, horrible microphonics), Ultimate Ears Super Fi 5 Pro (decent bass, but still not exciting enough in the treble region), Ultimate Ears Triple Fi 10 (boomy bass, sibilant treble, poor fit, but despite all of that my favorite in-ears to date).

My review will focus on a comparison of this IEM to its predecessor the Triple Fi 10 (which I will refer to as TF10 from now on), and will hopefully help you decide whether it's worth it to invest another $400.

Form: UE900 fit is 100% better than the TF10's. The tips no longer protrude straight out from your ears, it now feels more like a custom IEM and \\"sits\\" on the inner part of your outer ear. It also lies flush so that you can actually sleep on your side with these on. In addition, the barrel where the sound exits is much smaller on the UE900 and appears to be 1 medium-sized channel and 1 tiny channel rather than the 2 large channels of the bulkier TF10. With any of the stock silicon tips (S, M, L) the TF10 would slip out of my ear simply because the barrel was as large as my ear canal. The stock Comply T500 foam tips allowed the TF10's to stay in my ears and form a nice seal, but the tradeoff was the treble and high-mids became muffled/veiled. The barrel of the UE900 is much smaller and both silicon and foam tips (Comply Ts500) stay in my ear canal without slipping out.

Sound: There is so much debate about whether driver burn-in exists. Maybe the driver changes its signature or maybe you adjust to the sound, the end result is the same: you listen to these headphones over a period of time and see whether you like it or not. Right out of the box the UE900 retain the \\"exciting\\" sound of the TF10's. The TF10's were somewhat harsh in the highs (with silicon tips), very veiled in the mids (with foam tips), and boomy in the lows (sometimes headache-inducing). My least favorite aspect of the TF10's were the mids. With vocal songs I felt like there was always a curtain between my ears and the voice no matter how deeply I tried to insert the TF10's. The UE900's has less harsh highs (I haven't cringed much yet), more prominent mids (though still slightly veiled in comparison to my Sennheiser Momentums), and a 20% reduction in bass quantity (but more comfortable to listen to). In summary the UE900 has a gentle U-shape frequency response rather than the sharp V-shape of the TF10's. The UE900 manages to maintain an exciting sound and appears to be more resolving so now I am actually hearing more details in some of my songs. Keep in mind that the UE900 accomplishes this all with the stock Comply foam tips.

Durability: As I have only recently received the headset, I can't evaluate how the plastic housing of the UE900 or its braided cable will hold up over time.

Accessories: Not a huge factor in purchasing an IEM. It has a nice magnetic-hinged glossy plastic box, a carrying case, 3 different sizes of comply Ts500 tips, and I think 4 different sizes of silicon tips. It comes with an Apple compatible blue braided cable plus a backup black cable without any remote (a nice touch, as my TF10 cable broke within 1 year)

My music preferences lean toward pop, techno, vocal, and alternative rock. My sources are Galaxy Nexus GSM, Lenovo X230. No amp required.

product_title: Onkyo Integrated Stereo Amplifier
review_headline: Clean minimalist design, future-proof, great price point
review_body: Very pleased that I made the switch from the Cambridge 651A, as this unit's 24 bit Wolfson makes streaming a no-brainer.  The remote is terrible, however you should be using a master one anyway.  Negatives: Have detected transformer noise when not plugged into a power conditioning strip.  The subwoofer LFE out does not have an adjustable crossover setting and Onkyo does not publish what the crossover frequency is. Channel separation is not 100% accurate, as detected by setting the balance entirely to one side and still hearing sound in the "off" channel.  Stereo imagery is moderate at best.  Positives: PM bass is an improvement over traditional Loudness, hi grade build quality, impedence switch is useful for parallel speaker configuration, male vocals sound very realistic without the common bloated bass many other units produce, treble detail is excellent.  The move away from traditional source labels future-proofs the design and allows greater configuration freedom.  If your needs are reliability and simplicity without breaking the bank, you cannot go wrong with this integrated amp.  If you're looking for a more premium sound, look for a unit with a dual mono-block preamp section, a toroidal transformer power supply, and a class A or AB amplifier section.  I'm looking into some offerings from NAD, however their traditional input labels are a deal breaker for me.  I do not own a single CD or vinyl, so I do not want those labels on my amp (along with other legacy mediums such as DVD).  Also, 7 segment displays are an eye sore in the HD era we are in, so a lack of one is another necessity. This unit fits all my prerequisites minus the dual mono and toroidal.

review_headline: A little box with a lot of Boom
review_body:
The school where I work recently gave me the task to find a new sound system for the gym. I was looking for something small and durable but also something powerful that would fit my needs for when I teach to the kids and for extracurricular activities.

Features
This sound system is fairly simple. It has an iPod dock for any apple device with a 16 pin connector (not iPhone 5 compatible yet) and an audio input at the back. You can also connect wireless devices via Bluetooth.

In terms of looks it look very sleek. The one I got is all black with a red beats by Dre logo on the front (There is also a white and grey version available). Both side of the device are equipped with handles for easy portability. The system can be plugged to a power outlet or, if you want to use it on the go, you will need six D-cell batteries (Seems like a little much doesn't it?) that can be place in a latch under the boombox.

Performance
Like most products made by the company, this one delivers a good sound quality. I can easily project sounds through the whole gym without any problems. The sounds does become a little distorted at a higher volume but nothing really major. The reach of the system when connected to Bluetooth is far better than I ever could of expected. I can leave my phone in my office (which is at the other end of the gym) and still get a
great connection. The remote control that came with the device on the other can not reach that far.

The beats by Dre Beatbox is also very sturdy. It received quite a few hits in the last month and there is no sign of malfunctions yet.

The Price Tag
The price tag is a little high (399.99 on sale when i got it) but the quality is there so it is worth it. Can you get something similar for a lower price? Probably, the features are basic and pretty much standard on every recent model.

The Bottom Line
Powerful, durable and great looking, this product is reliable and a great acquisition for any music lover as long as you don't mind a small jab to the wallet.

product_title: iHome iDL45BC Dual Charging Stereo FM Clock Radio with Lightning Dock and USB Charge/Play - Black
review_body:
iHome has so many versions of this \\"Home System\\" that I've lost track. Most of them are within this price range and under one-hundred dollars. I have to say, this is probably the best, most basic, `all you need' model yet. It will take your iPod, iPhone or iPad. Sure, the clock works great with two alarms and the capacity to set to weekdays or weekends or a combo. The clock sets itself, as well as the time and calendar with a simple click of the `clock' button. You also are suggested to `update your iD45 firmware'; meaning your iHome settings are upgraded to the latest devices, meaning your clock is readily updatable without waiting for those early bugs to be fixed. You can listen to your \\"device\\", the radio (AM/FM) and other portable devices through the auxiliary input in the back. It also has that `snooze' button or `naps' that go for (9) settings up to (2) hours. It's just easy to operate.

The sound? It is the best so far, as now there is an equalizer allowing you to set the treble, bass and balance. PLUS, 3D Sound. This feature is new, but the difference is remarkable, as you really get a fuller sound compared to all other iHome docks I have heard. It will fill a small room without any distortion.

The top of the unit is `flush' with the buttons, making it look sleek and the Flexible 30-pin connector is long enough that you can leave your iPhone/iPod case on and it still works. An Otterbox would be too large. All these units have that proprietary power plug that hangs so you have to place it on the bottom of the two wall sockets. It also has a silly wafer-thin remote that you can lose the first day, but...

The look is good, the sound is great and the use is easy. This is a keeper, finally.

review_headline: VERY Impressive.  Emotiva has made me a fan of their amps.
review_body:
I recently learned that you can never have too much amplification, that the quality of amplification makes a huge difference and also that the way amplification is measured is different from manufacturer to manufacturer. I decided to buy a new high end receiver and mistakenly purchased a receiver instead of separates-which I quickly regretted. I wondered why my speakers didn't sound better with music? Why they did not sound as robust as I thought they would? I was using a 100W per channel Rotel Reciever which is very high end and it sounds amazing for Home Theater. I decided to give the Emotiva XPA-3 which provides 200W per channel into 8 ohms for 3 channels and see if that would give me the boost I needed while using the Rotel essentially as a Pre-Amp for the front 3 channels. Of course, this thing is a beast and I had a hard time getting it in to the basement on own at close to 60 pounds!

When I plugged it in and played John Mayer's Continuum, I was stunned by the depth and soundstage of the music as well as new detail that I didn't hear before. Now, I have Bowers and Wilkins Tower speakers so they are power hungry and you could tell right away that they loved the Emotiva. I then played the opening scene of James Bond's Quantum of Solace with a car chase. Holy Cow! I then went back to music and listened to some Michael Jackson and then Black Keys. In less than an hour-I decided I was going to be using my expensive Rotel receiver as a Pre-Amp on the front 3 channels. This thing has amazing true power and I had heard that Emotiva will make your speakers sing-And that is exactly what this does. You will hear things like you never have if you are going from 100W to 200W per channel. A HUGE difference. Keep in mind the Rotel is pretty high end and the Emotiva at 200W per channel is a no brainer. Detail is very, very impressive as well. At the current price point-if you need to boost your front 3 channels-There is nothing even close to this that you can get this good in this price range not to mention the great 5 year warranty. I was skeptical as I briefly had an Emotiva Pre-Amp that I thought was only so-so, but their X Series Amps? Wow.

The reason the item gets 4 stars is because I actually do not love it for the center channel. I have found the voice on my Bowers and Wilkins center speaker to actually lack a little depth and \\"Breathiness.\\" It left me wanting more although it was very good. Perhaps I am being very picky-but I was surprised that it was not better and I tested it with a number of different movies such as Inglorius Basterds and Casino Royale that have a lot of dialogue. When it came to action scenes, it is a monster-but the delicate voice doesn't quite cut it so I ended up Bridging an NAD Amp in to Mono which is 300W in to 8 ohms and pairing that with the Emotiva 2 channels and have the center channel of Emotiva not currently powering anything. Not ideal, but I am picky.

Overall I am extremely happy with my purchase and would look toward Emotiva again if I ever needed an AMP. product_title: Klipsch Image Noise-Isolating Earphone
review_body:
I have owned the Klipsch S4i earphones for some time and like them alot for the price. I have therefore been curious about the X10's, but didn't want to spend $300+ for a set of earbuds. When the price recently fell to $90, I couldn't resist. Except for the lack of iPhone controls, the X10's are superior to the S4i's in every way. The highs are smoother, the bass is tighter and a bit stronger, and the midrange detail (one of the S4i's real strengths) is outstanding. The X10's also fit better than the S4i's, possibly due to their very small size. The cables are also a little thicker, and the case is much, much nicer.

One cannot expect a huge soundstage from tiny earbuds, but the X10's soundstage is surprisingly good. It is easy to locate different instruments in space, and the music doesn't seem to be playing only in my head. What I especially appreciate is how the dynamics of orchestral music really come alive. Everything sounds really solid, even at very high volume, with no noticeable distortion. Mind you, I'm driving the X10's with my iPhone and a desktop Mac, not an expensive sound system. I don't know whether adding a moderately-priced portable headphone amp would make the X10's sound even better, but it's an interesting question.

Although I have decades of experience listening to high-end audio systems, I have relatively little experience listening to in-ear headphones; but the X10's have definitely made me a happy camper. It's hard to imagine that anyone would be disappointed in these at the current selling price of $90. My guess is that the only reason the X10's are being so heavily discounted is that most buyers are going for the X10i (currently selling for $300) to get the iPhone controls.

product_title: ADS Instant FM Music
review_headline: USB Analog FM Reciever/Tuner for both MS Windows and Linux
review_body:
Works really good in Windows 8, including Linux using the radio_usb_si470x module/driver.

I just found mplayer's \\"-nocache\\" might be required when using a fifo file for USB Audio devices leading to buffer under-runs. Users can also try \\"mplayer -ao alsa\\" instead of using pulseaudio.

Windows 8, if you listen hard enough, you'll likely hear some gaps or skipping, but the audio seems to be made quite subtle or well blended. As such, you won't notice it much unless you're paying attention to details. (After using Linux mplayer's \\"-nocache\\" option, audio seems to be of better quality under Linux versus Windows.)

Since this product uses a Silicon chip, similar to the \\"Silicon USB FM Radio Reference Design USBFMRADIO-RD\\", Silicon offers a software radio which works adequately with this \\"ADS Tech Instant FM Music\\" device. Another feature with the Silicon software, it offers to upgrade the firmware on this ADS Tech device which may fix some pops or skipping.

For Linux (mplayer) users using the command line with the provided \\"/dev/radio0\\" device file, this device can be easily managed by adding some lines to your bashrc file. The below lines contain a small clipping of my favorite stations within Fairbanks, Alaska. You may need to enable the \\"lirc\\" Configure/USE flag to allow mplayer to use remote commands, while also creating a \\"$ mkfifo ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\" and using \\"-input -slave\\" command line options.

$HOME/.bashrc
alias mplayer-103.9=\\"mplayer -ao alsa -quiet -slave -input file=${HOME}/.mplayer/input -radio adevice=hw=2:arate=96000:channels=88.3-88.3_KZVV,88.7-88.7_WGCN,89.9-89.9_KUAC,91.5-91.5_KSUA,91.9-91.9_KHRI,93.5-93.5_KDJF,94.3-94.3_KWDD,95.9-95.9_KXLR,96.9-96.9_KYSC,98.1-98.1_KWLF,100.3-100.3_KJNP,101.1-101.1_KAKQ,102.5-102.5_KIAK,103.9-103.9_KTDZ,104.7-104.7_KKED -rawaudio rate=96000 radio://14/capture\\"
alias mplayer-usbrad-cmd-95.9=\\"echo 'radio_set_channel 8' > ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\"
alias mplayer-usbrad-cmd-96.9=\\"echo 'radio_set_channel 9' > ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\"
alias mplayer-usbrad-cmd-100.3=\\"echo 'radio_set_channel 11' > ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\"
alias mplayer-usbrad-cmd-down=\\"echo 'radio_step_channel -1' > ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\"
alias mplayer-usbrad-cmd-up=\\"echo 'radio_step_channel 1' > ${HOME}/.mplayer/input\\"

NOTE: I have yet to add the \\"-nocache\\" to my bashrc file and omitting the \\"-ao alsa\\". The \\"-rawaudio rate=96000\\" is definitely required, else mplayer will exit trying to play at a higher rate.

Pros:
1) Provides adequate FM radio reception.
2) Usable in both, Linux and Windows.
3) Outputs 96000 Hz audio rate. (Almost 2 x 48000Hz.)

Cons (Mostly Windows related):
1) The Windows software radios tend to forget the saved stations.
2) Windows software radios tend to have very tiny GUI buttons and sliders.
3) Windows 8 Media Center does not recognize this radio tuner, as this device does not provide a TV Tuner device! (There is a third party plugin, but it costs money.)
4) There are third party software radio applications such as Icecat, but they require finicky EMail registration, and provide no useful additional features and appear more troublesome to navigate versus the already adequate ADS Tech and Silicon software radios. (If I'm not mistaken, these third party software radio applications are meant for LCD panels for vehicles, but still are difficult to navigate!)

Bottom line, the device is decent, but if you'd like a little bit higher quality, then you'll have to buy a more than $100 Hauppauge PCI/PCIE TV tuner device providing the analogue FM reception. Or wait for another 5-10 years for digital FM radio to evolve.

Here's a few more command line incantations piping the unsampled output from mplayer to aplay. APlay has the ability to use libsamplerate, providing possibly better resampling than mplayers resampling? (Use -ao ifyou're using ALSA and not Jack)

Just pipe the audio to test.mpg file for later review/comparison tests:
$ mplayer -ao jack -quiet -slave -input file=${HOME}/.mplayer/input -radio adevice=hw=1:arate=96000:channels=88.3-88.3_KZVV,88.7-88.7_WGCN,89.9-89.9_KUAC,91.5-91.5_KSUA,91.9-91.9_KHRI,93.5-93.5_KDJF,94.3-94.3_KWDD,95.9-95.9_KXLR,96.9-96.9_KYSC,98.1-98.1_KWLF,100.3-100.3_KJNP,101.1-101.1_KAKQ,102.5-102.5_KIAK,103.9-103.9_KTDZ,104.7-104.7_KKED -rawaudio rate=96000 radio://14/capture -ao pcm:file=/dev/stdout > test.mpg -af-adv force=2 -quiet -really-quiet

Pipe the audio to aplay stdin directly:
$ mplayer -ao jack -quiet -slave -input file=${HOME}/.mplayer/input -radio adevice=hw=1:arate=96000:channels=88.3-88.3_KZVV,88.7-88.7_WGCN,89.9-89.9_KUAC,91.5-91.5_KSUA,91.9-91.9_KHRI,93.5-93.5_KDJF,94.3-94.3_KWDD,95.9-95.9_KXLR,96.9-96.9_KYSC,98.1-98.1_KWLF,100.3-100.3_KJNP,101.1-101.1_KAKQ,102.5-102.5_KIAK,103.9-103.9_KTDZ,104.7-104.7_KKED -rawaudio rate=96000 radio://14/capture -ao pcm:file=/dev/stdout -af-adv force=2 -quiet -really-quiet -autosync 30 | aplay -

(Autosync option is utilized to attempt to reduce any slight stuttering with audio playback. Very minor sync issue might occur during piping the stream to aplay.)

After owning other DJ oriented portable headphones such as the Audio-Technica ATH-M50, Allen & Heath XD-53, and the Audio-Technica Proo700MKIIANV, I can very safely say these are the best portable/DJ headphones available today.

The construction is the most solid and well-built I have ever seen in my life. An insanely flexible and durable headband with metal 'wings' to hold the shielded cups, and each cable provided being made of tough kevlar.

The accessories are fantastic, from the highly custom shields, to the several available cables, to the color of the overall headphones themselves.

The sound is stellar. A more open soundstage than you would normally expect from a closed-back headphone, with a surprising level of detail and instrument separation. The bass is rich and deep and hearty, and certainly not overpowering. The mids are slightly recessed but still pack a good punch, and the highs have a wonderful roll-off so that they sound sound harsh. A perfect sound signature for DJ's and serious portable headphone fans alike.

The only thing I could possibly want more is better detail/more forward mids, but that's about it. A nearly perfect headphone, ladies and gentlemen. Do NOT hesitate to purchase the M-100's if you're considering it.

Please see my video review of these headphones for far more detailed reviews and to hear many more of my thoughts on the headphones. Simply search \\"M-100 Review\\" on YouTube, and it will be the one by me, Leon.

V-MODA has struck gold.

~Leon Dota

product_title: Logitech Li-ion Battery for Harmony One Remote 880 890 720 900 (LATEST VERSION))
review_headline: White Label 930mah is what you want!
review_body:
This is not a verified purchase review since I bought mine elsewhere. But just wanted to say this is exactly what you want. There seems to be confusion among people. Some are not happy because they think they should be getting the blue label 950mah version. Well, that version is faulty and many users, including me, have experienced the swelling/bloating issue. You'll need to pry out your battery. Here's a tip to pry out your battery... Remove the battery cover. Cut an expired credit card in half lengthwise and slide it under the battery that's still stuck. Using the credit card and some jiggling, try and slide the battery out as much as possible. Then use an A clamp to grip the entire remote. Make sure the point of pressure is resting on the exposed part of the battery. Cut a cardboard paper or get some cloth to layer the side with the buttons so your clamp doesn't scratch your remote. Once you have the A clamp on properly, just slide out your remote. The clamp will be holding firmly onto the battery while the entire remote will be sliding out. It won't slide out entirely, but just enough so you can undo the A clamp and remove the battery manually.

If you contact Logitech, they will most likely send you a white label 930mah version since this one does not have the swelling issues.

product_title: Yurbuds Ironman Inspire In-Ear Earbud Sport Headphones with TwistLock Technology Earphones, Sweat Resistant, White
review_headline: Awful sound takes on a new meaning with these headphones
review_body:
I love high end headphones. I also love to workout, and am aware that I destroy my headphones on a regular basis, so I'm not bringing a $300 pair of IEMs with me to the gym. I usually go with a cheaper pair around the $30 range because I know I'll ruin them sooner than later. I know I'm giving up sound quality, but I figure it's no big deal, because I'm focusing on the workout, and the music is just there in the background.

Until I met these.

They sound so bad. SO VERY BAD. I get better sound quality out of the disposable headphones they give you on airplanes. The highs are non-existant. The bass and the mids are so muddled. Stuff some cotton balls in your ears, then try to listen to music through a soup can, and you get the idea of what these sound like. They are so bad that I just turn off my music during my workout and listen to whatever crappy house music my gym is blaring on the loudspeaker. I cannot concentrate on what I'm doing, they are that bad! And no, you won't get used to them. I've been using them for 3 months and no change.

So why 3 stars instead of 1? Because sound aside, they are the perfect headphone for the gym! I have small ears and find most buds extremely uncomfortable. I forget these are even in, they fit so well. They do not come out. And they are sweat proof. The fact that I'm still complaining about them 3 months later says something about their toughness. I've usually destroyed them by now.

So I'm torn. I don't want to go back to a pair of headphones that slip and fall out, but I cannot listen to these for a second longer. Hopefully the silicon covers over the buds can be transfered to a different pair of headphones that don't sound so terrible.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I was skeptical to buy this remote because there were mixed reviews on Amazon and all of the “professional” installers told me to avoid Logitech remotes. I figured I’d give it a shot before I committed to buying a $600 setup that the pros were trying to talk me into. One I received it I let it sit in the box for about 3 months before I set it up because I thought it would be a major hassle. Once I got fed up with using 3 remotes and spending 5 minutes teaching every babysitter how to use the entertainment system, I finally cracked it open and set it up.
It was surprisingly easy to set up the remote. Simply download the software on your PC, hook up the remote with the provided cable and go through a series of menus to tell what devices you use and for what. The remote is activity based so if you want to watch TV you just press “watch TV” and it will turn on the TV, input source and AV receiver if you have one. Also works with my TIVO just as well as the old TIVO remote did.
All of my components are in a closed cabinet so I would have to keep the door open to use the old remotes. Not anymore. The RF blasters work great.
The only negative is that sometimes when switching from activities (DVD to Watch TV) the input on the TV doesn’t change. Not a big deal as you can work each component separately with this remote and switch it manually. Also the software is a little cumbersome when adding/deleting devices but manageable with some patience.
All in all it is a good universal remote and, I think, worth the money. The pros all tried to talk me into much more expensive options, some of which only they can program with software that is only available to professional installers.

product_title: Panasonic TY-EW3D3MU 3D Active Shutter Eyewear for Panasonic 3D HDTVs (Medium) (2011 Model)
review_headline: So much more comfortable than the knock-offs. For 2011, NOT 2012 TV's
review_body:
I originally purchased a well regarded pair of less expensive 3D glasses for my 2011 model Panny Plasma. They work well, and numerous reviewers claimed they were as good as, or better than the name brand glasses. It is true that they work well and were a fraction of the cost of the Panasonic brands, but then I found these Panasonic brand name glasses via Amazon Market and purchased them for the same price as the much cheaper knock-off (approximately $28.00). They were listed as \\"Used-like new.) I have to say that the comfort level of the Panasonic brand is markedly better than the knock-offs. They seem to weigh almost nothing, are comfortable on the nose, with or without prescription glasses, and can be comfortably worn for extended times. Viewing angles and distances seem very good. However, as seems to be true with any 3D system, the glasses definitely darken the picture and I could not imagine watching more than one movie without taking an extended break from the 3D experience. Definitely, watching some, not all, 3D movies is a great experience, but the movie needs to be fairly bright to begin with for a more enjoyable experience. 3D TV still has a way to go. I would like to add that the seller was exceptional, responding within seconds to my e-mails and prepared to remedy any problems. however, the glasses work perfectly. Also, because they are Panasonic brand, if you are using a Panasonic TV you have absolutely no special connections to make. Simply charge 30 minutes before the first use, turn on your movie, and turn them on. They connect immediately. They even allow you to watch a 3D movie that everyone else is watching in 3D in 2D if doing so is more comfortable for you. I would never pay the MSRP for these, but at $28.00 to $30.00 they are reasonable.
PLEASE REMEMBER...These are for the 2011 models and NOT for the 2012 models. The 2012 models use an entirely different means of communication with the glasses and do NOT work with this model.

review_headline: Great system but no more updates
review_body:

We had a problem with the remote right after we bought it. I contacted the company, and they replied promptly and had me ship it to them and took care of the problem quickly. I would rate it 5 stars if the company still offered firmware updates, etc.

We love our George. Great sound, easy to use, lots of options, and originally great support. Sadly, the company no longer makes the product and stopped doing updates after 2008. It's a shame that a company and product with such potential went out of business while the companies producing garbage products abound. Our George does not work in the dock with the iPhones we have had, including 3, 3G, and 4S. It will charge the phone, but it won't play the music. It just says, \\"George needs your iPod.\\" Fortunately, purchasing an extra auxiliary cord can fix that problem, as the iPhone does work if it is plugged into the auxiliary jack. (For those who don't know how to do that, just go to any store that carries electronics and get an auxiliary cord. Plug one end into the aux jack on the back of George and the other into the headphone jack on the phone. Press the aux button on the George remote.) If you need to charge and play at the same time, just dock the phone to charge it while it plays through the auxiliary jack.

In addition to the music stored on the phone, we are able to play Pandora this way, too.

One good thing is that at this point, Chestnut Hill still answers questions about the George. I don't know how long that will last, but I appreciate it while it's there. Not that they can do much due to no more updates, but if you just have basic questions or problems after purchasing it, they are currently still available for basic support.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V573 7.1-Channel Network AV Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Some background on myself. I'm a Nashville trained Audio Engineer with 12 years experience in both live audio and studio tracking/mixing. I'm a bit of a stickler when it comes to the output quality of my home systems.

I bought this to replace a brand new Onkyo HT-RC460 which had a failed HDMI card within two weeks of ownership. Talk about a blessing in disguise!

The Onkyo was an okay replacement for our standard living room setup. This was not going to be for my home theater, but this Yamaha receiver sounds spectacular. The By far the best I've tested in this range. I've had a $1200 Denon in the past and this thing blows it away. How Yamaha has managed this is beyond me. It just seems to have more punch and clarity than Onkyo's or any other brand's offerings in this range. It is also extremely easy to setup and customize.

I have heard some grumbling over the interface and it's block style text. Let me just say I'm coming from Onkyo's gorgeous interface which was great, but lacked a lot of features. The Yamaha block system is fast, straightforward, and lets you customize to a much high degree of detail. It's a vastly superior system. After using it for a few days, I much prefer it to the \\"pretty\\" interfaces that Onkyo and others offer.

The iOS remote app is almost perfect. It's smooth, fast, does what it's supposed to and doesn't crash! Yamaha has really put some time into this one. Even more so with the iPad version. It is visually stunning and more than makes up for any lack of beauty in the onscreen UI. The only drawback to the iOS App is that it only gives you the ability to adjust treble & bass. The onscreen interface allows you to adjust specific bands and each speaker, but maybe Yamaha will add that via an update in the future(fingers crossed!)

It's going to be really difficult to not pick up another one of these to replace the Sony unit in my theater.

I highly recommend the Yamaha RX-V573!

product_title: Cowon 16 GB Video Player
review_headline: Very happy with it + USB connection explained
review_body:
I'm happy with my new Cowon C2. Read bellow.

Interface:
I've read a lot of complaints about the interface being "weird" or "unusual" on the web. Well, you have to be wise interpreting these things. People were saying that the interface is difficult to figure out. No one was saying that the design of the interface is bad and no one was specific about what's weird about it. I thought: "it's an mp3 player, how hard can it be to figure it out?" and I was right. It's not difficult to work with at all. Especially if your mp3 player is a personal thing for you (not just something to push a button on and hear music), then you'll love exploring the interface and learning what's where. It's different than most others, but in a good way. Visually it looks great to me. Not flashy or bold at all. The way I like it.

Battery and a little comparison:
This is my third Cowon, I had and loved an iAudio7 for years. iAudio7 had an insane battery (rated at about 60 hrs and worked close to that in practice) which puts every other mp3 player to shame. C2 is rated at 55 hrs, but you won't listen to music without turning on that screen (which is a lot bigger than that of iAudio7) a few times, so you'll get less than 55. I can't give a number yet (I've had it for 2 or 3 weeks), but I can tell you that it's a decent number.
I've had an iAudio9 for a while too. It's a very good device too. C2 is in a slightly different class, because of a bigger screen and more functions. But anyway, strictly comparing the experience of browsing through your folders and listening to your music and working the control buttons, C2 is on par or slightly better than iAudio7 (and I LOVE iAudio7!) C2 is bigger, which can be good or bad (looking at the screen or putting it in your pocket), but provides a more pleasant visual experience. Plus C2 has a touch screen. All of these three devices have to be removed from your pocket to be handled (on C2 you can program some buttons to do play/pause or volume control when screen is locked.)
Let me just add this little comparison too: I tried an "E series walkman mp3 player" from sony for a few days before getting the C2. You don't expect a sony walkman to have major design issues, right? well, with lock activated, it's on button will get pushed in your pocket repeatedly, which makes the device turn it's screen on to tell you that it's off and you need to unlock it first to turn it on. That will consume all your battery charge quickly if you walk around with it. Can you believe it? Everything else was as good as iAudio9 on that walkman. C2 is much better compared to the walkman with the on button (because you have to push and keep the on button for it to react), but it's not flawless, because it does not have a mechanical lock, like iAudio7 had.
Sound quality seems good to me. I don't listen to a lot of flac and wave files though, and my headphones aren't expensive either (I use 30-40 $ earphones). So I'm not your "audiophile" reviewer, but you wouldn't really need me be one either, Apparantly there is a consensus: Cowon products sound very good.

USB connection:
There is a lot of discussion about how unstable or tight the connection is. I read enough of them to get to the answer (thanks to the great people of internet who help you just because they want to.) It's simple and it works:
1- Pull the cover up, not down (towards the screen not the metal back), which gives you enough room to work with.
2- Hold your device in your hand and push the connector in firmly. There are little bumps on the lower side of the connector. Push until those bumps get to the edge of the hole in the device.
The connection will be very stable and firm.

product_title: Winegard SS-3000 Amplified Indoor UHF/VHF Antenna
review_body:
Winegard SS-3000 Amplified Indoor UHF/VHF Antenna addressed the main problem that I had, I couldn't get CBS and NBC affiliates (only available via VHF in my area) with my much smaller UHF antenna. However, all of the stations that I am receiving are within 12-20 miles of my location. As with any antenna, your results will vary based on the situation that you are attempting to address.

Some background information:

What antenna do you need? I found the web page antennaweb dot org to be very helpful. If you put in your zip code, it will provide a listing of broadcast stations that are theoretically possible to receive in that area. This will also tell you what RF channel those stations transmit on and make recommendations as to which antenna is needed. If you are looking at this review, it probably means that you need an indoor antenna vice an outdoor one. If, after typing in your zip at antenna web you see stations you want that transmit on RF channel 13 or lower, then you will need a VHF antenna. However, if all the channels you are interested in are on RF channel 14 or higher, then you may be able to get by with only a UHF antenna.
Likewise, antennaweb dot org will provide the azimuth and range from your location to the station. This will help you adjust the antenna to get the best reception.

Specifics about this antenna:
So, after checking the web and thinking deep thoughts about the stations that carry your favorite shows (or your ability to get those shows via the web), you find that you need a VHF antenna, this particular antenna might be effective for you. If, however, all the stations that you want are UHF, then you definitely should get a different antenna.

When I initially installed this antenna without the reflector, I lost all UHF stations except for the strongest one. Then I installed the reflector, ran a channel scan on the TV and got back most of the UHF stations that I had lost.

Thisantenna did allow me to get two VHF channels that previously were only available under the best possible conditions.

Summary: This indoor antenna provides very good VHF reception and reasonable UHF reception.

product_title: Sennheiser MM30 Headphones
review_body:
For $40, these are a steal. I've had my pair for almost 6 months and they work just as good as they did when they came out of the box. Sennheiser gives a lifetime warranty, and I don't think I'm gonna be using it anytime soon.

As far as sound quality goes, I can't complain. They are not as good as $100 pairs of headphones, but I've compared them to the HD280, and they are more than comparable. I didn't really know what to expect when I got mine, seeing as they are $40, but I was pleasantly surprised. The bass is nice and punchy, but it strikes a good balance. The bass doesn't distort music like with some other headphones I've gotten, and they also don't sound tinny.

My only complaint is the build quality; when you take them out of the box, they feel like a cheap $5 pair of headphones. The sound controls are a little bulky and aren't sleek/stylish for lack of a better word, and the cord if paper thin. But like I said, I've had these for 6 months and counting, so the cheap feeling construction must not affect reliability too much.

Overall, great headphones. The sound quality is great, and the volume/mic controls are useful, especially when working out. Despite the build quality, I would definitely recommend these to anyone whose in the market for relatively inexpensive headphones.

1. Stretches the image. This is really annoying as you can lose some HUD information. And we did play with all the settings (both PS3 and TV) and it never really got any better. Worse yet, the best it looks is when you use the 4:3 ratio - and it's still stretched inside that.
2. Ghosting. There are some moments in dark areas where you can still see the other players screen. You can eventually block it out but if the other player starts lighting up the screen with explosions, gun fire, etc. it can really get in the way of seeing your image.

Other than those cons it does do the job just be wary that it's not by any means perfected. As cheap as they are, it's worth a buy and see how you like it. product_title: SIIG CE-MT0R12-S1 13-27 Inches Articulating Triple Monitor Desk Mount
review_body:
PACKAGING/ASSEMBLY ISSUES

As I was assembling the mount, I noticed one of the vesa mount plates had no torque at all and sagged downwards. I exchanged the mount for a new one. The second mount I received had to be sent back as well. The holes drilled into the center post were much smaller than the screws provided. I confirmed the size difference with the center pole I still had from the first kit. I suppose I could re-tap and thread the holes or find smaller metric screws, but this is America and if I wanted to make my own mount, I wouldn't have bought a kit from China in the first place. I returned the second kit and got a third replacement. Good news is that the pieces all fit together. Bad news, there was red clay all over the mount and plastic bags that the parts came in. I spent ten minutes wiping the clay from the pieces. Keep in mind, this unit was sealed and new in the box. There was minor scuffing on the plastic caps beneath the clay. The durability test was probably throwing it on the ground.

PERFORMANCE ISSUES

I have three 24\\" VW246H monitors on this rig. The monitors are too big wrap around you, like you would expect when playing an eyeinfinity game. Also, both side monitors are raised about an inch higher than the center monitor. These two elements combined create massive asymmetrical bezels (area inbetween the monitors). I could angle both side monitors downwards and deal with the height differences to correct the asymmetrical bezels, or I could blame China.

PERSONAL NOTES

This is my first and last experience with SIIG. I will save for the XFX model [[ASIN:B0050BOCY4 XFX FXTRISTANDX Triple Display Monitor Stand]]. I'm going to find some clay and return this piece of **** the way they sent it to me!

product_title: Belkin High Speed HDMI Cable, Supports HDMI 2.0 (10 Feet)
review_body:
The product description says: \\"Connect a laptop to an HDTV,\\" and the packaging says the same thing in at least four places, plus a diagram on the back. Kids, this is a regular HDMI cable. If you have a laptop with a regular (Type A) HDMI port, you can use this or any other regular HDMI cable to connect it to an HDTV; you don't need a special cable. (As the package says in two places, \\"Your laptop must have an HDMI port.\\") On the plus side, you can use this here cable for a lot more than just connecting your laptop to your HDTV. You can connect your Blu-Ray player to your HDTV (as Belkin would say, \\"must have an HDMI port\\"). You can connect the HDMI port on your high-definition cable box to your HDTV. You can even connect your Roku to your HDTV assuming they have HDMI ports. Get the picture? It's an HDMI cable.

Protip: There's a Web site called monoprice that will sell you an equivalent cable for one sixth the price of this cable. Just sayin'. But I'll give this cable a good rating anyway because it's a good cable.

Across the years, I was listening to my LP's less and less, because my old Dual 1019, purchased in 1967, had slowly deteriorated to the point where one channel had become intermittent.

I decided to look for a replacement, and after an exhaustive search I decided on the Audio Technica AT-LP-120-USB which I purchased about two months ago

All I can say is WOW! Why did I wait so long!

My LP's sound better than I remember them from 1967! It's such a treat to hear them again! There seems to be a warmth to the sound of vinyl that CD's just don't give.

I highly recommend the LP-120 for casual listeners like me. You won't be sorry!

product_title: Sony ICFC717PJ Nature Sounds Clock Radio
review_body: I have searched for a clock radio that has everything on one package, and to my knowledge, no one makes it.  This has a lot of what I want, such as the projection feature, week-day & weekend dual alarms (wish it was a daily set), temperature display (only has indoor, wish it had outdoor as well), AM-FM radio (wish it had short-wave as well and NOAA weather alert), and dimable display (it has 3 settings, wish it had auto-dim when the lights go out).  Overall, I can live with this radio and it has some nice features.  However, I do wish it offered more of the features I listed above, as well as a couple of other items of note.  Sony should have made the unit a litttle larger to accommodate some of those features listed, as well as being able to accommodate 2 larger speakers instead of the 1 small one it has.  I do agree with several other reviewers that the sound should be better.  The radio reception is outstanding, but the sound is VERY tinny.  My old clock radio that cost a fraction of the price, had much better sound.  But overall, in comparison to what I find on the market, it will work for me until my ultimate radio finally becomes available.  I do love the projection and the inoor temperature features.

review_body:
i already have one of these, so when i needed to put another tv on the wall in another room why wouldnt i get the same one? a third of the price you could pay, but at least half the best buy price.

the product: supports most vesa standard mounting types, i just put a 40" led tv (25lbs) on this mount and it stays up just fine, this mount holds up to 60lbs, my 60" plasma weighs 66lbs so that will give you an idea of how much a tv weighs.

this mount has tilt up and down and side to side with a full motion, i use it when i am in bed and also when i am on my eliptical machine on the other side of the room, i just extend it out away from the wall (about 10 inches) and swing it around so i can see it while i am working out.

it is constructed really well and looks and feels solid, high quality product 5/5.

a really great design in this product is the mounting hole placement, there are only two and they are vertical so you only have to find one stud in the wall to mount it.

uses two screws to mount on a stud, not sure if they are included or not but you can get them at any hardware store, make sure you get screws that are rated for 100lbs or more to be safe, and you can find the stud on your wall by doing one of the following: try a magnet and run it along the wall until it sticks, if it does you have metal studs, you can drill right through them, if your studs are wooden, you can just knuckle tap the wall until the tone changes from hollow to dull, if you live in a newer house the studs should be 16"(center to center) apart in the wall, measure 16" from the left and right of the nearest light switch on the wall (the light switch casing is attached to a stud in the wall, it is either on the right or left of the stud, so you know for sure that the first stud is there),mark a little x on the wall on both marks and tap to see if it sounds hollow, the duller sound should be the stud. if your house is older the studs may be 24" apart. you can buy anchor bolts that will hold a tv on the wall by just going through the drywall, but i wouldnt do that, too risky!. dont be afraid to do it yourself, its easy, you could also run your cable from your box inside the wall up behind the tv, no one will see behind there so it doesnt have to be pretty, just run a level up the wall from the cable outlet and make a small hole and fish for the cable, you can do it!, a plate for the wall costs about $2. good luck! :)

product_title: CyberPower Standby Desktop UPS
review_headline: Wrecked my equipment more than a regular powerstrip, customer service was terrible.
review_body:
Recently I bought this to protect my new rig I bought. I usually just use a regular power strip, but I was afraid of blowing up my new fancy computer. One day I was in my house, doing my regular thing when the power went out. It started doing the loud beeping thing (which by the way, it didn't even keep my computer on like it was supposed to, for even a second) and then I just kinda sat there. I smelt burning, and I was really scared. When the power came back, my computer turned on fine, monitors alright. I was relieved. But instead, it turns out it blew something in my subwoofer because now it didn't work at all (after extensive testing, it is definitely the subwoofer, not anything else, audio jacks, etc.)

It wasn't even a lightning storm, or anything. I've had power outages all the time. So I got kind of angry that it just kind of decided to blow up the circuits in my sub for basically no reason. I set up a warranty thing with Cyberpower. I sent them an e-mail and they decided to tell me to just call them soon. I did all of this within the required 10 day period. I called them, asking about my warranty. The woman on the phone just says "what? WHAT?!!?" as if she were losing service, but she was really angry. I called back after she hung up within 5 seconds of me calling her. It went straight to voicemail after a ring or two. I called her one more time, instead from a different place thinking it was service issues (which I don't usually have, but considered her location) and once again, straight to voicemail.

No followup from them, nothing. Now I have to use a separate powerstrip AND this UPS, because for some reason the battery on the UPS (that didn't even support my computer) is already near dead, and I can't plug in more than a few things into it. It has shut off my computer due to excessive power usage more than 3 times, which is more than the amount of times it's saved me from a power outage (0 times).

I just ended up getting new speakers from a friend because after being shunned that day, it was beyond the 10-day period, AND I just wasn't having it.

Next time I'm going to try to buy from a better company. Considering recently I purchased a router from a company (MediaBridge to be specific), e-mailed them with a question about the router messing up rarely, and they sent me a BRAND NEW ONE NO QUESTIONS ASKED, I can see the difference in customer service that CyberPower was really lacking.

product_title: Antennas Direct
review_headline: One of the best products I've ever purchased!
review_body:
After years of having cable, and always being frustrated with the high bills and nothing to watch (despite the hundreds of channels) my wife and I were both fed up. We mostly use Netflix streaming, blu-rays, DLNA from my home server, etc..., and found we didn't have any real need for cable TV anymore. I bought this antenna and installed it in my attic back in January 2011. We've now had this product for over 2 years, and with the cable bill eliminated it has easily paid for itself many times over. We live 45 miles north of the broadcast towers in Dallas, and the antenna picks up 70 channels. 70 channels may seem like a lot, but once you delete all the junk or foreign language channels the number is more like 26. However, 26 channels for free is plenty! Fox, NBC, ABC, CBS, PBS, CW, ION, Qubo, and all of the other channels in our area come in flawlessly with perfect 1080i or 720p picture quality. My daughter also loves Qubo, and we like the content much more than Nickelodeon, Disney Channel, etc....

One important tip on this antenna (and all attic / outdoor antennas). Be sure to buy a powered amplifier. You need to install it within three or four feet of the antenna inside your attic in order to have a strong signal to every outlet in your house. If you don't have an electrical outlet in your attic there are amps that will allow you to send power up one of the coax jacks in your house, and still be able to use that coax for a TV. Also, I had to install the antenna on the south edge of my attic facing towards the towers down in Dallas to ensure every channel came in strong. Once it's installed though you can forget about it, and just enjoy many years of free TV channels.

With the money saved I also upgraded my cable Internet to their fastest plan of 30 Mbps down / 5 Mbps up. We used to pay $150 per month for cable TV and a much slower Internet plan. Now we only pay $52 (including tax), and receive much faster Internet.

product_title: Electrified ELPLP49 / V13H010L49 Replacement Lamp with Housing for Epson Projectors
review_headline: Inferior quality product - unreliable in Epson 8350
review_body:
I purchased 3 lamps for my Epson 8350 projector, after the original factory installed lamp failed. I live in South Africa, and had the lamps shipped to a trans-shipment company in California, who then on-shipped them to me. I immediately installed one of the lamps. I noticed a yellow tint on the left of the screen, but decided the projector was acting up. I took it to the local Epson agents, who wanted to replace the \\"light engine\\" (at a cost approaching the cost of a new projector). I decided to live with it.

A week later the projector wouldn't switch on (it powered up, but couldn't succesfully \\"strike\\" the lamp). I swopped the lamp for the 2nd one in the batch of 3. It worked. 2 days later, same problem. I installed the 3rd lamp - it wouldn't work. I took a chance and installed the 1st lamp again - which inexplicably came back to life. And so started a pattern that repeated itself every day for the last couple of months (I use the projector as my TV) - I'd try to switch the projector on, the lamp wouldn't strike, I'd swop the lamp for the other working lamp and it would work... until I tried again the next day. This has been going on for months now, and I was convinced my projector was faulty - until a friend on mine suggested I try purchasing a genuine Epson lamp.

2 days ago, I installed the genuine Epson lamp - the projector immediately came to life. Last night I switched it on, and it fired right up. Tonight, same story. The problem was the lamps that had been supplied. Not only do the lamps obviously not agree with the Epson 8350 projector they were supplied for, but out of the 3 lamps, one never worked, and now that I've installed the genuine lamp, the yellow tint on the side of the screen has miraculously disappeared as well.

These inferior quality lamps have resulted in many, many hours of frustration, 2 trips to the Epson agents, and a significant waste of money. I wrote to Electrified before posting my review on Amazon inthe hope that they would do something to make this right - they refused.

Caveat emptor!
