product_title: NXG 6 ALL-WEATHER SPEAKER - OUTDOOR/INDOOR/MARINE -BLACK
review_body:
I'm in construction and last winter we were doing a buildout for a Noodes restrant in State College PA. I was there for the demo. While the demo guys were pulling down walls I noticed some black speakers up in the bar joists. The place we were gutting was a bar and these were above the dance floor. There were around 12 or more of these speakers the last tenant left. I pointed them out to the Demo contractor who has rights to everything he takes out the door. I talked him into giving me 5 of these with the mounting brackets. Brought them home and didn't think much about them until I was finishing a room in my house as a theater. I just purchased a Sony STR DN 1030 Receiver which is a superb receiver which costs like a mid priced unit but the sound and features are way above what I expected. It's a 7.1 system , 145 watts per channel which is unheard of for this priced unit and is usually reserved for the Sony ES series ( elevated standards). Any rate I had already hooked up my very old but superior Jamo BX 200s (circa 1991) for the fronts. A pair of infinity bookshelve speakers 2 way with 8 in woofer. I cur rhe front of these cabinets off leaving about 2" of the sides and neatly built them into my walls for the rears. Also excellent sound. I have 2 subs hooked up as this Sony has an extra assignable Pre out either mono rear or dual sub, which I am using. I have a Jamo 300 powered sub ( love it) on one side and a powered JBL 12 " on the other side. I wanted to take advantage of the last pair of speaker outs. My choices are. A single mono rear, a pair of rear surround, or (new to me) a pair of front HIGH speakers. I love the sound go my Jamo BX 200 s in the front but I thought it would be nice to bring a front signal up to the height of the rear surrounds , mainly for music when I'm walking around it brightens and gives clarity to the front . At any rate, the point of all this is I had no idea of the quality of these 5 free speakers I got from this remodel. I did not want to have sat talkie speakers hanging off of a wall anywhere so I removed the font section where the speakers are mounted, and I removed the crossovers, cut out the drywall near 2 studs in the front and mounted these 2 speakers as built ins. First off I was blown away with the magnets these drivers have. The woofer ag is huge. I've seen cheapo 12 inch speakers with mallet magnets. The magnets are almost as wide as the whole speaker abd there is a magnet on this tweeter which almost looks like a miniature of the woofer! It too is bigger than a silver dollar and about as thick as 4 or 5 dollars worth,
Bottom line is I really lucked out with these and plan on purchasing a few more pairs because I have seen a lot of data lite indoor/outdoor type speakers being a builder and I have never ever seen quality or heard quality like these speakers. I remember talking to a college kids about this bar we were remodeling and they Sid it was really loud in there.
Have total confidence in buying these. I have 5 and plan on at least doubling these!

1) They are not particularly adjustable: I have a small head and these tend to put a bit too much pressure on my jaw after an hour or so of wear. I'm hoping my body adjusts to this in time.
2) I bought these primarily to drown out the noise of the metro that I take every day in the Bay Area (BART) commuting to and from work: while they block out the lower frequency grinding the annoying high pitched whining still persists. They were obviously designed for in-air use to block out low frequency plane engine rumbling, but I think it would be more useful to have a model that could block out a broader spectrum of frequencies for those of us not using these on a plane.

Still, the sound quality is quite excellent as I expect from Bose, and the headphones definitely allow me to feel worlds away when I want to be. Thank you Bose!

product_title: Tecsun CR-1100 DSP AM/FM Stereo Radio (English Manual)
review_headline: Great Bang for the Buck Radio with Quirks
review_body:
This radio performs better than expected in a number of ways, and slightly disappointing in others.

First off, FM tuner selectivity, sensitivity, and freedom from multipath distortion is very good indeed.

Secondly, the AM tuner, while being slightly above average in sensitivity and selectivity, is not the best for noise immunity. It seems as though the DSP gets easily confused by EFI from other digital sources and passes it through the detector and audio, rather than screening it out. The radio seems to eliminate standard AM noise issues very well.

While operation is fairly straight forward, the CR-1100's operation is fairly intuitive, but very poorly documented.

The Aux in/line out seems to be a tap at the front end of the audio amplifier, and if you plug in an auxiliary source (like an iPod) it mixes the IPOD audio with that of the radio if the radio happens to be on, but if you turn off the radio first, the CR-1100 will turn itself on automatically when it detects audio from your iPod, and your sound will be radio free, and clear as a bell with no interference.

Be aware that when listening to the FM radio in Stereo, or an AUX source in stereo, you will only hear the left channel from the CR-1100's speaker. You'll hear both channels when listening through headphones. (When listening to the radio through its speaker, it's best to set the FM tuner to mono (so you'll hear both L & R channels) for best listening enjoyment through the speaker.)

With earphones, at very low listening levels, there can be left/right channel imbalance, as well as a significant diminution of bass output (only at very low listening levels.) (With listening levels being numbered from 1-10, this would only be at listening levels below one)

The audio tone is kind of lightweight for a radio of this size, though I've heard worse, I've heard better as well. Tone is not quite as good as that of the CCRadio 2, but tuning ability is almost as good. Tone quality is also a little better from the Sangean CL-100.

So, ranking for tone quality, from best to worst;
1. Sangean CL-100
2. CCRadio2
3. Tecsun CR-1100.

Radio reception performance is, from best to worst;
1. CCRadio2
2. Tecsun CR-1100
3. Sangean CL-100.

Keep in mind, the CCRadio costs over three times as much, and the CL-100 twice as much as the Tecsun. This radio punches way above its price class.

Build quality seems about average.

Overall, the Tecsun CR-1100 is easily worth the money, warts and all.ng ability is almost as good. Tone quality is also a little better from the Sangean CL-100.

I have been using this indoors, hidden behind the window curtains, and I now receive more channels and more stable signal than three very well-reviewed indoor antennas I used before.

My RadioShack antenna used to get 44 channels from my 16th floor apartment with unobstructed signal. But when I moved to a house in a fairly wooded neighborhood, I needed a new antenna. Here are some more details:

Location: Cleveland area

Antenna placement: at the window on first floor. 5' from the ground. decently wooded neighborhood. the next house somewhat blocking the signal.

Reception: received 27 channels (out of 44 available within 40 miles). Signal is not stable for four of the channels, though. This is way better than the RadioShack antenna that got only 6 channels. MyGica A50 got 10 channels. Winegard FL5000C received 12.

Overall, it does a very good job as an indoor antenna. It has not become an eye sore, being hidden behind the curtain. I have purchased good (well shielded) coaxial cable for use with it.

These actually surprised me because none of my devices support apt-X so I was expecting a decrease in sound quality but I really don't hear any quality loss. There are trade-offs however. I have big ears and these headphones start to hurt after long periods of listening. They also do not eliminate any background noise so if you are primarily in a noisy environment, you may want to consider different headphones. The plus side is that these get very loud.

product_title: Denon Globe Cruiser In-Ear Wireless Headphones
review_body:
Well, I purchased these in DEC12 while on leave from Afghanistan. I originally went shopping for the new \\"Jaybird BlueBuds X,\\" but they were not to be found at any stores near my home. However, I did come across these at Crutchfield, and seeing as how 1) I was intent to get something, and 2) they were geared toward travel (which I was going to be doing) - I decided to give them a shot.

I have to say, it's been a pretty good experience. I haven't had any of the bluetooth issues. Perhaps Denon has remedied the issues? Or, perhaps it's the device others are pairing it to (I've been using it with an iPhone 4).

Second, the sound out of these things if just phenomenal. Seriously, your money won't buy better. On a side note, Denon includes a set of Comply foam tips (same material used for hearing protection ear plugs). These are outstanding! If the included size doesn't fit you perfectly, you can buy other sizes and styles made for these specific Denon ear buds from Comply's website.

Third, the travel features are pretty cool if you will in fact be using these to travel. On my way back to Afghanistan, I used the included cord to hook them up in the plane and enjoy one of the in flight movies - worked like a charm.

However, there are a few drawbacks. They look a bit odd, they're awkward to put on at first (although you get the hang of it after a while), and the battery life is only about 5 hours.

In the end, if I'd come across the BlueBuds X during my shopping trip I probably would have purchased them simply for the 8 hour battery life...but all things considered, I don't know that I would've gotten the superior set of ear buds - particularly considering how well these lend to travel.

product_title: JBL OnTour IBT Bluetooth Wireless Speaker
review_headline: Wow, what great sound for a small speaker!
review_body: Out of all the bluetooth wireless speakers I researched, I decided on this one. And I am not sorry I did.. it's great!  Here is why. I wanted something small, that sounded large, and could fill a large space with great sounding music. I wanted something that did not have to be plugged in. I wanted a bluetooth connection to my mobile devices. I wanted to place the speaker on a wall in the basement to listen to my playlist while working out. This JBL OnTour IBT Bluetooth Wireless Speaker fit the bill perfectly!! A lot of other speakers I researched had bad reviews or could not be placed where/how I had planned. However, I found that this one has a bracket that can be attached on the back to make it stand up. Well I simply ran picture wire through that bracket to hang it on the wall. Woohoo! Instant wall speaker! Once I paired it to my Motorola Droid Razr Maxx and my Xoom tablet, this speaker easily connects every time to either device. And it sounds great! It has a power button on top, and I always turn it off when I'm done, to save batteries. The volume buttons control the volume of the music on my phone, and my phone volume buttons also control the speaker volume. It sounds great at full volume without any clipping or distortion. If you like a thumping heavy base, you won't get it from this (and perhaps not from any wireless bluetooth speaker). But for me, the sound fills the large space very well, and it has a crisp, full sound. At full volume it is hard to believe that such a large sound is coming from such a small speaker!!! So far I have not had any problems with this speaker, and I'm very happy with it. Highly recommended.

product_title: TERK Omni-Directional, Amplified Digital Flat Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body:
First of all, when I read most the of reviews on indoor antennas, most of the comments are not completely related to the antennas themselves. It could be the TV demodulator, the location of your house, the structure of the home or the way you positioned it. So I am writing this review to give you a general introduction based on my own experience.

1. Omi-directional vs. Directional

Directional antenna has higher antenna gain in a certain direction. So if you position it well, you will get better signal. On the other hand, omi-directional antenna normally has a broader antenna pattern and tend to behave the same (if built well) in all positions. Most of the indoor omi-directional antenna is tuned to be 10dBi antenna gain and 3-4 dB less then directional antenna. I live pretty far from the TV station transmitter and there is no way to set up outdoor antenna for me.

2. Amp or no amp?

Most people are not very clear out whether they need an low noise amplifier or not. If you live far from the station, the signal reaching your antenna will be very weak. By using a low-noise amplifier, you can have a better sensitivity of your overall digital receiver, again not just the antenna, your receiver and TV demodulator as well, and you will get more channels. If you live very close to the TV station, you don't need a LNA. If you use one, since it is always on, the signal reaching your TV will be saturated and you will actually lose some channels. [...] will give you a better idea.

3. My experience

First I saw a lot of people prefer the Mohu flap antenna. Then I tried to find the specification of their product and all I got is it looks nice and receive some more channels. My technical knowledge does not convince to spend double my dollars on such a product. I compared a couple of antennas from Fry's, including Terk FDTV2A, RCA 1650 and some Philips antennas. Terk gives me the best experience overall. But I do believeif you position the RCA 1650 well enough, you will get same amount of watchable channels. BTW, I am using a vertical position pointing to north where my TV station transmitter is.

product_title: Sony BDVN890W/Z Blu-ray Home Theater Systems (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great system with a ridiculous flaw
review_body:
Having read all the reviews by other customers leaves me with little more to add; most importantly:

- The system DOES accept and is able to decode Dolby Digital Surround signal from outside source, unlike what's been mentioned in other reviews.

- It also can play all media formats that I've tried to throw at it so far; MKV,M2TS,MP4,WMV,AVI to mention a few.

- Setup was a breeze except for mounting the surround speakers on wall mounts (not included) that you have to provide yourself. If you don't want to do that, buy the higher model (BDV-N990W) which comes with tall boys for the front and surround speakers.

Now to the reason I didn't give it 5 stars:
This state-of-the-art system DOES NOT have a shuffle function!!!!!!!!
I searched thoroughly through the manuals, online, and finally contacted Sony customer support and they confirmed that the shuffle function is only available for the iPhone/iPod only!!
I find it hard to believe that such a great product would be missing one of the most basic functions any $10 media player in the market would have. What were the "designers" of the system (if they could be called so) thinking, just beats me!!!
No shuffle, means you have to manually skip or, the hard way, is to create randomized play lists and save them under windows media player and then play it though the system to get the shuffle effect.
I don't know if this is something that Sony can fix through a future firmware update, but it's definitely a MAJOR frustration that we shouldn't have had to deal with in the first place.
Otherwise, the system delivers all that it promises in an elegant fashion fit for my living room and yours.

The frame however does feel a little tight putting it on the first time, but it seems to adjust to your head-size after a while.

Also battery life is very pleasing, I got around 11 to 13 sessions (I can't exactly remember) of about 40 minutes of playback with my iPhone. It lasted me a week's worth of commuting before I needed to recharge, which was great.

Also if there is one bad thing about the device is probably the padding at the top end of the frame, the protective plastic seems to fray a bit.

All in all, it's a great device to have to listen music to!

product_title: Creative Sound Blaster Axx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone
review_body:
I got this item because I wanted an option besides headphones or my Mac's internal speakers for things like movies or music. I cannot speak to its usefulness as a tool for making calls, videoconferencing, etc.

The item is nice looking. The look and feel of the controls on it is pleasing, and it is fairly responsive. The sound that comes from it is louder and of better quality than my internal speakers, so it suits my needs. I have successfully used it via USB and bluetooth with both my MacBook and my iPhone.

That said, there are some big flaws. The first, out of the box, is that while it is wireless and bluetooth-capable, it has no on-board battery to speak of. So wireless is a bit over-reaching. It basically has to be within a couple feet of my computer at all times in order to be useful. Figure that into your desk-scape. While it would be possible to have it plugged into a power outlet across the room and connect via bluetooth, the item does not ship with a power adapter! So wireless--not so much. (You can purchase an adapter, but that's like selling a bicycle without pedals IMHO.)

Another drawback is that it's difficult, sometimes, to get it to register as the sound output device. I can generally do so successfully, but there are times when I have to restart the computer and sorta power-cycle the speaker (it has no on/off switch per se) before I'm able to get it to work. And sometimes, I have to suck it up and use bluetooth even though it's plugged in via USB for reasons that escape me. I would say that, in addition to the fact that it sometimes seems to have its own idea of where the volume is set, causes me to think one might figure that into a purchasing decision. (I have once, in fact, had it plugged into the computer, which was powered on, and have the entire unit go black, as if it was not receiving any power.)

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this product. It's pricier than some similar speakers for no benefit I can see. It might be of use to someone who wants to use it primarily for calls and the like, but I am guessing there are likely established players in that realm.

product_title: iHome IH70 Computer Stereo Speaker System with Dock for iPod (Silver)
review_body:
I bought two sets of these speakers for about $50 per pair about two years ago. One for me and one for my son. Over the last six months my set of speakers has failed to power up. I tried messing with the cables to see where the problem lies to no avail. I finally got fed up and Googled the issue. I found several people with the same problem, but I did not find a solution. The speakers are stuck in sync mode (green light on top) even though they have never been used to sync my iPod touch to a computer.

I decided to go on the iHome support page to see if they had any suggestions. I found nothing but the manual, so I contacted their support. I received a timely response that said the unit needed repair. This was not acceptable, so I responded with a note of disapproval. I got a list of issues it could be that I will examine to try to avoid wasting money, but I am doubtful that it can be repaired. Bottom line is they are defective since other people are having the exact same issues. They were connected to a surge protector the entire time, so this problem was not from abuse or a power surge. Thankfully, my son's speakers are working fine. I do not plan to buy products from iHome in the future although I was impressed with the timely responses they sent me. Maybe they will read this review and understand that is not enough to keep customers happy.

product_title: Polk Audio Surroundbar IHT 3000 Home Entertainment System (Black)
review_headline: Great Sound, Sub Woofer Wouldn't Connect
review_body:
My fiance and I were excited to get this Soundbar and try it out because we didn't have any kind of sound system for our TV. We hooked it up, got it going. The sound was awesome! I mean, it's a soundbar so it's not going to be surround-sound.. but for what it is, awesome sound. The sub woofer gave amazing bass, it was excellent for playing music. I loved it.

The problem was that the sub woofer would sometimes cut out in the middle of watching something. Which was distracting and annoying. We changed the channels and got it working again, all was well. Next time we went to turn it on it wasn't working again... changed channels, nothing. It finally kicked in about 20 minutes into the show I was watching. The next day I wanted to play music through the TV.. couldn't get the sub woofer to connect at all. I tried turning it on and off, changing the channels, everything I could think of. The soundbar was working just fine, but there was no bass since it wasn't connecting to the sub woofer.

We decided to just return it and get something else. The issue with this sub woofer is that it is wireless but uses WiFi to connect to the soundbar. WHY they would use WiFi instead of blue tooth is beyond me. If you have wireless internet it's going to interfere with it. And if you live in an apartment where there are multiple wireless internet networks all around you... forget about it. What would have easily fixed this was giving the sub woofer an OPTION to be wireless (we were putting it close enough that a wire wouldn't have mattered) and to also make it wireless via Blue Tooth.. like every other wireless sound system on the market.

We ended up purchasing a wired 5:1 sound system and it's working well for what we wanted.

Cons:

And secondly the charger, while USB, connects to the headphones by a non standard tiny round plug rather than a normal mini usb. If you loose it, you are screwed.

What I haven't checked yet is the mic with skype/facetime, nor the longevity of the battery. I will update with these after a bit.

product_title: Yamaha PRO 500 High-Fidelity Premium Over-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Best premium headphones you never heard of
review_body:
Ok so this is the first time I have ever written a review for a product. This just goes to show you how satisfied I am with these headphones. I have owned several headphones such as the Sennheiser HD 650, Audio Technica ATH-M50, Bose QuietComfort 15, and Bowers & Wilkins P5 yet all of these did not seem to suit my tastes in terms of sound quality and design. Now let my move on and talk about my pros and cons for these headphones.

Let me first tell you about the pros of these headphones. When people sometimes are looking for a headphone they sometimes base their decisions on the bass. Let me first make it clear that these headphones are NOT bass monsters. Rather than getting and overpowering bass you instead get a deep and rich bass as though the song you are listening to is intended to. When you listen carefully you can really feel the deepness of the bass which is great. In regards to the overall sound quality, I would like to say that the lows and mids are excellent and as for the highs they are "strong" and distinct. Moving on to the design I have to say they are gorgeous and will attract the attention of onlookers which isn't a bad thing. The build of the headphones seem to be pretty sturdy all-around and are very comfortable. These are just a few of the pros so now let me move on to the cons.

The cons of these headphones are very minute. First the headphone are a little heavier than your average headphone but if you can overlook the slight heaviness you will be getting an excellent sound experience. The next thing I wanted to address is that these headphones are large. I have a large dome and they fit perfectly to the point that I do not have to adjust them at all. However if you have a small noggin these may be too big for you to fit. The third and final con would of course be the price of the premium headphones. Let me iterate that this is a premium headphone for normally about $399 but I got it on sale for $279. If there was nosale I would have eventually purchased these and would have been glad to purchase them for $399. For the quality of these headphones the $399 price would still be worth it. I definitely understand why people would be put off by the price.

If you are looking for a headphone that lets you listen to how the music is intended to be listened to and doesn't drown you in heavy bass then are the headphones for you. Enjoy!!!

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body: I've been using these occasionally for the past year as a point of reference for open-backed headphone sound (though I'm not trying to imply that they are reference quality cans from either Sennheiser or in general.) The best attribute of these headphones is the design - I'd argue that they are some of the nicest looking headphones out there. In addition they are also very light and comfortable. They are made almost entirely out of plastic (with a few metal parts) but build quality seems pretty good. The cable is about 8-9ft long, is flexible (but with a rubbery cover) and is detachable. One gripe I have to mention is that the jack is 1/4in and the 1/8in adapter included makes for a very bulky and awkward connection with portable devices and even with laptop computers. On to the sound: the best part of their sound is the mid-range, which has a clear, sparkling quality. I find the bass a bit lacking (with most material) although what is there is well defined and has a fair extension. Part of this low-end problem (aside from the open design and their particular acoustic tuning) may be the large resonance bump in driver impedance (from the rated 50 ohm) at low frequencies - peaking at nearly 320 ohm around 100Hz - which reduces the driver sensitivity at low frequencies even when used with a quality amp. Nevertheless, the low end can be improved by the use of equalization (either software or hardware enabled). The highs are well represented though they don't seem to extend as much as on my main cans (the closed-back Audio-Technica ATH-A900) or even as much as on the highly underrated, and substantially cheaper Superlux HD681 (although, all things considered, the HD598 are technically superior to the Superlux). Overall, for sound quality, comfort, etc., I'd break things down like this:    Bass Extension: 5.5/10  Bass Impact: 5/10  Bass Texture: 6/10 (solid)  Mids Quality: 8.5/10  Highs Extension: 6/10  Highs Quality: 7/10 (vivid)  Highs Texture: 6/10 (fairly soft)  Detail/Transparency: 7.5/10 (clear)  Dynamics: 7.5/10 (natural)  Soundstage: 7.5/10  Imaging: 7/10    Other:  Isolation: 2/10 (open design)  Comfort: 9/10  Design/Aesthetics: 10/10  Portability: 4/10 (large size)  Improvement w/ Amplification: 6/10 (Note: It can be driven by portable devices but amping would be recommended)  Value at MSRP: (8/10)    Overall these are very comfortable and quite competent cans, which excel with material that is not bass heavy, such as classical music, jazz, disco/pop, some electronica fare, etc. Compared to other cans in their class (e.g. Beyerdynamic DT990-Pro, AKG K612-Pro, etc.) they are a bit expensive at MSRP but a fair deal when found for less than $200.    ----- Computer/audio gear used -----  MacBook-Pro w/ Mac OS X 10.6.8  XMOS USB 2.0 Audio Reference Design Asynchronous DAC (44.1-192kHz/24bit),  HiFiMeDIY Sabre USB DAC (32-96kHz/24bit),  Onkyo C7030 Cd-player,  Denon DP-300F turntable w/ AT120E cartridge,  Matrix M-Stage Headphone Amp,  FiiO E12-Mont Blanc Headphone Amp,  Sennheiser HD-598 open headphones (50 ohm, 100dB/mW),  Audio-Technica ATH-A900 closed-back headphones (40 ohm, 101dB/mW), and  Superlux HD-681 semi-open headphones (32 ohm, 98dB/mW)  Playback software: Audacity, iTunes, VLC  Digital source quality: standard CD 44.1kHz/16bit, and native HD 88.2-96kHz/24bit

product_title: Pyle Home PTCDS7UI Retro Vintage Turntable with CD/MP3/Casette/Radio/USB/SD, Aux-In and Vinyl-to-MP3 Encoding
review_headline: Initial Review of Turntable & Audio Performance
review_body:
I bought Counting Crows' "August & Everything After" 180 gram vinyl (reviewed separately) for two reasons: 1. wanted to see for myself the difference between 180 gram vinyl (hype?) and original vinyl purchased 20 years ago. 2. I also purchased this Pyle product to convert vinyl to MP3s.

As reviews of earlier Pyle all-in-one models state, sound quality and volume is acceptable for small areas like apartment living rooms. With the volume turned up past 75% and the x-bass turned on, the speakers tended to distort the lows. Think older car speakers playing rich bass music like R&B or Hip-Hop. Music from my iPhone 5 also had acceptable sound quality and volume. I have no plans to test or use the radio, cassette or CD player.

On this Pyle unit "August" played and sounded smoothly. My original vinyl albums ranged from periodically skipping to being unplayable because the arm wouldn't stay in the grooves. I'm old enough to remember tricks vinyl DJs used to mitigate record skipping. I weighted down the stylus head by taping quarter coins to it. I tested performance by playing an album that skipped a lot, taped a second quarter coin to the stylus head and retested. The end result was a total of 4 quarter coins taped to the stylus head. I'd estimate that ~95% of skipping has been mitigated.

Vinyl to MP3 conversion will be tested at a later date and this review is planned to be updated accordingly.

product_title: Philips Fidelio SoundSphere Docking Speaker with AirPlay
review_headline: Reliability Issues hinder a great sounding product
review_body:
I bought the Philips DS9800W after listening to a few Air-play enabled speakers in the market.
The Philips speakers are hands-down, the best sounding and looking speakers out there.
They beat out the Zeppelin and various Airplay speakers available here.
The sound quality is first rate for a small speaker.
But the reliability is terrible. In the one year I had it, its been sent back to the repair centre in Singapore 6 times!!

On the first time ( 7 days after I bought it), Philips replaced it with a set of brand new speakers.
The second pair failed to detect the wifi from an Apple Airport Extreme after 2 months.
All other iOS devices have no problem with the wifi.
Since then the speaker have been sent in for repairs roughly after every 2 months.
The wifi board was replaced each time.

The problem is that the internal wifi loses link after you stop playing music for 24 to 48 hours.
Then you need to re-attach the wifi signal and it takes a few attempts before it locks.
The speakers are about 2 m from the Airport Extreme, so distance is not the reason for its poor performance.
The are numerous complaints about its wifi performance in the Philips Forum site.

I hope Philips find a long term solution to this issue. This is a fantastic sounding product, its potential limited by its poor reliability.

review_body: I am a new audiophile but I love deep rich bass....not sure if the true audiophiles will let me join the club but I know what I like and will deal with that....I have some high end equipment Caver amps and pre amps plus Klipsh speakers ...I have owned tons of headphones from Bose to Beats all in the 100-200 price range and I thought I would move up to the 300-500 range. Please know that I am still learning about audiophile headphones but I don't think these are quite there.... I listen to all kinds of music...rock..classic..rap..country and r and b plus jazz...the professional beats that I own are still my favorite...the bass is simply incredible and I continue my search to find rich deep base and more detailed high end sound that the beats seam to lack....I would not recommend these and suggest that you spend the extra $200 plus bucks on some of the better Senheisser phones and move into the $500 price range in order to be completely happy...that is my plan !

product_title: FiiO E10 USB DAC Headphone Amplifier
review_body:
I had heard about how usb DACs could bring quality headphones to life, and as a self proclaimed audiophile I needed to check this out. I did some research and decided on the E10 over others mainly because it seemed to have good performance for the price.

Other products like the Apogee ONE are nice, but a little too expensive. The interface is simple with switches for gain and bass, and the volume knob is pretty self explanatory! Unlike the E7 and E17, there is no display, but there is not a need for one.

Oh yeah, and the audio coming out of this thing is amazing. I'm using my E10 with the Audio Technica ATH-M50s and music sounds amazing. (It will work great with any headphones, I just bring this up because the M50s are quite popular.) The DAC will bring out parts of your music you have never heard before.

One downside is that this is not marketed as a \\"portable\\" DAC/amp like other FiiO products, but I don't see a reason to carry this around with anyway. It is perfect for use at a desk.

Overall, the FiiO E10 is a great product and should be a definite consideration if in the market for a dac/amp. However, if you are happy with the current quality of your music, or don't tend to listen for little embellishments in music this might not be for you. But for an audiophile the E10 is a must have.

product_title: Audioengine P4 (Pr.) 2-Way Passive Bookshelf Speakers
review_headline: Audioengine P4 Bamboo; Part of an AirPlay System
review_body:
I own powered versions of Audioengine speakers including the A2s (black), A5s (white) and S8 subwoofer. The A2s and S8 are the sound system for my bedroom TV, and the A5s and another subwoofer are the sound system in my living room.

I wanted to create an office Apple AirPlay Wi-Fi music system powered by a Griffin Twenty 20-watt (per channel) amp paired with an Apple Airport Express (previous model). The Twenty has an AC socket for the Airport Express and connects to it with a short, supplied optical Toslink cable. I needed some speakers for the output and decided on the P4s. (The system can be addressed through iTunes or directly by an iPhone, iPad or iPod.)

The P4s are smaller than the A5s, with a 4\\" woofer rather than the 5\\" in the A5s, losing a bit of low end (58 vs. 50 Hz). The laminated, \\"carbonized\\" bamboo cabinet - the term is never explained - is gorgeous, with a deep honey tone, and each speaker seems as if it were carved from a solid block. There are brass mounting sockets on the back and bottom of each speaker, and a rubber pad on the bottom.

The resulting system is exactly what I was looking for, an AirPlay system that plays music effortlessly at any reasonable volume. The P4s simply play the music with no coloration. I recommend them as I do all the Audioengine products.

The Griffin Twenty has an outlet for a powered subwoofer, and I may add one on the future, but only because I enjoy pipe organ music.

product_title: Silicon Power DDR3-1333 240PIN Single Channel
review_headline: Great sound, good fit, but since the left channel became persnickity I rarely use them
review_body:
I really, really like these headphones, and really want them to work. The sound is solid--nice and clear, bass is good enough even for me, mid-range is fine for music and talk, high end is clear and not annoying. The fit is good, even though I've got a bit of a fat head (or so they say), even if the cushions get to be a little warm after a while. The check pattern is a bit much, but I can't see it when the headphones are on my head.

The cable is \\"Tangle-Free, Stress-Relief\\", and it's true that I haven't had problems with tangles. In theory the cable will disconnect near the headphones if the cable gets caught, \\"a great feature for active users.\\" I'm probably less active than most, yet somehow I damaged the cable fairly quickly in spite of the connection near the headphones, or possibly because of it. I don't take them out running or biking, so they're used around the house as I'm reading or washing dishes or on the NordicTrack.

The damage is in the short wire near the headphones, not the long one. I've replaced the long cable and that doesn't fix the problem. If I'm sitting perfectly still and I can hold the wire in just the right position, I get left and right sound. If I move or even sneeze, the left channel cuts out and I get to fight with the wire until it connects again.

The sound is wonderful, but the inconvenience of using these headphones keeps me from using them most of the time. If they worked they'd get five stars easily.

review_body:
the thing that cough my eye for this BT Receiver was the price and the size, I've had it for a couple of weeks and its working properly and as intended. . .

i just want to point out one thing, i read in some reviews that this BT Receiver had to be paired every single time you turn it ON, i have to say that it is not true,

To pair the device for the first time you have to press the power button for 7 seconds until you see the blue and red lights blinking, then you can head to your device Bluetooth settings (i've used it with an Ipod Touch 4g, Samsung Galaxy S3 & Windows 8 PC) it should appear in your options, if asked for pin just put 0000 and done.

I use this BT Receiver with my Ipod Touch mostly, so after i use it, i turn the Bluetooth off on my ipod, when i want to use it again here is what i do,,,

turn my Ipod's bluetooth and the BT Receiver ON, i dont have to do anything else, they pair on their own,
to achieve this, you have to PRESS the power button ONLY until you see the first blue light ( press for about 5 secs) and let go of the power button. If you keep holding power you will get the BT Receiver to go into discovery mode, (blue and red blinking lights) prompting you to pair the device again,

Pros;
-Good Price
-Small size
-Easy to use
-Has a good range with no obstructions
-Good Battery Life (i've used it for 7 consecutive hours with battery left and more than 11 cummulative hrs)
-Works while charging (will turn off after plugging it in (if On)you just have to turn it back on and let it re-pair by itself (will keep a constant red light with the flashing blue)

Cons:
-The building materials feel a little fragile, especially the power button and the 3.5mm cable coming out of this device which is thinner that what some would expect (about the thickness of ipod's earphones)
-Losses considerable amount of communication after going through some obstacleslike a door or a wall
-Paired it with two PCs and with one of the them the audio had some lag about a sec or two, (really bad when watching videos, but could of been the BT on the PC that was at fault but just letting you know)
-The usb cable is not a standard usb to micro/mini-usb cable, so if you lose your charging cable you may be out of luck

Over all

i think that this is a good purchase and good device,
i have used this on my car and its excellent, also good in my house as long as i dont keep going to different rooms
i would recommend it to my friends...

I've had good luck using just the smooth side, but I suppose if you have a really dirty screen you could scrub with the rougher side. The two smaller ones have been parceled out to my laptop case and my travel kit with the singles wipes. The packaging says that the cloths are washable, which is nice.

product_title: Fixed Frame Projection Screen
review_headline: Great deal and a great screen
review_body:
Summary:
The ER120WH1 is a fantastic screen -- reasonably priced, sturdy, lightweight, and easy to mount.

Usage:
In combination with an Epson 8350 projector (ceiling mounted, 16' from screen), I use the screen in an entertainment area that is a cross between a theater room and rec room -- good ambient lighting control but often with the back portion of the space used for pool or foosball during movie watching. Seating is in an arc that spans the room on a 10-12' radius from the center of the screen and there are no issues with viewing angle on the sides impacting image quality.

Pros:
- Performance for the price is fantastic. I spent a lot of time cross-shopping other brands and other Elite screens and this one really is the best combination to be found right now. Elite offers other fabrics tuned for brighter ambient conditions (at a cost of sacrificing contrast) -- if I had more daylight exposure I might have gone that route but am very happy with my choice.
- The packaging is really as bulletproof as described. The thick PVC pipe which encased the screen particularly impressed me. This thing is really not going to be damaged in transport.
- Color rendition and contrast have been excellent both in darkened room conditions and in moderate to normal ambient lighting.
- The black frame does a great job of capturing any overspill and looks better than we expected for a screen in this price range (my wife was dubious as to whether we should have gone upmarket with a wooden frame but was relieved and pleasantly surprised when she saw it).
- The mounting system is simple and effective -- no complaints about the mounting process and the screen is very firmly in place.

Cons:
- The assembly process is much discussed on Amazon, YouTube, etc -- I didn't find it as bad as expected from those discussions but you want to set your expectations correctly. The process is truly not that difficult and whileI did have a friend help with assembly it could be very reasonably assembled by yourself. Connecting the frames to the elbow brackets requires some patience and muscle, but the really challenging part was getting the mounting clips installed (part of the screen tensioning process). While they get much easier as you progress through the installation, the first few are really painful and involved a significant amount of muttering/swearing.
- The delivery service used is sub-par for Amazon. They called to schedule delivery, leaving a nearly inaudible and somewhat cryptic message. When I returned their call it took significant effort to verify what they had called about, and the delivery window they offered was very broad (think cable repair schedules). Made me glad that the packing was so good.

review_headline: Does Exactly What I Imagined and What It Was Designed To Do
review_body:
I bought this cable because it looked like it could solve the issue I was having with compatibility between my iPhone 5 and the after-martket iPod/iPhone integration kit I bought, which had previously worked fine with iPhone 4/4S. I have the Neo ProLink 2.0 installed in my 2005 Honda Accord LX with factory radio. The factory radio has No bells and whistles, such as auxiliary input or satellite radio, ect. Occasionally Neo Car Audio releases a firmware update to improve compatibility between it's integration kits and the iDevices. A firmware update has not yet been made available for iPhone 5, so I thought this cable would solve the problem by letting me listen to the iPhone through the headphone jack.

Sure enough, and as I had wished and suspected, this cable securely hooked on to the car integration kit's 30-pin connector and provided the same flawless sound through the radio's CD-C/AUX mode through the iPhone 5's headphone jack.

I fear that this product is receiving low ratings from people who are expecting too much from this adapter. It's only an auxiliary adapter and only carries audio. It is not intended (or possible) for an aux line to carry the type of integration commands you might expect from an iPhone/iPod integration. It just carries sound. Period. Control is left to the beautiful touchscreen on your device.

So, if you're on the market for a quality product that does as it is intended to do, look no further.

product_title: Creative Aurvana Air Active Clip-on Earphones
review_headline: Best Quality Audio/Durable In-Ear Headphone Ever
review_body:
The Aurvana Air is an In-Ear headphone that excells where every other headphone fails. When i was searching for headphones, I had very specific criteria defined. Firstly, I wanted a headphone with SUPERIOR audio quality. Next, it had to be an in-ear headphone that i could use for both gaming and exercise. Baring that in mind, I'm a bit OCD with the feeling that my headphones could fall off mid workout, so I opted out of a traditional earbud design and preferred an over-the-ear one instead. Lastly, I wanted something that reduced outside noise, but only by about 30%-50%. I wanted to feel distanced from others while listening, but be able to hear others and anyone calling out to me.

I have broken out the Pros and Cons below to hit my specific care-abouts. Also, I purchased another high quality in-ear product from Sony (Sony In-Ear Sport Headphones XBAS65B) designed not to fall off the ear and I returned them immediately in comparison.

Audio Quality: Simply put, you cannot find another in-ear headphone that delivers the same level of Audio quality. The highs are crystal clear and the mids compete where other's fail. Traditional In-ear headphones often have difficulty providing bass or even a sense of bass line due to the size, design and structure of the product. For an in-ear headphone, the Aurvana Airs provide a solid supporting bass that flows with the mids nicely, but couldn't possibly take over. Simply put, they make you feel as if the sound is the environment around you. In games, I constantly keep my friend and I up to date on enemy movement in BF3 because the clarity REALLY IS THAT GOOD. It has saved us more times than i can recount by letting him know what I'm hearing. Also, You are not drowned by bass and unrealistically modified sound. The only caveat (if you can even call it one) is that without the mesh screens, the highs can be a slight bit sharp, but i wouldn't wear it without them anyway. 9/10

Design Quality: Next to theaudio, this is where the Airs really excel. It needed to stay on my ear and be durable. I have owned these headphones for over a year, wearing them easily for 2-3 HOURS A DAY, between exercise and gaming. NEVER ONCE have I felt that they were going to break and they have NEVER fallen off my ear, even when accidentally pulling the cord with my hand. Because the earbud swivels, it allows you to find a \\"sweet spot\\" of comfort and stability on the ear. Again, my OCD tendencies have always left me concerned about earbuds popping out, but after a few weeks, this dissipated and I never thought of it again while wearing them. Only caveat to some might be the length of the cord could seem a little short. I like them short for exercise so this didn't bother me at all. 10/10

Comfort: I've had over-the-ear buds similar to this in the past that were painful after 20 minutes. The headphones were slightly uncomfortable for the first month or so after about an hour of use, but that's simply because I hadn't used headphones like these in years, so i had to \\"build ear endurance\\" so to say. As of writing this, I can leave these on for 2-3 hours and not even notice they're on at times. The fact that they are so light and that the majority of the weight is supported by the inner ear portion and not the actualy ear lobe, make them extremely comfortable. My only caveat would be that putting them on and off feels like a hassle at times, however, when you think of the amount of time you would have to spend readjusting and putting earbuds back in your ear, this is completely negotiable. You get good at taking them on and off quickly after a while. 9/10

Price: So, we've reached the real reason most people may not purchase these headphones. These originally retailed for $199.99. This would certainly have been a deal breaker for me, even knowing how great they are, I Just couldn't justify paying a major-brand headset price for high-grade earbuds. I will say, I bought these on sale at about 70% off ($60)which was more than reasonable. If you can get them for $100 or less (totally possible on Amazon or ebay), I would recommend the purchase. 7/10

Overall: They are simply the best earphones I've ever worn, and this is coming from a man that never wore earphones longer than 30 mins tops due to irritation or poor design. If you need new headphones and can get them for $100 or less, looking elsewhere is a waste of time. 9/10

Extra Credit:

Classiness: They come in a freaking display case and a leather satchel/pouch for travel. No brainer people. 10/10

product_title: Motorola Signal Booster 4-Port BDA-S4 Cable Modem TV HDTV Amplifier
review_body:
I have a single cable entering my home, that Comcast installed.

For at least a year I was able to use a cheap passive 2-Way Splitter and watch both my TV thru a TiVo Premiere, and access the Internet at 25Mbps (nice). But recently, for an unknown reason, the Internet Signal became too weak to access the Web. The TiVo continued to work, as apparently it does not require as strong a signal.

If I removed the Splitter, and connected the cable directly to my Cable Modem, the Internet would work. But I want to watch TV, too !

Every call to Comcast ended with them wanting to send a Technician over - while charging me $50 for the house call. Although I have had skilled and professional Comcast Techs over in the past, I've found the majority do nothing but turn my Cable Modem on and off, and usually leave with no solution.

So I proceeded to eliminate the obvious. I inspected the Cable outside my home. It looked in excellent shape, physically. Indoors, I swapped Splitters. I swapped Cables. No improvement.

But by searching the Internet, I finally learned something new: I COULD CHECK THE SIGNAL STRENGTH MYSELF, WITH EQUIPMENT I ALREADY OWN !

My TiVo Premiere, and probably every DVR, has a sub-menu that will display Signal Strength. I discovered mine was 67. On a scale up to 100, 67 is not good.

And my Zoom 5341 Cable Modem (very recent and DOCSIS 3.0) has a Signal Strength display as well. I expect pretty much any Cable Modem will have this function. Just open MS Explorer, type in 192.168.100.1 as an address, and you'll be taken to the access page. Log In, and on a sub-menu the Signal Strength will be displayed.

Mine was in the -5.5 to -6.5 range, on all channels. Awful.

So I purchased and installed the BDA-S4. The Signal Strength on TiVo leaped from 67 to 89 ! Nice. But the Cable Modem was reporting no Signal at all - Zero.

I called Comcast again, and armed with thisknowledge, emphasized how bad my Signal Strength was, for both devices. The tech on the phone was impressed I could read the Signals. For the first time I felt in control.

He tried to fix it, running me through the usual turn-it-on turn-it-off reboot drill, to no effect. Each time I checked the Signals and told him how poor the Signal was.

At last he said he needed to talk to another tech - and simply disappeared. He did not hang up on me, but must have been gone for 30 minutes or more. I never spoke to him again.

But what did happen, is quite suddenly the Internet worked ! My Signal had increased from -6.0 to +6.0. Very nice.

Clearly Comcast did something, at their home office, that corrected my signal. No tech needed to visit at all.

I'm still using my BDA-S4, though ultimately I probably don't need it. It looks to be very well made, and effective.

Bottom Line: Before you purchase any Amplifier, CHECK THE SIGNAL STRENGTH yourself. Your DVR and your Cable Modem should have this function already, you just need to know where to look.

Good Luck !

review_body: I had these headphones for maybe a couple of years before they died.  After owning several other cheap headphones and a couple much more expensive sets of headphones, I can say that these are good for budget headphones (I think I picked mine up at Target for $15 in 2003).  The independent volume controls for each ear were nice, although the feature was more a novelty than a necessity.  I really liked that the cord only attached to one side, then was connected to the other can via a wire across the headband (and, speaking of the headband, it was fairly comfortable).  I thought they sounded better than a friend's $20 Sony headphones, and they were more comfortable than any other headphones I had previously owned. There were only two things that I didn't like.  Although they appear at first glance to be closed-back headphones, they actually are not sealed, so they don't block any ambient noise.  But more importantly, despite my careful handling, one side stopped working after a while, making the headphones practically useless.

product_title: Logitech UE Smart Radio
review_body:
Pros: Small, portable. Surprisingly good (but not great) mono sound. Easy to use and set up, although controls not very intuitive. Seven day alarm, again not very intuitive to set up. The LCD is bright and easy to read, even for my old eyes. Six station presets a nice touch. All plastic but well built. Battery is great feature.

Cons: Lots of stations, but it's Logitech's choice not yours. Unable to add your own URL's (ie your favorite stations or paid services. UE Smart Radio server software (for streaming your own music) is worthless, check the forums! No blue tooth - a radio this expensive should have blue tooth. No audio output jacks other than an ear phone jack. Logitech's support is unresponsive, not helpful. Can not access Google or Amazon cloud music services, or iTunes. No WIFI N support. Requires moderate to strong WIFI signal for good sound, may not play in areas of your home where signal is weak. No support for third party Apps to add features or services.

Bottom Line: If you're a newbie to internet radio and want an easy (but not painless) way to get started, perhaps this radio is for you. Experienced users should look elsewhere.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts Universal Projector Mount
review_body:
Product is as described. Well made, sturdy, I don't expect the projector to fall off the ceiling anytime soon.
They even provide mounting bolts to attach the device to a concrete ceiling!
If you were to buy just the nuts/bolts/hardware separately, it would likely set you back more than the total price they are selling this at - it cost me less than seventeen dollars.

The instructions are a different matter. Looks like they were written in another language which is extremely polite and sometimes apologetic, then translated by an automatic translator (such as Google Translate). While the instructions do convey the broad idea - attach the device to the ceiling, attach your projector to the device, and you are good to go - there is a certain charm about the extreme politeness coupled with a vague sense that the instruction writer never actually attempted to set up a projector on his/her own before writing the instructions.

As well, there seems to be a shortage of paper at the factory; a single sheet comprises all of the instructions, with tiny drawings, polite suggestions, and well, I sensed some sort of 'good luck' sentiment.

The sales pictures here on the Amazon site were more helpful than the setup instructions.

However, once you get it all set up - not exactly rocket science - its all good.

Rating is 5 stars for the device, a single star for the instructions, three stars for the helpful pictures on the amazon sales page.
Addition April 1 2015:
Someone from the company called me the other day, apologizing for the issues I faced and offering to make changes to the instructions that I had commented on.
Interestingly enough, I received a rewritten set this afternoon for me to review, with detailed pictures to illustrate the process. Quite impressed
by their initial interest as well as actually following up on my suggestions. Not changing the star rating until the instructions are finalized, though, but definitely they are making moves in the right direction.

review_headline: Good Product, a little confusing to set-up
review_body:
I purchased these headphones for my girlfriend who likes to listen to music while she runs, but she found the cords from her headphones bouncing around to be pretty annoying. So this product fixes that problem pretty well. She says it feels great to listen to music while running without feeling tethered to something.

I give this product a 3 out of 5 mainly because of the set-up process and how it connects to a bluetooth-enabled device. As well as the item that was shipped to me was slightly broken. It has a rattling noise in one of the earbuds that can be heard while playing music. (I have requested to return the item and get a new one so I will update this review with a possible 4-star if that goes well)

I read another review that said the instruction manual was not exactly correct in stating how to connect the headphones to a bluetooth device. I had that in mind so after following the instructions, and having it not be able to connect. I still messed around with it for a little while before I got it to connect. (This was connecting to a iPod Nano 7th Gen). One other complaint I have is that you have to manually connect the headphones every time you want to use them, even if bluetooth hasn't been turned off on the device. This could be due to the new gen iPod but it is really only a minor annoyance.

Other than that the price of these wireless headphones is great, especially compared to other bluetooth headphones, the comfort level is pretty good, the quality of sound is also pretty good, and the build of the headphones is decent (except for the rattling earbud in the item I received) and the seller shipped it rather quickly.

product_title: Maximal Power 18650(2)-2600+FC18650 2-Pieces Rechargeable Li-ion Batteries and Rapid Dual Channel Charger
review_headline: Recessed positive terminal prevents use in normal applications
review_body:
These batteries are not like your typical AA, AAA, C, or D cell batteries. Normally, the negative terminal sticks out slightly beyond the battery wrap (cover) and the positive terminal sticks out even further. The terminals on these batteries, are both recessed, so there is no continuity between two batteries in series (placed end to end). I purchased the batteries, along with the quick charger. They came in nine days instead of two days (Amazon Prime) and arrived with no paperwork. (Every battery charger I have ever purchased at a retailer contained instructions and warranty. This had neither)
These batteries were intended for a high power flashlight, but are useless with the recessed terminals. The description said nothing of the unconventional design. The other reviewer said the charger makes it worth the price, but what use is a good charger for batteries you can't use?
If this combination works for you, go ahead and buy it, but make sure before you buy.

review_headline: Kaito Meloson  M 7 radio/ music player
review_body:
I thought I would share my thoughts on this great little radio with you.

While this radio is not very big, 6 inches long by 3 1/2 inches high, it has surprising high quality sound and volume.

radio reception:

The radio works well on FM band and pulls in many hard to get stations in my fringe receiving area, it also does a fairly good job on AM band, but not as good as when on FM , this is not a down check, it seems to be quite common in DSP technology radios no matter what brand ( I own several DSP radios) however, no other DSP radio I own outshines this little rig on AM). This radio tunes through direct keypad entry, by auto scan, or by the tuning dial control, it sports 50 presets per band.

construction:

The radio seems quite well made and sturdy, all switches and controls are smooth and work well.

Music player:

The unit sports a basic digital music player that uses a micro SD card (not included) and supports MP3 and WMA formats, you can access different music files through the key pad or using the tuning dial control.

power supply:

The unit comes with a common, off the shelf Li-ion battery, BL 5C, 3.7 volts, 1000 mAH, this will run the rig for about 8-10 hours. These batteries only cost about 5 bucks, so, if you go camping like I do, you might want to have another battery as a backup for extended stays in the great outdoors. The radio can be charged by a USB port on your computer, or with a common USB type cell phone charger. The unit has a charge regulator built in, and a red light when charging and a green light when full, just like a Kindle fire does. When I use this unit as a desk radio, I usually have it plugged into my cell phone wall wart, that way the battery is always fresh when I go portable.

The radio comes with a battery, a USB cable and a audio input cord to use on the AUX input, and a well written (in good English) owners manual, it also includes a wrist strap.

In closing, I recommend this radio/player as a good buy at this price point, sound reproduction is amazing for it's size, and you won't go broke buying AA batteries for it.

product_title: Mini Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds Stereo Headphones w/ Microphone for iPhone, iPad, iPod, Android, smart phones, and other Bluetooth devices
review_headline: So far, EXACTLY what I needed...
review_body:
After many reviews and comparisons, I found Ausiosynq's BT Earbuds by happen stance reading blogs. They were compared to the BackBeatGO B/T Earbuds in sound and quality.

I chose these since they were marked discount at over HALF the price of the BackBeatGO (Planetronics?) What's there to lose on a chance?

I have had these a few days and I like how they charged fairly fast and the sound quality is admissible for my needs. I play Disc Golf competitively and I needed a B/T set of Buds that:
- I did not want to spend a large amount of money on
- I needed them to be portable
- I needed them with good range from my phone (a GSIII)
- I needed them to be lightweight
- I did NOT need noise cancellation since I like to hear some things around me (like traffic, people, and Fore!)
- I simply needed them to work

Overall, I like them so far. They came with a proprietary type of USB to Pin type of charger, but that is expected with how small and lightweight these are. They do not use the MicoUSB connection like others. The connecting cable between earbuds is fairly short, so you do not have a long cord hanging from in front of you or behind your neck.

The buttons (Right earbud: up/down and on/off) are small and require some getting used to when you go to click them for your needs. Being that the buds are so small, it almost causes a problem when you have large fingers, but after all, I bought them because they are SMALL. (so no gripes here)

Audio quality is good, not great, but good; I bought these for their functionality and use NOT for superb audio quality. If you are looking for a good set of high audio quality B/T headphones... look elsewhere, but be honest, you get what you pay for and what you need. (this fits me fine)

The B/T connection process was simple, so the volume can be adjusted from your device AND the ear buds themselves. Find the balance between the two and you can decide if you would rather go up/down on the ear buds or your device (to avoid the large finger/small ear bud scenario)

Additional Items in package:
- Individual Instruction Sheet: The package itself comes with a very basic set of instructions. Seems that the seller decided to include this with the kit to avoid drama and address customers needs BEFORE they arose. Kudos to them.. more sellers need to do this.
- USB to Pin connection charger
- AC Wall Outlet with USB connection (to plug your chargers USB cable connection into)
- 3 sets of silicone ear buds for different sizes
- plastic ear clips to keep the ear buds in place: these seem flimsy, but they are really light weight and not irritating to the skin, so it pays off. Other conditions: they can unsnap easily from the ear bud at times if you are trying to deeply adjust your ear bud seating in your ear.

So far I really enjoy the Audiosynq in-ear buds. I have not taken a phone call with them over the past few days, but it does provide the audible phone alert that I have a text message/email according to me device settings; so I cannot tell you how good/bad the microphone/conversation quality is.

Take them as they are and so far I will take them for what they are worth. Technology has come a long way and this is a small set of B/T earbuds that is not heavy on weight and seems good in quality.

product_title: Harman Kardon AVR 1700 5.1-Channel Network-Connected Audio/Video Receiver with AirPlay
review_body:
I absolutely am thrilled with my 1700, and the sale price at which I purchased it (much less than half price, brand new from retailer). I did lots of research and you should too. Read the forums, read the reviews. First of all, yes it is lightweight because it is a different technology on the power supply. While it was once true that the heavier the better, that just isn't the case anymore, necessarily. If anyone tells you it is, they are probably just stuck with notions of the past. Perhaps on the highest of high end stuff, maybe there is a difference when it comes to power supplies, but I highly doubt it... and seriously doubt whether a human ear could discern the difference even on like setups. Undoubtedly the majority of 'listening' occurs with sub-standard source material (ie. internet radio, 192kb mp3's, TV audio, etc) and as a daily-listening living-room workhorse, this receiver does exceptionally well. How many of us really sit on the couch in a perfectly silent room, with our perfectly recorded loss-less media playing? Kind of like the $100+ cables discussion. No need to buy them. If you have good-to-excellent quality speakers, and your sound source is good-to-excellent, this receiver will push it just fine and will sound excellent in the process. There is some bad info out there about Class D, etc. Don't believe all the audiophile hype, and if you are pushing $10,000+ speakers, you ain't buyin' an AVR 1700 anyway. Move on. You either want this receiver for the features that it DOES have, or you don't. If you do, you won't be disappointed.

The newer technology 'enhancements' are really nice to have (vTuner, ethernet, AirPlay, etc) I love being able to listen to online radio stations without using my laptop, or physically hooking up my iPod for my mp3's (both via 1/8\\" stereo to RCA's) like I used to have to do on my 15 year old avr. Heck, while listening to Pandora on the iPhone, you can even turn the AVR 1700 on from the iPhone. Sometimes I mess with my baby son and turn it on from the garage when I get home from work. He is like 'wowwwwwwwwww!' when the music just starts playin' and then baba walks through the door. Haha.

A couple complaints:
1. HK NEVER responded to my 3 separate requests about functionality. Really crap customer service and inexcusable to just not reply.
2. If you can find the UK version of the manual, it will clarify for you, one of the frustrating questions I had that I never got an answer to after countless searches (actual steps involved in networking DO NOT match the US version of instructions). Refer to #1. Thanks HK.
3. The radioharmankardon dot com (HK web based vTuner online station interface) is pretty bad. Looks/feels/operates very old school and is very slow. Number/selection of stations is good, but with its' slowness (both on web, and on device) just too painful to really get into. You are lucky to setup a couple of genre folders and favorites in each and call it a day. It would be mind numbing to navigate more than a handful of stations, in a 'just browsin' kinda way.
4. setting up said vTuner station guide is missing a piece of information too. I will just tell you now, the receiver \\"ID\\" # is your mac address, good luck finding that info nugget. Refer to #1. Thanks HK.
5. The iPhone HK app sucks, mine will NOT control my 1700. Pissed.
6. I have heard the Media manager sucks too, although I have yet to find out. Will update later.

If I remember correctly, also, the HDMI isn't pass-through, so if that matters to you it may be a deal breaker. I didn't think it would be a big deal, but turns out I really wish it were. review_headline: Not terrible -- at least it's cheap.
review_body:
I bought this as a gift for my daughter. I couldn't see buying her an ipod or anything that I would regret when she inevitably lost or broke it, so I figured this was a good entry-level device. She loves it, but will soon realize how limited it is.

As a media player, it's pretty decent. I'm used to quirky devices and this definitely falls into that category.

It comes with one simple game and no way to add more. Adding media files is pretty easy, but the interface of the player is clunky.

No way I can tell to remove icons from the "desktop", although you can temporarily move things around (like I said, quirky).

It comes with a few other odd choices of apps like a "search" which doesn't seem to do anything (no network connectivity) and a speaking Chinese-English dictionary.

I found it strange that it came with 2 batteries, especially since one of them wouldn't hold a charge for more than 30 minutes. The other one worked fine though.

For me, the most entertaining factor was the instruction booklet. Translated into very amusing english, the instructions used the maximum number of words to provide the minimum set of instructions.

All in all, my 7 year old daughter likes it and I won't really care when it gets stepped on or left out in the rain.

product_title: JVC Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black
review_headline: Single Best Headset I Have Ever Used
review_body:
I've tried a lot of headsets and headphones over the years and I can honestly say the JVC HANC250 are the best. Now I know there are more accurate headphones out there and ones with better noise canceling, or are more comfortable, or have more flashy features, but no other single headphone represents the best mix of features like these do.

I bought my first JVC HANC250 back in 2009 and I was immediately surprised at the difference in sound quality they represented. I had tried Bose and Sennheiser headphones before this, but none of those other \\"high end\\" headphones showed this level of improvement to sound quality. (Bose QC3 and even the new QC15 were particularly disappointing. Sorry Bose fans...) It's like the first time you hear studio monitors. The difference is undeniable even for the \\"non-audiophile.\\" And let me take a moment to state that I am not an audiophile. My hearing is decent, but I work with and know many people that have hearing above my own.

I can best describe the audio quality as reference levels. The EQ curve is very flat. No crazy heavy bass or piercing highs. It's like a good set of studio monitors. All frequencies are well represented, but no frequency is obviously louder then the others. I call them my reference headphones and it bugs the hell out of my audiophile friends. For what ever reason they assume that any headphone under a grand are trash. I can't hear much of a difference in their studio headphones over these, so I think I will stick with the $100 headphones...

The headphones will work unpowered (which is great in a pinch) but the audio quality is severely diminished. It sounds about like a cheap pair of headphones that came for free with your Sony Walkman in 1992. Bad.

The noise canceling feature works well. I use it to block noise on planes and in a crowded office space. It's not like you can't hear anything outside the headset though. Everything is just much harder to hear. People's voices sound as if they are in the other room even though they are standing next to you. It's pleasantly peaceful. Like a college library.

Battery life is amazing. They say 50 hours and they mean it. When the battery starts to die, the noise cancelling will kickoff when very loud sounds happen around you. Then loud things you are listening to will temporarily stop the powered parts of the headphones. The first time it happened I had forgotten that the headphone was powered (despite turning it \\"on\\" every time I used them) and I thought the headphones had started to break. This was after two weeks of solid use. The battery life is outstanding.

The earphones are lightweight, but not flimsy-feeling like the Bose headphones. The earpads are soft, comfortable, don't make your face leak, and after a short time, are completely forgotten on your head. (I wear glasses!) After 3.5 years of use I JUST this weekend (12.29.2012) wore out the earpads. Replacements can be bought from JVC.com using part number \\"J34899-001\\" and cost $14 each. Worth it.

The audio cable is the low point for these headphones. The cable isn't extremely short or anything, but every once in a while you will feel like you could use just one more foot of cable. Luckily the audio cable isn't hardwired into the headphones and you can replace it with a 3.5mm cable. Unfortunately not ANY 3.5mm cable will do. The plug for the cable on the headphones is like an older iPhone, that is to say, it's recessed into the plastic. So the best replacements are iPhone headphone cables. (sometimes called \\"slim\\" 3.5mm) It's really hard to find them in black though...

I've bought 2 pairs personally and I had the studio that I work for buy me a pair. I used all three pairs nearly non-stop for a combined use-time of about 7 years. None of them have ever broken beyond repair. JVC has made something special here folks. Whenever someone asks me about a good set of headphones I don't even think about it. The JVC HANC250 are the best pair of headphones. Period.

product_title: Sony 8GB S Series MP3 Player Black with Bluetooth Wireless Headphones
review_body:
PROS:
- The bluetooth capability is nice since I use it while running. It limits the amount of wire hanging around me while I run.

- Syncing WMP playlists is a great feature. I like that its software integrates with WMP for managing playlists. Then you can select the playlist and choose shuffle mode to have a nice mix of your music which is nice when I am running.

- The clip-on headset controller is a nice feature. I clip it onto the collar of my running jacket and it stays. This helps keep the earbud wires out of the way.

CONS:
- While the bluetooth capability is nice, make sure you charge the blue tooth head set often. I charged it fully one day, used it while running. Two days later I went for a run and about 15 minutes into the run the headset died. The Walkman has a standby mode to conserve its battery when it is not in use, but the headset does not appear to. You will have to turn off the headset after every use to keep the charge. Also, there is no way to tell the level of charge on the headset so you will not know when the headset is going to run down. With today's technology you would think that Sony could create a headset that has a standby mode to conserve its battery as well.

- While you can select a playlist and use shuffle mode as I described, the Walkman will often "forget" that you were in shuffle mode and start playing your music in order (not shuffled). Another issue is that the player will "forget" what track you were listening to. This can be annoying when you put an audio book on the player. I have owned other Sony Walkman MP3 players and they all suffer from these annoyances. I was hoping they would be fixed with this Walkman, but they were not.

- The bluetooth headset has controls on it which are fine if you are standing still and do not have gloves on. I run in cold weather and wear gloves. I tried to adjust the volume with gloves on while running and ended up turning off the headset. I had to stop running and take off my gloves to set the headset correctly.

- You need a proprietary cable to charge the bluetooth headset. This seems like a poor attempt on Sony's part to supply a cable that can be lost and cause us to have to buy a replacement from them.

- If you do not like the earbuds that come attached to the bluetooth headset, you are not in luck. The headset controller should have been designed to allow other earbuds to be attached. If the earbuds have issues in the future then the headset controller will no longer be useful.

I would have given this player 4 stars if Sony had addressed the issues in its previous models. The only real upgrade was the bluetooth capability. The issues with it "forgetting" shuffle mode, or which track you were listening to, is very annoying.
