product_title: urBeats In-Ear Headphone - White
review_headline: urBeats not as bad as you'd think. *Update 11/13/2013* Durability issue
review_body:
I currently have Meelectroncis M6, Ultimate Ears Superfi and V-Moda Crossfade LP. I replaced my Superfi with the M6 because I didn't want to spend too much on headphones to work out in. Little did I know that sweat will break IEMs not desigened for it. $$$ lesson learned. I'm no audiophile, but after testing out various headphones, I guess I'm 80% bass head most of the time.

I bought the urBeats to pair with my HTC 8x after I plugged in a pair of my friends Beats Solos. The difference was bass heavnly clear at a very low volume level. I love my V-Moda cans, but the reality is for my use case, urBeats made sense with my budget and my phone.

Pros:
- Build quality is better than most have reported. Cord is thin, but far from flemsy.
- Tangle free cord is nice
- Bass is great - I've burned them in for about 2 days and I think it made a difference. could be just me.
- Case is very useful for more than just the headphones.
- Design is a major plus for me. I like the metal and black/red color.

Cons:
-Price. I wish they were more like $80, but not too bad.
-Eartips supply could have been better. M6's had at least 2 more options. Superfi came with foam tips plus more assortment of tips.

If you have a beats powered device, I'd say its worth it. The sound just sounds different in a good way. I know I've read users talking bad about the Beats by Dre brand, but in my case I believe it delivered.

These are not recommended for the audiophile or those who don't like a lot of thump in their listening experience. Others have reported fitting problems, and I'd say those are valid if you've never worked with IEMs before. I'm working with finding the perfect fit and so far I'm using the triple flange tips that came with my M6 and they work great. These IEMs are not for working out, so don't even think you can.

Conclusion: If you are a Beats fan or just like heavy bass,I'd recommend them. Especially if you have a Beats powered device. If you have an HTC 8x, I think its worth a look.

UPDATE: After a couple of months with these IEMs they are much better than I thought it would be. It really depends on the source (mp3 player, smartphone, other) but in general there is a lot more to these than just plain bass.

My current set up is using Sony's MW600 wireless headphone adaptor and Motorola's Motoactv watch. The Motoactv tends to lean bass heavy on the EQ, but I think it works perfect. I listen to a lot of R&B, and that works well with urBeats. What was most surprising was when playing more acoustic/vocal centered music (Cannonball by Damian Rice or any Tyrone Well's songs)the vocals appear to be more up front. I'm not an audiophile, however, I've researched enough to understand that urBeats won't have an extended sound stage, but there is sound separation. The bass from the guitar will not over power the vocals and the highs are not bad here. I've enjoyed my time with the urBeats and will continue to use them for my R&B/HipHop music. I will be purchasing a paire of IEMs that have even more stage and imaging though. Sony's XBA series looks to be my next purchase because it has warmer tones than your average armature driver (which isn't exactly flat eq)

UPDATE: 11/13/2013

So the durability of these IEMs are questionable. I don't run with them and do nothing extreamly out of the ordinary. I have stuffed them into coat pockets and regular pockets which I think could be what caused them to stop working completely on smartphones and most recently mp3 players. Sound will not come if I use it on my HTC 8X or BB Z10. It kind of worked with my iPod nano/iPod 4th gen, but the right bud no longer works without wiggling the cable. I purchased these because they were advertised as durable, but that is definitely not the case here. I've adjusted my rating from 4 to 2 stars. They lasted almost a year, but at $99 you expect it to last far longer especially if they are being used for commuting and office scenarios.

Also it's quick to move from one exercise to another exercise unlike many other exercise systems--especially compared to weights. product_title: Sony MDR-J10 Headphones
review_body:
I have looked for and bought many earphones over many years in search of a pair that would stay in my ears during various workouts. I have yet to find them. These come the closest.

Earbuds always fall out of my left ear, and sometimes out of both ears. These stay on my head and in my ears. The left one won't stay in my ear as well as the right one, which makes the music sound a little farther away than in my right ear. Annoying, but not the end of the world for $9. I have my very expensive closed back Sennheisers for sessions in my living room chair for when I want to seriously listen to music.

I'm impressed with the sound, too, for so little money. I can't attest to quality degradation compared to past Sony buds, and I'm no expert audiophile, but I'm not looking for terrific sound quality while I'm working out; music motivates me to keep working out, but I'm not listening to every note. I'm happy if they stay in my ears, don't hiss or spit at me, and don't quit. And I don't need them to last a lifetime, not even the rest of mine. Replacing them every 6 months to a year sounds ok with me.

The cord length (right at 4 feet) is just right for me. I'm 5'2\\". It gives me plenty of length. Does it tangle? Hell yes. The little slider thing just cuts down on the amount that CAN tangle by about 18\\". The rest tangles just fine. And that's no matter how carefully I wrap it, band it, and shove it into a tight spot in my purse. But that's no different than most other cords. It doesn't tangle while I'm running, doesn't catch on handlebars, weight bars, etc.. That's nice.

So if you have trouble keeping buds in your ears, try these. They are the best I've found so far.

product_title: HiFiMan - HE-500 Headphones
review_headline: Best headphone I’ve ever heard and ever plan to
review_body:
A few years ago I got trapped in the world of the audiophile. That meant I started to think that spending more on headphones than some people will spend on a car wasn’t all that insane. This purchase was the culmination of that journey for me. It joins my Heir Audio 4.A’s as some of the last headphones I ever plan on purchasing.

SOUND:

This is what you really care about, right? The sound. Well, in short, if you want to hear an accurate representation of your highest-quality music than look no further. I love the sound of these. I prefer neutral, genre-agnostic headphones. If there’s bass in a track I really want to hear it. If it’s not then I don’t. I want to hear what was recorded, not what some headphone manufacturer thinks I should hear (I’m looking at you, Beats).

ERGONOMICS:

These headphones are pretty solidly built. They’re a bit heavy when compared to smaller headphones but I don’t find it to be too much or that it strains my head after long listening sessions. I would recommend the velour pads over the pleather ones if only for how they effect the sound. I’m up in the air as to which is more comfortable. The band doesn’t have a great deal of padding but, then again, it doesn’t really need it.

THE CABLE:

As far as I’m concerned this is where this headphone falls flat. The cable sounds just fine but it’s not in any way shielded and my god is it stiff! I’ve bought bare wire from the hardware store that had more flex than this stuff! I ended up getting an after-market cable for around $200. Best decision I made.

POWER:

While this doesn’t need as much power as other orthodynamic headphones, it still needs a solid amp to drive it. My AMP is a Schiit Lyr. It’s a good price and plenty powerful. I’ve also heard great things about Burson Audio if you want to take a step up in price. Either way, give this headphone a solid, powerful amp and it willsing for you.

CONCLUSION:

If you want a true audiophile headphone, don’t care about isolation and have a music collection that is truly varied, then this is the headphone for you.

BONUS POINTS:

Are you also a gamer? I am. Oh am I… This headphone has an amazing soundstage and the way I end up testing this is on games with good sound. With these headphones not only does everything sound amazingly real and vivid but I can tell exactly where anything is. Some games are better than others but in a good game I’ll be able to quickly distinguish which direction a sound is coming from, even among a myriad of other sounds.

And if I'm staying at home, I'd have my higher-quality wired speakers plugged into whatever system I'm using. So, where does that leave this product?

CONNECTING:

Hooking it up to my iMac was easy and the mac saw the device right away. No problems there, even though the device told me to enter a code number, I didn't have to. Must be a PC thing.

USAGE:

A few places that I can think of to use it:

* Outside on the patio or deck if one does not have outdoor speakers

* When one is expecting a call (not in your home) and wants to listen to music but still hear the phone ring.

* Anyplace where one does not have a speaker system and yet does have a Bluetooth device that can play music (rare).

After charging the battery for an hour or so (till the blue light goes away as directed by instructions), I walked outside to my patio and the device had no trouble still picking up the signal.

The voice command aspect is quite interesting, but somewhat limited. I was expecting this thing to start up i-tunes on command and move the volume levels. Well, I was expecting a bit too much, as usual. You have to speak very clearly and close. \\"Hello Monster Micro\\" and it asks for your command, limited to about 10 commands in all and some sub-commands once you get past these. It's not going to do a conversation with you and you must say the prompt each time. Took a while to get into that mode, sort of slow on the uptake.

SOUND QUALITY:

Outdoors the sound diminished quite a bit because there are no walls to reverberate the sound, it simply trails off into the air. But this is the same with any speaker outdoors.

The sound quality otherwise was OK. Personally, I would expect more for 200 dollars but since the size is small, it's not bad for small sized device. There is not much low end here folks. Don't go looking for a thumping bass, it's not going to happen. However, I was pleasantly surprised how nice classical music sounded on this thing. And some pop sounds were fine as well. It's not a full-aural experience that you get with good stereo speakers. Mid-range is great, but not a lot of volume power. It's about 6.5 out of the 10 that normal speakers would have in terms of power.

CONS:

There is a concern about the lithium battery. I searched all over the device for a place to get access to replace it should it die. Zero. Which means sending this into the manufacturer (and all the shipping hassles that involves) to get a new battery.

I'm not happy with the amount of packaging that the device came in, (it seemed excessive) and the niche aspect of it overall as a product bothers me a bit. If it had a place to plug in a SD card or a Flash drive and could read music and play it, I think you'd have more marketability with this particular device. It does have a mic which brings up other possibilities.

* * * * * * *

review_headline: Are we listening to the same headphones?
review_body:
These headphones are way better than any other Beats headphones I've used. I'm serious about my headphones. I listen to mostly jazz all day. I mix acoustic music. I'm stunned by the outright lies I'm seeing in a lot of these reviews. Plasticy? These things are made of metal! And I love the sound. I can't stand the studios or the pros, or the mixrs, but these sound great. I describe them as... musical. I find I prefer listening to music to these than with my trusty old Beyer Dynamic 880's,

There's so much anger against the brand. Why are there so many voracious Beats haters out there? There are many other headphone brands that cost more than their quality. I suspect it has something to do with taking something technical (the accurate reproduction of sound), and turning it into a fashion accessory. To those audiophile nerds out there for whom this irks them I say... get a life! Let people buy and wear what they want! If someone wants a fashion accessory, let them have it! Myself, I just listen to what I want to.

These would get 5 stars, but I do think they are priced too high. And whomever finds a solution to the batteries running down when you leave your headphones on with no signal, they get my 5 stars...

product_title: (NEW) AYL Portable Bluetooth Wireless Version 4.0 Rechargeable Mini Speaker System for PC / Cell Phone / Tablet / MP3 Player + 3 Year Warranty
review_headline: Cute Mini Speaker -- Smaller than the Palm of My Hand
review_body:
This tiny Bluetooth speaker surprised me by the volume it can put out, although, of course, it doesn't have the rich sound of a more expensive system. Still, this speaker is fantastic for taking on the road, putting in a corner of a dorm room, or even just moving your music from room to room. It comes with a micro-USB to USB cable and a vinyl/plastic storage bag.

It took me a few tries to get the device paired, not because of a faulty Bluetooth connection but because the directions were not clear about how to get to the pairing mode. The directions said to hold the button down until the blue light flashed \\"rapidly,\\" but the light flashes faster BEFORE it enters pairing mode. You have to hold it down for a bit longer to get the light to flash even faster. Once paired, the speaker is a breeze to use. Simply select it from your speaker choices from your device. (I wish it had a more identifiable name that something like looks like a serial number, but, hey, the connection works.) The volume button isn't as sensitive as I'd like, so, like many similar speakers, it's best to control the initial volume from the device, not the speaker.

The speaker charges through your computer or, if you have your own USB wall plug (that is, it is not included), using house current. You won't get high fidelity from this little guy, but you will get decent sound, much better than I expected from such a tiny speaker. The big drawback of a Bluetooth speaker, no matter how big or expensive, is the range: you must have your device relatively nearby for wireless connectivity. Note: I received this product from the manufacturer to review.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann

product_title: Panasonic RP-HTX7-G1 Monitor Headphones
review_body: PROS: I bought these headphones at Target for about $50 in 2007 because I was flying frequently and my dinky little earbuds weren't doing the job. I loved the style and looked forward to hearing movies and music better over the typical din of commercial air travel. And they didn't disappoint: screaming babies and jet engines really can't compete with the sound that comes through these headphones. Do they completely block all outside sound? No. I still know the baby is screaming or the plane is flying, but the reduction in interference is considerable and exactly what I wanted in a pair of inexpensive headphones.  What I was surprised to find is the dramatic improvement in sound quality over standard earbuds. All of my music is mp3 quality, so for me to own a super-high-end pair of headphones would be pretty much pointless - they only transmit what is in the source (and cancel noise). That said, the richness of sound I get from these headphones is far better than I expected.  This set is comfortable to wear for an extended period of time (8 - 9 hours with a break every 2 hours between in-flight movies). I was worried when I first bought these that the headband would absorb oil from my hair and scalp and smell bad, but thankfully that has not happened.  CON: I am a petite woman, and I appreciated that the earpieces slide on the metal bit to adjust to the size of my head. However, it took only a few months after purchase for the tension that holds them in place to release and now they slide freely up and down - no longer a great fit. In fact, one side now has no tension and the other has only a little bit, so the earpieces want to sit in completely different places on my head. I devised a work-around involving rubber bands, but this option is not aesthetically pleasing so I tend to not wear these headphones around in public. If not for this problem, I would give this product five stars.  Update: After about 6 years of use, the black "pleather" coating on the ear pieces started to flake off as other reviewers have mentioned. I found a replacement pair of ear cushions that do the job decently enough, so these headphones are still going strong. Because they don't fit me super well, I gave them to my husband and he wears them all the time.

product_title: Marantz NR1602 AV Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Amazing hardware, poor software and docs
review_body:
[UPDATED]

THE GOOD:

- Great all in one AV receiver, I've got it hooked up with one single hdmi to the TV and output to polk audio speakers, and have inputs coming in from a Mac Mini, DVD player and a Wii, and switching between inputs is a breeze (well almost, why is there no \\"game\\" button on the remote?)

- Amp is really great, beautiful sound hooked up to polk audio speakers, 50W is plenty for my setup

- Love having airplay, super easy to use

- Internet radio built-in is really a great feature (although you could do the same though airplay and a connected mac or iphone it's even simpler this way), but the interface... (see below in the bad)

- Initial setup wizards are very helpful (but good luck customizing inputs if they don't fit the presets)

- Built-in networking with firmware upgrade - nice (and I really like that it's ethernet rather than wifi although some might prefer wifi if you don't have an ethernet port next to your AV setup)

- IOS/iPhone/iPad app: when it works it's ok, but a lot of times it's slow, if they fixed that and ui it would be great.

- Web controller for the amp functions is actually decent (and much more responsive than the ios app) but the system setup part is very basic

THE BAD: (I hope someone at Marantz reads this!)

- IOS app improvements needed:
- fix the bugs, slow loading
- needs an iPad version.
- App should load the last device connected instead of going back to device connection list, back button is sometimes not responsive.
- All screens should have a refresh button to refresh status from the amp since it doesn't always do it automatically. All screens other than the device home screen should have a home button to go back to the device's home screen.
- Maybe if there's a way to preload all the favorites into a scroll list instead of the way it works right now (with up/down arrows to go through pages and it seems to connect to the amp for each page.)

- Web controller: this could have been a great feature, it's a built-in web server you can open in any web browser to access some of the unit's system settings (but not all settings for some mysterious reason), the interface for the system setup is horrible, really, this is web design from the early 90's done on a spare weekend using microsoft frontpage. This would be a really convenient way to setup inputs and favorite internet radio stations for example if it was properly designed. The interface for the amp functions (changing source/volume) is pretty decent and useful.

- On screen interface (internet radio and system menus) design is outdated, it's not too bad but looks clunky in the day of touch interfaces, completely confusing menus, clunky ui, no on-screen help/explanation for what features do.

- Remote control is not bad, but has weird omissions (no game button when it's one of the preset inputs?) and some completely mysterious buttons (docs are not much help), typical remote with way too many buttons - also the source and volume buttons are very easy to confuse, which is annoying. It would be much better if they simplified remote controls to only have input source and volume controls, and put the more advanced features in the web controller and IOS apps.

- Documentation is really badly designed and poorly written, the manual is helpful in some cases to do the initial hook ups but boy is that layout confusing and messy, and some sentences just don't make any sense at all.

- Some preset inputs cannot be changed, or I can't figure out how. The system menus to control inputs are very confusing so not sure yet if I haven't figured it out, or some settings just can't be customized.

Since the unit has internet firmware updates there's a remote chance Marantz could address some of the shortcomings, but I am not holding my breath to see morethan bug fixes and minor tweaks. If they improved the on-screen interface of the web controller and actually made it usable to control all the unit settings that would help a lot. Best hope is that the IOS app will eventually get good and will help with most of the UI problems.

CONCLUSION: A great AV receiver/amp with some very convenient features (airplay!) and some really annoying shortcomings (bad software interface design, poor ios app) but no deal breaker. I am overall happy with it.

product_title: Beyerdynamic Headphone
review_headline: Very Good Low Impedance (32 Ohm), beware impedance mismatch, Plus Update
review_body:
First, the people who say these headphones sound bad likely have an impedance mismatch. You must purchase the correct impedance (Ohms) to match your audio device(s). If you're listening through a low impedance device like an MP3 player or a computer, you must order the low impedance model (32 Ohm). If you get this wrong they will sound bad and you would need to exchange them or else purchase an high-powered amp to make your wrong choice sound good. I'm far from expert on Ohm's Law and such so google \\"headphone impedance\\" for yourself and learn as much as you can.

I bought these to replace AKG K240s (too little bass) for home studio mixing and general listening. I have the AKGs and three other pairs, all under $100. I wanted to stop messing with it and just get the best I could within reason. These 32 Ohm headphones have the overall clarity and highly defined bass that was lacking in all the others. If you get the impedance correct you shouldn't need any amplifier with these. Any inexpensive amp like the Fiio would likely degrade the already high-quality sound.

These are an open-type headphone (as opposed to \\"closed/sealed\\"). A small amount of sound is intended to exit through the backs of the ear-pieces to make them sound more like listening to floor or bookshelf speakers. The sound leakage is just barely enough to disturb a partner who is reading or trying to sleep.

These are super-soft, padded velour-like ear-pads. The travel adjustment for the ear pieces is not great. My head is medium-large (7 3/8) but my ears and lobes are very small. If the travel was any less at all, they would be uncomfortable as they wouldn't completely fit over my ears. As it is the bottom of my lobes just barely fit to hang loosely inside the cups without touching. Anyone with a large head or large ears might find these uncomfortable for long sessions.

The cable is is not intended to be user-replaceable but is more stout than any I've owned.

The price seems to fluctuates fairly greatly so if the price puts you off, check back daily as they occasionally seem to drop below $300 and some reviewers say that they've gone as low as $199 here. Mine arrived billed at approx. $100 less than the price that was listed that day on Amazon. I'm not sure why but I'm not complaining.

Update June, 2014:

I have had these since December, 2012. I use these cans many hours each day, some days more than eight hours. They still sound great but I find the comfort fair at best for long sessions. My ears are very small so again, anyone with a large head or large ears would probably find these uncomfortable for long sessions.

These original velour pads tend to become matted every few months and need to be removed for cleaning. After one and one-half years, the thin plastic membrane that holds the original velour ear pads/covers to the set is now disintegrating and the original pads will need to be replaced the next time I take the pads off to wash them. Genuine replacement pads are fairly pricey but there are inexpensive third party foam replacement pads (not velour) here: [[ASIN:B00HBSNUO2 Brotrade 1 Pair Replacement Earpad Ear Pads Compatible With Beyerdynamic Dt880 Dt860 Dt990 Dt770 And AKG K270 K242 K271MK2 K240S K240MK2 K272HD Professional Headphone]]. Some reviewers say these 3rd party foam pads do not sound as good as the originals. I'll review the foam pads in a few months after I replace the originals and have had ample time to judge them. I'm hoping that the foam might increase the long-term wearing comfort.

[Update: After 3 weeks of heavy use I like these 3rd party foam pads better than the OEM. Very little difference in fidelity plus improved comfort. End update.]

As much as I try to take care, I have dropped these approaching or maybe even exceeding one hundred times. They have held up with no problem except a small piece of plastic broke loose. It can beglued and it doesn't affect anything so I would have to say the build quality is very good. I have run over the cable with my chair casters at least a hundred times and the original cable is still going strong.

The best thing about these, and what I was hoping for, is the overall clarity and precisely defined bass. It is here in spades. If there is a better-sounding pair of low impedance cans in the same price range I would love to know about them. These are darn good, the best I have yet experienced in this price range or lower.

product_title: Monster iSport Immersion In-Ear Headphones with ControlTalk
review_headline: Klipsch a much better and cheaper option
review_body:
Had high hopes for these. Long time user of Klipsch S4's but have gone through 2 pairs of those in less than a year. Sweating and general use always seem to fry one of the earbuds on those so I thought I'd try these. The L shaped plug, the flat wire and the \\"rugged\\" build of these jumped out at me and I was looking forward to using them. 3 months later...I wish I had bought another set of Klipsch.

Good

Sound is good. Not great, but definitely good, and certainly good enough for any non-audiophile. Great midrange, so-so base and treble not too tinny.

Noise cancellation is great. These tips make a great seal and once you get the right size, you can drown the whole world out if you wish.

Sizing options - Comes with about 5 different sizes of tips and the optional \\"clips\\" that really wedge the buds into your ear and keep them there.

Bad

Painful. It took me about an hour combining different sized tips and clips until I got the best fit possible, and they were still too painful to keep in for very long. The \\"clip\\" makes the bud put downward pressure on the cartilage in your ear and it wont take long before you decide to drop the \\"clip\\" all together.

Huge and Heavy - These buds are huge, and look a bit ridiculous in your ear. What's worse, they are heavy. I'm pretty sure the reason these things come with the clips is because they'd never stay in your ear without them. Just sitting at the computer you'd probably be alright, but if you ride, run or lift with these things...no way they're going to stay in.

Worthless in-line remote. While you're riding, be prepared for your iPod/iphone volume to max out when you're least expecting it. You;ll be riding along and all the sudden, BAM, you're going deaf. It also frequently skips ahead or restarts a song with no input from you as well. Not sure why it happens other than the inline remote just being crappily made. Also, it's heavy! The already heavy left-side earbud is noticeably heavier than the right side bud, due to the huge plastic inline remote.

I'd never buy these again, or anything else from this product line. Certainly not when other more comfortable, better sounding buds are available for less money. If the Klipsch had an L-shape plug they'd be ideal. In any event, don't waste your money on these.

product_title: iHome iP1C Studio Series Speaker System for 30-Pin iPhone/iPod
review_headline: iHome IP1 I-POD / I-PHONE Docking Station
review_body:
I've known about this particular product for quite a few years now since I read through the original reviews in many established and respected audio and videophile magazines. What many have stated is very true - it's extremely powerful for the size and the sound is much larger than the actual system foot-print. Yes, the style is rather unique as one can look upon it as a "work of art" or something that looks like speaker drivers with an incomplete enclosure.

With regard to the sound, it is true that the bass and particularly the treble can be pronounced if not too bright. However, you want a system to have this type of capability as it is this attribute that adds to a system's dynamic range, sense of spaciousness and depth. It is also true that it might appear to some that you can't really lower the treble far enough for those that are adverse to the higher octives however, one can also supplement that with adjusting the tonal aspects on their respective music device. It is much better to be able to tone a system "down" versus a dull system where you can't make it appear any "livelier" no matter how far you push the parameter settings up.

This system easily goes for $250-$300 but given it's been on Amazon for as low as $99 in recent times, there isn't much more to be said (by the way, the other well reviewed i-Home docking station, the "boombox" IP4 is also a great product which I recently got for my daughter but I can say daddy is very very elated with the above said IP1 "classic" system).

You don't have to look further than the delicate 1" silk dome tweeters that this little system can drive (and for those that like to pay for elaborate packaging, this item not only comes in a pretty outer wrapping, it is also physically well and securely packaged by Amazon).

product_title: Klipsch HD Theater SB 3 Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer
review_body:
I was looking for a replacement for a traditional 5.1 system that I was using for the last 10 years. The system was getting dated and tired; as well, the unsightly wires were tiring and I wasn't interested in hiring a crew to rip holes in my wall for a new overpriced Bose system. So I searched high and low for a replacement. I looked into sound-bar technology because I wanted a cleaner look but didn't want to sacrifice the traditional surround sound feel. Quite honestly, Klipsch was the last name that I looked at. Their tag line is \\"Keepers of the Sound\\"...and all I can say is WOW, WOW, WOW.
This system is absolutely spectacular. My room is about 20ft by 20ft with standard height ceilings so nothing out of the ordinary. But this system, with it's clean lines, uncomplicated set-up and wireless sub-woofer does not disappoint. The system has a \\"3D\\" mode which, for the purest of listeners, may not reach to the finesse level of a very high end 5.1 or 7.1 system, but this Klipsch is a super, super product that I would recommend to anyone who wants to experience a film at home in a way that I did not think possible. Watching the first 10 minutes of the Avengers was literally like sitting in the theater; complete with my couch vibrating from this thunderous 300 watt system. The room was filled with sound but nothing, absolutely nothing was lost in the experience. The dialog was crisp, the action was intense and the music filled the room.
If you are looking for a system that delivers the hype, look no further than Klipsch.

After that subwoofer cone was destroyed by a hyperactive German Shepherd puppy, and the replacement speaker (an old car sub) tore itself apart due to dryrot, I decided it was time for a powered sub.

I was all set to buy a Sony 10\\" powered sub from Best Buy for $129 or so, then it went out of stock. I found this one on Amazon and was immediately interested since it was a Yamaha. There's no other brand-name sub that compares at this price point. The others in the $100 range were either smaller, less powerful, did not play frequencies as low, or all of the above.

Once installed I let it run for several hours at a low volume for a bit of a break-in, then I turned the dial on the sub to about half and listened to some music at a moderate level. The performance was superb. A quick trip to the rap music channel confirmed that this sub gets extremely low. It's also punchy enough for rock music. The inaugural movie was \\"The Bourne Legacy\\", and again, the sub was phenomenal. It is absolutely capable of rattling the walls and filling a great room with vaulted ceilings full of bass. This thing is a STEAL at $89.

product_title: Monoprice Noise Isolating Earphones
review_headline: Impressive sound, but not for everyone.
review_body:
Monoprice may not be a well known name in the earphone world, but their 'enhanced bass' model(also known as the 8320) has amassed something of a cult following. I first stumbled upon them at a Head-Fi review and my attention was snared by their unique look and the abundant praise being heaped upon them. At only eight dollars, it was a chance worth taking.

To start, we'll tackle the packaging and accessories. Well, uhm...wait, there isn't any, is there? This is no exaggeration - the pair I ordered from Monoprice themselves did not contain any sort of packaging at all, only the earphones themselves and the tips that came fitted onto them in a small plastic bag. As many others have stated, the stock tips are unimpressive and fail to achieve a seal with most users. Replacement tips such as the Sony Hybrids work well, as do certain foam tips, but these cost just as much if not more than the earphones themselves. While likely a consequence of the tiny cost, this makes the Monoprice earphones seem like an incomplete product.

The build quality is decent. The housings are quite large and made out of plastic, but they don't feel fragile and I haven't noticed any obvious defects after months of use. The cable is another story; covered in nylon, it looks fine at first glance but tangles easily. It's also very microphonic, and wearing the earphones cable down is not recommended. Instead, loop the cable over your ear, as this will help tame the cord noise.

The comfort and fit is a bit frustrating. Even when worn over the ear, the housings are large and have some sharp edges, which is bad news for those with smaller ears. They stay in well enough once a proper seal is achieved, but using them as an exercise pair is ill advised due to the iffy comfort and the aforementioned microphonics, which are still somewhat present even when worn over the ear.

Very fortunately, the Monoprice's don't stumble when it comes to sound quality. Their greatest strengths are clarity and detail, which blows similarly priced competitors out of the water. Most budget sets feature a thick veil and a claustrophobic sound, but the Monoprice's are stunningly clear, wide and open. I will say that the 'enhanced bass' title these earphones carry is slightly misleading; don't get me wrong, they carry some punch and impact, but those looking for heavy thump for brain blasting beats won't be satisfied. The treble carries some extension, rare for a product of this price, and there is no real harshness that plagues other budget earphones.

While the Monoprice's carry some impressive sound quality for a mere $8, I still can't easily recommend them to everyone. The lack of packaging, lousy stock tips and potential comfort issues will be more than some are willing to deal with. As well, those searching for a more consumer friendly sound with heavy bass should consider something else, like a Meelectronics M9(or an M6 for those that like to exercise with their music). For sheer clarity though, I feel that the Monoprice earphones shame several competitors and certainly stand out as unique - both in sound and appearance - in this crowded price range. Recommended, but not without some reservations.

product_title: Timex T736S Dual Alarm Clock Radio with Time Projector and Jumbo Display (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I have been the owner of an older Timex Nature Sounds Alarm clock and loved it for its loud volume. However it is an older clock that had the old daylight savings time in it's memory. So I had to try and remember to set the clock forward and backward twice a year to correspond to the new daylight savings dates. I got tired of being late or early for work. So I decided to retire my beloved alarm clock. I carefully read all the reviews for alarm clocks and came back to this alarm clock as the best value for the money. I did review all types and all brands of radio alarm clocks before settling on this clock.
Now I was concerned as many of the personal reviews of this clock did state this clock was basically junk. But owning a Timex, and purchasing it through Amazon gave me the confidence to purchase the clock. (Amazon's return policy cannot be beat by anyone anywhere.)
Once I got the clock, I plugged in the clock and it did indeed automatically have my EST come up immediately. However, I wanted to set it to my work clock. It was simply wonderful to have direct type in time. (IE if you want the time to be 9:31am, just type in the 9, then 3, then 1, then the am button.)
There are many features I love about this clock. But the two features I love and need are two separate alarms and the time projector. My eyes are getting old and have a hard time seeing without my glasses. My last Timex could not be read without my glasses being put on. I can actually easily read the numbers on this clock as they are very large. But to be able to look up at my ceiling and see the time in about 12" numbers is priceless. The light is red and does not bother my sleep at all.
Now I will say the slide switches to turn the alarm on do not seem to be as heavy duty as my old push button set button. But they are tight and do not feel cheap. Only time will tell. But the previous negative reviews all seemed to have a problem according to them within days or a few weeks. Ireceived my alarm clock and started using it on October 30'th, 2012. This review is being written on December 13'th, 2012. So after 6 weeks, I can say I have had no problems with this alarm clock and it is worth every penny spent on it.
Something to be aware of and perhaps the reason for some of the negative reviews is that the alarms build up in volume. And when the alarm time arrives,......it takes a good 20 seconds before the volume gets loud enough for me to hear it. Then after 20 seconds you can start to hear the buzzer and after another 10 seconds it becomes extremely loud. The nature sounds do not take as long to reach full volume. Either way has worked flawlessly and awoken my wife and myself without fail.

product_title: JBL Cinema 300 5.1 Speaker System (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
What's in the box?

-the speakers (I should hope)
-black speaker cables (good quality) -- 3 medium length 2 longer for the surrounds
-stands for speakers (easy to attach/detach if you wall mount like I do)
-sub cable
-screws

Mounting

The speakers have keyhole mounts on the back; the center has two. They are fairly lightweight and I'm confidently mounting them with adhesive cable tie wall mounts as I live in an apartment and cannot drill my wall. The satellites have weight but are not too heavy to mount without screws.

Sound Quality

Superb. TAKE YOUR TIME to position the speakers well, especially the sub. Familiarize yourself with the sub cutoff and find a perfect range. One common tip for sub positioning (which is MASSIVELY important) is to put the sub where you sit, and crawl around the room for the place where it sounds the best. Then, put the sub there. These speakers sound great at louder volumes and good and roommate-sleeping-in-the-next-room-over volumes.

Appearance

Beautiful glossy finger-print attracting goodness. Look better in person than online. Especially the sub. That is one beautiful subwoofer. It looks like some sort of modern architecture. Alas, I wish it didn't have a rounded top as I can't put anything on top of it. I bought this with a yamaha 371 receiver. They match each other beautiful, both sonically and aesthetically.

I am incredibly happy with my purchase.

product_title: Thinksound ts02+mic 8mm High Definition Passive Noise Isolating Wooden Headphone
review_body:
I've listened to several in-ear monitors in the $100 or less range, and based on a few hours with the Thinksounds, these are the most balanced, musical set I've found by far. Since people are looking to answer the question \\"Should I buy these?\\", I'll go ahead and list the only negative I've found first. (Keep on reading for the many positives, though!) The kit includes 4 ear bud cushions, ranging in size from small to x-large. Unfortunately for me, my ear canal is somewhere between L and XL, and there's a pretty significant jump in size from the two. I don't fault the manufacturer on this; the inclusion of 4 cushion sizes is very reasonable. However, I found a good solution: I use the largest size, and insert them a little less than I'm used to. Now I've got the sound I want, with minimal fuss.

Speaking of the sound....it's incredible! Very airy, and yet there's plenty of tight, natural bass. For instance, the bass guitar on the Beatles \\"Come Together\\" has a good amount of \\"oomph\\", and the syncopated kick drum on the chorus is deep and punchy...not at all murky or unfocused. You can hear the abrupt release of the notes on Paul's bass. More impressive, the vocals, guitars and keyboards don't get lost in all this. In fact, all the detail's still in there! The subtle rockabilly reverb on John's voice... the variations in the intensity of the mildly-distorted rhythm guitar...the distinct attack of the keyboards (electric piano and organ if I'm correct)...it all blends together so evenly. Just the slightest touch of analog tape hiss lingers over quieter passages. (This is a compliment of course.)

I listen to mostly 'classic rock' instrumentation, along with jazz and some orchestral. I would describe my ideal setup as follows: give me neutral, detailed mid-range and an \\"airy but not too bright\\" high-end above all! Follow that with ample bass, but only if it's focused, punchy, and natural....and doesn't smear the crucial frequencies into a blur. The TS-2 handles this request remarkably well. (Just for fun, I sampled a couple of bass-heavy tracks from perhaps the most 'low-end enabled' album I own: Paul's Boutique. Bass freaks might not be impressed, but I was.)

The soundstage is impressive, and wide, for an in-ear monitor. It feels like the sound spreads out beyond your ears, instead of aiming directly inward at your eardrums. Every instrument exists in its own distinct space, lending more detail to the music. As a music geek, it's always fun to hear new things in songs you've listened to hundreds of times.

As a value-added bonus, these ear buds actually look good! The real wood housing is coupled to an aluminum enclosure. The combination of cherry-finish wood and silver metal are very pleasing to the eye. Way better than the cheap plastic alternatives. The build quality seems good, but if I have any issues, I'll update my review. I haven't even tested the microphone. For me, it's just a value-added bonus. My phone doesn't even have any songs on it, but I might have to drop a few on it based on this feature.

product_title: Sony MDR-XB600 Extra Bass 40mm Driver Premium Headphones
review_headline: Sony MDRXB600 Extra Bass Over the Head 40mm Driver Headphone, Black: Good for dance Music, uninspired for everything else.
review_body:
The Sony MDRXB600 (hearafter, XB600) are very good for dance and trance and funk and what have you. If you want or need nuances, that don't add up to \\"thud,\\" look elsewhere.

The Good:
Very good base response.
Nice visual and ergonomic design (except in terms of color).
Flat, tangle resistant cord.
Folding design for transport.
Compact.

The Bad:
Way too warm in everything *but* the base.
They feel a lot like plastic.
Three words: \\"the color brown.\\"

The Ugly:
See, \\"the color brown,\\" above.

If you can't brush your teeth without dance music, you will probably love the MDR600. If you listen to anything else with any regularity, your mileage *will* vary.

Sound is the point of headphones and the XB600s are not a balanced design when it comes to sound. They emphasize bass at the expense of everything else and that simply doesn't work for anything but the most in-your-face forms of dance music.

The sound: no one ever taught them the meaning of the word \\"nuance.\\"

The Sony XB600s have a very sharp, defined base response, but they suffer from the problem that audiophiles warn you about when talking about extra-base headphones: they've got nothing good to offer highs and the midrange and it shows. This makes them very limited headphones. They *need* dance music because they're very limited when it comes to anything else.

On the XB600s, the Black-Eyed Peas's numbers, \\"Boom Boom Pow\\" and \\"My Humps\\" come across as their most basic component, the rhythm that tells you when to put your feet down but the vocals and subtle percussion that hangs out in the background and gives the numbers the charm and complexity that makes them more than just a dance-hall metronome.

Sound quality like the XB600s is exclusive in that it excludes whole genres of music that require real accuracy in sound reproduction. The XB600 is good for dance music, but you really don't want to use them for classical, pop, or many forms of rock. It is hard to like Eric Clapton's, \\"Layla\\" with the guitar sounding like it's being played under a couple of blankets or the smooth, fluidity of a Bach 'cello piece hacked to pieces by 'phones that seem to strip out all the brighter contrasting notes of the 'cello's voice.

In terms of looks and physical design, the XB600s are nothing to write home about. They're... okay.

They have a sort of plastic feel to them that removes a lot of your confidence in their robustness (especially compared to the last XB-serie's steel-and-looks-like-steel design). They *do* fold, in two different ways in fact, but so what? If you want portability, you can sacrifice the thudding base and buy equivalent high-end bud headphones for around the same price and use them without having to live through the XB600's frankensound and Sony makes them.

Summing up.

I personally think the only thing that is wrong with Sony products is that I don't own more of them. Sony makes some of the best consumer-level headphones out there and has some of the best ideas. Sony is a fine company that makes fine products, but the XB600s are not one of their greatest successes.

If you're into bass, bass, bass and nothing else, the XB600s will satisfy you eminently (four stars!), but if you want to brush your teeth to anything but dance music, you can do better.

review_headline: 21st Century Must-Have--but what's with the buzzing??
review_body:
I think the idea of this product is great. USB has become the new outlet for many electronics and so it naturally makes sense to create a handy plug-in that connects right to your usual outlet. I charged up my Kindle and MP3 player with it and it worked great.

There is a distinct, mosquito-like buzz that emits from this thing though. If you're older or have weak ears you may not hear it, but if you DO hear it you will be annoyed. The curious thing is that it only buzzes when it's plugged in but not in use. If you connect a USB device to it the buzzing stops. When you unplug it, the buzzing returns. Thus, if you do not want to be driven into insanity, this outlet attachment would only be able to be used when you are actually going to be charging something. You will not want to plug it in and leave it there.

So, unfortunately, I cannot give this a positive rating. It works as advertised, it's a great idea, but the mosquito sound makes it almost useless for me. It's the kind of annoying sound that haunts your dreams and makes you think you can still hear it even after it's gone. Fix that, RCA, and you'll have a 5-star product.

The final blow is the necessity of firguring out the setup sequence by watching a light blink.  Come on, guys.  Bring back the HDR 140 that we all love. product_title: Polk Audio PSW505 12-Inch Powered Subwoofer (Single, Black)
review_body: I added one of my old Radio Shack passive sub-woofers to my Polk Monitors in my office, fed by a Yamaha AV receiver, some years ago. The speakers, recycled AV receiver and DVD player are used in my 11ft x 12ft home office to listen to my CDs as I peruse the web. My LR HDTV has a better system - including an inexpensive 10\\" Sony subwoofer. I ordered the 12\\" Polk to replace it, sending it to my office. Sadly, the new subwoofer wouldn't fit in the LR - but just fit perfectly in my office... go figure! The new Infinity speakers I also received in that order easily displaced the old Monitors. Wow! Great improvement - such classics as Paul Simon's 'Graceland' and 'The Rhythm of the Saints' albums came alive with real bass... as did several display items on shelves around the room. Several items hit the floor, adding to the experience. I'll admit that the sound level was 'significant' - but the bass was clear and unmuddied, if that's an appropriate term. The only negative I can think of affects me as a short wave radio listener. The sub-woofer's power supply, a switching type producing a rich and strong source of radio frequency interference. The noise is there as long as the subwoofer is plugged into the wall. I remedied that with a switchable outlet box, with added transient protection. An odd problem, it joins the myriad of consumer electronics in my home that must be disconnected before I can do some serious shortwave listening. Aurally, the Polk PSW505 deserved 5 stars.

product_title: RHA CA-200 Black Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones - 3 year warranty
review_headline: If you're thinking about buying them, stop thinking.
review_body:
Durability B+
Comfort A-
Value A+
Audio Quality B+
Noise Cancellation A-

OVERALL A-

These headphones are the best you're going to find in this price range since Koss bumped the portapros above 30 (HATEFUL WORDS). They're a little tight at first like a lot of the low and mid end Sennheisers, and I wear glasses so this can be a problem but the RHA's come with sufficient padding and wiggle room on the headphone mounts to accommodate a wide variety of headshapes easily.

Adjusting the headset is awkward and takes a little time, but once you get them adjusted they should stay in place for you if you're not constantly unpacking and repacking.

The detachable cord is great except it gives a lot of stethoscope effect (the only reason for an A- in sound cancellation) because of the cloth covering. I rubbed it with a little bit of oil to prevent it from scratching against my shirt and it has worked wonders. Pets and kids are jumping at me a lot, so it's nice to have songs interrupted instead of getting garroted by an excited puppy during a guitar solo. It also makes the eventual necessary storage that much easier because i can wrap the cord around the headband. I only wish I could find a good integrated mic for these.

As others have noted, you have to turn the volume up pretty high to get decent balance for a while, but once the headphones have 'broken in' a little bit the balance will come at lower volumes, saving your ears and battery life.

We really wanted a hidden antenna and, after reading the reviews of this one, we bought it. It arrived today and I installed it a few hours ago.

Holy. Living. Puck.

I was nearly at a loss for words. Not only were all of our channels crystal clear (with no wiggling of rabbit ears, and no knob turning), but we actually picked up 16 new stations (granted, they were all some version of public tv from nearby cities).

I do not work for this company, I do not work for Amazon. I am but a humble public school physics teacher. But I really cannot speak highly enough of this antenna.

And perhaps best of all, it hides right behind a quilt we have hanging on the wall!!!

review_body:
I did a side-by-side comparison between these and the [[ASIN:B006IBILRO AKG K550]]. Ultimately, I prefer the K-550 because it's a better fit (though imperfect). The ATH-A900X has a novel \\"self-adjusting\\" design, which really means that it's not adjustable. On my head, which is medium-sized, the ATH-A900X simply sag down too far. It feels like wearing a loose helmet. Plus, these headphones are huge and, for lack of a more scientific term, dorky-looking. product_title: Eton Scorpion Multifunction Radio
review_body:

Thus, don't expect to charge it, put it in your pack for a few hours and then use it. You'll have to recharge it again before use. So, the available DC plug in charger is probably not of much use.

The solar panel is slow but works. However that assumes you can carry the unit on the outside of your pack and in fairly direct sunlight for fairly long time periods (think hours not minutes). The unit doesn't seem to charge very well, or at all, in low light / cloudy conditions. The crank generation seems to work best. A saving grace is that it does seem to be usuable while charging, assuming a net positive difference.

Bottom line: given the price, it's OK but you'll have to expect to work within its limitations. That is, short immediate use bursts of a few minutes at a time then expect to have to recharge. Truly an 'emergency' device for use when other alternatives aren't available, in my view.

product_title: Ultrasone S-Logic Surround Sound Professional Headphones - Black
review_body:
I have the 580 now and once owned the 780's, but didn't compare side by side.

1. Sound: The 580 is great out of box, no eq'ing needed. Well balanced, though some might find the bass a little too fat, it will appeal to most. The mid is recessed but I don't think mids sound good in a closed headphone anyways (get the seashell effect).
As for the 780', sound is great for movies like it is advertised for. The bass has a low thud and not fat, which is great for door slams, engine rumbles and explosions. Like everyone says it is sibilant, it has a treble-y hiss sound. But this is good for sounds effects, glass shattering, etc.

2. Flaws: For the 780: the sibilance is noticeable. Sssss sounds on vocals. The feeling my hearing will hurt with the sharp treble exposure. I tried tweaking the treble on an eq, but then I couldn't get the rest of the sounds balanced, the vocals would have an a.m. radio sound midrange when I turned down the trebles, then turning down mids just messed things up more.
With 580's I can't think of anything I would tweak. The bass isn't hammer-like either, so i can listen for hours without fatigue. If you want to see what I mean by hard-bass ear fatigue, try the Klipsh image one.

3. Both on comfort: The foam thing at the top gets uncomfortable, feels hard. But since these go around your ear, I have no ear pain and can wear at work all day.
Also, it blocks out high sounds like waterfalls but not only muffles talking ok. My senheiser cx20's blocked noise better, though talking was blocked better it was still audible. Cx20's sound was pretty great too but I was getting wax pushed in over time (sorry)

I recommend 580 for closed. However, if you dont need noise isolation my beyerdynamic dt 990 beat any closed headphone by a mile.
Note: Yes i burned all my headphones by playing overnight for about a week. Some say 150 hours burn for 780 but that is ridiculous, not worth it if that is truly required

edit: after about 9 months, the seam started to tear about a quarter of the circle. After using the dt990 I think these and all closed headphones sounds compressed and cupped. And in ear monitors like my cx20's sound almost as good.

product_title: Sony CD Walkman« Portable CD Player
review_headline: Battery placement, button placement are not great.
review_body:
This would be my third Sony Walkman over a period of a decade (or more). The first lasted forever (years), took tons of abuse, traveled well, and was great. It eventually started skipping, and then died. The second also worked well the first year, then I stopped using it as much, and it eventually started skipping badly, and by year two I replaced it with this model. I'm assuming Sony just isn't making these quite as well as they use to, based on some of the reviews.

This one works well, thus far (one month in), almost daily use. No skipping. Sound is the same (good quality). Otherwise, I don't really care for this model. Battery placement is a nuisance unlike past models. I purchased this one for a relative, who is technologically challenged. The two previous models' buttons were on the top, easy to see and use, larger in size. The operational buttons on this newer model are on the side, very small, and a bit hard to see. I set this up with a power source, and some small speakers and subwoofer, so it is not used as a `walkman', but rather as a cd player that is not moved unless it must be turned on or off, etc. (because accessing the buttons is impossible without picking it up).

For my purpose as stated above, this model is an inexpensive alternative to a full sized CD Player, and works \\"okay\\" in that capacity. Judging from reviews of other models, this seems to be the best of the units. Here's hoping it'll last a while.

review_body:
Fact:
HD over the air (OTA) is uncompressed, and is a better quality than Cable or Satellite:

I have the ClearStream 4 and 5. Yes you need both...one VHF, the other UHF....while you might get some bleed-over and pickup a VHF on a UHF antenna, quit being cheap and do it right. Get two mounting poles, 30 or 40\\" each...you cannot fit both of these on one pole. When mounting, keep them a couple of feet apart.

I live 35miles from the transmitters (Wash DC area), and pickup all the usual local channels in HD no flickering no static, just clear HD. I mounted these in my attic, no problems.

Look at antennapoint.com and see where you are in relation to the towers. Look on tvguide.com put in your location and select OTA to see what stations you will get OTA.

Note: One of the antenna comes with a signal combiner to mux together the UHF and VHF signal. Use a 3' cable for each and antenna to the signal combiner. If you're missing any channels, or a bit skippy in the reception...get the Winegard 8700 amp, works great.

product_title: Grounded Universal 2 in 1 Plug Adapter
review_headline: This is a great dual plug adapter for people going to South Africa!
review_body:
It has been a long time since I have been to Joburg but if you are going there you need one of these. This is a plug that has the socket to plug into their AC wall socket and it fits a long list of other countries mating plugs.

This adapter is first class quality and safely insulated to protect you while using it. I have used the smaller travel kit size plugs hundreds of times. On occasion I felt they were not safe especially when you were trying to unplug them from a 220 VAC socket and you had to put your fingers into the socket recess to unplug the small travel kit sized adapter. This is more of an industrial quality. This one is suited for people going to South Africa and wanting to plug in their power plugs from America or from the UK, Ireland, China, Australia, Italy, Switzerland, India, Israel, Singapore or Europe. It is important that you read which country's plugs the adapter will fit into and also make sure that your appliance plug will fit into the adapter. This is a rugged and heavy duty style adapter and it is well made. The outlet side of the adapter will accept two plugs for the countries listed above. One outlet plug can be grounded and the other ungrounded.

One of the major issues of overseas travel is having the right plug to get AC power to charge or use your devices. You would think that with all of the global standardization on some items that this would be something universal but it couldn't be more complicated. You have to do your homework before you leave home and make sure that you carry the right adapters with you or device with you.

Plug adapters simply change the physical/mechanical shape and plug style of the plug and they do nothing to adapt the voltage or frequency of the AC power. I will provide a list of items to check for your travel.

Items to check:
1. Check the voltage and frequency of your devices. If they have a switch to change the voltage from 110 VAC to 220 VAC that is good and such devices are usually items like hair dryers and curling irons.
2. Note that changing the voltage with a switch has no effect on the frequency of the power and your 60 Hz hair dryer will operate slower at 50 Hz than it will at 60 Hz.
3. Some more modern devices like laptop computers, electronic tablets, mobile phones come with chargers that will operate on 110 or 220 VAC and 50 or 60 Hz. These are sometimes called universal power supplies. This is much easier but you still have to carry an adapter to fit the plug style for the country you are in.
4. If you have a device that uses only 110 VAC or 220VAC only then you must also carry a step up or a step down transformer to convert the voltage to the proper level for your device. You must also make sure that the transformer is capable to output enough watts to power the device you are trying to use. A transformer rated at 150 watts for example will not operate an electric hair dryer rated at 1200 watts. When you are talking about high power devices it is really best to purchase one that can use 110/220 VAC with a switch selection built into it. Just remember to select the right voltage before you plug it in and use it!
5. You can buy a power converter to use with AC devices but to be honest I never used them as they are not as safe or as universal as a transformer. Modern electronic devices are not safe with these converters and frankly the more modern devices have the universal power supplies that I mentioned and you will not need a transformer or a converter to charge and use your device. You will just need a plug adapter.
6. Most countries use the same power ratings country wide but there are exceptions like Japan and Brazil. When in doubt always ask and check the wall plug to see if it is marked like in a hotel.

I can't imagine it sounding much better for those two cans when I pair them with the DAC-100, diminishing returns have definitely set in! For lower-impedance headphones, like Audez'e, HifiMan, Grado, I wouldn't recommend this as a headphone amp, but for high impedance headphones this amp really shines. I also use this as a DAC/pre-amp for my 2 Polk towers, and they've never sounded better. If you need a high quality DAC and/or a high quality headphone amp for high-impedance headphones, this is a product to seriously consider.

product_title: Creative Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: The future is near. It's hear! I mean here!
review_body:
I needed a decent set of speakers to fill a small-ish flat with music and movies. The D200s do this VERY well, and you'll be hard pressed to find better speakers for the money. You'd be hard pressed to find better speakers for even 1.5x the money!

Here's a quick overview of how I use them. I own an Early 2011 Macbook Pro 15\\", Blackberry Playbook, Samsung Galaxy S3 (Android 4), iPhone 4S, Asus Transformer (TF101), and 2008 white Macbook. All have built-in bluetooth and all stream seamlessly to the speakers. No extra drivers/software needed. It's awesome being able to connect all these devices to the same set of speakers. Note that only one device at a time can be paired with the speakers.

The speakers have a power button on the back which puts them into low power standby. They can be wakened simply by connecting to them on your device and then outputting sound to them. No need to go to the speakers and switch them back on. I have noticed they appear to stay on forever if you don't switch them off which is a bit of a bummer since automatic standby would be more convenient, since they can be woken up wirelessly.

How do they sound? Great! They pack a good amount of bass, sometimes a bit too much, making lower quality video audio sound muffled (especially voices). They can be cranked up pretty high too without distortion; just make sure to crank them on the speakers themselves rather than maxing our your device volume. The speaker and device volume are independent.

I highly recommend them if you're looking for a relatively compact pair of bluetooth speakers with good sound for an awesome price.

product_title: HDMI-High-Speed
review_headline: Now that's great HDMI. Works great. Good Value.
review_body:
The [[ASIN:B003XM1WE0 BlueRigger High Speed HDMI cable with Ethernet, Supports 3D and Audio Return (10 Feet)]] appears to be well made from quality materials. I especially like the woven heavy nylon outer insulation. It's flexible and durable.

I used it in my bedroom home theater setup to connect the audio/video via HDMI from a [[ASIN:B005CLPP84 Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player]] to my wall mounted [[ASIN:B004MN8HYW Samsung PN51D550 51-Inch 1080p 600 Hz 3D Plasma HDTV (Black) [2011 MODEL]]]. Since I haven't spent the extra $$$ to upgrade the Sony STR-DE945 receiver to an AVR with HDMI capability, I needed to find a creative way of getting Dolby 5.1 surround sound to the Sony receiver. I then used a [[ASIN:B005LJQOPK BlueRigger Digital Optical Audio Toslink Cable (15 feet)- CL3 Rated]] connected to the digital optical output of the Samsung HDTV to the optical digital input of the receiver.

The BlueRigger HDMI cable's outer insulation is made of such a durable woven nylon material that it retains a \\"memory\\" from being coiled up in the shipping box. When I connected it to the [[ASIN:B005CLPP84 Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player]], it twisted and wouldn't allow the light little box to sit flat on the AV stand. I recommend that the cable be stretched out flat on the floor. I placed a heavy (2 - 3 lb.) book on the cable at the ends and a couple in between for a few hours until the cable lost this memory and no longer twisted when I finished connecting the components. I hid the cable and all others running to and from the wall mounted tv with a [[ASIN:B0015EA3NO Wiremold CMK30 Flat Screen Television Cord Cover Kit, White]] that I painted to match the wall's paint. Now I can watch movies streamed from the [[ASIN:B005CLPP84 Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player]] in Dolby 5.1 surround sound and I have saved some $$$ at least for now until I decide that I simply MUST upgrade the receiver to a modern HDMI 3-D ready AV receiver.

review_body:
[By the way this is Bethanne's Son reviewing}

I purchased these earbuds about a month ago and they sound good. For those of you who want to get crazy bass out of these skullcandys consider using a headphone amplifier. I'm using $100 digiZoid ZO portable headphone amp [[ASIN:B00747N5ZE Digizoid ZO 2 Personal Subwoofer]] and these earbuds sound absolutely amazing!! They have very clear but powerful bass without over powering the rest of the music. They have very decent sound stage creating a surround sound feel with a clear division between instruments. Be careful to take the earbuds slowly out of your ears to avoid inverting the speaker cone and scaring yourself into thinking you have broken your new earbuds. You will know if you have inverted the speaker cone if you hear half volume out of one ear. To fix it simply blow into the speaker to pop the cone back into its original shape but be aware that inverting the speaker cone is not good for the earbuds and should be avoided if possible. To sum it up these headphones are great with or without an amp but if you want crazy bass I recommend an amp.

review_headline: Hours of tech support and still does not work
review_body:
Four tech support calls, two days, probably six hours of effort and it still doesn't turn on my TV correctly. Working with tech support I have become an expert in every aspect of remote controls, and this is a very bad sign because I got the Harmony just so I could control my devices without effort. I'm an engineer and good at setting up hardware and this Harmony system just doesn't work well. It turns out the Harmony Touch, being the newest model, hasn't had all the software features implemented like in the older models. So you buy the latest greatest model and get less capability. They plan to upgrade the fimware but there is no estimated time for that to happen. The Harmony is tripping up over powering on commands and switching inputs commands. To fix this you can edit the steps it takes, but the editing of steps is so limited (many remote commands cannot be used; time delays cannot be inserted where you want, etc, etc) as to be of no help. Numerous other buggy issues.

The build seems good. Second level support is supposed to contact me. I'll see if they can help because I really don't want to use my four orignal remotes. review_headline: Replacement DLP Bulb for my Toshiba TV
review_body:
***** Update November 2013 *****

I've had the bulb a year now. No problems at all, works great.

I did notice that the vendor I bought it from is no longer listed as a seller... And looking at all the negative reviews of failed bulbs I'd caution anyone who buys this to look into who the seller is. The one I bought from was a legit used electronics recycler who also had their own webpage selling stuff too.

My review is still 5 stars, cause the bulb I got has been great. And as far as I could tell, it was genuine Toshiba.

****** Original Review *******

I have a 52\\" Toshiba DLP television, about 7yrs old. The first bulb lasted about 3 yrs, the 2nd (replaced under extended warranty from Toshiba) lasted about 3 yrs. After it blew I looked for a less expensive alternative and bought an \\"OEM-Compatible/Equivalent\\" bulb from a large eBay bulb seller. The first one from them was very dark so I returned it (at my cost, ~$15 bucks!) and they sent me another. The 2nd bulb never seemed to get as bright as the original Toshiba one and would flicker after starting up for a few minutes. But for ~$65 bucks I kept it. Almost exactly 12 months later, it blew. So this time I wanted to find a \\"real\\" OEM bulb without paying stupid Toshiba prices...

I found this one on Amazon for a great price and bought it. I also like that the vendor is basically recycling damaged, but new TV equipment (check out their website [...])

It arrived on time, well packaged. I had it installed in minutes and my TV up and working again.
The picture was brighter with this bulb than when using the \\"oem-equivalent\\" I purchased last time. The picture came up quicker too and without any flicker.
The bulb did say \\"Toshiba\\" on it, so I assume it truly is a Toshiba bulb.

A bit of a surprise, but possibly a cost savings on Toshiba's part, the housing was all plastic (whereas my old ones had metal) and the lens cover is only a vertical strip of plastic vs. a whole circular lens. My first two Toshiba OEM bulbs had entire circular lens so when the bulb blew it was all contained, no mess. My last \\"oem-equivalent\\" bulb did not, so after removing the blown bulb I had to use a vacuum to get the remainder of the bulb out of the TV (and be careful removing the blown bulb). I assume when this one blows I'll have to do the same clean up routine.

I'm only a few days into using this bulb and if anything negative happens, I'll post an update. I'm pleased to see the vendor does offer a 12 month warranty which gives me more confidence that this is a true Toshiba OEM bulb.

product_title: Sony WMDDT1 DAT Walkman Digital Audio Tape Player
review_body:
© 2012 Amazon member Portable Goodness. No unauthorised reproduction permitted.

Description

The WMD-DT1 DAT Player was released around 1993, so clearly any you buy now will be a used item. It's a well made unit with a sliding cover to hide the main controls when not in use. This model is I believe the world's smallest playback only DAT player (only micro DATs beat it size wise). It runs on two AA batteries (expect around 4-6 hrs) and can take a mains adapter (3 volt centre pin +). Tape Loading is quick; The WMD-DT1 gives a quick spin of the tape forward then back to assure correct tape tension etc. It has standard FFW RWD controls along with track search in both directions. Talking of which they are tactile and well placed; the whole unit (battery door aside) is well thought out. Aesthetically, it's attractive and high end. Handling and operating the unit is pleasing and satisfying.

Things to look out for are the battery door catch issue (they are often broken, mine proved fixable with small Velcro strap) and the nice rubberised finish on the left hand side of the player can wear off. This appears to be an afterthought by Sony as the rubber was applied directly to the shiny plastic bodywork with seemingly no prepping of the surface (it's also rather thin). If using the remote control with headphones it utilities one of Sony's many proprietary plugs meaning the supplied original Sony earphones must be used (micro plug connection). Thankfully there is a separate standard 3.5 mm jack on the unit side. This DAT player is designed for those people who have a decent DAT recorder at home - this unit will play at various sample rates.

Sound

The unit is clean and unassuming sounding and never fatiguing. Freq response is very good. Initially the sound does not do anything to impress you, but here, it's a good thing. A case of long term satisfaction rather than short term appeal. Ideally you should use decent quality headphones - I've used Grado SR60'S and Sennheiser HD 590. Although these are Hi-Fi cans, the Walkman drove them with ease. The unit can sound a bit cold depending on the recording. Bass can be boosted via the R/C although I never felt the need. The sound stage was fairly good and layering of sound is usually convincing with things rarely becoming muddied or congested. Sneaker Pimps \\"Becoming X\\" can be just this...but this DAT player seems to navigate it's way through well. Bass is a little light but does not detract from the proceedings being tuneful and agile. Vocals appear well rendered. Transients are well reproduced - this may be a portable but you won't be short changed sound wise. Overall it was enjoyable to listen to.

Verdict

It's a beautiful thing to look at (for audio gear). The operation, size, sound and design make this a desirable item. Wait till you pop the tape door for the first time and see the heads; I challenge you to think anything other than \\"cute\\"! A great fun device for all those tape heads who like the advantages of DAT and fancy taking it around and about to get even more enjoyment out of it. product_title: Sony MDR-J10 Headphones
review_body:
I ordered these as a replacement for the exact same type, which were 5+ years old. Those worked just fine for many years. They occasionally would go out on one side, but fiddling with the cord usually brought the sound back. Until a few weeks ago, when I could only hear the music on the left. I ordered another, and the sound was better than my old pair. These are not fancy headphones meant for audiophiles, they're sport-style headphones meant to stay in place during a workout. I find most earbuds uncomfortable (though I haven't tried any really pricey ones, my limit is under $15 for now), maybe because I have small ears.

These headphones stay in place relatively well at the gym, but on a run around the neighborhood, I find myself fiddling with them quite a bit. One reason for this problem is that there's no clip, and I wear them attached to my Motoactv which I wear on my wrist. My arm moves back and forth, and the cord is jostled up and down, so the earphones tend to get jiggled out of place. Being able to clip these to my shirt would help keep them in my ears and would probably also result in a longer life for the cord. All the bouncing is most likely what finally took out my old pair.

For the record, I have tried threading them under my shirt, but the movement of my arm is still just too much. Again, being able to clip these to my shirt would really help. For the price though, these are great for someone who wants sport-style earphones for workouts. They are not sound isolating, which is good if you exercise outdoors and want to be able to hear what's going on around you.

product_title: ELPLP49 Complete Replacement Lamp Module
review_body:
I wanted to add my 2 cents since this bulb has such inconsistent reviews.

I was hesitant as none of the bulbs Amazon carries had consistently good reviews, but I was even more hesitant to plop down 300 bucks for an OEM replacement when 3rd party ones were a quarter of the price. I purchased this bulb and it arrived quickly (via PRIME), well packed, and no damage to any box. The bulb itself was also well packed and safe inside it's own box. Yes, it's 3rd party and does not look identical to the OEM Epson bulb, but it installed and fits fine, screws and all. My projector is mounted on the ceiling, so the one reviewer that noticed the bulb was missing a screw was cause for concern, but mine turned out just fine. The moment of truth, the projector powered up fine and the picture was just as good as before. Initially I thought it wasn't as bright as OEM, but turned out it just takes this bulb longer to fully warm up vs OEM. That longer warm-up time is the only negative I can see so far, but if I have to wait an extra 10 seconds or pay 4 times the price, I will gladly wait the extra 10 seconds.

One other item that deserves mentioning. These bulbs contain mercury, so they cannot be simply tossed in the trash. The seller included a free return shipping label to send the bulb back for proper recycling. They even included a little pamphlet stating they make no money from recycling, and it actually costs them a little, but it is nice to see a company being responsible and helping the environment when they can.

I hope to have a favorable review in 6 months as well. I guess I did pretty well with my OEM bulb, over 2200 hours before it died. I hope to get close with this bulb too.

But unlike the other automatic time set feature on most other clocks, this one is preset to a timezone and time. And you actually have to set the time instead of it determining what the actual time really is. The support for DST is partial at best. There is a button to enable/disable DST but that part is manual, much like the setting of the alarm clock.

Not exactly what I was expecting but should have known given the cost. It is slightly better than old alarm clock in the way it can actually support DST. My previous only had logic for the previous rules for DST which are no longer in support so I had to manually set the clock on back to back weekends twice a year.

Overall, a good basic alarm clock with all the standard features.
