product_title: SOL REPUBLIC Tracks HD On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Top Alternative to Beats By Dre
review_body:
I wanted to learn more about these headphones after seeing Michael Phelps wearing them at the Olympics, and I'm sure that's the case for a lot of people. I figured if he had them as a celebrity in a non-TV commercial capacity but truly for personal use, they probably sound good. After reading about them and reading reviews online, I decided to buy a pair and would just sell them if I didn't like them. I normally don't hesitate to try headphones or earphones, but I had kind of sworn never to buy headphones that cost more than $100. I had tried the Beats by Dre at Best Buy and didn't like what I heard, and I thought they were definitely overpriced for the sound quality. I sort of worried that headphones over $100 were largely a ripoff.

I absolutely loved the headphones when I first tried them and felt they were worth the money. I thought the bass level was pretty much exactly what I'd been looking for--I'd been wanting something like an SUV sound system in my ears. Normally, it takes me time to like headphones and then as I adjust to them they sound better, unless they are just awful from the get-go.

This was kind of the opposite.

Now that I've had these headphones for a while, I have more criticisms.

Comfort

At first, my only problem with them was that they were uncomfortable after about an hour. Apparently, these headphones are comfortable for some people and not for others. If this helps add any perspective, I will say that all headphones with this sort of big ear-cup design hurt my ears. I think these, in particular, are just too tight and put too my pressure on my ears. I also have an asymmetrical head with the left ear being bigger, and that's the ear that these headphones seem to bother the most. So, if big cup headphones bother you or you have an asymmetrical body type or big ears--which I think the majority of people do have asymmetrical bodies--these probably will be uncomfortable to you after a while. This is a pretty big strike to me, because I like to sit and listen to music for hours. And with these, I'm always having to adjust the \\"cans\\" on my ears because they get uncomfortable. I do wear glasses, but the glasses are not really the problem--it's the way the cans press against my ears.

Sound Quality

Most of the time, I still feel these headphones have the kind of bass I was looking for and satisfactory sound quality. Sometimes, the sound strikes me as a little bit muddy, particular in the mids. Sounds are not always as crisp as I'd like, and I think that at least some of the time that's about how I have the cans situated on my ears--not always just about the song in question, the track's quality, the genre or the headphones' shortcomings (although I think all of these play a role at some point). I have tried to play around with positioning the headphones because of the discomfort they cause my ears, but that and readjusting the cans because of discomfort definitely seem to affect the sound quality and the amount of bass I'm hearing. I wish I could just sit and not have to fiddle with the headphones at all, but that's just not the case because they get uncomfortable or they slide a little out of position enough to affect the sound. I can't really slide the cans up the headband more, either, without them not fitting perfectly on my ears or becoming more uncomfortable than they already are.

One of the reviews I read here said there's minimal sound leakage at full volume. That's just not true. I would say \\"in my opinion,\\" but there's just no way that's an opinion. A few days ago, I took my headphones off and laid them to the side...I thought I had unplugged them from my laptop, and I started streaming a talk show from the internet. Normally, if sound is coming from headphones that are plugged up, you know because the sound is not loud and not clear--especially if you're listening to people talking through the headphones. For quitesome time, these headphones were still plugged into my laptop, but I thought the show was playing through my laptop speakers--that's almost exactly what it sounds like if you put these headphones down and turn something up full blast in a largely silent environment...that or iPhone speakers. It's not going to be that way with the cans covering your ears, obviously, but there's bound to be leakage. This was the loudest and clearest I've ever heard headphones lying around--I could hear what people from the talk show were saying perfectly.

And this matches what another review here was saying about using these cans as portable speakers--you really could. I wouldn't, just because, like I said, they sound like laptop speakers (which sound horrible, to me) and the sound is not quite loud enough. But if this doesn't bother you, they could be used as speakers.

Style

They're a little bit ugly (the cans part) and bulky, to me. The good thing is you can buy the headband in different colors. I bought my pair from Best Buy, and when I went to Best Buy not only were these headphones seemingly hidden (in favor of the Beats family) but there were very few of them and only one color for the HD pair--black--when I wanted the white one. You might run into that issue if you buy these in the store, but you can come online and get blue, white, grey, etc. Because of that, I might buy another color or two in the near future. I haven't seen some of the ugly colored headbands/cans that Phelps wore at the Olympics, but even he had a few different colored headbands and cans. The other really good thing about these headphones is if something goes wrong with one part, you don't have to dish out another $130 for a completely new pair. You can just replace the cans or the headband or the cables. Again, the internet might be your friend there.

--
Conclusion

I now question whether or not I would buy these if I had it to do over again, to behonest, especially given the comfort issue. I think if it weren't for that, I'd still be on cloud nine with these headphones. I don't think the sound quality is perfect, but it's amazing for the money and what other big name brands out there offer at higher prices. I think this is the closest you can come to the higher-end Beats by Dre without spending that amount of money. I have cheaper earphones that I was happy enough with overall, despite not getting big bass, and I think the comfort issue could end up driving me back to those, ultimately...which I feel is a shame.

Let me start off by saying, this is not my first sound system I have ever owned. My last one was bose 5's and 7's, Harmon Kardon receiver and a validyne 1200 watt sub-woofer. Yea, killer system for sure, but pricey!
Now to the Onkyo system. Always heard good things about them, but was hesitant to purchase a home theater in a box. Never as good as buying individual components, but a lot less expensive.
Without reading the instruction booklet, I hooked everything up. I installed 16 gauge wire, instead of the thin wire that came with this unit. However, really could not tell the difference. Just an FYI on that. Use the EQ setup in the full mode. This is a great way to set up the sound for your individual room you are sitting in. Takes about 10 minutes and worked great. Highly recommend doing this!
I went with the high front speaker setup instead of the back speaker setup. Didn't like looking at the back of the speakers when entering the room. Actually, wife didn't, so there! With the speakers set up this way, the sound was great. So, what I have are a left and right front, left and right high, center, left and right surround and a sub working. What they consider the surround are the speakers mounted on the wall across from where you are sitting, just for clarity.
All in all, thought the manual was confusing, but doing the EQ setup, makes up for it. Is this as good as my other setup? No, but compared to what I spent on that system compared to this, this is a good sound for the money. If you want a knock out system that rocks the house, get separate components, but do your home work.

product_title: Yurbuds Ironman Inspire In-Ear Earbud Sport Headphones with TwistLock Technology Earphones, Sweat Resistant, White
review_headline: Doesn't like to stay in my ears
review_body:
The reviews here seem to be split between people who can't get these earbuds to stay in while exercising and those that can.

I've seen the video instructions from Yurbuds on how to put these in your ear and I've read the instructions and tips from people on many internet boards. I can get these to stay in my ear until I start to sweat during my run. The molded end-cap is made of vinyl so it becomes slippery when wet with sweat. The cords are thin don't have a 'slick' coating on them, it's more like a rubber coating and they seem to 'grab' on clothing. This causes the a slight tug on the earplugs when running (I wear the cords down my back and into an iPhone arm band).

When they slip or pop out, not 'if' but 'when', it's almost impossible to get them to stay in place in my ear again because now the vinyl earplug is wet with sweat and it has nothing to grip on while in my ear.

That's my experience, anyway. I know several others here haven't had that problem, so YMMV. I'm going to be returning them for something else, I just don't know what I'll go to yet.

UPDATE 9/10/12: I contacted Yurbuds customer service about my issues. They responded very quickly, within 1 business day, and asked me to provide more info. They asked for a close-up picture of a quarter next to my ear (to help determine sizing). After sending that to them, they responded 2 days later with another request for a picture of the Yurbuds in my ear (again, for sizing). I sent that in to them.

One day later and they responded letting me know I needed a different size Yurbud. I had size 5 and needed a 4. They were sending me size 4's and should expect to receive them in a few days.

Four business days later and I had a pair of brand-new Yurbuds, size 4. I have to admit that I'm very impressed with how well this company stands behind their product and responds to customer issues. I will be trying the new Yurbuds in the next few days and will update my post.

UPDATE 9/19/12: After using the new, smaller Yurbuds, the problems of them falling out of my ears remain. I'm glad many here have been able to use these and have them stay in, it just doesn't work for me. As I mention in my review, I've viewed the videos and web pages on how to insert these into your ears, so it's not like I don't know how to use them.

The second, and almost as import, gripe I have about these are the cords. They're made of rubber and there's a high 'friction' level with them. When they rub against any of my clothing the cord seems to 'grab' the clothes. This causes a pull on the Yurbud and more often than not, it pulls out of my ear. This has happened while running, sitting, moving, turning my head to look around, etc. I'm sure the rubber coating is good for keeping moisture out, but it's a terrible idea when being used for something that's advertised as being designed for athletes.

I still have good things to say about Yurbuds customer support. They were responsive and really tried to solve my problem. Other than that, I can't recommend this product. I moved to MEElectronics M6-BK wrap-around earbuds instead (see my review here: [[ASIN:B0038W0K2K MEElectronics M6-BK Sport Sound-Isolating In-Ear Headphones for iPod, iPhone, MP3/CD/DVD Players (Black)]]).

UPDATE 10/17/12: After having lived with these headphones for several weeks now, I have really grown to hate the cords. As I mentioned previously, they are 'high-friction' cords that seem to 'grab' on my clothes. This happens every single time I use these headphones! I have a polyester jacket and these cords seem to 'stick' to the jacket all the time, pulling the earbuds out. I can't understand why Yurbuds would choose this material to make cords. It's terrible! I now use these earbuds as little as possible and only when I don't have my M6-BK's with me.

review_headline: Antenna does what it says! Great reception!
review_body: I am an Over the Road truck driver that has a dedicated run, which means, basically, that I go to the same place most of the time. My run takes me from York, PA to Georgetown, IN, which is approximately 7-8 miles from Louisville, KY. I had a \\"truck stop\\" mirror mounted tv antenna in my truck that was ok, but reception wasn't always the best, and I felt like there should be more channels that close to a major city (Louisville)! Upon reading other reviews of this product, I was convinced that it HAD to be better than what I had! I was going to purchase this product at WalMart, but at $80.00, I was reluctant to spend that much in this economy, while I already had something that \\"worked ok\\". I found one that was \\"refurbished\\" on Amazon for $9.99 plus shipping! I couldn't resist that deal! Upon receiving the antenna, I decided to do a test between the new and the old! I left my old antenna hooked up, and did a \\"channel scan\\". The scan revealed \\"15 channels\\", but after going thru the channels, I discovered that only 12 channels actually came in (three were completely non-existent, black screens!), and of the 12, probably 3 of those were very pixelated and \\"choppy\\"! I installed the new ClearStream Micron-R antenna, placed it on my dashboard, and ran the same channel scan once again! The new scan revealed that I now had 25 CHANNELS! I ran a test through the channels, and virtually EVERY CHANNEL worked! Some of the channels were slightly pixelated and choppy, but still very watchable! I am extremely happy with the antenna! The only bad thing that I could say about it is that, in a truck setting (not mounted, moving it back and forth to the dashboard, etc.), it tends to come apart alot! Not really a problem, as putting it together is very simple....just a pain sometimes! Other than that, it works GREAT, and I couldn't ask for anything better....except maybe a Directv Dish on my truck! LOL! Don't hesitate to buy this antenna, especially if you can find a \\"refurbished\\" deal like I got! Thanks to Antennas Direct for a great deal!

product_title: Belkin 7-Outlet Home/Office Surge Protector
review_body:
A Belkin Surge protector with a serious design flaw gets a one star rating, especially considering the high prices of Belkin Products which bring high expectations. The surge protection function, and Belkin's warranty and customer service, however they may be, are not addressed in this review.
This product is marketed and priced for its aesthetics, particularly the flat plug, which leaves no excuse for Belkin to have incorporated a bonehead design flaw in the product.
This surge protector has slots in the rear so the unit can be aligned with screws properly positioned in the wall and then repositioned downward so it is locked in place over the screwheads. The screwhead slots are placed \\"backward\\". If the surge protector is mounted vertically on a wall, it needs to be mounted upside down or it will not lock in place over the screwheads. If it is mounted upside down, it will still function, but it will look terrible and the ground hole on the 3 prong receptacles will be upside down. This is a stupid inexcusable design flaw and it indicates a lack of quality control or accountability in Belkin;s design department. If Belkin is so lax about putting expensive products into production that have aesthetic design flaws, how can the consumer be confident that Belkin takes pains to ensure that its protective products really protect. For example I have no idea whether this product really protects against surges to its rated design specs, nor would I have any easy way of finding out. I trusted Belkin. If Belkin screws up the aesthetics and still delivers a product that protects against surges as it should, its not that big of a deal. But this experience makes me wonder whether Belkin can be trusted to protect the electronic equipment upon which so many of us depend.

product_title: La Crosse Technology BC-700 Alpha Power Battery Charger
review_headline: Effective charger for AA & AAA batteries
review_body:
When I made the decision to start using rechargeable batteries, little did I realize you really need to be an electrical engineer to be successful at this endeavor.

However, it soon became evident that my 'Everready 15 Minute Charger' was leaving my batteries useless after only a few charges.

So, I embarked on additional research. Wow - talk about confusing! 200 mA charging; 2500 mAh capacity; 350mA discharging (700mA charging); Capacity (mAh) / Current (mA) = 1/C.

Huh? All I want to do is recharge my rechargeable batteries.

Well, after you get past the details of electrical science, the La Crosse Technology BC-700 is a very effective - and fairly easy to use - charger that keeps your rechargeable batteries working at their full capacity.

You SHOULD understand at least the basics of the charge modes (Charge, Discharge, Test and Refresh). For batteries that have lost capacity, you need to run in the DISCHARGE/REFRESH mode to restore their ability to hold a full charge. While this can take several days or more, it very effectively restores batteries to their full capacity. Also, as you read from the input of the 'electrical scientist' reviewers, a lower charge rate is usually better (however, the La Crosse defaults to that lower charge rate).

Anyway, I'm up and running with rechargeable batteries thanks to this unit!

product_title: TERK Dual-Drive, Amplified Indoor / Outdoor FM Antenna
review_body:

I replaced the 300 ohm lead-in from this antenna with shielded coax (as recommended by another reviewer) and instantly received a better signal, but still not usable.

At this point I ordered the Terk FM Pro antenna. Amazing! I received a clear signal with no hint of background noise of any kind! I then attached the power unit to the antenna, but as soon as I switched on the power, I got a hiss and a lot of background noise! I tried using the \\"amplifier\\" at both ends of my 75 ohm shielded coax. When it was connected at the antenna end, the results were better, but still not as good as with the antenna alone. Maybe some guru in the audience can explain that to me . . . Bottom line, I am happy to report that I can now enjoy hiss and static free, crystal clear, FM music in my shop!

review_headline: Epson Power Lite Cinema compatible ..... sort of
review_body:
Now its a given every set of glasses acts differently with different hardware. These Glasses actually do work with the Epson projectors i have an Epson PowerLite Home Cinema 3010.

here is the review essentially and make of it what you will.

The glasses are wonderfully comfortable and its a shame the rest did not match up. They fit nice with a good amount of bend and they do not have issues with to much frame being visible. They also sit on the nose extermely well.

That being said its the only great part of the glasses.

1.) they do not sync when just turned on. If its documentation that was missing from my shipment thats possible but I had to fiddle with it to get it to sync. Essentially when I first turned it on it would sync for 2 seconds and then lose sync and the IR emitter position is not the problem as 2 epson and 1 sony worked just fine.
To get it to work you have to turn them on let them fail and then tap the power button 1 time ( do not hold as they will turn off ). This sometimes synced first try sometimes second or third but it always worked. I could of lived with this.

2.) The major downfall of the glasses in my evaluation of them was extreme ghosting or crosstalk. It was very easy to see the other frame in the other eye to the point you could very easily notice it on contrasted areas. It seemed that the refresh rate was bad on the glasses they just do not get that opaque in comparison to others. This is a catch 22 with glasses currentl on the market since it was also a pair of glasses that seemed to have less of a tint than the sony or epson glasses.

If it wasnt for the crosstalk I could justify a 4 but then again if it wasnt for how comfortable the glasses are I would have given them a 2.

product_title: Diesel Vektr by Monster
review_headline: Stunning sound - crisp, balanced, perfect; stylish design with comfortable earpieces
review_body:
Diesel Vektr by Monster strives to be a stylish and sleek set of headphones that delivers crisp dynamic sound. With the partnership between Diesel and Monster, I was intrigued to give this a try. I am not disappointed. I am pleasantly impressed with the sound quality and comfort of the Diesel Vektr.

* Stylish design. I like the sleek, triangular look on the sides of the headphone. It has a glossy and sleek look. Very jaggy and edgy.

* The sound is amazing. Out of the box, the sound is crisp and balanced. The lows are very apparent and booming, yet the vocals, mids, and highs still sound equally as clear. Other headphones and headsets I've tried either have too much bass that overwhelms the mids and highs, or too much mid and high clarity but not enough crisp lows and bass. The Diesel Vektr has an ideal balance that makes sound feel enhanced and as if you were having front row seats.

* Can hear just about anything. When using cheap, inexpensive ear buds or headphones, it's difficult to hear all of the chords, background noise, and small intricate sounds. I thought my Creative Alpha Gaming Headset picked up most of the sounds, but I was wrong. The Diesel Vektr really brings all of the sounds to life.

* A good alternative to Beats audio and Bose. Performance is comparable, for the fraction of the cost. I would describe this as the little brother of Beats Audio. Not quite there with brand name power yet, but waiting to be discovered.

* Headphones are foldable and can be taken on the go.

This is by far my favorite pair of headphones so far. The sound quality is top notch. Everything just feels clear and fresh. It is very difficult to find a pair of headphones with powerful booming bass but still enough balance for vocals, mids, and highs to sound crisp.

product_title: Sylvania 4 GB 2.8-Inch Touch Screen Video MP3 Player with Expandable Memory Slot, Built-In Speakerphone
review_body:
I almost did not get this because of the reviews. But in the end, price won over my fears because this was something I purchased for my 4 year old. Just got it today and it's working fine so far. If it dies prematurely, I'll be sure to update. Otherwise, I wanted to address a few things from the reviews that scared me off.

First of all, yes, the software that comes with the player for converting videos does not work. I have uninstalled and reinstalled a couple of times. I've tried different file types as well. It simply does not work. Also, I find it a bit weird that in the manual it says the formats of files the player supports because I've found it to be untrue. Under video it says it is compatible only with AVI files. I have software that converts files to AVI and the player did not recognize it. It kept saying file error.

In my frustration, I dropped a few different video file types into the player and found that it actually works with WMV. That was a pleasant surprise as I was beginning to think I received a defective player. It also tells you in the software that it works with WMV and AVI, but I couldn't get it to work with AVI.

Another thing I should mention is that the file transfer time is super slow. I love that you can just drag and drop files, because it's simple and convenient. But waiting for a 700 mb video to transfer over took about 5 or 6 minutes. It's not my computer, it's the player. So perhaps I will invest in an external card for movies so that transfer times aren't an issue.

Calibrating the touch screen was not very hard. But it seems to be sort of flimsy and works better with a stylus. The speaker is not very loud at all, so if you plan on using it without the earbuds, this may not be the one you should choose. The earbuds that came with it are too big for my little man's tiny ears, so you may want to find some meant for tiny ears if you're also getting this for a little person.

The instructions are sort of vague at times, so there's a bit of figuring out to do with how some things work. But overall, I'd say it's worth it. Another sort of small issue I had is that in the manual it says that it goes into charge mode when it's not in USB mode and the indicator light will be red while it needs to charge, then turn green when it's done charging. Ours did not turn green. I don't let my kids use any electronics until they've been fully charged and this one was plugged in for a few hours thanks to us not knowing it was done. The little battery stopped flashing, so I figured it was done charging, but the light stayed red.

My 4 year old is loving it so far, we've put some movies and songs on it and he's used it for a few hours without any major complaints. One thing I don't like is that it's very easy to delete items, which he's done unintentionally to a few songs already. But other than that, I would recommend it if you want something cheap and (so far) functional.

review_body:

The biggest problem for me with the RS 170 is sound gaps in songs where there is a pause or a low sound. The best example is for classical music when I'm doing homework. This is a hard problem to illustrate so I'll do my best here:

I notice this only with instrumental music- for me that includes classical, folk metal, soundtracks and things like this. Because this type of music often involves just a few instruments that don't have a lot of bass and have sharp stops and starts, you hear static during these silents pats. The same thing happens in quite scenes in movies where there is mostly just dialogue happening and not a lot of other background noise.

Now, it's entirely possible, that the headset I have is bad and this is something I'll have to check with Amazon/Sennheiser when I get time in the next few days, but for now.

One thing that helps minimize this problem is to have the headset volume low and the stereo/computer/tv volume high.

I've tried plenty of other wireless headsets though so I can say with confidence the RS170 is leaps and bounds ahead of its competition. I think if it was $200 it would be an excellent value, but at it's current price, it's decent.

product_title: SIIG CE-KV0411-S1 2-Port DisplayPort KVM Switch
review_body:
This is the 4th different DisplayPort KVM i've purchased and the only one that works with my setup.

I use it to switch between my 2012 Macbook Pro Retina (yes the thunderbolt port is backwards compatible with DisplayPort displays) and my windows desktop (with a dual link DVI mini display port adapter) connected to my 27\\" Apple Cinema Display (not the thunderbolt one). I have an apple wired keyboard, logitech g35 headset, and my iPhone dock plugged into the KVM as well. Both computers connect to my monitor perfectly at the native 2560 x 1440 resolution. All of the function keys on my apple keyboard work flawlessly as well (brightness, playback controls, volume, etc..). I currently have both my keyboard and iPhone dock plugged into the back of the monitor, and the monitor's USB plugged into the KVM. My headphones are plugged directly into the KVM (they're USB headphones). ALL three devices switch seamlessly between my two computers and my iPhone continues to charge. A couple of other KVM's i've tried would take forever to switch back and forth, this one seems very fast.

The only thing i don't like is that all the USB ports are on the front of the unit instead of the back which would make for a cleaner installation.

I didn't use their included cables since it wouldn't really work for my setup, so i cant vouch for their quality. My setup is as such: My laptop is parked under my monitor stand and the KVM is further away on the side of my desk. SInce i use my monitor's included magsafe power adapter to charge my laptop I needed an [[ASIN:B0045I85FA apple cinema display extension cable]]. And since the output on the KVM is DisplayPort instead of miniDisplayPort i needed a [[ASIN:B003N3DTKY miniDisplayPort to DisplayPort adapter]]. On my desktop, my video card doesnt have DisplayPort output so i got a [[ASIN:B005LYSCNW Kanex C247DL Dual-link DVI with USB to Mini DisplayPort Converter]]. So then i just needed a couple of M/M DisplayPort to miniDisplayport cables and M/M A/B USB cables to connect back to my desktop and laptop. All in all my particular setup turned out to be quite expensive, but then again, when you got a grand invested in your monitor, what's a couple hundred extra dollars to be able to switch back and forth between your laptop and your PC.

product_title: Logitech Harmony One Advanced Universal Remote
review_body:
Have been loving this universal remote due to its ability to program multiple 'activities' (changing settings on multiple devices at once). Finally put the other 6 or so remotes in a drawer and haven't touched them since getting the Harmony One operational.

My previous semi-universal remote was a Harmony 300, which has only a single 'activity' button: 'watch TV', which can turn on up to 4 devices. But, with only one such activity, I had to keep using many of the other remotes (or manually switch modes on the Harmony) to switch to Apple TV, Blu-ray, etc. Nobody understood the long sequence of buttons to push except me.

As other reviewers have commented, the Harmony One is (mostly) baby-sitter proof. Anybody can operate your system regardless of the complexity.

The remote 'knows' what is turned on and to what setting. So, when you first start watching TV, e.g., it knows to turn things on - in my case the TV, the DirecTV DVR, an HDMI switch and a receiver ... and what to set things at - setting the proper inputs/etc. When you start another activity while things are already on, it knows to leave things on and only change what needs changing - e.g., in my case watching AppleTV changes by TV and HDMI/optical switch inputs, turns the DirecTV off and the AppleTV on.

The 'off' button turns off anything the Harmony One thinks is on. (So of course, if anybody manually hit a power switch, things will get out of sync.)

The software setup had me screaming. The web-based Harmony setup let me log into my account, but did not let me transfer any settings from my Harmony 300 to the Harmony One ... even though every single device was already there. So, I had to find the exact model of all of my devices and start from scratch. Then, the web site stopped responding. For hours. So, I installed the desktop-based software, which also had me log into the MyHarmony account. It was completely unaware of anything I had done on the Myharmony site, and I had to start all over again, entering every single device and with no transfer from the 300. Then the fine-tuning process came along when I had to slighly modify this input or that ... and even though I knew exactly what command needed to be changed, the software forced me through this interview-style process. Just hated the process. But, that's weeks ago now, and the emotion has drained (until typing here), and on a day to day basis, actually USING the remote has made life so simple.

No problems with charging, or getting warm in the charger, but I've only had it for a few weeks. As someone else noted, the power of the infrared transmitters goes down dramatically before the battery indicator even reads 1/2 charge, so I find I re-charge it as soon as I notice that one device or another isn't getting turned on.

The Help button is great, particularly for people not familiar with your system's nerdy details. Creative was Creative Labs and you likely owned a Sound Blaster sound card from them at one point. They moved into personal audio products such as MP3 players and speakers but it has been only recently that they have produced headphones of the quality that these are.

Here is a hint, if these had another brand name on them, they would be at least 50% more expensive for the exact same quality. With Creative being less known in headphones, you get a huge value for your dollar. Now that does come at a few expenses like the design being a bit bulky and not as sleek as other brands. They are also not as durable as other brands but if you take care of them, the sound you get for under a hundred dollars is amazing.

It is true these have a burn in period and are very easy to put in incorrectly. If this is your first pair of in-ear headphones, read the review about the proper way of installing them to make you maximizing your enjoyment.

review_body:
Everything that Belden said is absolutely true. I had pretty much the same experience with this product. I was in the market for headphones, I found it for $10, took it home, discovered that it required batteries, did not include a power adapter, and was oddly missing instructions. After doing a little troubleshooting online, I got the thing plugged in, and it worked... for about ten minutes. The audio kept switching to the local radio station or would simply shut off, so I kept having to hit reset and scan, but the transmitter is far too weak to out-do the many powerful radio signals flying through the air. product_title: Sennheiser HD 439 Closed-Back Headphones (Black)
review_headline: These Headphones Feel & Perform Like a Mercedes-Benz E550
review_body:
I have had Sennheiser earbuds that lasted for over 5 years. And another pair of 2 years that are still going strong.

I decided to try the HD 439 to see what their over-ear full sized headphones could possibly offer me.

My first over-the-ear headphones were the V-Moda Crossfade LP.

These headphones however have a very much different feel... They are more refined, balanced & relaxing yet also subtly aggressive in their sound signature. Forgive the analogy but these perform like a Mercedes Benz E550 .

While the V-Moda Crossfade LP, perform like they are a Ford Mustang GT500 Shelby.

Both are excellent cars but in a DIFFERENT way.

The V-Moda Crossfade LP's for the money offer you extremely high-performance drivers. (50mm 5-30,000 Frequency response compared to Sennheiser HD 439 - 40mm 17-22,500 Frequency response.)

Very capable drivers... But the drawback is this: The handling/balance/neutral response in these headphones is not up to par with the extreme performance. In other words, the sound signature is slightly unbalanced. The headphones are EXTREMELY aggressive in their sound signature because the extremely high detail the drivers are able to reproduce in sound tracks is not combined with a equally balanced response in rendering it.

A Ford Mustang GT500 Shelby will probably perform just as well as many BMW & Mercedes cars on a circuit race track. But here is the thing: The Mustang is going to dance around the track... The tires will spin off traction, the car will skid on sharp corners and it will basically dance around the road whereas a BMW or Mercedes will just move right through.

The same thing I have noticed with the V-Moda Crossfade LP headphones. They are like a mustang. Instead of just moving through the sound... They dance, skid & slide through the sound because the 50mm drivers have way too much performance in proportion to how much the manufacturer put intobalancing the response.

They V-Moda Crossfade LP's are not as a result relaxing, luxury & comfort providing headphones. They are more like \\"muscle headphones\\" with as much performance capability put into the drivers from a linear/objective perspective in terms of specs. But not performance from a subjective perspective in terms of EXPERIENCE from the specs.

When you compare the Mustang according to engine specs to Mercedes. Bang for the buck in terms of engine specs: The Ford Mustang is the winner. But the usability and being able to experience the specs out of a engine... The Mercedes is the winner.

The V-Moda Crossfade LP's is basically a uncivilized, unrefined and poorly behaved bad boy in it's sound signature. It is not a pair of refined headphones, It is a pair of rawly specced headphones. This is both a good thing and a bad thing. It has a very rugged feel and look as well. It is so interesting how similar it is in it's attributes to a Ford Mustang in a automobile perspective.

I get the details of all the high's, mids and lows from the Crossfade. I get the sound stage and the instrument separation. I receive the same driver performance from the V-Moda Crossfade LP that I receive from $300-$400 headphones but I receive the driver performance in a VERY unrefined, aggressive and animalistic manner.

From a automobile perspective, it's like the headphones have an engine found in high-end exotic super cars but lack the fancy suspension, tires, brakes and electronic stability control technology built in sync with the engine to deliver the full actual experience of the entire spec range.

The result? The sound performance feels like it's being limited slightly by audio physics. In the V-Moda, I feel that they are extremely high-performance and very capable but it has an unequal proportional ratio of performance to balanced response.

V-Moda Crossfade LPs - SLIGHTLY unbalanced sound signature that feels they are being actually limited to their maximum potential because the driver performance and capabilities are too good for the handling in it's response.

These headphones are generally disliked by audiophiles but keep in mind that most audiophiles are extremely picky over slight unbalances that probably will not irritate the majority of listeners at all.

A positive of their unrefined response is this: It makes it very fun, unpredictable, aggressive and enjoyable in terms of a roller coaster type feel.

But it comes at a price... It's not relaxing & it doesn't offer comfort to the ears. It can make your ears tired from all the aggression. Even if the music is soothing like Mozart or Beethoven... You really feel like these headphones hate being tamed and they are ready to blow up with aggression at any chance they get..

It's like when you want to be chauffeured around... Instead of being in a Mercedes Benz or something similar. You are being chauffeured around in a Ford Mustang GT500 Shelby with 650 HP for god sakes!

That's where the Sennheiser HD 439 comes in handy.

Although the driver performance in the HD 439 is significantly less than the V-Moda Crossfade LP - the balanced response and the experience of allowing you to perceive it's driver's performance subtly and passively is much much better.

It is very relaxing, comfortable and subtle in it's performance. But these headphones also have a weird split personality similar to a Mercedes Benz. Although it's relaxing, comfortable and subtle in performance.... It has a passive aggressive feel when the sound track is \\"demanding\\"...

Like a high-performance Mercedes with the gas pedal floored... It has shows you all the aggression, power and capability it has but subtly and fully balanced onto the road.

These headphones will not dance around with aggression. The simply prove their performance calmly. And performance they have indeed. They prefer being calm and balanced but seem not to hesitate to deliver a subtly passive-aggressive balanced high-performance showcase. Just like a luxury sedan Mercedes Benz E550.

This calm subtly balanced high-performance is a breath of fresh relaxing air in luxury when I simply am not in the mood for aggressive high-performance and just would like to rest with music instead of jam with music.

The detachable cables are a plus as I see these lasting for a good 20 years. The only con is they don't come with a case but no big deal really. Just take good care of them and you can also buy a case yourself.

These are very comfortable. They are made from high quality hard plastic. (Plastic doesn't automatically mean cheap or low-quality.) The noise isolation is also good as well.

Sennheiser HD 439 serve a different purpose and the V-Moda Crossfade LP serve a different purpose. But both come out equal and both are $100 dollars.

Please forgive me for comparing headphones to automobiles but I just find it so fascinating how a german audio company can resemble the characteristics of a german automobile company and how a american audio company can resemble the characteristics of a american automobile company.

Ford = V-Moda

Mercedes Benz = Sennheiser

I feel there is something to it...

PS. Beats By Dre (All models) should not be compared to V-Moda Crossfade LP. Beats are like the ricer cars with a overly tuned-up artificial performance and a extremely mediocre engine except they are sold for a Ferrari price tag. V-Moda's are like a muscle car with a solid respectable high-performance engine that are at least sold for a proper fair price.

product_title: Juiced Systems Extra Long Galaxy Tablet 7.0/7.7/8.9/10.1/ Note 10.1 & Note 8.0 - 30 Pin Charging & Micro USB Dual charging Cable - 6.5 ft Length (2 meters)
review_headline: Highest quality aftermarket cable I have seen
review_body:
I have ordered a couple of different aftermarket cables for charging my Samsung Galaxy Tab Plus. Several of them were of such low quality materials and construction that they fell apart the first time I used them, due to a \\"quick-assemble\\" connector that snaps together, making it easy to break.

This Juiced-Systems cable uses a molded type of connector for the tablet connection so that it stays together. The cables also have a pretty high quality strain relief that looks like it will last a long time.

I did have some confusion over the internal wiring of the cable due to the fact that a cable like this cannot support USB. However, it appears that the tablet connector is wired all the way through to the USB port, so it will charge at a high rate from the OEM charger and transfer data with a computer. The micro-usb connector only has the voltage pins connected, so any phone will charge at a low rate, typically 500mA, and will not connect to a computer.

I have also a Samsung Galaxy Note that draws a lot of power, so I was hoping that the cable was setup to support high rate charging for both devices. I found a phone number on Juiced Systems' website and I called them up and talked to the engineer that designed the cable. We talked about the wiring and how I can expect it to work compared to what I was hoping for. He said that he thought it would be possible to support high rate charging on both connectors with a change to the construction, but would have to do some research. He was really helpful and very well-informed on cables, wiring, and Samsung charger technology. In short, the support from Juiced Systems is phenomenal.

This cable is not exactly what I wanted, but I can continue using this cable for my tablet and am looking forward to V.2 that will hopefully support high rate charging on both connectors.

I had to give 5-stars because the engineer I spoke to was so helpful and offered to listen to my concerns. Iwould definitely do business with them again.

product_title: Mediabridge Coaxial Cable (50 Feet) with F-Male Connectors - Ultra Series - Tri-Shielded UL CL2 In-Wall Rated RG6 Digital Audio / Video - Includes Removable EZ Grip Caps (Part# CJ50-6BF-N1 )
review_body: I purchased this cable to use with my RCAANT751R indoor/outdoor antenna to replace a small indoor RCA antenna. The previous antenna I had was connected to RG59 cable. RG59 is a class of cable that is of lower quality than RG6. I found out that my house was wired with the older, RG59 cable. I used to have signal problems with my old indoor antenna, because every time the cable moved, my signal distored. I decided to invest in this quad shield cable even though there are cheaper varieties for this size of cable. The item description lists this as triple shielded, but the wire I received is actually a quad shield cable. This is important because quad shield refers to a metal mesh that surrounds the internal copper wire, protecting it from signal distortion that can occur when other electronic devices or electric cables interfere with signalling. This cable also came with rubberized casing around the f-connector nut. This makes it easier to hand-tighten your cable. I recommend giving the nut a quarter turn with the correct sized wrench to ensure a firm connection. This cable also had a copper wire inside that was too long for my device. I had to clip about 3mm off with some fine wire cutters. You must be careful when treating the internal copper cable, as nicking the wire or splicing it with a knife could result in serious damage to your cable. There are many tools online to help you install cable through the wall. I had to run this cable through my attic to connect it up with an antenna I installed there. The process was fairly straightforward, but you want to protect the ends of the cable from damage by covering them (they sell electrician's tools for feeding cable through wires, and it's possible to jerry-rig some of your own). You might want to Google \\"The Family Man: Tips for Coaxial Cable Wiring\\" for helpful tips on installation. As always when working with any electrical cables in the walls of your house, you want to shut off the power in your house, have a flashlight ready, and organize your tool set beforehand. You can also obtain stud finding tools and current locators if you do not already have cable in your walls. This cable has made a world of difference for my TV reception, as I can now access over 20 channels at 83% signal reception or better. This cable is a great deal. I saw one at my local big box hardware store that was only 6 ft long, not quad shield, and for about the same price.

review_body: Why I didn't buy this stand years ago, I don't know. I had my player on a bookcase but that is no longer feasible, so I looked to see what was available in Crosley stands and found this one. It is absolutely perfect. I am not using the wires, because I no longer have LPs, but it will make a great place for books/magazines. review_body:
Update Oct 18 2012: 4 month with this SB, it's really good... BUT ... THERE IS NO AUDIO OUT!!! This is really annoying especially if you want to use wireless headphones. Why would Yamaha engineers forget a simple audio out jack! -1

I am writing this product review, b/c I couldn't find constructive reviews about this sound bar before I purchased it.

The YSP is replacing a HK 245 5.1 system. It was a decent setup - but really 5 things bothered me:
1. dialogs vs action scene volume were completely off
2. I had wires all across my home
3. I couldn't connect more that 2 HDMI device.
4. It didn't support 7.1
5. size matters - an good receiver is just huge

YSP came in its box. I hooked it to my digital sources, my subwoofer (I really recommend using a external one it sounds so much better) and my TV. I could easily hook my 3 external devices - Satellite, WDTV and XBOX. Setup was extremely simple compare to the HK. Finally I turned it on and my favorite demo: \\"The Art of Flight\\" in 1080p/7.1.

DAMN THIS SOUND-BAR SOUNDS GREAT!

Right there, I could hear a huge difference with me previous system. The room was filled with so many contrats - it was like 3D sound... really good.
I went for a dialog scene, and yes I could hear without adjusting volume between action/dialog.

Bottom line, I do recommend the YSP. It's an excellent (if not the best) front speaker. For those who enjoy surround sound (like hearing steps behind you), there might be better options - It might just be my room setup but all the great sound I heard came from the front... not the back as they advertise. This is perfectly fine with me, I honestly prefer it this way.

See let's review my points:
1. The YSP has UniVolume - it auto detects sudden changes in volumes
2. I still have wires but much less that before - plus they are all in one location
3. I can now connect 4 HDMI devices
4. It does 7.1 TrueHD DTS AC3... you name it.
5. Exit my receiver - the is nothing more that the great sound bar sticked on wall

I should also mention that you cannot use YSP along with a Receiver.

Last but not least, $2000 for this device is a rip off. However if you are willing to search the net a little, you can find like new auctions wich usually range around the $1200. Still pricy.. but well worth the purchase.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 8 GB 3rd Generatio
review_body:
I got a silver 4GB for Christmas before the 4th Gen Nano came out. Almost 5 years later, this little baby is still going strong. I haven't needed to replace nor repair it. The body and screen have held up very nicely, no major scratches on the screen or anything (except that one dented corner where I dropped it Day One, hah). The backlight is still bright and I can read it even in sunlight. It's still fast, and doesn't skip or lag or fail.

In fact, I haven't had any problems with it for quite a long time. I remember having to manually reset it a few times when it froze and couldn't be turned off, and once or twice I've had to wipe the whole thing and reinstall the software; but all that I can do in 10 minutes or less with no shipping it off anywhere or fighting customer service or paying anything extra.

When I first got it I was worried about the size - it's so thin! - I thought I might sit on it and break it or something. Let me tell you, I've sat on it enough times there's probably a permanent imprint. But like I said before, the body and screen are just fine. I'm also prone to dropping things, so It's not just me babying the unit, it's just well built.

I've heard/read so many bad things about the new Nanos that if I look into replacing this one any time in the current Gen (6), I will simply be buying a new 3G. I like the compact Goldilocks size, the shape is comfortable in my hand, and it hasn't failed me yet.

The only thing I don't like about the 3G Nano is that there are only two capacity options. 8 gigabytes is simply not enough for me, but it's old tech so I can forgive the lack of space. On the whole, I'll take less space and better quality over more space and a crap piece of tech any day.

product_title: ViewHD HDMI Splitter
review_body:
Let me start saying that this 2 channel HDMI splitter from ViewHD has being working over six months 24-7. But as others, I observed day one the unit gets hot, well over the components specs, and depending on your setup the unit may die quick, as reported. This uses a little metal enclosure with not openings, and so there is not air flow convention. Indeed I measured the internal temp going over 85C. So, to start I removed the cover to allow some air flow, but this was not enough for 24H working, so I had to add a small computer fan (see pictures above)

I am operating this in a nice open home environment around 24C (75F), no an equipment closet where things may get quite warmer. I use this with HD video up to 1080p (that creates and aggregate RGB clock rate under 4Gbps). With the cover opened I noticed first that the splitter chip has a small sink very hot (around 70C), then I saw a small chip that is a voltage regulator even hotter (around 75C), this measured with the cover open, I can imagine will be at least 10C worst when closed. Even worst if the unit is operated at higher rates, in a closet, or in a summer day with no AC on in the house (over 35C or 40C). Any of that is quite common, and may raise the splitter chip easily over 95C to a point where performance and product life is reduced, or just will die.

The main problem is a cheap voltage regulator (next to the HDMI input) that gets very hot and transfer heat all over the board, more importantly heats the splitter chip that is just next to it. This is known as an LDO (Low Drop Regulator) that must eat (convert to heat) 1.7V (5V-3.3V) times 0.5A (when using the 1080p rate) that is near 1W resulting in an increase of over 20C for this little Circuit board and no airflow. A serious designer would have used a chopper regulator that cost extra couple bucks but only has to eat a tenth of that power resulting in minimal temperature increase. And also it would have allowed using wider input voltage range if needed.
The other mayor design mistake is the absolute lack of heat transfer planning. The heat is hold in the PCB and then in an enclosure with no openings? I can not think of a worst choice.

To finalize, and to make the splitter working with my computer and a couple monitors is very tricky in the sequence that must be followed to get things going. I couldn't make it work until I reconnected the input with power applied, that goes against the rules of the manual that say \\"not to plug or unplug ports with power in the box\\". BTW, these rules go against the HDMI standard, which defines the interface, and handshake to be hot pluggable. Even the HDMI connectors are designed with this in mind to avoid any physical damage. I am suspecting that this behavior is probably because of a poor HDMI handshaking software design too, that can not behave as real plug and play, just like Windows would do, no matter of the types and number of monitors connected.

So, if you are a cheap as I am, and do not want to expend extra bucks, It may work and I'll be generous giving two stars, but only if you do the extra homework to keep it cool.

EDIT: I originally gave this product a one star review based upon the above. I purchased a different unit and had the same issue, I then started fiddling with the settings on the Blu-Ray Player, what I found was that the display settings of the Blu-Ray were set to HDMI Auto, once I dropped them to 720p, the device worked as expected... NOTE: you can only edit the settings while the box works, so you may have to connect it to a HDTV with HDMI ports first, drop the display settings to 720p and then test on the target tv... I tried 1080p, 1080i as well, but still didn't work, 720p was the sweet spot... Hopefully this helps someone else... I have updated the rating to 3 stars, it shipped quickly, arrived as promised, and was well packaged... I cannot give it more stars, because I returned it and didn't get it to work... I am using this for my bedroom TV that doubles as the 3rd monitor on my computer (I have 2 24\\" monitors under it, sitting on the desktop) so I needed to get a good angle down forr easy viewing from close up. The kit comes with various size screws to mount the hooks to your TV if you don't already have the screws that came with your TV. Installation is pretty easy. The instructions were easy to follow. Four bolts secure the mount to your wall, another 4 attaches the \\"hook\\" mechanism to the TV. Now just lift the TV up and set it onto the mount. 2 set screws (already screwed into place) tighten to secure the TV to the mount and prevent accidently knocking the TV off. I was able to mount this by myself by spreading the 2 arms and placing it over my head, resting it on my shoulders to support it while I set the 2 upper lag screws. review_headline: Great for Many Types of Music
review_body:
I've had these for a little over a year now, and these are great headphones. I use them to listen to pretty much every type of music, from classical, rock, rap/hip hop, dubstep, and everything in between, however I don't really listen to country. Before these I used Bose triports. When I first got these I was very excited, but was disappointed by the bass right away compared with the Bose headphones, and the bass is nowhere near that of Beats or even some cheap skull candy headphones a friend of mine has. The only time the bass feels lacking, however, is when listening to rap or dubstep. With some more complex dupstep, such as deadmau5, you get an immersive, near surround sound listening experience that completely engulfs you in the music, despite the open design. I have the EQ on my Android phone set to \\"Bass Punch\\", which fixes the problem quite well, but they sound somewhat strained. If you mainly listen to rap, get Beats. For most rock music, these are quite good, and you rarely notice any lack of bass. If your library consists mainly of classical music, stop reading this and buy these now! The mid is excellent on these, and the immersive sound I mentioned above applies here as well. These beautifully play Dvorak's requiem, as well as other similar pieces.
The bottom line is, if you have a very eclectic library as I do, there is probably a better choice. If your library focuses on rap or even some types of rock, get Beats. If you have mostly classical music, you can't go wrong with these. Dubstep is a tough call, because while these don't play the drops well, you will hear all of the details of the music, it just depends on what you are more interested in.

product_title: Sony ICF-C318 Automatic Time Set Clock Radio with Dual Alarm (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I bought this alarm clock about 1 year ago and have never regretted it. Here are the features about it I love:

-The display can be dimmed. While dimmed it is still visible day during the day and night, even from across the room. The light from the dimmed display is minimal and undisturbing. I like a dark room when I sleep. I previously returned another alarm clock because its backlight lit up my room and disturbed my sleep, even while dimmed. This display is just right--visible but not too bright.

-Two independent alarm clocks. My spouse and I wake up at different times, so this is very convenient. With a quick glance it is easy to tell which alarms are set. If using the radio alarm, both alarms use the same radio station, so they aren't completely independent. But that is no problem for us. One alarm can be radio while the other is a buzzer.

-Easy to change the alarm time. My spouse and I wake up a different times on different days of the week. We are always adjusting the alarm times. By rotating the knob up or down, it is very easy to change the alarm setting in either direction. A child can figure it out without reading a manual.

-Price. At under $20, this is a steal.

-Reliable. I had another Sony alarm clock for 30 years. It is still working, but I gave it to my kids. So far after over 1 year of daily use, I have no reason to expect anything less from this alarm clock. It is not as fancy as some other alarm clocks, but simple products last longer.

-Small size. It takes up minimal space on our dresser.

-Automatically adjusts for daylight savings, with battery backup. I set the time once when I first receive it. I don't have to worry about daylight savings. I don't have to worry about brown-outs. I don't have to worry about re-arranging my room.

Is the clock perfect? No. The analog radio is a bit challenging to set exactly on a station. I'd love to see the same clock but with adigital tuner. But it is just an alarm clock, so this is not a big deal to me.

I like this clock enough that I am getting another for my other kids whose alarm clock (a TIMEX I regret buying) broke after just 5 years.

product_title: Sony SS-B3000 Bookshelf Speakers (Pair, Black)
review_body:
Fit and Finish, Value = A+ Sound = B-/C+ or so (for me). I set these up in a large room with a 2012 Onkyo amp as Zone 2 speakers. At first, I was sitting in the other room and I thought I'd be returning them. After playing with them a bit, I realized they sound actually very good on axis (pointed right at your head) and at louder volumes. On my amp, at lower volumes they sound weak (this is pretty typical and something a dynamic volume adjusting EQ (music optimizer crap) will address). With my set up the bass is disappointing. I think ANY sub would outperform these. But I think the Onkyo does not EQ the Zone 2 output (which sucks) because I don't have a work around. I was thinking if I could get a filter that would boost 100 HZ and lower frequencies by maybe 3-6db that would help. The off-axis issue is still there.. I think that might be an issue with all brands. Idk.. overall I'm a bit bummed and not even sure what product I would have preferred or where to go to fix the issue even with unlimited budget.

Update - had a chance to compare my Onkyo SKS HT540 (front left and right only which are 2x5in with a 1in tweeter) to these. The Onkyo's were soooooo much more full in the lower end. They sounded like I had a sub hooked up in comparison. The Sony's are very articulate and give great musical detail, but the lower mids and bass (roughly I'd say from 100-400 HZ and below is crap). The sony's also have a weird boxy voice.. somewhere from 400-2k HZ there is just weird stuff happening until you crank it waay up and it evens out. If you are going to play these on blaring volume they are much better and handle the power decently. But at lower volume, when you go into another room it sounds like a cheap boom box is playing. It's bad! Going to return and try for the Polk Tsi 200's which are 1. significantly more expensive and 2. hopefully are tuned better (and can provide more low end than the 100's) because of the cross over freqs because I won't have a sub for my zone 2. I think if you have an eq, you could probably dial out some of the issues.. actually the ideal fix would be multiband compression.

product_title: Brainwavz M2 In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: One of the best IEM under 100
review_body:
The Brainwavz M2 advertises itself as a bass heavy, while still providing a warm and clear sound. And these headphones does a phenomenal job living up to those expectations. Before I bought these headphones, I worried about just how \\"bass heavy\\" these headphones were going to be. Since I listen to a wide variety of music, I wanted a pair with nice but not over powering bass. And this is where these headphones shine. The bass is heavy, strong, and thumping in your ears, yet it's still controlled perfectly. It knows when to pick up and become stronger, or when to settle down and let the voice, or other instruments to shine. And that I think is what I love most about these headphones. However the bass is not the only thing that shines, the mids are one of the best I've heard. It provides amazing clarity, while making sure the bass doesn't sacrifice any of it. While the treble in these headphones are not as strong as the other areas, it still provides great quality. For 60 dollars on amazon, that is a deal you can not pass up.

Pros:
Superb and dynamic Bass
Clear Mids
Great Treble
Sturdy Build Design (although the padding connecting the wire and buds could use a little work)

Cons:
Mediocre Fit (They feel a bit too big)
L shaped plug (Some people my like them I personally don't)
Rubber ear buds are hard to put on but I don't usually change them often

However, when I moved into my new place, I wanted my living room to have a clean look and I wanted the TV mounted a bit higher to keep it out of reach from little hands (i.e. kids). I initially purchased this mount because of it's inexpensive price but I ended up liking it so much, I bought two.

The quality is great, feels very solid and the various knobs are very tight but also easy to adjust. It can tilt and pull off the wall, allowing for a view from any angle. Also, it was incredibly easy to install: unboxing to mounting probably took 15 or 20 minutes.

A couple of other notes: I didn't use the stud finder as I have my own. I also didn't use the included wrench; it hurt my hand as I tightened the bolts. Instead I used my own.

All in all, I highly recommend this product for anyone looking for an mount for their flatscreen TV

And by the way, this does not have an output for a second set of speakers--talk about a step backward. They assume you're only using 5.1, but if you want to drive two sets of stereo speakers--you're out of luck. Also lacks simple bass and treble controls--has a control up to plus or minus 10db--simply not enough. My other Yamaha and Sony amplifiers do much better. And if you want to use the phones out as a work around, you can't--it cuts out the main outputs. My other Yamaha amps let you use phone out while still operating main speakers. So, although the unit appears to be very sophisticated, they really engineered themselves into a much inferior unit--what were they thinking? If none of the above apply to you, I'm sure you will love this product as it does do a lot of things. You earned your money, make sure you get the most out of your dollar.

product_title: Klipsch In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: An average consumer's review for average consumers
review_body:
I'm not a DJ, I don't believe vinyl has the best sound quality, and I don't spend thousands of dollars to get the perfectly reproduced sound of a recording made in the 70's.

I'm a guy to walks to a train to go to work, has a very boring job where I watch movies or listen to music to pass the time, and I enjoy playing video games in lieu of working out.

All that said, I'm completely blown away by these ear buds. I had spent $10-$20 on pairs in the past, and was always incredibly unsatisfied with everything about them; they were uncomfortable, had short wires, failed quickly, and more importantly had terrible sound quality.

I've worn these for hours at a time, and have never felt uncomfortable with them. I was very happy they give you several sizes to try out, so there should be the right size for everyone out of the package. I had a pair of the Image S4's, and lost one of the plugs... I found out buying replacement packs can be expensive, so be cautious when pulling them out of your jean pockets!

I wear these nightly on a very noisy light rail train, and these help drown out the noise even with no music playing. In my untrained opinion, it sounds like it cuts the volume by half, which is fantastic. The sound quality is amazing, and I only really use it for my iPod Classic, Android phone, Xbox 360, or my HP laptop (I'm not really convinced the \\"beats audio\\" stuff is an improvement over any other laptop I've had).

You will begin to notice incredibly subtle sounds in your music you would never hear in a car or with other cheaper headphones. The bass sounds amazing, and the high ends are never muffled, so long as your music files are high enough quality. You'll definitely notice when you have lower bitrate songs.

The only negatives I can come up with are that they can be easily tugged loose from the tight fit in the ear, and it doesn't come with a shirt clip as many comparable brands' do. One person mentioned the stiffness of the wires being a downside... it should be noted they DO straighten out over time; I've had mine for over three weeks, and they do still have a slight zig-zag, but it's certainly nothing to demote the product review over!

Very satisfied with these, coming from a lowly average music listener.

product_title: Ckitze Italy Universal to Italian Travel Power Plug Adapter
review_body:
First things first -- Adapters and Converters are two different animals.

Traveled to Italy from the United States in March with 7 teenage girls. Among all the different adapters furnished by each girl's parents, the girls mostly relied upon this adapter which I bought for my daughter and myself. Many of the girls brought international converter or adapter kits (from places like Brookstone, Target, WalMart), which were not only confusing to all of us, they were bulky and in the end useless.

I would recommend that parents sending their children (girls especially) to Italy -- purchase three of these to send overseas with them. Given that most students are only in their rooms to sleep and shower, camera batteries, laptops and cell phones are only being recharged at night when they sleep. One adapter won't be enough to fully charge *all* of these things. One I used throughout the night to run my sound machine app while keeping my iPhone fully charged and ready for the next day of sightseeing. Also remember that after showering, most of the girls were using their chargers to plug in blow dryers.

Do yourselves a favor...pick up three of these. They worked for us in Florence and in Rome. I am still not sure why, but a couple of the girls who brought similar 3 prong and 2 prong adapters had very little luck trying to charge their camera batteries. Were I to travel this trip again, I would have bought six of these - 3 for my daughter and three for me.

Best because this adapter is very small, it worked every time for us, other girls lined up to use them, they are inexpensive.
Tips: -- Apple products don't need voltage converters.
-- Pick up a hair dryer with dual voltage (Brookstone has a very good one that folds).

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade LP2 Limited Edition Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone
review_body:
I purchased these LP2 after about 10 or so hours of reading other reviews, comparing Beats to these, Audio Technica, Sennheiser & Grado Cans, it was a mixed review all around.

I wasn't certain if I wanted the on-ear experience, or the over-ear comfort. I'm glad I chose over-ear, because these LP2 absolutely kill any other on-ear with comfort.

I was torn between these and the Klipsch M40's, just because the Klipsh M40 comes with such a beautiful aesthetically pleasing look, along with the impressive set of drivers, so I purchased both pairs. This is a review solely for the Crossfade LP2 after 200-400 hours of constant, 10-12 hours a day usage, with mixed \\"dupstep\\", rock, hardcore/grindcore, hip-hop/rap, classical & of course some 80's classic rock & roll.

Pros -

Audio - Absolutely amazing high-low's. The gain isn't too strong that you have distortion when fully maxed out, and throw a FiiO E11 Portable Amp on these, and you truly get the experience. Deep, pleasing bass, all the highs perfectly coming through without any resonance or distortion. If you have these on your head without any amp, fully turned out with no EQ (this is the way music should be listened to, no EQ or Flat), you literally get the 8 inch subwoofer effect. You can feel the bass vibrating these cans, and you can hear everything you thought was there, and things you did not know existed.

EXTREME COMFORT - I literally wear these 8 hours a day at work, without any break (or need for a break) and these totally drown out all sound around you. Not only this, but with the size of the cans and the over-ear size of the cuffs, nobody can hear the music around you. These function in a similar manner to a mini-sound bar when connected through the Amp and laid on the table/desk, you get to experience these in a different manner.

Cord - The cord is a kevlar reinforced standard 3.5mm jack, with a right angle (35 degree) entry point to your MP3 player. The cord boasts ability to withstand knife/scissor cut, but I have not yet been able to test this. I will contest that my puppy (6 month old) was unable to destroy the cord when the opportunity was given.

Functionality - Long wearing periods go by as though you don't have anything on your head. I have a large head, and typically I wear a cap as well, so I have to wear these over something, and you literally do not feel them for many hours. Eventually, your ears will get tired of having these on, but that's at the 5-6 hour mark of constant music & wearing. No discomfort on the top of you head, or anywhere on your face from constant contact.

Cons-

Audio - These do not pack as much synthetic bass punch as a pair of Beats would, or as some pairs of Seinnheiser open cans would. The low's seem inconsistent when compared to mid-high, which is mostly due to the mid-gain on these headphones, when turned all the way up it seems that the drivers overpower the rest of the sound quality, but this is easily remedied with a small amp (FiiO E7/E9/E11) or just by not listening to at max volume. There have been only 10-15 hours of usage that these have actually been on my head with full volume on my music player, as you never need this, but for those of you who are bassheads, these are not the best headphones for you, but be warned - you will miss out on so much more if you pass these.

Functionality - These do not have a break-down, and the carrying case you are given feels.. at best, flimsy. It is not a quality issue, as you can tell it's a good hard shell by knocking on it, but it does not give the same feeling of pride as the Klipsch M40s will. This should not be a concern for those of you who will properly store, but please note you cannot disassemble anything on these but the cans side panel, which I had absolutely no care for.

tl;dr version--

These are impressive cans. As my second pair of sub $500 headphones, I was impressed from the get-go. After 20 hours of burn-in, the sound quality improved drastically. The bass was not as high as I would have liked, as they did not match my friends Beats, but in every other area of Audio, comfort, and aesthetics, these blow the Beats away (or for that matter, any other equally priced cans).

Comfort A+
Audio A
Aesthetics A
Cord A+

review_headline: Not bad, but not great either.

Overall a sleek design and a few good features like the indoor thermometer, but overall not very user friendly and the projection turning off really makes having it pointless. We all know what time it is when we go to bed, we need it for the waking hours, not the initial falling asleep hours.

(Update)** I've now been using this alarm clock for 2 months or so. I still like it and the projection is great during the week when I'm only getting 7 hours or so because it's still on when I wake up. On the weekend when I like to sleep in I'm still disappointed that the projector has turned itself off, but it's something that isn't bothering me much anymore. A great tip that I've tried is this: when it comes to the alarm off button, which you've probably read in this review and others that it's hard to find, I've super glued a small peice of plastic, which I stole from the tip of a sharpie marker cap clip, to this button and it's now super easy to find in the dark because it's now the only button on the whole alarm clock with texture. I'm sure there are better things to try and glue to this button, something that might look a little nicer, but I didn't spend much time thinking about it. I just wanted this thing to work and now it works great. product_title: Logitech S135i 30-Pin iPod Speaker Dock
review_headline: Logitech S135i Speaker Comparison with S715i and Cyber Acoustics
review_body:
UPDATE ON 5-6-12: On battery power at full volume and using the 3.5mm Aux Input with my mp3 player set at 1/2 volume, the Logitech S135i would consistently shut itself off after 5 minutes. I called Logitech Customer Support @ 1-646-454-3200. They said they had other reports of the Logitech S135i turning itself after 5 min. on battery power when using Aux Input, except from people using the iPhone, which had no docking port, only a head phone jack. So I figured it must have something to do with the Aux In voltage (sound level/volume input). I tried my mp3 player at max volume and the Logitech S135i didn't shut itself off. I tried the mp3 player at decreasing volume settings until I found the volume setting that caused the Logitech S135i to turn itself off. All testing was done to a maximum time of 1/2 hour, where applicable, as I figured any battery save feature would activate by then. Apparently the Logitech S135i has a sensor to determine that there is no input, based on the Aux In voltage, so that it would turn itself off to save battery power. Turning the Aux In device's volume up and/or the speaker volume down may help with other Logitech iPod speakers having this problem when using battery power and the Aux In. My Cyber Acoustics and Logitech S715i units did not shut themselves off using the Aux In and battery power, at any input volume setting.

I own a Sansa Clip mp3 player and I wanted an amplified, portable speaker with a 3.5mm input, that could use both battery and AC power, so I could listen to music, etc. while in my bedroom going to sleep, working in my shop, for a small gathering out on the patio, while camping, and for any time I didn't want to use headphones. I mainly listen to Classical, '40s Swing, '60s Folk, '70s Rock, and Country music. I also listen to eBooks and quite a bit of other (mainly) voice only recordings, Doreen Virtue and Abraham-Hicks in particular.

After reading many reviews, I bought a Logitech S135i, a Logitech S715i and a Cyber Acoustics Portable Digital Docking Speaker for iPod (Cyber Acoustics CA 461). I figured I'd compare them and keep the one I liked the best, gift my 2nd choice to a friend for their upcoming birthday, and return the 3rd choice.

I bought the Logitech units as reconditioned units from 2 different sellers on eBay, and the Cyber Acoustics unit new from Amazon. I purchased them all online within a few minutes of each other, all with free shipping. The Amazon purchase was (of course) the last to arrive, by 2 days. Still, they all arrived within 7 Business Days of being ordered, not bad for \\"free shipping.\\"

Keep in mind that the max volume with all 3 units is dependent on how \\"hot\\" (high volume level) the music on your player was recorded at. Some songs I used for testing were plenty loud, while others were soft enough that I had to turn the Clip volume up to 3/4 or more. I prefer to not have to turn my Clip up over 1/2 volume, to make its battery last longer for both run time and # of recharge cycles, since it has a non replaceable rechargeable battery.

My (marginally) first choice is the Logitech S715i. It is the largest, heaviest and most expensive of the three, but has the highest volume (when plugged in to AC, when on battery power there is a DRASTIC drop in volume and bass), and slightly better sound than the Logitech S135i. I do not like the S715i built in rechargeable battery, since if I'm in a no power situation like camping, when the battery runs down I'm out of music. (I have a Solar Charger I can use for my Clip). With 4 AA battery power like the S135i and Cyber Acoustics units, I can take some extra batteries along and keep the music, etc. going. And since I use eneloop rechargeable batteries, the expense of going through several sets of batteries is practically non-existent. A minus is that when on battery power, the S715i has slightly lower volume and lesser sound quality than either the S135i or Cyber Acoustics units, whether they were on AC or battery power. I do not yet know what the actual run time on battery power is for any of these units. Unlike some reviewers of the S715i, I have not had any problem with the unit shutting off after a certain elapsed time when using the Aux Input, using either AC or battery power. Note: None of these units will recharge an iPod, etc. while operating on battery power.

My second (almost first) choice is the Logitech S135i. It has the second highest volume, which is not a whole lot less than the S715i, and its sound quality (with bass boost on for most songs) was not significantly less than the S715i, either. The bass boost feature does boost the bass some, but seems to provide an overall fuller sound more than an actual bass boost only. Even with adjusting the EQ on my Clip some material sounded better with the bass boost on, and some better with it off. The S135i did not decrease in volume when running on batteries.
