review_headline: Ah, Logitech, why do you test our relationship so?
review_body:
I am a long-time admirer of Logitech products for their design. My early Logitech products worked beautifully. Honestly, I don't know what has happened to their quality control in the last few years. This product turns itself off regularly, and not only while streaming. As another reviewer noted, it does not securely support the iPod/iPhone while it's plugged into the unit. I can put up with a certain amount of quirkiness, but this turning-itself-off thing is really getting on my nerves. It gets unhappy when you use the audio-in jack (lots of static), but unlike the Logitech Pure-Fi, it works a little bit. The Pure-Fi audio input jack doesn't work at all.

I believe I heard that Logitech got a new CEO recently (haven't fact-checked this) and I'm hoping, if true, better quality control is high on his list of goals.

The positives on this product include it's mobility. I carry it from room to room during the day and needed it to be compact, light, and able to play without the A/C adapter plugged in. I've read complaints in other reviews about sound quality, but it's fine for me, as I most often use it to listen to podcasts.

Please, Logitech, this loyal consumer needs a little more love. Give me better quality products and I will remain loyal. Otherwise, I really need to start looking for another manufacturer who is more sensitive to my needs.

product_title: Satellite Speaker Stands
review_body:
I purchased 2 pairs of these stands to go with my surround system. However, all I have is a logitech surround system, designed for a computer, so the speakers themselves are of \\"computer speaker\\" profile. The speakers are incredibly nice, just hard to mount at the right spot. These are about the only stands I could find for a reasonable price that could support them.

The stands work with \\"computer speaker\\" profile speakers, that is, the kind that are designed to be set on a desk, and with typical home theater speakers, the kind that you can mount with fancy screw-holes. They are quite nice, and have excellent cable management that goes through the shaft. The bases are sufficiently heavy for most speakers, but since mine weigh basically nothing, your mileage may very. They're also very adjustable, which is a nice feature.

This product isn't without it's downsides, however, which is why it only has 4 stars. The downsides are fairly petty, though, so they may not apply to you. First, the double-sided tape that comes with them is pretty bad. Since I'm not in an area prone to the house shaking often (earthquakes, hurricanes, etc.), it's not that big of a deal, but if you need the double-sided tape you may want to purchase some higher quality tape. Additionally, the bases are of a bizarre shape. They do this curvy bridge-like thing, and have a triangle-shaped base. The triangle makes it difficult to place in a rectangular room with rectangular furniture, and the weird curvy-bridge of the base means I can't really \\"build around it\\", such as putting my computer on top of one of the bases or hiding it under something.

All things considered, though, these speaker stands are fairly decent and I would purchase them again if I have a need to.

Oh, and if you are concerned about material, I do not believe these are made out of lead. If you are unsure, it wouldn't be hard to keep them away from children and pets.

product_title: Duronic HDS3 Mini 3 Port Gold HDMI Auto Switch PIANO BLACK 3x1 (3 way input 1 output HDMI Switcher)
review_headline: Doesn't work with either DisplayPort-to-HDMI or DVI-to-HDMI adapters for me
review_body:
I have purchased this to share a DVI monitor between my two computers, one being a laptop with a DisplayPort output, and the other - a desktop with DVI output. It's a well-known fact that both DisplayPort++ and DVI are fully compatible with the HDMI standard (only video signal is transmitted for DVI, of course), and a small, passive adapter works well in either case.

The following combo works perfectly with my Netgear HDMI switch (GCS1792):
1st laptop: DisplayPort++ output, DisplayPort to HDMI passive adapter, HDMI cable to the Netgear HDMI switch
2nd computer: DVI output, DVI-to-HDMI passive adapter, HDMI cable to the Netgear HDMI switch
Netgear HDMI switch: HDMI cable and an HDMI-to-DVI adapter on the monitor end

When I've replaced the switch (that costs around $200) with this tiny box that was supposed to do the same thing at my workplace, NOTHING worked. That is, the red led was on (and pointed to the right device), and everything seemed to be working, but I couldn't get the picture displayed on the shared monitor despite doing all required things. The same was true of the second computer with a DVI output and a DVI-to-HDMI adapter.

Still, when I decided to check the hardware itself and connected this tiny box between my wife's tablet PC with an HDMI output, and an HDMI cable going to her monitor, everything worked perfectly. As far as the monitor is connected through an HDMI to DVI adapter, looks like there are no problems with adapters on the Output end.

So it seems the box has problems when the input is converted to HDMI from either DVI or DisplayPort. A disappointment: the cheapskate has lost again. But it's a cheap disappointment, though :-)

product_title: iRulu Brand 4GB USB MP3 WMA Music Player FM Radio Voice Recorder(Black)
review_body:
Here's how this torture device will break you:

* No pause function. It's a stop-and-reset-everything-to-the-beginning button.
* No fast-forward function. It's a slightly-faster-forward-than-playing-it-all-over-again function.
* Hair-trigger lose-your-place feature. If the little seek nib slips, you're on to the next file.
* No folder browsing. Plod through your files sequentially, one-by-one, from the beginning each time.
* Jumblicious Files! Your folders are ignored. Files are piled together in no discernible sequence.
* Non-functioning delete. If you ask it to delete a file of dubious identification, it just doesn't bother.

I listen to podcasts of 30 to 120 minutes each. The seek slider skips ten seconds of content per second of holding the little nib. Do the math. That means skipping forward by one hour takes SIX MINUTES of carefully and obsessively holding the slider and watching the progress without juggling or you have to do it all over again. So if you want to invest your afternoon memorizing file names and individually pawing through them in no particular order, and then spend a portion of your life carefully not moving your thumb on the seek nipple while watching the progress indicator so as not to overshoot the end, only to have to do it all over again when the device gets jiggled, then this little number is perfect for you!

Maybe I can use it as a memory stick, but at this point, I wouldn't trust it with any data of value.

product_title: Harman Kardon AVR 2650 7.1 Channel 95-Watt Audio/Video Receiver with HDMI v.1.4a, 3-D, Deep Color and Audio Return Channel (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I must say I am a bit disappointed in this receiver. This is my 3rd Harman Kardon, my first was an AVR 235 that I upgraded a couple years ago to the AVR 254. The 254 was quite a bit ahead of the 235 in terms of features and benefits and was a great upgrade. Due to a power surge in my home, my 254 was fried so I upgraded to the 2650.

The 2650 is the current HK model and the 2nd highest in the lineup; it is 2 models ahead of the 254. But it doesn't feel like 2 models newer.

The menus are identical to the 254, something I think should have been updated by now. The only difference is they added a couple minor features the 2650 has to the old menu system. The remote control is the same one as the 254 had.

Power wise, the 254 was 50x7 while the 2650 has almost double that with 95x7. To be honest, it doesn't feel like double the power...either the 254 was underrated or the 2650 is overrated, because it really sounds like maybe a 20watt/channel difference at most. There is a difference, and the 2650 is better, but not significantly better. I chose, and paid more, for the 2650 over last year's 3600 because of the power output...this is making me question my decision a little.

Inputs/outputs are a wash for me, but the 2650 for some will be considered a downgrade in this regard. I use all 7 speaker outputs, the sub pre-out, HDMI 1 input, HDMI output, and a single composite audio input. Everything else is there but not needed. The 2650 adds, over the 254, 2 more HDMI inputs (I have to use an external HDMI switch due to a two-room setup I have so this is meaningless to me), Ethernet input, Bridge IIIP input, Optical Out, Zone 2 composite output, Sirius input and a USB input.

The 2650 loses over the 254 a number of input/outputs...a few which can be 100% deal breakers for some buyers: lost 2 composite video/audio inputs, lost 3 S-video inputs and 2 S-video outputs, lost the XM input, lost the coax digital output,and for the bigger deal items: lost the 8 channel audio input, lost the 7 channel pre-out output, and lost the component video output.

The USB input is a far better solution for firmware updates than the 254 had, though I never updated my 254. What is stupid is there is an Ethernet input on the unit that you can't utilize for firmware updates. The Dolby Volume feature is a huge plus...a carryover from the previous 2600/3600 models. I haven't tried the Ethernet input for music streaming; I have a PS3 and would rather use that. The Bridge IIIP docking station is pricey and not well reviewed so I will pass on that and use my Bluetooth streaming device instead.

Though the 254 was not advertised as 3D ready, 3D worked just fine through it. The 2650 has some audio pass through and control for the TV; useless feature I don't want/need...I want my HK to control everything sound related, period. The 2650 has the same great sound quality I've grown to love and was the reason why I didn't shop other brands. All of the audio processing is exactly the same as the 254.

Overall, I still love the 2650. I loved my 254 and this is an improvement over that; but for the cost difference I expected a bigger improvement. Honestly, if you want a new HK receiver I would purchase a used or new 2600/3600 instead...those have the important improvements like Dolby Volume control without the extra cost associated with the 2650.

review_headline: Great sound for the whole house
review_body:
A friend showed my his play:5 and play:3 at his house and I was less than wow'd. He was having network issues completely unrelated to the Sonos but we didn't realize it at the time. I have been using several Apple AirPort Expresses with generic computer speakers to spread music throughout the house but that system is less than reliable. The dependence on iTunes or an iOS device to push music left me wanting. So I decided to make the purchase and I have to say this system is incredible on so many different levels.

First: setup. Push two buttons. Done. Want to add another speaker? Push two buttons. Done.

Second: the controller is really cool. You can group speakers to play the same music on more than one room. You can pair speakers to play true stereo. All on the fly, all from the controller.

Third: Music selection is extensive. Pandora, Slacker, Spotify, Last.fm, rdio, iheartradio, itunes and local music shares are all included. You cannot run out of music!

Fourth: Multiple stations at once. If you have 2 speakers you can play 2 music sources AT THE SAME TIME. If you have 10 speakers, 10 sources. Or you can play one source on 3 speakers, another source on just one speaker, and a third source on the other 6. Mix and match is no problem and the music is synchronized so two speakers on the same station are not playing with lag between them.

I put the same review for the Sonos play:5 and play:3 but the only difference is the play:5 has a built in bridge and 2 more drivers than the play:3. If you only get the play:3 you will want to buy a bridge as well.

Pros: everything except

Cons: the price

The units are expensive. Despite that I have no intention of returning them.

product_title: Logitech Bluetooth Wireless Speaker
review_headline: WOW - Loud and has Bass!!  Works with Android!
review_body:
My initial try at a Bluetooth speaker was the SoundFreaq Side Kick, which at $99 is a great speaker; but lacked the bass I was looking for. I wish this Logitech speaker had the USB port for charging a phone and the remote control buttons like the SoundFreak but I can live without that (most control is done via the phone anyhow).

When I first hooked this speaker to my phone (took about 30 seconds out of the box to get it working via Bluetooth) I was like... WOW, now this is what I'm looking for! And that was playing with it in my car off the speaker's battery. When I got home and plugged it in then the bass really kicked in. Great sound. There are not many other features really, no other bells and whistles, but boy does it sound nice (especially if you place it in a corner so the rear firing woofers can do their thing.)

For $119 it sounds better (I think) than the $300 Bose or $189 Altech Lansing units.

I wish, like others here, that Logitech provided an option to play at full sound quality when on battery power at the expense of battery life. A \\"battery saver\\" option button would have been nice to provide us the choice. However, I happened to have a spare Belkin UPS from an old AT&T UVerse modem that provided 12V output (no inverter). This works great to provide it with \\"wall power\\" and then runs at full volume. This UPS (bu3dc000-12v) is a little big to lug around but will probably provide 10 - 12 hours of battery power for an outdoor party. If it dies then I'd get the 6 or so hours from the internal battery. Nice!

I did get it to work via Bluetooth on my Windows 7 PC also. When pairing use the code \\"0000\\". Then you can use your PC for your music source, however with no remote control options on the speaker (besides volume) you must use your PC to switch songs. So ultimately doing it via my phone is nice as I have full control in my hand.

I think Logitech is missing the boat a bit on this by onlyadvertising it as an Apple iPod/iPhone/iPad accessory when it should work with any Bluetooth device. I have an Android based HTC Thunderbolt and it works great. In fact it is louder via Bluetooth then when I plug it in via the 1/4\\" audio cable.

product_title: Steren 526-111WH Standard HDMI Pigtail + F Jack Wall Plate, White
review_body: I purchased 2 of these wall jacks and tried to wire them into my house with a 30' HDMI v1.4 cable.  My TV would get no signal with everything connected.  I tried just 1 jack and the other side the HDMI cable, and it worked, but the picture was flashing on the TV.  I disconnected both jacks and only used the 30' cable and it worked flawlessly.  My only take is that the wall jack HDMI connection isn't v1.4.  The jacks did work, but just not with each other and with that long of a cable that wasn't the same version of HDMI.  If you have a 3D TV, I wouldn't buy this wall jack, as you will probably be disappointed.  If you have a standard TV, just make sure that your cables are v1.3 otherwise you probably get a flashy picture, if you get picture at all.  As far as the jack itself, it was a little brittle.  One of my HDMI connections had bent out of the wall jack, but I was able to bend it back.  The seller should provide some documentation as to what version HDMI this jack is.

product_title: Skullcandy Hesh Headphones w/ Mic
review_headline: To Hesh or not to Hesh
review_body:
Alright so here's the skinny on the ever popular and relatively stylish Hesh:

Comfort: These headphones are, over-all comfortable. My head is on the larger side and they have the perfect snugness for me. I Think headphones should be tight enough to stay on but loose enough not to smoosh your brain. These fit the bill as far as I'm concerned. i have rather short hair SPECIFICALLY for the reason that I wear headphones everywhere because I don't like it messing up my hair (girl thing). These headphones do make my ears A LITTLE SWEATY after awhile(but hey I do live in Cali). If you have a lot of hair, you may take issue with these headphones just because the cups are a little toasty.

Sound: I think the biggest issue with judging sound is people have to be comparative. So I will say outright that I am comparing these to my favorite headphones of all time, my LP V-Moda headphones. Compared to my V-Moda headphones, these actually have a pretty comparable bass. These headphones provide some good sound AT HIGH VOLUME LEVELS. At low volume levels there's NO DEPTH at all. The Hesh are pretty awesome all around. They produce GREAT rock!!! However I find them to be on the shallow side as far as the sound goes. certainly not V-Moda caliber depth, but the sound is nice and smooth anyways so they are worth comparing to high caliber headphones.
These headphones will leak sound. Just as almost all over-ear headphones do. If you want non-leak headphones, get ear buds. No good headphones will just not leak sound unless you like your music quiet and bass. But chances are if you're looking at these, you're a rocker like me.
*I judge Headphones sound by how well they do on the Radio Sunnydale album. I'm not a rap fanatic so I won't try to judge bass beats.

Durability: Pretty acceptable in terms of durability. They have a slightly cheap feel to them when you first start using them, but they really are pretty solid. If you don't go out of your wayto smash at them, they should last like forever (barring you having to send them back for technical difficulties). The band looks plasticy, but It's really mostly made of canvas. I haven't had mine long enough to really get dirty, but as long as you don't spill anything on the canvas, they should be great. That being said, I'm not real sure if these are worth 50 dollars based on build alone. The ear cups aren't very high quality material, which is why i think they can get sweaty. I got mine for 25 bucks, I think if you get them for under 40, its a sweet deal. I would pay 50 for these on a low budget. Otherwise, you'll be happier going for V-moda LP(the memory foam and surround sound in the LPs are drool worthy).

Style: They're pretty stylish. Just saying. The color really pops the way I thought it would.

(Note: The headphones/earphones I own are V-Moda LP, Skullcandy Ink'd, Zumreed, WESC Maracas.) I try to balance style and sound. The Zumreeds and Maracas are lower sound quality than hesh. about the same as the Ink'd. lower than V-moda.

review_body:
Purchased this unit from J&R in lower Manhattan with 5.1 polk tl250- waiting on sub... Got a pretty good deal, they knocked $50 off receiver and $50 off speakers.

So once I carried these suckers home on subway I had 5.1 wired up in a couple of hours. Set up YPAO without trip pod and calibrated once, played some tunes, sounded ok, used my tri pod, and man did that make a difference. The sound is beautiful, considering I am lacking a sub woofer-so consequently not so great with hip hop (actually roots sounding great right now) but jazz shines...

Eventually I plan to wire zone B in bedroom, gonna get a couple more polk tl250 satellites. Looking forward to sound throughout house.

I had a lot of trouble getting my mac pro vga>hdmi and digital out working properly running through the rx-v573. The on screen GUI is seriously lacking on this yamaha, it needs some polish for sure. I found all other integration strait forward, my apple tv3, xbox 360, and direct tv receiver. My sharp aquos syncs nicely with yamaha, allowing to operate sound from direct tv remote.

2 days later of not giving up. I did finally get my mac pro synced up by using the \\"option\\" button and selecting the proper audio out. This was confusing because the same option was available through \\"setup\\" on remote.

Wish there was a wifi plug for network, need to figure out how to get router and cable box over here. Still have not used airplay, mainly because I have apple tv.

Despite hiccup with setup on mac and other gripes I would rate this box a 5 out of 5. Go get one!

product_title: Cambre SW1W-BC Sky Shelf On Wall Single Wide Wood AV Shelf System
review_body:
First the good - the shelf looks nice, and the screws the go into a stud are very strong. You could use them to do pull ups without a problem.

Now the bad - there is no way on earth that this could possibly hold 50 pounds. I put a 40 pound receiver on it, and it collapsed instantaneously. The problem is that whoever designed the method for attaching to the wall bracket was... I don't know. I'm bewildered how anyone could even design such a system.

There is a wall bracket, which you put into a stud. it is ok, although the part that rests against the wall is angled, instead of flush against the wall. This means you have to really indent the wall to get it secure. A flat backed bracket would have avoided this issue.

Then comes the worst part - to attach the arms you use a system... well, I can't even describe it because it is so convoluted. The bottom line is that all of the force of the shelf is being supported by about 2-3 threads on a pair of screws. It makes no sense, and it failed instantaneously.

Search elsewhere... I replaced it with [[ASIN:B00155PSXS Peerless Adjustable Component Shelf for AV EQ]] - that beast does the job

Also, though these isolate sound fairly well, they do sound more \\"open\\" than my last ones.

I've listened to:
Mama Who Bore Me--Spring Awakening (static prominent in beginning sections)
City Hall and other songs--Vienna Teng
Drilled a Wire Through My Cheek--Blue October
Sleep-Eric Whitacre (static VERY prominent on this one)

Overall, I'm pleased with this purchase!

review_headline: Well Padded and Functional Tripod Bag
review_body:
I've spent some time researching a tripod bag for my Manfrotto 190XPROB tripod and 498RC2 ball head. I also have a Manfrotto 681B monopod and 234RC monopod head that I wanted keep in the bag as well.

I recently visited my local camera shop and came across this bag. The salesperson had both the tripod and monopod (I own) on display and tried it out in the bag.

This is a well made bag and well padded. Like a previous reviewer had mentioned, it would have been good to see YKK zipper on this bag. I'm a sewist and familiar with that brand. There are two zipper heads that start at each end of the zipper and meet in the middle. Initially, I noticed that I had a hard time pulling the zipper around the bag. I ended up rolling the hard edges along the inside of the zipper towards the inner bag. This softened the edges around the head/curve of the bag. I was then able to zip the bag closed. I then carefully ran each zipper head back and forth until the zipper ran smoothly along the bag.

The bag has an adjustable web strap that runs a long the length of the bag. Can be worn as a shoulder bag or as a sling bag. At the narrow end of the bag is small padded handle if you to hand carry the bag.

I'm happy to report that I can store and carry both monopod and tripod with their respective heads in the bag. It can be quite heavy to have both in the bag, but I'm using this mostly for transporting my equipment. Having the padding is a plus as I don't feel the tripod/monopod hitting against my back. Also, I don't have to worry about damaging the equipment. I highly recommend this bag if you want to protect your tripod and ballhead.

I will be back to post updates and wear and tear on this bag.

product_title: Denon AVR-1312 5.1 Channel AV Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
let me preface this review: i am NOT an audiophile that has to spend thousands on the best components and speakers every few years.
I have been researching a home theater receiver for well over a year now. I've been wanting to upgrade from my old Sony SEN-5500(circa 1999)to something with HDMI inputs instead of the ancient Red/White/Yellow RCA jacks the old SONY had. the old unit's remote no longer turned down the volume and the center channel no longer sent a signal to the speaker.
I had narrowed it down to the Onkyo TX-NR509 or the Denon 1312. personally i liked that the Onkyo had a USB port on the front and a slightly higher wattage output, but the Denon has 4 separate 75W amps built in; instead of one 300W amp split 4 ways. It sounds like i'm splitting hairs, but there really is a noticeable difference.
I ended up going with the Denon because of the price. I found it on WOOT(sorry, Amazon. don't hate me) for $125. i just couldn't pass up that price.
the old Sony speakers have always met my needs and i honestly thought they sounded pretty good. with the Denon they sound Incredible! i cannot get over how crisp and clear the sound is. the mids and highs are really quite remarkable. the dialogue on movies and TV is GREAT!
my only gripe is that i cannot adjust the bass any higher than +6. i know these speakers can \\"thump\\" a lot harder than the Denon will allow, because i've done it with the old receiver. short of cranking the volume up to and having to listen out in the garage, there's no way to \\"thump\\" at lower volumes. but this is a MINOR gripe and i can deal with it -- looking at getting the either the SONY SAW3800 sub or the Onkyo SKW204 sub.

the one thing you need to be conscious of when you get your Denon, is this sucker puts out some considerable heat. you will need to give it lots of space. the owner's manual recommends giving 6\\" front and sides, 8\\" or more in the back and at least 12\\" above. and they really aren't kidding.

overall i am INCREDIBLY happy with this receiver. if i could give it 9.5 out of 10, i would. i just couldn't pass on the price(again, very sorry Amazon). it more than meets my needs and i don't believe i'll need to upgrade for many years to come.

you will NOT be disappointed with the receiver.lly aren't kidding.

overall i am INCREDIBLY happy with this receiver. if i could give it 9.5 out of 10, i would. i just couldn't pass on the price(again, very sorry Amazon). it more than meets my needs and i don't believe i'll need to upgrade for many years to come.

you will NOT be disappointed with the receiver.

product_title: AudioVox RC105 Dual Wake Clock Radio with 0.9-Inch Green Display (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great clock radio with one small flaw
review_body:
I have been using this clock radio for almost 3 years, and I really like it. It has a readable display which is not too bright, nice loud dual alarms which are easy to set, and a nap button which allows you to sleep for 10 minutes to 2 hours without changing your regular alarm settings. I love this nap feature, but it is also the source of the one flaw: once you set the nap button, there is no way to turn it off. (You can change the length of the nap to a minimum of 10 minutes, but that's it.) More than once, I have hit this button by accident when I meant to turn the alarm off, and it's annoying to have to wait 10 minutes for the nap alarm to sound so I can shut it off.

Other than this one quibble, it's an excellent clock for a very reasonable price.

product_title: Midland HH50 Pocket Weather Radio
review_body: This thing is even smaller than I realized, which means I'm more likely to put in my pocket and have it when I need it.  I tested it at home and it immediately went to the right frequency.  It has great sound for such a little radio, so there isn't an issue with being able to hear it clearly.  It doesn't have SAME, but for the price and simplicity, this radio is hard to beat.

product_title: Dynex™ - Mini DisplayPort-to-VGA Adapter DX-AP180
review_headline: Works great on first-gen HP Envy 14
review_body:
I got this to connect my first-gen HP Envy 14 to a VGA projector/monitor and it's worked great. This specific computer doesn't have a built-in VGA port and it's been well-documented online that the mini-displayport on this computer is buggy. I've tried many supposedly supported active adapters and they have not worked. I'm sure they would probably would work with other computers such as newer macbook models but they don't seem to work with the HP Envy 14.

I've been using this adapter for about a year now and it's worked great for me. I've also used it successfully with my friends' macbooks (for some reason many people with macs don't carry around their adapters).

One thing to note is that I can't seem to get full resolution support on external monitors with this adapter. This may be because of the conversion process though. My laptop's native resolution is 1600x900 and I am only able to output at 4:3 resolutions with a VGA cable (like 1024x768). This is ok for my purposes though because most projectors can only output at this resolution. I am able to get full 1920x1080 resolution with an HDMI cable.

All being said, this adapter is great for its purposes and is the only adapter that has worked for my HP Envy 14.

product_title: Sewell 2 Port 1x2 Powered Hdmi Splitter V 1.3b 3D Certified-Up to 1080p
review_body:
We needed something so that in my gamesroom/studio I could watch TV while working on the computers as the flat screen was over my shoulder to my left.

Simple solution. Open the box, plug in the power, use an additional HDMI cable [[ASIN:B0019EHU8G Mediabridge Ultra Series - High Speed HDMI Cable with Ethernet - (6 Feet) - Category 2 Certified - Supports 3D & Audio Return Channel [Latest HDMI Version Available]]]to go from the source (Shaw Gateway in our case) to the input, original flat screen HDMI in output one and one 50 foot shielded HDMI cable [[ASIN:B004GW25WY BlueRigger HDMI Cable (50 ft) - CL3 Rated for In-wall Installation]] to go behind the couches and over to the corner where we used our new [[ASIN:B004LXK8LI Viewsonic VX2453MH-LED 24-Inch Ultra-thin Widescreen LED Monitor - Black]].

It works perfectly. High Definition video and audio on the Viewsonic monitor as well as of course on the existing Sony 42 flat screen. And with limited real estate on my desk (all ready have 5 24 inch flat monitors as well as [[ASIN:B007UNMLBG Wacom Cintiq 24HD Graphic Monitor (CINTIQ24HD)]] for our HP Windows 7, Mac mini 2011 and mac mini 2010 (media server). Simply press the input selector on the Viewsonic monitor and I can switch back to seeing the screen for the mac mini 2010 which we use mainly as a itunes media server.

Very impressed. Thought I was going to have to spend a couple hundred dollars but solution solved with this splitter.

product_title: CLA-NHWC: i.Trek Universal Hardwire Cable with Lighter Socket and Power Switch for M... Universal Hardwire Cable with Lighter Socket and Power Switch for M...
review_headline: Reverse Wiring, Ruins Center Pin Positive devices
review_body: Be aware! This is wired reversed from most devices that will likely be plugged into it. The center pin is not positive, the outer wall is. It will immediately fry, smoke, roast, burn up whatever is plugged into it that is wired with the center pin positive. This can unexpectedly turn into a very expensive mistake depending on what you decide to plug in first. Extremely poor description to not have important information like this included on the product page.

product_title: TRIPP LITE DisplayPort 10
review_body:
I bought this for a small office. I have a modem, a 16 port switch, a router, and a print server plugged into it. There's also a printer plugged in to the surge protector side of it. It works very well and I'm sure it will provide us with enough battery backup for the occasional power outages that we have. To be honest, it's probably a little overkill based on what we have plugged in to it, but the lower VA UPS's were not much cheaper so we decided to go with this one.

I do like the LCD display, though we have ours sitting on top of a cabinet so we have to get on a stool to actually read it (if we ever need to). I love the fact that you can turn the beeping off too. Our other UPS's are APC and we can not turn the beeping off on those. In the one small office that this one is in, there are also three additional APC UPS's. So you can imagine the noise when the power goes out. In the future I expect that we'll switch all of our UPS's over to ones made by Tripp Lite.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 8 GB Video MP3 Player
review_headline: Best mp3 player on the market hands down.
review_body:
Sandisk stopped making these a few years ago and as a result you can find them on amazon for literally HUNDREDS of dollars (msrp was $90 when I got mine). They do two things together that no other mp3 player will: 1. Combines both the internal and external (sd card) memory into ONE library so when you shuffle it will randomly go through all your songs (most will separate them). 2.plays virtually ANY and EVERY format of music Audible, FLAC, MP3, OGG, WMA, WMA (DRM) making it highly desirable by music professionals.
On top of that, it sounds amazing, (pick up some nice earbuds and try it out), It has a super easy and most important FAST and snappy, lag-free interface unlike most (even the new fuze+), a physical scroll wheel that you can use without looking at (unlike the touch ones with ipods and great for running, gym, cycling (I can operate volume and searching tracks through my pocket without taking my eyes of the road)) and an awesome audiobook feature that allows you to speed up the reading, enabling you to go through the book 33% faster. My friends all wonder how I work so much and read so much, well I have an hour commute and this is perfect.
Microsdhc? hell yes. I have a $30 16gb in mine which makes for a $120 ipod user-jealous 24gb mp3 player(evil laugh).
To top it off it's reliable, I got this for my 18th birthday almost 7 years ago and am now purchasing an identical one today only because the battery is not lasting very long anymore. It will freeze on the rare occasion but always comes back. Also syncs great with Windows Media player.

Only cons would be that the screen scratches easily, but you can get a screen protector, and the screen is not really big enough to watch movies on, it will work in a pinch though and still looks nice, but at this price it still bows ipods out of the water.

review_body:

product_title: BIC AMERICA V-80 8" 100 Watt Powered Subwoofer
review_body:
I purchased this subwoofer on May 24, 2011 to compliment my 2.0 set of Swan D1010MKii speakers. It was a great pairing, and the subwoofer's auto-on feature worked well. I was able to adjust the crossover point as well as intensity/volume. It definitely gets powerful at its highest setting, enough to overpower my relatively small D1010MKii speakers.

If it wasn't for what I'm about to write, I'd give this sub a solid 5 stars.

However, on March 9th, 2012, the sub started emitting loud buzzing sounds, in varying intensity and tone. This persisted even after disconnecting the audio cable. Attempts to turn the sub off by switching the switch to \\"OFF\\" did not work. An electrical burning smell came from the subwoofer. I'm away at college from August until May, except for short breaks... so the total amount of time I've had with this sub (and have used it) is about 5 months. And, this subwoofer is plugged into an Uninterruptible Power Supply, specifically for power conditioning (not for battery backup), along with my other computer equipment.. so it's unlikely that an electrical surge damaged this sub.

I could forgive the random failure, though... and it normally wouldn't affect my rating, because failures happen. However, I attempted to contact BIC America to see if they would replace the sub, as there is a warranty of 1 year on the electrical components. However, my e-mail did not get a response after two business days. Also, I attempted to call their technical support phone number, but got no answer. In desperation, I tried calling the SALES number, still no response. These calls were placed during the specified business hours.

So, as much as I enjoyed this sub, it's now a $100 piece of wood sitting in the corner of my room, and BIC America doesn't seem to care. I had never heard of the brand, but I put faith in them. Now I regret not buying a comparable Polk Audio subwoofer, which is a more widely known and reputable brand.

=== UPDATE 03/15/12 ===
I was finally able to get in touch with their technical support on 3/14/12. The person I spoke with was very nice, and said he would send me e-mail instructions on how to get my subwoofer fixed under warranty. I did not receive the e-mail until today, 03/15/12. The e-mail instructs me to TAKE APART THE SUBWOOFER MYSELF, remove the amplifier, and ship it to them for repair via UPS or FedEx. Shipping charges are not covered. If you ask me, they should just send me a brand new subwoofer, ask me to put my old one in the box, and send it back.. although I suppose shipping would be expensive. Let's see how long it takes to get back...

=== UPDATE 03/16/12 ===
I've just shipped the subwoofer to BIC America ... it cost $15 to ship it via UPS Ground from my town in NY to Anaheim, CA where BIC America is. Overall, I have a very sour taste in my mouth from all of this... First, it took forever (3 days) to get in touch with their technical support. Second, I have to cover shipping charges on a product that failed within the first year with minimal use. Third, I had to take the subwoofer apart myself to get the amplifier out to send it to them. They are supposedly repairing it and sending it back. Sure, the repair is free of charge... but what if it happens again? Do I wait another three days to get in touch with them, take the subwoofer apart again, spend the $15 to ship it to them for repair? If you ask me, skip right over this subwoofer... go for a reputable brand, one that won't take three days to get in contact with, and won't make you take your own subwoofer apart.

=== UPDATE 04/16/2012 ===
UPS Tracking shows that BIC America received my subwoofer on March 26th, 2012. I have yet to receive any word from BIC America that they received my subwoofer, or that it's been shipped back to me. I called their warranty/tech support department, and was told that the delay is because of the \\"holiday weekend\\" (Easter).They aren't even open on the weekend, so I fail to see what difference that makes. He said it takes 10-15 days to repair. They've had it for 15 business days - I haven't heard a word from them. The guy on the phone is the same guy that I called to request warranty replacement, so they must be a fairly small business ... and apparently, they don't care very much about your business. I've now been without my subwoofer for a little over a month. This wouldn't be that a big deal if the customer service wasn't total garbage.

=== Final Update 4/19/2012 ===
Incidentally enough, I got home on the 16th to find the replacement/repaired part from BIC America waiting for me. I installed it in the subwoofer, and gave it a test... everything seemed to be fine. The replacement part didn't look any different.. and I can only hope that mine failed just as a random chance, rather than due to a defect. The subwoofer is working great now, and I hope I don't have to deal with their warranty again. All in all, I was without my subwoofer for over a month... and it took them 3 weeks to get the part back to me after they received it. Again, is it a good subwoofer? Yeah, I love it. I just hope you don't have to deal with their RMA process.

After checking it inside and out for any objects that could be causing it, I isolated the sound to the woofer itself. I called BIC America, and this time, I was able to get an answer on the first call. We determined over the phone that the woofer is bad, and again, I'll have to send it to them (at my cost) to have it replaced. Maybe I have bad luck... but I certainly haven't abused it. Most of the time it's on 1/2 volume or less, and it's powered by a computer sound card... in any case, another failed part. review_body: I wore this pair of headphones for about half an hour and already it was becoming very uncomfortable - actually borderline painful. So I will be extra careful not to stress these headphones.  I'm not sure how they break so easily.  The construction looks reasonably sturdy to me. If mine ever break, then you can be certain that there is a design flaw. I never abuse my electronics equipment.

product_title: NuForce NE700X In-ear Headphones
review_body:
The Good - I have bought two pairs of the NE-700X since April 2011 and they have been the best earbuds I have owned (compared to Shure, Logitech and Bose). The highs are crystal clear, the mids are crisp and the bass is pretty damn good (Bose good). After 50 hours of break-in, they were so good I bought another pair as my backup.

The Bad - These earbuds are fragile. I have gone through 3 pairs so far. My original pair died last week, initially the left earbud lost sound and then gradually the right earbud died. The original backup pair lost sound pretty much after the 50 hour break-in period (both sides had nothing but static). The replacement of that pair lasted about 2 months, with the right earbud slowly losing sound and then promptly losing sound altogether. I got it replaced and it's my last remaining pair.

The Verdict - Having purchased two pairs and going through three pairs in less than a year, it's unlikely this last pair will survive until summer (and I don't take it to the gym or do anything vigorous with them!). Nuforce has excellent customer service and replaced these pairs without question. My two pairs are still under warranty but at this point, I just don't want to keep receiving replacements to burn-in and hope to make it past the three month mark.

So 2 stars for excellent sound (when it's working) and 1 star for great customer service. Unfortunately, that means two lost stars for lack of durability. If Nuforce can solve this durability issue, they would quickly have me back as a repeat customer.

product_title: Onkyo DX7555 Audiophile Single Disc CD Player
review_headline: Sounds OK, but missing a feature
review_body:
I've had the DX-7555 for a couple of years. The overall sound is pleasing and very smooth. It's a solid, attractive unit and it even has a jog dial. It works pretty well with my NAD C-372 int. amp. However, I have one major complaint and one minor one.

The major complaint is that the DX-7555 cannot show you the total remaining time left in random playback mode. It will show you the remaining time left in the current track, but that's far less helpful to me. This is a real annoyance, and one that interferes with my enjoyment of the unit. My minor complaint is that the front panel button layout causes me to usually have to figure out which button does what. There aren't that many buttons, it's just that what's there just isn't what's in my head as to how it should be. I could live with that, but the \\"remaining time\\" issue bugged me for quite some time.

Finally, I gave up and got a c.1997 Sony CDP-XA20ES off Audiogon. This unit isn't as smooth-sounding as the Onkyo, but I daresay it is more detailed and has tighter bass, as well. And it shows me the random remaining time. I'd love to put the Onkyo into my \\"other\\" system, but there's that \\"random remaining time\\" issue. Don't know yet, what it's fate will be.

I do think it's a good sounding CD player and maybe about as good as it gets in its price range. Onkyo, what were you thinking?

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_body: I purchased this MP3 player specifically for working out, mainly walking/jogging/walking.  As a recent purchase, this is a first impressions review.  The size, weight and convenience is great as compared to using a iPod Touch or smartphone, both of which I have been using.  The clip is strong and sturdy enough to handle the bouncing of movement with out coming loose.  When I clip it on my jacket the controls, especially the volume controls, are easily assessable, especially compared to having a phone on my hip holster or pocket or when using an armband with the iTouch.  Music is easily transferred using Windows Explorer or a music program.  I've not used it with Windows Media Player or iTunes as I personally use Media Monkey but it syncs fine with MM so I'm guessing it would do fine with other programs.  I've only used the Music feature and the FM radio but plan on using the Voice Recorder in the future.  The FM player is no worse or better than others I've had in the past on MP3 players.  The sound is fine but the reception is always weak.  My main use is for listening to ballgames when I'm at home or at the game, so even with weaker reception (which affects the sound quality) it has always been listenable.  If I was wanting to focus on listening to music, I would rate it worse but usable most of the time.  I won't say much about the included headphones other than I have better headphones that I use with it but I also don't expect much from headphones included with devices at this price.  I don't use a music service so I cannot comment on using Rhapsody. For what I bought this for (working out & listening to my music and podcast) and using my own headphones I would rate this player 5 stars for the combination of price/form/usability.  The one feature I have not been able to assess is the battery life.  Even if I only get 12 of the 15 hours advertised, I will still be able to use it for 8 workouts (2 weeks) between charges.  I also have not needed to use the microSDcard slot yet but may test it out at a later time.  I will say having the slot assessable on the outside, instead of inside the unit like the battery compartment like many devices, would be a convenience.  I'm also not concerned that the battery is not user replaceable because at this price buying a new unit instead of a battery after a few years would not be an issue.  My workouts have become less worrisome and stressful as I don't have to worry about the Sansa as I did with my iTouch or cell phone.  The Sansa does what I need it to do very well.

product_title: Sennheiser Closed Circumaural Hi-Fi Headphone
review_body:
I bought these as a replacement for the HD 201's that my wife (ahem) snapped in half during a tantr--- err discussion. I warmed up to the 201's after not really feeling them and after being wholly disappointed with the 202s (for my application). I mainly use my headphones during my commute to work on the BART subway using an iPod Nano 6th. I listen to mostly jazz (traditional, smooth, Latin, vocals, contemporary) some R & B, gospel (although with rare exception, I try not to use gospel as a reference as many times the recording quality just isn't there) and then everything else filling in the gaps- all at 256kbps/44100.

Out of the box these cans seemed compressed as if something was holding the music back. It was like hungry and enthusiastic dogs were being held back by chains they were trying feverishly to escape. Obviously the Nano's little digital amp isn't the best harbinger of power for these Sennheisers. I then tried them in my desktop's RealTek HD Sound card and the sound was A LOT better. The highs jumped out (I like by highs a little brighter than most folks), the lows were there but was still a little muddy and not as pronounced as I would like. Example, listening to Chris Botti and Yo-Yo Ma on the Live in Boston's Cinema Paradiso, I look to hear the resonance from Ma's cello and the woody pluck from the double bass... neither of which (especially from the double bass) that I normally hear with my house speakers and even from my cheap $14 Phillips in ear buds from CVS. I next tried the same songs coming out of my H/K AVR 1600 and I got even better highs, more warmth in the middle and more punch in the bass- still not what I was looking for, but better.

The 10\\" cord does not bother me as I bought them for commuting purposes and the short cable is welcome to me from that standpoint. I have extenders if I need more length at home.

These are not the best headphones I've encountered but at the $29 pricepoint. These would make pretty good home headphones for your receiver or desktop or dedicated headphone amp. I will continue to use these during my commute- I admit there is a cool factor to wearing a pair of Sennheiser cans over some cheap earbuds- especially the ubiquitous white things. While I wish they sounded better with my Nano, I can live with the sound-- using the \\"rock\\" EQ setting which gives me a little more bass and treble. These fit comfortably on my fat round head and the cups are featherweight lite on my ears and eyeglass temples. Being closed cups, they do cut out a lot of surrounding noise on the BART and on the noisy CNG powered employee shuttle bus I ride. For $29 not bad. Constructed well, sounds OK with my Nano, better with the desktop and even better with a powerful amp at home. I suspect if I let these play in the H/K for a few hours, the break in may loosen up the drivers. Like I said, they seem capable but seems like something is holding them back. Give em a try.

product_title: XANTECH AC1 Controlled AC Outlet (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I am using this switched outlet for something other than it's primary purpose. I have this switch as part of a hybrid renewable energy system. When the battery bank runs too low, I have a relay that senses the drop and cuts the load from the battery bank to save the batteries from being completely discharged. Before I purchased this item, the batteries would remain cut off from the inverter until they were sufficiently recharged by the solar panels and wind turbine. That could be problematic during a time with no wind or sun, which could last a week or more here in Alaska.

With the addition of this switched outlet, when the battery bank goes low, this AC outlet becomes active, powering a battery charger to quickly recharge the batteries from commercial power. It may sound counterintuitive to recharge a renewable energy system with commercial power, but leaving a battery bank in a discharged state for a long time can shorten battery life, so charging them quickly helps to prevent replacing the batteries ahead of their time. Once charged, the outlet cuts off and the system resumes it's normal operation.

product_title: MartinLogan Vista High-Performance Electrostatic Speaker (Single, Black Ash/Black Aluminum)
review_body: First of all, I'd like to point out that I have been the highly satisfied owner of a pair of Martin Logan Source speakers for over a year now. The Sources \\"changed my world\\" and opened up a new and different dimension in my music. I heard details and timbre changes in instruments that added a new dimension to the realism. A clarity that seems to float in mid air and accuracy that puts you right there, in the band with the music all around you. The Sources presented the concept of both sound stage and depth in ways beyond comprehension. They totally blew away any speaker I had ever heard before. I've been madly in love with them and an AVID Martin Logan supporter ever since.   So when Audio Advisor offered the Martin Logan Vistas on sale for LESS then HALF PRICE. I was (needless to say) intrigued. I placed a call to Martin Logan and asked them what my \\"biggest bang for the buck\\" was as far as an upgrade path (given that I already owned a pair of Sources). The reply came without hesitation; \\"Vistas\\". Next I called Audio Advisor and asked about the differences I might expect to hear with the Vistas. I was further assured that the lows to mid lows were more solid and accurate. Other words used were; larger sound stage, better imaging, great clarity and openess, etc...   So I went ahead and ordered a pair of Vistas sight unseen, mostly because I trust ML and Audio Advisor. Still a part of me deep down in, was a little skeptical. The Sources sound so much better than anything I had ever heard. It didn't seem possible that there could be much more room for improvement. So convinced was I that my Sources couldn't be bested, that when my Vistas arrived they sat sealed in their boxes for 4 days. While I worked up the nerve to disconnect and box up my beloved Sources, and break out my new Vistas.   Prior to swapping them out (an ordeal that took over an hour). I enjoyed one last 2 hour listening session with my Sources. The final verdict? Folks; I'm here to tell you - the Vistas sound as much better than my Sources, than the Sources do everything else! I don't know how, but the Vistas sound noticably \\"BIGGER\\"; and with that comes more realistic Highs, Mids AND Lows. Once again I am hearing things in my music I've never heard before - not even on my Sources! Its difficult to describe, but the Vistas are more precise more delicate, more accurate.   They add a final bit of magic; (a subtle finishing touch) to the highs. The upper Mids have more body, ie. trumpets and horns aren't quite as bright and possees a bit more \\"bite\\". End result; they sound more \\"real\\" (I should know I was a trumpet player for over 14 years). The mids and lower mids are tighter and more accurate. As for the lows? It's too soon to evaluate because they haven't broken in yet, but whats there out of the box is very TIGHT and controlled. I can say, after only a couple hours of listening; the lows have matured significantly. It took several hours for my Sources to break in. Once they had, the difference was stark. They went from having \\"OK\\" bass to sounding AMAZING down low.   Last but certainly not least. The Vistas add more depth, ambience and also a \\"new\\" vertical element to the sound stage. The Sources added left to right accuracy to the sound stage I had never before experienced PLUS they added depth and a feeling of size and ambience that was amazing. The Vistas improve on these elements while adding a \\"vertical presence\\". For instance in my Big Band jazz, the high hat symbols sound like they are positioned a few feet above the bells of the sax players (which already sound \\"down front\\" and closer to me). Just like in real life!   Long story short? These things are worth EVERY BIT of $4300.00. But to get them for less than half that? Its the deal of a lifetime! People listen, if you enjoy good music; beg, borrow or steal the $$$ to get these before they're gone! If I could afford it, I'd buy two more; just \\"Because\\"!  note:    I audition my speakers using only 96khz/24 bit and 192khz/24 bit flac files though a high resolution Burr-Brown PCM 1792, 24-bit D/A converter. My \\"front end\\" has a rated Signal to Noise of 124dbA and is fed to a  Class D stereo amp capable of delivering 350 watts per channel into 4 ohms. The amps have an extremely fast slew rate; even at high current and a damping ratio in excess of 1000. My speaker wires are short runs of 24 individually insulated #24 copper conductors per channel (equivalent cross section of a single 10 gauge conductor). Twisted and braided for optimum noise immunity.

product_title: XtremeMac Luna SST Dual Alarm Clock with Detachable Speaker for iPod and iPhone
review_body:
After reading many reviews and listening to the sound of competing - and more expensive - models at different retailers, the price for this made it worth a try. I am very pleasantly surprised in a number of ways. First, in terms of sound, it is pretty impressive for such a small device. It definitely is not a unit to crank, but that's not the point. On the other hand, it fills our bedroom with reasonable quality sound when played at low to mid volumes. The lows are a little thin, but vocals come though very crisply and the mid-range is totally acceptable. Simply put, it sounds bigger than it is, but it is not a sound system.

Second, the form factor is very appealing. It is a smaller unit than the pictures make it appear - which is a plus for the nightstand in my opinion. The clock is dimmable and it is a very mellow orange tone. Consequently, it is totally visible, but does not light the room at night. It is slimmer and very understated in its appearance. My wife commented positively on its appearance, which is a rarity for most electronics.

I have read comments that are negative about the controls, but I see no problems. I actually like the dial control on top. I have some concern about the app for iPhone, but I will defer comment and judgment until I have used it for a while. As with most devices these days, the instructions are weak, so i will play with it on weekends until confident it will work reliably.

The dock options are good, but I have an iPhone case with a dock protector. So, I purchased the blue cel dock extender for $7 (high quality product as well!) rather than take the phone out of its case each night and synch is perfectly fine even with the extender.

The remote is a nice addition, but really it is best for adjusting volume and skipping song to song. Jumping between albums, playlists, etc, needs to be done from the the phone/ipod.

At the $45 +/- price point, it is an outstanding value. Sound quality and appearance are very slick for the money. Initial impressions are very good. Solid option for an iPhone alarm clock!

product_title: Belkin F8Z359tt06INCHP Y Adapter; Mini Stereo Plug, Headphone Splitter
review_body:
A lot of these 3.5 mm adapter reviews say conflicting things about whether or not stereo sound is maintained. In my experience, this cable keeps the stereo sound and has an added benefit as well. Not only is stereo sound maintained, but because of an added and unexpected benefit, the cable is extremely adaptable.

In short, this adapter carries stereo signal FROM every input/output TO every input/output, making it extremely versatile.

I am using it to connect my PC monitor and my Xbox 360 to my computer speakers. The Speakers take their INPUT from one of the female jacks, the Xbox 360 connects to the speakers through the other female jacks and the monitor connects to the speakers through the male 3.5mm plug. In other words, one of the female jacks combines the stereo signals from both devices (Xbox and monitor) and it remains in stereo!! I haven't tried to use both devices simultaneously, so I'm not sure if it is mixing the signals, but I do know that a signal can make it into one of the female jacks, through the male end and back out the other female end without having volume or signal quality diminished

I believe the volume level is somewhat diminished from the computer monitor audio output (male), but the volume from the Xbox (female) is perfect and the sound quality is great in both!

In short, this adapter carries stereo signals FROM every input/output TO every input/output, making it extremely versatile.

These headphones don't do it all -- as with most products tasked with meeting a very specific need, there are trade-offs, so I'm surprised to see so many negative reviews, considering. If you want them to stay in your ears, there may be comfort or convenience trade-offs. If you want them to be priced a certain way, rugged and portable, they're not going to sound like your $280 noise-cancelling can headphones. Period.

This is also not a plug-and-play product. Sennheiser includes about 5 different variations of each little component for a reason -- the user is meant to test them out and customize for the best and most comfortable fit.

The one complaint I've read here that I share is that the bass could be better. Not sure if the price point and investment in the design caused them to skimp on price, but I would have payed the extra $$ for better sound. If I could have rated these 3.5 stars, I would have for the sound.

All that said, in all of the reviews of athlete-targeted headphones, I've not found one model that receives consistently good feedback. I do believe that Sennheiser has made a good effort with these headphones, and it's on the user to spend the necessary time to customize to get the full potential out of them.

product_title: Denon AH-NC800 Advanced Noise Canceling Headphones
review_body:
I recently decided to replace my aging earbuds with some quality sounding travel friendly headphones. My father wouldn't let me be cheap and take his QC15, so I simply decided on getting my own pair. Since I'm a college student I wanted something I could carry around and wear on the flights. I ran across these off a recommendation from HeadRoom and decided that they seemed to fit the bill. After a few weeks here's my opinion.

> Sound Quality (Great):
This is one of the big selling points of these headphones. To those who haven't owned high end (~$200+) headphones before, this will definitely be a step up. The sound is fairly spacious and detailed. While several travel headphones usually offer a more colored sound, these stick to the reference style of giving even balance to all types of input. Denon is widely lauded as the kings of closed back sound, and it really shows here. At this price range however, you'll definitely find better sounding headphones, such as the D2000 or AKG Q701. However, I haven't seen a travel friendly model sounding better than this one, and very very few closed back versions. Definitely a richer sound than the QC15 and a more balanced sound that Beats which is more colored to favor certain music. I'd wager it is even with the cheaper Audio Technica ATH-M50.

To people who buy these, I'd recommend some burn in time first. For my pair they started off sounding somewhat muffled and quiet unless I really turned up the volume. After some hours of listening they seemed to, for lack of a better term, loosen up and sounded much better, and didn't need quite as much power. I know the concept of burn in is a somewhat controversial one, but I felt that it was somewhat true in this case, though not in my other headphones.

> Noise Cancellation (Poor):
This is certainly not the highlight of these headphones. The noise cancellation is very good at getting rid of certain very specific sounds (like a refrigerator oran air conditioner), but seems to be engineered to be less intrusive than on other noise cancelling headphones. Some might not even be able to discern that it cancels anything. It also produces an audible hiss, which is present in nearly all noise cancelling devices, but especially true in this one. You do get very good battery life, and I estimated mine at going around 38 hours on one battery. The slight advantage here is that you don't feel the pressure on your ear as much as if you were wearing the Bose QC 15 (which definitely feels heavy after a few hours to me), but whereas the Bose do a fantastic job in cancelling airplane/keyboards/footsteps/low frequency noise, the NC800 are simply not a worthy set in this area alone.

> Audio Restorer (?)
- In addition to the noise cancellation, there is another feature called audio restorer. In theory it is supposed to improve the sound of low quality sources. I don't know about quality, but it does use battery power to give you some extra volume, which is useful if your portable music player doesn't have a very strong output. By and large I myself never touch this feature, since the volume boost also happens with noise cancelling turned on.

> Features (Good):
These were the real reason why I purchased these instead of the Denon D2000. Noise cancelling headphones by definition come with some attractive features. First, the most delicate and likely to break part of any headphone is the cable. Here, we have 2 detachable/replaceable cables of varying lengths that ensure you won't accidentally bend the jack or tear the cable and have to send it back. Second, the fold-able design allows for great portability. It fits into a very compact case, and since it folds both sideways and inward, it has a smaller profile than the Bose QC15. Lastly it comes with a very solid hardback case which is convenient and fairly compact.

The big advantage to these over some other competing noise cancellation models is the ability to play music without noise cancellation. Your battery can be dead and the headphones will them simply be headphones, unlike Bose where a dead battery is a dead headphones.

> Comfort (Great):
Another big selling point here is the comfort of these headphones. Definitely a lighter and softer fit than the Bose in my opinion. The pads are a memory foam type of material and are immensely soft when they arrive and even softer a week later. To me personally they don't feel heavy, though it should be noted that any noise cancelling headphone will be heavier than most normal ones. It is somewhat uncomfortable when wearing glasses, but I have yet to find a set of headphones that don't have this problem.

Do note that just like most headphones with leather pads, they may feel hot and sweaty after a while depending on your skin and your environment. This was a minor issue when I was sitting outside on a sunny day and once sitting in an car, but otherwise I haven't noticed any regular issues.

> Conclusion:
So why did I buy these? Incredible sound in a travel friendly package. I also really wanted the detachable cable as two of my headphones have suffered a broken cable at the hands of some careless roommates. Treat it as if the noise cancellation feature were absent as I really don't know that anyone will find it satisfactory or even on par with competing models.

I also purchased these used from Electronics Expo, but they arrived look brand new in original packaging with not as much a scratch or dent anywhere to be seen. The 170$ price at the time was fantastic putting these in the same range as the Audio Technica M50. Otherwise I might have gone with those instead. All in all I've had a good experience and I feel these would be good for traveling listener who wants a near-audiophile experience.

review_body:
I auditioned the Polk RTi4s at home against the Infinity P153s. They are quality speakers worth the current asking price, and a real steal at the deep discounts sometimes available. (for the full comparison review, search Amazon for \\"Infinity P153\\".

PROS:
- fairly flat frequency response.
- bass can be very good for a 5\\" woofer, IF carefully placed.
- nicely extended highs.
- no offensive peaks, dips, or distortion.
- well constructed and attractive with grilles on or off.

CONS:
- needs subwoofer to cover range under 100Hz or so.
- perhaps too polite, feels like it's \\"holding back\\".
- not as emotionally involving as I had hoped.
- for me, the less expensive Infinity P153 were better overall.

In terms of accuracy, the Polk's won the comparison against the Infinity P153s due to their more extended low end and flatter response overall. However they did not elicit the emotional involvement I normally experience with my favorite music. The Infinities were simply more satisfying to listen to for most types of music. I listened to all types of music, and in many cases I preferred the Polks.

Conclusion: I chose the Infinity P153s since my system is for enjoyment first, accuracy second. These Polks may well be perfect for some people. My co-worker is also a critical listener, and bought the Polks from me after listening to them.

product_title: STREET by 50 Wired Over-Ear Headphones
review_body:
Just by virtue of being rapper branded headphones, these are going to get some really negative reviews on the audiophile headphone sites. I was curious to hear them myself, but because I really dislike the sound of Monster's Beats I did not have high expectations for these. My first impression out of the box was that the bass was powerful alright but the rest of the sound was strangely unnatural. Having now spent a few days with them, I actually think they are pretty good, but not for everyone.

First off, the packaging is certainly elaborate. The headphones themselves appear to be just a big piece of plastic. However, the headband is actually a durable polymer, and it is lined with comfortable leather. The cable, conveniently, comes with a microphone. The pads are large enough to surround the ears, and clamping is good enough for decent isolation and solid bass but not so tight they are uncomfortable.

The sound is what is interesting and different. First, the bass. The bass is excellent, both with good extension and lots of impact. The bass extension rivals the Sony XB 500/700 but the bass has more impact than the bass of either of those phones. Some listeners will find the bass overemphasized to the point of dislike, others will find it good for some music and not so good for other music. However, if you want emphasized bass, the bass is controlled and tuneful unlike the uncontrolled tuneless thump of Beats. The lower mid range is a little recessed which tends to make voices sound like they are a bit further away and the upper mid range to lower treble is over emphasized which can sometimes make vocals sound a bit too harsh or honky. However, overall voices, particularly male voices sound smooth and clear. Even on songs where bass is very heavy, words can be discerned. Highs are a bit rolled off and the upper highs are missing. Thus triangles and high cymbals don't ring, they clink. Soundstage is outstanding for a closed headphone, and the sound is distributed widely rather than one dimensional. The rolled off highs make them a poor choice for classical music, but they work well for popular music which is often recorded overly \\"hot\\" with too much treble. The rolled off highs reduce fatigue.

I like them a lot for songs with male vocals in the bass baritone range and I think they make excellent headphones for rap and hip hop. For more acoustic music I generally don't care for them because the ringing of guitars, and some of the detail gets lost. Certain singers like Leonard Cohen and Lou Reed sound really great with these. Unfortunately female voices can become unnatural. I think some of the high pitched stuff on Kanye West albums sounds like it is being sung through a kazoo.

If I put these down and put on a more natural sounding headphone like the Sennheiser HD 595 I am almost shocked by how \\"natural\\" the Sennheisers sound in comparison.

I like these SMS by 50 a lot, but I think they are a specialty headphone. For example I think the V-Moda M80/V-80 is a better all rounder although a bit less comfortable on the ears. Also, at the price there are many many superb headphones available. review_body:
My beloved workhorse old Panny DVD player finally wore out after 9 or 10 years.

So, after about year (literally) of looking in stores, looking online, and looking at magazine reviews, I discovered that what I wanted probably was not out there.

My wants: 5.1 Surround, DVD/CD player, easy viewing readout, easy remote that does not require a telescopic sight to 'hit' the sweetspot on the player, no BluRay, no WiFi (WiFi is nice . . . but I wanted to pay for quality, not more gew-gaws.) review_headline: So far, pleasantly surprised but beware of...
review_body: I purchased this unit after seeing it at Frys listed at over $320. To be fair, they say they price match internet deals. The iPhone app written by Onkyo was pitiful. It looks decent but kept failing. I read the reviews and decided to pay $5 for the O Remote app and it worked on launch. I was able to add my NAS as a DLNA media server and Pandora.    Everything is sweet now!    I hope it works for you. If not, do call Onkyo customer support number listed in the book. review_body: I wanted this thing so long, and now that I have it, it really is a let down. First, the good - the form factor is great. It pairs well with my iphone with the included rubber band for one convienent package. And it does a pretty good job at making the music louder. I connect with an iPhone LOD and rarely need to move higher than volume level 10-11 (out of 60).  The bad - While the sound is \\"louder\\", it isn't necessarily \\"fuller\\" as I expected from reading the reviews of this product. Also, I get absolutely TERRIBLE crackling in both the 3.5m output jacks and the input jack if a cable is moved during playback. As a portable amp/DAC, some movement will occur, so my playback often sounds bad. Cleaning the jacks hasn't helped, and I get this same sound on different input cables and phones.  The ugly - The DAC, well, it just doesn't work. I only get sound out of the right channel. Searching online indicates this is a common problem.  As a result, I give this unit a solid 3 stars. It does serve the main purpose of why I bought it - to drive my Hd598s without having to have the volume cranked way up. product_title: Denon AKDL1 Dedicated Link Cable (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I am fairly happy with my purchase of this cable. I do have a single, serious reservation that I wish DENON would fix, then I could be completely happy. Here's my deal:

The cable is marketed as basically tangle free. And, that's true... OUT OF THE BOX! What they don't tell you is how the cable gets bent and crooked and twisted and tangled after you have played a lot of music.

I love music. I listen to mostly \\"Rock\\" from the 80s 90s and 2000s. I slip into some Jazz when feeling funky, some Blues with blistering guitars when in the mood, and some times some classical music. Needless to say, I play music a LOT via these cable, roughly 20 hours on an average day. Sometimes it will run for a few days straight.

What DENON did not engineer into this product was the variance in weight of sending digital music (basically data, zeros and ones) over the cable, over long periods of time. Maybe they did not test the product for as many hours as they should have before shipping it. The bottom line, though, and my aggravation, is that playing too much music over the cable cause the cable to begin to bend at the bottom, and then eventually begin to twist into such a tight mess that the cable cannot even lay flat anymore. Crap!

I invited my best friend, who used to work over at the Apple Genius Bar, to come over for a look and tell me what she thought. She's one of the brightest field engineers Apple ever had, so I was confident she could at least help me understand what the bleep was happening to my very expensive cable. Here's the scoop, as I can best understand it:

1) Audio sent over this cable must be converted from Analog (what we hear) to Digital (basically, a series of computer zeros and ones), are sent over the cable, then must be converted back to Analog to be reproduced by the speakers, and thus hearable to our ears.
2) The data (again, zeros and ones) travels over the cable at very high speeds, much higher than the average speaker system is design to handle. As you will see, also too fast for this fancy cable...
3) As the high speed data travel through the cable, the lighter data (zeros) naturally migrates to the top of the cable [ie, stratification], and the heavier data (the ones) tends to migrate to the bottom of the cable.
4) It takes quite a bit of use, but after many hours of consistent music playback, the heavier data signals cause the bottom of the cable to visually begin to bend. First, it just starts out as a minor bending, but over time, the cable begins to twist and then turn into a tight spiral about 3 inches in diameter. I do not know if there is any significance to the size of the diameter.
5) The twisting is permanent, and no amount of untwisting, stretching, pulling, yanking or ironing boarding will straighten it out. So, it now looks like crap in my expensive home theater system.
6) And, \\"no\\" to you smart heads that will try to say: 'Play a different style of music, maybe the cable will even itself out.' It doesn't work that way, mo-rons. So, stop leaving comments about that.
7) According to my friend, there is no known method for untangling this spider web of a mess. I have wasted my money. She also stressed that, depending on the type of music you *tend* to play (there's no pure science to this part), the cable could bend more or bend less: it appears unscientifically that Jazz, Flute music of any kind, and Spoken Word Poetry/Music tend to do the least damage to the cable, while Death Metal (expected) and Acoustic Guitar-driven Blues (totally unexpected by me) tend to do the most damage. Other musically genres tend to stand somewhere in the middle.

All that being said, I love Amazon and they have graciously allowed me to return the product for a full refund.

What strikes me is that the 100 watt system really isn't much louder than the 50 watt system, however the 100 watt system provides much higher quality sound. For example, when I turn the 50 watt system up all the way it creaks and there is a lot of distortion, but when I turn the 100 watt system up all the way the sound is perfect. Even when playing really loud, complex music the 100 watt system delivers clean, crisp sound, and it does so EVEN when turned up to the highest volume level.

Here is the breakdown of the three Coby MP3 systems available. These are the power measures THEY are claiming are in their systems, you can decide for yourself how they actually perform:

CSMP67 50W Multimedia Speaker System: 30 watt subwoofer, 2 10 watt satellites = 50 watts
CS-MP77 75-Watt System: 35 watt subwoofer, 2 20 watt satellites = 75 watts
CSMP80 100 Watt System: 50 watt subwoofer, 20 25 watt satellites = 100 watts

review_headline: Very lightweight, decent sound, works with hats while running.
review_body:

Don't seem overly durable but for the cost I wasn't expecting much. I also have a pair of in ear Sennheiser's and some Phillips in-ear's as well. The Sennheiser's have slightly better sound to them although the bass output of these is close to the Senn's. These lose a very small amount of acoustics due to the ear pieces not completing a seal in the ear but very minimal loss. My music still sounds great and with plenty of bass if not a little on the tinny side for the highs.

The in-ear headphones which I've paid lots for and used for a while sound great but just don't stay in while running unless you have the right ear size to exactly fit their custom adapters. I felt like every run I was reaching up to adjust them and that frankly pissed me off. ;) I use running to de-stress and unwind a little. These fit nicely in the ears and provide great sound without having to mess with them. (These are my initial comments, after I run today I'll update with any issues if any.)

For those that wear hats/glasses while running, these so far fit fine under or over the top of my adidas running hat and work with my Costa Del Mar sunglasses. I have slim frames (over the ear part) on my glasses so results will vary for others.

Cord is plenty long if not a little too long but will accommodate most body types and lengths. That's all I have for now. Again, I will update post run today if any issues pop up that I feel should be recognized.

Four stars for build quality (just don't seem to be very sturdy but time will tell) and sound quality is slightly less than higher end models. For the cost though, they are dang close though!

UPDATE: After using them running I am still impressed. Sound was great and I really liked the lightweight feeling of both the headset and cord. The cord was a little long (I'm 6'2\\") but I ran it down my shirt to my Ipod on my shorts and it was light enough that it didn't bother at all. Also if you wear the hat, it almost helps to keep a little additional pressure on the ear pieces which, for me, improved the sound quality slightly. All in all good short term assessment. Will update later if it breaks or any negatives are noticed.
