product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_headline: Just reaffirming what another reviewer, Joshua Brooks, has wrote
review_body: This review basically reaffirms what another reviewer, Joshua Brooks, has written on this headphone set. Just like Josh, I compared this the Technica ATH-ANC7B to the Bose C15 and Sennheiser PXC 450. Like him, I came to the same conclusions regarding 3 different judging criteria, quality of sound/music, build quality and noise canceling capability. Summaries of each of these are below. Please note that all facts (i.e., prices, etc.) are applicable at time review was written, Nov. 2011).  Build quality  Bose C15 - despite being about $300 these things are quite poorly built. One would think that they were a K-Mart product.  Sennheiser PXC 450 - best build quality. Sturdily built, even though only $200 in price.  Technica - Also well built albeit only slightly less well built than the Sennheiser (but much better than the Boise). This is despite the fact that these are only $150.  Sound/Music quality  Bose C15 - Mediocre compared to the other two.   Sennheiser PXC 450 - best of three.   Technica - Considerably better than Bose but only slightly worse than the Sennheiser.   Sound Cancelation Capability  Bose C15 - Far better than the other two. Leaves them in the dust.   Sennheiser PXC 450 - Worst of the three. Far worse than Bose and slightly worse than Technica.   Technica - Slightly better than Sennheiser but far worse than Bose.   In short, considering the fact that the TEchnica is about $150 while the Sennheiser about $220 and the Bose $300, the Technica gives the best bang for the buck in terms of aggregate performance.   PS- I have not tested these things for sound \\"leakage\\" and hence cannot opine on that quality criteria.

review_headline: Great headphones! Lose the excessive packaging...
review_body: I received a pair of Monster iSport Immersion headphones through a review program with full rights to talk the good, the bad, and the ugly in return that I have an option to keep them.  I'll start with the ugly, too much of a packaging footprint. In a time of going green I felt guilty opening the nice graphic box to find a cool looking plastic display case inside with the headphones resting in a pair of little blue ears.  Once the headphones are out the packaging they tuck nicely into a little pouch with a super functional clip closure - easy in and easy out. The bad - you're done with the packaging - into the recycle bin - that was a waste.  The good, there are a few so I'll start with the cord. Simply put, this is one headphone cord that doesn't seem to tangle like others - I currently have 4 other headphones that tangle. Secondly, the fit - although not an automatic fit at first try, after swapping eartips and ear hooks I got them dialed in. For me the fit is critical as I'm thrashing terrain on my mountain bike and trail running and have to slow up if the earphone pops out - this has not happened with the iSports. Thirdly, the sound is clean with ample bass - sounds great with no wind interference - if you ride you know what I mean. One last one - the phone and music control function (next song, volume, etc) work really well - better than pulling out the iPhone to adjust.   These iSports are keepers.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 1100 Universal Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: First off - I work in IT (so I know a thing or two about computers) and am usually pretty open-minded and patient when it comes to new hardware and software. That said...  This remote control is so horrible that it is ridiculous.  Where do I even begin? The software is s..........l.........o...........w, and after you've gone and configured your device, it often has you start all the way at the beginning again, and do everything over. I've pressed every button on the remote for my satellite receiver and have had it tell me that the satellite was successfully configured 3 times, only to have it come back and say I have \\"no device that changes channels\\". What am I supposed to do, buy a brand new receiver? (The one I have, by the way, is four months old.)  Even without the satellite, I tried to program it to play a CD using my Philipps cd player (doesn't get much more basic than that, does it?) and it either turned on the CD player to \\"AUX\\" (not to \\"CD\\"), or the remote completely freezes and can only be reset by connecting it to a computer or removing the battery. Pressing \\"HELP\\" also causes the remote to freeze, and the \\"HELP\\" page is BLANK.  In the days of tablets and affordable technology, this remote is like a very expensive blast from the past - it's like using one of those giant cell phones from the 1990s to try and send a .jpg as an email attachment. Not gonna happen.  As I usually don't believe horribly negative product reviews (because I usually assume it's the end user that's the problem, not the product) I will give you one piece of advice if you decide to purchase this remote anyway...save the receipt, the packaging, the packaging slip, and anything else you will need to SEND IT BACK!

review_headline: Great value. Perfect for basic needs.
review_body: Have connected my cable, Panasonic Blu Ray player and computer to this box. Auto switching works perfectly. I did not need the remote or the AC adapter (adapter has to be purchased separately). I had a small hiccup initially, when the box would not switch away from the Blu Ray player. I have since turned off the quick start mode and have had no problems. Picture quality remains intact when passing signal through this box. Functionality and build quality are excellent for a product costing a little over  ten bucks.

review_body:

product_title: Nuforce DIA-BLACK Digital Input Amplifier (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I originally contacted Nuforce to ask if they had a product that would be a simple bridge between the upcoming iCloud Match service and speakers. I had previously thought of getting an Apple TV but since I have TiVo it would have been somewhat redundant (Netflix). The iCloud is 256 Kbps and the upgrade in quality, matched by a high quality Nuforce DAC feeding a pair of excellent bookshelf speakers seemed like a high fidelity approach to a home system that would fit my small living room and serve TV, PS3, TiVo and Airport Express iCloud feed. I had already bought Nuforce's Icon HDP headphone amp for my computer workstation so I was happy with their quality.

Bottom line is that the audio quality is, well, a difficult thing to characterize for me in words. Suffice to say that if the recording is well made, like live or in the room with you sounding, the sound from the Dia will be he same. Quality in, quality out. iCloud is serving pretty well save for some wireless signal drops. I also bought Nuforce's Tangent E5 speakers. Figured that although they didn't make them, merely resold them, they were an approved match and they have not disappointed.

So my search is over. I have a small, efficient, portable system. I do suggest for customers looking the setup three optical devices that you buy a coaxial interface box with a Dynex Digital RCA audio cable to use the coax connection. To use the optical out port from an Airport Express there seems to be just one cable available: the Belkin 6' Digital Toslink Optical Audio Cable with Line-Out Adapter. The little 3.5 mm adapter for the Airport Express is the key to the connection.

product_title: VideoSecu Mounts Tilt TV Wall Mount
review_body: I have installed 3, 55\\" TV using wall mounts. The first 2 were with $125+ mounts, both of which tilted but the tilt locks were not very easy to use - plastic handles, no leverage. product_title: Philips WiFi MP4 Player with Android
review_headline: Not the iPod, but isn't that the point?
review_body: This is the first MP3 player I've owned. Oh, my last phone played MP3s, as does my current one. But I've never had an MP3 only device until now. Of course the point of this thing is that it isn't JUST MP3s. No, it connects to the Android store and that gives you, oh, all sorts of fun things to do!  The device itself is smaller than my Samsung Galaxy Smartphone, but it is, I do believe, a bit larger than the iPod. It has a lovely screen that works quite well if you look at it just right. If it is at the incorrect angle, it looks really odd. On the other hand, the touch screen works well for playing games like Angry Birds and Plants vs Zombies, both of which I was able to download from Amazon's Android ap store.  As for the music and video quality, well, the music quality seems good. It's at least as good as my phone when it's playing music. The ear buds that come with it are better than what I had before, so that's a plus. I had no problem using the Songbird MP3 player software, though I also downloaded Amazon's MP3 player and that seems to work well, too.  Video sound and picture quality are also quite good, but that problem I mentioned before of having to look at it just right rears its ugly head when looking at videos. Also I had a 1:33 ratio vid playing that was resized to 16:9, and I couldn't find a way to make it go back to the correct ratio. I do have a Netflix account and Netflix app on this, but I can't ever get it to play videos, so nothing to report on streaming quality.  That said, I haven't any other complaints. The setup with my wireless connection was easy and it synched nicely with everything it needed to.  I'm not sure if this is a good buy compared with the iPod, but I will say that its a good quality device and gets the job done.

product_title: Sony BDV-E570 Blu-ray Player Home Entertainment System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Performance falls a tiny bit short, but it delivers on the basics
review_body:
This is almost a great system. Almost.

While it delivers great sound, and DVDs look awesome, in just about every other way there are at least some shortcomings. (And I did update the firmware folks).

1. The remote - It controls some of my Sharp Aquos TV functions, but not others. So I still need my TV remote with me. What's the point?

2. Slow - the thing is so annoyingly slow to power up (and then start a blu ray). In the mornings I like to listen to the radio. You turn it on and every day you are greeted with the screen \\"please wait.\\" My cheapest 3 dollar radio will turn on right away - sheesh. For disc watching - by the time you get through the boot up, and it finally accepts a disc, it takes another good minute to get some discs going (and often for me, begin skipping trailers). Most of the web enabled functions are also slow (see below).

3. Hit or miss USB and networking - No video functionality on the USB stick. Music and pics work fine. Want to try the web apps like Pandora or Netflix? Well often they are slow to connect to your wifi. Try to be patient. The DLNA networking with my Windows 7 laptop is pretty useless. Video is choppy, pics are slow to load, and music doesn't load at all.

In sum, there's lots of bells and whistles, but most features fall short in execution.

June 2012 update - I just noticed a bunch of new streaming apps have appeared. That's pretty nice! While I still think this has more bugs than it should, and plods more than it should, I've grown to appreciate the web functionality and sound and video that it does very well. I'm notching it up to 4 stars.

product_title: Belkin Components F8M066ttP Tune Cast Universal Inline
review_body: I have used several FM transmitters over the last several years. This Belkin is the latest. Pros include a digital display with two saved presets. Great so you can swap between channels if one starts to fade. My family lives in a more rural area, so its not too challenging to get an open frequency or two, though I could see that this might be an issue in more urban settings.  The Belkin is easy to connect, both to the iPod(through the ear-bud connector) and to the vehicle(via a cigarette-lighter connection).  Cons include other channels creeping in on the frequency being used. I also wish that the transmitter would charge my ipod. I have had units that do this, but in all fairness, this one is just not set up for that function. I will say the volume is also marginal at best. I've discovered that setting my ipod to 50% and controlling the volume from the radio at that point provides the best volume without distortion, but that's not the most resounding endorsement.  For us, the Belkin has been a decent add to our vehicle. The CD player died a few months back, and we haven't wanted to replace the whole head unit. So this does give us some control over our audio options. For the price, its not a bad option for our family. But your mileage may vary.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Fuze+ 8 GB MP3 Player
review_headline: Way Too Slow, Crashes Too Often
review_body: I wanted to come back to Amazon and write a review on this particular Sansa MP3 player. I am not happy with it at all. This is the 4th type of Sansa player we have had in our family and I have never had such a bad experience as I have with this particular model. The response time on this model is horrific. Power it up and it takes a full 2 minutes before you can do anything with it. Push a control and count to 5 before it responds to your touch. The controls on this player are touch sensitive and not real buttons such as on the original Fuze. The controls are all over the place. It takes constant pushing, rubbing, etc to try and get a response, or it blasts through 3-4 changes with barely a nudge. You can't pick it up without it forwarding a song, pausing, etc. It crashes on me about every 3rd or 4th use making a horrible buzzing sound that only stops when you hold the power button down for about 15 seconds. I updated the firmware as soon as I got it and it acts like this after the fact. No new updates have come down so I'm stuck with it. When it plays, it sounds great, the graphics are clear, but it is just too much of a pain. My 11 year old daughter has the original Fuze and it is so much more user friendly. She constantly asks me why is my player so slow?!! If you need a good player, buy the original Fuze and wait till Sansa develops a better product. If I didn't have so much time spent in building my catalog, I would def ask for a refund. Hope this helps.

product_title: IHOME Rechargeable Mini Speakers
review_body: I travel on business around half the time to every corner of the world as a band manager and music industry consultant. My tools for the road are a MacBook Air, an iPad and the iPhone. They're extremely portable and very powerful at the same time for getting things done as well as providing entertainment during the long business trips. I'm also a guitar player and plug the guitar into any of these devices to play and record music in my spare time. I decided that I needed very portable speakers so I don't have to always use the headset to listen to music or playing the guitar.  I looked at a variety of options and decided to go with the iHM79SC. Having a few iHome units around in the house, I felt reasonably confident that this unit would do the job. I'm happy to say that these speakers actually exceeded my expectations in every possible way. It's as small and light as I hoped it to be and it sounds as good as I expected it to be. One important thing for me with a set of speakers is stereo separation and being able to place the two speakers about two feet apart really is the clincher in getting a good room-filling sound.  As far as sound quality, one has to expect tradeoffs for getting something this small and portable. You're simply not going to get the deep low-end and clear midrange with silky highs with speakers this size. But it's certainly good enough for most hotel rooms to hook up your laptop and iOS devices. I also use it at home now hooked up to an AirPort Express to stream music from the iPhone anywhere in the house. This is one of those devices that really made me feel like I'm getting a big bang for the buck and that doesn't happen often. I'm one very happy camper with this tiny speaker set.

product_title: Positive Grid JamUp Plug - Audio Interface for iPad, iPhone
review_headline: Finally figured out what the iPhone was invented for!
review_body:
Seriously. If you play guitar or bass and own a compatible Apple device, you need this product.
I ordered and purchased the companion product JamUp Pro and the two products together are fantastic. The JamUp Plug is about the size of a 9 volt battery and about half the weight.Its made of white plastic. It has a male input on the length side and two inputs on one of the ends. A large input to plug your guitar cable into and a small input for headphones, earbuds or a mini speaker. The product looks and feels like its made really cheaply, which is why I gave it a four star rating. If it holds up I will come back and upgrade the rating. Only time will tell.

I think you need some sort of app to interface with this device, and there are a few. I purchased JamUp pro from iTunes. There is a free version, however, it got such great reviews that I bought the full version and am really, really pleased with it. JamUp Pro is an amp modeling tool and has a really nice interface. I used it right out of the gate with the JamPlug. If you want to read about it look up JamUp Pro in iTunes.

The two products together are exactly what the iPhone/iPod/iPad were invented for. I can plug in my guitar and some headphones, record some track, jam to songs, practice, whatever, and with great sound and little to no setup time or equipment to haul around.

Good job on this one!

review_body: These are a great value, if purchased with a protection plan. I would recommend purchasing these from an electronics store with at least a two year protection plan. No earbuds at this price range will last long with 6-12 hours of use almost every day like I use them.  Now that that's out of the way, these sound great. Good bass, good mids, clear highs. These sound clearer than my Altec Lansing UHP106's bought for the same price and don't have the cord-sound interference that those had. The bass isn't as loud as those, but that's not a big deal to me. I like the angled design so you always know automatically which bud goes on which ear. These are very light with a tight fit in my ear, so I'm not worried about them ever falling out. I couldn't care less about the on-cord volume adjust, but it's cool to know it's there, I guess.   I really do love them and it's great to know I can get a free replacement pair for a least two years when they inevitably stop working.

product_title: Nuvo Tier Black Metallic Frame
review_headline: Nice Look, Not the Same Color As Pictured
review_body: Pros:  First off, the table has a nice, sleek look to it that really enhances my living room.  The pieces of wood are pretty heavy and can definitely take on a lot of weight.  The table is elegant and its transparent design hides the fact that the table is actually very strong.  I was concerned about getting a table shipped to my door, but there were no problems.  The pieces were safely packed into the box with extra padding.  Only the bottom shelf had a tiny scratch on it.  Also, it took about 30 mins to put together, but I would recommend having someone to help you.   Cons:  The \\"cherry wood top\\" as displayed in the picture is not the same color of wood that was shipped to me.  The table that I received was more of a mocha/ dark rosewood color.  I didn't mind the difference, but be careful if you are actually looking for that lighter cherry wood finish.   The table is pretty low.  It is about an inch lower than my last table.  So far, the height hasn't been an issue because my couch sits a little low.    The biggest problem I had was that my new receiver could barely fit on the middle shelf.  In order for it to squeeze through I had to take off the side metal bars and push it through.  There is still some room for ventilation, but I'm disappointed that the shelf wasn't designed to be a little taller to accommodate these receivers.  If I have to take the receiver out of the table in the future, I am going to have to take the side metal piece off.  Not a huge deal, just slightly annoying.    Overall, I'm pretty satisfied with this product.  It looks great in my living room and it shipped quickly, without any harm to the pieces.  I ordered 2 Atlantic media bins for the lower shelf to hold DVDs and other items.  I think the shelf with the bins is going to look great.  If you are looking for a low, sleek design then I would recommend this product.

product_title: Ports HDMI Powered Splitter for Full HD
review_body: This splitter works well at creating two hdmi signals.  Only problems are it runs very warm (make sure you keep it in a ventilated area), the power light is very bright, and it puts off RF interference.  When it's idle, a small amount of interference can be heard through my battery powered am radio (usually tuned to 560).  When it's working, it makes the radio unlistenable.  I listed to talk radio often and this is irritating- I have to unplug the splitter at times.  The interference isn't coming through the house wiring (the radio powered by batteries), and I checked the splitter power adapter on it's own- no noise.  It's definitely the splitter itself.  Just something to consider if you're looking at buying.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-the-Ear Headphones
review_body: I've heard good and bad reviews about these headphones. I didn't know who to trust, so I decided to buy some for myself. Right out of the box, I started wearing them and I found them to be pretty comfortable. But after a couple hours, I could actually feel them pressing against my head, before I couldn't. But that sensation went away fairly quickly. The sound quality on these were a little rusty at first, but after \\"burning in\\" the speakers, they started to sound better. They started to actually leave my jaw dropped. I compared them to Beats Pro and well, I found the Beats inferior in style, sound quality, AND comfort. But I must say that the Crossfades are a bass biased headphone. What that means is if you like bass, this is the headphone for you. Also, these do have a nice extent of passive noise cancellation. I think it cancels up to 10 or 12 db. Like I said before, these headphones are a bass biased pair headphones. With that being said, that means these headphones are bad for certain genres such as: Rock, Metal, Jazz, etc. The bass just overpowers the song. But, that does mean that these headphones work good with other genres such as: Rap, Pop, Dubstep, etc. If you're into that type of music then go ahead, be my guest and buy these headphones.  *EDIT*  It's been about 3 weeks since I got these and they are still going strong. The only problem is a little chip in the black plastic surrounding the metal faceplates. It was no big deal though, I just painted over it. Also, the speakers sound even better than better. They have better highs, mids, and bass now, even considering the conditions I've put it through. Dropped probably 15+ times. Once off a 20 ft drop; harsh weather: snow, hail, massive rain. Best constructed headphones I've used. Most durable also.

product_title: Polk Audio CS20 Center Channel Speaker (Black)
review_headline: Polk Audio CS20 Center Channel Speaker
review_body: I have a Yamaha VR-X671 7.1 receiver with two Polk TSi400 speakers. The Yamaha is setup in bi-amp mode. The speakers are set in \\"large mode'. This is Yamaha talk for setting up the speakers to do more base I believe. I do not have a sub woofer so this mode seems to give good base without burning the paint off the walls. I am not an expert on audio but it sounds good to me. I use this setup in a 24x20 room with a TV and internet radio. I bought the Polk CS20 to try and get clearer dialog with the TV. I use mainly over the air TV and Netflix. Occasionally I play videos from a computer of NAS server as well. The CS20 does improve the dialog for my ears. I bought the black speaker even though I have cherry finished main speakers. The cherry finish is $50 more and according to the spec the standard speaker grill covers the cherry anyway. I guess some people remove the grills to see the finish. The only downside to this speaker is it is big and heavy. The weight of the speaker dictated that I set it on a shelf under the TV. I'm in California so I don't want this thing flying around the room when the next 5.8 quake hits. If you do mount it on the wall or over the TV a substantial shelf will be needed. The center speaker seems to mainly be useful for video dialog and does not help much with music to my ears. Overall I am pleased with this purchase.

product_title: Acoustic Research Xsight Universal Remote Control
review_headline: Outstanding! EZ to program and very well designed!
review_body: I've found this remote to be near ideal. It is, as promised, extremely easy to program. Many codes for various audio & video components are carried onboard, and a simple, logical programming sequence helps you find the appropriate codes for your devices. If you wish to have full(er) functionality, installing AR's software and accessing their web-based code library dials in your remote very nicely. There you simply enter your component's model number or alternatively, the component's remote control model number, and Voila! you're off to the races! Once I had the hang of the process, I was able to program components in under four or five minutes. The remote itself exudes quality; the blue backlighing provides illumination of   all buttons. And it is ideally illuminated: bright enough for good viewing but not too bright in your darkened viewing area or theater. As well, the remote's lighting features motion-sensing activation: pick it up, the lighting comes on; set it down, it extinguishes after a few seconds. The only nits I've encountered thus far are these: two buttons, whose functions are oft used, are decidedly on the smallish side. Still, with the fine backlighting on offer, one can quickly adapt to this shortcoming. I am extremely happy and impressed with the design of this unit. I cannot imagine what those universal remotes which cost multiples of this unit can bring to the table that would improve on its overall user-friendliness.   My family is near ecstatic with this remote!

product_title: Sennheiser Digital Wireless Headphones
review_headline: FINALLY!  Wireless that works the way it should.
review_body: First, let me say that I don't really consider myself a \\"die-hard\\" audiophile, that said, besides owning these rs180 wireless phones, I also own Sennheiser hd-555, hd-598, and the hd-650 corded cans.  I appreciate solid performing headphones and the rs180's fill that need exceptionally well and have the big added benefit of being cordless.  I'm not going to go into a full sound quality breakdown here, but I will say for those familiar with the 598's and 650's, the RS180's IMHO fall somewhere between the two.  Closer to the 598's I think.  A little better mids and bass than the 598's.  Brighter, airier, but not quite the very fine overall perfomance of the 650's in regards to soundstaging and imaging. Although, I do think they work better than the hd 650's for movie watching.  But not with music.  This really is an incredible achievment for a wireless headset.    Set up was as simple as it gets.  I tried connecting through both the headphone jack and also the zone2 outs on my pioneer vsx-819h (used for home theater).  There was really not a noticable difference in the quality of sound between the two connections, so I decided to stay with the phone jack for ease of use.  Charging the headset took about 8 hours.  Once charged I was able to stroll out into my back yard (150ft) with no signal loss at all.  I also haven't experienced any problems with my wireless network as described in some other reviews that I've read.  I found the headset to be light and comfortable (a bit heavier than the hd555's they will replace for movie watching) and have worn them for up to four hours so far with no sense of fatigue or any other difficulties.  I also connected them to my Denon AVR-3312CI (used for music) and found them to be very competant for music appreciation.  Though as stated above, they won't be replacing my hd-650's for this purpose.  I would also add that so far I haven't experienced any drop outs or noticible back ground noise at all.  I've been very impressive.   As for the controls, yes it's a bit of a bother having to turn both the base and headset on before use.  And yes, the controls on the headset take a little getting used to.  However, I find both issues to be very minor and believe the perfomance of these phones far out-weighs the few negatives.    Overall, I would most definitely recommend these to anyone looking for solid performing wireless headphones.

product_title: Monster Cable Earth Wind and Fire Gratitude In-ear Headphones
review_body:
I listened to a wide range of music on these headphones in order to review them properly. I listened to Classical (Vivaldi, Mendelssohn, Bach, and Mozart) , a cappella (anonymous 4 and collegiate), Swing (Benny Goodman) plus a bunch of my favorites (Cowboy Junkie's Trinity Sessions, Gillian Welch, and Emmylou Harris and a few other isolated songs).

The sound on these truly was superb, I heard elements of the pieces that I had not heard before. The clarity of the sound was very good on all the pieces I tested but was best for the vocal pieces. I tried to find something bass-heavy but my musical tastes tend more towards vocalists (especially singer songwriter types) so I can not comment on how these handle heavy bass. The classical music I listened to sounded fine (good but not mind blowing) but where they really shone is on the vocal pieces and on Jazz.

These came with 12 pairs of different sized ear buds. I have very small ears (because I am a very small person) and I was able to find buds that fit perfectly. I admit this favorably biases me towards these because I usually just have to make do with buds that almost work but really kind of fall out of my ears. Also, the packaging of these is done very well so these would make a good gift. They come with a suede case with a leather carrying case for the headphones.

My take, if you listen to a lot of vocal music, you may want to take a serious look at these. For me and the type of music I listen to, these really are worth the money. If you listen to primarily instrumental music or a lot of classical music, you should probably look at other headphones.

product_title: Etymotic Research In-Ear Headset with 3-Button Remote Control for iPod, iPhone, iPad
review_body: I bought this headset to use with my iPhone for a train trip over the Christmas season in 2011. Gladly, they arrived on time and I tested them out at home before taking my trip to see how much noise they would isolate. First, I tried the 3-flange tips that were already mounted on the headset. However, even after inserting them with the recommended method from their website, I found them to be too uncomfortable to wear that deep in the ear. In addition to that, the seal was unstable and would allow sound in with slight movements of I my head. Both sizes of 3-flange inserts gave the same results. I can't fault the design, it may just be the way my ears are made. Fortunately, they provided 3 different types of inserts, two of which are foam.   The glider type is the easiest to insert and provides very good isolation. However, the foam inserts are the best in my opinion. These have to be pinched or rolled between your thumb and finger then inserted into the ear. Once inserted, the foam slowly expands to the shape of your ear canal and most outside sounds are blocked. Once you turn on your music, the outside world disappears. Plus, these are the most comfortable to wear for long periods of time (I fell asleep on the train with them in for over an hour).   As for the sound, they sound very clean and clear. With the deep insertion, and isolation, I've heard details in songs I never heard before. The midrange and highs are well balanced and the bass response is clean without distortion or rumble. At first I thought they should have deeper bass, but I'm not sure I could tolerate those frequencies that deep in my ear for long, so I'm satisfied as is. Some may disagree but it works for me. I haven't used the inline mic control for phone calls yet, only music playback so I can't speak to the quality of the mic yet. However, I love the free Awareness App that works with the headset and allows ambient noise to be picked up by the microphone so you don't miss things going on around you while wearing your headset. It's very well thought out.   Pros:  Nice price point. Great sound isolation. Good sound quality. Nice options for ear tips to fit different people.   Cons:  Cable noise can be bothersome if you're on he move.

product_title: URC WR7 Universal Remote Control for up to 7 A/V Components with 4 Favorite Channel Buttons
review_headline: Good enough to prompt my praise
review_body:
This remote does what I need it to do. I don't think I would be any happier with one of those $200+ gizmos. My major goal was to make my surround sound system easy enough for my wife to use without complaining (much.) She is somewhat of a technophobe, or at the very least, not \\"turned on\\" by technology.

I have a bit of a complex system with a Yamaha receiver, Panasonic HD TV, TIVO, DVD Player, and a Roku Box for Netflix. Every one of these require separate input selections and operating controls. The different remotes drive my wife crazy. She gets angry when she can't \\"just figure out how to watch TV.\\" WR7 to the rescue!

I'm not going to claim that I programed my system in 10 minutes. It probably took me an hour or more to get it the way I wanted it. This remote is an advanced piece of technology with numerous options, including macros that let you program a series of successive commands. I continued to tweak things for several days till I got the easiest one-button setups I could conjure up. My wife loves it, and that makes me happy.

On the down side, a few minor quibbles.

1) Why a VCR button? VCRs are nearly extinct, but I guess they didn't get the memo. I use it for my DVR instead, and I would rather have the button actually labeled that way. There is also a CD button, but I venture that most everyone doubles their DVD player as a CD player. For my money, I would prefer a PC button instead as computers and dedicated servers are figuring more into entertainment systems these days.

2) You have to get a little creative for special functions and remember your setups. For instance, there is no \\"TIVO button\\" function, so you have to choose an alternative and remember it. Likewise for the \\"Home\\" button on the Roku, and the input selectors and sound programs for my surround receiver. A bit of ingenuity and creativity overcomes these things.

For the money, I could hardly be happier. Overall, this is a great product that does an excellent job of solving what is admittedly a very complex dilemma.tedly a very complex dilemma.

Turns out they are in a new format called MP3.  Well, I can handle this. After understanding the issue, the problem was simple. I need a new CD player that can play the format. In addition, I need a car adapter.  Went back to Amazon and saw a nice looking unit, so I bought it, a case, and a car adaptor kit. Put a new CD into my nice new machine, plugged in the ear buds, and tested it. Instead of  a gripping story in sound I only got a display reporting \\"READING\\". Great, I thought, it is reading the new format and soon I will hear sound. No such luck.  The unit has the worst kind of failure, failed out right out of the box. Moreover, this is a common problem as reported in other reviews.  While people who have a unit that works seem to like them, I'm unhappy. I'll pay more attention to the reviews, and over time, become wiser.

product_title: Sony PRS-T1 6" Digital E-Ink Pearl eReader with Wi-Fi (Black)
review_body: I was desperate to find an e-ink device with pinch-to-zoom, so I jumped on this as soon as I knew of it.  Now I'm sorry I did.  The device does work at the simplest level, but press it in any way and it falls to pieces.  I took my standard set of ebooks (all PDFs) I use daily in my NookColor that is contained on a 32GB MicroSD and loaded it into the Sony.  Almost immediately the (already slow) device went pretty much dead.  Opening the list of books either takes 10-15 minutes (no, I'm not exaggerating) or completely locks up.  Pressing reset does nothing.  Pressing the on/off switch brings up a screen asking if I really want to shutdown and when I select \\"Yes\\", it freezes again.  I frequently get a message saying \\"The ContentManager has stopped working\\".  This message is displayed in response to my attempt to enter three different \\"modules\\".  After a hour of trying, I gave up on trying to do anything with the reader with a large microSD installed, it just can't handle it.  After giving up on the microSD I removed the card and rebooted (waiting another 5 minutes).  I then opened the preinstalled Jules Verne novel and got to see page one, and the reader locked up again.  Reboot again, wait some more, try a different preinstalled book, ok, this one opens without crashing, whoopee!  I finally get to try the pinch to zoom, and yes it does work, but it's very clumsy and difficult to use.  Partially this is unavoidable, since the screen is e-ink, there is no feedback to see the size change as you pinch.  My biggest complaint here is that the resize is slow and repaints the screen twice when you finish your resize (once apparently is a simple pixel zoom and the second time actually re-renders the fonts).  Why would they do something so stupid? Beats me.  I could go on and on with my experiences, but I'll just skip to the conclusion.  Conclusion: An acceptable reader that is similar to the Kindle graphite model but is far less polished.  Crashes frequently, hangs mysteriously, overall the firmware is a fiasco.  Although the pinch to zoom feature should make this device far nicer to use than a Kindle, poor execution leaves it as a device that should be avoided.  Since I've now used most of the major ereaders, some people might like to know of ereaders that I would recommend.  I use the NookColor most of the time, it is a very good reading system, but does crash occasionally, and battery life is typical of an LCD system, so power needs to be available regularly.  The Kindle DX has an excellent screen and will last a very long time on a charge.  The DX is awkward to navigate for large format PDFs, but the screen is large enough that this isn't too much of an issue.  The standard Kindle graphite 6 inch is acceptable, but only for simple fiction, not formatted text books.  The iPad is a good reading device, but is too large and heavy for my taste.  The MacBook Air isn't really a reader, but is small enough and much more convenient to use than the iPad.

product_title: Peel Universal Controller (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
So I plugged the powered dongle into my router, put the battery powered Peel infrared blaster in the living room and after a few minutes the Peel App on my iPhone knew what was on and could change channels and adjust volume automatically. As I started using it more I grew more enamored with it. Can't find your physical remote, no big deal just grab your phone and watch away. It controls my LG TV, and the DVR of my Verizon FiOS box. Based on my age, gender, and genre interests it also suggested some shows that would appeal to my demographic. Not bad, not bad at all... Then came the bad news, It doesn't recognize my DVD/VCR combo unit or my WD Live Hub box, so there is no way to control those devices from the phone. Also, I can only control it from the same WiFi network... why can't this be an option from web based console preferences, I understand the potential for joking/abuse if you can change channels from another zip code, but it could also serve as remote support for someone who doesn't know how to operate your TV. Also with an online console they could potentially they let you design/share custom remote control layouts and commands and send them to your phone. Finally, while it may get the big show right, I wish there was a traditional guide list on the phone with everything on it that I could flick through and change channels from.

PROS:
+ Easy to set up
+ Fun to use
+ Fairly smart at finding programming

CONS:
- Doesn't support devices not in its library
- No full listing grid
- Can't customize remotes or enter digits
- Can't use it from a separate network or 3G

product_title: Philips 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Alarm Clock Speaker Dock
review_body: I searched for a good iPod/iPhone clock radio for awhile. Most had the dock on top which I don't like on a nightstand since you could possibly knock the phone out if you reach across it during the night while charging/docked. The Philips has the dock in the front and the docking connector is spring loaded so it fits my iPhone WITH the case on...huge plus. There is a rubber bumper to keep the case from moving around if you're pressing on the phone display.   Likes: Front dock connector, 3 brightness levels, High (good for daytime, too bright for night), Low (good for night, not too bright not too dim) and OFF. Nice to find a clock radio that can actually turn off the display if wanted. Small footprint, saves space and is out of the way. Clock is displayed in white not neon blue or some other bright color that you don't want glaring in your face all night. Graduwake slowly ramps up the sound and can be turned off. Sound is decent, wasn't expecting home theater sound but perfect for playing your playlist or listening to radio.   Dislikes: Small clock display. Not too big a deal since it's most likely going to be near your face if used in a bedroom. MAJOR FLAW: When using the wake to radio feature, the radio station is always displayed, over-riding the CLOCK. Very annoying when lying in bed and wondering how much time you have until you have to get up since you can't tell the time....from a clock. It doesn't appear this can be changed or turned off unless the radio is turned off and the clock returns. I would prefer there is at least a button that could be pressed to check time or give the user the option to show the clock or Philips had the display return to the clock and keep a small station ID in the corner. I know what radio station I'm listening to since I set it....I want to know the TIME. Also, not a big deal but like other reviewers stated the clock does not auto-synch/update when phone is docked. Not a huge issue since just hold the set time button for 3-4 seconds and it re-synchs quickly.  Despite the one major flaw, very well designed and easy to use. Would be nice if Philips designed an app to automatically play your own playlists instead of having to create a custom playlist. I would recommend this to anyone wanting a decently priced iPod/iPhone dock who can live with everything mentioned above.

review_body: This was just what the doctor ordered to hook my speakers up to my TV. I couldn't believe just how difficult it was to find this connection and for the price I couldn't go wrong. I didn't want to go wires but I did need to have some way to use the ear phones. My husband says I am deaf as I have the TV so loud. I can now watch TV with ear phones on or off without my husband shouting that I have the volume too loud. product_title: Yamaha CRX-330BL Micro Component Receiver CD Player Unit (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
This is definitely a 5 star product when taking the price I paid ($187 for a B-Stock unit) into consideration. Yes there are some limitations....no AM (truly not missed by me), only 20w per channel and the equalizer is limited to Treble & Bass, but I have found that The Yamaha CRX-330 outputs a nice warm sound that doesn't require much tweaking. iPod control with the supplied remote control is a nice touch, but scrolling through the iPod menus from accross the room is useless since I can't read my iPod screen from there (not a criticism of the unit....just a fact).

One caveat: as others have mentioned, the remote is critical. The receiver sports a very minimalist design in regard to it's button array. This is beacuse you need to use the remote to access many of the units sub-menus. Luckily the remote is well made and feels quite sturdy despite it's small size. Still, don't lose or break it, or you're S.O.L.

As this unit comes without speakers, I paired the CRX-330 with some extra Mirage Nanosat Satellites I had but found the sound to be wanting. This was due to the frequency response of the satellites (110 Hz - 20 kHz). Once I added in my Mirage Nano S8 Subwoofer (33 Hz - 120 Hz) things were much better. Nice full and natural sound from both CD's & my iPod. Highly recommended as a budget conscious bedroom or office stereo system.

product_title: JLab Go Waterproof / Sweatproof / Sports MP3 Player Headphones - 4 GB - Black/Gray
review_body: I recently started training for a triathlon and found I was bored by swimming. So I looked for a waterproof MP3 player that wasn't too expensive. I didn't want a case for my ipod, because they change so much that the next time I buy one it won't fit in the case. So I came across this. For $50, it was worth it. Honestly, I could care less about the quality of the music, as long as I could hear it. I didn't expect much for that money. So far the music actually sounds pretty good (depending on how much water gets in my ears at any given time.) I saw people complaining about sound quality, but that is not what I found to be the biggest issue. These headphones are not very adjustable, and don't fit my  head that well. Additionally, they don't stay on once I do get them on. And forget push starts, they'll come right off! I had originally bought 1 for me and 1 from my husband, but he tried mine and said he hated them so I sent it back unopened. I finagled it so I tuck the back of the headphones into the strap of my goggles to keep it in place. It's not ideal and sometimes makes my goggles uncomfortable b/c of the positioning, but for $50 and music while I swim, it was worth it to me. So if your expectations aren't too high, these are for you. They work. But it takes a little bit more work to make them work for you.  The other thing people might not like is the fact that it will only play mp3 and wma files. If you have a lot of itunes music, it will take some extra work. I really only use it on shuffle, but if you want super organized playlists, don't bother.  You plug it into your computer and it shows up as a drive, and you drag and drop your music. Easy as can be.  UPDATE: beware that even if you are an amazon prime member you will still be charged $5 to return this item. Not Fair.

product_title: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this Logitech Harmony One Advanced remote for my husband because we have a brand new tv, brand new wi-fi bluray player, brand new 3D bluray player and a DVR. The website says all of our devices are compatible with this remote. However, we can only get one activity to work on the remote which makes this a waste of time. Says \\"easy 30 minute setup\\". NOT TRUE. It takes 15-20 minutes just to download any changes you make from the PC to the remote. We spent 8 hours attempting setup the first day, another 6-8 hours the second day, including 5.5 hours on the phone with customer service, only to be told that they needed to escalate our incident and that the next level of support will call in 1 or 2 days. Sent an email to support online, still have heard nothing - 1 day later. I guess if the setup had worked, I'd be happy and rate this as a good product... If it doesn't work and you have to get help via customer service, you're screwed. I'm so unsatisfied with this product and will never buy another Logitech Harmony remote again. Even if this remote starts to work for us, which I'm starting to doubt, It's not worth the amount of time we've wasted! Oh, and after I got an incident # on the phone, when I opened an incident online, I got a new #. There were 2000 incidents opened within 5 hours... So, I'm not the only one!!!

product_title: JBL On Beat Loudspeaker Dock for iPad, iPod and iPhone
review_headline: A Nicely Versatile Speaker System That Has One Drawback
review_body:
For use as an amplifier, this device does a good job. It produces good sound quality and amplification without thundering bass tones that are often associated with external speaker systems. This dock accomodates the following Apple products: iphone, ipod, and iphone which makes it very attractive to dedicated users of those devices. Its design is relatively compact and it offers portability. I've used it in several large interior spaces and it compares favorably to my much larger and older sound system that circuits through much of the house. I also used it outdoors when I left it on the patio as I prepped my garden for winter. Not sure if my neighbors would have objected on a warm weather day, but it produced nice sound and I didn't consider it invasive by any means since I was able to control the amplification. This dock also has an output jack that attaches to the tv (for which cable is not provided). It was fairly easy to hook it up to watch video on the tv as well since I had the the compatible cable/cord.
The only negatives that I can see is that it really can't be used as an alarm clock by which you can be awaken to music. Given the built in shutdowns for Apple devices, I can't figure out how to override it. This is not important to me, but some people would no doubt want that feature. Also, you cannot adjust to landscape orientation when using the iPad.
The suggested price of this device ($169) might turn some potential buyers off, but that doesn't seem like a realistic price and it appears that it can be purchased for significantly less.

product_title: Burton Technologies AcoustiBuds
review_headline: The smallest size is much too big for my big ears!
review_body:
I bought these in hopes of finding something to go ontop of my iPhone's included earbuds, to help them stay in my ears better, and to hear the amazing bass they produce better.

When I put them on the earbuds, the Acoustibuds tore the grey silicon gasket right off since you have to twist the Acoustibuds to get them to fit! That's not cool!

Once they were attached to my earbuds, I had a heck of a time fitting the smallest available size (4) into my ears. The things kept falling out. I twisted and twisted, and it left my ears feeling more raw than what I was dealing with before (black sponge covers for the earbuds.

After I managed to get the \\"fins\\" into my ear halfway, the sound that they produced was very \\"tinny\\" and distant. They say that they enhance bass. It's more like they eliminate the bass, which is incredibly disappointing. I'd like to return them, but I'm going to try to give them away to somebody else who might have bigger ears than I - and I've got pretty big ears.

If they made a size 1, perhaps they might fit and actually work as described. But Including the three largest sizes 4-6, and the fact that the size 4 doesn't fit the average person - it's sad. I was excited that these were made in the USA, but it stinks that they don't work as advertised.

product_title: Bose 141 Pair Fullrange Bookshelf Speakers
review_headline: Bottom line: I listen to music a LOT more
review_body: I do my listening at home via our (small) living room home theater type rig and a while back I realized how unsatisfying my Infinity 5-way system was to me - specifically the two front speakers for regular stereo. I upgraded my receiver to a decent Sony unit and replaced the Infinity spkrs with a pair of 141's. I am fairly knowledgeable about electronics and audio products and I'm aware of the drawbacks to some Bose products such as the weak construct of some of their overpriced NR headphones and the inherent flaw in the direct/reflecting speaker theory. [Reflecting off what? A flat wall on one side and a heavy fabric curtain on the other? Result: unbalanced sound, unless one designs the room around the speakers.]   These are budget speakers. However, instead of a 3rd rate tweeter/woofer config, Bose opted for a single 4.5\\" fullrange driver in the 141 and that's the beauty - and the limitation - to this speaker. The mids and highs are abundant and crisp, with even frequency response from lower mids on up, and a particular intangible smoothness, that \\"Bose sound\\" that one expects from speakers costing a great deal more.   OK, what about the bass? As stand-alone bookshelf speakers these might do quite well provided you have a graphic EQ either in the hardware of your rig or in your playback software (Winamp, etc) - I can't report since I haven't used them in that function. However with a subwoofer (passive Infinity) the overall sound is, above all, pleasing. I listen to music and great deal more than I used to and every time I play a track I notice how much I enjoy the flavor of the sound. Movies, TV and other video are also enhanced and sooner or later I'll need a 3rd unit to use as my center speaker (where the hell am I gonna find a single Bose 141?).  One negative reviewer points out that these are no match for a $1000 set of speakers from a reputable manufacturer. To that, I can add: the sun will rise in the east tomorrow. I will note that the price I'm seeing online new - $199 at Amazon - is a bit nuts for such a basic speaker. I bought these used off Craigs for a ridiculously low price, but I'd recommend them in the $75-$100 range which is easy to find.  I listen more. I'm listening now. Isn't that what it's all about?

This is how I ran the test, played it normal without enabling the equalizer on using my Galaxy Nexus.  By default, clarity is both there for S4 and 310LP.  The 310LP does sounds louder on the same volume settings.  Bass reproduction came up more noticeable on the 310LP.  Enabling the equalizer, ran the Bass Boost at 40% and 3D effect on MAX balance and it evens out the Bass on both headphones.  This just shows that the Klipsch by default, doesn't throws a low Bass effect.  However, it can still play deep boom sound when you play with the equalizer.    The sound on 310LP feels more a little 3D too, which may be good or bad depending on what type of music you are playing.    Bottom-line the difference in sound quality is negligible as there is a small difference, 5 out of 5 for both headset.  Remember we are talking about Headsets which is less than $100, so maybe it would be better to not say, \\"My $400 headset has diamonds with gold wires are way better\\", now that is a 10 which I would give double the 5.   The deciding factor maybe the price, 310LP for me which cost $49.99 at the time of this review.  The S4 costs me more than that when I got this back when it first came out, you might get a good deal on it now.    Warranty.  1 year for Klipsch, 30 days for Sony.

product_title: Acoustic Research Xsight Universal Remote Control
review_headline: Good remote, concerned with the website
review_body: I decided to finally have my own home theater system. The downside of course is that I ended up with 3 remotes. I was searching for an universal remote. And when I found this remote on woot for $40 with shipping, and decent reviews I decided to buy it.  My first impressions were generally positive. The outer packaging is very good. The remote itself, though not a work of art, looks very neat. Although once you add the 3 AA batteries, it is a little heavy, but not a deal breaker for me. The devices I wanted to control were the TV, Cable box and a Pioneer AV receiver. My DVD/BD player would be the Sony PS3. And I do not want to shell down another $50 to get a IR to bluetooth converter. So I don't mind an extra Sony remote.  One thing I did after opening the box, was to go through the manual, and work along with the manual. It is a well written manual and not a 6-8 font printed sheet with complicated instructions. There are about 48 pages and I covered adding devices and couple of activities in about an hour. Adding the devices were easy and so were setting up activities such as \\"Hello\\" and \\"Good Bye\\". They all worked. You can teach a function to the remote and add soft keys. I tried it and it did work.  Most of the modifications are done on their website. The software that comes along with it simply opens up the website, where you add the functions and then the software downloads them to the remote. And the UI on the website is simple. I have no prior experience with universal remotes. I just knew what I wanted the remote to do for me and this remote accomplished them. I don't know whether other remotes, cheaper or expensive, perform these actions better.  The only concern I had was their website. First from an IT point of view, a web application must be platform independent. I don't see the software doing a lot that would prevent AR techs to create something that works on all OS. But, they have decided to go along with Windows+IE only platform. I personally use a Mac, but I have my work laptop and I also have Windows running on the VM on Mac. Again, it was not totally frustrating. It is just a point of view. Second, when the website works, it works great. Simple yet adequate. But, while setting up the remote, the website wouldn't let me login after the initial setup. I thought I somehow forgot the password, though I did successfully login once, but when I clicked on forgot password link, it said my email address was not valid. I tried to create another account with another email ID and whichever email ID I used, it said that the email address was already registered. I gave up and tried after half an hour and it started working. Since most of the things can only be done on the website, I think it would be easier for them to a) Maintain the website properly or b) Give everyone a offline application and push updates every now and then.  To summarize, for a beginner, who is willing to go through a very well written manual, this is a decent remote. Its worth $40. But the website did frustrate me once and I hope it doesn't continue.

product_title: Audio Technica ATH-ANC23 QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones
review_body: I've tried quite a few different models of active noise-cancelling headphones, and these are by far the most effective at blocking outside noise.  I had been using an old pair of Panasonic RP-HC70's to try to reduce the amount of ambient noise at work, and while the ANC was reasonably effective, the open-ear design still let in a good bit of sound.  I then tried over-the-ear Able Planet NC500SC's, which did a better job of blocking out voices and other noise, but they were just too bulky to wear comfortably all day.    After doing some research, I decided to try some in-ear models to see if they would be more effective or more comfortable. I picked up a pair of Koss QZ77's, which worked ok, but the proprietary eartips just didn't fit me quite right and the ANC was only mediocre. Finally, I settled on these Audio-Technicas. With the foam tips installed, I squished them down, slid them into my ears, and immediately heard the difference.  Within a few seconds of putting them on, the foam eartips expanded and started blocking nearly all of the outside noise (you can actually hear it getting quieter and quieter).  I then turned on the noise cancelling, and was amazed by just how well it worked. Unlike most noise-cancelling headphones, these have almost no audible hiss when the ANC is turned on.    My only complaint would be that the cords are a little stiff, which makes them prone to being somewhat loud when you move around.  I generally wear these at my desk, so it isn't a huge problem for me, but it might be if you were using them while walking, exercising, etc.  Supposedly cord microphonics are fairly common with the Comply S400 eartips, so maybe I'll try some other options once the included pair wear out.

product_title: Logitech Harmony One Advanced Universal Remote
review_headline: LCD is junk........it this a kids toy???
review_body:
Harmony One is built with low grade plastic, 3rd world manufacturing processes, no attention to detail, and apparently no presales endurance testing. The buttons resist when pushed because they were manufactured poorly and rub on the plastic face of the remote. The software works but is slow to respond and the UI/LCD display is extremely cheap. The LCD is like something you would find on a toy for kids. I expected an iphone type of touchscreen but it isn't anywhere close. The pixels will puke out if you set it down to hard or it falls from your hand onto the couch. Obviously a remote control is going to be dropped and thrown around but this thing had never been build/stress tested or that would have been addressed. I can honestly compare the quality of the display/UI to toys my kids have that cost 30 dollars or below. So why is it when paying 250-300 dollars for a remote they can't make it more durable and create a more smartphone like software and display? Exactly.......run, don't walk away from this lemon.

I wouldn't recommend this remote to anyone unless the price came down under 40 dollars per unit. That is more than likely more than it cost to produce it. I would recommend an iPhone or smartphone remote option. Better interfaces, quality, and can be upgraded/updated if there are software bugs. This thing is weak.

product_title: Grundig G4000A AM/FM Shortwave Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: G4000A radio has great sensitivity, selectivity
review_body: This radio performs well, and has as many controls as my ham receiver did. The tuning is rock solid, and scanning channels by holding down the up or down arrow key lets you find stations pretty quickly, although if you think you will scan the radio's entire short-wave coverage in one sitting, expect a long time \\"spinning the dial.\\" The double-conversion system provides the level of performance (selectivity and absence of images) you would expect from a first-class, professional receiver.    What others have complained about pertaining to the whip antenna may be accurate. As long as you treat it gently, it seems as though it will survive. However, I notice where there may be an intermittent change in signal strength as I move the antenna slightly. Can't verify if it is a real problem or just using it in a noisy environment.     Speaking of noisy (radio) environments, this receiver's sensitivity allows it to pick up any signals you don't want. No amount of filtering will kill on-channel interference. You have to go to the source (I was a radio engineer and still have a commercial FCC license). If you live with computers and wired networks, expect a lot of noise scattered around random points on the dial. Routers and their CAT-5 cables and computers and their peripheral devices with wiring all serve as great broadband noise emitters. Although all this digital equipment operates within FCC Part 15 rules, when you're within 100 ft of this equipment, expect interference, especially on the shortwave bands. It's amazing to think of how we've created such a noisy RF environment with all this \\"necessary\\" equipment that we can't live without.    I think there are two solutions to this problem--neither necessarily practical, but perhaps edifying:  1. Turn off ALL digital equipment in your home, and if you have close-by neighbors (e.g., apartments, townhouses), get them to shut down all digital equipment.    2. Take the radio on battery power to a secluded spot in the woods faraway from everything and enjoy a \\"quiet, noise-free\\" listening experience, only interrupted by the sounds of birds, the rustling of trees in the breeze or the sound of water flowing over stones and rocks in a creek.     By the way, leave all your portable, digital toys (cell phone, smart phone, etc.) at home, too. Maybe a time away from everything digital isn't so bad, after all.     And if all this quietness is too noisy for you, you can always tune into the FM band (whereby frequency modulation provides a quiet, noise-free signal, and the radio performs well) and listen to the whatever the stations churn out--which, if you're in the Philadelphia area, is for the most part pretty noisy.

product_title: Library Style CD Storage Cabinet
review_headline: A lot of storage in a little space!
review_body: [[ASIN:B00006453T Appothecary Style CD Storage Cabinet, Walnut]]  We have too much media and not enough organization.  This unit addresses our needs.  The 325 capacity unit is comprised of the 4 and 5 drawer unit plus the two shelf unit.  They stack and are shipped in two separate boxes. They are secured (and I use that word loosely) with two small metal clips that you screw to the back to attach the two.  Once attached, a lift and tilt could upset your setup.   Some sites list this as being made of oak. It is not. It is solid wood (probably birch), and is made in China. The finish is very attractive with a rustic look.  The finish is not entirely even, so this piece isn't \\"too perfect.\\"  It fits our casual lifestyle well.  The legs give the unit a less bulky feel and are a nice touch. The drawers slide in and out easily, and are interchangeable.  The walnut finish is lighter and has more red in it than I would have imagined based on my knowledge of a walnut stain as well as the photos and images found on the web.   It is easy to assemble with a screwdriver and a fair amount of muscle. You might want to get some tap in feet protectors, as the bare wood legs are in direct contact with the floor.  The item is well packed, and it needs to be, given the long haul from China to CA and then to IA via UPS ground.  The packaging is sturdy with a double thickness cardboard and strategically placed fitted Styrofoam. If not for both of those features, this item would not have made the transit safely, as the box was crushed, dented and torn in multiple places.    This is a good free-standing storage solution for CDs, DVDs and even VHS tapes.  It blends well with most furnishings and its relatively small footprint makes this a good solution for our media storage. Well, I am happy to report that these extenders were the perfect solution to our needs. The picture is extremely clear, and the sound quality is perfect. Best of all, they are powered by the HDMI ports so there is no external power adapter required!!!    The HDMI cable that is attached is extremely heavy duty! product_title: ARCTIC Sound Headphones P311
review_body:
After having owned a Motorola S9 since April 2009, I'm mixed.
The sound is great-- I'm not an audiophile, but I know good sound when I hear it.

Numerous people at stores, clerks who are BT users have commented, and said they really liked the sound too when I let them try them.

What I like about the P311, compared to the S9:

The S9's \\"earbuds\\" form hurt my ears if I wore it for more than 3 hours.
The \\"headset stereo muff\\" form is WAAAAAY better. My ears do not hurt, it's rather comfy.

The S9 did the phone only out of the left ear piece. This was fine because hearing the call in stereo always kind of made me feel a little buggy.

The P311 has stereo quality phone, and music. I.e., both ears. It's still weird, but I am getting use to it.

The S9 was dropped regularly by my old Samsung I760, and while I used for for only 2 months on my HTC Trophy, it just never worked all that well. Sadly, the battery died- died before I could figure out what it was.

So far, the P311 has not been dropped by my phone, and works well.

There's no huge battery pocket in back, so while they still bulge in back, it's not AS bad, when you've sat down, and are leaning back against your chair.

All the controls are on the right side, so that makes it nicer-- I used to forget with the S9, and would change the volume instead of skipping song tracks. Or I'd activate the phone instead of pausing the music to talk with someone standing in front of me.

Volume controls are on top, and track changing is on the bottom. A large central button makes answering calls, pausing/activating music really easy.

Not once has the P311 just dropped out in a call, or a music track. I like that. S9 was notorious for dropping music. Which really stunk, because I liked their style.

What I don't like....
It's bulky. If you're into fashion, and feel weird about bulky stuff off yourhead then you might wind up being self-conscious. It's one thing to wear nice big comfy headphones at home, and another to do so while you're out and about town. People are constantly looking at me, and asking-- what are those. And while I don't mind answering questions, they're a real conversation piece/starter when in the market.

Don't try to use them for working out in the gym, because they will fall off your head-- regularly. It appears the comfy ear piece (reminds me of my really old leather covered Sony's) is really thick, so the part that would rest on the top of your ear does not actually get over the ear-- unless you've got ears that stick out real far, normally.

The ear pieces do not extend like wired headphones, so if you have a larger head, they may not fit.

I've yet to figure out how to activate voice command for them. It seems like they're more for answering calls, than for making a call.

Beyond that, generally speaking, they're a nice head set. For the price, they're good for now.

product_title: Sony ICF-C7IP Clock Radio for iPod and iPhone with Hidden Sliding Dock Tray
review_headline: Five Reasons To Buy A Different Clock
review_body:
1. The light. The face of the clock is a giant blue beacon like an alien spaceship landing in the bedroom. Even the dimmest setting could be used as a flashlight. No joke. The whole darn bedroom is bathed in bright blue. Hideous.

2. No music. Because the light is so so so bright, we can't use the iPod feature to wake up. We have to close the thing in a drawer to keep the light from keeping us awake. And we don't to bust an iPod over this clock if it gets jostled in a drawer. So...no soothing music from the iPod in the morning...just...

3. The awful tone of the alarm. It's a terrible noise. Yes--I know the \\"beep beep beep\\" is supposed to be annoying enough to wake you. But this sounds like the horn of a demonic clown right in your ear. Plus, you get about three slow beeps before it begins to go bonkers, beeping so fast it makes you think \\"holy hell it's Armageddon.\\"

4. Snooze dangers. If the alarm is going off and you press the snooze button, it gives you the option of resetting how long you want to snooze for. Not really a problem--unless you're like me, and in the groggy early hours you're not fully coherent, and you press the snooze multiple times by accident, changing the snooze setting, and next thing you know you're late.

5. The interface is not intuitive. I don't know--maybe I'm getting old. But it took me a good half hour just to figure out how to set the alarms. If you're the kind of person who fusses with lots of electronics, you might not have a problem. But if you're like me and want something simple and streamlined, look elsewhere.

Good luck with your clock shopping! Hope this helps.

product_title: SONOS P3 Color
review_headline: This is the beginning of something great!
review_body:
I had been in the market a while looking for a quality and integrated wireless whole home audio solution. The prospect of running wires throughout my house into each room was daunting (and so 'old school'). The wireless solutions I had seen up till now either didn't have the quality sound or ease of use I was looking for. Finally, I needed a product that would pass the 'wife acceptance factor'. My family had to be able to use it easily.

I am very happy to say the Sonos Play:3 system delivers on all of my requirements!

I purchased two Play:3 Zone Players and the Wireless Bridge. I went with 2 units because I wanted to pair them together in the same room and use them in 'stereo mode', delivering discrete Left and Right audio to each speaker. All I needed to do was plug in the power cord on each speaker and I was in business.

Installation and setup could not have been easier. Plug in the bridge, connect the included Cat5 wire to your router and run the install CD. Connecting the speakers was as simple as following the step by step on screen tutorial. Next up is creating your music library and linking to your preferred music services. In my case, I pointed the Sonos to look for my large music collection housed on my Windows Home Server. It quickly found and indexed my music library, including the playlists. While it was doing that, I also connected it to my Napster account. It was within this app that I created a stereo pair with my two Play:3 speakers. Again, logical and easy to follow.

Once the system was up and running, I put the speakers to the sound test. As mentioned above, quality of sound was extremely important to me, and these speakers delivered. It is absolutely incredible the amount of power (yet clean and crisp) these speakers can put out.

The very best part of the Sonos experience is in the ease of use. I downloaded both the iPhone/iTouch and the iPad app. Although excellent, the iPhone app pales in comparison to the simple, full screen experience that the iPad can give. Whether it is my Windows Home Server library or the Napster subscription service (or Pandora , Rhapsody, Sirius, Spotify, Mog, Internet Radio or others) I am pulling from, the application blends each experience into a single interface. Further, creating playlists on the fly was extremely simple.

In summary, I couldn't be more pleased by the overall Sonos solution. It has surpassed every expectation and I am sure to be expanding my Sonos network to other speakers inside and outside my home in the near future. I recommend if you are on the fence on purchasing a wireless whole home audio solution, you give the Sonos serious consideration. There are less expensive solutions out there, but nothing that blends quality sound and workmanship into a simple to use everyday interface the family can use and enjoy.

product_title: Archos Vision 18b 8 GB Video MP3 Player with 1.8-Inch Screen and FM Radio (Black)
review_body:
Let's get right to the point: This is a squeaky, clunky player. It does the job, but the buttons feel cheap and don't always register presses, the UI is clunky and doesn't work intuitively, and the screen quality is sub-par, displaying video so poor and low-resolution that you might as well skip using this as a video player.

However, it is also compact, thin, lightweight, and has 8GB of built-in storage. Pictures look okay on it, and music sounds fine. It's not an audiophile's device, but it works for listening to some tunes on the go.

The FM radio works as you'd expect, as long as you have headphones attached. I don't listen to the radio, so that's not really important to me anyway. It's nice to have the option, though.

The included ear buds are terrible quality. Don't even bother. Run out and get something else, because they don't do the audio any favors, and they're uncomfortable as well.

I'm using this as a stand-in for my lost Sansa Clip+ and while it does the trick, it pales in comparison. Other things I would have liked would be some sort of slipcase, and perhaps an SD card slot so I can expand the memory. In fact, if it had an SD card slot, I'd give it an extra star in the rating. Unfortunately, it's stuck with the not-quite 8GB that is built in.

Every time I turn it on after charging via USB it goes through a file update (not a firmware update, but an update of the music files, even if I didn't change anything). This file update can take a couple minutes, and it seriously detracts from the player's usefulness as a spur-of-the-moment, on-the-go sort of device. It stinks to be ready for music and instead you're faced with a screen that just says \\"updating...\\" for a while.

Another thing I really don't like is that, despite the color screen, it doesn't display album art. What's the point to this screen, anyway? It can't display video very well. It's too small for decent photos. Why bother with a color screen at all if you're not going to display album art from file tags?

This is passable as a cheap MP3 player. It's certainly WAY better than the Coby pieces of junk that litter the tech world, and it's better than the GE players I've used, but for around the same price you can get a decent Sandisk Sansa. Even if it has lower built-in storage, at least a Sansa will allow you to use a micro SD card to have more space. This thing is great for kids, people who lose their technology, and those who are desperate and find it at a bargain price.
