review_headline: One of the best of the lower priced ear buds
review_body: What I like about these is that they are sturdier than most of the competition.  They also have clearer highs and a very good bass.  They are excellent for music (I love opera and classical, but also listen to country and rock) but even more outstanding for audio books.    These are great to travel with.  Also, the wire is sturdier than other ear buds except for the true audiophile ones that cost tons.

product_title: Coby CA81BLK Dual USB Power Adapter/Charger for MP3 Players (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: this charging system works great for me. I ride my motorcycle a lot and don't take my computer with me and this lets me charge up my mp3 anywhere with a wall plug

product_title: Cheetah APTMM2B TV Wall Mount for 20-75" TVs up to VESA 600 and 165lbs, and fits 16” And 24” Wall Studs, and includes a Tilt TV Bracket, a 10' Twisted Veins HDMI Cable and a 6" 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_headline: Why pay for a more expensive mount that does the same thing?
review_body: What's in the box:  Wall mount  All screws needed to mount on wall  Extra screws to be used for just about any tv to attach mount to  An extra leveler (works better than the one on mount)  HDMI cable (designed for 1080p and 3d movies)    Sure it's a \\"cheap\\" wall mount, but \\"cheap\\" only applies to the price, every other aspect of the product is quality.  Well there is only one part that's pretty cheap, the leveler on the actual product (not the second included one) is slightly off (verified with my craftsmen leveler).  But hey for $30 or less, does it really matter that the leveler is crap and the rest of the product isn't?  Especially since you're purchasing a wall mount WITH a leveler and not a leveler WITH a wall mount.  Moving on, the quality of the steel seems sound and well made.  I've had this product on my wall for about a year now, and my parents have had the same one for 4 years.  So far no fallen tvs or \\"bouncy/rattling\\" ones (if you live by rail roads or a high truck traffic area or even by an airport, you know what I mean when the vibrations begin to move through the house).  I'm hanging a 40' CCFL LCD tv that weighs about 50lbs.  They provide you with more than adequate screws to hold everything up and plenty of extra parts in case you don't have what you need.  I highly recommend this wall mount, just make sure you have a leveler on hand that's of quality to double check the one that comes automatically on board.

product_title: Eton American Red Cross FR160 Self-Powered AM/FM/NOAA Weather Radio with Flashlight, Solar Power, and Cell Phone Charger
review_body: This is a terrific radio especially in light of the numerous power outages. It's only about the size of a pound of butter, easy to carry around and has an easy-to-use crank if you don't have enough sun to power the solar cells. LOVE IT!!!

product_title: Bump Wireless Mobile Speaker
review_body: Very happy with the bump wireless speaker. I listen to several internet shows to go to sleep and this is perfect since my computer is in another room. It has good clear sound, at all volume levels, especially down at low volume if you have to worry about disturbing people during the night. The volume controls are very easy to use. Its compact and light weight, yet still sturdy, for the bed stand. It was simple to set up out of the box. No software to load, it just started working right away, which was a relief. Also, being so light and portable, I can cart it around the house with me while doing chores during the day. Had it a month and so far so good. A great little product.

product_title: Philips Fidelio DS3000 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Premium Charging Speaker Dock
review_headline: love it but just one tiny thing...
review_body: love the size, design and sound and the fun app that comes along when you plug in the phone...the only complaint I have is that there is no remote, that is very nitpicky but other than that I love this product!

product_title: XGear White XGR360 Shield Polycarbonate Swivel Shell For Apple iPad 2
review_body: Bought this from XBox for $56.  Product came with white cover already peeling back from plastic base.  In less than a month the plastic tabs that keep it in the closed position were broken.  Received only gentle use.  Cheap product.  Arrived looking cheap.  Went out looking cheaper.

product_title: Jensen 3-Speed Stereo Turntable with AM/FM Stereo Radio (Silver)
review_body: I have a number of lp records and little cash.  This player lets me listen to my records.  For the  money it was a good investment

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body: I bought this for my 7 year old daughter for her  birthday, and she LOVES it!  Now her older sister is saving up so she can get the newer version.

product_title: Viewsonics VSIS-EU Cable TV Ground Loop Isolator
review_body:
We moved into a new house and once we got our TV hooked up I noticed this annoying buzzing. I tried turning the TV volume down and cable box volume up, I tried messing with the sound mix to make it go away and I was on the verge of calling the cable company or Geek Squad to come out and take a look. It was making me nuts!

I came across this product while searching about the buzzing issue and gave it a shot as a last ditch effort. It worked!! It was super easy to hook-up and the buzzing has been gone ever since. AWESOME!

product_title: Philips SHS3200WT/37 Flexible Earhook Headphones White
review_body: The iPod standard earphone do not fit in my ears even if I'm just walking. I bought the earhook specifically for jogging. It is quite comfortable, lightweight, and with enough sound quality. By the way its price is so cheap that later I purchased a white spare. I shall comment that if you want to use a cap and sunglasses, the top of your ear can be a little pressured by the 3 items sharing the space.

product_title: Pioneer SP-BS21-LR 80-Watts RMS 2-Way Speakers (Pair)
review_body: Just a note that the Amazon page for the SP-BS21-LR lists the wrong, physical dimensions for the speaker cabinets. According to Pioneer's website, each speaker is 7-1/8\\" x 12-5/8\\" x 8-1/16\\" (W x H x D).

product_title: Mediabridge ULTRA Series RCA Y-Adapter (12 Inches) - 1-Female to 2-Male for Digital Audio or Subwoofer - (Part# CYA-2M1F-P )
review_body: I gave this four stars only because I would like to see a version where they make the two male connections on one end and a single male on the other that is about 5 feet so you don't have to buy another cable in order to connect it to the stereo. Other than that this is an excellent product.

product_title: Sony ICF-S79V Weather Band Shower Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Radio Doesn't Hold Up To Long Term Use
review_body: The radio seems good at first but they don't hold up to long-term use in the shower. I've had two of these which have died after several months of use, and am trying a different brand instead.

product_title: Creative EP-630 In Ear Noise Isolating Headphones
review_body: I love these headphones, but some sellers are selling counterfeits.  It's really easy to tell if you're buying them new; the counterfeits come in a little pouch and the sound is terrible.  Google \\"counterfeit creative 630\\" for an article with pictures of counterfeit packaging vs. normal hard-plastic packaging.  My first pair lasted about a year and then one side stopped working.  I use them a lot, and for this price a years worth of use seems reasonable to me.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I had this one and Audio Technica M50 at the same time. First time, I heard both of these. It was 50% that I would return Bose. After two weeks, Bose went back to the store. The sound of M50 is much tighter, cleaner. Both mid range vocal and trebles were smoother. I enjoyed all kind of music with M50. Bose have more base but not deep and precise like M50. I give 2 stars for this because of comfort when wearing it. Bose is lighter and fit better on me. But the sound quality still won. I decided to return QC15 NOT because of the price. I would do the same even for same price as M50...I know many people still like QC15 but try M50 also before make your decision.

product_title: C&E 1.5-Feet 3.5mm Stereo Male to Female Extension Cable
review_body: Great price and the cable is sturdy and is not flimsy. There is not a noticeable difference in sound quality.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APTMSB Flat Screen TV Wall Mount Bracket Designed for 32"-55" Plasma LED LCD TV (Actually Fits 20-55" TVs) Includes Free 10' Braided High Speed HDMI Cable With Ethernet
review_body: This is a solid, well constructed mount which should serve well if installed according to the instructions.  Great value if you care about your TV.  The only issue I had was that both the installed spirit level and the included torpedo level were broken on arrival.  Not a problem since I have levels, but it could be for the casual installer without a good supply of levels.

product_title: Beats By Dr. Dre Tour High-resolution In-ear Headphones
review_body: Outstanding costumer service. They were brand new, unopened box and everything. Here's the thing though...the 10 dollar earbuds from walmart sound WAY better than the beats. I don't know why this headphones are SO expensive when the quality is not really great. Great service though. Please don't waste your money on these though.

product_title: HDE RJ45 Ethernet Splitter
review_body: As is the case many times, you get what you pay for.  I opened the product when it arrived and it immediately came apart...  I was able to snap it back together after rearranging the pieces but I have little confidence in the splitter being able to provide a reliable signal for my broadband...

product_title: OREI 3 in 1 Schuko Travel Adapter Plug with USB and Surge Protection
review_body: We just came back from a Russian vacation.  I bought this adapter to take with me for my hair dryer.  When we got there I attached it to my dryer, turned the dryer on and it worked great...never had a problem.

product_title: Dynex DX-AC1200 Universal AC Adapter
review_body: Its too bad that vendors sell these electronic devices but do not provide enough technical specifications.  On this power adapter, the smallest plug was 2 mm.  My 7.5 Vdc requirement was for a baby monitor that needed a 1.5-1.7mm plug instead. As this is being rated as 'universal' I incorrectly assumed all plug sizes would be available. Sure there are other smaller amperage adapters available from Dynex (with the 1.5-1.7mm plugs), however the 500 ma version had negative reviews due to unstable voltages and etc.  Its an excellent product for the price, just be mindful of the plug size you may need before ordering.

product_title: HIGH QUALITY AC POWER TRAVEL ADAPTER PLUG FOR AUSTRALIA CHINA NEW ZEALAND ARGENTINA FIJI ISLANDS / WITH DUAL PLUG-IN PORTS AND SURGE PROTECTION / GROUNDED
review_headline: the double charge is worth it!
review_body: Very small to fit anywhere in your luggage.. I loved the double charge option... this was great.. reliable.. worked everytime.. now if I could just get it back from my friend who moved to NZ after taking a month long vacation there...wheres my plug!?!?!?

product_title: Koss Porta Pro On Ear Headphones with Case
review_body: The earphones are fine, but they create too much pressure physically on the skull (ears).  They don't just sit, they squeeze onto your ears.  Definitely a minus for me.  Maybe I'll get used to them, but so far I feel it was a bad call.

product_title: GPX Digital Audio Player with 2 GB Installed Flash Memory - Silver
review_body: Bought this for a friend and loaded his favorite songs on it. He liked it at first, but hardly plays it now.

product_title: Cables Unlimited Cables Unlimited HDMI Male to Male Cable
review_body: There is not much to say about a HDMI cable.  There is not any real difference between cables except price.  This cable is a good quality molded design at a very low price. I have used it for a few weeks and it performs just as you would expect, perfectly.

product_title: C&E Power Extension Cord 18AWG, Black, NEMA 5-15P to NEMA 5-15R, 10 Amp, 1 Foot, CNE458644
review_body: The item I received was not what I ordered. Beware, my order was fulfilled by Miriam Holdings LLC. The item I received was a 5-pack of 1 foot monitor/PC power cords. Buyer beware!

product_title: Mediabridge ULTRA Series HDMI Cable (3 Foot) - High-Speed Supports Ethernet, 3D and Audio Return [Newest Standard]
review_body: I was recommended this product and very glad. This HDMI cable is a great deal for a great product. Do not think paying more will get you a better product.

product_title: AudioQuest RCA Male-to-Male Preamp Jumpers-2 pack
review_body: This item is a small but worthwhile improvement. It replaced factory supplied jumpers of lower quality  and after making the change and some burn in time,I feel the system improved,especially in upper mids  and high frequencies.Satisfied with the change,however I really wanted the \\"older\\" version which appeared  to have better rca plugs and domestic wire.

product_title: High Speed Hdmi Cable Black Nylon Brading with 24k Gold Plated Tips (50ft)
review_body: This cables has a pretty strong build, set to last forever. I strongly recommend if you need a strong and long lasting hdmi cable.

product_title: Sennheiser On-Ear 926MHz Wireless RF Headphones with Charging Cradle
review_body: I bought this item for my husband who is very hard of hearing.  He used it the first day while we watched TV.  It was wonderful to sit there and not have the volume of the TV up so high that it hurt my ears.  He said the quality is great.  The sound is crisp and clear.

product_title: Zeikos Rechargeable AA 2900mAh Batteries
review_body: Batteries are not as advertised. They have to be slow charged, do not last long, and are very light. I doubt they are 2900mah.

product_title: Coby Isolation Stereo Earphones with Volume Control
review_body: These were good, quality gems.  I espcecially like the volume control that I had at my fingertips.  They worked very well.

product_title: C Crane Co CC2B Radio-2 AM FM/Weather and 2-Meter Ham Band (Black Mica)
review_body: Replaced a Sony $29.95 radio and it didn't get as many stations as it did.  I am very disappointed after spending $149.95 on an average radio

product_title: Tripp Lite Isobar 8 Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip 25ft Cord Right Angle Plug Diagnostic LEDs (ISOBAR825ULTRA)
review_body: I use the Tripp lite industrial line at home and at work, this one will protect my Samsung fridge. Tripp Lite always makes good quality products. It fits the plug well, not much more can be said, I'm not an electrical engineer, so I don't know how to actually test it.

product_title: Tenergy 9V 250mAh NiMH high capacity rechargeable Battery
review_body: This product was selected for use in multiple portable wireless microphones.  Eight 9V batteries were originally purchased.  Two batteries warped and became dangerous to use.  The remaining 6 batteries all had malfunctioning tops that popped out of the wrapping and became unusable.  The company sent me 4 replacement batteries and I just another one pop out of the wrapping.  These batteries are cheap for a reason - they aren't as durable as some other brands.  If you intend for them to be used frequently, then I recommend spending the money to get a better battery.

product_title: Energy ESW-C8 8-Inch Subwoofer (Black)
review_headline: Wow! Great output in small package
review_body: Bass delivered by this sub unit is more than satisfying for it's size. I placed the sub in a room with a very high ceiling and was a bit apprehensive in doing so. I was pleasantly surprised; deep, clean room filling lows. This is a perfect sub if you do not want to overwhelm a room with bone jarring sound. It takes up very little space, sounds superb and the finish is incredible! Not much has been said on the topic of finish; no need to elaborate, this unit is beautiful. This item still sells for $300 or more from some retailers and is worth every penny. Getting one for $150 makes it the best deal in audio/video I've seen in years...

product_title: Crosley Mini Turntable with Full-Range Stereo Speakers
review_body:
I was a little nervous as what is a \\"good\\" sound is always so relative but I am very pleased with this record player.

First, it looks cool.

Second, it plays all formats.

Third, it plays it loud enough and with a reasonable range that I can enjoy my records.

If you are looking for pristine sound then look elsewhere but if you like a glass of wine and the warm welcome of some old records that crackly here and there then you will enjoy this.

product_title: Cheetah APTMM2B TV Wall Mount for 20-75" TVs up to VESA 600 and 165lbs, and fits 16” And 24” Wall Studs, and includes a Tilt TV Bracket, a 10' Twisted Veins HDMI Cable and a 6" 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_body: This tv mount is cheap and solid.  Easy to install, low profile, and includes a level... what more could you ask for.  Includes all necessary mounting hardware to install on several different surfaces.  Mounted my 40\\" lcd and it actually makes my room look bigger now.  Don't be fooled by the cheap price, but if you feel like being a tool and going to Best Buy, then go and waste your money there.

product_title: PowerBridge TSPBIW-6 Total Solution Power and Cable Management (Each)
review_body: This was very easy to use, I'm a 62 year old granny and put it in myself.  The end result looks wonderful, no ugly wires hanging from the set.  You realy need this if you are going to hang your new big screen tv on your wall.

product_title: GTMax 3.5mm LED FM Transmitter with SD Slot for Microsoft Zune 4GB 8GB
review_body:
I take this to trash. Bad design, flexible arm for connection is poor, signal plug its the worst. When use the charge option with usb to mp3 causes interference.
I loose my money. I regret to technoligy in 21th century still use FM transmitters to listen mp3 in cars. But if you need quality to listen music you like in you car, you have to spend more of $45 bucks.

product_title: iTour-POP Ultra Portable Rechargeable Speaker for iPod, Sansa, Zune, iPhone 4, BlackBerry, HTC EVO, DROID, Samsung Wave, Galaxy S
review_body: great little speaker,i have incredible 2 phone and speaker is lacking,but this turns phone into room music.Only thing i would change is a longer cord,have to pick up phone and speaker at same time.Size is perfect for pocket or bag,love it so far.

product_title: Naxa NAM-984 Dual Handheld Wireless Microphone Starter Kit with Wireless FM Receiver
review_body: I do not recommend buying these mics because they are of very poor quality and malfunctions. do not throw your money because they buy and the two only one works very hard and bad sound. Find something more than money and buy something of better quality.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_body: I had given a pair of these headphones to my son and they were amazing for the price.  I have more expensive headphones but they don't have the sound quality that these have.  The sound is clear and natural with a present bass without sounding too boomy or overtaking the rest of the music.  I listen to many genres of music including rock, metal, jazz, alternative, folk, and classical, and these headphones work with all types of music.   What is also important is that they fit comfortably in my ears.  My son has had his for over a year and a half and he is not easy on his headphones, and they have held up well.   If you are looking for in-ear headphones and want great quality at a reasonable price, look no further.

product_title: Mediabridge ULTRA Series Subwoofer Cable (8 Feet) - Dual Shielded with Gold Plated RCA to RCA Connectors - Black
review_body: I am no audio expert but I do know that the overpriced audio cables from brick and mortar shops TEN times this price are not worth it.  I bought this cable for my home theater system and have been very happy with it.  The cable is very well made which was surprising considering the price of this cable.

product_title: Emerson Portable Radio CD Player
review_body: Just got it today and is just what I was expecting.  I like the compact size. Unlike others I saw that were bulky and round shaped, this fits nicely on the counter.  The sound is clear and so far so good.

product_title: Tenergy Propel CR123A Lithium Photo Battery with PTC Protected
review_body: If you use these suckers up quick like I do than this is an awesome deal. Usually for the price you only get 1-2 at the store so you feel good getting a pack of 12. they may not last as long in storage but at the rate I use them I don't notice and they seem to last just as long as any name brand battery cause I haven't seen any significant gain or lose in product time.

product_title: ViewHD Two Input HDMI to RGB Component YPbPr / VGA 2x1 Switch Converter Support 5.1CH Surround Sound
review_body:
Have an old HD Yamaha projector and had it hook up directly to BD and image and sound great. Now I aquire a Apple TV2 and had problems, with this adapter solved the problem of the Apple TV but now my BD does not send image just sound . Any suggestion anybody with similar problem.
Eric

product_title: FiiO E5 Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: It makes me want to buy another one to plug to this one
review_body: The sound that comes out of this little device is beyond amazing, I was a bit skeptic on buying an item I have never heard about but I am glad I got this! The quality of sound that comes out of it is great, you don't just hear Bass, you hear the Treble as well which is great because I'm a producer and I want to hear it all. It goes well with my Sennheiser HD 598.

product_title: Sennheiser Active Noise-Canceling Headphones
review_body: I've had these cans two days and I'm already pretty darn pleased. Contrary to some of the negative reviews, I HAVE experienced significant noise reduction. The headphones successfully tuned out my ceiling fans, my neighbors a/c unit, my outdoor fountains, and the little girls screaming in the backyard next door. Color me HAPPY! Noise reduction may not be as good as Bose, but it's just fine for my needs. Haven't tried them on a plane, but I'm not a frequent traveller by plane, so I'm not that concerned.     True, these headphones are LARGE, but in my case, that was actually a deciding factor. I have a large head and large ears (only one bike helmet manufacturer makes a helmet big enough for me if that gives you a clue) and these fit perfectly and comfortably. I added the FiiO E5 Headphone Amplifier (smart move!) and even before a good break-in period, I already love these cans.     Tight, solid bass, silky mid-range, and crisp highs. No complaints, just a lot of smiles!

product_title: Polk Audio RC80i 2-Way In-Ceiling Speakers (Pair, White)
review_body: We use these speakers in our outdoor patio cover.  They provide really good sound for what we're wanting this for.  They're not for the audiophile but if you want to add speakers somewhere that provide good sound and in a moist environment, these speakers are a great buy.

product_title: Koss UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones
review_body: I'm very hard on my electronics, and for years my headphones would only last a few weeks or months.  I started getting the UR40 because they looked comfy (they are) and was impressed by how long they survived my \\"headphones curse.\\"  I think I've gotten maybe four pairs over the past three years?  That's a huge record for me!  In other words, they're well-built, and I keep coming back to them whenever I need a new one.  The sound quality is great and so is the price.  They're not $100 sound-canceling masterpieces, but if you wanted those you'd have to pay $100, so I think these are a great bargain for the low price.

product_title: URC RFS200 PowerPak Bundle with MasterControl RF20 and PowerBlaster
review_body: The remote is a great option if like us your LCD TV and other sources generate a lot of LCD interference.  It was pretty easy to set up and works consistently well.  Please note that you can only have one per house.  I would also be cautious if you lived in an apartment building or row of town homes.  If you are in close quarters, the possibility of RF interference might be higher....

product_title: Amazon Kindle 3g skin silicone case cover, neoprene sleeve, accessory bundle, screen protector, MiniSuit LCD Cleaner
review_body: What I bought in accesories were all great except for the screen protector.  It left a greater glare on the screen than without it, and it left air bubbles under it.  The tabs on it stuck to it and left a paper glue area there and when I finally took the screen protector off, carefully, it left some air bubbles on my Kindle screen

product_title: Panasonic Lightweight Headphones with XBS Port
review_body: These actually have a really nice sound to them, out of 4 sets of headphones I got at the same time (2 Koss 1JBuds) they were pretty close to being the best....both in sound and comfort.  Unfortunately, the connection to my Sansa Clip+ isn't great.  It's the only set that has an L Shaped plug and I don't know if that has anything to do with it, but if I move around at all there is static or loss of volume or both.

product_title: Visual Land V-Clip Pro 4 GB MP3 Player with Speaker
review_body: If you want something cheap and will play music then get it but it really kind of stinks, i wasn't impressed much. The buttons are hard to work with, the clip broke off within the first couple hours I got it, and theres no shuffle, which I really dont like because I want to listen to ALL my music, not just each band one after another in alphabetical order. I dont like it that much. But its an okay music player if you just want something temporary.

product_title: FINIGO 3.5mm In-Ear Stereo Earphones w/ On-off & Mic For Apple iPhone 6 / 6 Plus / 5 / 5S /5C, HTC One (E8), One (M8), Samsung Galaxy S5 Android Smartphone
review_body: These are magnificent~!  Pricey but worth the difference~!  I own and run my own 'net music station for many years, and listen on a low-power transmitter around the neighborhood.  I make a practice of listening to me while in the hammock daytimes and upon retiring at night.  I am big on frequency response re the quality of music I play to the many hundreds of listeners.  As an audiophile I was happy until I heard my stereo signal with the radio's regular earplugs; then I heard on the Bose plugs...no comparison~!  Of course the plugs' stability is perfect; no movement or danger of them popping out, whether walking or relaxing.  You owe it to yourself to hear your radio thu a Bose set of plugs~!

product_title: Key Finders & Remote finder by Where's the Remote? Keyfinders. Remote Control, Wallet, Pet, Cell phone, Locator (Free Extra Batteries)
review_body: When I was asked  to rate this product the first time, the only complaint I had was that the battery cover kept coming off and I finally lost it altogether. Debby you are awesome. Thanks so much for sending me a replacement receiver AND a new and inproved receiver. I didn't even ask, it just arrived in the mail today. Blessings on your business. I am thinking about buying 2 more for birthday gifts.

product_title: Etymotic Research In-Ear Headset with 3-Button Remote Control for iPod, iPhone, iPad
review_body: I am no expert in sound, so understand that first when reading my review. Here was my situation. I had the basic ipod headset. I would blast music at work to cancel out people talking so I could concentrate. It got so bad people told me they could hear the songs, as I had to raise the volume so high. I did a bunch of research and these seemed to be able to drain out talking. And they do the job. I can't hear people talking when I have them in. I use the earpieces that are like soft earplugs and they fit comfortably. Takes some getting used to, but by the second day no problem. I recently took them on a plane too, drowned out all talking, but still was able to hear hum of engine, which to me was no big deal. I was able to listen to what I wanted to on the plan without having to blast volume. Worth the money for me and would definitely recommend.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player
review_body: This mp3 player is great for my music needs. Plenty of space and very easy to use. Shop arond, you might be able to find a better price.

product_title: Polk Audio PSW505 12-Inch Powered Subwoofer (Single, Black)
review_body: Money leaker, who posted in 2009 has hit the nail on the head about features.  I don't have this subwoofer, but can note that it has the features you need - LTE in, crossover control, auto power off/standby.  I have a 12\\" Klipsch powered subwoofer and it has the same items as noted here, but the Polk is at a much lower price.  I bought my Klipsch 12 years ago for around $400, so this is a steal.  12\\" is the perfect size as you will be able to shake your house if desired but even at lower levels provide a full sound with really pretty small speakers.    I am running the sub with Infinity SM-Video center, Infinity SM-85 front, and Infinity C205 rears with a Yamaha RX-V595a Dolby Digital 5.1 100W equal channel power receiver.  I previously used SM-125 (3 way, with 12\\" drivers) as mains and the SM-85 for rear, but it was overkill.  The sub goes lower than the SM-125s and really fills the gaps, even with the smaller 85's.  I set the crossover for about 125 Hz.    While this does not specifically address the Polk speaker, I hope that you can realize a 12\\" sub is worth the money and both Polk and Klipsch make good ones.  I was actually thinking of buying this, but don't think my wife would approve....  Polk speakers generally have a punchier bass than the Klipsch, which I prefer.  I don't think Polk was making subs when I bought mine or else it wasn't carried by the stereo shop I purchased the sub at.  If I didn't already have a sub, this would be in the Amazon cart right now.

product_title: PARENT ASIN for Etymotic Research ER6i
review_headline: Great Sound, Great Isolation, Didnt last more than a year
review_body: Great Sound, Great Isolation, Didnt last more than a year and a half.  To be fair I used them a lot in that time frame jogging with them and working out with them.      I remembered them kinda of bothering my ear holes occasionally.   I really liked that they give you very large selection of different tips to put on the ends of the ear phone so if you got little ears or big ears like me, you will prolly be able to find that fits you the best.     FYI  The warranty is only good for a year  for this product.

product_title: DL123A Duracell Ultra Lithium 8 Batteries-CR123A
review_headline: Good value - bad packaging and delivery
review_body: I had been looking for a good source to purchase CR 123A  batteries in larger quantities and came across this offering through Amazon.com.  The prospect of being able to buy 8 batteries at this price point was a compelling value, so I placed the order and with the benefit of Amazon Prime, I was supposed to have received the batteries in two days.  However, on the date of expected delivery I received notification from both Amazon (good communication, by the way) and UPS regarding an issue with the packaging (that it had been damaged) and that I should expect further shipment delays as they remedied the situation.  I ended up receiving the batteries several days later in what was most likely the original \\"damaged\\" padded envelope (ripped and taped), and inside I found a small ziplock bag with the eight CR 123A batteries.  A couple of issues with this... (1) not sure how I can be sure these are actually new batteries as they are not in factory/original packaging and (2) if they are going to be shipped in a padded envelope, I suggest that more care be taken in securing the flaps, etc.    While the value is hard to debate, I am left wondering whether I've actually received what I paid for.  Here's to hoping for a long, full battery life.

product_title: Altec Lansing iMT320 inMotion Compact iPod speaker dock
review_body:
I bought my wife an iPod for Christmas. She really enjoys listening to music while she's cooking, so a docking speaker system seemed like the next logical step; I bought this Altec Lansing set for Valentine's day. Considering it's size, this speaker system delivers on sound. Don't get me wrong, the speakers aren't perfect, but they provide strong, clear sound without noticeable distortion. If you try to max out the volume, it starts to sound a little tinny, but otherwise it's great.

As far as portability goes, I didn't even realize it could use batteries until I came back to write my review. That's something I'll have to look into. In the mean time, the speaker set does fold up nicely with it's vinyl cover, but then the clunky AC adapter still needs to be dealt with (if you're not using batteries). If portability is a selling point for this system, then I think it would have been nice if there was some kind of storage slot where you can keep the adapter while it's not in use.

Bottom line, this speaker system has good sound (it's not Bose quality, but you're also only paying $50, so why would you expect superb sound). It's fairly portable, just make sure you don't lose track of the adapter.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V867BL 7.2-Channel Home Theater Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: My Onkyo receiver was plagued with problems on the HDMI board, forcing me to turn the unit off and on several times, switch device inputs, and scream loudly at it before it would detect and process the input.  I wanted a network connected receiver, that did everything my Onkyo did when it worked.  The Yamaha RX-V867 does everything I wanted, plus more.    I also purchased the bluetooth docking device to work with my laptops and android devices, and I'm very pleased I did so.  Setting up and operating the device is a breeze, and the abundance of HDMI and other inputs promises to keep me happy for many years to come.  The second zone is wonderful for controlling my outdoor speakers on our patio, and I love the fact that I can control the volume on that channel independently from that of the indside speakers.  It supports 7.2 outputs in various configurations, and the preset surround templates are actually useful and pleasing to the ear.    The sound quality is excellent, and would do speakers far better than mine justice.  I do plan on upgrading to Polk or Klipsch as soon as I find the extra fun money.    I have nothing but good things to say about this device, and I'm so happy that I made the decision to purchase this make and model.  There were two things I was looking for in a new A/V receiver: excellent video and sound quality, and easy versatility.  The Yamaha RX-V867 nailed both, and it has hardly had a resting moment since I set it up.

product_title: TDK Wireless High Fidelity Headphones
review_body:
Nice physical design. Relatively light for home use. Note that it has no built-in battery charger. This is something that can be more problematic than it seems at first.

Pros:
- Decent, clear sound.
- Didn't notice much interference.

Cons:
- Need batteries on both ends. Would have been good if the transmitter had a charger so you didn't have to change batteries on the receiver and transmitter. So, you need a separate charger which can charge at least 4 or 8 AAA batteries. Presently, I'm using the 12 year old headphone I am replacing to charge the batteries.
- Need to have the transmitter and the receiver close by in order to sync them. If you turn off either, you need to get up close to sync them again.
- Because it is made for use with portable devices, it only uses two AAA batteries for the receiver and the same for the transmitter. This makes them less powerful than other headphones. Need to turn up volume significantly in order to hear it well.
- Further, changing batteries for the dongle requires the kind of handling that will probably limit its life substantially (the way MP3 headphones wires wear out quickly). So, I'm not too confident that it will last long.

In all, good headphones but the lack of a charger or cradle in which to charge it makes it troublesome to use regularly. If I can find good rechargeable batteries and a good charger, I can probably put up with this unit. But still, for 2012, this is way too much work.

As for the sound quality, I can't complain at all. They have about 50 percent noise cancellation, and the quality of my music is great. The only thing I would recommend is to be nice to them, and maybe put them in a case instead of your pocket, so you don't knot them up.   If you're looking for a pair of skullcandy earbuds, these blow the ink'd series out of the water.

He loves it as well.    That prompted me to buy this third one, and after a bit of fumbling around trying to get the \\"external\\" SDHC micro to open up, I am again a happy camper. I now have three of those, so that is 12 gigs of music or stories, or \\"old time radio shows\\".  Great fun.  Hope this one lasts as long as its predecessors did! product_title: Recoton CW1521 Audio 1/4-Inch to 1/8-Inch Stereo Adapter (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: As another reviewer pointed out, the picture in this listing is a monaural adapter, showing only one band around the plug, where stereo plugs have two. I took a chance that the written description was accurate -- that this was a stereo 1/4\\" to 1/8\\" adapter. I needed it right away, so I had it overnighted.    What I received was not only a monaural, not stereo, adapter, it wasn't even a 1/4\\" to 1/8\\" adapter. What I received was a mono-to-stereo 1/8\\" to 1/8\\" adapter.    With this kind of uncertainty you might want to opt for a different item with a clearer, more consistent listing.

product_title: Sony MDR-XB300 Extra Bass Headphones (Old Version)
review_headline: These are great for bass but if you want a more balanced headphone look elsewhere.
review_body: I have a pair of Sennheiser PXC-350 noise cancelling headphones that I absolutely love, but they're just way too big for portable use.  I used to just buy cheap skullcandy earbuds for when I was out in about but the sound quality was always horrible and they would usually crap out after a couple months.  I decided to upgrade and I moved over to the Dre Beats Tour earbuds.  To me they didn't sound all that much better than the skullcandys but they did last longer.  Once those died, I decided I was done with earbuds so i started looking for a pair of headphones.  I was looking for something with good bass emphasis for listening to dubstep, hip hop, and dance music.  I narrowed it down between this and the AKG K518LE.      I had a chance to try the AKG before buying and instantly fell in love with the sound but they were just too tight.  After about 30 minutes of listening I had to take them off because they were clamping on my ears so hard.  Because of this, i decided to go with the Sony and ordered them sight unseen.  Admittedly, they don't sound quite as good as the AKG, but that being said they are less than half the price and most importantly, they are super comfy.      Now for the sound.  The bass on these is awesome.  It's got a well defined, tight bass that maintains really well at high volumes.  However, the mids and highs are a bit muffled.  The bass is definitely dominant in these headphones and the other tones are somewhat in the background.  They are by no means a balanced pair of headphones but like I said, I wanted something for dubstep, hip hop, and dance music and for that they work great.

product_title: Sennheiser HD 238 Open Aire Stereo Headphones -
review_headline: Great value, good sound - but nurse that cable!
review_body:
I am giving these headphones five stars based on the current Amazon price of around $82. At that price, they are a steal.

First, my credentials. I own three sets of Sennheisers (PX-100, HD 238, HD 25-1 II). These are in the middle of that range - better than the $50 PX-100s, weaker than the $200 HD 25-1 II.

The strength of these phones lies in their sound quality, which is excellent for this price range. Sennheisers are generally \\"dark\\"-sounding phones, which means they tend to emphasise bass at the expense of the highs. This tends to get the feet tapping, but also means that Sennheisers do not always present the sound as the recording artist originally intended. These phones are less dark than the PX-100s, but not as neutral as the HD 25-1 IIs. Generally, I like the slight bass emphasis. The listener gets drawn into the music, especially rock and bass-heavy tracks. The headphones also have reasonable clarity - better than the cheaper Sennheisers, but a long way short of the HD 25-1 II cans.

The phones are open-backed, which means they do not block out noise. This is bad on public transport (you have to crank them up to dangerously loud levels) but good when walking or jogging, as you are more aware of traffic.

The headphones have two weaknesses. Firstly, they do not fold up well. This reduces their usefulness as portable phones, which is a shame as I think this is the market they should be targeting. The cheaper PX-100s are really awesome for that. Secondly, they have a weak cable (a problem with many of the cheaper Sennheisers). My girfriend snapped her cable near the plug while jogging, and had to get it fixed (she also snapped the cable on the PX-100s twice).

In short, these are great headphones for the price, but have a fragile cable and are not so good for commuting on public transport.

review_headline: Neat Device - Lots to be Revealed When You Talk to Customer Support
review_body: The squeezebox is a neat little product and Amazon offers it for the lowest price I could find.  It was very easy to install and was up and running w/ in a few minutes.  I had lots of problems importing Itunes into the server library and then had to contact customer service.  I had several bad experiences with their 1st level of support - I completely erased my entire Itunes library b/c of some confusion between the Logitech employee and myself.  They also recommend a 3rd party software to use for tagging (sometimes the server does not recognize Itunes extensions), and then will not support any questions in regards to that software.  That is a bad business practice in my opinion - you can't point the finger at 1 w/o helping with both.  I got referred to Tier II help and made it to 1 call - the consultant missed his phone time frame on both occasions so I just gave up.  The biggest negative that is not published is that their server will not recognize any Itunes tracks downloaded during or before 2008 - so forget about those being in your library.  Overall, I ended up with about 7,000 songs that I have access to, but it does not allow me so see my entire external drive.  I would recommend this product to a friend, but it would be with the warnings and expectations of frustrations that I describe above.  The concept of having the squeezebox server running on your PC and then being able to ad devices is appealing to me - I will probably add a couple of their alarm clock style units at some point.

product_title: Sennheiser Sport Earbud Line Stereo Neckband Headphone
review_headline: Seemed great at first, then fell to pieces
review_body: Before getting these headphones, I had tried a pair of Sonys that sounded terrible and wouldn't stay put in my ears while I was running, so I was very pleased at first when these Sennheisers a) sounded very good and b) stayed comfortably in my ears for the whole run. I perspire heavily, so I was prepared to forgive them when occasionally one side or the other would clog with water and stop playing. All I had to do was slip that side out of my ear, lift the driest corner of my t-shirt I could find and give the earpiece a wipe, all while running. The sound would start up from that earpiece again so I would just pop it back in my ear and continue on my way. Yesterday however, the clogged earpiece just fell apart during the aforementioned process, and from the most gentle wipe. What happened was that the green silicone cap around the earpiece fell off. It seems that the silicone was what was holding the little speaker into the plastic frame of the headphones and so, when it fell off, the speaker fell out, although still attached by about an inch of wire. Looking at it, it seems as though the metal screen over the little speaker was corroded where it had been covered by the green silicone and the corrosion caused the glue holding the silicone on to fail. Of course, I had lost the silicone piece so I couldn't glue it all back together. I may be able to repair it some other way but having paid sixty bucks for these, I expected them to last more than 5 months. Before the Sonys first mentioned above, I had two pairs of Sony behind-the-heads in a row that cost twenty bucks each and each lasted more than two years.

product_title: Sony MHCEC709iP Mini Hi-Fi Shelf System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This system has several regretable design features.  First, the antenna has a unique plug that prevents the supplied antenna from being easily replaced by a better antenna.  The supplied antenna is probably OK for urban areas but is likely not sufficient for more remote locations.  Second, the speakers use very fine wires and a phone type connector.  This makes it very difficult to connect other speakers to the system.  Given the very fine wire used in the speaker connection, I find it very doubtful that this system is able to deliver anything like the advertised 360 watts of music power.  The third problem is that Sony is now designing obsolescence into their bookshelf systems.    I have purchased two Sony bookshelf systems, this one most recently.  My older set lasted a couple of years before the receiver stopped working.      The last few times I attempted to change stations, the system kicked me out of radio mode whenever I attempted to change stations.  Now, this replacement set behaved the same way right out of the box.  Any attempt to set the radio station results in the system switching to another input mode.    Sony used to make quality electronics.  Then their CD readers and writers began having problems with the lazer burning out fairly quickly.  After a couple of such failures, I stopped considering Sony as an alternative for computer devices.    Now their bookshelf systems are showing systematic failures in the radio functions of their systems.  While I regret seeing the downfall of what used to be a quality company, I am forced to conclude that Sony is now designing its' electronics with built in obsolescence.  Unfortunately, this means that the lifetime of the system you purchase may well not even last out the warrantee period and most likely won't last very much longer than the warrantee.    Regretfully, I can only recommend that consumers avoid Sony products until Sony finally get the idea that selling junk isn't a very smart way to run a company.Not all consumers are so stupid that they'll just replace failing equipment with another similar device from the same manufacturer.  Or, to quote a cliche, you can fool some of the people some of the time, but you can't fool all of the people all of the time.

product_title: Visual Land V-Clip Pro 4 GB MP3 Player with Speaker
review_headline: It works... but with many shortcomings
review_body:
I own several MP3 players, so I had certain minimum expectations: I wanted to be able to stop and start from where I left of, and I wanted to be able to control the volume up and down with a single button. This MP3 player does not do either of these simple functions. If someone figured out how to do either of these functions, I would greatly appreciate a response via comments with your tips.

Below is complete run down of my likes and dislikes for the player.

I liked:

1. The clip on the player is very nice, I like being able to clip it to anything (update: it broke off after 2 months of occasional use)

2. I like having a speaker in addition to the earphones. Granted it is not a great speaker, but sometimes you want to continue listening without the earphones and it is handy

3. Nice size

4. Controls are reasonably easy to use, even though the screen is very small and text is tiny and hard to see, but controls themselves are solid

5. You recharge the unit either by plugging into USB port of the computer, or to the included recharger with USB port. This little recharger might be the best part of the package. I already used it to recharge my phone.

I don't like:

1. When you stop listening, the device has no memory where you left off and you have to remember and navigate to the same place using the tiny screen. This is almost a deal breaker for me, as I want to listen to recorded lectures and finding the place where I left off is very difficult.

2. You can make volume control louder with a press of one button, but I did not found a way to lower the sound with one button. I found how to do it by navigating the controls though several levels of menus. When you are out and about it is difficult as the screen is small and I can't see the menus well, and if you are in the sun - forget it. I found that I can lower the volume by pulling the earphone a bit out of my ear. This is how I have been doing it - pretty crude.

3. As I mentioned the screen is small, the text is small and faint, it is hard to see in good light, not possible to use in the sun light.
Note: what you see in the stock photo is not real text, but a plastic screen cover with printed text. I only wish the text was so big and bright as that image.

4. The recharger does not indicate when the unit is fully charged. It has a red light which stays on red (apparently indicating that it is plugged in only), it never turns green as I expected to tell me the unit is fully charged. I left it plugged it for over 24 hours. (see attached photo)

5. It is very hard to see when the unit is charged or lower on charge. It has tiny bars somewhere on the display, but they are very hard to see because they are so small. My other units take regular AAA, so I can just carry a spare AAA battery and replace it when it is out juice, but not with this unit. You need to plan ahead when to recharge it, but planning is not easy when it is hard to see that the unit is low.

6. The manual is useless, it does not have much information. There is a version of the manual loaded on the MP3 it self or you can down load a \\"full\\" version from the web site. I read both, they are almost identical. The full version has more legal disclaimers. However, as example, neither tells you that the menu button is the \\"execute\\" key. It is the key which you need to push to complete the operation. You have to figure that out on your own.

I bought this unit as a lightening deal, so at that discounted price of $17 I am keeping it as a backup. But I would not buy it again and I cannot recommend it.

product_title: Tripp Lite Isobar 6 Outlet Under-Monitor Surge Protector, Dual USB Charging Ports, 8 ft. Cord, & $100K INSURANCE (MT-6PLUS)
review_headline: Good, but Tripp Lite needs to improve on design & construction
review_body: Having purchased this a few months ago, it has protected my TV (plugged into the unswitched outlet) & computer from a brief power outage & several flickers. In that sense I'm glad I purchased it. I don't use this as an under-the-monitor unit because I have a laptop. Rather I use it to protect my home entertainment system where it sits snugly with my DVD player & VCR. Being that I also don't want my electronic devices to draw \\"phantom power\\", I purchased this so that I can leave things I don't use much powered completely off without having to reach behind things or under the table. But as there are 2 LEDs that are always on even when the master power is off, I was concerned about the surge protector drawing phantom power. So I used a watt meter & found that it only draws 1/2 watt with no load, which is considerably less than each of the things I have plugged into it.    My concern is its design & quality of construction. The master power switch sticks when I depress it. The overall shape & feel of the switches are kinda strange. I don't understand why they can't be square or round. The switches should also be a different color from the casing to make them more visible, as well as the lettering on the front & back, which are difficult if not impossible to read. The documentation on the layout of the outlets & their purpose is really bad. The picture on the box cover contained the only useful information, so I took a picture of it for future reference. The power cord should also be detachable like Tripp Lite's UPS version so that I can use the cord length I want. The cord on this unit is much too long for my use. I want to open this unit to see what makes it tick & to see how I can replace the cord, but I can't since the screws are not removable without special tools. I guess if it ever breaks I can get a free replacement. Hopefully by then Tripp Lite will have a new and improved version. It's too bad there aren't too many choices out there. If more manufacturers madethese things & advertised them as a part of your home entertainment system instead of for big fat monitors that few people & businesses have these days, there would probably be better products.

product_title: Belkin 12 Outlet Surge Protector with 8-Foot Power Cord and Telephone and Coax Protection (BV112230-08-BLK)
review_headline: Surge Protectors and Power Strips aren't created equal.
review_body:
Personally, I don't feel purchasing surge protectors is an option. I guess we could run around and unplug everything whenever a storm hits, but we're not always at home. Here's the deal. We'd end up buying a power strip anyway. Surge protectors serve the same purpose, but also provide protection from changes in electrical current. In other words, a surge protector can block power surges; a power strip cannot.

I've purchased a few over the years, but this is why I like this model the best:

-- Plug for the wall socket lays flat verses sticking out. Helps in those tight spaces.

-- Twelve outlets. That alone is an OMG feature, but it's how the outlets are laid out. Three are on each side for the bulky plugs with six straight down the middle. Awesome design that's very roomy.

-- Has an eight-foot cord. That's a huge deal for us.

-- Safety covers for the unused outlets. This way, dust can't get in.

On the box, it says the Ultimate protects your HDTV, Stereo system, gaming console, Digital Video Recorder/Blu-ray, Desktop Computer, Router, Laptop, Printer, Answering Machine, Home Appliances, Digital Alarm Clock, Cell-Phone Charger.

A couple months before receiving this, we purchased another brand with less outlets that did the same (meaning it was for Home/Office) for about the same price at a local hardware store. This is a much better deal.

review_headline: Good, as long as they're fitted properly
review_body: When I first tried these, I thought they didn't work. Switching them on seemed to make no difference. However, the good reviews I'd read encouraged me to persevere. So I put on the slightly larger ear pieces and made sure they were properly crammed into my head, and they worked really well. The length of these is at least another six inches from what my old ipod headphones were.     8/10   - These may not be thousand dollar head phones but these are audiophile headphones. I take 2 points Because I wish they would get a bit louder, but for the average person these are perfectly loud enough. They drown out the noise in a talkative movie theater line perfectly. product_title: OmniMount Echo 63 63-Inch Video Table (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I received this item yesterday, and spent about an hour unpacking and assembling it.  It looks great and matches well with other similarly manufactured items (i.e. IKEA dark brown finish).     We are using it as a stand for a Sony 60\\" DLP TV, and to house a large Onkyo A/V Receiver, DVD Player, DVR, and a few small peripherals.  Assembly was easy for one person as long as you can decipher the diagrams (which is why I rated it 4 stars).      In case you are like me and prefer detailed assembly instructions, please read-on:      Assembly Instructions:    1. Unpack all items from main box    2. Place top panel topside down on floor so that threaded inserts are facing upwards (this is the large panel with 1 completely smooth/hole-free finished surface)    3. Thread the (4) long rods securely into metal inserts at exposed surface of top panel (knurled/textured ends of rods pointed downward)    4. Insert (4) wooden dowel pins into the remaining holes in the exposed surface of the top panel (feel free to lightly tap with butt-end of screwdriver to seat dowels completely into holes)    5. Align short, end panels with rods inserted in step 3, and then slide down over rods to seat against top panel (with enough background light you can look through the holes in the panels to gently guide the rods freely through the panels)    6. Insert (4) wooden dowel pins into remaining holes in end panels (feel free to lightly tap with butt-end of screwdriver to seat dowels into holes)    7. Lift bottom panel into position over the projected ends of the metal rods and lower into position (NOTE: strongly suggest you enlist a partner to help with alignment and to avoid scratching the finish of the panel - Alternate: cover exposed ends of rods with cardboard until you can ensure all are aligned with holes in bottom panel)    8. Once the bottom panel is seated over the dowels and rods, loosely thread the (4) \\"mushroom\\" type fasteners provided onto the ends of the metal rods and then tighten securely once fitted (it really helps to use a combo driver with an Allen tip - otherwise the provided tool will suffice)    9. Align metal legs over threaded inserts at corners of exposed cabinet base, and then secure with (2) provided screws at each (always install fasteners loosely at first, and then tighten once aligned)    10. Carefully align plastic inserts over open ends of legs, and then press into place to fit (I added heavy-duty, adhesive backed, felt pads to protect our wood floor when moving the cabinet around - this also makes it easier to move when loaded)    11. Lift/rotate the cabinet into upright position and then proceed with A/V equipment placement (plastic covers can be inserted into rear channel to organize wires as needed (I didn't use these since the components and a basket hid all the wiring)      I decided to load the heaviest items toward the far ends of the (lower) component shelf to reduce sagging of the shelf material over time.    Hope ths helps!

product_title: Z-Line Keira TV Stand - Mocha
review_headline: Gorgeous and practical modern TV stand
review_body:
After failing to find a modern-looking entertainment stand at big-name furniture stores like BoConcept and Room and Board, I decided to take a chance with this Z-Line stand on Amazon. I couldn't have been happier with the result.

Appearance-wise, the Z-Line is gorgeous with beautiful smoked glass panes and attractive dark wood arms. If you have modern furniture, this will fit in quite well. As a stand, it's also extremely solid. Mine holds a 37\\" Samsung TV on the top shelf, with a Wii and an XBox standing on one side of it; on the middle shelf I have (from left to right) a PS3, a large center speaker, and an old Apple TV; on the bottom I have an APC power conditioner and a very heavy Onkyo receiver. Despite all this equipment the stand still looks airy and spacious. I've had the stand set up like this for 9 months so far and have observed no bowing of the glass panes nor scratches.

Other pluses are easy access to cords and excellent ventilation--both thanks to the open back and sides. Assembly was also *unbelievably* easy. The pieces actually came with stickered tabs indicating which pieces attach to which.

The only potential drawback is cord management. Though it is possible to hide cords by snaking them down the center backing, for most people this will be impractical--especially if you have both a power conditioner and a large receiver. Even with a couple cords showing in the back, however, it remains a beautiful piece of furniture.

product_title: Premium Bluetooth Keyboard Folio Case and Stand for Apple iPad 2 WiFi / AT&T / Verizon **Includes Accessory Bag and Screen Cloth
review_body: Premium Bluetooth Keyboard Folio Case and Stand for Apple iPad 2 WiFi / AT&T / Verizon **Includes Accessory Bag and Screen Cloth     I bought the above iPad2 case from Accessorie Genie about three weeks back.  I have since returned it and have been promptly reimbursed by the seller.      As a product, it basically did what it promised to do - providing a bluetooth enabled keyboard for the iPad2.  However I was not happy with the material used, especially for the insides (resin?).  The case was wobbly when stood up.  The keyboard had some keys elevated than the rest.  The bluetooth connection was patchy (I used it for only a couple of days).  The case added considerable bulk (can't help much, if you want a keyboard, I guess). The connection/charging light was all but invisible.  I just couldn't figure out the charging status because the indicator light was very feeble.  And I don't think the keyboard carried all the 'lights' that were mentioned in the documentation.      Documentation was probably the biggest bummer for this product.  A one page, two-side printed color spread was sent along with the product that went much beyond testing the capabilities of the English language in describing the various features of the product.  I do not object to occasional spelling mistakes or even differences in usage between American vs. British vs. Asian vs. Any Other English.  I know I don't speak Queen's English either.  However, offering a page full of gibberish as a user manual is disrespecting the buyer.  A company that can manufacture a decent enough product can surely come up with a simple one pager that neatly describes the key features of the product in plain English.  If you get a chance to go through the documentation, you will know what I mean.  I don't have a copy of it with me - else I could have quoted from it. Yes - bad documentation does not necessarily ruin the quality of the product.  However, when I was not able to figure out whether the unit was charging or not (because the 'indicator lights' were either off or were non-existent), the user manual could not help me much.      Finally, a prospective buyer of this or any other similar products from other sellers should carefully weigh these considerations.  I say this because I cannot honestly blame the seller or the product quality 100%  for my decision to return the product.  1. Any bluetooth keyboard + case for your ipad2 will certainly make your sleek and slim tablet quite bulky.  Be sure you are OK with that before buying the cover.   2. You need to be 100% convinced that the way you use the ipad calls for a separate hard keyboard - for web surfing and those occasional short emails, the ipad soft keyboard should be more than enough  3. Even if you type a lot, if you don't travel much or do much of the typing at home,  you may be better off sticking to a simple, slim iPad2 cover and buying a separate, full-sized bluetooth keyboard (I hope there is one out there that works with the iPad) that you can use when you are at home

review_headline: Yes, they are indeed the best multimedia PC speakers right now.
review_body: Read some reviews on a magazine about these speakers and went here to read more reviews. Altough I've know the B&W brand before as a highly rated audiophile speakers company I've always follow a rule when buying audio products and that is to hear it myself and then decide. Well, I went to an Apple store and heard them and got a very good impresion about the sound and image of those speakers. I did buy them for my PC and gave them my final test in my home. Well, I have to say I am very impressed and ended with a very big smile. I love audio (I consider myself and audiophile) and these is why I don't hesitate to buy expensive speakers if those will provide me a great audio experience and these speakers do deliver. What I like most, apart from the cristaline and warm sound they provide, is how good they are at creating an IMAGE or what is called the 3D sound every good stereo setup should provide. In most cases to obtain this you have to place the speakers in an angle to create an imaginary triangle between the speakers and you. Well, in with this speakers one only have to place the speakers in front of you, one on the left side, one in the rigth side, always maintaining the same lenght, and you in the center, -that will be you in front of the monitor or screen-, and the IMAGE and 3D sound is there. I can hear perfectly well the warm voice in the center, the drum also in the center but behind, the piano at the left, the guitar at the right, etc. Just for this good IMAGING they provide the speakers should be worth the price but you also can add with this speakers the great sound as I said before. I would describe the sound as a very european-sound, like my Triangle speakers or the similar sounding Focal speakers for home use, that is: crystal clear high, warm, fresh and defined vocals and good but not overwhelming bass. You can feel the bass but it won't shake the room as some people would like. The sound these MM-1 speakers provide could be defined as the most anti-BOSE sounding speakers, so if you have heard BOSE speakers before you can get the idea. product_title: Sennheiser Portable Neckband Headphone with Dynamic Bass
review_headline: These are VERY quiet and thus USELESS at the gym
review_body: I have both a S545 Walkman and a 4th gen iPod Nano. I have been using Sennheiser's PMX 60 earphones for awhile. I recently checked out Sennheiser's website and saw that they made a new behind the neck model, so I ordered them from Amazon.  You have to REALLY crank up the volume on either device to achieve a volume loud enough to drown out ambient noise. And by that, I mean MAX volume. So if you're on a cardio machine at a gym, max volume might not even cut it with these. The PMX 60's and two different behind the neck models from Sony are so much louder. If I used max volume with any of these I'd go deaf.  Even if having your iPod, Walkman, etc on maximum volume is ok with you, there's another problem. Others around you can easily hear what you're listening to. With my other earphones on loud, others around me can kind of tell that I'm listening to something but not as clearly as with these PMX 90's. These are also very thick, but I guess that's to be expected with the supposed emphasis on bass. So how is the bass? It's ok...not great, but ok. Not leaps and bounds better than the other behind the neck earphones that I have. But maybe the bass is the problem with the volume being so quiet? The little woofers are hogging all the power? I don't know. All I know is that these are only really good if you're in an already quiet environment and just want to listen to soft quiet music. But if that's the case, why spend fifty bucks? A fifteen dollar pair at quiet volume will suit you just fine.  These PMX 90's are a huge disappointment. My search continues.  Save your money!  11/11/11 edit: I came back to look at other people's reviews and was pleased to see that many others had the same gripes that I did. These are ill-fitting and too quiet to be useful. I noticed that others also called out the PMX60's which I desperately wish Sennheiser would bring back (or at least a new model very similar to them). But then...I also noticed some very positive reviews. Surprise, surprise- they're all from people that got these for free via Amazon's Vine program. If you sort the reviews by date, you'll see all bad reviews until a few Vine \\"top reviewers\\" were bribed with a free pair around Sept 2011. But even then, some of them still gave bad reviews.  Look, from time to time every company puts out a dud. It happens. I wish Sennhesier would just accept this, discontinue the PMX 90, and replace it with a loud, tighter-fitting neckband model. I'd be all over it. The discontinued PMX 60's are going for twice as much as they originally cost from third party sellers. After I returned my PMX 90, I ended up buying not one, but two pairs of PMX 60's from a third party seller.

review_body:
I have owned this product for over a year. This surge protector works wonderfully and has not caused any problems yet. It also looks cool. I highly recommend it.

***Update***
I have owned this product for 3 years, and it still performs well. I have encountered multiple power outages while using this product, and every electronic connected to this surge protector is still working well. I have had the opportunity to use the phone cable in/out on this surge protector and can verify this product's ability to protect equipment attached to its phone cable in/out. When my silver AT&T modem was connected directly into the wall, it would die after any electrical surge. It got to the point where I had to have AT&T replace their modem multiple times in one year. At that point, I bought a very nice Netgear wireless router. I didn't want the router to die like my AT&T modem did, nor did I want to replace anymore modems, so I bought 2 phone cables to use in connecting both the modem and router into the surge protector. I ran one phone cable directly from the wall to the surge protector, and then one phone cable directly from the surge protector to the modem. Then, I ran one ethernet cable from the modem to the Netgear wireless router. It has been 2 years since I hooked the modem and router into this product, and both the modem and router are still working like new. Neither has experienced one red light of death since hooking them up. I was concerned about lag when connecting my modem and router into this product, so I played multiplayer games online using this setup while connecting both my Playstation 3 and computer into the router. I never experience any lag. I still highly recommend this product.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body: I did some research on headphones, looking for the best bang for the buck. But  I also wanted amazing sound, only because I am particularly picky about sound quality. I always   knew about Sennheiser and their audiophile headphones, but never looked into them. So I did some   review searching and found that the HD 518 headphones were very exceptional in terms of comfort and sound capability.   So I recently bought them and boy have they changed my outlook on headphones. They have such great open   clarity to them when the music is playing. They were a little cloudy a first, but after a few  hours of \\"burn in\\", they sounded phenomenal. They have such a dynamic range, both lows and highs   are covered without distortion, and you can actually hear recording mistakes in your music at times. People  say the bass was not that great or sufficient, but if you have a great pre-amp or hi-fi stereo eq, you can get as much  bass as you will ever really need, in terms of an audiophile's standpoint. I would recommend these to anyone  who wants to get serious about sound quality for a great price tag. They are also built well, considering the plastic  headband.

product_title: iTour-POP Ultra Portable Rechargeable Speaker for iPod, Sansa, Zune, iPhone 4, BlackBerry, HTC EVO, DROID, Samsung Wave, Galaxy S
review_headline: Best in it's class, and I tried them all...
review_body:
I purchased this and four other brands/models because I wanted to hear with my own ears which ones were the best in this micro portable speaker category.
The ones I tried were:
X-Mini Max II Capsule Speakers (White)
X-Mini II Capsule Speaker (Red)
Satechi SD Mini Portable Pocket Speaker
iHome iHM60LT Rechargeable Mini Speaker (Blue Translucent)
iTour-POP Ultra Portable Rechargeable Speaker
I did not include the Altec Lansing iM-237 Orbit Speaker since it is not rechargeable.

Sound quality, on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the best of the group, and 1 being the built-in speaker in an iPhone or iPod Touch:
iTour: 10/10
iHome: 8.5/10
Satechi: 7
X-Mini II: 7
X-Mini Max II: 4

The iTour-POP wins it, no contest really. Amazing full sound and low distortion from a speaker this size. It's a little bigger in diameter than the others, but not as tall. Stays put, even at high volume. The next three all sound pretty good, if you didn't hear them side by side with the others, you'd be pretty satisfied with purchasing any of them. These three all suffer from 'walking' across the table at high volume, the bass thumps just make them jump a little with every beat, with the iHome being the worst at that. Not a huge deal, but it could drag itself and your $150 Nano of the counter and onto the floor...
The Satechi is the only one with the built-in SD slot, which is pretty cool.
Finally, the X-Mini Max II: what a disapointment, horrible sound quality compared to the rest, especially the lower frequencies. Very tinny and distorts more than the others. Cross this one off your list.

product_title: HiFiMan RE-0 In-Ear Stereo Headphones
review_body: My experience mirrors that of some of the other reviewers who rated these 1 star. Before I go into why you absolutely shouldn't waste your money on these, I'll recap the reasons you might be tempted to do just that. Yes, the sound is great and tough to beat at this price point if you value clarity and transparency. Nothing is exaggerated; you'll hear your music the way it actually sounds without any coloration via the common tactic of boosted bass and blunted highs. Uncompromising fidelity isn't my preferred sound (mostly because it will make bad recordings and lower-bitrate music unlistenable), but if it's yours, I'd love to be able to recommend these.     Unfortunately, I can't, because their durability is shockingly, unbelievably bad. I've never had such a terrible experience with any other product or company. I got them this time last year after a nearly monthlong delay because the company's president, by his own admission, forgot to (have someone else) ship my order. After only two months of ownership, during which I probably listened to them a dozen times or less (I ordered the more musical and identically priced Hippo VB at the same time and immediately preferred them), the left earpiece came apart in my ear. Whoever thought it was a good idea to join two pieces of metal with some kind of cheap glue was mistaken.     And so my epic journey with Head-Direct's customer service began. I explained my situation to someone who referred to herself as \\"Ms. T,\\" which isn't the sort of alias that inspires confidence. In fact, it made me feel like I was doing business with a shady operation since their customer service rep was apparently uncomfortable providing a first or last name. Leaving aside my misgivings about her nom de plume, I shipped back the defective pair at my expense and received... a clearly used pair in return. It would've been one thing if they had fixed and returned my original pair, but instead they sent me some sort of beat-up demo unit with dirty eartips and severe scratches all over the housings and cable splitter. The splitter was so badly scratched that the make and model markings were gone. I once again contacted the mysterious Ms. T and expressed, as politely as possible, that this wasn't OK but that a refund would be. Sadly, my request was denied because more than 30 days had passed since the initial purchase. Instead, she sent me a brand-new pair while letting me keep the filthy and abused pair. (Hooray?) Much as I wanted no more to do with the RE0 or Head-Direct by that point, I was out of options. After a month of email correspondence and several trips to the post office, I had a new and functional pair of earphones.     Fast-forward to this year. The replacement pair had spent most of the previous 9 months in a protective pouch, unused. I decided, therefore, to sell it to a friend before moving from Seoul back to the US. A few days after the earphones changed hands, my friend contacted me to say that the right-side earpiece had gone out. I promised that I would get in touch with Head-Direct and send her out a new pair. My friend shipped them back to me from Korea for inspection, and indeed the right side was completely silent. I contacted Head-Direct, hoping for a quick swap, especially given my history with the product and their bungling attempts to make things right. I received the following email in response:     Hello Tony,    You purchased the REO on May 13, 2010 at this time your warranty has expired.      Kindest regards,  Ms. T.    Head-Direct Corporation / HiFiMAN  Customer Service Team     I didn't know whether to laugh or cry, especially given the perverse juxtaposition of her \\"tough luck, chump\\" message and her upbeat signature. But here my story ends, a year later and about $90 poorer (this includes the cost of both initial and return shipping). In short, owning these earphones has been a hugely unpleasant ordeal and I deeply regret ever buying them. If their customer service were more sympathetic, I would temper my criticism, but any company that thinks discarding disappointed customers is acceptable business practice deserves to fail. Please do yourself a favor and buy anything but these.    Thanks for reading.
