product_title: Philips Headband Headphones -Red/Black
review_body:
These headphones are everything ear buds are not: they're comfortable, rich in bass, and keep noise out the old-fashioned way, by encircling the ears with large sound-insulating pads. They produce a big, strong sound from MP3 players that tend to be underpowered.

In a departure from the more rigid headsets of the past, the earpieces swivel on the headband so that they may be packed flat in a briefcase or perhaps alongside a laptop in its case.

The flat, very flexible wiring, resists tangling; and a three-ft. extension cable is provided should you want to use these in your recliner next to your home stereo system.

But there's a problem: the engineers have overshot the mark in battling the scourge of tiny sound. The bass is impressive, and mellow can be good up to a point; but unfortunately, the bass bias is so strong that the overall sound is muddled and unclear. Although I would not go as far as to say that single-driver systems are incapable of producing deep bass without sacrificing mid-and-upper-range clarity, these headphones could certainly use the addition of a tweeter. Curiously, the uppermost frequencies, which produce the characteristic overtones of instruments and voices, are still present.

Usually I have to run my iPod in bass-boost mode, but with this headset I have to switch to bass-reducing EQ, and still there is too much mid-bass mush. Plugging into my home stereo system the situation is even worse, although there I could probably skew the EQ enough to compensate. A treble boost at the sound source is needed to make speech fully intelligible. The overall sound is pleasant, if dishonest; and the noise-insulating quality of these `phones prevents the sounds of the outside world from overwhelming the weak treble. In spite of my disappointment with the unbalanced frequency response, there may be occasions when I will find these useful inasmuch as my primary alternatives are various pairs of tinny-sounding miniatures. Call me Goldilocks, but I'm still waiting for the headphones that are \\"just right.\\"m still waiting for the headphones that are \\"just right.\\"

review_headline: Good Reader With Lots Of Options
review_body: I bought the iRiver Story HD a couple of days ago, after reading mixed reviews about it.  I was pleasantly surprised by it's design and features.  Some reviews complained about the brown back (awful color, easily scratched), little plastic buttons (hard to push), and general sluggishness (slow to download, slow to load).  I found none of these to be true.  I own a new Kindle and a Nook Simple Touch - and the Story competes with them quite well.  It does have a very nice screen and the selection of books is the best of any eReader.  Also you can read many different format books, so you aren't as limited as you are with some eReaders.  Plus, you can use a standard SD card with it and you can also change the battery.  The wireless access to Google Books is a real plus - it's the first dedicated eReader that has this access.  If you're considering an eReader it's definitely worth a look.

product_title: Sennheiser MM 80i Headphone for iPhones, iPads, or iPods (Black)(Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Overpriced and undervoiced: a terrible choice for the money
review_body: The Sennheiser MM80i Travel earphones do not deliver a sound quality remotely commensurate with their price tag.  They're basically okay-sounding, though severely lacking in bass and midrange; and considering that they function well as noise-blocking earplugs, for a fraction of the price the MM80i earphones might make an okay choice -- but at this high a price, they're just a terrible choice and should definitely be avoided in favor of the great-sounding high-end earbuds from competing brands such as [[ASIN:B0019RBJOE Ultimate Ears]], [[ASIN:B000POI4ZY Shure]], or [[ASIN:B001D7709I Klipsch]].  These Sennheisers don't even really sound better than the stock iPhone earbuds.    Sound quality: Thin, almost tinny, cold and anemic.  Very treble-heavy, amazingly weak in bass and midrange.  As a test, I compared the MM80i earphones directly against a set of [[ASIN:B0009Q4PHO Ultimate Ears SuperFi 5 Pro]] in-ear earphones, which were sold until recently at the exact same price point as the MM80i.  While listening to the exact same music, and ranging over genres from classical to rock to hip-hop, the deliciously rich, deep sound of the dual-driver Ultimate Ears simply embarrassed the weak, metallic sound delivered by these Sennheisers.  This isn't some subtle \\"golden ear\\" audiophile thing; the difference is night and day, and other listeners confirmed my opinion.  Switching from the Sennheisers to the Ultimate Ears was a revelation; going back to the Sennheisers again afterward just drained all the richness and beauty out of the music.    While listening, I found myself reaching desperately for the \\"Treble Reducer\\" equalizer setting in iTunes, but even heavily boosting the bass and midrange couldn't begin to compensate for the terrible low-and-midrange sound and tinny treble of the Sennheiser drivers.  Through these treble-heavy Sennheisers, familiar music becomes a strange experience: the hi-hat cymbal overshadows the actual music in many R&B and hip-hop tracks, and a classical orchestra's cello and bass are nearly inaudible.  And while trying to EQ-compensate for the Sennheisers' weak bass, I found it all too easy to induce a lot of unpleasant buzzing -- something that should be totally absent from earphones at this price.  Simply put, for the money, the sound quality is shockingly poor.    Noise blocking: The MM80s do NOT provide active noise cancellation (despite being named \\"Travel\\" earphones), but they do act as very good earplugs for passive noise blocking.  I found that  I couldn't hear people talking right next to me, even while listening to relatively quiet music on the MM80i.  Frequent airplane travellers should still look for an active noise-cancelling headphone instead.     Form and features: Good, but unimpressive considering the price. The iPhone-style remote/mic on these earphones is unnecessarily large and bulky, as big as a ballpoint pen cap, and indeed it has a cheap but functional pen-style clip.  I found the buttons worked well with both a MacBook Pro and an iPhone.  Also included with the MM80i earphones are all the accessories you could want, including a neat little case (whose internal cord-spool almost instantly came unglued), comfortable basic over-the-ear cable hooks, and several different sizes of earplug. (Even though iPhone earbuds usually fall out of my ears, I found the already-attached medium size worked better than the large plugs, but it's nice to have a variety of sizes to try.)    In short: Avoid these earphones at all costs -- but especially at this cost.  There are many far better-sounding expensive earphones from other high-end audio companies. Sennheiser should be ashamed to have released a product as weak as the MM80i at this price.

product_title: JVC Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black
review_body:
I bought these as a replacement for my Sony MDR-NC60's. The Sony's were out of stock at Amazon, and I needed something fast.

I used these headphones on a trip from the US to London. Both ways, I was seated next to the engines. I was not impressed with the noise cancelling ability. I found them not as impressive as what I recall of the Sony's. To be fair, I had not tested the Sony headsets in this type of noise environment, but my gut tells me the Sony was better.

I also do not like the fact that to replace the battery, you have to pull off the ear muff. Much easier on the Sony. Otherwise, very nice packaging, excellent sound quality and good comfort (I would venture more comfortable than the Sonys). However, it's the noise cancelling ability which will save your ears.

In the end, I'm voting with my wallet. The JVCs will go to a friend as a gift, and I'm getting the Sony. I would recommend those over this one.

By the way, the reviewer who said that there's really no difference between noise cancelling devices, and that the extra money won't buy you much, is completely full of bunk. I've never tried the Bose, and I'm sure they are quite nice. But I have tried cheaper noise cancelling devices and the difference between a $50 noise cancelling headset and a $100 one is dramatic.

product_title: Numark NPM5 Active 5" Studio Monitors
review_body: I just received my Numark monitors last week, and I was blown-away by these speakers. I cannot believe how good they sound for the price. I read reviews for these monitors on many musician's sites before purchasing them. The reviews everywhere were 5 star, so I figured, how could I possibly go wrong with these? Well, I didn't! I would easily compare these monitors to others out there in the $200 to $400 price range. I cannot believe the low price that these monitors sell for. Do not let their price-range fool you by any means! These monitors are crystal clear in the low, high and mid ranges. They sound great both set \\"flat\\" as near field monitors for recording, and also by adding a little EQ \\"color\\" through an MP3 player or computer. I am not sure of the DB rating on the drivers in these monitors, but it must be very high, as they are very efficient. The drivers really put out some volume for the low 20 watt RMS power that the amplifier puts out. To put it simply, these things will get loud, and they are very clear while doing so. I have them sitting on angled foam isolation pads, on top of my computer desk, on either side of my 28\\" monitor, and they sound great. I have them runnng through a Creative Soundblaster X-FI Platinum sound card. I use the monitors to listen to MP3s/Wav files while working on my computer, and also to run my guitar and keyboard through, for creating music. They excel equally at both tasks. The monitors are very sturdy (and large), and have some significant weight to them. Especially the one with the amplifier in it. That (amp) monitor also has all of the controls on the back of it: Gain (volume), Bass, Treble and power switch. It also has the speaker output terminals for connecting the amp to the other speaker. The speaker termnials are the thread and screw type, so your speaker wires will not be coming loose any time soon, even if you have to move the monitors around constantly. The sound inputs for the (amp) monitor are standard female RCAjacks. I am running a 1/8\\" stereo to dual RCA male cable from my computer to the (amp) monitor, and it works great. This cable is NOT included with the monitors however, but can be purchased cheaply on Amazon, or at any Radio Shack store. The cables included with the monitors are standard speaker wires (about 10 feet), and a dual Male to Male RCA cable (about 6 feet). There is also a very bright blue LED power light on the front of the (amp) monitor. It is behind the speaker grill so the light is diffused, and really doesn't bother me. Some people have stated that it is annoying, but I actually think it is kinda cool. As I said before, these monitors sound great. The highs are crystal clear all the way uo to 20KHZ, and you can really hear things like cymbals, and high instument notes very clearly. The mids are very clear as well with a lot of emphasis on vocals. Most standard speakers make this area sound \\"muddy\\" and Suppressed. The lows are very \\"punchy,\\" and hit very hard down to around 65HZ. They do not distort or vibrate at all on the low end. I listen to (and play) mostly rock music, so I prefer the punchy low end sound that these monitors produce. If you are into Rap, Trance, Dance, or any other heavy low end bass music you might want to consider getting a sub-woofer to add to these monitors. Although that would probably color the sound, and defeat the entire purpose that you are purchasing \\"reference-monitors\\" for. I would highly recommend these monitors for anyone on a budget, or just looking for a great set of monitors/speakers at any price range. They work great for recording, or just listening to music in general. If you get them to replace one of those \\"colored\\" 2.1 or 5.1 computer speaker sets, you will notice a huge difference in sound quality right away. The sound difference is like night and day with these monitors. Take my word for it, and try these for yourself. Trust me, for the price, you cannot go wrong!

product_title: Velocity Micro Cruz Reader, Black (R101)
review_body:
I've owned the Cruz Reader for nearly three weeks, now, and out of the box it was rather disappointing. I understood it was a limited function device prior to purchasing but believed it would, at least, be responsive within its limits. Such was not the case. Most of the problem seems to be with the speed of the CPU (533 MHz) and translates into very slow everything. Apps loaded slowly; the touchscreen responded slowly; page turns in ereaders were slow; everything was slow. Video was sluggish regardless of bit rate, file size, resolution, or encoding method. Even audio playback of music files was lack luster.

But...

I was able to root the device and install a \\"hacked\\" ROM. Doing so allowed for pumping the CPU up to 800 MHz and the world changed. It's still not up to par with higher end Android tablets or iPads, however, it does everything it should have done (according to its promotional material) out of the box and does it very well. It's still a resistive touch screen rather than capacitive but I've used early PDAs (Palm, HPaqs, etc.) so I'm rather accustomed to the feel. Apps install fine and run as they should and it even works with older incarnations of the Android Appstore. All-in-all, I'm quite happy with the device as of this writing. The only downside, even after hacking is it still is stuck with Android 2.0.

It would be difficult to recommend the purchase to anyone who wants to do anything other than read books without having to root and apply third party hacks. But if you're familiar with UNIX based OSes or Android rooting and hacking, it's worth the price and turns a sub-$100 reader into a functional Android tablet.

product_title: -   Bose Acoustimass 3 Series IV - 2.1-channel speaker system and Onkyo Receiver Bundle
review_body:
I have this system and it came bundled as shown and decided one day to remove the Bose speakers and connect the Klipsch SB-2 that I had sitting on my bookshelf. The sound was lacking depth and I was yearning for a better sound. It seemed that the highs were clipped at the higher end and the bass was clipped at the lower end. As Bose likes to say, those bass sounds are not \\"real\\". I for one don't feel a defined bass with no power is \\"real\\". I had the Onkyo set to its highest bass and the Super Bass turned on but the bass was still weak. I had read somewhere that the mid-range is channeled to the Acoustimass Module which is basically a mid-range speaker encased in a box thus rendering it mono. When you do that the sound stage is lost. In a lot of music the mid-range is very important to the sound and musicality. Someone mentioned that the sound can be quite hard to listen to for a long period of time. It is true. The treble is artificially raised to the point where your ears start to tire after a short time. I think it was done to give the illusion of clarity.
I am glad that I installed the Klipsch because my music have come to life. The sound stage that was lacking is now more fully there. I've never heard my system sound so much better. I am running the speakers with the Onkyo CD/Amplifier that is shown. I cannot say enough for the Onkyo receiver. It really puts out. Unfortunately it was putting out on an anemic speaker system. Now, I notice all the sounds that I hadn't noticed before on the Bose system. Ironically, it is Bose that markets its speaker for clarity. Yes, it does have some clarity but in the process it clipped away portions of the highs, the mid-range and the lows when it went with the small cube speakers and \\"bass\\" module. They just cannot beat two full speakers especially the Klipsch SB-2. In effect, I upgraded to two speakers with premium one inch tweeters and 6.5\\" woofers. These speakers do not need a sub-woofer because the bass is so powerfulbut yet defined. Adding a sub-woofer would be nullifying some of the definition of the bass that you get from the speakers.
If you already have one of these systems, I recommend that you try connecting them to a Klipsch SB-2. You will be glad that you did when you finally discover premium sound.

Update to my review:
It has been a while since I reviewed this product and now need to add an update. I have since improved my system by removing the Klipsch speakers and replaced them with Yamaha NS-25t speakers. I noticed that the Klipsch was lacking somewhat in the clarity department when it comes to the highs. The low ends were there but needed more power. I wanted to improve the sound even more. I had these two medium sized floor standing speakers and decided to give them a try. I should have done this a long time ago. I was too caught up with the brand name and that is why I did not go with the Yamaha speakers. Now, I have the bass set to medium and I still get a powerful bass. The Onkyo can really put out. It made it even more apparent how weak the Bose \\"bass\\" module was. The highs are clear but not grating on the ears. They sound natural. I have also added an RCA subwoofer and that helped to fill the low end. It is unfortunate that Onkyo paired their cd player/amplifier with the Bose speakers. I don't think that Bose really evaluated the sound that came from the pairing as the sound sure is lacking. And it is not Onkyo's fault. Their cd player/amplifier is adequate for the job. Yes, it is a basic amplifier with a built in cd player but it works very well with a set of medium sized Yamaha floor standing speaker.

Another update to my review:
After about a couple of weeks using the Yamaha NS-25t I noticed that the treble and mid-range was sort of lacking the presence that they needed so brought out my Polk Audio Monitor 50 tower speakers. I had avoided using them because of space constraints and the fact that the bass was somewhat lacking. But now that I am running an RCA powered subwoofer the bass would not be a problem. Further, I had read on the description on Amazon that these speakers are designed to even work with unpretentious amplifiers. And the Onkyo that I am using is just that. An unpretentious amplifier with a cd player built in. I wanted more from my stereo so I dug out the speakers from my closet and put them to the test. Boy, I should have done this a long time ago. The treble is clear and present and natural sounding. The mid-range was very good. The bass was decent as they have two woofers in each speaker. But the low end was somewhat lacking. But with the subwoofer the bass was complete. The bass did not have the tight definition as these are ported speakers after all. But they have enough definition for my purpose (listening to mostly rock and pop music).

product_title: Sony MDRE828LP/SLV Lightweight Earbuds (Silver)
review_body:
These really are terrific earbuds for the price- High value here! I got these to replace the fairly lousy headphones that came with my Sony Walkman. [[ASIN:B00006JQ06 Sony SRF59SILVER AM/FM Walkman Stereo Radio]] They pair very well with the Walkman and also sound great on my MP3 players. They have proven to be fairly robust over time despite many snags of the cord on door handles, tool belt, etc.

Maybe my ears aren't as sensitive as they once were, but these sound great to me. Also, this reviewer never expects to find high fidelity through earbuds, no matter how nice they are or how much they cost. I let my home receiver take care of that need. For the money, then, these will stack up nicely to many pricier models. Indeed, I don't know that I would spend the dough for ones that purport to deliver vastly greater performance; that would be money wasted on these ears.

The ergonomics are nice and fit my ears securely without being too tight. They only come with one set of foam covers, however, so you'll be out of luck if the size of your ear doesn't match well with these. Some other earbuds do come with fittings that allow for a custom fit. Still, I find these to be comfortable, secure, and positioned in my ear to maximize sound transmission.

The mini jack at the end of these is set at a 90 degree angle to the cord. This may not matter to most, but I find that this setup resists separating from the player when it gets snagged. Nice touch, if that is what it is meant for.

A very cheap plastic case comes with these 'buds that allows you to carry them without fear of creating a Gordian knot. Cheap as it is, it is also surprisingly effective. I was going to toss it initially, but I'm glad I didn't. I find myself appreciating having my earbuds tucked away in my lunch box, tangle free and separated from stuff that would invariably end up on the cables of my other 'buds.

Are there better earbuds out there? I'd say yes, there probably are. But these are solid, great-sounding earphones at a price that's hard to beat. Super combination and recommended at four stars.ut these are solid, great-sounding earphones at a price that's hard to beat. Super combination and recommended at four stars.

However it is tiny compared to the standard rooftop antennas you see everywhere.  And it is not heavy.    Definitely a good buy for me.

review_headline: Some things it gets right, and some things are just wrong...
review_body:
First let me state that this beast is a thing of beauty, although I don't really understand why it has to be so big! It's clearly aimed at the music lover with an iPod that wants to pump up the volume with at least a 2.1 one-piece unit the size of a 8\\" sub-woofer enclosure (it's an 11 1/4\\" cube weighing 16.3 lbs)! For my purposes, which is really buying a great-sounding digital alarm clock. It's overkill, but in a really good way. At least in some regards...

The pros:

- a gorgeous piano-finish exterior;
- a well-designed and functional (for the most part) remote control;
- in a word, FANTASTIC, adjustable sound (via separate bass, and treble controls and a 5\\" sub-woofer that adjusts from 0-15 dB);
- a nice digital display that's not overly bright (though it can't be adjusted);
- two methods of tweaking your settings (via remote or a one-button knob on the unit's front that does everything the remote does);
- iPod support (the entire Apple spectrum, it appears, but not certain iPhones: more on that later), allowing complete control of the iPod from the remote or the one-button interface on the unit (I, myself, do not have an iPod);
- A digital AM/FM tuner with auto-tuning, allowing 10 presets for each band;
- An alarm setup that allows you the choice of buzzer, iPod, or radio;

And now the cons: granted, you might not care about these issues as much as I do; keep in mind that most of these deficits were acknowledged by Pyle's Tech Support Dept. It's why he DIDN'T acknowledge that their were features that SHOULD be working that I have suspicions. My thoughts on that later, based on my experiences with Pyle today, both with their website and with Tech Support...

- the clock appears ONLY as the 24-hour format; it cannot be adjusted to 12-hour (despite the fact that tech support insisted that it could be);
- the display cannot be switched at will from the station frequency to the clock, except when programming the time or the alarm, and then it just bounces back to the station once either is set;
- there is no standby mode, i.e. the clock will not appear when you power off the unit;
- the remote cannot place the unit in standby mode, only 5, 15, 30 minute sleep settings or sleep off, which in this instance means NO sleep mode is available, it does NOT mean standby!
- though the Amazon site (AND the product's box) says there are dual alarms,in fact, there is only one;
- there appears to be no support for iPhones on the unit, and the included adapter does not accommodate my iPhone 3G. Actually, I can't see how it accommodates ANY iPhone, since the adapter is entirely sealed on one end! Also, except for the mention on the box and by Amazon (clearly parroting what the box says, so it's not Amazon's fault), there is no mention in the manual WHATSOEVER about the unit's use with an iPhone!

- the alarm must then be turned on again, after it has been activated;
- The user manual is poorly written and omits details which I only learned about today from Tech Support (most of which was useless or incorrect);

I guess the earlier 3 reviewers were enamored of the sound this unit produces (not to mention its good looks), both of which are impressive, I'll admit. I wonder what there experiences have been after having spent some time \\"kicking the tires\\" for a while.

Now for more bad news: I would advise potential buyers to keep looking, if for no other reasons than the two I experienced TODAY: first, having downloaded the user's manual from the Pyle website before purchasing the unit last week, I went back to the website today looking for answers on some of these issues. The model PHS150B is no longereven listed in any of the searches I performed, not even among their discontinued products. Now why exactly IS that? I know it's possible that they may just be cleaning up the product's feature set on the website, but I doubt it.Since every trace of the unit's existence has been removed for some reason in the last few days, it may be that they now take the view that the unit is just not ready for prime time yet.

It is easy to use, easy to carry around, easy on the budget but gives you big sound, you are only limited on how many songs you can store.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 8 GB 6th Generation
review_headline: Good product but the instructions are awful
review_body: You have to more or less figure out for yourself how to  take advantage of the product features because of the  very limited instructions provided in the package.  Fortunately the Apple website is very helpful.  Otherwise I am very pleased with my nano and it is perfect for listening to music while I walk, which is what I bought it for.

product_title: C&E HDMI Male to DVI Male, CL2 rated, 3 Feet, CNE543932
review_body: Cable arrived quickly and appears to be well made.  Radio Shack wanted $40.00 for theirs.  My guess is they don't sell a lot at that price.

product_title: ROXY by JBL Reference 250 In-Ear Headphone with Microphone - Blue/Green
review_body: Until I managed to crush one of the earbuds in my car door, these served me perfectly. They are bright and thus hard to loose, appealing, and very functional. Since I ended up with one-sided headphones, I am buying another set just like it.

product_title: Premier Mounts FLIP LCD Flip-Down Mount, Silver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I used this product to mount a 15 inch TV/DVD combo in my Casita travel trailer. It is an excellent mount, easy to install, and attractive. I am sure it would also work well to mount under a cabinet. Swivels and tilts easily. Very sturdy product. Good instructions. Includes all hardware, but I had to get a few other materials to mount mine since it is installed under a fiberglass cabinet in the Casita (plywood to secure the bolts). I highly recommend.

product_title: Ambient Weather WR-088-TAN Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Weather Radio, Flashlight, Cell Phone Charger (Wounded Warrier Project® Desert Tan)
review_body: The radio has good reception and operates for about 20 minutes off 5 minute charge. The unit operates while charging. Charger for phones works too. The LED flashlight operates as expected, is fairly bright and works even after the radio no longer operates due to low charge. Have not had the chance to charge using the solar panels, but the unit does display that it is charging when in sunlight.   I have purchased the following rechargeable batteries as replacement: [[ASIN:B000ROP15S Replacement Battery For AT&T/LUCENT 9510/9550 - 6V 700mAh (NiMH) 9550]] but have not tried those yet.

product_title: Apple iPod shuffle 2 GB 4th Generation
review_body: Plays music, withstands copious sweat, synchs great.  Little awesome, adorable piece of technology for working out.  Convenient and few features so it does what it's supposed to...well.  Can't run without this IPOD.  I love it.

product_title: Magnavox DV200MW8 DVD/VHS Combo Player [Electronics]
review_body: We did not receive a remote that worked.  I contacted the seller and sent the non-working remote back, but never received a working remote. This was wasted money when I could have bought a brand new one for a little more money.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body:
I ordered this product because of the price it was the lowest comparing with other sellers. I was afraid that I'll get a product with scratches
or something like that . however, it was in a great condition NEW . ! I'm really satisfied with this purchase .

product_title: Philips AZ302 CD/MP3 Soundmachine
review_body: I generally like Philips products, but this one is a loser. Stopped working in 6 months. Poorly made, it was obvious from the beginning that it wasn't going to last long. A shame, as it worked well up until it died, and there aren't many of these cheap boomboxes that play MP3 CD's.

product_title: BlueRigger Basic High Speed HDMI Cable - 6.6 Feet - Supports 4K, Ultra HD, 3D, 1080p, Ethernet and Audio Return (Latest Standard)
review_body: I got two of these cables (one extra just in case) to hook up my xbox 360 to my TV for better graphics than the cable that comes with the xbox. The graphics are crisper and clearer, I don't have to fiddle with the 3 white/yellow/red vga connections when reconnecting the xbox to the tv, and it's so cheap - what's not to like?

product_title: Logitech Speaker for iPod and iPhone
review_headline: A Great Player with some Flaws - A MUST READ!
review_body:
Well this is my second iphone/ipod player.

i originally had the pure-fi logitech anywhere 2 - [[ASIN:B001G5Z82I Logitech Pure-Fi Anywhere 2 Compact Docking Speakers for iPod and iPhone (Black)]] and loved it.

used it at the park, out on the patio, at games, etc. Good sound quality and good remote control functionality.

I had a pretty good deal on this new s715i -straight from logitech for only eig hty bucks. So sold my old one - hard to part with it considering how much i used it and jumped on this one.

+ great sound quality - more full sound - bass is kicking
+ looks updated. very modern look
+ battery lasts a while
+ easy to use - power and volume.

-battery meter is a bit confusing. why not list a couple of leds like the pure-fi did?

-bass kicks out unplugged. not a huge deal but i'd rather have less battery or give me a button!

-HUGE HUGE ANNOYANCE - not even with my thin iphone 4 case - Griffin Reveal [[ASIN:B003TFFC5Q Griffin Technology Reveal for iPhone 4 (Black)]] - would it dock! so i have to take it out of the case everytime! soo frustrating.

-remote not responsive. i dont mind the limited functionality - the pure-fi let u access menus etc. but u have to have a really good line of sight to use it!

-travel case is cheap and flimsy. The pure-fi had a nice cushiony case - this is flimsy as hell! there is as much loose space as being inside a

-charger doesn't wrap nicely like the pure-fi. u just roll it up in a tangled mess. the pure-fi would have prongs that would fold in for compactness and you can roll the wire around it nicely.

come to think of it - aside from the sound quality and looks there is so many faults. I just wish they improved on the pure-fi :(

aside from that it's a great player. though not exactly the \\"upgrade\\" i was hoping for.

product_title: JVC Air Cushion Headphone
review_body: These headphones were purchased to replace my laptop and IPod ones that failed after nearly 3 years. These blow my previous ones away, I no longer need a earphone amplifier for my IPod :D. I only have to turn my volume up about30% and anything above that will hurts my ears :O. Sound is richer and warmer and satisfactory, especially for price I paid. I'm very happy with these, recommended.

product_title: Bose SoundDock 10 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock
review_headline: High Quality Sound, Mega-Volume, Handsome to Look At
review_body: I just purchased the Bose SoundDock 10 Digital Music System from an Apple outlet product retailer in Saudi Arabia. My goals were to purchase a music sound delivery system that sounds fantastic, doesn't have messy separate components and wires, etc. to deal with, is relatively small and easy on the eyes....I went home, opened the box, un-packed it, set it up (plugged it in), plugged my I-Touch I-pod into the docking station (all of this took abt 5 minutes) and listened...other listeners who happened to be in the large living-room at the time, raised their eye-brows at the crisp, full sound that firmly filled the living space. I found the sound to surprisingly crisp & full with zero distortion at high volume...the physical shape/design of the unit is strikingly handsome and takes up only 18 inches of horizontal space. I was pleased that Bose brought me a simple, high-quality sound machine in a small package...it met all my goals...Bravo-Bose~!  (This is my second Bose product...about a year ago, i purchased Bose headphones for walking with my I-Pod...and they are also an awesome product).

product_title: Skullcandy SCS-SCBP3.5 Skullcrushers Subwoofer Stereo Headphones
review_body: After reading some reviews about this product not being able to do well with heavy metal and hard rock type music, I decided to just give it a shot since they were at a pretty decent price. I'm glad I did. These headphones are amazing. They sound great, are very durable, very comfortable, and block out other sounds very well. These will always be one of my top choices for over-ear headphones now that I have used them for a while. I definitely recommend them.

product_title: Jensen 3-Speed Stereo Turntable with AM/FM Stereo Radio (Silver)
review_body: This was exactly what I was looking for. It shipped SUPER fast. It's got a slight wobble to it, but a mat will fix that, and the wobble doesn't effect the sound quality at all. I've been playing 30-40-50-year-old records and they sound just as good as the brand new ones do. This is a good investment for your money. I've recommended it to several of my friends! The speakers are plenty loud enough for me to play a record in my living room and hear it in my kitchen. Some of the older records are quieter, so maybe that's what some of the other reviews were referring to when they say it wasn't loud enough? The radio gets great reception. This is a great product, I'm glad I bought it!

product_title: TV Ears 2.3 MHZ Wireless Headset System with 10 Replacement Ear Tips
review_body: I ordered the TV ears due to ads and promotions I have seen ove the last yeaar or so.  At at the same time, I also ordered another manufactors wireless headset for TV listening.  I found the TV ears work but you lose reception if you turn your head or hold a drink in front of your receiver below your chin! Also, the range is very limited and you can't move around and retain reception. In addition to this, on occasions they will get a hum that you can't eliminate.  I found the headset TV listening  are far superior-better sound reception and you can go any where in the house or out doors without losing reception.

product_title: RiteAV 3.5mm Male to Stereo RCA Male Cable
review_body: I got this cord and plugged it into my stereo in the living room and then when I tried to unplug it from the stereo, the casing came off one of the RCA cables and I had to delicately pull the wire out with pliers. The sound quality is great, though. My only suggestion is if you're planning on buying one cord for multiple rooms, buy a chord for each room/stereo and don't try to unplug them and move them. Especially at $1.78 a chord, they don't get much cheaper.

product_title: Sony Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones
review_body: I bought these at walmart fo $50. They are very nice good quality. They fold up really well and comes with a nice carry case or bag and plane adapter. The sound quality is great.  I wish I had found them here earlier.

product_title: SMOKIN' BUDS White/Black
review_body:
I purchased this because my 2 month old Woodees Classic IEM's are having a connection problem and are being shipped back next week. I wanted a decent backup set.

Compared to the Woodees, these don't sound bad, but everything sounds subdued. The bass response is not as accurately produced, and dominates the mid and high frequencies, but is softer in comparison. Volume sounds softer at the same settings. Fit feels awkward, but surprisingly it stays in better the the Woodees even if a shake my head or jog. The cord is a lot sturdier as well.

With the Woodees, everything is balanced almost perfectly, though it sounds a bit bright, and the bass response is quick, deeper, and compliments the mids and highs so nicely. There is a drastic difference in volume, making the Woodees sound twice as loud.

Overall, the Skullcandy Smokin Buds are okay. It costs about $25, compared to $45 for the Woodees. The fact that they feel more durable and stay in my ears better makes these IEM'S great for workouts and running, but on a sonic level, do not compare to the Woodees Classic.

product_title: Polk Audio CS10 Center Channel Speaker Single
review_body:
Many here have commented on how big this center channel speaker is, I do not feel it is that big at all.

If you look at the dimensions you can easily see if this will fit into your existing setup or not, If you are expecting some tiny little speaker that you can tuck away this is not that, but at the same time its not all that big.

I actually prefer a speaker with some size and weight The box size is required to help produce the type of sound this is capable of, as the center channel is extremely important in both dialog and sound FX. You maybe surprised at just how much sound in todays movies is actually mixed to the center channel.

This is why it really can not be a wimpy little speaker like the type that come with many theater in a box systems, those sound tiny and are inferior by comparison.

As for the sound from this speaker I would say it is very good, it may be a tad nasal on some male dialog but this is slight and does not take away from the over all sound quality which produces nice clear highs and very good base response for this price range.

The build quality is top notch, the weight the construction this is a solid build right down to the black lacquer sides, no cheep plastic here.

To sum it up this speaker is a great buy, and you really can't go wrong with this purchase.

product_title: BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer
review_body: [[ASIN:B0015A8Y5M BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer]]    I bought this sub with the intent to replace a weak little Aiwa sub in my office.  Pretty small room but I am a bass head til death.  When I got it I unplugged my Klipsch rpw-10 and plug in the Bic.  I sat in on the built in TV shelf that sits empty (built in is for a CRT).  My room is 15x11 or so, open on on side to dining room/kitchen.  The room is configured sideways  with the TV over the fireplace and the satellites apporx. 6 feet from each side of the TV.  All settings the same,I set the volume on 5 and went to a rap station.    At -10 it was louder by double over my RPW-10.  Listening to this sub makes me feel like my Klipsch may have a clipping problem, I can't believe how much louder this Bic sub is.  I ran upstair and the whole house was trembling with low end bliss.  My crosses and frame were buzzing and the vents on my roof were making noise.  This thing really does a wonderful job.  It is very powerful and unlike many subs, the woofer is jumping out of the box.    For the money I feel this is sub is a steal.  I haven't gone into any deep testing as of yet, my wife was bothered by me pounding the room lol.  She never once said that with the Klipsch.  My only data so far is how much louder and stronger it is over my Klipsch.  The Klipsch is going to the office, no question.  People that rate this sub by saying \\"good for the money\\" are understating this sub.  From a long standing audioholoic, I am very surprised by this sub.  I want 2 :)

product_title: iHome iP97 Dual Alarm Clock Radio for iPod and iPhone
review_body: I love this alarm clock. It was either this or the iP9 and this was a little cheaper so I went ahead and bought this. It does the same as the ip9 but looks like a regular old alarm clock. I have an iPhone 4 and I was worried about it not being compatiable like my own radio and it plays it perfecrtly and will pause the music and play your ringtone if someone calls while you are listening to music. The gradual sleep and wake was tricky to figure out but once you get it, you'll love that too. I'm very happy with my purchase.

product_title: HDMI-High-Speed
review_body: These cables are inexpensive, feel and look high quality, and deliver perfect image quality. I've since purchased several other sizes. Not much else to say - these are just great!

product_title: Philips GoGear Raga MP3 Player
review_body:
I think this player is probably a bit overpriced given the limited gigs, but it is reliable and holds a charge well. Like some other reviewers I'm not crazy about the Philips GoGear software, but once you acclimate to the navigation and other mechanics, it's at least unmanageable. And for its faults, it doesn't slow down the rest of my system like iTunes.

If you're a serious music guy or gal, you're going to need a much bigger device than this, and chances are you won't be checking out this player to begin with. I would recommend this device for predominantly: a) people looking for a light player to accompany them during workouts/running; or b) a gift for children who want an MP3 player but lack a large collection of music (or who might be likely to lose interest in a couple of months).

product_title: Yamaha MCR-140WH Micro Component System (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I just bought it recently so I would have to write an update if it breaks soon - otherwise, the sound is quite amazing. I don't have a comparison versus the Bose (some people suggest, though, that the Yamaha is better + it costs half the price) but I was using a standard CD player before, and in comparison to that the Yamaha sounds as if you were in a concert hall. The setup is easy (duh -I did it so it has to be) and it works great right away - no need to fiddle with the controls (which someone might actually enjoy but not me;-)). So far so perfect!
Update: 2 years later still going strong, hope I am not jinxing it with this review! :-))

product_title: Logitech S135i 30-Pin iPod Speaker Dock
review_headline: Great sound  for a little money and size!
review_body: I was looking for something to listen to my ipod in my cubicle at work and tried many different options. Came across this little guy and at first was a little put off by the size (usually these little units don't sound very good) but decided to give it a try and I'm glad I did.     Logitech makes great quality products for computers such at keyboards, mice and PC speakers. What many people don't know is that they make great docks for Ipods (I own a 3+ year old logitech audio station book shelf unit that's still kicking). The unit is almost cute looking and is fairly straight forward to use. No bells and whistles (No radio, EQ, remote etc.) just volume control, bass switch and on and off. Plus a AC plug and audio-in in the back for non Apple media players, smartphones and laptops. Plus it runs on 4 AA batteries for about 10 hours of power according to Logitech. It will also charge your Ipod when mounted.    I'd rate the sound quality at above average to great and the bass response is suprisingly good for a unit this small and it's pretty loud to boot. Don't think your going to get the same sound quality as a Bose unit, but for a small room, kitchen, patio, office or cubicle this does the trick. Plus its portable. It does break up a little at high volume but that's to be expected for a unit this small.

product_title: JBuds J2 Premium Hi-FI Noise Isolating Earbuds Style Headphones (Onyx Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: these head phones are def what you pay for, i dont understand how someone could charge $50 for they originaly. i just got them and will fo show return them, and usualy i dont write reviews but this one needed one. the sound is very poor and sounds like you are listening to music behind a wall. its very DISTANT! i do not recomend them, and the buds are poorly designed and dont fit well, and there are open gaps between your eardrum and the outside noise.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body:
So much hoopla and excellent reviews over these little machines for nothing. I know people are raving about it and can't wait to get one, just cannot figure out why. My mp3 player broke and I needed a replacement. Wanted the Zune as I am a musician and audio quality was the most important issue for me. Found they are not making any new ones and only updating to the new Windows7 phone.

As far as the ITouch 4, the display is very nice and looks pretty. An easy machine to navigate around. Internet access is fine, nice to get my mail now and then, and it has a couple of nice apps for music. Most apps are totally useless, a lot of nonsense games, and most apps are \\"I'm wasting my time\\" apps, at least that I have found. The \\"find a restaurant\\" app is good, there are several. Stanza is a good app if you want to read some ebooks and you can upload them from your calibre collection. It is not close to a kindle but will do in a pinch. You eyes do get tired from the contrast.

The absolute worse thing is the battery life, there is none. It does not even last a day!! This is unacceptable to me and I have no idea why people have not been screaming about it. They just accept it and shrug their shoulders. I spend more time charging the thing the using it. My little mp3 player from lasted a month. And I can tell you, as long as people accept this terrible situation, it will not change.

As far as the music, well...........if you are an audiophile forget it. I have tweaked and have the best ear buds and it is just barely acceptable. There are several cheaper little mp3 players that sound so much better. The external speakers are useless. So if you want this to listen to classical music, you best keep looking. Now that they are no longer making the Zune, it is a dilemma. Needless to say I was very disappointed.

So, now I have an expensive little mail getter and will look elsewhere for something to play my music.

Speaking of mail. If you set up a pop account you are okay, but if you have Gmail or yahoo or any of the other mail clients that uses imap, it will delete all your mail in your mailbox on your computer. I know, it deleted mine and you cannot get it back unless you forward it to a different address. It works fine with the pop mail addresses. So make sure you check it out.

so overall out of 10 at least in my opinion

product_title: iHome iP28 Portable Travel Alarm Clock for iPod and iPhone (Black)
review_body: This baby packs a mean punch. It is small but the sound quality is epic. The button layout is smooth and it is ultra portable. Nice!

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body: I purchased the ipod because I wanted to download books.  I am an avid reader and enjoy having it read to me.  This is my first experience with an ipod.  When I recieved it, I was surprised to have to go to my computor to download the programs for set up and was disappointed it didn't have the instructions with it, instructing me to download the instruction manual to my computor.  It took me a couple hours to get all completed and I am still learning about what it is capable of.  I did purchase an accessory so I could just plug it in to an outlet and charge it since I am not always around my computor.  Still learning and am enjoying hearing the books I have downloaded.

product_title: Mount-It! Samsung UN55B8500 LED HDTV Compatible Dual-Arm Swivel Wall Mount **FREE HDMI CABLE**
review_body: DO NOT go to a retailer and pay $250 for a similar mount. It has tight tolerences and everything fits well. Easy to install, assuming you don't need instructions written by someone who speaks, writes or understands english. If you are reasonably handy, the instructions aren't really totally necessary anyway.

product_title: Coby Deep Bass Headphones with Stereo Earphones
review_body: I highly recommended this headphone. I bought it from One(1)StopShop in Amazon and that seller's rock! Ordered on Wednesday afternoon and received Saturday afternoon. The only con is people can here the sound comes from the headphone. The small earbud work fine too.

product_title: Polk Audio Monitor 70 3-Way Floorstanding Speaker (Single)
review_body: Very impressed.    I have had these speakers for about a year and half... they continue to sound better with each full listen.    Just an amazing product/deal from our friends at Polk.

product_title: NuForce Icon uDAC-2 Silver Digital Audio Converter
review_headline: Fine for what I needed it for.
review_body: I bought the uDAC-2 to ensure that my new Beyerdynamic DT990 250ohm headphones would have all the power they needed. I didn't buy it too much for increase in sound quality, and more for the amplifier. The amplifier works great, and I can push the 990's way past what my headphone jack will allow. It was plug-and-play, and immediately recognized by my computer. I just had to disconnect my desktop speakers, as for some reason they were getting the sound. The quality of the sound, while I did not expect anything spectacular from $120, did not change at all. I've completely burned in everything, with well over 200 hours on my uDAC and the cans, but no change. I'm not too disappointed as the quality was already quite good, but a bit of a let-down there. That knocked off one star, but I would still recommend this to anyone looking for a cheap way to power their high impedance headphones.

product_title: Cables Unlimited ZIP-AUDIO-CD3 ZipLinq Retractable 3.5mm Audio Cable - Black
review_body: After only a month of use, this product has stopped staying extended. It is supposed to extend to fixed points then stop. Now, it just tries to retract constantly. Don't waste your money.    Pro:  Sound quality is good. Worked well for a month.    Cons:  Only worked for a month before it broke.

product_title: FiiO E5 Headphone Amplifier
review_body: I use this to rehearse drums for my bands. It works great! It amplifies the volume just enough so I can work out parts.

product_title: MEElectronics Clarity Series Ceramic In-Ear Headphone with In-Line Microphone and Remote for iPhone and Smartphones
review_headline: A great buy with great customer service.
review_body: I'm no great audiophile, but I really love the sound in these headphones.  It's not as bass heavy as other headphones, but I actually like that feature.  There's more to music that the bass...    They are a bit fragile, but when my set developed wiring problems, customer service was extremely fast, responsive, and professional.  I was particularly impressed by how fast they got a new set out to me.

product_title: BlueRigger Basic High Speed HDMI Cable - 6.6 Feet - Supports 4K, Ultra HD, 3D, 1080p, Ethernet and Audio Return (Latest Standard)
review_body:
I've purchased this brand of cables TWICE. I keep coming back to order more as I add more \\"stuff\\" to my home theater and game system. These cables are an awesome value, provide awesome picture clarity, no sync problems, excellent performance on audio feedback channel, no issues what so ever. There is NO reason to pay 5x, 10x...20x more for \\"brand name\\" cables. These cables to do the SAME JOB as good if not better and keeps your money in your pocket!

Don't overpay for brand name cables from a big box store! Monster charges upwards of $50-$60 for the same $5 cable here. Think about buying 6 of these cables for the DVR, cable box, BluRay, XBox360, Roku, etc and the savings ADD UP! That's like putting $300 back in your pocket, which paid for my home receiver.

product_title: RCA Sport Neckband Headphones
review_body: Great for sitting at a desk listening to music (which is what I bought them for) but probably not the best if you're going to be leaning back/lying down because of the \\"behind the neck\\" piece.

product_title: USBCELL MXAA02 AA Rechargable Battery - 2 Cell Pack
review_body: I recieved my first USBcell's as a gift at a conference. I am currently using them on a dialy basis and I have to say that in 2011 they are better than any of these reviews claim.  I keep a pair in my computer bag so that when I travel I have them, and I have a couple of sets for the house. It is true that the charging time is long but if you keep a couple of pairs around you can exchange them and charge the used ones in the mean time.  As for the life of the batteries I have gotten just as much use out of them as a standard alkaline cell.  They now have lights on them that let you know when the battery is fully charged, and the USB connections seem to work fine on my laptop without being tight or pulling apart.  I love using them, and while they are a bit expensive the ease of recharging them and keeping alkaline batteries out of landfills suites me just fine.  I'm sure that other rechargeable batteries work well too, but the universal USB charger makes it effortless to find a place to get a charge and I don't have to worry about loosing to the trash because someone in the house doesn't realize they are rechargeable.

product_title: iHome IH70 Computer Stereo Speaker System with Dock for iPod (Silver)
review_body: On the first one I ordered, the right speaker didn't work straight out of the box.  The next one I ordered was dusty right out of the box and had a scuff mark on one of the speakers right out of the box.  It stopped working after about 9 months (stuck in sync mode, which I've never even used, since I can't plug anything into the usb ports at work).  While it worked the sound was great, although I don't believe the engineers who designed the unit understood that volume is logarithmic and not linear, as the volume difference between the lowest level and the next level up is pretty big.  Also, it did pop loudly when being turned off and sometimes it wouldn't respond to the volume buttons or the remote - which could have been part of the same flaw that makes it stick in sync mode.  I e-mailed ihome asking if there was any way to reset it or anything and received an e-mail back asking for me to ship it back insured and send them $40 (the price I paid originally) to have it repaired.  Thanks, but no thanks.  Never buying iHome again.

product_title: Mediabridge ULTRA Series HDMI Cable (3 Foot) - High-Speed Supports Ethernet, 3D and Audio Return [Newest Standard]
review_body: I needed a high speed cable for my Samsung 55\\" D8000 3D TV. Of course the local retailer assured me I would need the Monster or the Chocolate cable to get the \\"true\\" picture quality out of my 3D TV. He said I could return the high price cable so I bought it. Meanwhile I ordered the Mediabridge cable online.       I hooked the high price cable up and watched a Nascar race on my DVR. Absolutely stunning picture. Kept up with the speed of the race with no loss in picture quality. Then, I hooked up the Mediabridge cable and watched the exact same race. The result? ABSOLUTELY STUNNING PICTURE! I saw no difference between the 2 cables. I did the same test in 3D. I watched IMAX: Under the Sea in 3D. This time, I had someone else hook up the cables so I had no idea which cable I was watching. After watching the movie twice, I really couldn't tell the difference but I decided to pick 1 over the other and it just happened to be the Mediabridge cable.      So I returned the high price cable and will use the $$ I saved buying Happy meals for a month.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 300 Remote Control 915-000143 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
My wife and I recently moved and we lost the remote to our 32\\" Samsung LCD television for our bedroom in the process. I couldn't find an exact replacement from Samsung, but I have a higher-end Harmony remote for our entertainment center in the living room so I started shopping around for lower-end Harmony remotes for the bedroom. I didn't need all the bells and whistles of the higher-end Harmony series as it's just controlling a television and eventually a cable box. I stumbled on this one and since it was only a few dollars more than the basic universal remote, decided to jump on it. Prime had it here a day later.

The remote is built well and feels like it will last. It's straightforward with the buttons laid out where you can eventually learn them. Setup was a snap. I plugged the remote into my MacBook Pro and went to their website. I logged in and typed in the model number from my TV and viola! It set it up in a couple of minutes and it was good to go. My other Harmony remote is backlit so using it at night is easy. I don't expect that out of a sub-$50 remote, but it's a feature I didn't realize I really liked until it was gone. Also, the buttons are a little bit cluttered. This remote does it all and more, but to make that possible, it's got buttons. Some of the buttons get a little small and the inability to see them at night makes using it by feel a little difficult.

However, these are small trade-offs for a very nice, comfortable, easy-to-use remote from a great manufacturer. Overall I'm pleased and don't feel like either of the cons I listed detract from the value of the remote. I give it five stars across the board. Enjoy!

Pros:
* Straightforward design
* Very easy to setup

Cons:
* Hard to see at night
* Buttons are a little cluttered

product_title: Monster MC 1000HD-1M Ultra-High Speed HDTV HDMI Cable (1 meter),15.8Gbps (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Not All HDMIs Are Created Equal.
review_body: Background:    High Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) is the best audio / video (a/v) digital interface ever made. It achieves superb a/v performance at a reasonable cost compared with other digital cables such as Toslink (Toshiba Link) & S/PDIF (Sony / Philips Digital InterFace). The HDMI standard / version is also improving with time & this digital interface is here to stay for a very long time to come.    I'm tired of reading about 1's & 0's digital theory that's been beaten to death by consumers & critics alike. There are many things that may be theoretically correct but practically it proves out to be otherwise. In my experience, the quality of materials used / implemented does have an impact on performance with all digital cables & components. It comes down to one's budget, expectations & understanding of electronics.    Over the years, I have tried / used many branded & non-branded HDMI cables. The following are a few branded HDMI cables that I currently use in my a/v system:    1) Monster MC 1000HD, priced @ USD59/2m [[ASIN:B000UF3FT8 Monster MC 1000HD-2M Ultra-High Speed HDTV HDMI Cable (2 meters)]],  2) Pangea Audio HD-24PC, priced @ USD70/2m [[ASIN:B0031Y5I68 Pangea Audio HD-24PC HDMI Cable 4% Silver Plated (2 Meter)]],  3) AudioQuest X Cable, priced @ USD30/6.5ft [[ASIN:B00092HOCQ AudioQuest HDMI X cable - HDMI plugs 2m (6.56') braided cable]] &  4) Mediabridge Ultra Series, priced @ USD10/6ft [[ASIN:B0019EHU8G Mediabridge Ultra Series - High Speed HDMI Cable with Ethernet - Category 2 Certified - Supports 3D & Audio Return Channel [Latest HDMI Version Available] - (6 Feet)]].    I've used the above V1.4 HDMI cables, of different lengths, with LaCie LaCinema Media Player, Pioneer DVD Player, Oppo Bluray Player, HD Cable Box along with a 17in Dell LCD TV, 32in Panasonic LCD TV, 42in Panasonic Plasma & a 50in Panasonic Plasma TV.    Performance & rating:    Here's my take on the HDMI cables listed above:    1) Pangea Audio HD-24PC priced @ USD70/2m:Rating: 5 Stars.    The good: Build quality is second to none. The cable will surely outlive the components it's being used with. Impeccable black level performance & I'm truly floored using this HDMI on a 50in Panasonic Plasma TV. It truly stands out with it's price to performance ratio. It's a real bargain because of the good discount & free shipping in Amazon.    The not so good: Thick & a lil' stiff just like their power cables, so not very ideal for flush wall mounted displays. Needs ample space behind the TV for cable management.    2) AudioQuest X Cable priced @ USD30/6.5ft:    Rating: 5 Stars.    The good: Very good build quality. A lil' thinner & so easier to handle than the Pangea Audio HDMI. Great performance for large screen displays. Just a tad less impressive with black level performance than the Pangea Audio HDMI. It's a very good purchase especially at the heavily discounted price & free shipping in Amazon. It w'd be hard to find a HDMI cable at this price that can beat the X Cable for build quality & performance.    The not so good: Nothing at all. Really, it's that impressive for the current listed price.    3) Mediabridge Ultra Series priced @ USD10/6ft:    Rating: 4 Stars.    The good: For the price, one of the best budget HDMIs out there. Very good for small screen displays & surely an upgrade to really cheap freebies that we get with most Bluray players, DVD players, Cable box etc.    The not so good: Cheap build quality when compared to the other HDMI cables that I have. Not recommended with displays larger than 40in as picture quality is a tad less crisp when compared to the other HDMI cables that I have in my system.    4) Monster MC 1000HD, priced @ USD59/2m:    Rating: 3 Stars.    The good: Good build quality, better than the Mediabridge HDMI but falls short in aesthetics & build quality when compared with Pangea Audio & AudioQuest HDMI. Performance is just as good as the AudioQuest HDMI cable.    The not so good: At half the cost the AudioQuest HDMI, with the heavy discount & better build quality, is a better buy / bargain. It's time for Monster to offer better discount on all their cables.    Conclusion:    For display screen sizes below 40in, sources less than 1080p & cable lengths below 2m, a $10/m HDMI is just as good / effective as a $100/m & above HDMI cable. If U are unhappy with a $10/m HDMI only then sh'd U try something a lil' more expensive than that.    For display screen sizes above 40in, the more robustly made Pangea & AudioQuest HDMI cables did make a difference in my system. The blacks were a lil' more well defined. The overall picture quality was a tad smoother, deeper & clearer.    There are some brands of HDMI that are priced @ $100/m & above. At that level, one gets to buy exotic HDMI jewelry. It surely will have great build, finish, EMI / RFI shielding etc but it does not necessarily improve performance under the above conditions of screen size, source strength & cable length. It's surely not for everyone.    The savings made on a `value for money' HDMI cable can be used to buy something else in the a/v system that can actually make a visible & audible difference, such as power cords, power conditioners, interconnects etc, just to name a few components that truly matter to me.     In my experience, Silver is surely the best conductor for a/v, closely followed by Copper. I also prefer to use solid core cables over stranded cables & Silver plating over Gold plating wherever circumstance & budget permit. Gold & Platinum plating is used only because they are noble metals & do not easily corrode (oxidize) like Copper & Silver. Brass is cheap & is 360 percent less conductive than Copper. I'm surprised to see Gold plated Brass connectors still being used in most pro a/v systems & cables including HDMI. I'm sure the use of Brass is the most effective way to keep cable costs low.    The Pangea Audio HDMI uses the best materials amongst all the HDMIs I've used & listed above. It uses 24AWG (American Wire Gauge) Silver plated solid Copper conductors. Unfortunately, it's terminated with Gold plated Brass connectors. I'm yet to get hold of a HDMI that meets all my expectations & yet be priced sensibly. In a/v U get what U pay for, even then, there is a level after which U reach a point of diminishing returns. That's were good homework / research really helps. Knowing were to draw that line is the key point in this hobby.    If the HDMI requirement is for a screen size above 40in, the source is full HD (1080p) & the cable length requirement is above 2m, then I'd recommend that one tries both - the cheap Mediabridge HDMI & a better grade HDMI from Pangea or Audioquest. Amazon has a very good return policy, so one c'd return the less impressive cable within 30 days of purchase. What more can one ask for?    Just my $0.02.    Brgds.

product_title: Sanyo NEW 1500 eneloop AA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries
review_body: The good:    1) Made in Japan.  2) Pre-charged & ready to use.  3) Rechargeable 1500X (X = times / cycles). I'm happy with just 500X.    The not so good:    1) 2000 mAh. That's not enough juice to provide stamina for power hungry devices.    Background:    For over 4yrs now, I've been using the 'made in Japan', Low Self Discharge (LSD) AA & AAA rechargeable batteries from Sanyo called Eneloop & Eneloop 1500. I use them with all the remote controls & electronic devices / gadgets that I have. I have over a dozen pairs of the Sanyo Eneloop batteries & I like to keep them organized. I have them all marked / labeled in pairs so that I don't mix the batteries when I'm charging them. The plain white color of the Sanyo Eneloop is a plus point here.     For remote controls, the Eneloops are perfect. A single charge c'd stay for more than a year. No complaints. It's when I use the Eneloops with the Canon PowerShot A590IS [[ASIN:B0011ZCDKS Canon PowerShot A590IS 8MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom]] that I wish that these batteries had a lil' more juice in them. I c'd barely touch an average of 200 shots with a single charge. That's when I gave the Sanyo Eneloop XX a try & I'm impressed with it. The milliampere-hour (mAh), a measurement of the electric charge transferred by a steady current of one Ampere for one hour (check Google for more detailed explanation), in the new Sanyo Eneloop XX has been upped to 2500 mAh. This increase of 500 mAh really shows an improvement in my compact camera's performance. I've already taken over 400 shots with the first charge & I'm still counting. Even the refresh time between shots have reduced a bit.    Conclusion:    Just a few yrs ago, the Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) used to be priced @ USD20 / 4pcs. It's now selling for about USD10 / 4pcs on Amazon & is very good value for money [[ASIN:B000IV2WAW SANYO eneloop 4 Pack AA NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries]]. The newer Sanyo Eneloop 1500 (rechargeable 1500X), with no performance advantage over the original Eneloop, is priced @ about USD15 / 4pcs. I got the Sanyo Eneloop XX (rechargeable 500X) from B&H, NYC @ USD20 / 4pcs [[ASIN:B004DW7S06 Sanyo Eneloop AA NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries - new 2500 mAh --eneloop xx -- 1 pack of 4 batteries - Limited Quantity]].    I'm sure the prices will eventually come down with more competition & with newer models getting released every year. For now, the Sanyo Eneloop XX sh'd only be considered for power hungry devices such as compact cameras & remote controlled toys. For everything else, the original Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) is still a very good purchase & has not run out of juice just yet.    I find 1500X a lil' over exaggerated. Even if I charge a pair of Sanyo Eneloop XXs every week, 500X will last me over 9yrs. I know I'll replace / upgrade these batteries in about 5yrs or so with whatever c'd be the latest & greatest in LSD rechargeable battery technology then. For 2000 mAh LSD rechargeable batteries, I'd stick with the original Sanyo Eneloop (rechargeable 1000X) & save some bucks.    For best results, I'm using the Sanyo Eneloop batteries with La Crosse Technology BC-700 power battery charger [[ASIN:B000RSOV50 La Crosse Technology BC-700 Alpha Power Battery Charger]].    Just my $0.02.    Brgds.

product_title: FINIGO 3.5mm In-Ear Stereo Earphones w/ On-off & Mic For Apple iPhone 6 / 6 Plus / 5 / 5S /5C, HTC One (E8), One (M8), Samsung Galaxy S5 Android Smartphone
review_body:
I was standing in line to buy the first generation iPod Touch the day it was released, and the first thing I did after taking it out of the package was log into Amazon to order upgraded headphones. I settled on a mid-priced pair of Etymotic Research and immediately fell in love. So much so that I order a pair twice as expensive (and more than the Touch) so I could have an \\"at home\\" pair and a pair for \\"on the go\\". Flash forward to today, and both pair of ER headphones have failed. They've been coddled about as much as you could expect; always stored in their pouch. Sad.

Enter these Bose IE2 phones. After reading a number of positive user experiences (thanks guys!), I decided to try them. I've never been a big fan of the Bose hype, but I have to admit, I really like these phones. They're comfortable, they don't create any \\"compression\\" issues associated with other in-ear phones (I'll enjoy these in the air), and they practically disappear after you put them on. I've also been able to listen at substantially lower volume, which could be a product of the sensitivity difference (technical stuff).

I'm not nearly as blown away by the sound quality as I was with my Etymotic Research ER4P, make no mistake. The benefits of not having the silicone buds jammed in my head will undoubtedly be balanced with the ear fatigue of a less refined sound. Oh well.

Lastly, one of the big advantages to true in-ear phones is their passive noise cancellation. Insert them properly, and the noise of daily life goes from a \\"10\\" to a \\"2\\". These Bose phones offer no such cancellation. Again, oh well.

For the money, I can recommend them. If you've enjoyed really great in-ear phones, you're going to have to take the good with the bad...

product_title: Harman Kardon SB16 Soundbar and Wireless 100 Watt Subwoofer (Black)
review_headline: Bless your neighbors with your TV soundtrack
review_body:
Wow. The box was much bigger than I expected. The FedEx guy said, \\"You really plan to rock out your little house?\\" Yes, I do. Yes, I do. Took two people to carry it. But once I got it out of the box and hooked it up, it really doesn't take up much visual space at all. Woofer in the corner between the sofas with a plant on it (happy plant!) and soundbar just under the TV. The selling point for this is the lack of wires and hassle. It really is pretty simple. There are wires for power, but the woofer is wireless, getting it's signal from the soundbar.

So this morning I tried turning it up to full volume to see how loud it goes... one of my kids ran out of the living room covering her ears, and another came out of her room rubbing her eyes--woke her up. I turned it down... I try to be a good mom.

I plugged it into the TV first, and there was all kinds of static and distortion and the TV was still using it's own speakers. I couldn't fix it until I plugged it right into the DVD player. Suddenly it had excellent sound. The woofer picks up the bass perfectly, shakes the floor. It can be adjusted to pick up more of the higher range sounds, too, so it really blends with the soundbar.

This is really quality sound... not one of those systems that just picks up bass and thumps and has a tinny range beyond that... no, this is a truly excellent, full, well-balanced sound. I sing in church and I have a pretty opinionated ear, so...

I'm not totally sold on the surround-sound feature. There's a sense of sound moving from one point to another, but the soundbar just isn't big enough to make you feel like, say, something is flying from one side of the room to the other. Maybe if you had the soundbar right behind you and sat dead center. That would work.

Still, there is plenty of volume, excellent sound (when it's plugged into the DVD player). This gave me the bright idea to hook the speakers up to my computer and share my Pandora selection with my neighbors. They play xxx-rated music for my kids to hear in the backyard, so I thought maybe I could exact my revenge by playing some Bluegrass Gospel or something for them. For some reason when the speakers were plugged into the computer, there was alot of high range white noise. There's no Hz adjustment anywhere on the speakers, so I couldn't fix it. The manual says to adjust the track, but that didn't help, just muffled all sound. My other external computer speakers have no problem with white noise. Don't know what that was about. I think the wireless signal is getting mixed up with my computer's wireless internet and wireless keyboard and mouse. Internet is working pretty slowly too. Changing the wireless channel doesn't fix the problem. But anyway, it was plenty loud and got the neighbors to come out and look around. I have no idea what they were saying--couldn't hear them over the music. I won't use these speakers on my computer much because the white noise is annoying, and it doesn't have that problem with the DVD player. But now I have a weapon to protect my kids when the neighbors turn on their sick music.

I also played some Rossini (opera). Beautiful!!! Our pet cat didn't like it--he ran away. I think cats sort of sing opera when they want to fight, and I had it pretty loud. He felt threatened. Such feeling and depth coming from the speakers!

If you can get the right connection (I'm going to continue tinkering with the computer connection or get my computer and TV in one... figure something out) you'll have excellent sound from this system. If you're really particular about surround sound, you should get a different system and deal with the wires and separate speaker locations. If you have tons of wireless gadgets all over, you might have a problem. But this inconspicuous system will still allow your house to look like a home, while boosting your TV sound and getting you rightinto the action. The downside: your neighbors and cats will not love you. Maybe that's okay.ats will not love you. Maybe that's okay.

review_headline: As near to perfect as possible
review_body: I am anxiously awaiting the delivery next week of my second Walkman. The first, a black 16GB, was purchased one year ago and still looks and runs like brand new out of the box. The newer one will be a black 8GB and it will be adequate for my song volume. I agree 1000% with the favorable reviews on Amazon...honestly have not had problem one over the past year. Keys to my success include not touching the unit until I had read the mfgr. comments and reviews that experienced problems, attacking the software with an open mind, babying the unit from day one but not afraid to take it everywhere I go (taking care to ALWAYS protect it from damage). Gave up on screen protectors after the first couple of months (way too much hassle for my liking). Instead I purchased the full unit leather case from TUFLUV on Amazon...a beautiful product that's perfectly engineered for \\"S\\" units and supplies 100% protection to screen and all other parts of the unit. The only hazard it may not protect against is water. The case adds very little bulk, looks great and allows full access to all buttons and functions while doing its job. I also use the $20 white silicone case for less protection but slimmer profile when there is no danger lurking. If the full cover case is this gal's winter coat, the silicone case is her bikini for when she feels a little frisky.    Prior to purchasing the first unit I had the same angst, doubts, questions, etc. as the most paranoid reviewers. Yet here I am a year later buying another Sony \\"S\\" and not having a single doubt about the first or second decision. I currently have 900 songs and have created dozens of \\"playlists\\" to cover every mood, every time of day every day of week (the playlist feature is the secret to-die-for feature and probably the simplest and most efficient feature versus any MP3)! Don't hesitate to try the \\"S\\" units (but not the \\"E\\" units)! FYI I'm an age 67 \\"old fart\\" who loves his music, especially anything Gaither, anything Eagles and anything 50's, 60's and 70's country. Seniors will really appreciate the \\"S\\" units because they're exactly like the quality and reliability trusted from Sony for several decades. Also, thanks Amazon for years of great service and Marketplace.

product_title: Onkyo TX - NR609 7.2 Channel Network THX Certified A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: So far, I am really enjoying my TX-NR609. I upgraded from an old Technics 5.1 receiver that was over 10 years old and didn't have any of the new video formats for switching. The on screen display (OSD) is great - I really enjoy it for streaming audio and for USB connections such as our iPods. Though the OSD wasn't working originally when I got the system for USB and had to do a factory reset (thanks to Onkyo support for walking me through and helping with my problem). I only have my HDMI sources hooked into it so far and have not played..err..tested the video upconversion. The standby HDMI passthrough works most of the time with my DirecTV DVR. I have had motion video and no audio or audio and a static image on my screen. I did a firmware update (side note - it would be nice to know how to find current firmware loaded to know if there is an update) and it has helped some, but will have that problem every once in a while. My \\"fix\\" is to scroll through the format types of the DVR and that will re-sync the HDMI. Now onto the audio. Currently I am only using two Technics SB-LX90 tower speakers - 3 way with 15\\" woofers - and no other speakers (the receiver was the first part of my audio system remodel). The quality and clarity of the sound is as good or better than what I was used to with my old receiver. Though, I have noticed that I don't have as much thumping bass with the Onkyo as I did with the Technics - with 15s I used to shake the house and not need a separate sub, but no shaky-shaky now. Bass and Treble adjustments were a little hard to find especially compared to what I was used to with having a knob on the front panel. All in all, I'm happy with the Onkyo so far. Once I get a full surround system, I'll update my review on total sound quality.
