product_title: Yamaha EPH-30 In-Ear Headphones
review_body: I've always been the one friend who has to have inner-ear earphones. When people ask if they could borrow my earphones, I would tell them that they are inner-ear and they would ask someone else. I've gone from Shure, Sony, Ultimate Ears, and many other inner-ear earphone models. Although I love the products of these companies, the $100+ price tag is a bit discouraging especially when the earphones break down. That is when I came across these very affordable Yamaha EPH-30BL earphones.     I was a bit skeptical at the price. Does the price correlate to the quality of the earphones? When I received the product, the answer is both yes and no.     Yes:  - The package came in a very compact vacuum sealed plastic package. It comes with 3 different sized ear pieces (small, medium - default, large). I believe the medium is the universal size and I didn't have any problem or discomfort when putting them in my ears. However, ears do come in different sizes, hence, the two additional sized ear pieces.   - A lot of the reviews dislike the length of the left and right side of the earphones. The right side is longer than the left. I actually like this design. To the people who are unfamiliar with this design may have the right side wire dangle under their chin. I actually wrap the longer right side over the back of my neck. So now instead of having two potential wires get caught on my bag strap or jacket buttons, there's only one that I have to worry about.   - Because the price is so affordable, I won't feel as bad replacing these than something that cost me $100-$500. I was devastated when my other in-ears faltered. However, because these are really decently priced, I won't mind purchasing another pair, maybe 2 or 3.   - The actual sound is very clear, but a little fine tuning is required. (will explain in the \\"No\\" section).     No:  - Although the package did come in a very compact package, it only came with custom foam, pre-cut so the ear phones. No carrying case like other expensive ear-phones do. You'll have to be very careful during travel.   - The width of the wires do seem a little thin. I am very careful with all my ear-phones, but it is inevitable that they will eventually break. Because I only got these, I have yet to experience any mishaps. If they do break, I will definitely take up their warranty and try to get them replaced. I will update this review if that ever happens and my experience with their customer service.   - Sound. EXTREMELY BASS HEAVY. Because I am on the go a lot, I have an iPod shuffle with me. Something simple so I can listen to music and easily go to the next track if I want to with a push of a button. Unfortunately, the shuffle does not have an on-screen navigation system to the equalizer. I had to actually go within my iTunes playlist and change each song's EQ manually, which was a bit annoying. However, when I lower the bass, the bass is almost not present. So it's either no bass or a lot of bass. Nothing in the middle, which is a little disappointing.     Overall, the product is great so far. I've used them for a week and nothing bad yet other than it being bass heavy. I would buy this to temporarily replace higher end products.

product_title: Ocelot Banana Plugs, 24k Gold Plated Connectors, Open Screw Type, 12 Pair
review_body: I'm no AV expert, so I really have nothing to compare these banana plugs to.  However, they worked completely as advertised for my purposes: plugging my speaker wire into my amp without worrying about unscrewing/screwing in the amp posts.  Seriously, these are really easy to use, and for the price I don't see how mid-low end system owners would buy anything else.  For me, THX certified (or whatever other bells and whistles are advertised) plugs would be a complete waste of money.    FYI, these have 2 ways of installing wire.  There's a hole bored through the base as well as through the side of the plug itself.  So you can a) thread the wire through the plug, then screw the base in, locking the wire in place, or b) thread the wire through the base, then through the plug and screw the base in.    One reviewer complained of the tips of the plugs falling off.  The tips do screw out, but if they're loose, they do screw back on.    These are slightly cheaper in construction - meaning they're not insulated, and don't have the 'polish' that other brands might have (-1 star for that).  Otherwise, just what I wanted.

product_title: LAVA HD-2805 UHF/VHF Outdoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: So far, so good. I like thie one best.
review_body:
I just purchased the Lava 2805. This one seems to be the best so far. It gets all VHF (low and high) and UHF. Unfortunately, I don't get Fox la on channel 11-1 and My 13 on 13-1. First I started with the DB4. It got only 3 UHF channels. Then the Clearstream 5 that said VHF and UHF, but only got 2 channels on HIGH VHF. Today I installed the Lava and got almost everything. I will call the company tomorrow to see if purchasing an amplifier will help pull in FOX. My zip is 91040 and channel degrees are all between 86 degrees and 90 degrees. And all the transformers sit on the same mountain approximately 14.5 miles away at 1750 to 1875 elevation. By the way, this is on a single story house using a 10 ft mask.

I will also need to split the signal between multiple tv's. Though it has a dual output for 2 tv's, I tried splitting one of those outputs and the signal reduced over 50%.

I do feel this is an EXCELLENT antenna for the money.

review_body:

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body:
This is a review from someone who has never used and iPod Touch until this particular item. I purchased the 32GB 4th generation iPod Touch as a Christmas gift for my wife. She absolutely loves it and says it's pretty much the best Christmas present ever. We don't any iPhones or iPods aside from this one and I'm very impressed by it. Fortunately, I have been able to sneak some use out of it to write this review.

I am a big fan of the Android OS, but my Android device is on the older side (HTC G1) so it's not really much competition for this brand new iPod. First of all this thing is so slim. It's about 40% of the thickness of my old G1. The touchscreen is very responsive and the resolution on the display is amazing. The iPod's software is very fast, and there is almost no waiting for Apps to load up. As everyone knows, Apple's App store is loaded with thousands of Apps that pretty much do everything. My wife has found plenty to consume her time and to keep her off my case. I haven't used the camera much myself but the picture quality seems decent enough for posting pictures to Facebook and YouTube videos. About the only that I've heard my wife complain about is that it doesn't have 3G, so she can't check in on Foursquare unless she's somewhere that has WiFi.

In the short time that the iPod Touch has been in our family we have really been wowed by all it's capabilities and uses. I doubt that it will switch me from being an Android user but it just might.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa e260 4 GB MP3 Player with SD Expansion Slot
review_body:
This is my second SanDisk Sansa. Originally I owned the e250, 2GB Model. This little MP3 player is amazing. I've used it daily for long periods of time, plugged it into a transmitter for long road trips, used it on the porch, exercising, everywhere. My first one finally died about a month ago and I thought, \\"oh well, I won't need to replace it; my phone plays mp3's\\". I missed it within a day of its death.

If you are looking for a good, solid performing mp3 player, this is the one you want. I used my original sansa so much I wore the writing off the buttons. I have looked at many different mp3 players but SanDisk has a real winner here. The lanyard is useful, but this is player you'll want a good case for. The case that comes with the sansa leaves a lot to be desired (it's a basic slipcover, more for storage than for use of the device). The backlight is bright and I highly recommend toning it down a bit for longer battery life. Moving mp3s to the device is as simple as using a flash drive; drag and drop works perfectly.

The best part about the player in my opinion is that it has physical buttons. If you're using it in your pocket (which I do often) it is wonderful to be able to simply press the proper button to pause it. Another fantastic feature is the hold button. If you're listening to a particularly long file (i.e. audiobooks that are consolidated into a single file instead of broken down by chapters) and want to make sure you don't accidentally start the file over, the hold function is a lifesaver. Between the Sansa e200 series mp3 players and many others on the market, this one outperforms any that I looked at for ease of use, features, and size.

All in all, this is one of the best mp3 players you can find for a decent price that has all the functionality you could want without paying a small fortune for it.

product_title: NuForce - uDAC2-HP - USB / DAC - Headphone Amp - Black
review_body: I bought a pair of Audio-Technica ATH-m50s headphones(highly recommended by the way)[[ASIN:B000ULAP4U Audio-Technica ATH-M50S Studio Monitor Headphones]] in December. My iPod classic powered them well enough, but I was hoping to get a little more clarity out of my Inspiron 15R[[ASIN:B004K1EQO6 Dell Inspiron 15R 1198MRB 15.6-Inch Laptop (Mars Black)]]. I'd intitially disabled the SRS Premium Sound which gave some noticeable improvement, but I eventually wanted something to give me that extra clarity. The Nuforce Udac2-HP did exactly that. I especially noticed an improvement in the bass section of my music, and the drums came across more crisply.    For most, I don't think it blows away the sound coming from an iPod classic, but I am a critical listener so I appreciate the difference. Listening to Ben Folds sigh on \\"Brick\\" or hearing the metronome at the beginning of Green Day's \\"Time of Your Life\\" always brings a smile to my face.     NOTE: I'd read a lot from some guy on the internet who has some personal vendetta against the udac2, complaining that it clips your music and has too high of a jack impededence etc. etc. and basically that this was somehow a bad product. I have not had any clipping, even on my rock and pop tracks and the analog pot(ie volume changer) balances my channels just fine except at unlistenably quiet levels. Get this item if you are looking to improve your laptop audio to your headphones like I was, I would definitely buy it over again, and would definitely recommend it to a friend. The only tip I would give is to make sure you select Nuforce online as your amazon seller, not Kraft street audio or some other marketplace dealer. The included usb cable is maybe six or seven inches, about the perfect size for my setup.

product_title: Powermat Pmr-ppc4 Dual 1200 Rechargeable Backup Battery
review_headline: Cheaply made and flat out doesn't work
review_body: I'll give you some context and try to avoid ranting too much, but first let me spoil the punchline.  My experience with this was terrible; DON'T BUY IT.    I found myself at Kohl's with $20 in coupons to burn and found this thing.  I just bought a Thunderbolt which is a power hog.  We also have an iPod (4th G), and iPad (1), and several other devices with micro-USB charging.  This is supposed to support them all.  I walked out of Kohl's after spending $18 -- before coupon it was $38 -- thinking I got an absolute steal.    Problem is IT DOES NOT WORK AT ALL.    First you charge the device itself so that you can then give that power to other devices.  This worked fine.  They give you a little USB to micro-USB patch cable so you can charge with a computer, or with one of your own AC-USB adapters devices all come with now.  So far so good.    Then I try to charge my iPad.  Well, the Apple-based charger does not extend very far out of this thing, so I couldn't plug it in all the way and simply could not get the iPad to connect and start charging.  I do have a shell on the iPad and I thought it was creating the problem (this would be bad enough, don't we all know you have to account for shells and cases by now?).  So I took the case off, still won't plug in far enough.  So I grabbed our iPod without case and tried, same thing.    So at this point I'm thinking for $18 I'm down to a micro-USB charging backup only.  I'm ticked but it's still worth it.  So I have it all charged up, then I run out of battery on my Thunderbolt while on the road.  No problem, I have this new thing.  It did not charge it at all after about 10 minutes.  So I go home thinking I just need to give it more time.  I come back to the phone hours later and it is completely dead!  It had 10% battery before, now it's dead.    So it's going back to Kohl's, as it does absolutely nothing of what it says.  A couple other warning signs: it has very cheap material and construction.  It's nice looking despite those things -- proverbial lipstick on a pig.  But once you handle it and plug it in you can feel the cheapness.  As if the fact that it's getting spit out the bargain rack at Kohl's wasn't a good enough sign, take my word for it.  Unless I got my hands on a defective unit (I doubt it, an Amazon reviewer of the black model said exactly the same), this is slickly packaged thievery.  Shame on Powermat and any retailer still trying to get money for it.

product_title: Kaito KA1103 Worldband Radio
review_headline: Nice radio, for the price its tough to beat.
review_body: I recently bought this little radio after reading many positive reviews and I must say that for the price, the performance is tough to beat! I have found good ( not great ) reception on am. Not a huge surprise given the small size of the radio, limiting the size of the internal am ferrite bar antenna. FM however has been a pleasure, especially when using headphones! ( stereo ). Shortwave and SSB (single side band) is where this radio impresses me. I have logged radio Cuba, China and Russian broadcasts and many hams using the whip antenna! Using my PAR endfed outdoor antenna this thing is great! No front end overload at all. Strictly on performance I find this little gem to be more sensitive than my brand new Sangean 909x! Hard to imagine all this for about $90.00! The controls are somewhat unconventional and I can see how some dock it points for these design choices. The radio isn't perfect, a dedicated volume control would be a big plus. The pseudo analog dial is neither a plus nor a minus for me. It seems that some like it and others don't. In my opinion it is a very slight plus. It is nice to be able to glance down and get a quick 'visual' on my band location.  Personally it takes a little getting used to, but in no way do these design features diminishes its value when performance and price are factored in. The Radio was packaged very well and arrived in great condition. It included everything I would expect, AC adapter, earbuds and a longish 25' or so sw antenna. What surprised me was the inclusion of rechargeable batteries at this price point, a nice touch! The one issue I have had is with the rear stand. It is not real sturdy to begin with and bumping it onto a carpeted floor broke the tabs off of it.... ugh. In their defense I e-mailed them yesterday and received a reply today asking for my mailing information, they will be send a replacement! So far my experience has been a good one! For the price, the Kaito KA 1103 is hard to beat.

product_title: Sony Dash Personal Internet Viewer
review_headline: Sony Dash, Y U No Work!?
review_body: For those of you on the fence about this product, DO NOT PURCHASE IT.    I got this thing assuming it would be a fancy alarm clock.  Yeah, it's got some cool additional features, and can display internet material and play music, view photos, and maybe some other fancy things.  However, I apparently made the biggest mistake of all when I forgot the golden rule of products: Assuming that when I bought it and turned it on, that it would work. That, apparently, is too much to ask.      When I got the Dash and turned it on, it asked me to set the time zone, and then connect to a network before forcing me to update it. Then it rebooted, and didn't actually update, so I was taken to a screen with the menu choices of A) Returning to normal function, which would then restart it and take me back to the first screen and tell me that I HAD to reboot it (yes, an awesome infinite loop), or B) Take me to a page with a grayed out button to install the update (not an infinite loop, just a ridiculous dead end), or C) Restore factory settings, and once again, take me back to the first page FORCING me to update it, and leading to yet another infinite loop.    I will be calling Sony's support line tomorrow, as they are closed at the moment. But yes, believe it. This product doesn't work, out of the box. Simply amazing. Sony has definitely lost a customer forever.

product_title: Bear Motion 4gb Mp3 Multi Media Player with 2.8 Inch Touch Screen and 2.0 Mega Pixel Camera
review_body: I was worried when I ordered this that it wouldn't function correctly when I first opened it because of some of the other reviews, but it works just fine.  I bought this media player because I wanted to be able to browse through the songs like you can on an Ipod, but when I got the music on and I tested it, I figured out that although it shows you what song is playing you may not browse though the songs and select a particular song that you would like to listen to. Another thing that bothered me was that you can't use your fingers on the touch screen. You have to use the stylus on the touch screen, and by the way it does not a have a place to store the stylus on the device so you have to carry it around with you. Even though it says that the device is compatible with  macs, when I put the driver in it wouldn't work correctly. Besides that, the device itself is compatible with my mac, but it's very confusing to add songs videos and pictures, because the company didn't create any software similar to itunes that would organize this process. It has an ebook feature, but it only accepts TXT ebooks which is annoying because most ebooks come in PDF. You also can't turn pages on the ebooks, so it's not like an actual book. The reason why I rated the player a 4, is because it does everything it's supposed to do. It has a camera that also shoots video, and you can review the videos and photos you took on the device. The music plays clearly. There are a few games that you can play, it has a notebook, a calendar, a recorder, a stopwatch and a calculator. You can make changes to the system from the device. Overall, it does what it's supposed to do, but it is certainly not an Ipod.

review_headline: Increadible sound, amazing clarity, amazing bass.
review_body: I got this speaker after getting sick and tired of the static and cutting in and out on my sharper image wireless speakers. I picked this speaker up for $80 on ebay. It's a little bigger than what I wanted, but it looks good, and sounds amazing.    The pros:  Loud; I use this to listen to my stereo when I'm working on the car, or grilling on the porch, or somewhere else in my house besides my living room. I've never had to turn it up far at all, and the bass button really adds a serious bass boost. The sound is clear, the speaker is omnidirectional so you can fill a space with music and don't have to worry about which way the speaker is pointed  .  Clear; No popping of clicking in the sound. The speaker doesn't cut in and out even in front of the house, about 80ft from the transmitter.    Looks; It looks good, the blue light can be turned on or off and does add a nice touch at night.  Rain proof; Not that I sit out in the rain and listen to music, but when you use it for cookouts and parties it's good to know it can handle the elements.    Cons:    Price; it's about twice as much as some of the competitors and they give you 2 speakers.    Size, it is a bit on the big side, especially if you just want a small speaker to provide some background music.     The transmitter is always on. Not a huge deal, but my other set only turned on the transmitter when it received a audio signal.    Wish it came in black. I know everything is going the way of the ipod, but black looks and blends much better with everything than a big white speaker.    Overall, great product. Sounds like a wired speaker and fills a large area with music.

product_title: Geniatech iGrabber One Touch Video Grabber For MAC and PC, Push Button Recording

I checked the manufacturer's website for driver updates; the version on the CD was current (but I still suggest anyone buying it check first before installing).      I had to tweak a couple of settings in the iCapture software, to get the audio to come through the capture device and to set up the record quality.  Then, just select Record, give it a file name, and start grabbing video.  Nice and simple.    If you're looking for simpler to use for a non-technical person, get the Pinnacle capture for Mac.  Compared to this, Pinnacle has a lot smoother installation and operation, plus good instructions.  So why do I give this 5-stars?  Because it's about 1/3 the price, and ends up with just as good a result.  Just don't expect handholding through the installation or operation.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_body:
Ladies and gentlemen, just a few moments ago, these headphones gave up the ghost.

And I suddenly felt compelled to write a review expressing my (now) undying loyalty to this product. I've tried many other pairs of headphones in the past, but they inevitably failed under one or more of the following criteria: uncomfortable, perspiration inducing, headache inducing, easily breakable or the sound quality simply sucked. And I'm not being unrealistic, when I buy a pair of headphones I typically give them a lifespan of about a year--give or take a few months.

The Boss noise canceling headphones died a year after I bought them, one of the cups snapped off. Skull Candy made my skull sweaty. The Sennheiser's heavily dragged with their external battery unit, which also got in the way, plus they hurt my ears when I wore them with my glasses.

See, that's one thing most people can't appreciate--comfortably wearing headphones while also wearing glasses. Do you have any idea how much of a pain in the ass this is? Seriously. It really sucks. The pain is excruciating after thirty minutes, usually. A Saw movie could be made with one of the traps being Sennheiser headphones on a victim wearing prescription glasses. They could use the technique in Guantanamo as a method for extracting information. You get the idea.

Then four years ago I found this Audio-Technica (AT) set. For a meager hundred bucks I got a travel companion, a work / grad-school sanity-buddy, a battery saver. For the past four years I've had my AT headphones on about six-to-eight hours a day, every day. EVERY DAY. I sit at my desk while I work and listen to music, audiobooks, podcasts and wear my noise canceling headphones pretty much the ENTIRE time. And they have worked relentlessly well for all four years. Consider the math, five days a week, seven hours a day (let's be conservative) plus all the beatings this pair absorbed on my trips to Europe, New Zealand, etc.: 4 years x 52 weeks x 7 hours + 60hrs (buffer for weekends and local trips) = over 1,500 hours of constant use.

That number speaks for itself. They sound amazing. Feel amazing. Hold up valiantly through all the beatings they've inevitably had to shoulder.

FIVE SOLID STARS. Best $90 I've ever spent. Bought all my friends and family a pair.years x 52 weeks x 7 hours + 60hrs (buffer for weekends and local trips) = over 1,500 hours of constant use.

That number speaks for itself. They sound amazing. Feel amazing. Hold up valiantly through all the beatings they've inevitably had to shoulder.

FIVE SOLID STARS. Best $90 I've ever spent. Bought all my friends and family a pair.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16 GB Silver (6th Generation) Discontinued Model (in White Box)
review_body:
My first Apple product was a 4GB, 2nd generation nano. Loved it and it served me well for YEARS. Moved to an iPhone 3G about 2 years ago and loved it. Only gripe with the iPhone was that it was too bulky to use as an iPod when running, working in the yard, etc. I would still use my old 2nd gen Nano, but my music collection is roughly 2x the capacity it offers.

SO, let's cut to the chase: Sold my 2nd gen Nano for $50 and picked up a 6th gen, 16GB on CL for $110. LOVE IT!!! Love the clip, love the size, love the interface, love the FM radio. It's just great. I don't know if it's $190 great (retail), but it's sure as heck $110 great! Here are my responses to some of the negative feedback I've heard:

1) Form factor. If you like the old ones, there are plenty available.
2) Battery life. So far mine seems great.
3) No App Store, camera, or video playback. Are you serious?! Get a damn iPhone! Think about this, for just a second. When the Nano FIRST came out, it was designed to fill a role in the overall market. It did, and did it well. But WOW has the market changed! The fact that the new Nano doesn't have access to the app store, or a camera, or video feedback doesn't bother me at all. Would you really want to watch a video on this screen?!?!? Hahaha, that's rich. I don't like watching videos on my phone, much less the new Nano. That's what my 52\\" flat screen is for in my living room.

This is an awesome product, period. My only gripe is that the retail $ is high, but so what. Apple is run by smart people and they make a lot of $$$ for their shareholders, so good for them. If you want it, buy it. If you hate the price, find one used or wait. Highly recommend provided it fits your budget.

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Radio
review_headline: Weekly Lockups and Still Streams While OFF?
review_body: I won't replicate the excellent reviews that this radio has. It is very versatile and sounds excellent. When it's working it's fantastic.    I have almost weekly lockups that require the AC wall power supply to be pulled and then plugged back in. Then it takes another 15 minutes before the radio is ready to play again. Once it even required the encryption code for the router to be reentered. Not an easy task as it requires the characters to be entered in HEX!!! 26 two digit codes is 52 spins of the dial and a press of the main knob to enter each one. Why Logictech didn't put in something that would convert our normal plain English phrase into Hex I don't know. It makes the setup way more complicated than it needs to be.    Next I thought we had an intruder on our network. The router was blinking away early on a Sunday while all the machines in the house and shop were powered off. Just to be sure I went to each and every Internet capable device in our home and made sure they were completely off. The \\"intruder\\" went away when I unplugged the Squeezebox. The radio had been shut off with just it's clock display showing. Obviously it was active on the network either streaming or downloading something.    While it certainly has some bugs I won't return it. It's a product that I really enjoy. But if you purchase one be aware that the firmware still needs some work. product_title: Onkyo TX - NR609 7.2 Channel Network THX Certified A/V Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great mid-range AV Receiver with more than most others
review_body: I upgraded from an old non-HDMI Yamaha HTR-5850.    I looked at the following:  - [[ASIN:B003BIFOL8 Onkyo TX-SR608]]  - [[ASIN:B003IPC5FW Denon AVR-1911]]  - [[ASIN:B0039XQQX0 Pioneer VSX-1020-K]]  - [[ASIN:B004M8RPBI Pioneer VSX-1021-K]]  - [[ASIN:B003P2V52M Yamaha RX-V667]]  - A few others  - [[ASIN:B004UR487U Onkyo HT-RC360]] is also a very similar one that merits comparison, esp. with the price.    First impression:  - Box was well packaged.  - Easy to connect right out of the box.  I have a simple 5.1 set up, but even the 7.2 seems easy enough.  Plenty of space between things, except the power cord seems to be in a slightly awkward location, but definitely not a game changer or something to lose more than 5 minutes thought to.  - Plenty of ports (more on that below).  - Very nice and mostly intuitive GUI OSD.  I am one of those guys who does not read the manual unless I have to, and the only time I had to was knowing how to program in a radio station.  - Remote is just ok.  Could use a heavier feel to it and a better explanation of what things do.  I got used to it or use my iPhone remote (more on that below too).    Pros of this one:  - 6x HDMI inputs, one in front, one output.  - Network capable.  I use Pandora A LOT and it integrates nicely, but it has many other internet music capabilities.  - Nice On Screen Display (OSD) of its GUI (Graphical User Interface).  - 4K Support Via Marvell Qdeo (3840 x 2160 resolution vs 1920 x 1080, though most TVs do not support this, yet...).  - iPhone/iPad control app (give it a sec, I have more to say on this below).  - All the standard HDMI 1.4 features (HDMI stand by pass-through, 3D, Audio Return Channel).  - Powered Zone 2 audio out.  - iPhone/iPod connectivity right out of the box via your standard USB cable in the front (no need for an additional (more money) port, though one is available: [[ASIN:B0026RHPSU Onkyo UP-A1 Dock for the iPod]]).  - PC VGA In (but really, most have HDMI out now anyway).  - Optional [[ASIN:B0026RHRFQ Onkyo UP-HT1 HD Radio Tuner]].  - Superb Audio quality.  - Superb Video up-conversion.  I took an old DVD and set the output to 480i (standard definition) and let the Receiver up-convert it.  Then compared it to the output from my PS3 at 1080 as well as an old HD DVD player (lol) and a standalone DVD player with 1080 upconversion and this receiver just blew it away.  (Note: on a 50inch top of the line Sony TV.)  - DLNA (for connecting to a home media system or a PC with music).  - THX certification (just for show for me and the cool factor as I could not tell much difference).  - Of course it does Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD MA and all the other standard decoders.  - Ability to upgrade firmware via internet easily.    Cons of this one:  - No built-in HD Radio.  - No built-in AirPlay (like some Denon and the Pioneer VSX-1021-k).  - No video out for Zone 2.  - No PC control.      A few things to note:  - The iPhone remote is a bit lacking.  It does your basic things you expect it to: control the station, input, turn it on/off, change music from Pandora/DLNA/iPod connected/etc., but the volume could use some work and the ability to control bass/treble as big buttons instead of the volume is useless.  Two things I wish this had: The ability to vote for Pandora or any such interaction and the ability to fine tune the audio levels of each speaker.  Connecting it is easy and it is pretty simple to use.  Very nice bonus.    - When using the Stand-by through, you can choose \\"last used input\\", \\"a specific output\\", or \\"Auto\\".  If you change it, it powers on.  The \\"Auto\\" option can be flaky, sometimes switching to something that is off, but it after turning the thing I want it to be off then back on, it catches it.    - There is a cooling fan on the top but have yet to notice it, even in the dead silence of a scary movie, even after having the receiver going for 5-6 hours straight for a few days in a row.  Maybe it will later on.    I am very pleased with this and would(and have already) recommend this as a purchase.      Update 06/20/11:  - Added the Onkyo HT-RC360 as a comparable option.  One of the only major difference is the price and lack of THX.  Should definitely be on people's radar!  Thanks Joshua.  - A couple minor grammar things.    Since having this for a couple months now I have to say I am still quite happy with this receiver.  Here are a few updates:  - I barely notice the fan at all.  Sometimes I will get up and check to see if it is even running (out of curiosity) and can see/hear it when I am up close.  It was mentioned that cleaning this may be an issue.  Thanks Mastercard!  - HDMI Stand-By Pass-Through is not a problem.  The \\"Auto\\" works pretty well with only 3 or 4 times in the past couple months it has been finicky, in which case I whip out my iPhone or the remote to change it.  - The iPhone app is quite basic but I like it.  I can control Pandora, the input, and the volume, which is all anyone really needs.  - On Android you can use a DLNA player such as 2Player and select this receiver as the target to stream music.  Thanks George!  - Sound quality and video quality are still going strong / well.

product_title: AmazonBasics Universal Fixed TV Wall Mount for 26- to 50-Inch Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: AmazonBasics Fixed Mount for 26 to 50-inch TVs - Functional Mount, But Review Your Options
review_body:
The [[ASIN:B002TLTE7I AmazonBasics Universal Fixed TV Wall Mount for 26 to 50-inch Displays]] is a good basic universal mount. Some preparation is required for the installation. It is meant to be used for setups where the TV is close to the wall. If you don't need to tilt or turn your screen, this is an OK option. But given the product's limitations, alternatives are available that are a better value.

PROS:
++ Supports medium to larger sized TV's from 26 to 50 inches
++ Relatively quick and simple installation (1 to 2 hours)
++ Simple compact design is functional
++ Designed for low-profile picture mounting
++ Nice assortment of included screws and anchors for wood or masonry wall mounting
++ Weight rating up to 200 pounds, sufficient for most large flat panel TVs
++ Frustration free packaging
++ 1 year warrantee

CONS:
-- Not designed for adjusting viewing angles
-- Low clearance limits room for cable connections; you should connect your cables before mounting, or if you are handy you can increase clearance with custom spacers
-- Alternatives provide more versatility and features at a better value

ALTERNATIVES:
~~ Alternative low profile mounts like the [[ASIN:B002TZ4CRG VideoSecu Low Profile Ultra Slim Wall Mount for 26-46 inch TVs]] provide similar features for less
~~ Cable mounts like the [[ASIN:B003FVJ5UC Telehook TH-400-LED Slim Wire TV Mount]] make dismounting and remounting easier; however, it does have a lower weight rating
~~ Tilt mounts like the [[ASIN:B002TLTE6Y AmazonBasics Universal Tilt TV Wall Mount for 34 to 65-Inch Displays]] allow for easier adjustment of viewing angles

INSTALLATION

Installation difficulty varies depending on your mounting surface. The basic steps are: prepare the surface, screw in the wall plate, attach the mounting arms to your TV, mount the TV on the wall plate and lock it into place. The videos on the Amazon product page are very helpful. Installation of a 32 inch TV took me an hour working alone. Most of that time was spent installing the wall plate.

Though much is provided, you may still need additional tools. The manual lists the requirements as an electric drill, a 3mm drill bit (for wood), a 12mm drill bit (for masonry), a hammer, a pencil and a Philips screwdriver.

The included stud-finder allows you to find a good place to install the wall plate, while the bubble level helps you keep it level. Tools such as an Allen key and a hex wrench are also supplied. There were also plenty of extra parts, including bolts, fasteners and extension arms.

The vertical arms can also be augmented with extensions to improve the clearance and stability. This is most important for larger TVs. Spacers are provided to adjust for screens with recessed backs. Some people may be able to lift their TVs onto the wall mount on their own, but many will need a helper for heavier TVs.

Connect your cables to the back of your TV before mounting. Moving cables afterwards will require you to dismount. The TV can slide horizontally till you lock it into place. Locking the TV to the wall mount requires a locking latch that isn't provided. Your TV viewing angle may be limited by the fixed mount. If this is an issue, look into the alternatives that provide tilt and pan functionality.

CONCLUSION

This product will work as advertised. But tilt or articulating mounts may be a better fit for some TVs. And there are similar mounts that are more affordable. Explore the alternatives. product_title: CyberPower Intelligent LCD Series UPS  Mini-Tower
review_body: I purchased this CyberPower UPS to replace the smaller capacity battery UPS unit(APC 450VA Back-UPS (BE450G)) for my main PC (I have 2 of these smaller APC brand UPS units. 1 for the other PC and 1 for my home theater system where they work as intended with much smaller power load needs). The APC unit would only run for about 2 minutes on the main computer, during which time you get a warning siren, then they just stop as the battery runs low. This is OK to just shut down the system if you are sitting at the computer when the power fails. My main computer runs about 10-14 hours a day so this unit gets a real workout. This CyberPower UPS unit has a USB cable that runs to the PC so you can see the current UPS system status(battery charge level etc) as well as review any current/past power interruptions from your PC monitor. The screen show a history of 3 past power conditions: 1-Power outages, 2-Under voltage, 3-Over voltage conditions in 1 of 4 time frames: Last week, 4 weeks, 12 weeks and 24 weeks. From this screen you can set the UPS to put your computer into either 'turn off' or 'hibernate' mode(your choice) when the battery gets low. There is also a functional front panel display. On my system I have a 'custom built' computer with 600w PSU, dual core AMD 7850 CPU, 4 GByte Memory, 2 CD/DVD burners and 4 Hitachi 1Tbyte HDDs, a Samsung SyncMaster 2494 24\\" widescreen 1080p monitor and eVGA GeForce GT 240 GPU on the Battery UPS side. With this power load I get about 18 minutes of run time. I put my printer, 10 external HD drives and other external products on the non-battery side of the CyberPower which are Surge-only protection outlets. This saves battery power during power failures on devices I don't need to keep running. I also love the real time on-screen capability.  I live over 1 mile back in the woods off of a gravel and dirt road in the NE Georgia mountains and we get power problems quite often here mostly from tree limbs falling on the power lines. This unitis great for me because I can usually finish what I'm working on and then close my apps before system shutdown. I will definitely purchase other CyberPower units in the future.    05/11/2011 I have purchased another of these units for my Home Theater system about a week ago. I don't know the standby running time since I haven't had a power failure yet. The main reason for this unit was to protect the electronics.

product_title: Sony RMVLZ620 Universal Remote Control (Black)
review_body: I bought this remote to replace the SONY RM-V302 I had previously, which worked like a champ for a decade.  When I was in the market for a replacement, I figured logically that a newer Sony remote would have a minimum of equivalent compatibility with my Zenith tv.      Apparently logic does not apply to Sony as this absolutely does NOT work with Zenith tv's with any supplied codes.  After that did not work, I used the feature that tries all TV codes.  Amazingly, NONE of them worked.  It's not as if programming a remote is even remotely close to the realm of difficult.  I went through this process twice more in addition just to verify I had not hit a wrong key inadvertently.  I had not.        I did some searching, including viewing Sony's website for this, and there is a nice little disclaimer at the bottom saying if the manufacturer's code does not work, you may be required to try all TV codes until you find one that works.  Given that there's 100,000 combinations and a large subset of that devoted to TV's, there is no way in hell I am spending the time to go through every possible combination.  Purely ridiculous.      I could buy an $8 RCA remote that would be guaranteed to work, but I went with Sony due to brand-name recognition and previous relatively positive experiences with similar products.  In the end, this remote is literally useless to me for it's primary function, and given that returning it would be more trouble than it's worth, I broke it intentionally out of spite.  It's functionality remains about the same.  So, I am going back to the previous remote I had which I've located for sale on ebay.  This remote ate a portion of my wallet and, more importantly, my time.      Proceed with caution and make sure returning is an easy option if you go with this remote.  As I found out, there are no guarantees.    Update :  I purchased a Sony RMVZ320 from the local Best Buy on the basis that returning would be cake, and this is my synopsis :   - It has nearly thesame design as this *but* with GREATER compatibility with legacy products and at $10+ less cost.      - It still did not work 100% on my Zenith tv.  The number buttons did not work, though everything else did.      - Unless you absolutely need the 1 extra device to go from 7 to 8 max and the learning capability, which is stated to be flakey in it's reliability, I would recommend the Sony RMVZ320 emphatically over this.  Far better value per dollar.

product_title: Audio Technica Music Phone Headphone Adapter
review_body: I had hoped that this product would work as an extension for Apple gear, but it does not.    The volume control does not adjust the volume on the device.  The volume control will change the signal level going through the extension, but, unlike the Apple headphones, it will not adjust the device's volume level.  If the volume is turned way down on the device, it's impossible to use this extension to turn it up.      The control button works in some cases but not others.  On an iPhone, the control button works just like the iPhone control button.  However, on an Apple Laptop the control button doesn't work properly (e.g., pausing and skipping in iTunes).    The microphone does work in both cases.    One rather significant downside is that if you use your regular Apple headphones with this extension, you will lose all of the functionality inherent in the Apple headphones.  The volume control, control button and microphone on your Apple headphones will not work through this extension.    If you are looking for a good extension for Apple gear, I would suggest you keep looking.

product_title: microFidelity Mini Amplifier, Model 100 Black
review_body: I have purchased 20 of these thus far as a component in a new consumer-oriented listening system.  Of the 20, two of them suddenly died.  They were used less than a total of 15 hours and at less than full volume.  Some of the speakers they powered were a pair of 8 ohms, some were a pair of 4 ohms.  It may be that 4 ohm speakers do not have sufficient resistance for the 24 volt power supply that is provided.  I have not been able to verify this hypothesis, and I did not see any company literature describing this limitation.        You get a spark when attaching the power supply, and they get fairly warm to the touch.  These are, in my opinion, minor compromises of design for a very impressive device that functions well when it when it doesn't die.  All in all, I recommend the amp because it is modestly priced for what it can do.  You won't be out of a lot of money if it fails, and perhaps you will have better luck than I have had.        The company is now producing a more powerful version (model 200) at a slightly higher price.  I have not tested that model.  The older version offered all the power that I needed.  Maybe the new model is more reliable.  Hope so; it's a terrific design concept.

You can adjust the bass and treble, and after doing so, I had no problem with it being overwhelming or bloated. Controls are simple and intuitive. It has a small remote with a storage pocket on the unit itself, a great convenience. The unit can run on ac power, or 8 size d batteries, (which make up a lot of the weight.) If you find yourself using the batteries a lot, make sure you get high quality rechargeable ones with a high mAH rating, and a quality charger. It also features an FM radio which seems to pull in stations fairly well. If you like a full rich sound that can hold together at higher volumes, this will be tough to beat at it's price point. But first be sure the size and weight won't be an issue for you, and the retro boombox styling is to your taste.

product_title: Philips MZ-7 Executive Microsystem (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great little unit, but spare parts are tough, so here's some tips
review_body:
I bought this nifty little unit used for $60. It sounded great both with a CD, and with the tuner section, but I bought it from someone in a large city, with a myriad of station choices, while I live in a smaller area where signals can be iffy.
I got it home, and hooked up my own small bookshelf speakers(1970's era Polk Mini Monitors) with 14ga wires, since the stock Philips speakers are hardwired with about 30ga wire, which is no good for clean sound. The stock speakers sound fine, and will sound better when I re-wire them.
The next problem was that the AM antenna connects using a connector much like a cordless phone battery connector, and I found that this unit, for all its clean & modern styling dates to the early-to-mid 1990's, and Philips has no parts for it.....or so they thought. After emailing, phoning and chatting with Philips in the US and having ZERO luck, I decided to go closer to the source, Philips in Europe. Eventually, I found a current Philips model, the FWM-387 which uses the exact same connector for its MW(aka AM) antenna and ordered it for half of what the same antenna would cost from Philips USA. Speaking of those losers, they also stock the same antenna, and they now know they can cross-reference this part, which is #994000001192.
Overall, it's a nice little unit. The FM reception is really pretty good, especially since I connected TWO dipole antennas equivalent to the [[ASIN:B000EIOQBM Petra 880-1100 Fm Dipole Antenna]] in a cross configuration.
I'm astonished at the power this little unit puts out, at a pretty clean THD. I wish it had a phono jack, but I guess I'll just have to buy an outboard phono preamp.
I'd give this 5 stars, but it loses 1 star thanks to the inept, ignorant US support staff, as well as Amazon's \\"award-winning staff\\", who refuse to update their statement that this item was first listed on Amazon on Sept. 4, 1973(?!?!?)

(I subsequently sold the Polks, and moved to a pair of KEF Chorale III two-ways on 23\\" steel stands, and it makes me almost not miss my Yamaha CR-840 and AR-11s....almost)ands, and it makes me almost not miss my Yamaha CR-840 and AR-11s....almost)

product_title: Logitech Harmony Adapter for PlayStation 3 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Works quite well, no more IR dongle on the USB
review_body: This review is going to be a little different than most others, because I'm using the PS3 Harmony adaptor with a Pronto remote control, not a Harmony. At one time, the Pronto was a favorite among those looking to consolidate their remotes and have a high level of control over the look and feel of the remote. The line has since been discontinued by Philips, and the community on RemoteCentral is starting to whither, but I still have one, and I needed a better solution than the [[ASIN:B000R5H7KE BluWave Infrared Remote]] I've been using.    With a set of codes retrieved from the RemoteCentral site, I was able to map all the necessary codes for the PS3 through the Harmony adapter. The only code I'm having a problem with is the OFF code, but I've got some experimentation to do with that before I declare it a non-working code. There's even a note with the codes that says that OFF is actually a macro on the Harmony, so it's not as easy as a single code to issue an OFF command.    The IR detection range on the adapter is good; much better than the IR dongle I was using. Setup was as easy as plugging in the adapter and pairing it with the PS3 using the instructions provided with the adapter. Rather than have it powered up all the time, I have it plugged into the switched outlet on my AV receiver, which may be part of the problem of the OFF code not working. I might be turning off the receiver before the PS3 gets the full OFF command.     That's one of the tradeoffs of the power of the Pronto, lots of fiddling, whereas Harmony remotes tend to \\"just work\\" and that's where I'll be headed when I find a good price on a Harmony One. In the meantime, this adapter is a nice stepping stone, as it works with the Pronto, and it will work with a future Harmony.    $40 is more than $15 for a USB IR dongle, but I'm glad that I spent the extra money to get something that has a good IR detection range and will provide me with an upgrade path for the future.

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Radio
review_headline: Excellent Internet Radio and Music Player!
review_body: It's rare that you can take something out of the box and get it working so easily.  But, the setup was very easy to do.  I already had a Pandora account so that was easy and I already knew what to expect.  I was amazed that it also lists all of my local AM and FM stations with no additional setup.  I suppose it keys on the user's Zip Code for that.  I downloaded the Squeezebox Server software from the Logitech website and installed that.  It automatically scans and finds your music files and catalogs them in various ways by Artist, Title, Album, etc.  The user interface is easy to learn too.     I ordered out the accessory battery and remote control kit from Logitech for about $50.  There's a seller on Amazon and elsewhere selling them for 3-4X that amount so stay away from those people.  The battery installation is easy and the battery is charging whenever the Squeezebox is connected to the AC power adapter.  So, when you want to take your music with you anywhere that your wireless internet will reach... just unplug it and go!    My wife doesn't even need her iPod anymore as she now has access to the entire music collection on the NAS plus so much more.  I made her a radio station on Pandora she just loves!    I'm very well satisfied with this product.

product_title: Sony CMTBX20i Micro Hi-Fi Shelf System (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Good value, but not the best sound or reliability
review_body: I have had this little bookshelf system for about three years and have overall enjoyed it. The sound it puts out is decent. Like another reviewer said, the speakers lack bass extension for very bass driven music but most of the time its fine. It fills the room I have it in well, which is about 13x16ft. It handles musical climaxes well. The tuner also seems to work well, and the included antenna for am and fm worked fine. I only had a few reception problems with stereo fm on occasion, but they clear up if you switch to mono mode. I do have a few complaints about the system, though. First, after about two years the cd player began making strange clicking sounds, and then started skipping frequently. I didn't use it for a few days and it was back to normal. Every now and then, however, the player still makes strange noises while playing. Second, if you are listening at very quiet levels, the standard noise of the cd player can be distracting. It is a slight hissing sound that just comes from the player itself, as the disc spins. This is only noticeable if the volume is very low. Third, the headphone jack has a bit of noise. It is nothing major and should not bother or even be noticed my most, but with a good pair of headphones it can be heard in soft musical passages. Fourth, the speaker grilles aren't removable which became a problem for me when a screw on the speaker driver came loose and began rattling around. I had to cut the front fabric off to repair this. Also, you can't adjust the EQ (changes the amount of treble/bass you get) without the remote which is a pain if you loose it or it breaks. Last, it isn't really practical to upgrade the speakers because of the low power output and low impedance. The only reasonable option would be Klipsch or other very efficient speakers and most of those cost about as much as a new, better quality shelf system.    Now, I know that I have identified several problems, but the the truth is that I enjoy listening to this sony system. It works well for what it is made for, which is for uncritical listening and a fun basic shelf system. I got mine for about $100 and i would definetly say it was worth the money. For a large step up in performance you would have to double that price. On the whole, i would recommend this syetem, with the few reservations mentioned above.

product_title: Sennheiser Closed Circumaural Hi-Fi Headphone
review_body: I've had these headphones for about a month now, and I must say I am extremely impressed by their performance!  This is my first venture into the \\"audiophile\\" zone for around the ear headphones.  I previously had a pair of Klipsch S4 earbuds.  They were very impressive, but I needed something that would be comfortable for long periods of time and wouldn't be constantly falling out of my ears.  These fit the bill perfectly.    The sound - The quality of the sound that these headphones put out is outstanding.  They sound alright when I have them plugged directly into my computer or ipod, but they really shine when I have them running through my Yamaha stereo (RX-V363).  They do tend to suck power, so my ipod has to be turned up much higher to get decent volume out of these as opposed to the stock earbuds that it came with.  The sound is very balanced with smooth highs and accurate lows.  DO NOT buy these if you want an extremely bass heavy sound.  They do pump out bass, but it is by no means overpowering.  The bass is never farty or flat.  It has a very even response the whole way across the board.    The feel - I have never had a pair of headphones that were as comfortable as these.  They wrap completely around my ears and the pads are very soft.  After wearing them for 5 minutes I forget that they're even on my head.  That is until I try and look down at something.  I have a ridiculously narrow head, and I'm pretty sure that's why they fall off so easily.  For normal wear at a desk or in bed, they're perfect.  They're obviously not made for active use and therefore I don't think this really detracts from their overall awesomeness.    The quality - They seem to be very well made.  Most of the parts of the 'phones are replaceable, but I don't foresee that being necessary.  The cable is very solid and is plenty long for anything I use them for (it's about 10-12' long with the extention attached).  I've run over it several times with my desk chair and it isn't so much as flattened in those spots.      Overall these headphones outperformed my expectations.  They are extremely clear and every instrument can be heard individually.  Very impressive.   I definitely recommend them.

product_title: Harman Kardon HK 3390 80W Stereo Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Go back to 2-channel if you love loud music!
review_body: Like many of us we have now built our sound system around the HDTV with a 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound system. I have very high quality surround sound set-up and it is GREAT for blu-ray movies and Dolby digital. Amazing even. But is just does not cut it when it comes to blasting out the tunes. I have a pair of very high quality full range 300 watt big box speakers in moth balls and finally bought this amp to drive them to put them back into service. I could not believe the difference and what I was missing! This amp has no trouble at all driving them and plenty of head room. The sound is loud & clear and most importantly split into true 2-channel \\"stereo\\" as many recordings are meant to be.    So on the plus side is the amp is loud, clear, well built (it's big so check dimensions), and looks great. It is a good value for the price.[...]Has true phono input for you turn-table guys. If you're looking for an \\"old stlye\\" 2-channel analog stereo receiver, then this is it.    On the minus side is it could be improved. It lacks a mid-range control and has very basic bass & treble controls. My old analog amps that wore out always had a \\"loudness\\" button for lower volume to boost bass & this unit does not. The bass & treble control do not work with the remote & for me this is one of the worst things about it. There is no ipod dock connection for this unit so ipod is via y-cord RCA only and remote will not work it. Other Harmon Kardon units do have ipod docks. There is no digital input like optical at all, again other HD units do have them. Also no HDMI ports.    However, it is not to say I am not enjoying the heck out of it. Harmon Kardon offers the missing features described above on more $$$$ units but I was not willing to bite. I got what I paid for, an old-fashion muscle amp, and I could not be happier. I can blow the windows out without any distortion. I may damage my hearing.....cool. ROCK ON!!!!

review_body: I have had these headphones for a few weeks now with quite a few hrs of use everyday, and they are pretty awesome, I have a simple setup with my computer portable player and home theater receiver. They sound good on all of them, I was using a pair of MDR-V700 before which are not bad for the price and have held up well over many years of use, but when comparing them to the Ultrasone 900's they have a much muddier bass, and don't seam to have as decent of a midrage as well. With the Ultrasone 900s I have noticed a few new things in music that I own because of the range on sound production I think it add a bit of airiness when the tracks are recored in a way that includes it, one track during the into I can hear a buzz/hiss of an amp that is in the background of other instruments that I cannot hear on my home theatre or other headphones.    One of my friends has tried them out from time to time to compare, they are very heavy into bass and can't even really hear the amp buzz/hiss that I can in the song above, their thoughts are that the sound production on the the headphones is excellent and to have a very sharp/tight sound on bass, midrange, and highs, but wishes they had more of a physical thump on the low end.    There clear and quick respons of the speakers makes for sound production of music as interments playing together at the same time. If you are looking for a pair of headphones that brings out all the interments during your usage then these are defiantly for you. I don't Know if they are totally worth the full price tag but I managed to pick them up for a fair discount which makes them totally worth the purchase, so if you can find them on a decent sales then defiantly check them out.

product_title: Yamaha YBA-10WH Bluetooth Wireless Audio Receiver for Select Yamaha Home Theater Receivers (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I've been using a Yamaha receiver for quite awhile and connected the YDS-10 iPod dock about a year ago to the unit to enjoy the catalog of music I was storing on my iPod. I'd been seeing some of the reviews here and elsewhere where people have complained about some sound problems with the YBA-10...the bluetooth option for wirelessly listening to music from an iPhone. We have 3 family members all with iPhones and after pairing each device with the Yamaha receiver its as easy as the push of a few buttons to have music playing thru the audio system from any of the devices. I haven't experienced any audio problems and the device was very easy to hook up and configure to use.    Couldn't be happier with the device!!

review_body: This wire is indeed very flat, and the copper does appear high grade.  However, many wires use good copper.  These were the only advantages to this wire. Worse than that the adhesive plastic is difficult to peel from the flat solid copper.  I wanted the copper naked for good contact; so, the speakers would work. I was able to get one speaker to work and not the other, but was able to get both speakers to work with other wire.  I tried scraping the wire with my fingernail, pliers, and a razor blade. As usual, I did not find solid (as opposed to stranded) wire to be easy to work with.  Personally, I hope to return this wire and will purchase some 12 G Stinger Pro wire instead.  I'll just hide that wire along the base board with a cover designed for that. From past experience, I know the Stinger wire is easy to work with and does a decent job for sound quality on the cheap.

review_body: I really like this cable, good quality. I had a cable 25 Ft. didn't connect most of the time, but this new cable is great, connects every time I turn on the receiver.

review_headline: Much better than a portable DVD
review_body:

If you have young kids you know that they can watch the same movie 50 times in a row. You also know that kids are TERRIBLE with dvd's. I got tired of mine getting destroyed so I bought a lifetime license for DVDfab and just save everything as an MKV file.

This unit replaced a portable DVD player our 4th portable we have had. You know what happens eventually they stop playing dvd's even though the displays continue to work fine.

There's allot to like here a compact package that features a huge screen, built in battery and can output HD to your tv. This thing has tons of features it can play movies, music, pictures. I would prefer a D pad that has up /down/ left/ right and enter buttons to navigate I would of even been ok if the unit was an inch taller to accommodate those buttons. video output

Good tech support

the bad

button & menu layout

product_title: Barnes & Noble NOOK COLOR eBook Reader (WiFi Only)
review_headline: Good for casual reading. Not better than a Kindle as a true ereader device
review_body:
Bought mine days ago and returned just today. It is an ok device but does not truly shine as an ereader and I will expand on it shortly.

1st, this is more a hybrid device than an ereader. An ereader basically is for reading documents in an electronic format. Examples of good ereaders: Kindle (of course), Nook 1st generation and Sony. Nook Color, besides allowing you to read, let you browse internet, listen music, play some games and much more tablet oriented stuff. Of course, there is nothing wrong on that until you start thinking about how important color and internet are for just reading a simple book.

So, what's cool or nice:

-Internet.
Full color internet experience, with nice virtual keyboard and ok browser. Touching the screen and keyboard is like an iPad or similar tablets, but is comfortable enough for short emails or using Wikipedia or Google.

-PDF support
With Nook Color not only you can read PDFs in a nice full color screen but you can expand or zoom in at will, move along pages with a simple touch or even rotate and read in landspace mode. This feature is really amazing and the selling point if reading PDFs is your only or most important task.

-Full color screen
Pretty obvious. If you like magazines or would like to get electronic subscriptions of any of them, look no further. The resolution, colors and screen is perfect, a real pleasure to read using a NC. Depending of the magazine you can also extract or read the text or article portion only, leaving images apart.

BUT!... not everything is perfect ...

-No landscape mode for books
You have landscape mode while reading PDFs but not while reading regular ePub books. This was a real surprise to me, a bad one! Landscape mode allows you to rotate and read poetry or technical books without cutting the paragraph or breaking lines. With no Landscape mode you are forced to read every book \\"as is\\" and for a hybrid table which costs more than $200.00, in my opinion, it is not acceptable. My Kindle 3 rotates and it's 50% cheaper!

-LCD screen
I must admit this device has less glare issues than iPad or Galaxy, but if you have read using eink technology you would not go back and change to LCD again. Reading on a Nook Color for several hours is not easy for your eyes. And forget about using it at your pool or outdoors, unless is cloudy or you find the perfect angle; the glare will bother you while reading anyway. Indoor is a different story but it created some eye strain on me anyway, specially after long reading sessions.

-Heavy
For serious readers (those who read novels, fiction books, technical books) or more than 2 or 3 weeks per month, please think again before buying. With about 18oz your hands and wrist will start complaining soon and if you don't have a desk or something to put your NC on, your choices are using your tummy, chest, lap or knee as additional support. A deal breaker. Being a Kindle 3 owner I know what I'm talking about. You can hold a Kindle 3 with one hand and read for hours with little or no problems at all.

-Battery
Only 8 hrs of continue use, average. I bought it a Tuesday, read for about 5 hrs that day, went to bed (leave it on but in sleeping mode). Next day morning turned it on, used it 1 more hour and soon after that the device was at 16% of battery life. (I barely used internet and brightness was at minimum) Another important point about battery and charge is that the Nook Color must be charged via wall, not USB or computer unless screen is off, which means you must forget about using the device during the charging process. The adapter is also proprietary so you can't use your Nook 1st gen adapter or the one some Androids use, I don't like that, I don't like proprietary stuff. The more standard, the more common, the better to replace or find.

-No zoom or ability to enlarge images
An image wiy Kindle 3 rotates and it's 50% cheaper! -LCD screen I must admit this device has less glare issues than iPad or Galaxy, but if you have read using eink technology you would not go back and change to LCD again. Reading on a Nook Color for several hours is not easy for your eyes. And forget about using it at your pool or outdoors, unless is cloudy or you find the perfect angle; the glare will bother you while reading anyway. With about 18oz your hands and wrist will start complaining soon and if you don't have a desk or something to put your NC on, your choices are using your tummy, chest, lap or knee as additional support. I bought it a Tuesday, read for about 5 hrs that day, went to bed (leave it on but in sleeping mode). Next day morning turned it on, used it 1 more hour and soon after that the device was at 16% of battery life. (I barely used internet and brightness was at minimum) Another important point about battery and charge is that the Nook Color must be charged via wall, not USB or computer unless screen is off, which means you must forget about using the device during the charging process. The adapter is also proprietary so you can't use your Nook 1st gen adapter or the one some Androids use, I don't like that, I don't like proprietary stuff. The more standard, the more common, the better to replace or find. -No zoom or ability to enlarge images An image with wrapping text around in that cool book? If you can't read it or maybe is too small, then sorry...you're out of luck.You have (at the moment of this review) no way to click, expand or enlarge that image. If you read mostly novels this means nothing to you. But if you read technical books with some images or illustrations on it, the size will be so small that is basically useless and not readable at all. I can't believe this simple feature is absent and I can only hope for a future fix via firmware -Android based but not full access to Android market Shame on you B&N. This device could be a real hit if was not so closed or locked. As usual, this device will be hacked for those with brave hearts or basic computer skills (actually, it has been) but warranty will not be honored and it's a hassle to keep it up to date after official B&N firmware upgrades, in case you hacked or rooted the device; also you won't be able to read books in-store if you root it. While B&N keeps selling the unit without Android Market or a restricted version of it, this device will be like having a Magnum revolver in your hands without any bullets. So much power with Android/Linux but you just can't use it. -No \\"read me\\" feature For a $200.00 tablet, I would expect this feature. The Kindle it's not so powerful in terms of hardware or processor and it reads the English books for you. Summary If you read a lot, portability and battery life are important for you, forget about Nook Color. If you are a casual reader, looking for a fun device and distractions (Internet, Games, etc) Nook color will fit your bill. Just keep in mind that Nook Color is not a true ereader though, but more like a tablet with reading abilities; if you are aware of that and eye strain is not a concern, this can be a great buy. For now, I will pass. My Kindle 3 is simpler and lighter and does very good what it suppose to do: let me read (or read for me) my favorite books. Most novels and technical books are not in color so I don't need a tablet with Internet access to enjoy them, why bother then?

product_title: Onkyo HT-S7300 7.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver and Speaker Package with iPod Dock (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

product_title: H2O Audio Amphibx Waterproof Armband for iPhone
review_body: Initially when I bought this I was stoked at the idea of being able to listen to my Ipod Touch underwater. Imagine my surprise when 4 laps into my swim there was no more sound. I sent the case and the ipod back as requested and after a prolonged delay the message I got was:     \\"In the case of the Armband you own, the only thing that isn't completely open and shut is the blue gasket that has to be double-checked that it is tucked into its little groove before the unit is closed. If there is no defect, and the case is properly clasped, this is the only factor that can cause a leak. We do try to make our products as automatic and simple as we can, but there is still always going to be a slight element of oversight required when a static seal is involved. We definitely support testing the case a with a piece of tissue paper in there before you put another iPod in.\\"    In other words they couldn't find the problem and so they assumed it was because some fiddly part of the closure mechanism hadn't closed properly even though I specifically followed the enclosed instructions!    In my opinion this is a complete rip-off, and judging by the reviews I've seen here recently others have had the same experience. product_title: Philips HTS3251B/F7 Home Theater (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Amazon.com description is Wrong! No IPOD DOCK!
review_body: I purchased this item as a christmas present for my mom and dad and while the unit sounds great and the blueray player is   really sharp...i am still dissapointed! First of all: Amazon's product description is WRONG! NO IPOD DOCK IS INCLUDED!!!    The second issue with this system was mentioned by another reviewer but i want to confirm what he said. When you turn off the   reciever the audio playback forgets that you had set it to an alternate sound source such as you would do if you wanted to   hook up your cable box audio out. So the next time you turn it back on the sound has defaulted back to Blueray and you have to   hit the audio source button multiple times to get to coaxial/optical/etc. input that you hooked your cable box to. For many   people this may not be a problem but for 75 year old parents who are not very technically savy this is not good!    Another issue i noticed was that you can not update the firmware on the player using the SD Card slot! You only get 2 options:  1. Update via internet (Can be a problem if you only have wireless internet because you have to run a network cable)  2. Update via cd recordable (People with limited or no computer skills will have trouble with this method-Unzipping and Burning CD-R)    Final issue i have with this system is that for the price they are charging they should at least include a wireless adaptor for internet access!  Especially when you have a system that has internet radio and netflix!    I wanted a simple to operate surround system for my parents and i am not sure this system fits the bill. I may have to return it and get a cheap surround   reciever and speakers instead.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Adapter for PlayStation 3 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Excellent addition to my Logitech remote

product_title: Audio-Technica Adjustable Aluminum Clip-On Headphones
review_headline: Aluminum Alloy to Fuel Your Cybernetic Audiophile Transformation
review_body:
Corny title aside, I have to admit that these are my new favorite headphones. Although I was not inspired by Shin Megami Tensei to buy these, it was certainly the unusual use of brushed metal backs on these headphones that first caught my eye. And let me tell you, stock photos just don't do these things justice--you've got to have them unboxed and in your hands to truly appreciate them. I've noticed that the brushed metal look is all the rage these days, and Audio-Technica jumps on the bandwagon with superb execution. Sure, some may say these things look cheap, but all I've gotten since wearing them are lots of compliments and abundant amounts of curiosity. For the sake of not going on a long yarn, I will break my review up into three sections: aesthetics, functionality of design, and sound quality. Let's begin.

Aesthetics--
As mentioned before, these things look GREAT. There's nothing like the gleam of an aluminum alloy backing with the Audio-Technica symbol proudly emblazoned upon it to assert quality. The clips are small,much smaller than one would assume based on the picture. Think maybe the same diameter as a golf ball. Detail is impressive, as the silver and black color scheme works together well, and little details like ridges on the black ring surrounding the ear cushion and similar parallel lines on the aluminum parts just look good. The clip mechanism is definitely eye-catching, too--holding $50 phones to your head with little more than a piece of wire and rubber is, at the very least, ambitious.

Functionality--
This is where AT runs into trouble, alas. What looks good on paper isn't always carried out well. The positives include an adjustable clip mechanism that can be moved upwards and downwards as one attempts to create the best possible fit. This is a definite advantage few other phones on the market can attest to. The clip is a little barebones, though--the little pointed part on the rubber rests on the back of my ear, and although it's far from uncomfortable, the OUCH factor after removing after a few hours is notable. The asymmetrical cable length is an issue, too. As noted before, the weight of the cable makes it a little unbalanced, and the left clip in particular tends to dislodge without too much effort sometimes. It's also hilariously short: if you don't have an extender, be prepared to hunch down if you're over 5'5\\". Had H. neanderthalensis still walked amongst us, these would be his clips of choice. The memory foam cushion is almost decadently luxurious, however--I've never felt foam so soft. It molds to your ear shape in time, too. On top of it, the cable is braided, which makes it more resistant to temperature fluctuations and a bit more tangle resistant; these cables are far from tangle proof, though, so exercise care.

Sound--
For many, this is the only part of the review that matters. And for those people, I need to make something clear--these headphones DO have bass, it's just more subdued and punchy rather than explosive. If you need a serious boom, these won't deliver. But to call them bass deficient is either being impatient (burn-in, anyone) or somewhat bass-spoiled. It pops up when it needs to and doesn't leave a hole in the music, so it works for me. Mids and highs are where these phones are specialized, though. I've never loved classical music before now, but it seems this past week I've been addicted to Vocalise op. 34. The notes are clear, beautiful, sublime and perhaps even ephemeral. Is it a good charger, no, it's freaking fantastic, until you 'smoke it' like I did, then it's junk.

product_title: SweetPea3 2 GB MP3 Player for Kids
review_headline: There has to be something better.
review_body: I'll start by saying that we might have bought a lemon.  Perhaps I would echo some of the enthusiastic reviews if I wasn't sending my dead unit back.    I'll also add that when it did work, my 16 month old loved it.    However, there are some problems with this player's design.  I understand that making the SweetPea difficult to use makes it hard for your kid to mess it up, but why make it so frustrating?  Changing the volume takes 5 separate steps.  Replacing the battery involves finding a small screw-driver and removing 2 tiny screws.  That's not a problem if the batteries last a while, but if they die frequently, it's a real chore.  Want to change play-lists?  Well, it's back to the child-proof menu system and several steps later you're done.    A suggestion for the SweetPea4:  Put a child proof switch on the unit that shuts off access to the controls.  That way your kid can't crank the volume to 11 without your help, but you can actually make some adjustments to the device when you need to without invoking menu system.  The current user interface is very frustrating.    Again, if all of these compromises had meant that the device was indestructible, they would be easier to overlook.  The fact that ours died after only a couple of weeks of light use is disheartening.    Update:  Interesting to see Anne C's comments.  Unlike Anne, I have had no such luck with the company.  When I contacted them, they told me to take my problem to the reseller.  Still waiting for my replacement unit.  I will update again when it arrives.    Update 2:  My replacement unit has arrived and so far... It works!  Battery life seems much improved, and all the basics are good.  I still wish there was an easier way to make simple changes like switching play-lists, but I guess I am in the minority here.  If set-it-and-forget-it truly meets your needs, and you don't foresee making frequent adjustments, then the SweetPea3 fits the bill.  I still think there is room for improvement, and I'm hopeful for the SweetPea4.
