product_title: RCA ANT1650F Flat Digital Amplified Indoor TV Antenna
review_body: Design:  The antenna comes with a metallic base that you can attach it to stand it up with.  The problem is the location of the coax on the back and where it is to the metal bracket.  You have to bend the coax over the bracket to make it sit correctly.  Also if you are trying to wall mount the antenna it will not sit flush against the wall and sticks out like a sore thumb even though it is thin.  If they moved the coax output to a side or provided a flat coax cable it would be better.  The piano black is nice but it shows fingerprints and dust easily.    Reception:  Just like with any other antenna the higher you have it the better the reception.  I do have troubles pulling in local stations at time and not able to find a solution yet.  With it being powered and multi-directional it should pick up all signals well.  It does put out good sound and picture when the signal is available.  The strength of the signal needs to be high though to get anything out of it.  Otherwise there is a bit too much tiling.

review_headline: Good clock, just not loud enough

I never tried out the radio (I don't like to wake up to the morning DJ's yelling) so I just stuck with the buzzer. As it turns out, the alarm on my iPhone is louder than this clock. For this reason only I had to return it.

If you prefer the radio to a buzzer, this might be a good choice, otherwise I'd look for something else.

review_body: I was back and forth between the PSW505 and the BIC F12. I decided on the Polk, I do not regret it at all. Many people out there say Polk is not known for there sub woofers. The MTX one was not bad it shook the whole house and sounded good, but i wanted to try something else. This polk hits much lower notes then my MTX, also it is clearer sounding. The bass notes are tight and clear. This sub is great for $229.00, it works very well with any size home theater. I have it placed in my 18x30 basement room and it rocks. Dont waste your time thinking it over like me and just get this one.

review_body: I was extremely disappointed in this product. There was constant static caused by other electronic instruments in the room. The sound quality was below average. The infrared has extremely limited range. Basically the only way for me to use these headphones was to sit along in a closet 2ft away from the infrared hub. product_title: Ultimate Ears 200vi Noise-Isolating Headset
review_body: The Logitech Ultimate Ears 200vi headset has a lot of unique features. I love having controls on the cord to adjust the volume, pause the songs, and change songs. While I used the earbuds only with an iPod, the manual states they are also compatible with an iPhone and allow you to take calls using the microphone as well as listen to music. There is also some functionality with Blackberries and MacBooks, but since I don't have these items I am not able to speak to these functions.    The sound quality of this headset was better than the standard earbuds that come with an iPod. While I was not overwhelmed with how they sounded, I think these earbuds are a good value. They are noise-isolating, not noice-cancelling, so not all background noise is eliminated, but sounds are muffled. The extra features, such as the controls on the cord, add to the value. Another added feature is the small plastic carrying case that is included. While it's not fancy, I've not received a case with other brands at a comparable price, so this was a nice bonus.     A great feature to these earbuds is the five sizes of silicone ear cushions which are included. I don't get a good fit from the standard iPod earbuds or others I have purchased. I liked the fit I got with these earbuds when I used one of the smaller-sized ear cushions. Overall, a good value and good quality product. It might be a good option for teens that want a better sound quality than the standard iPod earbuds provide, but need a smaller size to fit in their ears properly.

product_title: BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer
review_headline: Best value sub, but placement is key.
review_body: I've had for about 3 months now.  You can't beat the value as many on this post has mentioned.  I initially used it in my bedroom, but for some reason it didn't sound that great for music.  Was using a Sony STR DH800, then the Onkyo 608.   It was ok for movies.  One thing, you will want to bolt down or remove any rattling furniture or doors you might have.  The rattling will drive you nuts.  Another thing, turning it up all the way could damage the woofer depending on what you are listening to.  I switched it out of my bedroom w/ a more sophisticated sub I had in my den (JBL SP101 I bought 8 years ago).  In my bedroom, the JBL is more tight and refined than the BIC was.  Also doesn't rattle my furniture, but is still pretty loud.  The BIC sounds better after tweaking in my den than in my bedroom. Placement was key since as I moved it around the sound quality went up and down.  All in all, this is a good entry level sub for those gents who are financially challenged.  For me, I will soon switch out for something better, don't know yet however.  It will be fun searching.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_headline: It's Hard For Me to Review These Fairly
review_body: As I said, it's hard for me to review these fairly.  Reason is, they simply don't fit my ears, and because they don't, they sound terrible.  At least, this is what I'm speculating.  Since the trick for getting any bass with ear buds is to get them really in your ears, if you can't, then they'll sound unlistenably thin and tinny.  I have to assume that's what some of the other reviewers who complained about the bass on these were also experiencing, because no one - and I mean no one - would think that these sounded good if they heard what my ears were hearing.  And there's no way that a respected company like Klipsch would put out a product like this unless it was sounding a lot better for some people.    I've always had a problem finding ear buds that fit my ears.  iPod earbuds, no way, and my fiancee's Bose earbuds didn't work well for me either.  The only ones that worked for me have been these old Sonys that were about 35 bucks and maybe now discontinued.  They've always served me pretty well, but I was hoping for an upgrade.  For me, at least, these were not the answer.  Now I'm in a pickle:  I would LOVE to get a pair of good sounding earbuds with excellent passive sound isolation (I'm worried that the combination of the iPod and NYC subways are wreaking havoc on my ears), but I don't want to throw down a bunch of money for another pair that won't work.  Stupid question, but are ear buds like swimsuits?  Will they let you return them after you've tried them on?

review_headline: It really did rock. Now it just turns itself on and off.
review_body:
My Yamaha RXV-795 finally died after ten solid years of use. To replace it, I procrastinated the purchase to research for two months on what would provide the most features, performance, minimal technical issues and make me happy. I think I have found it with this piece. I have had it three days. These three days have made me realize that my Klipsch Synergy speakers weren't getting what they deserved. I have my Xbox, PS3 and Cable TV all running HDMI. I put in \\"The Dark Knight\\" after using the MCACC for calibration and was floored. The typical tester scene (bat bike vs. the semi) was pristine clear, video was awesome with the sound stage and surround blowing me away. I have just put it up to -7 for Tool's 10,000 Days album on the \\"Rosetta Stoned\\" track. Holy ****! Unbelievable. It remained clear, instrument placement obvious, superb vocals, clean highs, tight lows, and I have heard things unnoticed before with the old receiver. Gamers: Get this if you're in the market and work for a living. Call of Duty: Black Ops sounds frigging ridiculous.

I realize that this is not an audiophile piece. This is a mid-range consumer item designed to bring the latest technology with excellent sound. Both are delivered in a very aesthetically pleasing appearance. It is an excellent deal, well worth every penny (so far) and I am very pleased I picked this in the end. Who knows. I may upgrade to the 1120. I have 27 days left. :)

Update 11/06/13: Almost to the day of the month and three years later, this thing has started to have a mind of it's own. Out of nowhere, it has turned itself on and off, has refused to turn off at times or even turn back on. I have unplugged it, disconnected all devices and reconnected everything and nothing will settle the behavior this thing has developed. Since Pioneer's warranty is crap, it's well outside of being worth even a bench fee. To that point, if you buy your Pioneer receiver online, they won't honor the warranty at all. Fairwarning: If you intend to have this receiver for a long haul, don't bother. You will be sorely disappointed and out a chunk of money. I am now looking into Denon as a better option for replacing this extremely expensive paper weight.

product_title: JVC Stc30Xgdu3 30-Minute Super Vhs-C Video Tape (3 Pk)
review_headline: In 1990 SVHS was a good as it gets for consumer video.
review_body: Bought these tapes last year for my old JVC SVHS camcorder.  Worked fine except i had to rip off the flimsy top cover of each tape due to a problem in the loading basket of my camcorder.  Not a design problem of the tape.  Tape is consistently clear and steady audio, even with my mono unit.  Picture quality is good but if you transfer it to digital video on a computer or even to dvd, the quality fades to almost unacceptable.  If your going to put stuff on dvd or digital video, don't bother with analog video tapes like this.  Also, hooking up a SVHS player to a HD TV, like an LCD, it's going to convert the analog to digital in real time so it's gonna look grainy and awful. For best results, hook up your svhs player directly to an analog tube (direct view) television with s-video cable and audio jacks.  A good quality tv like the rca/ge thompson sets from the mid 90's (fixed of course) usually still have an outstanding picture today.  Some models had pictures tubes that were made poorly, in mexico or \\"usa\\" (that were actually made by illegal aliens in the us).  My rca ctc-185 has a 30\\" crt that was made in italy and you would have to see it to believe how clear, colorful and bright the picture is after 15 years of use everyday.  It was fixed 5 times for power surges and that parts were available at radioshack (fuse, rectifier diodes).  I don't know why i'm rambling on about all this useless stuff but I just gotta say they made things pretty well back in the 90's.

Instead, I spent four times the price of the speakers to buy a standard power adapter at Radio Shack, so my $4 speakers ended up costing more than $20.  If you want surprisingly decent portable speakers for a very low price and don't mind using only batteries to operate them, thse are great. product_title: Mediabridge ULTRA Series HDMI Cable (3 Foot) - High-Speed Supports Ethernet, 3D and Audio Return [Newest Standard]
review_headline: Best HDMI cable on the market!
review_body: Okay okay. maybe not \\"the best\\" but bang for your buck you can't beat Media Bridge.  I've been using these cables now for 2 years and also been using/recommending them to friends, family and people I've helped set up blu-ray players, HDTV's etc.  $10 for a cable with high quality wrapping, gold plated connectors, 6ft length and Cat 2 certification.   Look up other 'name brands' and you could end up paying $50-$120 for a cable like this.  Each cable comes in its own box, wrapped with both connectors covered by a plastic connector to avoid damage.      I've not had a single failed cable yet from Media Bridge, and even if one does fail.. at $10 it is a cheap replacement.   DO NOT BE FOOLED by expensive HDMI cables.  HDMI cables are not like your older component/composite/SVideo cables.    Those cables transmit \\"analog\\" signals.  In other words think of a sound wave. That is your signal.  Air distorts the signal so why not nitrogen infuse the cable for less corrosion and resistance.  All that fancy stuff works on those cables since it helps prevent signal degradation    HDMI cables work in \\"digital\\"   that means 1's and 0's    while you still transmit a \\"signal\\" the HDMI line carries it as 0's and 1's to the source by reading the signal it got from either your cable line or satellite etc.  a $1000 cable vs a $1 cable won't make any difference in your signal since they both get the same identical signal. You are just paying for \\"name\\" and \\"flair\\"  a $150 cable can fail just as fast or easy as a $1 cable.       As I said earlier, I've yet to have a failed cable from Media Bridge or had someone come back to me saying the cable failed.  Excellent product at an excellent price.   Currently I use 1 cable for my Samsung 40in 1080p TV   1 cable for a 46in Sharp 1080p TV  and 1 cable for a PS3 and it detects as 1080p no problem.    I've also tested these out with the 360(friend has a 360) and his Sony TV gets 1080p perfect picture and his 360 also gets 1080p on them.  He was upset too because he spent $80 on a cable and the Media Bridge was just as good

product_title: NuForce - NE-6 - Earphones
review_headline: Audiophile's take on the terrific NE-6 earphones
review_body: The NuForce NE-6 earphones are very good sounding earphones and an exceptional value.    I am a long time audiophile (some would say audiophool) and my main audio system is definitely reference quality helping me appreciate what recorded music can and should sound like.  I generally share my biases at the start of my reviews so there is no ambiguity about where I am coming form.  And I have many points of view regarding headphones/earphones.  Although head and earphones can match and often surpass the accuracy and resolution of high end speakers they do not get the sound stage right.  The music always appears to be coming from the middle of your head versus from a natural space in front of you.  So spending a lot of coin to achieve the last degree of accuracy and tonal quality but never achieving even a remotely lifelike soundstage seems like a fool's errand to me (unless you are using the earphones as performing musician - a whole different kettle of fish).  There are headphone amps that add circuitry to correct this but then you are mucking up the sound quality with another layer of processing.   I prefer the sound and comfort of over the earphones to in-ear phones but for anything active or on-the-go, forget that.  Even just walking around who wants to use big ol' \\"cans\\".  So unless your are listening at home I opt for in-ear.  Finally, my point of view is that nearly all earphone use today is with iPods/MP3 players.  While iPods are capable of excellent sound quality, practically that is rarely achieved.  The music files need to be lossless and many of the devices lack the output  juice to drive phones to their dynamic potential.  Because of all this my feeling is that phones for an iPod should not cost a lot.    Well these baby's cost less than ANY Apple iPod.  An excellent starting place.  They come with four different earpieces.  Finding the right one is critical because if you don't get a solid seal inside your ear you will not hear the bass these phones arecapable of producing.  The sound of the NE-6 phones is very musical.  Very good detail and great tonal balance.  The strength of the phones is in the mid-range where most of the music lives.  The errors of the phones are ones of omission.  The treble lacks that last bit of sparkle but for long term listening that is a thousand times preferable to pumped up, exaggerated, hurt your ears high notes.   The slightly rolled off top end is in balanced with a lack of the lowest notes - to my ears the bass rolls of around 30 or 40 Hz - but make no mistake, there are plenty of deep and realistic low notes.  Perhaps most meaningful, these phones sound many time better than the standard white earbuds.  Better in every respect.  To get better sound than these you will need to spend three times their cost.    The quality of the phones seems solid for the price.  NuForce is the real deal too.  They are coming on strong as a company offering an expanding line of superb sounding products at industry altering, reasonable prices.      If you listen to highly compressed digital files (e.g. 128 kbps) using an inexpensive iPod/MP3 player have your fingers run to Amazon.com, don't walk, and pick up a pair of the NE-6 earphones.  It's a most complementary match.  And a waste to spend more and a crime to keep listening to the stock white phones.  If the ratings allowed a half star I'd give the NE-6's 4 & 1/2 stars.  For value they'd get 5 stars plus.  For absolute sound, 4 stars, which for the price is a home run.  I'd also like to see all earphones come with flat wires to minimize tangling.    Bottom Line: You can spend more or less for phones but why when these sound so good and are less than $40.

product_title: Belkin Conserve Valet with Energy-Saving USB Charging Station
review_headline: It saves power and organizes your charging
review_body: I've read quite a few very intelligent reviews that criticize this device.    I suspect some of them may relate to a defective batch, and some folks found this device to be underwhelming.  It serves a purpose that many just weren't thinking about.    Either way, I must say I really loved this product for a variety of reasons.  I've been unplugging my power bricks for recharging devices for a long time, ever since I got a special meter that detects energy usage and learned these chargers cost money even when not in use.  So to start, this product actually addresses a specific need that I suspect a lot of people didn't realize they had.    Does it charge everything?  No.  I charges my phone, my wife's, and our 2 bluetooth headsets (at the same time).  I've tested it on mp3 players, and it charges all of my various ones.  It failed to charge PS3 controllers, which I think is a big shame.  This seems to be because of amperage limitations.    It consistently left all my devices fully charged, with the unit off by the time I returned to unplug them.  Based on the wattage I saved, I will save $81 per year, according to this: [[ASIN:B000RGF29Q P3 International P4460 Kill A Watt EZ Electricity Usage Monitor]] and my power bill's rate.    Operation is simple.  Push the green button and it will charge until everything is charged.  It has an indicator lamp.    I love the fit and finish.  The construction quality is good.  The rubbery top and the slight angle present my phones in an attractive way.  The usb cables provided (two, a micro USB and a mini USB) were too short for my use.  I think you should simply expect to buy your own as I did (before I even had this thing).  Wrapping them around the slot beneath the tray, and plugging into one of the 4 USB ports is a snap and it provides an uncluttered look.  Consider how cluttered 4 charging devices can be!    To sum it up: this is a device that solves a very specific problem.  If you're only looking for a USB hub, this is goingto seem like overkill.  If you're trying to charge something large, this won't support it (which is a legitimate complaint a few have, but I don't share).  However, it fits my needs perfectly and worked perfectly.

The Terk TV44 will support 4 rooms IF a separate switch is used between the Terk and recievers. It will only support two receivers mainly as is on Legacy LNB dishes (must use all 4 in and out ports, two lines to each LNB) and can be used for three receivers on a triple sat dish with switch built-in on LNB head. If your dish is only a twin sat dish, then you only need a TV42, not this TV44. But like I said, it only does two receivers mainly, not four as is with no other parts.

product_title: MartinLogan Motion 12 Floorstanding Speaker (Black Ash, each) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: A Reasonably Priced Fabulous MartinLogan Speaker
review_body:
I am not an audiophile, just someone who likes to listen to music. I probably would not be able to differentiate between the nuances that distinguish an $80,000 pair of Avalon Acoustics speakers from a pair that cost a couple thousand, but I also have never been one is satisfied to buy a pre-packaged system of components. I have always shopped at high end audio stores but my purchases are on the lower end of what they have to offer. I have always looked for the best sounding speakers I can get for the best value.

Set up was easy. Install the grill covers and since the speaker will be sitting on carpet, I installed the included MiniETC spikes. These pointed feet screw into the bottom of the speaker, firmly situating it on the floor which improves bass response and imaging. These are sharp feet and may damage a normal floor. Once installed the speakers should not be moved or the spikes may break or the floor harmed. The speakers arrive with rubber feet so if more concerned about flooring damage, than ideal sound, they can be left as they arrive from the factory. Wiring is easy because either bare wire or banana plugs may be used.

For the last three weeks I have been listening to the MartinLogan Motion 12 and am simply blown-away by its quality. The room is a large open style family room and kitchen configuration with a vaulted ceiling. It is easy for sound to get lost in this space. I followed the User Manual guidelines and allowed for a 72 hour break in period which essentially entailed playing the speaker at 90 dB before doing any critical listening, but even at that volume it was impossible not to be impressed.

product_title: Eveready Battery Co Ener 4Pk Aa Hyd Battery Nh15bp-4 Batteries Eveready
review_headline: Everything Old Is New Again featuring the Energizer Bunny
review_body:
This product is advertised as the [[ASIN:B0041FWAXK NEW Energizer Rechargeable NiMH AA Batteries]]. But once you received it, you may be shocked to find out that: the rated capacity of those NEW batteries is just '2300mAh', lower than the previous generation of '2500mAh' Energizer NiMH cells. So are you really getting a new and improved product, or just some old inventory from many years ago?

The fact is, Energizer has discontinued the '2500mAh' series of rechargeable AA NiMH cells, presumably due to massive complaints about rapid-self-discharge problem. All new Energizer rechargeable AA cells on the market now are rated '2300mAh'.

I have tested four of those new cells, using the Discharge/Refresh function of my [[ASIN:B00077AA5Q La Crosse BC-900]] charger/analyzer. Here are my findings:
- Fresh out of the package, those cells hold an average of 330mAh, or just 14% of the full capacity.
- After fully charging them for the first time, they hold an average of 1040mAh.
- After two more discharge/charge cycles, the average capacity improved to 2340mAh

Based on the above observations, I can conclude that those 'New' Energizer cells are just ordinary NiMH cells with lower capacity. They are not the LSD (low-self-discharge) type pioneered by [[ASIN:B000IV2WAW SANYO eneloop]]. This is very disappointing, because other name-brand battery makers have already introduced LSD products similar to eneloop, such as the [[ASIN:B001KYFZ6Y Rayovac Hybrid]] and [[ASIN:B000XSA60I Duracell Pre Charged]]. In contrast, the Energizer Bunny simply 'rolled back' its battery technology to circa 2004.

The only positive thing I can say about those 2300mAh Energizer cells is: they _probably_ don't self-discharge as badly as previous generation of 2500mAh cells.

In summary, those so-called 'New' Energizer NiMH cells have capacity just slightly higher than LSD NiMH cells (2000-2100mAh), yet do not offer the advantage of lower self discharge rate. As of this writing, this product is priced at nearly 2x higher than LSD cells. So it is just a bad deal.is priced at nearly 2x higher than LSD cells. So it is just a bad deal.

I looked back at the ad on the partner site (OWC- MacSales.com) and yes, in very, very fine print there is a disclaimer that it only works on one Mac at a time.  It renders the drive pretty useless as a network backup device to be used with Time Machine unless you're only using one computer.  It's too bad because otherwise it seems like a very good product.  If you're only needing to backup one computer on your network it will be just fine I'm sure.  Just don't expect more than that from this product. product_title: Axis 41700 Compact Digital Indoor Antenna
review_body: My review is mainly directed at people living in urban (downtwown or brick buildings):    Obviously the price is great, and it's coax for the connection so of course install is easy. But does it work? I suspect a suburban liver may have a very different review than an urban dweller. This device absolutely does something, my reception did indeed improve. Unfortunatley this is a digital device, so going from \\"no signal\\" to just enough signal to be frustrated by what I'm missing isn't much of an improvement.    Why do I think I'm having this problem: My problem, and one that is going to be likely to impact anyone else who lived in an urban environment, I live in an old brick building in a city with taller buildings. So I'm getting no direct signal other than what can bass through several brick walls and steel modern buildings. Now I'm less than five direct miles from almost every transmitter in town, but I'll wager that if I was 50 miles out and in a wood-frame house in a suburb I'd be getting a better signal.    The other issue other urban dwellers will have is even if you're willing to run coax all over the home you are still unlikely to have more than two directions you can point your antenna at, and you're unlikely to have those pointing towards your local transmitters and be unobstructed.    With all that working against it I think this antenna does a darn good job, just not good enough to make a workable difference in my particular case for the reasons above. I have no problem believing this antenna is objectively a 4 or 5 star item for someone in a penthouse or a suburb with fortunate proximity to a signal source.

When I'm done using mine, I simply detach the cord, wrap it LOOSELY around the headphone band, and connect the male end to the female end so that I don't lose the cord in transit. product_title: Bose SoundDock Portable 30-Pin iPod/iPhone Speaker Dock
review_headline: Good sound, but seriously overpriced like much of Bose equipment
review_body:
This portable sound dock probably has the best overall sound quality on the market for all the currently available portable iPod players that are battery-powered (however the competition here is frankly not very impressive, so saying that it is the best of this group is still perhaps not a ringing endorsement of the sound quality - no one would confuse it with the latest KEF speakers). In any case, the sound quality is listenable and certainly decent for such a small player.

It does have a number of nice design features, including the ability to switch playlists and artists using the remote control, depending on where you are in the iPod menu system. If you select one of your playlists, you can scroll through all of your playlists and select any one of them. If you are within an artist menu, you can do the same thing in terms of moving up and down through all of your artists. However, it does have some major limitations, principally that you cannot control any function of the dock without the remote control, suggesting that losing or damaging the remote control is basically going to render the dock unusable.

I also think frankly that it is seriously overpriced, and would recommend searching for a used or reconditioned one (I bought mine slightly used and saved significant money). Bose obviously thinks highly of themselves and believes that no one should be able to buy Bose equipment at any kind of discount. I frankly don't think that their stuff merits such a special status, but they have been very successful in their own marketing and rigid price control efforts. My first unit was DOA, suggesting that despite their great emphasis on list pricing only, they haven't got the quality control thing down, at least not quite yet. For these various issues (price, questionable QC), they should lose one star at least. But still, good player with good sound, and decent battery life. If they sold it for $300, and allowed you to control dock functions without the remote, would be five stars.

December 2012 Update

Some interesting and troubling developments. After several years, the speaker cones began to buzz rather badly. This was because the voice coil had essentially disconnected from the speaker cone. I took the dock apart and was shocked to discover how cheap the speakers were - a single driver that is running full range and without equalization except for some support at the low-end from a transmission line loading (a fairly standard Bose approach). The drivers couldn't have cost more than $5-$10. I replaced them with a polypropylene cone driver that cost $24 apiece - what a transformation of the sound, esp in terms of vocals. It is worth mentioning that these five dollar drivers were the heart of a $400 music dock. In light of this discovery, I have changed my rating to three stars and further downgraded my impression of Bose in general. product_title: Velodyne VX-11
review_headline: Velodyne quality at an unbeatable price
review_body: The Velodyne name has been synonymous with fine subwoofers for years.  In my audiophile days prior to CDs, I listened to a number of Velodyne subs in various high-end audio shops.  At that time, the Velodyne selections were fewer in number and the prices were in the high hundreds to a couple of thousand dollars.  As much as I wanted a Velodyne then, I couldn't justify the price.  So I was somewhat skeptical that the Velodyne sound could be had for this price when I ordered the VX-11.  Any speaker can rumble low frequencies, but a good sub provides punch and clarity to the low frequencies.  The reviews I read were very favorable, and I am pleased to confirm those ratings.  Definitely a quality subwoofer at a bargain price, especially considering that the subwoofer is self-powered with an onboard 100W amplifier and doesn't require an external power source (like back in the day).  Of course the VX-11 won't stack up to the higher-end models from Velodyne (also available from Amazon), but for the price point you won't find a better sub.  It's amazing what an excellent sub can do for your listening experience.  Two controls are provided that allow adjustments to the volume of the sub and the crossover point, or the point at which the sub begins to kick in and produce the lower frequencies that your regular speakers cannot.  There is no right answer to these settings - it's a matter of personal taste.  Tweak the knobs, sit back, and be blown away!

product_title: Kingston Apple 667MHz DDR2 SoDimm iMac and Macbook Memory
review_headline: iMac users Do Not Hesitate to do this yourself!
review_body:
My iMac \\"Agatha\\" is almost 4 years old now. When I first hired her she was lightning fast. At least it seemed that way to me.
But after I've learned to use her better and for more things to do all at once she seem to be taking a little more time to think things over between applications.

We considered (she and I) getting her \\"implants\\" to boost her confidence and make her feel younger again. I assured her that I loved her and she would always be good enough for me, and more than I really deserved, but you know how they get when they feel old.

I was worried about the cost of the surgery down at the Genius Bar, but it didn't seem like a do it yourself project to me, I was afraid of damaging her.
We bought the Kingston kit 4GB size.

I lay her on her back propped up on a book, removed two phillips screws from the center bottom panel, revealing two boards and two levers.
Popped the levers open with my fingers, wiggled the boards loose, put in the two kit boards, closed the levers, replaced the panel (two screws), and the job was done.
plugged her in and now she the fastest thing on the planet again (or it seems that way to me).

The only ill effect is that I seem to have lost that little spinning wheel that used to show up when I asked Agatha to do something different than what we were doing.
I'm not sure where it went, but its okay I never knew what it was for anyway. She doesn't seem to miss it.

Now she moves from task to task, almost before I ask her, and seems quite pleased with herself about it.
I recommend this to anyone who wants to give a special Christmas present to the one they love, in my case Aggie.
And don't be afraid to do it yourself. It is \\"me\\" proof and doesn't need anymore instructions than the simple few I've just shared.

Edward M. Cline Raleigh NC.

The form-factor of the ear-cups was smaller than I expected but they were nonetheless comfortable - I had to fully extend both arms to fit the cups over my ears properly, and even then it was still touching the top of my head. I have a large but not huge head, so if you wear a hat bigger than 7 5/8 these headphones may simply be too small for you.    Follow-up comment: the noise-canceling stopped functioning after only four hours of use. The power light no longer turns on, and I know it's not the batteries fault - I tried four different ones, all of which work fine in a torch, and the unit still doesn't function. review_body: This Sharp mini component system is one of the worst purchases I have made in years. This renders the speakers useless to anyone that wants to better fill their room with sound by spreading the speakers apart.  Luckily, I had an old set of Sony speakers with functional long wires, and they worked with the Sharp player.    Unless I'm missing something in the manual, there is no \\"OFF\\" function.  That's right, you have to unplug this piece of junk just to properly turn it off.  There is what Sharp calls \\"stand-by\\" mode.  However, this mode consists of the display giving off an annoying Las Vegas style laser light show in your bedroom, which likely draws more power than simply leaving the unit in regular \\"ON\\" mode. If anyone knows how to make stand-by mode resemble and actual OFF mode, please advise.      How an well known electronics company like Sharp can screw up two basic functional aspects of their product is absolutely mind-boggling.  I will never buy anything from Sharp again.

After setting it to receive NOAA notifications for your area, you'll not be without proper warning.  You cannot not hear this!! It would wake the dead!!  And it is true that you cannot set it for the type of warning you want (for instance, you will get flood warnings whether you need them or not), it is your option to ignore the warnings not relevant to your situation. This is a good thing since I sleep like a rock and would not hear the tornado siren.  And when not sleeping, generally DirecTV is on and I can hear the warnings through-out the rest of the house.      A must have as far as I'm concerned.

product_title: Sony Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones
review_body: I purchased these without first reading the Amazon reviews and was concerned once I had read them that the headphones would be worthless. I recently tried them out on two cross country flights using five different airplanes. My conclusion is that they do, indeed, work on reducing the constant rumbling background noise but only reduce it by about one third. If you push them hard against your ears they will cancel another third but, of course, this is not practical. Part of the reason that they do do not block out more noise is because the earcups rest on the ears, they do not surround the ears. For this reason they are also uncomfortable if you wear glasses as they push the ears into the glasses' sidepieces. On one flight my row mate had a set of expensive Bose noise canceling headphones with ear cushions that surround the ears and he let me try them. I found that the noise cancelling was far superior but that there was a constant, noticeable, white noise hiss that was as irritating as the remaining noise from the Sony. The smaller earcups on the Sony also make it easier to pack. I only listened to the in-flight channels so cannot comment on sound quality.

Gets very good reception, sound is better quality than an alarm clock radio, but I wouldn't classify it as a premium sound system - if you're not an audiophile then you'll be extremely happy.  There's a little counter light underneath that is great for seeing a little bit without ruining your night vision.  The remote control was unfortunately line of sight to the front only - we don't really use the remote.  The flip-down MP3 holder is pretty slick - it uses a standard headphone jack to plug in, so it works on almost any MP3 player, phone, etc. - the holder is big enough to hold an iPhone or even the Evo, but with a bumper on the Evo didn't quite fit.  The instructions are decent and you do want to read them for the installation as it comes with a cool paper template that makes measuring for the installation really easy.  Only complaints are the remote not being bluetooth or something that would work from the back / through a wall, and the 10 channel presets need to be cycled through instead of forward/reverse navigation (to go from 2 to 1 preset you need to go up to 10 then start back over at 1).

product_title: Phoenix Gold DTX-960 Studio Reference Grade Toslink-to-Toslink Cable, 6 meters
review_body: So, lets break down their selling points:    * High-performance fiber optic cable with highly polished elements    Quality of fiber really only matters for the length of a run.  As long as the light shows up at the end, the cable works.  At a insane length of 6m, I hardly think fiber quality maters as long as it isn't opaque.  \\"Highly polished elements\\" refer to the ends of the fiber.  If the light cannot get into the fiber, you don't have a connection.  As long as they don't cut the fiber with a chainsaw, you should be good for 6m.  Nothing special.    * Accurate audio signal transfer for greater clarity with enhanced transparency    Accurate signal transfer means that this cable delivers the light from point A to point B.  If they didn't do this, they couldn't market this as a TosLink cable.  Basically tells you that you aren't buying an expensive rope.    * Gold-plated connections for low signal loss, improved conductivity and oxidation resistance    This one leaves me lost for words.  Now why would gold plating help the transfer of light?  It doesn't.  It doesn't matter if the cable can conduct electric as the sole purpose of the cable is to transfer light, in fact, it might be seen as a reason to not buy this cable as it could accidentally short something else out.  And oxidation resistance, if they had made the connectors out of plastic they would not run into oxidation problems in the first place.  There is no reason to use metal.  It just wastes the already scarce gold supplies we have.     * Extra durable blackscope opaque jacket, all metal non-magnetic barrel    Ok, they say it is durable.  This might be important if you expect to yank this cable out and stomp on it daily.  If you are using this cable in a studio environment then it isn't going to be moved very often if at all.  Again, waste of metal.    * Measures 6 meters (20 feet)    Only valid selling point in the entire description.  I can't imagine them not being able to measure.    In short, if youwant an optical cable, get the cheapest that works.  If it breaks, buy another cheap one.  You can find 6 meter cables for a few bucks.  As long as light goes from point A to point B, you will get the best sound quality the connected devices can offer.

product_title: MartinLogan Motion 8 Center Channel Speaker (Piano Black, each)
review_body:
Martin Logan - once a very high end speaker company - has now entered the market of mere mortals. These are for those who want an upgrade from the standard fare Cambridge Soundworks, Boston Accoustics, etc. speakers.

This is the center channel speaker for a home theater package. At a minimum, you will also need two front speakers, two surrounds and a sub. The ML Motion line-up has all of these options - or you can try to match from other manufacturers. HOWEVER, be forewarned that these are 4 ohm speakers. You will need to be very careful to match these with others to be sure you are not missing parts of the register, and are still timber matched.

I found this center channel to be very crisp, clear and tight. Since the center channel is mostly for dialogue, I really focused on watching tv and movies with this - and not music. Both male and female voices were crisp and clear. I did not notice any muddled dialogue.

The speaker itself is beautiful. It is a very shiny high gloss black. It is a fingerprint magnet, but comes with a wipe cloth. The posts are a bit different than you are used to seeing, but they work well for both bare wire and bannana clips. The speaker uses two 4\\" paper cone drivers and a tweeter. The tweeter is really the key to these speakers, as the cone drivers are fairly standard fare.

The speakers come with ample mounting hardware for either wall/surface vertical/horizontal mounting. The MartinLogan plaque comes attached to the side for vertical mounting, but can be pulled off and reattached to the bottom for (more common) horizontal mounting (or it can be removed alltogether). I don't think the grill can be removed, and mine came with an extremely small white mark on the grill that could not be wiped off - not sure what it is, but I couldn't wipe or scrape it off.

One downside is that this is not a very efficient speaker. I haven't measured it myself, but it seems to be published at 89 dB @ 4 Ohms.

It is tough to tell for sure, but I don't think the second 4\\" cone is a slave. It seems to be wired.

If I were in the market for a 5.1 system of these, I would suggest the [[ASIN:B0035FZ124 MartinLogan Motion 4 Bookshelf Speaker (Piano Black, each)]] for fronts, [[ASIN:B0035FZ11K MartinLogan Motion 2 Bookshelf Speaker (Piano Black, each)]] for surrounds, and a [[ASIN:B002O3W2SO MartinLogan Dynamo 1000 12-inch Wireless Ready Subwoofer (Single, Black)]]. In my opinion, going with floorstanding speakers at this level is not necessary. You really won't see (er, hear) much of an improvement over the bookshelf models. (Of course, I'm speaking in generalities here, since I have not reviewed these specific bookshelf vs. floorstanding speakers.)ll for sure, but I don't think the second 4\\" cone is a slave. It seems to be wired. product_title: Sony BRAVIA DAV-DZ170 Home Theater System
review_headline: Really Nice Setup With Really Nice Price
review_body: Sony's Bravia line has yet to disappoint me.  This home theater in a box is a really nice setup.  It doesn't have the flexibility of a high-end receiver like a Denon or Onkyo, but that's not really what a home theater in a box setup is supposed to do.  It has one HDMI output, but no HDMI inputs, and only one optical input.  If you've got a newer model tv, that's all you need most of the time.  If you can run all of your HDMI sources into your tv, you can just run the one optical cable to this receiver and you're ready to go.  It's plenty powerful for most living rooms and gets loud without losing much resolution.  The subwoofer the weakest aspect of this set, but it's not that bad.  You can turn it up in the settings if you want a little more bottom end.  I take it back, the weakest aspect of this set is the proprietary input system for the speaker wires.  Sony isn't the only company to do this, so it's hard to single them out here, but it's still annoying.  I prefer to use lower gauge speaker wires, but the proprietary speaker plugs make that almost impossible.    Overall, I prefer this setup to most component systems because A) it doesn't take up much space B) it reproduces sounds evenly and accurately C) the DVD upconversion is pretty good and D) the price is very nice.  I down-sized from a 7.1 component setup and don't regret it for a second.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8GB (4th Generation)
review_body: I have been reluctant to buy into the whole Apple brand.  The idea of being locked into iTunes and Apple for everything just wasn't appealing-- still doesn't appeal! review_body: I am very impressed with this.  Set-up is very simple and I have it sounding great pretty much immediately. What I lvoe is that the sound is very, very balanced and you don't have to mess with each speaker like a traditional 5.1 system to make it all sound right in your particular room (the 5.1 sound system in my bedroom is always getting tweaked and I'm never 100% happy with it)    As other reviews have mentioned, the sub is built into the receiver.  This means that the sub has to be in front of you to use the remote.  no problem for me, that's where I wanted it anyway.  But that could be an issue for some.  the sub is pretty tall, so I had to change some thigns around in my entertainment unit, but thats not a big deal really.    the biggest problem I have is that Sony loves using propritary wire connectors for the speaker wires.  there is no reason for this.  The wire isn't that long either.  I assume sony sells a longer one at a ridulous price.  But that's ok.  Despite the connectors, these are just plain old speaker wires. product_title: Onkyo HT-RC270 7.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this receiver from amazon when the gold box deal came out.  It was a great find to go with my martin logans that I purchased from a similar amazon deal.  This was my first time setting up speakers and a receiver and it was a breeze, though it was time consuming.  I purchased the speaker wire myself and banana plugged it and ran it through some walls and under my baseboard to my receiver.  This took about 6 hours or so, but I didn't have any bumps in the road.  Connecting the speakers to the receiver was fairly easy and the auto calibration is amazing.  I had an issue where my rear speakers were plugged in incorrectly.  I had them in side rear and not just rear.  The calibration came up with an error, but I was able to fix it after seeing which speakers were registering an error.  It works perfectly with all of my devices (PS3, Dell Zino, Cable box).   I have a 3d tv and it looks great running through the receiver.  I would also recommend purchasing a universal remote.  I went with the harmony 900 and I love it.  It was also very easy to set up.  The sound is great on my speakers/receiver combo and I highly recommend it.

product_title: AudioQuest K2 Terminated Speaker Cable - UST 2.44 m Plugs 8' Pair (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Reminisce with me of days of yore when our beloveds walked in somber glades
review_body: Do you remember her on that somber summer day, when she sat below the willow trees and plaited your hair with the fresh dandelions of summer.  Do you see there beside her, in the grass, those terrible AudioQuest K2 Terminated Speaker Cables -- serpent-like and full of foreboding coiled evil.    Water the fields with your tears, they will not bring her back.  Listen to the crystal clear sound of mountain bells reverberating against your eardrums.  That clarity is AudioQuest K2 Terminated Speaker Cables sounding the death knell to everything you have loved, and will ever love.    As the salt water wells in your eyes, cradle these $6000 cables close to your slowly fading heart, and gnaw rabidly on its rugged rubberized insulation.  Nothing can stop the inevitable rupturing of your sanity.  Feel the last vibrations of hope fade from your soul as you dangle these premium cables from the willow branches above.  Swing now from your neck, pendulous, as you mark time for the approach of the next idiot who would spend $6000 for a god damn pair of speaker cables.

review_body: Took this All-in-one travel plug to Hungary, Serbia, and Austria. Never had an issue. Totally familiarized myself on it's setup before I left the country. product_title: DISCWASHER - REFILL FOR RECORD CARE SYS (RCARD1046)
review_headline: Got dirty vinyl? Clean it with Discwasher!
review_body: If you are a lover of vinyl, you will want to keep it clean. This is the perfect way to clean it. Unless it is EXTREMELY dirty, this will take everything off of your records. Now, I give this a 4 out of 5 for two reasons. 1: If you buy the new kit that comes with the brush, it is crap. Use one of the original brushes. It goes one way, making sure that it will pick up dirt and dust, but the new brush does not go one way, making sure that you will pick NOTHING up. 2: It is very easy to use too much discwasher. If you put too much on, it will not come off the record, and if not taken care of ASAP, it will dry and ruin the record. Don't be too generous. Just put a small amount on and it will work great. So, if you listen to vinyl and care about it, this is a must have.

product_title: Griffin RoadTrip 4030-ROAD Ipod FM transmitter with cradle and charger for Ipod - White
review_body: It is not bad at all, I have a 2G iPod touch and it works great with it. I couldn't find any reviews saying if it worked with 2nd generation itouch but it does, it just doesn't charge, which is kind of good because it won't kill your battery life. The plastic adapters are a little small for my itouch, but you could still force the iPod in without breaking anything. It also comes with a cable so you can use a usb power source to power the transmitter, but that way won't charge any iPod because it plugs into the headphone jack. It fits fine in my car,and it doesn't slide around in my car's power outlet. The sound quality is better than I expected, overall if you are ok with it not charging, and want a good FM transmitter, I would recommend this one.

product_title: Sennheiser Closed Circumaural Hi-Fi Headphone
review_body: Tryed this pair of HD428s on high output and low, good equipment and cheap. Compared it to my open air HD414 headphones from 1978 (open air tends to push sound, but these closed HPs isolate and concentrate sound better). For the money, you can't beat these closed circumaurals for sound exclusion (ambient noise just barely audible), comfort (light wgt), and performs well on all equipment. If you want to spend $2-500 on headphones for slight changes in technical performance, go ahead. Sennheiser is way ahead of the curve on headphones, they have been for decades. You will not be disappointed in good bass, not punchy, great mids, not mushy, and clear highs, not screamy. It even makes a Sony Discman sound great. Cheap soundcards are no problem, good soundcards even better. The video dude on this HD428 was right. Great sound isolation of jet noise for long flights even at low volume. Only downside to them was the plastic headpiece makes occasional noise when head or jaw moves, but design is very comfortable. Good job Sennheiser!

Headband a bit large for my head, even at smallest extension.  (On edit - barely the right size if I push them back a bit.  Anybody with a smaller head than mine would be out of luck.)    If you are going to be upright and not moving vigorously, they should be fine, and they sure are cheap! Although this adapter is wired to carry the audio also, you should be aware that not all MacBook models actually have audio folded onto the HDMI output, and not all HDMI TV's will actually accept the audio. In my case, my Panasonic TV (only 1.5 years old), will not work with the Moshi and MBA for audio.

This is not really a big problem for me since I want my audio (carried separately from the headphone output) to go directly into my sound system anyway, because my sound system is simple stereo. Be sure to check all your electronics for audio compatibility before ordering, because the HDMI standards and connectors have not yet been finalized, especially if your components are even as little as a year old.

Using a separate audio cable, I was able to stream a Netflix movie with no problem. Although it's a bit expensive for a mere cable, it's less expensive than a Roku or Apple TV or Netflix enabled wireless Blu-Ray player, which are the alternatives.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4-WH In-Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphone, White
review_headline: The design, materials and sound make these an all around winner
review_body: Like many of you out there, I have gone through the cornucopia of ear buds through the years.  I usually buy the 30-40 dollar brands with good reviews (Sennheiser CX-300, Radius Atomic Bass etc.)  Its seems that while living up to the reviews, they lack an element that gives them that \\"over the top\\" feeling.  The CX-300's are bright and full sounding, but they don't have the \\"girth\\" of the S4's.  Sound quality aside, the CX-300's are constructed of plastic and have little re-enforcement around the wire stress zones.  To me, this is as important as the sound drivers because what good are ear buds with no signal?  The S4's have a sturdy wire casing and a solid rubber wrap around the stress points.  The Radius Atomic Bass have the same build problems as well.  They have an amazing bass response, but the fit of these required constant tweaking for me and the wire casing wore out on the left ear after 4 months.  The S4's have a build quality far superior to any ear bud in the 30-40 dollar range.    As for the sound, these will make you want to burn your music to 320kps or FLAC files... no kidding.  These are so detailed, you can hear a difference in the compression ratio's of the songs on your mp3 player.  The dual magnet drivers reproduce every kHz with very little color.  The experts are right about these.    These fit me best with the \\"wire behind the ear\\" method.  There is a wire toggle to cinch up the loose wire.  I wear them with the wire behind me as well.  With a jacket on, these are almost invisible.  The oval ear tips are indeed more comfortable as well, but I highly recommend getting the Comply T-100 foam tips for superior comfort.  Its not that the silicone tips irritate the ears, I just noticed that if I moved my jaw around while jogging or chewing gum, the seal in the ear canal gets broken after a while. The foam tips are also more secure and much more comfortable, its the difference between having a chunk of plastic or soft foam in your ear canal.    I recommend breaking these in for at least 24 hrs.  Just plug them into the earphone jack of your computer and put your music library on shuffle (and repeat if you have less than 24hrs of music).  Turn up the volume to about 30% louder than normal and forget about them for a day.  This is VERY IMPORTANT... for any ear bud.  Its like a new pair of nice running shoes, they may cost 200 bucks, but they won't feel right until you put some serious miles on them.      I highly recommend these ear buds for the all around design and sound quality.  You will not be disappointed!

product_title: PowerGenix ZR-PGX1HRAA-4B 1 Hour Quick Charger with 4 AA 1.6v NiZn Rechargeable Batteries
review_headline: Safety hazard - hydrogen outgassing from NiZn cells
review_body: These NiZn batteries produce significant amounts of hydrogen gas under some conditions that are normal operating conditions for other types of AA batteries such as nickel metal hydride (NiMH) batteries.    First, these NiZn batteries operated well for a few dozen cycles in a one-cell flashlight with about a 0.5 watt power draw.     But a couple of days ago I put them in a two-cell flashlight with about a 1.75 watt power draw. This light is waterproof, sealed with o-rings. The batteries worked fine when I used the light to walk through the woods a few times and for other short duration uses.     Tonight I used the light for about an hour and a half to two hours. While working on some plumbing I noticed that the flat rubber switch cover was distended into a hemisphere, bulging out half an inch above its housing. This happened during a period of a few minutes since the time I had last handled the light. The rubber cover felt hard when touched, and I couldn't press the switch to turn the light off. Subjectively, it felt like pressing my thumb on a 10-speed bicycle tire to check its tire pressure. The head of the milled aluminum flashlight was somewhat more than lukewarm, but that is its normal operating temperature. The lamp was operating at normal brightness. Nothing else seemed unusual.    I was wearing safety glasses at the time, and unscrewed the tailcap next to an air vent. The gas pressure escaped with a pop. When removed, the batteries were slightly warm. There was a small drop of clear liquid at the base of one of the batteries, but no other visible residue. The batteries themselves were not bulged, which means that they must have effective gas vents built in. One of the batteries measured 1.62v no-load voltage shortly after being removed from the light, and the other measured 1.58v.     Reading up on this, I found that the gas is hydrogen, generated by the nickel-zinc chemistry in these batteries under the \\"right\\" conditions.     If I hadn't noticed it, these batteries would have kept producing hydrogen until something stopped them. This particular flashlight has a weak point as far as pressure buildup is concerned, which is its on-off switch.     But I have another flashlight that's machined from heavier aluminum alloy, and it doesn't have an on-off switch, for reliability and ruggedness reasons. You turn it on and off by turning its waterproof sealed tailcap. The failure mode on that one would be blowing the head or tail off.     These batteries are going in the garbage bin in the next few minutes.     Powergenix needs to start printing an informational warning on the packs of these batteries about a substantial pressure buildup of explosive hydrogen gas, that these batteries produce in significant amounts.     Amazon also should include an informational safety note on the product page about this. Granted, few people will use these batteries in sealed units where the gas can build up to high enough pressures for something to give way, but it's not a vanishing number of people either.    Update: Dec 28, 2010 -  According to an e-mail I received from \\"N. Lee the Engineer,\\" who has also reviewed these batteries, the hydrogen is generated when two or more batteries are used in series, and one battery becomes more discharged than the other(s). Hydrogen is generated by a NiZn battery whose voltage falls below 0.42 volts, as electricity flows through it from another battery that is at its normal voltage.     In short, using only one of these batteries, in a one-cell device, could not cause the battery to produce hydrogen.    He included a link to a better explanation of this. From that article:    \\"So if you are discharging your series string of NiZn cells at 1 amp, and one cell drops to <0.4V, hydrogen is being generated at a rate of 14ml/minute. ... You can see that the internal pressure of the cell can rise rapidly if a NiZn cell is overdischarged.\\"

product_title: Boston Acoustics P400 Aluminum On-Wall 3-Channel Speaker (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Good Start to a TV Sound System
review_body: We recently remodelled our family room, and as part of that project we installed a new media system.  We chose this Boston Acoustics soundbar for the front left, front right, and center channels of our 5.1 sound system for the TV.    This soundbar is actually three speaker-sets (one for the left channel, one for the center channel, and one for the right channel), with each speaker set including a 4-1/2 inch speaker, a 4-1/2 inch passive radiator, and a 1 inch tweeter.  Unlike some soundbars, this one does not include any audio decoders, equalizers, amplifiers, or other electronics.  It is just speakers. So you need some kind of audio/video receiver with amplifiers and the required audio decoder(s) to drive these speakers.    The best thing about this soundbar is the high quality sound.  It produces very clear sound that extends well down to the lower mid-range frequencies where a separate subwoofer can take over.  All soundbars are DEFINITELY not the same.  There are so many cheap soundbars out there that cost much less than this one, but every one of them I have heard produces cheap sound that lacks a clean lower midrange response.  They almost always sound tinny.  This one doesn't. This soundbar is definitely not inexpensive.  Perhaps you could find something that sounds just as good as this for less money.  If so, then buy it.  However, I did not find it.     The spatial separation is adequate, but not as great as one might get from separate left and right speakers that can be placed as far apart as desired.  Other than the price, this is the only drawback to this soundbar.  However, this is more than compensated for by the clean, aesthetic, installation with no visible wires.  We mounted our LCD TV from the ceiling, and we mounted this soundbar directly beneath the TV.  It looks terrific.  When matched with a set of rear channel speakers and a good subwoofer, this soundbar can provide a theater-like experience in your home.     Bottom line:  this soundbar looksand sounds great.  If the quality of the sound, and the appearance of the installation are important to you, and if you can afford it, then you should consider this soundbar.

review_body: I first found out about the headphones almost 9 months ago, and I had no idea why they hadn't appeared on Amazon two, three, four months after Panasonic's announcement. I finally saw them here for $129.99, which I purchased right away.  A few days after placing my order, the price had dropped by $20 and a week later by another $5. On September 1st, however, my headphones arrived.  The lowdown:  They look much more stylish in real life than they appear in Amazon's picture. They feel and are of quality build, and they are very comfortable. The hard case that they come in is a real bonus, as it really protects them quite well. When you wear the headphones, they sit very comfortably on your head and around your ears. In fact, the comfort of the headphones is one major factor that wouldn't be lost on anyone. I immediately put the supplied battery in the unit and turned it on to make sure it worked. It did. From that day on, Sep. 1st, I haven't had a need to turn the unit back on. The passive noise cancelling works so well that I almost don't hear the people talking at the next table at a coffee shop, or at the library.  I have tried the unit in different places, and believe me, I never felt that I needed to turn the active noise cancelling on. The headphones are that good.  So if you are on the fence whether to buy these or not, buy them! At this price point, and especially compared to Bose 15 headphones--both in terms of price and performance-- these are just magnificent.  But let me tell you one thing that I don't like about these headphones, and this is only from my standpoint. When you wear these, despite being very comfortable, they kind of look (and sit) splayed out on the head. I mean, I have seen headphones that look very stylish on the head with a nice fit, but these ones are not like those. When the headphones are on the table, by the stereo, or anywhere other than on your head, they look very good. It is only when you wear them that you see the aesthetic design could have been better, especially if you don't have much hair on your head. Other than that, it is just straight-As in all other aspects.

product_title: Emerson Simplicity High Fidelity AM/FM Table Radio with Companion Stereo Speaker – NR31
review_body: Like some of the other reviewers I always considered Emerson products to be less than adequate substitutes for higher-quality products. I used this radio at work for a couple of years, and now it sits in my kitchen providing really great sound either from FM or from an iPod plugged into the aux in jack.  No tone or balance controls, but that hasn't been a problem.  The sound is full, with plenty of bass.  This is a fraction of the price of the Tivoli/KLH radio, sounds at least as good to my ears, and is stereo as well.  A great buy.

product_title: Sony Walkman NWZ-E354 8GB Digital Music Player
review_body: this is my 2nd sony walkman mp3 player. i got this one for my wife. its small,easy to use easy to download music and any other media. simply drag to media box and it does the rest. or use windows media sync for mass downloads. it also has great battery life 30 hours. it sure beats itunes.

review_body: I have 5 of these of various colors and purposes. These fit perfectly in my ears and are incredibly comfortable for me. I use them for everything especially for running and working out. product_title: Atlona Technologies AT-HDVIEW VGA to HDMI Scaler Up to 1080p/60Hz (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Works well but you have to figure it out yourself
review_body: On receiving the Atlona, I plugged it into my laptop and into the HDMI port on my TV, allowing it to select input and output resolutions automatically.  The result was OK, but not perfect.  The image on the TV chopped off some of what appeared on my laptop screen.  I'm not sure if this is \\"overscan\\" or \\"underscan\\", but I wanted it to look better.  I switched to manual modes on the Atlona and discovered that all the input resolutions it claimed to support were not actually supported.  Regardless, simply switching the input resolution did not fix the over/under scan problem anyway.  The user manual contains a cryptic reference to fixing this by changing the TV's settings but it didn't offer any specific guidance, only noting that \\"all TVs are different\\".  After fiddling with the TV (a Sharp Aquos 52 inch LCD) and studying the manual for awhile, I discovered that when an input is configured for a PC, you have the option of displaying the video \\"bit by bit\\".  When I chose that option, the result was perfect, and it actually supported a sufficiently high resolution to get a good quality picture.  I was able to stream episodes of \\"The Event\\" I forgot to record on my DVR onto my TV with good results.    I'm happy with the unit.

product_title: Sanyo Eneloop AA NiMH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries - 4 Pack (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:

product_title: Apple iPod shuffle 2 GB Orange
review_body: This is the perfect platform to listen music from, it's VERY portable, just clip it anywhere on your clothes, and rock it.   The buttons make it very easy to change music, you don't have to looks through your iphone or ipad to skip song, just feel the buttons and skip the song, it's perfect when I\\"m on the track or on my motorcycle or any other situations when you don't want to take out the player and look at it to change songs. product_title: Bowers & Wilkins Zeppelin Mini Docking Speaker for iPod
review_body: I spent about 6 months on and off researching iPod dock systems.  I was willing to spend up to $300 to buy a device to play music stored on my iPhone 3G and iPd Nano, as I've transferred all music from CD's to iTunes on my MacBook, and our stereo speakers were old and needed replacement.  I checked Best Buy and was not happy with any of the products I could demo with my iPhone.  They all seemed cheap and the sound ranged from tinny to too much bass.  Interesting that the Bose display does not let you try your own music, only listen to a canned Bose music demo.  Went to my local Apple store to see what they carried and listened to the Mini Zepp.  Loved the sound quality, form factor and size so bought it from Amazon.    I couldn't be happier with this product.  We put it on a table in our living room.  It sounds great on low volume - I like to have it playing when reading.  I can crank up the volume and hear it well in the kitchen and throughout our house.  And of course, it looks awesome.  It is perfect for us and fits our needs.  I highly recommend.

product_title: AmazonBasics Universal Tilt TV Wall Mount for 34- to 65-Inch Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Don't waste your money at a big box store - this is a fantastic mount
review_body: We've got four televisions mounted on our walls, so I've got a bit of experience with different types of mounts.  When we decided to move our main TV above our fireplace I had to buy a tilt mount (I was hanging a 50\\" plasma - total 52lbs).  I was planning on just going to Costco and buying their mount again (they sell the 'Simplicity' brand mounts).   We order just about everything on Amazon so I decided to search here before I headed out to Costco, and I'm glad I did.    The mount arrived in the typical frustration-free packaging.   Everything was clearly marked and easily unboxed.  The mount is incredibly thick and sturdy.  I was also impressed by the built in level and the included stud finder.  I used neither, but they were nice touches.    Pros:  1. Incredibly sturdy.  This mount is built to last.    2. Nice tilt range of motion.    3. Level built into mount base.      4. Price.  25-50$ less than Costco's mount, and so much nicer.    Cons:  1. The mounting hardware was just okay (plastic anchors for concrete/plaster).  I like to use my own metal lag shields for concrete/plaster, but the holes in the mount are too small to fit the 3/8\\" lag screws I bought.  I rummaged around until I found a couple of other 3/8\\" lag screws that had a slightly less tapered end.  I installed 2 of my metal lag shields on the top edges of the mount along with 2 of the included thinner lag screws on the top as well, and then installed 3 of the remaining included plastic lag screws and anchors on the bottom of the mount.  Overkill?  Maybe, but I'm kind of OCD about making sure this thing stays where I put it.      2. The concrete anchors require a 12mm drill bit.  Seriously, no one sells a 12mm bit.  You can use a 15/32\\" which is about .003\\" smaller and should work fine, but I was a bit flustered by this as well.       This mount is a great value and crushes the Costco mounts in quality.  I wish the holes in the mount were a tiny bit larger, though.  I would highly recommend this product to anyone.

product_title: Vantage Point AX2ACL01-B Tilt Ceiling Mount for 20" to 42" Displays (Black)
review_body: I purchased this ceiling mount for a new Samsung 40\\" LED LCD TV.  I liked the finished look of it and its compact size since I wanted the TV up closer to the ceiling but also have the ability to tilt the TV down a bit towards the bed since it would be used in our bedroom.  I made a mistake when ordering and did not realize that the TV had a 400mm screw pattern and this mount could only support up to 200mm.  I could not find another model I liked so I contacted Vantage Point support and they offered to send me a custom adapter plate they had designed to make it work with the Samsung.  The adapter plate arrived just a few days later as promised and it worked well.    The instructions are pretty much pictoral in nature but were easy enough to understand with a little bit of trial and error.  The materials are also very solid so there is no doubt they will be able to hold the load.  My only hardware issue was with the provided mounting screws to attach the whole thing to the ceiling stud.  Even with the pilot hole drilled I was having to apply so much torque to the screws I was breaking them.  Mostly likely due to the hardness of the wood.  I ended up buying some heftier lag bolts from Home Depot and was able to attach the whole thing fine.    Very happy with the end result.  It was easy to make the final horizontal and tilt adjustments to get it just the way I wanted it and it looks good.  I'm happy with the quality and value of the product and would recommend Vantage Point to others.

product_title: Sony SA-W3000/Z Subwoofer (Each, Black)
review_headline: Great addition to my soundbar setup
review_body:
I added this sub to a recent soundbar purchase, not to a real home theater setup (but I have thoughts on that as well below).

I bought the soundbar to help crank up the volume from a 50\\" Panasonic plasma in our family room. This is the most used / watched TV in the house, but the sound has always been weak (even my hate-to-spend-money-on-these-things wife agreed). I bought a decent 6 speaker Vizio soundbar and hooked it up. Much better sound, but ehhh still needed more. Enter this sub, which rounds out the sound so much better than the little tiny 8\\" wireless subs that come with most soundbar+sub packages.

I have the sub tucked behind the TV stand / cabinet, which is nice since it's out of site but kind of a pain since I can't be satisfied with a single volume and x-over setting for all situations. The room isn't huge, maybe 13'x20' but this combo could fill more space I think. Wood floors could be why. This combo cranks very well for movies (Matrix 2) and music (pandora via the blu-ray) but it's a little much for just watching the news or spongebob, etc. so I leave the soundbar off for day to day TV.

The sub auto-off works fine unless I have the volume set to a normal / non-movie level in which case it annoyingly shuts off even when there is clearly (by my ears) a bass component being lost when it clicks out. I'll just set it to always be on. I have a 5.0 setup in my basement (surround, no sub) which has been fine, I planned to add a sub and the priority has gone down over the years. I hooked this up to try it out, reset the system to use and balance with the sub, and it was a little weak in surround. The addition wasn't a impressive as with the tinny soundbar. Right below the other room so same size, but carpeted and suspended ceiling soaks up some I think. It sounded great when I just cranked music and set the receiver to 2.1 mode, really great actually. This thing can get loud, don't get me wrong, but for a full surround HT setup I think most folks will expect more.

Pros: price (when I got it $120's), several connection options, performance as part of a 2.1 / soundbar setup (ideal use IMO)
Cons: self-off triggers well above no signal, not enough for a 5.1 (or larger room) surround setup

Not sure why Amazon has currently decided to not sell the sub themselves, as far as I am concerned everything was as advertised / listed....expect more. Pros: price (when I got it $120's), several connection options, performance as part of a 2.1 / soundbar setup (ideal use IMO) Cons: self-off triggers well above no signal, not enough for a 5.1 (or larger room) surround setup Not sure why Amazon has currently decided to not sell the sub themselves, as far as I am concerned everything was as advertised / listed....

product_title: DLO HomeDock HD Entertainment Dock for iPod (Black)
review_headline: DLO -- Consistently Good Ideas, Consistently Bad Execution
review_body: I should have learned by now, having both a Home Dock and Home Dock Delux.  Both fell short of my expectations, which are NOT elaborate.  I simply want a device that performs as advertised.    So I bought one, mostly as a cheap experiment (the HD Delux was $150). product_title: ZLive Speaker System with Docking and Recharging Station for Zune Players
review_body: I loooove the look of this system. The time is super convienent for my desk at work, as well as having the remote in case someone comes in my office or my phone rings. product_title: Apple iPod classic 160 GB (7th Generation) NEWEST MODEL
review_body: I am the ultimate music lover, I rotate through my music collection regularly.  The idea of an iPod that can hold around 40,000 songs was simply the best idea I had ever heard. And it was wonderful... at first.     I purchased my first iPod in October 2009 and in May 2010 it went into Hard Drive failure. The Genius Bar people fixed it.  I took it back home.  When I tried to reload music, I found the problem had not been fixed. When I returned to the Genius bar again, they gave me a replacement.  I thought it was just a fluke, but in October 2010, the same exact thing happened.  Once again, the problem was hard drive failure.  Now, not even two months later, the same issue happen.  At this point, the I even had the Genius bar check my computer to be sure it was not my MacBook causing the issue. (It was not).     So, in just over a year, I am onto iPod #4. While I use my iPod often, it is not abused.  It is in a padded case with screen protector, and has never been dropped, jostled, wet, or used to exercise.  The iPod technicians told me that my iPod is basically the last one with moving parts.  And because it has large parts and a big memory, it is a strain to run.  I basically have the St. Bernard of iPods. It's huge and wonderful, but a big slobbery mess!     While I have no complaints about the people technicians, they were helpful and patient, I do have a problem with the product.  Why bother to make something that will not last long? If I spend $249 on a product, I feel it reasonable for it to last longer than a few months.

product_title: GBC HeatSeal H115 ID Badge Pouch Laminator w/ 200 5mil Luggage Pouches
review_headline: You need to be handy with repairs
review_body: Purchased only the H115 badge laminator from this merchant, My Binding, back in March of 2010 at a great sale price of less than $15. 4.5\\" is the widest you can run laminating material through the machine and any length. You ONLY want to use 7 mil stock! Even though they say you can use 5 mil - DON'T unless you enjoy opening the machine up to pull out the material wrapped around the rollers (which nullifies the 1 yr warranty). Takes about 5 mins to heat up and after the 'smiley' face is lit, run material through the sealed short end side first; being careful to feed it through. Does not use 'carriers' even though the box of laminates tend to give you them. Involved in a large name badge project, I have assisted in running over 300 pieces through this machine and my husband only needed to take it apart twice for repairs. Seems to run quite hot and adhesive from the laminating pouches tends to get on the rollers, so be sure to run a piece of folded blank paper through a few times when you are done with your work to help remove some excess before turning off the machine to cool which tends to take ~ half hour. Have also made bookmarkers and small signs with this. Don't notice a real big difference between the pouches whether generic or name brand - they both do a fine job. Still works today, laminates well, and for us, it was a great purchase costwise but a pain for repairs and any problems we fix ourselves, but it would not be a deal if you had to send it in; so you'll have to decide for yourself if this will work for you.
