product_title: Asus M4A785TD-V Motherboard
review_body: Had to do an upgrade, and discovered to my horror (HORROR!) that everything was now SATA(!)...But...but...I've still got IDE! Thankfully this board is still available, with one precious IDE channel for my two drives. And a pretty decent price to boot!    And so began the Great Upgrade Of 2010. Of course the board works well, has connections for all sorts of peripherals -- internal and external USB, HDMI, onboard video and audio etc. -- everything you'd need for a mid-level computer even in this day and age.    Some notes of interest:    First, documentation is pretty good. The bits that aren't explained involve more advanced BIOS settings, so most users wouldn't be messing with that anyway. That said, would be nice if there was SOME elaboration on those settings.    Second, I was loading this motherboard with the AMD Athlon II X3 440 3.0GHz. Connected it all up, and Windows XP didn't boot -- kept crashing on mup.sys . After a whole lot of debugging, finally discovered that for some reason the motherboard was detecting 4 cores on the CPU, when it in fact has only 3. After setting the CPU Activation to \\"Manual\\", and disabling all but Cores 2 and 3, Windows finally booted up fine.    In fact, Windows thinks I've got a Phenom II X4 B40...this apparently can happen according to reviews for the CPU. Maybe when I get round to moving to Windows 7, I can actually use that 4th core...    Third, the motherboard does have some trouble with my Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse. Sometimes the board will reboot when I try to get into the BIOS with this keyboard plugged in. But plugging in a second non-wireless USB keyboard and using this to get into the BIOS did the trick.    So overall I do like the board. But it definitely has a few quirks, as highlighted above.

product_title: Sennheiser Dynamic High Grade Performance Premiere Headphones
review_headline: Great headphones - comparison with Denon AHD2000 and Seinheiser HD448
review_body: These are great headphones! They are extremely comfortable physically and as a listening experience. They are superlight and soft on the ears. The sound is very detailed and the bass seems well-balanced (not to soft not too loud). Note that there is a significant sound leak if you play the music at loud levels. They also don't isolate external sound/noise. So if you are listening at home that is great because you can hear the phone ringing, but they may not be a great choice if you listen while working next to someone at the office.     I typically listen music through my receiver (Harman Kardon HK 3390) and a Musical Fidelity V-DAC. I listen to pop, rock, post-rock, trip-hop and electronic.    Some comparisons that would help those who are considering various models:    I also own a pair Denon AHD2000 which sells at a similar price. I bought that pair to listen to music at the office (unlike the 595 those are closed cup, and hence don't leak sound). I like them both a lot but if I had to choose one of the two I would choose the Sennheiser (by a small margin). The Denon have incredible bass which I love but they feel like you are at the middle or the back row of a concert hall, while the 595s make you feel that you are more towards the front. The Sennheiser seem to be brighter have a bit more detail. In terms of quality of materials, I like the Denon more.    I also tried the Sennheiser HD448 (they sell a about half the price) before buying the Denon. As perhaps expected, those felt very inferior to the 595s. I returned them and bought the Denon which I kept. In my opinion either the Sennheiser 595 or the Denon AHD2000 are definitely worth the extra $100 - $120.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16 GB Purple
review_body: I've owned a few strictly mp3 players, none as cute, but all cheaper. I'm a guy and functionality comes first. Which means playing stored music is the main priority. The ipod does a pretty good job with sound quality. The ipod comes with a lot of features(very cool), what is odd (compared to other players) is, just scrolling thru all the features just to get to the option to play music. (I guess apple wants you to SEE the other options, as opposed to just hearing music) Eventually you can get thru and hear some music. The pretty visuals it displays so you can flip from album to album is also very pretty. (but I guess if itunes doesn't sell the music, the album artwork won't display- sad face-but not a showstopper)   With my other mp3 players, if you turn off the player in mid-song, the moment you turn it on, it proceeds to start playing right where you left off. The ipod wants you to re-discover it's menu options (come on man, play music!)  I like the ability to create playlists on the itunes and importing them to the ipod is very easy, and I dig that. What's odd is that if I want to shuffle the music, I have to do so on the itunes player, and import it again. On other players, once you flip to shuffle, it just shuffles the music.   Battery life- total crap. I own a Sansa e260, and use it at work. I can go over 18 hours on a single charge. I took this ipod out for a hike, and it was almost entirely drained after 2 hours (good thing I had my sansa in my backpack to finish the hike). But I guess that is the trade-off for such a diminutive music player.   The player is thin, and I'm careful with it. I don't dare exert any bending pressure on it, because it will break. The Sansa is twice as thick, had been dropped a few times, and keeps running. (the Sansa doesn't have any of the extra features like the ipod - Nike+, making videos, stuff like that).   Other knocks, ability to add extra memory(a feature that is not on very many players anymore). The Sansa has that ability(but probably not new Sansa models), not the ipod. With the ipod, the stated memory, is all there is.  Glitches, after two days with my ipod, it seized-up. Frozen. I went to youtube, and there is a button pushing, dial holding sequence that will allow you to reboot. That is what I did, and it worked.   With my Sansa, I was shaving, and I knocked it into a sinkful of water. Screech, it stopped working. I shook the water out, pulled the screws, removed the battery, and left it sit for the rest of the night. The next day, I re-assembled it, and it has been running great ever since. (If your Sansa e200 series freezes, pull the back, remove the battery, re-assemble, and that is your reboot)  But this is about the ipod. I like it, it has a lot of features, it's very pretty. It's delicate, battery life is short, I won't be out running in the rain with it on, kind of wish the option for \\"now playing\\" was the default for when you turn it on. No big disasters, mainly the big gig is the battery life.  Oh, and it's pretty.    I came back and changed this to one star. After running 5 miles, the ipod deleted my workout. POS.

review_headline: A sight and sound for sore eyes and ears
review_body: I'm not exactly an old hand with devices like this so please consider this to be a review from a lay user.  So I was a bit nervous when I received this 16GB MP3 player.  I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to set up and how enjoyable it has been to use.  Packaging and Installation   The packaging was surprisingly easy to use and I was happy that I was able to open this product without resort to scissors, screaming, cursing, slapping on the kitchen table followed by my usual end strategy: handing it to my daughter for her to open.  Installation was as simple as can be. Insert the USB cord and let nature (and your computer) take its course.  The USB cord was too short at 12\\" and that is my only complaint about installation.  Synching and downloading songs etc. already on my computer was simple and easily accomplished.  Audio and Visual Quality   Both were excellent. It is a small screen at 1.2\\" but the resolution and quality is first rate. I've listened to music and video while travelling and it is perfect for passing the time on a plane.  The ear phones are good and do a nice job filtering out the world around you. Access to FM radio is an added plus for me.  Touch screen functionality  The touch screen is functional and very efficient. However it does take some getting used to and it took me a while to learn how to navigate around.  Again, this may be a function of my generally not being a sophisticated user of high-tech gadgets but I had to go online and download a user manual in order to figure out some of the bells and whistles.  On balance I am quite happy with this product and don't hesitate in recommeding it to anyone that likes a well-made player that has top rate audio and visual capabilities.

product_title: Pro Ebiz 4 GB Video MP3/MP4 Player with 2.8-inch TFT Touchscreen
review_body:
This is possible the cheapest touch screen mp3 player I have ever seen. It works as said, but there are reasons for the price.

Pros:
- It plays MP3's without any interference from software. You can simply hook it up to a PC and transfer over to it like an external drive. I always love the ability to avoid having the use the same computer every time I plug in an mp3 player.

- Pictures look nice. The screen may not be mind blowing in clarity, but it makes your pics look nice enough.

- Opens txt files. Works well for people who can convert their ebooks.

- Battery life. My iPod Nano had a battery fail within months of ownership. Even after a year of near daily use, this player still can hold a charge for over a days worth of music.

- Plays video, but good luck getting the format just right.

- Price, nice and low.

Cons:
- Cheap construction. Everything about this player feels cheap. From the ill fitting silicone skin provided to the vinyl looking bendable touch screen. The player feels like it weighs about as much as a pencil, and makes crackling noises after only the slightest squeeze. The on switch up top ended up breaking off thus making the player only turn on when plugged in, and off when left on pause.

- Touch screen. I don't know who it was that said that this thing was mistaken for an iTouch, but they must work for this player company. The screen, while usable, requires hard presses and noticeably bends inward as you use it. It feels more like you are pushing buttons under a rubber sheet rather than touching a screen. The included stylus works well for navigation, but i find it odd that there is nowhere to put it. What am I supposed to do when I am done tinkering with it? Just throw the stylus in my pocket?

This player feels more like a toy than anything, which is why I ended up giving it to my little sister. She liked it, right up until it broke.

If you are looking for the lowest possible player out there that must have a touch screen, well this will work for you. If you can deal with buttons instead, there are a slew of better build options out there.hat must have a touch screen, well this will work for you. If you can deal with buttons instead, there are a slew of better build options out there.

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Radio
review_headline: Squeezebox Radio vs. Aluratek Internet Alarm Clock Radio
review_body: Comparison of Squeezebox Radio and Aluratek Internet Alarm Clock    Ease of Installation    Both units are easy to install, IF you have experience with networks. If you have to call the Geek Squad to install a new computer on your network, these both may be a challenge for you and you probably should seek assistance. Note the power button for the Aluratek is on the BACK.    Entry of 128 bit WEP keys on my secure wireless LAN was easy and intuitive, and yes, you can see the entire key as you enter it. Squeezebox' is entered combination-lock style and Aluratek's is entered cell phone style. The units remember this key if they are unplugged. Once the key is entered, the units will then both add themselves to your LAN. Wired LANs can skip this step.    Each unit works in conjunction with an online web site to add internet radio stations. Once you enter your user name and password into the unit, the web site will then immediately add all favorites on the site into your radio.   Note: when you enter the MAC address into V-tuner to set up your account for the Aluratek, you have to use the numbers above the keyboard. Numbers on the number pad to the right may look the same but will NOT work.    Each unit can play internet radio, play your own music collection, and in addition, the Aluratek has a built in FM tuner and can play music from a \\"thumb drive.\\"    Aluratek has a remote control as standard, on the Squeezebox this is an option.    Differences    Audio quality is better by far on the Squeezebox. The internal speaker sounds pretty good for a small radio. The speaker on the Aluratek is just what you would expect from a 4 inch clock radio speaker: OK but not great. At higher volumes it is pretty bad. Connecting external speakers to either makes either sound excellent and overcomes this difference.    The Aluratek has a built in FM tuner, in addition to being able to tune local radio stations that have a streaming service on the net. This tuner is not very good even set to higher sensitivity: it had trouble picking up a local station that comes in clearly on other tuners, and even then it was scratchy and only in MONO.    The Squeezebox is able to work with Squeezebox Server running on my NAS and therefore a constantly running PC is not required. The Aluratek requires a PC running Windows Media Player, or similar streaming source in order to play music from your local PC collection.    Fit and finish and general tactile feel of the Squeezebox Radio is better. The Squeezebox also can accommodate an optional battery pack making it truly portable.    The Squeezebox has 6 preset pushbuttons. I got this unit for my non-technically inclined and visually impaired mother. But with only power, volume, and 6 station preset buttons she can easily operate it. The Aluratek however has nested menus which are more confusing.    The clock display on the Aluratek is bigger and more easily read without your glasses. The clock display on the Squeezebox is smaller, only runs when the power is off, and gets miniscule when the radio power is turned on. The clock stays on when the Aluratek is powered up. The display on the Aluratek is REALLY bright and can light up a whole room at night. The intensity is not adjustable, only the duration.    The Aluratek is designed to be a clock radio. The buttons on the top are bigger and easier to locate in the dark or when you are sleepy. The buttons on the Squeezebox are on the front and smaller (and more numerous)    The Squeezebox updated itself immediately upon connection (took an hour!) but the Aluratek update is completely manual. I tried to do this but was unsuccessful; maybe this was because it already had the latest firmware. Some way to know the version on the website would be nice, then you could compare that to what is onboard the radio.    The Aluratek comes with extensive documentation in English and French: quick start guide, manual and a CD, but the Squeezebox comes with only a brief quick start guide.Overall impression     I give the Aluratek 4 stars, taking off points for the poor FM radio, the non-adjustable backlight and mediocre sound quality on the internal speaker. The Squeezebox Radio gets 5 stars...see my other review of the Squeezebox Classic and Whole House Music Systems.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-1120-K 7.1 Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: it was hard but..good thing i waited....
review_body: like so many of you i waited, try to look at as many reviews as possible, weight the pros and cons of every manufacturer and at the end for a number of resons i decide to go w the 1120. i was lucky enough that i got mine at an incredible price from [...] through amazon and pay less the MSRP, and also got one of the very first units 3 weeks before arrives in amazon, which give me some time to put it to the test before writing this review. product_title: Digital Innovations 10185 Skip Dr. Motorized AutoMax Scratch Repair System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This thing is unreal.  It has repaired every disc that I own that was scratched.  It will remove all light scratches with out any problem, deep scratches can be fixed with multiple runs.  It cleared up some of my worst cd's so that I could copy them with EAC or dBpoweramp flawlessly.  The only thing that is annoying is that it's kind of loud when operating, but you'll probably enjoy listening to it as it works.    It will NOT repair discs that have scratches on the side with the label, but then again, NOTHING can repair a disc damaged in that way, because that is where the data is stored. (for those of you who didn't know) If that's the case, just buy a new cd.

product_title: BlueRigger High speed HDMI Cable with Ethernet 10 Feet (3m) - Supports 3D and Audio Return [Latest Version]
review_body: Ordered 2 of these cables to route them neatly behind the wall which my original 6' cable was too short for, and although I got them fast and the price was really good, they did not work.  I used one to connect a Panasonic BD player to a 52\\" Sony Bravia, and all I got was static/snow.  Tried the other cable, and that one at least showed the picture, but was still overlaid with static/snow.  Switched back to the 6' HDMI cable that came with the player, and picture was crisp as before.  Something is wrong with these cables.  I also ordered TOSlink optical cables of the same length from the same manufacturer, but I didn't test those out yet.  I am setting my expectations low.      For the price I paid for them, it's not worth it for me to ship them back, but lesson learned.  Next time don't settle for low-quality generic cables.

product_title: Klipsch Synergy C-1 Center Channel Speaker (Single) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this speaker to replace an older Yamaha center that came with my old home theater in a box package. I also have the Synergy F-1 floor standing speakers and kind of wanted some uniformity up front at least. The price was right too $79 is an amazing price for a brand new speaker.  When I got this I replaced the Yamaha speaker while the system was on and as soon as both wires made contact I could tell a huge difference. The sound is much clearer now. I have found that I don't have to turn the volume of my system up as much as I used to for those quite conversation scenes. product_title: Sony Earbud with iPod Remote Control
review_headline: Great Buds for iPhone or iPod for the Price
review_body: I just picked up a pair of these, and so far I'm pretty impressed.  Overall they sound pretty good.  The bass is decent, but not overly boomy like some.  The treble is very clear and can be a little thin on brighter songs, but not bad by any stretch.  They are a HUGE improvement over the stock Apple buds that came with my iPhone 3GS both in terms of fit and sound quality.  They block out environmental noise pretty well and the cords don't make too much noise when moving.  They fit in my ears well and are comfortable to wear for extended periods.  Not the best sounding buds money can buy but give a good listening experience and are a great bang for the buck.  The remote works exactly like the stock Apple buds and is a VERY handy feature.  I can skip songs, play and stop music, and answer calls without having to dig my iPhone out of my pocket and unlock it.  Very handy.  If you hold the center button down it will activate the voice control features of the 3GS as well.  I certainly recommend these to anyone looking for a better sounding and better fitting alternative to the stock Apple remote & mic buds.  At less than half the price of the comparable Apple in-ear buds with remote and mic, they are a steal.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa View 16 GB Video MP3 Player (Black)
review_body: I bought the 16gb Sansa view for one thing, playing music and at that almost all using Rhapsody's \\"all you can eat\\" music service.    I've had it for a few months.  Overall the player does it's job.  16GB is plenty of room to load more than plenty of a variety of music and comedy for road trips, work, et al.  The sound quality is not great but good (although as with other devices, I've bought good ear buds for this).  I haven't had any issues yet that have required me to reformat it nor has it lost track of it's drm license (this has happened to me with others in the past and it sucks.  One night you load a bunch of music and then in the middle of the next day, it claims the license has expired).    I bought this because it was a 1/3 of the cost of a iPod touch 3rd gen.  Sure, it doesn't do all those other things.  But I'd rather do all those other things with other things (e.g. my phone, my laptop, etc).  I bought this because in likelihood in another year and a half, I'll be able to get a 32gb iPod iTouch for 35-50% of the price it is today.      Good things for me :  a) 16gb for less than a $100  b) Good sound  c) Plays well with Rhapsody / MS DRM  d) Can delete individual songs  e) Can rate songs  f) Menus are easy to navigate    I'm putting that out there so anyone reading this review knows what I'm valuing in my evaluation.    What I haven't liked so far :  a) When unplugged it from the USB having it plugged in overnight, more often than not it will continue to behave as if it's connected.  Shutting it off and turning it back on resolves the issue.  Nevertheless, it's odd and unnerving.    b) About a week ago the screen went \\"fuzzy\\".  Was able to turn it off and back on and it seemed fine.  Nevertheless, it's odd and unnerving.    c) I've had problems dropping playlists onto it and all the songs transferring.  This could be Rhapsody issue.    d) Can't delete playlists from the device

product_title: GN Netcom Jabra GN9350e Dual-Connection Wireless Headset with GN1000 RHL for Desk and IP Telephony
review_headline: Great idea, great sound but poor quality and support
review_body: I have owned this headset for about 10 months.  I wanted a wireless headset that would work with my home phone as well as my PC.  I had expected to link my DECT 6.0 compatible cordless phone.  In fact, I purchased a Panasonic KX-TGA101S because it was also DECT 6.0 compatible.  When I tried to link the phone to the headset wirelessly, it wouldn't work.  Even after much digging on the internet and calls to support to Panasonic, it turns out all DECT 6.0 devices are not compatible and I never could get it to work.  Forget about Jabra support, they were not responsive.  OK, I thought, I'll just connect the headset to the handset wire of a non-wireless phone.  It turns out my desk/phone connection configuration puts my phone and my PC out of reach of each other and I never did get both to work.  OK, so I have a great wireless headset just for my PC - annoying but at least it works.  Until a thunderstorm rolls through.  Even though I use a quality surge suppressor which has numerous other devices attached to it (laptop, speakers, print server, printer, ethernet hub) and dozens of other pieces of electronic equipment around the house (many without surge suppressors), this was the only device to bite the dust during the thunderstorm.  It wasn't even connected to the phone line, so the surge couldn't have come through that way.  In any case, it's now a very expensive pile of junk - and no response from Jabra support.  No more Jabra products for me.  It does look nice and it used to sound great too.  Two other small issues: 1) hanging the headset up on the charging station was a bit finicky and sometimes required substantial fiddling to get the headset to connect to allow charging.  2) I wish I'd gotten a stereo headset so I could listen to music as well.  Now I have a chance!  I'm going to try a Bluetooth solution next but that will require me to buy *another* home phone set :-(.

product_title: Sangean Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio
review_body: I use this daily on battery power. The battery life is very good, even with cheap, no-name nimh rechargeable batteries. Batteries recharge quickly.     I've had it over a year and it runs like a champ. The sound quality is good given the small speaker size.   This is an above average radio.

product_title: Datacomm 50-3323-WH-KIT Flat Panel TV Cable Organizer Kit with Power Solution - White
review_body: We built our new home, and the contractor was supposed to have dropped power behind an outside wall for future mounting of our HDTV...four holes in the drywall later, no power.    Faced with now having to figure out how to safely and legally run power to my set, I stumbled upon this little gem.    It works great.  Installation was a snap, and the cable management really makes everything look clean.    For the headaches that this averted, it's well worth the price, and probably more.

product_title: Mediabridge - 3 Port Smart HDMI Switch
review_body: I needed a HDMI switch for my front room to complete an over fireplace plasma install.  Already have the Onkyo 607 running down stairs with the full 7.1 and 65\\" LCD.  That was overkill for the front room, just wanted simple 58\\" plasma and Bose 2.1 Lifestly system for TV and occasional BluRay when too lazy to go down stairs.   I tried several other so called \\"high end\\" HDMI switches from Amazon first but this little puppy is the real deal.  Read the fine print on those other guys - they have an output cable length threshold spec.  In other words if your running a single HDMI pipe in-wall up to to your monitor and juggling inputs from say 10-20ft away (or even 35ft in my case) they dont cut it.  What you end up with is washed out signal.  After reading some other reviews I was still as skeptic given the price but believe my friends, no AC adaptor and the remote and IR are a nice to have but are really a throw away because the box just does what it should.  You power up a new source and guess what, it cuts over to it.  It seems revoluitonary compared to the other offerings but really its like \\"duh\\" that's how it should work.  So the remote and IR extender stay in the drawer and this little guy just works as he should with no external power what so ever.  About signal quality - its excellent!  Again I am running exacly 35ft of output length via V1.4 HDMI cable (I got the latest future forward V1.4 and it works fine with this switch FYI).  The picture is great at full 1080P and 24 fps mode also fine.  My two minor gripes are its actually a bit too small for my taste - it would be better to have a size and heft more consistent with the scale of typical aud/vid components and I also wish that all the i/o ports were on one side of the device.  Why have them opposing - its silly for cable managment.  But these are small issues for the 20usd price point and the flawless functionality.  Also I dont like having to buy a seperate audio switch to drive the Bose but that not realla complaint about this device.  Finally, make sure you are using quality patch cables (i.e. the shorties from your source to the switch input) becuase i had some flicker in one source until I isolated the cheap V1.3 patch cable.  In short you cant go wrong with this guy and the price is right.

product_title: Bose(R) In-Ear Adjustable Earbud Headphones
review_body: I've had a set of the Bose® In-Ear Headphones since spring and really like them. They have great sound and the in-ear fit works really well. They are pretty durable too. But, it works well for both my iPhone and laptop. The rubber tips will come off some force if you are yanking them out in your pocket. product_title: La Crosse Technology BC-9009 AlphaPower Battery Charger (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Updated: I THOUGHT this was the best battery charger I ever owned.
review_body:
This is a really outstanding product. I haven't used all the attachments but I have used the AA and the AAA batteries included. I think they have excellent charge retention and enough juice to power modern camera flashes. The charger may seem a little complicated but the included instructions make everything clear.

The power adapter on this model was under a recall program and La Crosse technology sent me a new power adapter very promptly. Double thumbs up for excellent service.

--------

Edit: I have had this product since november 2009 and as of June 2010 one of the four AA batteries has stopped working for no apparent reason.
I have always charged it with the rest of the batteries, used it in my camera flash together with the other 3 batteries that came with it. However, now when I put these four in the flash, it will not power on. By putting them in the charger, I have found that there is one dead battery.The charger fails to detect the battery so I cannot even recondition the battery. It is done for. And now I am left having to purchase another set of batteries. I don't know anyone who has had a similar experience with rechargeable batteries.

--------

Edit 2: August 9th 2010

Okay so maybe the battery is not what is dead. I have read numerous other people post that the charger will not 'see' the battery unless it has some current left in it. The remedy was to use one of the 'dumb' chargers to force charge the battery and then put it in the LaCrosse charger. I performed that once and sure enough, the battery came back to life. But I cannot keep doing that all the time. So I don't care if it was the battery or the charger, I wouldn't recommend this kit to anyone. I'm looking for another battery charger myself.

product_title: Sangean RCR-22 AM/FM Tuning Clock Radio (White)
review_body: The Sangean RCR-22 AM/FM Atomic Clock Radio will not receive the time signal from the radio transmitter in Colorado. I followed the directions carefully, several times, and for several days, with no success.        I looked at the Sangean RCR-22 AM/FM Atomic Clock Radio discussions, for advice. product_title: White Mini Microphone for iPhone 3G 3GS iPod 2nd 3rd Gen classic Video
review_body:

After getting it plugged in, the Voice Recorder software (pre-installed on all iPod Classics) did not show up on the menu. I quickly realized that my menu was full (due to the options I had selected for the front screen such as Pod Casts, Movies, Music, etc). Once I \\"reset menu options\\" on the iPod and again tried plugging in the mini-microphone, the Voice Recording option showed up. Once you have a recording saved, the Voice Recordings option always shows up, even if the microphone is not plugged in.

Testing shows promise. I bought this microphone to record gaming sessions (Dungeons & Dragons, World of Darkness, Call of Cthulhu and other tabletop games). Sitting the iPod Classic on top of a notebook on the table in front of me (laying flat) it sounds great. I also tested it from sitting across the table and standing across the room. The microphone is surprisingly clear. I've recorded 8 hour gaming sessions and only used about a third of the iPod Classic's battery power. review_headline: I know my radios and this is a winner (updated 8/11/11)
review_body:

product_title: SanDisk Sansa View 8 GB Video MP3 Player
review_body: I bought my Sansa View because I travel a lot, and wanted something to watch videos on during long flights. The Sansa View is perfect for this -- the battery lasts for 6-7 hours watching videos, AND, unlike a lot of other portable media players, it can keep playing while recharging -- so you can use its computer cable to hook it to a USB battery extender (a gizmo that takes 4 AA batteries and provides the same power output as a computer's USB port) and keep using it even longer!    You can watch long (more than 40 minutes) video files on it without problems -- and it even allows you to bookmark your place in a video so you can restart from the same place later!    With the newest firmware, video playback is excellent -- the audio and video sync up fine, and it has only frozen once the entire time I've owned it (and I use mine a *lot*). Earlier firmware versions may have had some problems in those areas, but those problems are fixed now -- which is why you should install the firmware upgrades from the manufacturer's website as soon as you get your new player!    The player can connect to the computer as a \\"mass storage device\\" (like a USB thumb drive), so you can just drag and drop audio and video files onto it without using any special programs. It comes with free \\"Sandisk Media Converter\\" software for converting video files into a format the player can handle -- I wasn't very happy with the results, but there are plenty of other free programs out there for converting video files, so you can use a different program to convert the videos if you want to.    Say goodbye to boring in-flight movies, this little gizmo is a traveler's best friend! If you're looking for a portable media player with EXCELLENT battery life that can keep you entertained for hours on end, this is *definitely* the one you should get!

product_title: HIGH QUALITY AC POWER TRAVEL ADAPTER PLUG FOR EUROPE GREECE (SPAIN PORTUGAL) CROATIA RUSSIA UKRAINE THAILAND INDONESIA BRAZIL CHILE PERU BOLIVIA / WITH TWO PLUG-IN PORTS AND BUILT-IN SURGE PROTECTOR!
review_body: If you're a frequent traveller like me, you know you need adaptors in foreign countries to plug things in and charge cell phones, computers etc.  So many places have inferior sockets, especially anything less than brand new 4 or 5 star hotels.  I've used low quality generic adaptors many times and finally got fed up with the plugs falling out of the sockets, especially when weighted down with other cables or power supplies.  Not only is it annoying but it's also really bad for electronics, having the power go on and off intermittently.  Finally a really well made adaptor that stays put!  The plugs are made to a very high standard and the fit into a socket is a lot tighter than others.  A recent trip to Europe (I used 3 different ones) proved this.  In direct comparison to a generic adaptor the solidity of the connection was vastly superior.  The extra outlet on the top also proved very handy without having to use an extra distribution adaptor.  Why would you plug in a $1000 laptop with a 99 cent adaptor and risk hard drive damage?      As an audiophile, I also know that better connections make better sound.  Anyone who uses high quality aftermarket cables knows this.  Power supply connections are no different.  Trust me, if you care about what you're plugging in, this is the only adaptor to get.  Also, any outlets that can be grounded, are.  A lot of adaptors have no ground connection, if there's something there it's usually a plastic pin.  In any case I bought the whole set and am very happy with them.  For a few extra bucks, they are worth every penny.  Buy these, you won't be sorry!

What I did expect was that they would produce sound that isn't objectionable, that they would work as advertised, and that they'd last for a while given careful use.      The sound was more or less as expected - not objectionable, not great, but better than the stock earbuds that come with the iPhone.  These K316s were consistently difficult to get seated properly in the ear - and then they'd often come unseated during exercise! But, hey, nothing's perfect, right?, and headphones for working out are difficult to do, so none of this would have been enough to really put me off these headphones.  What did put me off them is that four weeks into their use the rubber retaining ring around one of the phones popped off, and the metal diaphragm beneath it, as well.  For a couple of days I kept trying to put the thing back together, but it continually fell apart and I could hear vibration from where the diaphragm wasn't properly seated.      All in all, I would say, the worst headphones I've owned in terms of durability.  And these are supposed to be robust for working out.  No thanks!  Now I have to try to get my money back or get a replacement pair, which is going to involve hassle.  Meanwhile I have to find something else for working out.  I suggest you look elsewhere.

product_title: Keyspan by Tripp Lite PR-EZ1 Easy Presenter Presentation Remote Wireless with Laser
review_headline: Not Unobtrusive Or Comfortable For Me
review_body: I bought this to see how it compared with the other remote presenters I use (Honeywell's VERY small presenter, which I really like, but have had problems with it not working consistently, Targus AMP03US, Targus with a mouse feature, Kensington 33374, my favorite because I like the USB connection that fits right into the device when you're done, and Logi-Tech, which has a timer and buzzer to remind you it's break time.) This Keyspan is fine for it's effectiveness overall and has some features others don't have--reviewed on this page already. It's flat so it would fit in a shirt or suit pocket      *It measures about 3\\" long and 1 3/4\\" wide, with the grip part being only a bit less at 1 1/2\\" wide. It's metal with a ridge that goes around the edges. So, for someone with a small hand or a small palm, it's essentially like holding a small metal throat lozenge container.     *Because it's metal and flat, it slides easily and can be pushed aside and off the table or podium when moving learning material around.     *It's white on the button side and grey on the back side, which looks different than usual and training participants have all mentioned it to me--which says something about how obvious it is when you're holding it.     *It has no grip area and is not rounded, so instead of holding it between thumb and forefinger as you can with other small presenters, this one has to be held (by me, anyway) with the whole hand. The photo on this site that shows a woman holding it, shows that it is more of a visible device than an unobtrusive aid. See how she has it in the palm of her hand with the hand up?    I loaned it to three other trainers--two women and a man--and they all said the same things, especially when comparing them immediately with a more comfortable and less noticeable remote.     I think this would be better for someone who is showing a few slides as part of a company presentation, so everyone is focused on the slides. For my use, several hours a day, daily, there are some drawbacks that keep it from being the best choice.

product_title: Altec Lansing iM-237 Orbit Ultraportable Speaker for MP3 Players (Silver)
review_headline: Good Portable Speakers For Laptop or MP3 Player
review_body: Overall these Altec Lansing speakers do a good job with what they're meant for and how much they cost.  I wanted a small and portable speaker that was easy to take with me either when traveling or just having it in my laptop case.      I use them as a speaker for my MP3 player, generally when traveling - and the sound reasonably fills a hotel room with decent sound quality.  I also carry them with me in my laptop case so I have a portable speaker when I need to show a video on my laptop and need way more sound than the internal speakers on my laptop.    Both for the MP3 player and the laptop the speaker simply plugs into the headphone jack and provides good sound.  You never have to worry about missing the audio cable for the speaker because it's attached and neatly winds around the base, which is a really useful touch.      The speaker takes three AAA batteries and has an on/off switch.  There's no volume control on the speaker - volume is controlled by your MP3 player or laptop.   The speaker also has four rubber-covered feet so it doesn't scratch furniture, equipment or slide around.  It also comes from a snug zippered case that will protect the speaker when you toss it into an overnight bag or laptop case or backpack.    The audio cable is only about 8 inches which is plenty for most uses.  There is no power cord so you have to make sure you have 3 AAA batteries.  I wouldn't consider this as a primary home speaker or a big party speaker - but for around $25 to $30 it's a very good travel/portable speaker for music player or laptop.

review_headline: I'm very picky, but I give this thing the green light.
review_body: I just got this in yesterday. Our first child is due in the next few weeks, and my wife wanted to have some music to listen to during the labor process at the hospital. We have an 8GB Sansa Clip loaded with our favorite music, but I wasn't sure how I'd be able to play the music without lugging some 80's style boombox (with an aux input) on my shoulder into the hospital. Enter this Altec Lansing device, a gem in the rough. Obviously, right out of the box I was curious to test out the sound. This thing easily fits in the palm of your hand, and already comes equipped with a 10\\" aux connecting cable that wraps neatly inside the bottom of the speaker so you don't have to buy your own. The box says the battery life will last for up to 24 hours on 3 AAA batteries, though I haven't tested that claim yet. There's only an on/off button on the speaker, so you have to adjust the volume using the mp3 player itself. Personally, I like the simplicity, because I had streaming music in 15 seconds out of the box. The music quality is pretty good considering the size. If you expect something booming and crystal clear out of a portable speaker with a 2.5 inch diameter, good luck because it doesn't exist. Honestly, I thought this thing would be a one-time use item, but am now excited for the possibilities. For practical purposes this device has countless applications. I can throw it under the stroller, take it to the beach, and put it on the picnic table during BBQs. It even comes with a carry case with strap and caribiner clip. I'm not easily impressed... but I'm impressed.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones
review_headline: Finally a noise-cancelling headset that delivers!
review_body:
I work in a helpdesk support area. It is VERY noisy. We sit in pods which means there is no sound barrier available to block any of the noise of the people around you who are talking on the phone, talking live to another employee, talking to themselves out loud, singing to themselves, coughing, snorting, burping, etc. (I think you get the idea.) While I do need to be on the phone for about 10% of my day, for the rest of my day I am writing code. Effort that requires concentration and near SILENCE. I have tried a number of headphones and found them lacking.

Today was my last try. There is a guy near me that I was ready to throttle because he is SO noisy. I bought these headphones on my lunch hour. They cost far more than I would normally spend, but WOW it is amazing. As he was jabbering away, I slipped them on my head and hit the switch and...he was gone...AMAZING. At some moments, during the day today, he or one of the other rowdy members of my floor got especially loud, but they were barely noticeable and very EASY to tune out.

Yeah these are what I consider very expensive, but for me they represent sanity and the ability to finally focus and get my work done. With the economy the way it is, I don't want to make waves and be a big whiner about someone being noisy; something management doesn't appreciate. With these headphones in place, it no longer matters. They are stylish and major comfortable. Overall WELL worth what I paid for them.

product_title: Altec Lansing Octiv Mini Speaker System for iPhone and iPod (Black)
review_headline: Sounds great for such a space-saving speaker
review_body:

2. peripheries - Not only can I use an ipod with this, I can also use a male to male cable to connect it to any other device that takes headphones. I've tried connecting it also to my laptop as well as my mp3 player, and it worked well - very secure connections.

Granted, compared to a full-blown speaker set at its same price range, the sound is a bit muffled and the bass is a bit lacking, but for its portability, I think it's a good trade-off. The sound quality is also effected by the device playing the music, obviously. My mp3 player had better sound quality than my computer!

Overall, I like the design. It does seem somewhat top heavy, but nothing has tipped, yet, so far.

product_title: Sony STR-DH510 5.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
After much research, this is one of the only economically priced surround-sound amps that decodes the surround-sound information in the amp itself before passing video on up to the TV. Many of the HDMI switching amps out there only switch the video, and do NOT decode surround (due to the DRM encryption on some HDMI signals) only 2ch PCM.

Look over Sony's site, they have alot of good info for this unit. For the price it would be really hard to beat.

Nice Stuff:
-Surround decode from the HDMI sources
-The remote also controls my Sony Blu-ray player
-The Main L-R speaker outs are selectable to use either full range speakers, or small surround speakers
-You can Name all the inputs whatever you want
-For a small home theater, sound quality is good
-auto shut off after 30mins of inactivity

Not so nice stuff
-Only three (3) HDMI inputs, i could have used more for later, but for now all I needed was my DishNetwork box, Xbox and blu-ray
-Only one of the three digital audio inputs (2 optical, 1 coax) is programmable to any input. This would have been nice to be able to assign any of them to the remaining analog video inputs
-Analog video inputs (Wii in my case) do not go out the HDMI output. While I didn't expect this, it would have been a nice touch. As it is I have to change my TV's input to play Wii. This is no biggie, but it would have been nice!

In summary, this is a great replacement amp if you already had an older surround unit, or if you want to pick and chose your speakers. Like I said, it's nice that it has a built in selectable crossover for the main L-R speakers.

My last Sony amplifier has lasted nearly 8 years. The only reason for me to replace it was to make switching video sources easier.
There, this is my 2¢ on the matter

product_title: Monster MC800HD-1M Audio Video Cable
review_headline: Overpriced and feeding on consumer ignorance!
review_body: It says \\"advanced\\" in the product name. So it's got to be worth the inflated price. Plus, if I spend a thousand dollars on a TV, then I shouldn't skimp on the cable. His advice: \\"Cheap cables that cost 75 cents per foot work as well as those that cost $100 per foot,\\" said Mr. Kane. \\"With the latest HDMI cables, if you see a picture and hear the sound, you know it works.\\"

review_body: I have the DB4 antenna which works quite well. I bought this one and for me its better at locking in signals 40 miles away, and its a bit less directional. I have two of these in my attic pointing at 40 and 35 mile distant transmitters. It is useless for VHF, but very well for UHF. product_title: LG LHB977 1000-Watt Blu-ray Disc Home Theater In a Box (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this to pair with my new LED LCD LG 55lh90.  Awesome combo. Everything syncs great and is very easy to use.  I ran HDMI cables from my cable DVR box and xbox 360 in to the processor and then HDMI out to the TV.  The Built in Blu Ray means No other cables to connect.  All you do is push play on the remote and it starts up (no need to change inputs or anything.  Couldn't be easier)  As a heads up, with this set up I stated, you do not change the input setting on the Tv at all.  To go from xbox to cable you use the input selector on the processor only.  Blu Ray requires no specific selection.  Just push Play!    I will share that after I hooked up the system and turned it on for the 1st time, I thought I made a huge mistake.  It sounded weak and crappy.  Then I realized that each individual speaker has its own volume control and there are several presets for sound that can be chosen.  Within a few moments I had it sounding very good.  One setting is called \\"Bypass\\" and this seems to work best most of the time.  It plays sounds as it was recorded and gives the true surround sound (assuming the source supports this).  For Sports events I use \\"Game.\\"  I find that it more fully creates a surround experience (it sounds like you are in the stands clapping with the fans around you). Note: there is a \\"Sport\\" setting but my ears say \\"Game\\" is the way to go...just my opinion.    If you really want to be impressed, pop in Blu Ray version of Avatar.  Assuming you have a capable Tv, you will see how awesome this Blu Ray player is.  I don't see how the pic could possibly get any better than what I'm seeing.  2 thumbs up here.  As for sound, you truly get immersed in the experience.  This system is powerful and performs very well.  I was concerned at 1st because the sub does not have its own power cord.  I wasn't sure it would be able to do the job...rumbling and deep tones that I like.   Fear not, it performs well.      This system has many features as you will read, but other than what I have mentioned I only tried out the YouTube feature.  Pretty cool.  I plugged in ethernet cable to the processor and clicked on YouTube at the Main Menu.  I showed my family some funny video clips just to see how it worked.  Again, is really cool and it works, however I'll probably leave the computer stuff to my laptop.    Ok, now I will criticize a little bit.  Sound quality is very very good, but of course it could always be better.  Keep in mind this system is priced from $500 - $650.  There are other systems costing thousands of dollars for a reason and you would assume (or hope anyway) that they could outperform a HTIB like this at this price.  So with this said, this system does sound great...but it sounds great for the money!  Actually to be fair, it sounds better than the money i paid...it could fall into a higher priced category and it would stand up.  My one biggest criticism of which my dad agreed, is that the high's could stand some improvement.  I like that pronounced ting you get from some good tweeters and this is missing.  After closer inspection I realized that what looks like tweeters on these speakers is just decoration.  They are Not Tweeters.  If they put real tweeters here, of course the cost of the system would go up, but I bet the sound would be that much more amazing.  Again, just my observation and opinion.    In summary, considering price, ease of set up and use, and pic and sound quality, I would highly recommend this for anyone looking for this type of system.  For die hard enthusiasts, get your wallet out and go higher end, but for the rest of you this system will more than meet your expectations.  I am very happy with my purchase.    dave

product_title: Sony EX Style Headphones with Deep Bass Sound

review_body: I used this mount for a 52\\" sharp aquos. compared with the price of other mounts for this tv it could not be beat.  it supports the weight (52 lbs) of the tv well as long as it is flush with the wall.  attaching the mount to the tv upright (as directed) puts the part that attaches to the wall off center and caused the tv to sag on one side.  to resolve this i had to attach the mount to the tv upside down.  it fit with no problems and the tv sat square and even. review_body: I have an iPhone 3GS, and recently purchased an aux in adapter for my car. product_title: Apple iPod shuffle 2 GB Black
review_headline: Horrible redesign to a product that was great to begin with
review_body: I wish I read all the reviews for the new shuffle before I bought mine, but have had nothing but trouble with it.  I finally called Tech support and determined that the problem was caused by sweat getting into the control box on the headphones.  I bought the shuffle mainly for working out, but apparantly the new design does not account for people sweating when working out!!!  The Tech support told me the only fix was to cover the control box either with plastic wrap or saran wrap to prevent sweat from get into the unit while still being able to control the shuffle.  I understand the unit is only for working out but having to wrap the control box makes it look horrible.  I asked if Apple has any plans to release new headphones that were better sealed to prevent this from happening and the quick answer was \\"NO\\".  There is a solution for Apple....go back and produce the previous generation which everyone loved!  I have finally given up and wrapped the control box in saran wrap with tape at each end and the unit seems to be working fine now!    Symptoms included:  1) songs skipping 2)voiceover keeps interrupting the song to inform you of playlist, artist, and title of song (even if you disable this feature in iTunes) 3) volume keeps decreasing to an extremely low level 4) unable to skip to next song.

review_body: I am powering the system with a Harman Kardon AVR 347, and I could not be happier with the sound.  The mounting brackets included with the speakers allow for a supper clean, and space saving installation.    I listed to a lot of electronic music and hip hop, and this system definitely has the power to fill my medium sized room.  Movies are also incredible with the system, with a little receiver tweaking.  COD MW2 sounds crisp and loud with the system.  Very happy.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 2 GB MP3 Player - Black
review_body: We have been searching for a very portable MP3 player at a modest price (<$100) with good FM.  My wife had an old Creative Zen mini player which had very good FM, but the phone plug is dying.  So we tried the clip.  It had much worse FM reception than any other player including many older ones.  It was subject to frequent fading and noise when moving around.  When compared to the IVO M260 the M260 had fair sound with higher static than the old Zen, and was almost acceptable, but the Clip was totally unacceptable. review_headline: WR-2 Humane Waking System is GREAT.
review_body: I purchased this Sangean specifically for the HWS.  It is soooo nice to be woken gently as the volume of the radio increases.  That was worth the price by itself.  Sound quality is very good from the front firing speaker.  Operating instructions leave something to be desired.  The unit is a bit large and heavy for a clock radio.    Pros: Humane Waking System, attractive cabinet, very good sound quality, antennas included.    Cons: Operating manual, tiny remote (I don't use it), somewhat complicated operation.    Tips:  I had trouble with the LCD display light illuminating and waking me instead of the music from the radio.  Even at the dim setting it's like a landing light from an aircraft.  To keep the lamp turned off when the alarm sounds be sure to have the display light in the off position when setting the alarm and when resetting it.

review_headline: DOES NOT LOAD DIGITAL COPIES OF MOVIES
review_body: I bought the non-MX version of this player for my oldest daughter over a year ago and it worked flawlessly.  When my youngest daughter's little mp3 player broke, I felt she deserved a better player that let her watch movies so I bought this one thinking it was the same unit as her sister's. review_body: I am not a person who can write lengthy, articulate reviews on amazon. I apologize in advance. But, I do feel there are 2 things buyers should know:    1. This product does not read like a book, it is much harder to read this than a book because a glare bounces off the screen, and there is no backlighting (sorry for the non-technical term) so I feel myself squinting past the glare half the time, and I still haven't figured if there is a way to make the screen darker (I'm too lazy to read the manual, I just haven't figured out how to do it by pressing the buttons).    2. product_title: Insignia Pilot 4GB USB MP/MP3/FM /Bluetooth w/2.4" LCD (Black)
review_body: This will not be a thorough review, but rather a somewhat specific perspective-- mainly for mac users.    What I was looking for was a simple but reliable mp3 player that I could access as a simple USB drive on my Mac. This was surprisingly difficult in 2010. Players fell into three camps: OLD, WINDOWS-ONLY, or iPOD.    I don't like that the iPod/iTunes package becomes this very controlling, bossy system where you can't easily choose which files go where, and you are beholden to Apple, Inc. to manage your iTunes and your iPod as this tightly controlled synchronized purchasing portal.    So I was left with a few meager new choices, or something in the OLD camp.    I have an iAudio G3 from Cowon that I like and still use as a basic mp3 player. It has nice features and sounds ok. Records surprisingly well, but it's a little cumbersome to setup and use.    I also had an older Insignia player that I liked. At first I didn't like the idea of a rechargeable because of the lack of immediacy and need for planning ahead. But I've changed my mind there. Charging just is a little thing we all do now. Isn't it?    The NS-4V24 --4 GB (and 8V24 --8 GB) are really good players (if you can find them). They work with most types of media, they are mac friendly. They allow folder browsing (rather than exclusively requiring mp3 tags for sorting, etc.). They include an SD card slot and Bluetooth for headphones. They provide excellent recording quality.     Yes, quality recording. Unfortunately, it does not include a built-in microphone, or even a microphone input. But it has a line-level input (for devices with line or headphone outs). I had this old Radio Shack \\"Personal Amplifier\\" which is basically a little box with a pair of microphones on it, and a headphone jack. It boosts the signal enough for the NS-4V24's line input. And the record quality is clear and pleasant, good enough for music recording. It's not audiophile quality, but with a decent microphone pre-amp, you could make a respectable podcast. You'd need to convert the .wav file to an mp3 (with iTunes, or Audacity).    I've not been able to find the secret formula for using Handbrake or any other software to convert video to play on it (see someone's review below). And I have not been able to play a video on it (apart from the included demo vid). That's not what I bought it for, but it would be nice to know how. (If anyone can tell me the specific settings, please comment!)    [FYI: My favorite cheap earbuds? JVC HA-FX34 (\\"Marshmallow\\") Works nice with this player, and you can keep the volume nice and low and save your ears. Very comfortable. But I digress.]    The FM radio works great. Picks up finicky stations with clarity.    Unit completely charges in 4-5 hours. The specs say 25 hours for battery life. I'd say it's a bit less, but decent. There are settings for screen-saving, brightness, and digital volume control that when set conservatively, can prolong battery life. I don't use the player for Audible, or Rhapsody, but it supposedly supports these services.

product_title: VideoSecu PC to TV Converter VGA to RCA S-Video Mac Computer Laptop to Composite Video Switcher 1L7
review_headline: A solid value for hotel dwellers
review_body: If you are stuck at hotels all the time like I am, then sooner or later you will find yourself wanting to play a dvd or some other media on the hotel TV set using your laptop computer. This is the device you will need to hook up your laptop to any and all hotel TV sets that do not have an HDMI input or a built in DVD player. As long as it has an \\"aux\\" RCA input, you can use this adapter to convert the hotel TV into a monitor for your laptop. Big-box electronics stores often sell a similar adapter, but they also charge multiples of the price of this unit. This one is just as good- without the huge markup. I carry mine with the requisite RCA, VGA and USB cables in my checked luggage. All those cables are supplied with the unit. The picture is good enough although not equal to that produced by an HDMI connection or a DVD player. Highly recommended.

product_title: PARROT MKI9200 Bluetooth Car Kit with Streaming Music (PAIMKI9200)
review_headline: MIxed Feelings - Screen Gets Scratched Very Very Easily
review_body: I recently installed the MKi9200 myself in my Nissan Murano, the first problem I encountered was that all \\"professional\\" installers said they needed to splice almost 11 cables to make this work; this was of course unacceptable for me.  One thing is to install a new device in the car and the other is to go ahead and cut up half the wiring under the console.  Plus I don't really want anyone touching or messing around with the car's Bose Audio.    So I decided to look for another option or simply return this thing.  I found a company that makes harnesses to connect Parrot Kits to various cars.  Bought one (not cheap by the way) and decided to do this myself as I have some experience taking apart and installing things in cars.  Pulled everything out, installed the harness, the Parrot and everything worked fine.  Connected it to my 3GS iPhone, and again everything works perfect, exactly as advertised.    But I found the Parrot to have one huge flaw:  THE SCREEN !!!!    I works well at night, dusk and dawn; but during the day sometimes it can be hard to read.  And worst of all it gets scratched almost by just looking at it.  I wear glasses, have an iPod and an iPhone, have various cameras and other gadgets live a GPS with screens on them or lenses or glass. But nothing I have ever seen gets scratched as easily as the Parrot's screen.  I even have a special cloth to clean glasses and even with that it gets scratched.    I personally feel that I was ripped off by Parrot with the low quality of the screen materials.  I find this simply to be unacceptable, I would definitely rather pay 20 or 30 more dollars but be sure that the quality of the materials used are up to the daily use this thing is given.    Furthermore, I emailed Parrot and asked them what was going on, and they simply said to try and find a screen protector for it.  I think that is very poor and basic customer service also.  That is not a real solution once the screen is scratched it stays scratched, a screen protector only prevents further scratching.    Other than that the device works as advertised, and does make my driving much safer, nevertheless it's these \\"Details\\" that make having an MKi9200 a bit of a sweet and sour deal.  Works good, but the screen is so scratched I might as well have bought an MKi9000.  Plus customer service is more like a joke than anything else.    So bottom line I would definitely NOT recommend buying the MKi9200 model because the screen is a rip off, maybe the other models like the MKi9100 have a better screen, and if you feel you don't need one the MKi9000 is probably the best bet, as that part of the Parrot works very well.  Although the iPod/MP3 sound you get off it is mediocre at it's best.  I have tried playing around with the settings but there is no way to make the music that goes through the Parrot sound good.  Again, as a hands free gadget, it's great, all else is not quite up to my expectations.    And if you do, don't even take it out of the box before you buy or adapt a screen protector to it !!!!!!!!!!!!

product_title: ION Audio VCR 2 PC USB VHS Video to Computer Converter (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: OK for VIDEO only; don't buy if you need AUDIO too!
review_body: First the PRO:  It rather easily transfer your VHS tapes to PC in MPEG format.  It's very simply to setup and use.  I installed it on Windows 7 (64-bit) Home Premium with the latest drivers off of Ion's website.  No problems installing the software, and on first launch -- it recognized the unit and was ready to record.  The video quality is good.  You have to keep your expectations in check -- remember your source is old VHS video tape.  It's an analog low-resolution format -- not even close to what you get out of a DVD.  In my opinion, the transferred video is pretty accurate to the source VHS tape, and you can tweak the color fidelity a bit to improve it as well.    Now the CON:  The audio is horrible.  Horrible isn't a harsh enough word.  Even when a tape is not playing, there are loud pops and crackle coming through the software.  The pops and crackle are NOT from the VHS tape.  The audio quality ruins the captured video.  Next, are the audio sync issues.  If you digitize a tape containing 60+ minutes of footage, you'll notice that as time goes on -- the audio gets more and more out of sync with the video.  I digitized an old movie (recorded years ago from TV), and by the end of the movie the talking would occur a full 10-12 seconds BEFORE the matching video.  It's not slightly out of sync, it's completely off and ruins the movie.  Finally, it only records MONO audio.  I didn't notice this when I purchased the unit, and wish I would have.    Worse CON of all:  I contacted Ion's technical support for help with the noise issues - primarily the popping and crackling that came through the device -- even when a tape wasn't in the unit.  Instead of helping me out with VCR2PC, they sent instructions on reinstalling drivers for their Vinyl Turntable to PC product.  I have no clue why they did that.  On top of that, the entire first half of the technical support email reply was an ad highlighting other ION products.  I don't understand that -- why try and sell me anotherproduct, when I'm having trouble with the quality of the unit I already purchased?  No thanks.    A real live breathing human being doesn't read their technical support emails.  Either that, or they're non-English speaking.  I wrote a fairly detailed email about the issues I was experiencing, what I had tried, and asking for suggestions on what else I could do to improve the audio.  The reply had nothing to do with my questions or the product I was seeking help on.    BOTTOM LINE:  If all you're after is digitizing short home movies with NO audio, this product works great and is easy to use.  However, if you're looking to digitize long tapes and need audio -- look elsewhere.  You'll regret buying this unit.

product_title: Silicon Scientific HDTV Remote Controlled Rotating Antenna
review_body: Great antenna, low price, works great.    Easy to assemble, hookup straight forward.  There are 4 connecting straps that screw on to the antenna dipoles, screws included.  Most of the little tubes do not connect, they are for phasing the signal to the main dipoles. The long tubes in the back do not connect, they reflect back to the main dipoles.  Simply stick the aluminum tubes in the plastic holders like in the picture.  Then four connector straps in the four pre-drilled holes in the main/closest dipoles.  Done!     Antenna wire into the \\"IN\\" plug on the control unit.  Control unit has two outputs for two different TVs.  New TVs already have an ATSC tuner built in, no need for a converter box.  The plugs are standard \\"PAL\\" plugs, can get them at Radio Shack.    The antenna mount is a maximum pole diameter of 1 1/8 inches.  I used 1\\" water pipe in concrete up from the ground so as to not put holes in my roof.  The pre-attached antenna wire is about 25 feet long, did not measure, but was plenty long to go into the house.    HDTV from major channels look just like cable HDTV on a big screen, but free!!!

product_title: VideoSecu PC to TV Converter VGA to RCA S-Video Mac Computer Laptop to Composite Video Switcher 1L7
review_body: This thing is a lot smaller than it looks in the pictures -- it's about the size of a standard deck of playing cards, plus a little for the cords and such. It's almost exactly the same, but on my monitor, it creates a nearly-invisible \\"ghost\\" effect -- everything that's being displayed is slightly ghosted a few pixels to the right. It's very difficult to notice after you get used to it, but if you compare it to the straight VGA signal, there's a marked difference.    Secondly, the device doesn't appear to understand widescreen resolutions. It can accept widescreen VGA input and give it back as output correctly, but it can't resize it correctly for the video out. It will appear on the TV as a severely ghosted and torn image. This is fixed by setting the computer to display at a non-widescreen resolution. product_title: UN-55C8000 55" 1080p LED HDTV 3D Technology 8 000 000:1 Dynamic Contrast Ratio Auto Motion Plus 240 Hz 3D HyperReal Picture Engine SRS TruSurround HD Game Mode
review_headline: The Ultimate Big Screen HD Experience
review_body: With this just released 2010 Samsung, it's getting to the point that the only way they can improve the viewing experience is to offer \\"Smell-O-Vision\\" next.    After spending a week with this FANTASTIC television, I can only say that if you don't mind spending extra for a set that you can be happy with for years; a TV that won't make you wish you would have waited for the next and newest one down the line; a TV you will watch even if you've already seen the same ESPN Sports Highlights of the day three times, just to stare in awe at the unbelievable picture quality, then you'll want to own THIS one.    The blacks are the darkest I've seen on an LCD, the jutter and blur of fast-moving scenes, inherent in the LCD format, is pretty much a thing of the past with the 240hz and different motion settings.      It took about a half hour to calibrate the mode (I went for \\"Dynamic\\"), contrast, brightness, backlight, color and sharpness that was right for my eyes.  After comparing and tweaking and tweaking and comparing different settings, I finally settled for the right combination that is now, to my eyes, the most brilliant and impressive home TV picture I have ever seen.    I spent the last 2 and a half years with a SONY 52 inch XBR5. Back then, it was between that and the equivalent Samsung 52 inch.  The SONY's low glare screen and perhaps the name \\"SONY\\" made me opt for the Bravia.  I was wishing I'd gone \\"Samsung\\" within about 10 months, when the SONY all of a sudden starting having some serious \\"issues\\" with its picture.    Fortunately, I bought the extended warranty.  The techicians had discovered that all of the out of focus, double vision, lines of interference and sometimes even \\"all plaid\\" screen was a circuit board problem which would cost more to fix than the set (now nearly only two years old) was worth.    I was sent a check for the cost of a replacement, which was an XBR9, but also was now \\"only\\" 1800 dollars instead of thre 3500 I'd spent on the \\"5\\" two yearsearlier.  Ouch!    My wife and I waited did more research for about 8 more months while the SONY problem kept getting worse and worse.  Finally, we'd \\"had it\\" and put the warranty money toward the just out C8000 series from Samsung.    The LED backlight issues that Samsung was reportedly having are now a thing of the past with the 8000 series.  I see perfection.  I love this TV.  If you're not afraid to spend the 3200 dollars for almost the best money can buy (the C9000, from what my salesman told me, is the same picture but with the \\"guts\\" of the TV in the base (wow!) and the screen a mere 1/3 of an inch thick.  The 9000 remote also has a little TV in it if you have to take a bathroom break during the big game...you can \\"take it with you.\\"      I figured the additional bells and whistles weren't worth the extra 2500 dollars I'd have to spend, so I went with the \\"second best\\" from Samsung.    I haven't tried the 3D mode yet.  I need to buy glasses, but, honestly, I wasn't even aware it was 3D capable when I bought it.      The new brushed titanium thin frame is very cool, the shiny screen isn't that bad reflection-wise, and I do believe it makes the picture even clearer, and, I am just extremely happy with this set.  It's the best.  I can't imagine even \\"looking at another girl.\\"

product_title: Sennheiser In-Ear Stereo Headphone
review_body: OK, take 2.  My original review of this product got hijacked somehow.  After writing it, I checked back a couple hours later and my screen name and original title were there, but my review got replaced with what seemed like some guy's journal entry.  It had absoluterly nothing to do with this or any other product.  Strange.    Anyway - as mentioned in my original posting, this review is more a condemnation or earbud headphones in general than the Sennheiser CX300-B, which I decided to try after my \\"over ear\\" style Sony noise canceling headphones went on the fritz.  My past experience with earbuds was not good, although I had only ever tried the type that come with the iPod and not the \\"ear plug\\" type that go in the ear canal, like the Sennheiser CX300-B.  However, having owned a pair of Sennheiser over the ear headphones back in the 70's, my impression of the company and their products was good.  So, I decided to take the plunge.  What a mistake.    After opening the package (no easy feat - damn sound welded plastic clamshells!), I popped on the medium-sized bud covers (appropriate for my size ears) and inserted them into my ears.  I turned on my mp3 player and listened for a few minutes.  The sound was adequate - nothing spectacular.  I did notice they had decent bass and did block some external noise.  I kept listening as I stepped outside to go to the store.  I couldn't believe what I heard.  Every step I took was amplified in my head - like a booming bass drum.  Even the gentle bumping of the cord against my chest was amplified - a constant thump, thump, thump that was impossible to ignore.  As it turns out, the very feature that blocks a modicum of external noise, also amplifies any sound that travels through the body.  Even breathing is amplified!  As I walked, it sounded as though I was listening to someone breathe over a PA system!  I had hoped to use these while running, but there's no way that's going to happen.  In fact, the problem with amplified sound is so bad, I won't use them at all.    I am very disappointed in this product and will never  buy any ear plug style headphones again.  I don't understand why anyone would sell them, let alone use them.  They may have great sound reproduction, but the listening experience is totally ruined by the sounds that get amplified through the body.  It amazes me that people buy similar style products that sell for hundreds of dollars.  The only way you can enjoy the sound they produce is to sit perfectly still.  I'm glad I only paid about $16 for these things.  I won't return them because it'll be too much of a hassle - probably cost more to ship them back  than I paid.    BTW - The photo of the product is misleading.  The cord looks thicker than it actually is and there's no way it can be coiled as is shown in the photo.  It gives the impression the cord is more supple and flexible that it really is.  Also, one end of the cord is longer than the other.  Not sure why this is, but the thinness of the cord makes it prone to kinking and tangling.  In fact, since one side of the cord is longer than the other, it makes it even more prone to tangling.    Bottom line - steer clear of the Sennheiser CX300-B and all ear plug style earbuds.

product_title: La Crosse Technology BC-700 Alpha Power Battery Charger
review_body: BC-700 has the advanced features that I like: discharge, refresh, test, and charge each battery individually. 100-240VAC input makes worry free for international travel. I chose it over BC-900 because people's complains regarding BC-900 melting issue, I only use the lowest charging current anyway.     Desire this little gadget has more features:    1. \\"Just charge this cell for 1 minute\\" function    Rechargeable sometimes are reverse charged when work in series with other still-full rechargeable batteries. Even it's reserve charged a little, or at 0V, it's still good. In this case BC-700 refuses to charge it. I use another 'dummy' charger to charge the 0V or reverse charged battery for 1 minute so that it has about positive 1V voltage, then BC-700 can take it.    If BC-700 has this function, it'll save more batteries. They are not dead yet.    2. \\"Test bulb\\" function    In one of my old charger, there's a little chamber where a battery can be put in, then a button is pressed to see if it still can light up a little bulb, meaning it still can supply about 200mA current. This is more useful than using a multimeter/voltmeter to measure its voltage, since sometimes even the voltage is 1.25V, it may not be able to supply higher current because of its high internal Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR). Since BC-700 can measure battery's voltage, adding a little bulb will make it perfect for verifying a question battery.

product_title: Onkyo HT-S3300 5.1-Channel Home Theater Receiver and Speaker Package (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great system for small to medium sized rooms
review_body: The big caveat - this is not a system you build on due to the passive sub and audessy tuned speakers. If you're of a mind to buy an entry level system and slowly upgrade parts over time, you'd be better off looking elsewhere.      That being said, I've had a lot of surround sound systems over the years, and this one sounds better out of the box than anything I've had. The surround sound field is rich and convincing, and the sound is very \\"organic\\" for lack of a better word. Sometimes the sound out of lower cost systems can be flat and lifeless, but that definitely is not the case here. Plug in a high definition source and prepare to get blown away. Dolby HD and TrueHD are things you don't expect to find in a receiver of this class. If the system fits your needs, you'll be set for many years to come.
