review_headline: No problems.  Decent price.  Decent quality
review_body:
I have nothing bad to say about these discs. I've burned plenty of videos to watch on my particularly finicky Sony DVD player and they have played just fine. In addition the $25 Samsung dual-layer burner I got from NewEgg has had no problem burning these at full 16x speed.

ImgBurn reports these as UME02 discs.

Other than that, these discs also include a protective coating on the label side of the disc to protect the foil. So you don't have to expect any of the foil chipping off like you do on some of the really cheap discs.

There's really not much else to say. The price is right. They work well and they're fairly durable.

product_title: Scosche Dynamic Range Earphones with TapLINE Control Technology
review_body: The tapline controls are sticky and not smooth as Apple's original earphones for the iphone 3GS.  It's cheap manufacturing and it doesn't work sometimes.

product_title: Creative Labs Xmod Wireless Music System with X-Fi Technology (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Fast, easy, good sound, works with Windows 7
review_body: I'll try not to rehash what's already been said in the previous positive reviews but it's hard because this gadget is really great.    I was able to get this set up in less than a minute. Windows 7 Ultimate saw the transmitter right away. Hooked up the receiver to my home stereo and opened Youtube to test the sound and it played immediately. It does not interfere with my N network at all.     If you need to stream music from any computer to a home stereo, get this thing. It sounds great, and is extremely easy to get running. It has enabled me to carry around my laptop all over the house without interrupting Pandora or Foobar. Best of all, it's without having to listen to the horribly tinny built in speakers. I plan on getting a few more receivers for the garage, upstairs, etc. Maybe some full setups for the music lovers in my family for Christmas gifts as well!    Creative really nailed it with this, five stars all the way!

product_title: Philips High Performance Amplified Indoor Uhf/Vhf/Fm/HDTV Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I can't really say whether this unit was good or not. It did not work on either of the two TV's that I tried it on. My first clue should have been the arc that kept sparking every time I connected the power jack to the unit. NOT a happy customer here... Unit promptly returned to vendor... I will not order another of this brand...

product_title: Jensen 3-Speed Stereo Turntable with MP3 Encoding and AM/FM Stereo - JTA-450 (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I, like many others, ignored the bad reviews posted by other Amazon shoppers and ordered the Jansen JTA-450.  Upon arrival I couldn't wait to listen to some of my records.  After a quick set up I put my favorite record on the turntable and after a long high pitched screech the needle cut across the record leaving a deep groove in the vinyl.  DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT!

product_title: Zeimax Q38i Super Bass Inear Headphone Earphone Headset For Apple iPhone 6 / 6 Plus / 5 / 5S /5C, HTC One (E8), One (M8), Samsung Galaxy S5 Android Smartphone (Black)
review_body: I have had the CX380 for 3 months now and have to say I am disappointed. The sound quality is great when I can get the jack is adjusted right on my player. I have a mp3 player, ipod nano and an iPhone and I get the same static or poor jack (could be a short in the cable) connection in all 3 players. It drives me nuts. I am shopping for a new (not Sennheiser) pair of earphones. The cable/cord has a tacky surface which I am not totally in favor of. It has often stuck on my clothing or on me and pulled the earbud out of my ear which I then have to dry off the earbud and my ear of sweat in order to get a good fit again. Then of course readjust the phone jack to get a good sound connection. The right ear piece has an extra long cable/cord which I don't find helpful or necessary. Anyway, I don't recommend the CX380.

product_title: Yamaha YDS-11SL Universal iPod Dock for Select Yamaha Home Theater Receivers (Silver) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Plugged it into the receiver, put my ipod touch in it and used the remote to control it!  It was easy and it works great. And the price was very reasonable especially if you compare it to other ipod systems.  It was nice to not have to have another sound system to listen to the Ipod.  I  The only thing that was a let down was that I do not have video capability but that's only because it is not a feature with my reciever.  I wouls encourage any one with a Yahama reciever that has thee ipod dock option to use it before purchasing another speaker system to listen to their ipod.

product_title: Monster Standard THX-Certified Subwoofer Interconnect Cable (16 Ft) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: A lot of people say this is hogwash, but the very first time I went from a standard subwoofer cable to a Monster cable, the difference was immediate and huge. My subwoofer started putting out sound like I had never had before. Don't let anyone con you into believing that this is a farce, that anything will work. A better cable will definitely give you better sound.

product_title: Memorex 32025708 4.7GB 16X LightScribe DVD-R (20pk Spindle)
review_body: This is the first Memorex product I've used that has been a complete and utter failure. The labels burn beautifully, but the data? Doesn't exist. I attempted to make a backup copy of my new system as instructed, and you're only allowed one shot. I missed that shot, as it appears to the system that I have made my copy, yet there is no data on the disks. Now, I must purchase a back up copy from HP, if they ever answer my email (but that's another story). Run. Run, I tell you, from this horrible product and seek another source to make this truly great idea become a reality.

product_title: Aluratek LIBRE eBook Reader PRO - eBook reader - Flash: 2 GB - 5" - white
review_body: I have had this device for a week now and read a couple of ebooks in pdf format.  So my experience is about reading pdf books on this device.    1. Overall I like the layout of the keys and menus; all essential functions are readily available, page turns, increase fonts, landscape/portrait switch, all nicely done.  No need for touch screen (save some money on that);     2. pdf works great if it's text with pictures.  But it doesn't work with figures.  It translates all figures to words only, no lines, graphs are translated.  So it's not suitable to read science books, technical books.    3. Being the lowest priced ebook reader, its build quality is surprisingly good.      4. No problem reading photo scanned pdf books even with graphs. You need to turn off reflow for photo scanned books.  But the 5 inch screen is not that great for reading graph intensive pdf books.  Amazon Kindle DX would be the one if you read a lot technical pdf files.    5. It doesn't use E-Ink so there is no visible repainting of the screen.  The non-reflective LCD screen, in my view, works better.      Overall, very satisfied with Libre as my first ebook reader.  It's different from reading ebooks from netbook, because the ebook reader is designed specifically for reading ebooks and it's lighter, smaller and easier to carry around.

product_title: Sanus Home Theater Series Adjustable Height Speakers Stands for Satellite Speakers - Tear Drop base - 26"-39" Height - HTB3 (Black)
review_body: For the money, this is a great speaker stand. Easy to assemble, great adjustment range and the outer coating blends with most anything in a room. Excellent product which I'll tell my friends about. Thanks, Dutch [[ASIN:B0000CFYOL Sanus HTB3 Tear Drop Home Theater/Box Speaker Stands]]

product_title: Etymotic Research ER-4PT MicroPro Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Not much to say.  This is my second set in 7 years.  Love 'em.  Tried the $99 Bose - didn't like 'em so gave them to my kid.  If you're a bass freak you will not like these.  If you're an audiophile who wants to hear all of the subtle tones - as if you were listening live - then I believe you\\"ll like them a lot.  Only bad thing is noise if they rub on your clothes.  I hook the cords over my ear and run the main cord down my back.  That works great for yard work, skiing, biking, etc.  I always use them when traveling by airplane - makes the world go away.

product_title: Casio PZ4000B  Portable CD Player with Car Kit and 40-Second Anti-Shock
review_body: I had purchased this for myself. When I first recieved these, I thought the sound quality was good, I did like the manufacture suggested, let them play for a day or so.  I have found that as time has gone on the sound from these earbuds are just unbelieveable. For once, a set of earbuds that are very comfortable to have in for hours.  I would highly recommend these earbud.

product_title: La Crosse Technology BC-9009 AlphaPower Battery Charger (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Great piece of equipment. With it's many modes it provides just what I needed. Good sets (4 each) of batteries (both AA & AAA) come with it too. Will take some time to fully explore the many functions this charger provides.

product_title: Coby MP-C7082 MP3 Player with 1 GB Flash Memory with FM & Color Display (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Coby MP3 Player - sync process unclear
review_body: The demo tunes work fine.  However, after 1 week of working with   the player, I am still unable to get a clean load.    The player requires Win Media Play 11.  I was able to upgrade  and found that it now sees the player but complains about  space on the device and will not load the playlist.  It does  not allow for straight copying of the tunes.    The controls are simple but still confusing as to moving around   the menus.  I continually find that I have to back out and  start over and walk back through the menu to get to the  function that I am looking for.

product_title: ASUS Eee PC 900 / 900A / 900HA / 900HD / 900SD / 901 / 904HA / 1000 / 1000H / 1000HE / 1002HA / 1000XP / S101 Netbook Replacement AC Adapter
review_body: First of all the charger I received was white, despite it being black in the picture. Thankfully I didn't mind, but most of the time when I go to plug it in there's small visible and audible sparks between the prongs and most outlets I've used. The same usually happens if the 2nd part of the cord connecting to the box(don't know the name for it)comes loose and I have to reconnect it. Because of being frequently bent (my own fault) where it connects to the laptop the cord split exposing some wires and makes it so I have to have it at just the right angle to get a charge connection. I won't buy another one from this same source because I'd rather not worry if stray sparks from plugging it into an outlet will electrocute me.

product_title: Optical Extension Coupler
review_headline: works great at a low price
review_body: I used the  TosLink to Mini TosLink Cable [[ASIN:B001ZTXBMO Digital Optical Audio TosLink to Mini TosLink Cable, 12 FT]] along with an additional 25-foot toslink cable [[ASIN:B000V06UHQ RiteAV - Digital Optical Toslink Cable 25ft.]]and optical extension coupler[[ASIN:B0002MQGRC Optical Extension Coupler]]  to connect my iMac to my home theater.  I bought all the cables and connector for practically nothing compared to retail on Amazon.  It sounds fantastic--huge improvement over wireless (bluetooth) or RCA connections.  Don't waste money on expensive cables.  The cheap ones carry the digital signal just as well.

product_title: Zune HD Video MP3 Player
review_headline: I Like this better than my old Ipod Touch 8gb 2nd Gen
review_body: I like this better than my Ipod because the sound that comes out of these are a lot better quality than the ipod.    If you want a PMP full of Apps and you use your Mp3 player as a primary source of using the Internet. get your self a Ipod Touch.    But if you want a Mp3 player with GREAT sound, a really nice screen, and the ablitiy to pay only [...] a month and download a bunch of songs legally than get the Zune. The software (Zune) isnt the best but its comparable to itunes.       As for the Zune its self I havent had any problems with it, it took me only like a day to get use to the buttons and new interface(coming from the ipod touch UI) its really easy to get used to and the need for instructions is not needed(as some reviews complained about) Battery Life has been great.     Theres not much to say besides that this is a great alternative to the Ipod and for only [...]more you can get 8 more gigs than the Ipod touch.

product_title: Ion TTUSB Turntable with USB Record (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: get the program up date from manufactor
review_body: Works above what I imagined after I got the updated infro ( PROGRAM FROM MANUFACTOR) and BE careful needle breaks easly.

product_title: Sennheiser In-Ear Stereo Headphone
review_headline: expected more in terms of sound quality, but it's value for money.
review_body: i expected more in terms of sound quality, since they're senheissers, but i think my old sony ones sounded brighter and clearer.

product_title: Winegard GS-2200 Sensar III  Digital Ready Antenna
review_body: Worked perfectly the first time, with no adjustments.  The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is that I loose the signal sometimes when my microwave is running.  Why?  I don't know.  But, its not enough to get a bad review.

product_title: JBuds J2 Premium Hi-Fi Noise-Isolating Earbuds Style Headphones (White/Gray)
review_body: Good quality noise canceling buds. The sound is not a good as the original apple buds, but they are infinitely more comfortable, and they substantially reduce outside noise. The instructions claim the sound improves with use. We'll see. I use them instead of the apple buds, so that means they must be superior.

product_title: Logitech Pure-Fi Anywhere 2 Compact Docking Speakers for iPod and iPhone
review_headline: Worth  the  time  effort  and  money
review_body:
This speaker system lived up to its expectations in my view.

Sound quality and portability are great. Ease of use is excellent.

Friends who heard it asked how to get one.

I would order another if needed.

product_title: Sony Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones
review_body: Absolutely ineffective in attenuating truck cab noise. There was no difference between having the phones off or on. Maybe an ear cup design would work better than having the earpieces sit on top of the ears.

product_title: PCT MA28PN RF Amplifier Passive Return CATV Amp 8-Ports
review_headline: Works great with cable. No worries!
review_body: Works great! Just mount it, connect it up, and enjoy. I replaced an 8-port passive splitter for my cable-TV with this gem. I had a lot of noise and snow/weak signal and some occasional digital artifacts on my farthest away TV/TiVo. With this PCT-MA2-8P 8-port splitter/amplifier the noise is gone and the picture quality with the stronger signal is all that I could have asked for.  The price is a good deal.  Two notes: the Amazon page suggests 75 ohm terminators but there's no need for those and no mention of them in the manual.  PCT offers an optional power inserter, PCT-MPI-1G which allows plugging in the power adapter at one of the remote ends of the coax rather than directly connecting to the device.  I'd like that to allow me to have the power come from my UPS near a TV/TiVo rather than the line outlet in my wiring closet. Note that this device only works with antenna or cable, not satellite.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_body: Best ear phones I've ever owned. Sound quality is excellent including bass. With earphones sounds like I'm in a concert hall with sound coming from all directions.

product_title: Acoustic Research Tabletop Radio with Docking Station for iPod and MP3 Players
review_body: I received a defective unit of this product.  I asked for a new unit to be sent back in both my email and the box sent.  Discount Jungle \\"claims\\" radio was OK and gave only a partial refund.  BUYER BEWARE!

product_title: ION Audio VCR 2 PC USB VHS Video to Computer Converter (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: You might be better off getting an A/V converter with the red white and yellow connections that is compatible with any operating system and can connect to any device.  This product is nice b/c we didn't have a working VCR, but we have a Mac Linux and Windows PC in our house, and of course, it only works on the Windows PC (which is also the oldest and slowest of the three).  I wish they would support their product with other OSes, it would have made my life a lot easier.

product_title: Crumpler MD0709A 7 Million Dollar Home Grey/ Red Bag + Accessory Kit
review_body: I am a beginner photographer, but am experienced enough to know what I need from a camera bag. I highly recommend the Crumpler. The main compartment has velcro, making it 100% adjustable to your needs. Currently I have a Canon T1i body, 4 lenses (various sizes), electronic flash, and all the goodies that come along with it. The Crumpler not only holds all my camera gear, but a fair share of the crap I feel necessary to schlep along with me wherever I go.     I know the price is steep, but it really is worth it. This bag will last you forever, looks awesome, and is surprisingly comfortable to carry.

product_title: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touch Screen - OLD MODEL
review_headline: Know what you're getting yourself into...
review_body: First controller I ordered, the 'OK' key died resulting in a new controller being sent to me that I have not received (7th day so far). Second controller I ordered could not be programmed because apparently Logitech's servers are down. That one is getting shipped back to Amazon right now. One thing you must understand about this controller is that it uses a web-based updating procedure. If something goes wrong with this, however minor, and you can't access their servers, your s******. Do a Google search and you'll find plenty about this. I'm going back to the original controller(s). Sometimes the best tech is low tech.

product_title: Belkin Clamp On Surge Protector (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I use this on my work bench.  It works fine, clamps to the top.  The cord is pretty long and easily reaches the nearest outlet.  The only thing I don't really like is the size of the clamp.  It makes the whole unit rather large so depending what you are trying to do this may be too large to work.

product_title: Comply Foam Premium Earphone Tips - Isolation T-100 (Platinum, 3 Pairs, Large)
review_headline: The best thing since in ear headphones
review_body: I bought these for my earbuds because the silicon tips just fall out of my ears when exercising. They worked perfect for that. My headphons have never fallen out of my ears unexpectedly since I've had them. Added BONUS... they also improve sound quality and sound isolation due to the better seal. They are practically like ear plugs. More of the sound reaches your ear and less sounds from the outside get it. I would buy them again in a heartbeat.

product_title: IOGear 3-Port HDMI Switch with Remote GHDMIS3-Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This is a very simple solution for lack of HDMI connections, particularly when used with a universal remote like the Harmony series. My Samsung DLP only has 2 HDMI ports, so this lets me double the available ports with no pain and suffering. Works as advertised and no loss of video or audio quality as devices switch.

product_title: Audio Technica Audiophile Closed-Back Dynamic Headphones
review_body: Just received my headphones.  Wow.  These things are huge.  Sound is great but they are just too big.  I've never seen such big headphones.  They take up both sides of my head.  I wish I had checked the size before ordering.  My mistake.  They are light and comfortable so if you don't mind looking like an idiot you may not be bothered by the size.  Contrary to another reviewer, these headphones are definitely noisy to others nearby.  My husband kept telling me to turn the volume down.  As I mentioned, the sound is great.  No doubt the large size helps produce/enables this sound.  Still, I can't get over the how big they are.  They are going back.  P.S. Did I mention these headphones are huge?

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16 GB Silver
review_body: I knew that Apple was about to come out with a new iPod but it did not occur to me that they would put in a camera!  I was pissed when I found out that they didn't warn the market not to buy the older iPod with such a new and sweet iPod on the way out.  Other than that, I love iPods and I am having no issues, thus far with this one.

product_title: Sony ICFCDK50 Under Cabinet Kitchen CD Clock Radio
review_headline: Liked it, but the CD player wouldn't work
review_body: I just bought this for my mother as a gift, but when we installed it under the cabinet we noticed that the cd player wouldn't work. It was as if it wasn't reading the cd. I know this is not uncommon for burnt cds, but it wouldn't work on regular cds either. I returned it, but I'm worried that the next one will do the same.

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_body: I love this little guy.  Great on the go or just relaxing it gets you into the swing.

product_title: Zune 120 GB Video MP3 Player
review_body: I have one. Just got it in from repair. Hardware OK. Software is a Microsoft nightmare. Spent 1 hour trying to upload a disk. Zune lost the song names, cut off some of the songs. Zune has no import menu, like Ipod has. I also have a old Ipod. I strongly suggest you stick with Ipod. I wish I had.

product_title: Sony XDR-F1HD HD Radio Tuner (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: A super value if you like HD radio
review_body: This is a great product!  I can't believe retailers aren't carrying it.  It installs easily, picks up even weak stations (much better than a $500 tuner which sits next to it), and provides great sound quality through your amp.  The package isn't real pretty, but if you're more concerned with sound quality than how it looks, this is the one for you.

product_title: Easycap USB Video Capture Adapter
review_headline: How to get a signal when the device is recognized!
review_body: The red and yellow cables from your camcorder DO NOT correspond to the device. I plugged the red from the camcorder to the yellow on the device. I'm using a separate mic so the sound from the camera is irrelevant at this point.     On a different note: the EasyCap software caused my computer to crash. When installing the software, I was given a warning that it may cause problems with my computer and it did; within 24 hours, my computer stopped working and has not worked since. DO NOT USE THE EASYCAP.

product_title: C&E 6-Feet 1.8m PCD Basics Fiber Optic Audio Cable
review_body: overall great, nothing too crazy to complain about, except that it is only 6 feet, limited my possibilities at first, but once i got my TV stand all set up it was plenty long, so if you don't have a TV stand, 6 feet may not be long enough, just a fair warning for potential customers.

product_title: ThrustMaster Kart Challenge NW - Wheel and pedals set - Nintendo GAMECUBE, Nintendo Wii
review_body: My son never really liked the wii wheels where you put the controller in it and steered in mid air. He enjoyed using this as it turns more like an arcade wheel. I did read the reviews about the table, and sort of agree that a convenient table may be something many people don't have(we have a leather storage ottoman there, not a table.) We decided to use one of those [[ASIN:B0007YDUXI Table Mate]] trays, since we have those for the kids and it worked really well and use it for the wheel. It is adjustable and can be put away when the game isn't being played. Worked well for us!

product_title: GPX HC208B CD Boombox (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This is probably the best little CD/radio for the money!  Easy to use; remote works great across the room; good sound.  Would definitely get another one, if needed.

product_title: Altec Lansing inMotion MIX iMT800 Portable Digital Boom Box for iPhone and iPod
review_body: This has pretty great sound for it's size. The remote works well with it and it is also pretty nice to be able to just carry it anywhere to where you want to listen to it. The shapes makes it perfect for setting in corners. Which helps the passive subwolfers to work better anyways. The radio picks up very well even with the antenna down. Ipod docking is a snap. The only thing that would have made this perfect in all respects is a CD player also. All in all, pretty nice sound, compact, and great price compared to the bose system.

product_title: PowerGenix ZR-PGX1HRAA-4B 1 Hour Quick Charger with 4 AA 1.6v NiZn Rechargeable Batteries
review_body: If you want a better charger or battery than the PowerGenix NiZn (1.6 V-2500 mWh), you WILL NOT find it.   My Samsung SL30 digital camera goes through regular AA's and even rechargeable NimH's like they're for free. But it goes for days on these. They last a long time and charge very fast. Put simply, hands down it's one of the best products I've ever purchased.

product_title: Omnimount SW2 Table Top Swivel Fits up to 42-Inch Flat/27-Inch CRT Television (Espresso) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Simple to put together and turns easily. I've had two Table Top Swivels before, but I like this one the best. It is lightweight, yet turns effortlessly with my 32\\" flatscreen.

product_title: Yamaha YST-FSW150BL Advanced YST II Down-Firing Active Subwoofer
review_body: The unit is provided with only single wire connections, which works okay in an A/V application, but if you're intending to use it with a stereo receiver (that has left and right output connections), you'll need to go to an electronics store to buy a \\"Y\\" adapter because the unit doesn't ship with one.

product_title: High Speed HDMI Cable (1.5 Feet) With Ethernet - CL3 Certified - Supports 3D and Audio Return Channel, 1-Pack
review_body: these were just what I was looking for and at the price I was looking for

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 8 GB Video MP3 Player
review_body: I love my Sansa! I bought this little gatdet last year at Christmas for myself. I think I paid around $40 for it here on Amazon. Nobody even new what a Sansa was at the time. But, I researched other similar products and found the Sansa was the best bang for the buck.I bought the family more expensive, better known brands like the ipod, iriver,ect. and everyone has tried to swipe my Sansa at some time or another since then. They all prefer my Sansa-from the 7 year old all the way up the chain to my spouse. I wish I had realized how awesome the Sansa's video and musical abilities were, because I could have saved myself hundreds of dollars. The video quality is as good as my HDTV! I have about 40 music videos along with about 30 or so UTube Vids in addition to over 700 songs! And I still have storage left. The music quality is equal to the quality of what you download. Navigation through the applications is childplay. Downloading videos, music, pictures couldn't be any easier. Just plug the Sansa into your computer, sync a playlist(or all your music and video files)in your media player, and your done. You can also find your Sansa on your computer listed with your drives and just drag any file to your Sansa. I haven't had the first problem with any conversions either.The only thing I would change about the Sansa was the earbuds. They were a little too big for my ears, so I puchased some Sony earbuds.The Sansa earplugs, though, are probably fine for most guys.

product_title: Furman Elite-15 PF i 13-Outlet Linear Filtering AC Power Source
review_headline: Fair amt to leart about the back panel, but easy to use.
review_body: Don't have a super large system, so I got this Furman unit as I felt it was right for the power my system uses.  It's very easy to hook up and use, and seems to be built like a tank.  My only question of Furman is, \\"What if you have mono-block amps?\\" as there's only one of the 13 outlets on the back marked \\"amp\\", but as most amps are stereo and not mono-block, for the vast majority of us the question does not arise (true for me, too).  Anyway, it's a great value!    Mark Zimmerman, the Bipolar Bear, Chicago

product_title: Audio Unlimited Wireless Speakers with Remote
review_body: I have my laptop in the downstairs office with the wireless transmitter attached to it.  The two wireless speakers are on the next floor, and the usually work great, but I do occasionally have problems with them fading in and out while a song is playing. Overall, great buy, simple hookup, great sound quality!

product_title: Ultra High Performance HDMI Switcher, 3to1 Switch
review_headline: Works as Advertised - Remote Not Needed
review_body: Works perfectly and as advertised. Due to the auto select feature (selecting the cable who's device is on)the remote is not really needed.

product_title: Sanyo Eneloop NiMH Battery Charger with 4AA NiMH Rechargable Batteries (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This charger is excellent. The only disadvantage is that it lasts up to 4 or 5 hours charging the batteries. However, this is not so terrible if you don't care about it.    In any case, the charger accomplish its mission: charge batteries. I recommend it!

product_title: Altec Lansing Snugfit In-ear Earphone
review_body: So far, these have been great. I use the plugs that come standard on them and when I am listening to them, I cannot hear anything from outside. One minor drawback is that they require very little volume and on the lowest setting on my macbook pro, I sometimes need to turn itunes down to get it to a comfortable level. Also, perhaps of the low level, I get a lot of static. They work perfectly on my ipod touch and home stereo equipment.    I have also been told that no noise can be heard by others, even when listening to music at nearly uncomfortable levels. I don't listen to loud music when I am worried that others can hear, just in case.

product_title: Samsung HT-X50 5.1-Channel 5-Disc DVD Home Theater System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I hardly had used this system, was still shiny & new and it just stopped working. It would play for 10 minutes and shut off. I would never buy a product from this company again.

product_title: Recoton TSVG361 Component Video Cable Set ? 6 Feet
review_headline: Great cable at a great price
review_body: These have worked great for me. They were nice heavy duty cables and the picture has been great. Way cheaper than going to an electronics store and purchasing them.

product_title: Sennheiser Wireless Surround Sound Headphones
review_body: I need a pair of wireless headphones so that I can watch TV without waking the baby. These are great! The range is great, I was away from the base unit about 30 ft and it was still clear as a bell. The 3d emulation is pretty cool but sometimes it over enhances the sound, but just trun it off, there is a dedicated switch on the headset. The other cool thing is that it runs on AAA batteries, and they charge by placing it on the base. Man its really great. I bought a 2nd one and they both tune into the same base. So far I can't find anything bad about it. product_title: Aluratek AIREC01F WiFi Internet Radio - Home Theater Edition (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I have not figured out why sometimes when I turn the unit on, the last station I had it tuned to starts playing, but most of the time it just sets at Internet Radio and I have to go to either Station List or Favorites and re-select the station. product_title: Bose In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: They Still Hurt My Ears ... And They MUST Be Broken in.
review_body:
These earphones, which were advertised as not hurting the ears because they don't enter the ear canal, still hurt my ears, even though I have tried all the sizes of silicone tips provided. They just hurt the outer part of my ears where they rest, instead of the inner part, or ear canal. I don't understand why, since everyone has differently-shaped ears, these and other earbuds couldn't be supplied with a slightly fluid, mouldable type of tip which would adapt itself accurately to each ear. Now I am considerably lighter in the pocket, and still have sore ears after less than half an hour of wearing, and I am not happy.

The sound quality is acceptable for my purposes (AVE machine with music/voice background), but is not even close to that of my old BeyerDynamic DT-990 headphones (though maybe that is not a fair comparison; the DT-990's have me effectively sitting in the vocalist's lap, surrounded by the band, and are addictive with any music at all because of their sheer presence, astonishing clarity, balance, crispness and spatial placement).

The sound was very harsh in the mid/top and lacking in bass when I first got them, but I broke them in over 24 hrs (i.e. connected them to my iPod with some rhythmic, dynamic music cycling at just above comfortable listening volume) and left them for 24 hours, and pretty much all the harshness has gone and the bass, which was weak, has improved significantly. All in all, I wish I had gone for another in-ear product, as these ones still try to fall out of my ears to some extent (though the lanyard is well-designed and the clip helpful), do not transmit sufficient bass or optimum sound unless I hold them to my ears with a little pressure from my fingertips, and with normal wear and the smallest size tips they still hurt my ears, though not as much as in-ear phones do. YMMV.

(N.B. I have a neurological condition which makes me more sensitive than usual to pain, but not dramatically so. Nevertheless, as I seem to be the only one complaining about sore ears here, readers might wish to bear that in mind; they are certainly a lot less painful than the only other earbuds I've tried -- the standard Apple ones.)y one complaining about sore ears here, readers might wish to bear that in mind; they are certainly a lot less painful than the only other earbuds I've tried -- the standard Apple ones.)

review_body: I've had these headphones for about 2 weeks now, and I wanted to put up a review for those considering buying them.    You have to understand you will not get $300 Bose quality for $75, but for the price these earphones are excellent.    PROS   - Lightweight and very portable compared to the over-ear models   - Good sound isolation just from the fact that they go IN your ear, not over   - Noise cancellation is good   - Music is *crisp* You can actually hear the bass drum and other nuances that are usually lost.   - \\"Monitor\\" button lets you mute music and listen to the outside world without removing headphones (perfect for work interruptions)    CONS    - Cumbersome compared to other in-ear headphones (think iPod). The AAA battery pack is one the wire, and while this is necessary it does get in the way. If you thought iPod headphones got tangled easily, these are worse.    - Introduces hiss when you turn noise cancellation on    NOTE - Noise-cancellation technology does not kill all noise, it's better at eliminating constant noise, like engine noise.    I recently made a 150 mile road trip, and was noticeably more relaxed when I got done. The road noise disappeared and I listened to music. (Safe while driving? Maybe not, but I enjoyed it)    A friend has the over-ear Bose, and the Sonys are NOT that good, but there's a huge price difference. At the sub $100 price point I am happy with these headphones.    The thing I like best about them is being able to \\"tune out\\" at work and relax. You don't realize how much ambient distraction there is, and once you cut it out it's very peaceful.    Sony says these remove 90% of noise, to me it feels more like 70%    A solid buy, I recommend them.

product_title: C2G/Cables to Go 27027 Toslink Digital Audio Splitter (Black)
review_body: I was very skeptical when buying this spliiter/switch after seeing so many bad reviews. It worked for me after little trial and error and here is what I found. For all those who complained that these splitters/switches do not work, this is what you need to do to get it right. I bought this splitter from eforcity, so I cannot say about those shipped by other sellers.... It works both ways i.e. as a splitter and as a switch.    1. For it to act as a switch, the critical thing is that only one source needs to be ON. Some sources send signal even when on stand by mode. To check whether it sends out signal, just plug one end of the toslink cable into port of the source(cable box, ps3, etc) and check the other end for red light. when on stand by, the light should not be lit.    2. The second most important thing for this splitter/switch to work is the length of the cables used. I used all 1.5 ft cables and they work perfectly. Earlier I had 3 ft cables coming out of the cable box and ps3 to the splitter and then 1.5 ft cable to the home theater. The ps3 did not work but cable box worked (not consistently though) as the signal attenuated too much by the time it reached the home theater receiver. I am not sure if there is a shorter cable than 1.5 ft and it would be great if you do have them. 1.5 ft cables work fine. I got the 1.5 ft cables from RiteAV.    Finally, the basic test to see if it works is to check for the red light after the connections. Connect in the way shown below and check for the light near the * before connecting to the receiver. Make sure only one source is ON at a time. If you see light and it still does not work after plugging into the receiver then it means that the signal attenuated too much and your receiver cannot pick it.    source 1 -->  ...................splitter -->* receiver  source 2 -->    --> = 1.5 ft toslink cable  ignore the dots...    Good luck!.

product_title: Panasonic RP-HC55-S Noise-Cancelling Earbud Headphones
review_body: I had been looking for noise cancelling earbuds to eliminate wind noise while motorcycle riding (earphones mounted in the helmet are ineffective).  I had previously purchased the $20 garden variety \\"noise cancelling\\" earbuds, but their idea of noise cancelling was to add some hiss and increase the volume.  Not good at all. My son did the same thing but bought the $100 Sony's instead.  His worked great.  When I did my research on the subject, I saw these performed as well as the Sony's plus they did not stick out as far from your ear.  Just what I needed for the motorcycle.  Since these are for use while riding, noise cancelling is critical while sound quality takes a back seat.  These fill the bill completely.  On a motorcycle, the engine noise (At least for a big V-twin) disappears completely, wind noise is reduced by 50%, music sounds good, and you can still hear cars, horns, sirens, etc.  It was great to navigate through New York City with the phones plugged into the GPS.  Even as a country boy, all I had to do was listen to the sweet lady inside my head give me turn by turn directions to whatever destination I needed.  These are excellent earbuds for my needs.  Also, I used them the last time I flew commercial and they were great.  The engine noise disappeared and the music drown out the \\"Chatty Cathy's\\" I was sitting next to.  The only bad feature is one listed in many reviews.  the wire leading from the buds to the electronics/battery is too short.  If you do not have a shirt pocket to clip it too, it is clunky and cumbersome.

The only real negative I have with this device (and it's an annoying negative) is that the connection cord that plugs into your device is WAY too short! 8 inches to be precise. I don't know if this would have prevented me from buying this speaker, but it's a real drawback and poor design.

product_title: Chill Pill Mobile Speakers for iPod/Mp3 Players and Laptops
review_headline: Loved them for awhile, but then....
review_body:
[[ASIN:B001K33QSO Chill Pill Mobile Speakers iPod/MP3 Players & Laptops]]

I bought these after reading a very positive review in one of the Mac magazines. Loved them right away. I use them mostly when I watch videos on my ipod or my larger, folding Sony dvd viewer. They are compact, and sound good-not good enough for stereophiles or high end music listening, but great for lo to medium-fi listening. They pack easily and the speaker bodies are rugged.

The charge lasts longer than they say it will, I commonly got 10 hours from each charge. Couldn't use them with my portable radio (eton), it buzzed miserably. Can't have it plugged into the electric outlet and listen to it plugged into any device-buzzes badly. I can live with this, however, since can just about always plan my charging times based on my needs.

Unfortunately, my relative delight with the speakers has been squashed. After about 6 months of frequent, but careful use, the wires and connections all became useless and NO sound comes out at all. I am not rough on products, in fact, I tend to respect them quite a bit, and handle them with TLC. The cord retraction was great at first (very handy!), but it got consistently worse over time, until the cords no longer retracted at all, the caps of the cords fell off, and any slight movement of the cords began to lead to crackling/dropping sound coming from the speakers. They are now completely useless.

Also. the charge light doesn't no longer comes on when it's plugged in, though the speakers seem to have charged anyway. Who can tell, as NO sound comes out!

I'd like to give the product four stars, but due to complete product breakdown after 6 months of normal use, I'm going to go down all the way to 2. If they can make the cords more rugged and reliable, this product could really rock.

product_title: OmniMount Speaker Mounts 5-Pack (Black) (AB2BLACK5PK) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Just set-up and mounted new speakers using these mounts.  Installation was easy and had no problems with tightening or anchors as some previous reviewers had. product_title: Philips- DVP5990 - Multi Region DVD Player 1080P - upscaling

product_title: VideoSecu Tilt TV Wall Mount Bracket for most 37 to 70-Inch LCD LED Plasma Screen Display up to VESA 400X400 684X300 700X400mm with HDMI cable, Bubble Level MP502B 3KR
review_body: I was a little unsure about what to expect when I ordered this mount. I read the reviews and the top-heavy positive feedback convinced me to get it, but  I still had doubts. Ultimately I figured, if I need to spend $200 on a mount, I might as well take a $40 gamble. Wow, I wish I had these results at Vegas.    It looks great and is sturdy. My 46 in plasma is up and solid as a rock. I mounted my front side speakers on the sides of the TV so as to hide the mount so I essentially just have a TV sitting on my wall without anything visibly holding it up.    The system is easy to assemble, although the instructions do suffer from typical Asian translation problems. In the couple of other languages I can communicate in, I would never publish anything without a native speaker looking it over to say: yeah, that's not really how we speak, but I digress. The screws are shoddy like mentioned elsewhere, so get your own at a hardware store for an extra $5 or so. I also mounted a plywood plate between the bracket and wall because I just didn't feel safe mounting to only two studs, but the instructions say it's find to do it that way.    I am looking at mounting brackets the way I've come to understand HDMI cables: the prices at the box stores are crazy high because they have people who are plunking down $1,000 for a set and are excited as heck to get home to try it out. Then the salesperson says, do you have an HDMI cord? What about a mounting bracket? You won't get that true HD without the cord, and won't your set look great mounted on the wall all pretty and out of the way? Joe and Jane customer just want their TV so they fork out the bucks to use their new toy as soon as possible.     You don't need to be that Joe or Jane, get this mount.

product_title: Pyle Home 30-Watt Stereo Mini Power Amplifier
review_headline: Great little amplifier, excellent sound when used with good speakers
review_body: Pyle PCA1 was purchased to attach Bose 201 speakers with iPod. So far I am pleasantly surprised:  Pros:  - It is well built, small but pretty heavy (not a cheap plastic)  - The sound is excellent for classic or easy background music  - stays cool under normal load  - simple to install and use, just a power switch and volume knob  Cons:  - It needs a special conversion cable to connect your iPod or similar device. I think that manufacturer could simplify design and instead of cable, simply provide the RCA or 3.5mm stereo connectors on the back. Let the customer figure out how to attach the audio source.    If you attach small bookshelf speakers which are typically 2-way boxes, then you will have a decent, good sound, but no miracle. If you attach larger 3-way speakers with a good bass, then the sound will be excellent. Also, I tested with 8 ohm speakers so if you use 4 ohm speakers you should get more power from this little box.

product_title: 21st century rock
review_headline: You Get What You Pay For
review_body: Whether it's the encoding in the chip that comes embedded into the ink chambers, or the ink itself, something in the Chinese manufacture of these inks make them difficult to work with.  I am constantly having to play with color settings and print each page multiple times before getting anything right- changing out to these inks is the only hardware/software change I've made prior to this problem, so eliminating the variables, it is the ink that's causing the problems.  The blue, for instance, comes out looking hyper-electric, eclipsing the browns until I manually set the blue on a reduced intensity through the software.  Conversely, reds are muted until I up those.  Sometimes, though, I've noticed there is no solution;  nothing comes out right no matter how much you adjust it.    Printing from the Canon MP830 has always previously been a breeze, and I can see that the computer is conveying the right commands to the printer with a print preview that accurately shows what I want printed in the right colors, but after being spit out with this new ink in the printer, the pages look like something you would expect from the days of RGB dot matrix printing.        Go with OEM, save your self the hassle, even though it's much more expensive.  This Chinese-made garbage isn't worth the savings.

product_title: Yamaha YAS-71BL Front Surround System (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this for my father's birthday after considering the sony ht-ct100.  I listened the sony in best buy and the sound was weak and cold.  I originally liked the sony because it has more inputs (3 hdmi among others) than any reasonably priced sound bar, but after listening to it I felt the inputs were not worth it since my father's t.v. already has 4 hdmi outputs.  All I really needed was 2 optical inputs, which is exactly what the yamaha has.  So I bought the yamaha based on the reviews of its sound having never heard it.    Construction  This system is heavy and well made.  The glossy black finish is much nicer than the dull finish on the sony and it matches my father's panasonic plasma perfectly.  Overall the system is sexy, compact, and durable.    Features  The system could have more inputs, especially hdmi compatability or at least a video pass through.  However, if you are willing to use optical cables it is fine for 2 components.  Many sound bars only have a single audio input, so I can't fault the yamaha too much.      Sound  The sound on this system is unbelievable.  The room the system is in is huge with 20 ft ceilings and the system fills it with sound at 50% volume.  In fact it is too loud at half volume.  I was worried it would not sound much better than the t.v. speakers as the T.V. is the top of the line panasonic that has 4 speakers.  My worries were definately unjustified.  There is clear separation of the center channel speaker from the virtual surround speakers and the bass shakes the entire house when watching movies at 50% volume.  Basically, what you are getting is surround sound without the rear channel, so when watching sporting events the broadcasters voices are clearly separated from the crowd noise.  We have a much more expensive surround sound system with 7 bose speakers and a yamaha receiver in our basement and this thing sounds almost as good less the rear speaker effect.      Ease of use  The system sets up in minutes and adjustments are minimal.  It is nice that you can easily raise or lower the volume of the center channel, virtual surround speakers, or subwoofer using the remote.  This comes in handy if you would like more or less crowd noise when watching games.    For the price this system cannot be beat in my opinion.  I listened to the polk, boston acoustics, sony and samsung systems and this sounds the best by far and is cheaper than the others.  The only system that comes close is the boston acoustics but that only has a single input for sound.  I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a cheap easy way to get a movie theater effect in there house without having to run wires everywhere.  This system meets and exceeds my expectations.

product_title: SendStation Dock Extender for iPod (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Works with Otterbox Defender Case for iPhone 3GS.. with a little tweaking
review_body: I recently purchased this dock extender after plenty of research. Fits like a glove and works brilliantly. I am using my iPhone 3GS with the [[ASIN:B002FRTLHE Boston Acoustics HDUOIPW Duo-I Plus iPhone/iPod Dock AM/FM Stereo Radio and Clock Functions (Gloss White)]] and the dock extender works great. The back support really helps as well to keep the plugs from wobbling loose. It might be a little pricey, but it's the only clean-looking solution to iPod/iPhone case docking issues on the market right now.

product_title: Dayton Audio SVC2 RCA Jack To S-Video Plug Converter
review_headline: Output signal is dark and may have artifacts
review_body:
The output signal quality was unacceptable when used with an LCD monitor from Westinghouse. I tried two source devices, a Sony PS/2 and a Pioneer Laserdisc player. On the LCD monitor, there was a crosshatch artifact that was similar to herringbone distortion. I deemed the Dayton converter unacceptable when used with the LCD combination.

On the other TV that I tried, I got better luck, but I was still disappointed. The second TV is a large DLP. Here, I detected no artifacts nor any loss of signal quality, but the picture was substantially darker than when I went directly from the Laserdisc or from the PS/2 to the DLP TV with either direct SVIDEO or direct COMPOSITE. I deemed the Dayton converter marginally acceptable when used with this combination. I can't explain the difference between the two TV's I have.

My intended purpose was to use this converter with a Channel Plus SVM-22 UHF MTS Stereo modulator that only has SVIDEO in and then use a VCR that does not have SVIDEO out. For that purpose, this device is still just marginally acceptable because of the significant darkening of the signal. If I adjust the TV input to compensate for the darkening, the second input on the SVM-22 becomes too bright. I did some additional tests involving the laserdisc player, the Stereo modulator, and the Dayton converter. The Dayton conveter is solely responsible for the darkening.

If you buy a Dayton converter, you'll have no way of knowing beforehand if it will work at all with your setup. Even if you don't get the interference like I did with my LCD TV, you still be faced with the darkened signal. If your TV has individual settings for each input, you can probably correct the picture. I haven't found another product that will do the conversion, but I don't want to spend more than what a VCR with SVIDEO-out would cost. I threw the dice with this product and came up snake-eyes.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 520 Advanced Universal Remote ( 966191-0403 ) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I have had this for a couple months.  It works good - I'm surprised at how good.  I did lots of research so I wouldn't get stuck with an expensive block that pisses me off whenever I use it.  I got mine for well below $100, and the bang for the buck has turned out to be great.  The level of customizability and flexibility is amazing - they did a good job designing this thing.  Just be patient with the operation after your done with programming.  After setting it up, I realize how difficult it has to be to create a single device that can control so many components and do it fairly easily!  This review is long, but I figured you might want to know some tips and warnings to get it operating.      I like the features of having a button to access the \\"activities\\" - very nice to have it turn on all the components you want to use.  I also like having the button for \\"devices,\\" so that you can access the controls for a component directly.  The control lights up well - sometimes staying on too much; but you can push the \\"glow\\" button and turn the light off, so that it stops.  My wife is not tech savvy and with a little training, she can use it.  Buttons are easily accessible, despite some reviews I read.  The LED screen is a very helpful feature - especially using the \\"help\\" function.  One thing you have to be careful about is leaving the controller pointing at your system till all commands are sent - including delayed commands. Even if it messes up, just using the \\"help\\" button usually fixes it.    The programming was fairly easy - though you can make it as complicated as you want.  I think they updated the software to work better than some old reviews indicate.  Be sure to use all the software and firmware update options before you start programming.  You can do the programming in parts and edit as needed - basically connecting/disconnecting and taking it to your system to test it out. Just plan on spending plenty of time if you want a higher level of customization, becauseyou will want to keep testing it.    There are three levels of programming that you can use: (1) Basic predefined functions for the all-in-one operation, (2) advanced additional button assignments for the all-in-one operation, and (3) the Device (component) operation button assignments (which can have different assignments than the activities).  Its so much I gave out partway through the device buttons assignments - but you can cover almost everything with the basic and advanced assignments.  The basic assignment happens easily and automatically just by choosing your devices and assigning them to the activities, but it really is just basic controls - many buttons will be unassigned.  Doing the advanced assignments really cranks up the power and utility of the controller - but be sure you make lists for each activity and plan out what buttons do what function, and THEN be sure to assign similar functions from the different components to a button or you will go schizo trying to remember what you assigned under each activity (this is entirely under your control).  The device programming is more difficult because the default is to put most of the functions in the screen so you have to scroll through them; but you can reassign them to buttons.    Assigning functions to buttons is really easy.  You just choose what button you want to program, choose from a drop down menu what device you want it to control, and then choose from another menu which one of the device functions you want it to do.  All your specific devices functions are already downloaded and waiting to use. Fast and easy.    For me the most difficult task was dealing with components that power up slow, because the controller will send a signal when the component is not ready.  So you have to adjust the delay function, which is a little hard to find (use the online FAQ functions).  I also had problems getting the right commands to change the TV input source, so I had to find a work around (read the options for your type of input selection VERY carefully).    Enjoy!

review_headline: Good Luck Trying to Get SanDisk to Honor Their Warranty
review_body: I loved my Sansa Clip while it worked.  Three months after I bought it the battery stopped taking a charge. Instead, it just gets hot when I try to charge it. It has 9 months left of the one year manufacturer's warranty.  No problem I thought.    I registered the warranty on SanDisk's website (answering all of the questions that they asked).  I then reported the problem and requested replacement or repair.      SanDisk responded with an e-mail listing possible software fixes.  I tried them all and responded that it still did not work.      SanDisk responded with another e-mail asking a list of questions.  I responded with answers to all of their questions.      SanDisk responded with another e-mail asking another list of questions.  I responded with answers to all of their questions.       SanDisk responded with another e-mail asking another list of questions.  I responded with answers to all of their questions.    I am waiting for their next list of questions.  Other reviewers have reported getting similar runarounds.     UPDATE:    \\"Thanks for emailing SanDisk Technical Support. It is our goal to make sure you have all the resources you need to get the most from your product.    We appreciate your continued response and cooperation in trying to resolve the issue with your device. We will go ahead and process the RMA request.    Once the RMA is created, RMA department will review it in 24 - 48 hrs. If RMA gets approved you will receive two emails, first email will have the Return Instructions with the RMA# mentioned in it and the second email will have the link for the prepaid UPS Shipping label.    Do you agree to allow SanDisk to share your address, email and phone number with our shipping provider in order to create a shipping label for you?    Please print the label within 10 days as it will expire after that.    Once you print the label you are required to put the product in the padded envelope without any accessories, tape the label on top of it and take it to any UPS drop box or store, you can also use a UPS envelope available at most of the drop boxes and UPS Stores.    Once we receive the product it will take 7-10 business days for the processing then we will ship out the new product.\\"    The saga continues ....    UPDATE #2:    It has been a month since I shipped the defective Sansa Clip back to SanDisk.  Both UPS and SandDisk's website confirm that it was received by SandDisk.  So far, no replacement or any indication if or when a replacement will be sent.  I have e-mailed SandDisk about the status, but have received no response.    It is clear that SanDisk has no interest in even pretending to honor their warranty.  They simply want to make customers jump through hoops until they give up.

product_title: Sony ICFCL75iP Speaker Dock with Alarm Clock
review_headline: Never expected something this poor from Sony
review_body:
I wanted to love this item so badly. I really did. But it fails on so many levels.

1. The dock is horrible. I just cannot emphasize how bad it is. Plugging in my iPhone over and over again only to get the \\"accessory does not work with iPhone\\" message drives me absolutely bonkers. Rebooting the clock fixes it, but come on - rebooting your clock?

2. You can't browse or select which playlist/song/video to play on the clock itself. You have to select them on the iPhone. The clock functions as little more than an external speaker.

3. The USB port is not for a USB thumb drive. I don't know what it's for, but to get new songs/pictures onto the clock, you need to use a memory stick or SD card.

4. The pictures that it comes with cannot be removed. The nature pictures aren't horrible, but I don't want a picture of somebody else's kid showing up in my slideshow.

5. The screen is either too bright that it's distracting in a dark room, or basically off so that you cannot see it after the sun comes up. A light sensor or even just a dumb timer to turn off the super-dark night mode would have gone a long way.

6. The manual is poorly translated and all but useless. Some of the messages the clock displays are in funny engrish as well (\\"If the same file has already been added, the file is overwrited\\"). This is just sloppy.

7. It doesn't display the artwork when playing a song off of the iPhone. For music copied to the clock, it will display some of the artwork, but it won't display all of it (despite the artwork displaying fine in iTunes).

8. When playing songs that have copied to the clock's internal memory, it thinks they are all longer then they really are. The progress bar is therefore not very useful.

Before this list devolves into just a list of bugs, allow me to summarize briefly: It's junk. Considering how poor this thing functions, it is way overpriced. I highly recommend against it.

product_title: Klipsch Image S2 Comfort-Fit Noise-Isolating Earphones
review_body:
For years I avoided earbuds because I was never able to find a pair that fit me well. All the ones I tried wound up hurting my ears after just a short time and I reluctantly resigned myself to a lifetime of clip-ons. Sacrificing sound quality for comfort is a poor compromise and that's why I was delighted to find these earphones. The very first thing I noticed about them was how comfortable they are and how well they fit. Even after several hours, they felt good and I never got the urge to rip them out of my ears as I had done with other earbuds.

Of course, as important as the comfort factor is the sound quality and while these probably can't compete with earphones costing several times as much, the output sounded very good to me. Everything from Joaquin Rodrigo to Jethro Tull, Mahler to Metallica was clear, vibrant and distortion-free.

Like other earphones, the Klipsch S2 would probably benefit from being broken in for 24 to 36 hours. I plan to do that but right out of the box they sound terrific.

That function did not work for me, I had to set the time manually. Maybe it's because I live in Utah at the base of a mountian and it's not picking up a good signal. #2 is that the numbers on the clock are very bright. product_title: Skullcandy FMJ Earbuds / Headset
review_headline: Works with enV Touch VX11000 cell phone
review_body:
Another reviewer (\\"HappyMeil\\") must've had a bad pair. They definitely work with the enV Touch. You can answer an incoming call with the press of the button once if the phone is unlocked, or twice if the phone is locked. When you want to end your call, press the button once, and you will return to where you left off before you answered the call.

The microphone works well.

Please note, pressing the button on the earphones does not skip tracks or pause like they do with the iPhone. I think this is more a function of the iPhone than the earphones, or the enV Touch, since no where in the enV Touch's owner's manual does it suggest this capability exists.

The sound quality is excellent. Sound is louder than most earphones and I was surprised by how much I needed to lower the volume. The earphones have glorious amounts of bass, but seem balanced perfectly for the enV Touch. Multiple EQ settings on the phone easily toned down the bass for those seeking a truer sound balance.

Some reviews indicate that there are only 2 included ear piece sizes, but it looks like this was corrected in 2009. The package clearly has 3 sets of silicon ear pieces and 3 sets of memory foam ear pieces.

Sangean institutional radios have disabled audio input jacks, for example.) When you compare this model only with others of this type, it compares very well.

Update After Five Years: **************

I still think it's great! I'm buying another for use as a spare. The original works like new.

If you're looking at any of the opaque color versions of the Sangean DT-!20, KNOW THAT:

The DT-120 (white, for example) is NOT QUITE THE SAME RADIO as the DT-120-CL (Clear Case).
The white (that is, all opaque models) uses TWO AAA batteries in the case instead of one.

Some like this.

However, you may prefer this one battery clear case model. (I own both.) To it's intended customer, an extra battery means unnecessary battery expense. Pennies can add up, and to some people, that's important.) Remember that batteries are a valuable commodity in our prison system.

product_title: Terk HDTVAZ Amplified Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: In my NJ area, this works much better than others I have tried.
review_body:
I already had an amplified indoor HDTV antenna and it worked OK but I only received 15 channels and they all suffered from rain fade and even went out for a few seconds on coludy days. ie... almost daily short outages and I had to adjust the antenna for most channels. This became a pain as if I wanted to watch 3, 10, 17, 29 it was one way and 23, 61 and others another.

I was looking around and this Terk went on sale for cheap so I figured I would give it a try. I had used other indoor antennas before and was not expecting a big difference. Boy was I wrong. I hooked up this antenna and spent about 10 minutes adjusting it and after a little trial and error, the number of channels I received almost doubled to 28. I cant believe I receive channel 6 now as I have never received it before with any antenna I ever tried. 28 crisp clear channels and all for free and much much less rain fade and I have not had to adjust it at all after my initial adjustment.

READ the instructions as the two bipole antennas that come on it make a huge difference. I probably did what most do and extended them all the way and pointed them up in the air. This is not the best for the lower channels and you might not get many. I didnt get many channels until I read in the manual to shorten the antennas and dont point them up or in a \\"V\\" shape, point them horizontal. This made a HUGE difference and what got me channel 6.

I was so impressed, I ran a splitter and some cable and hooked this one antenna to three TV's and am seriously thinking of getting rid of my expensive Verizon Fios service. I dont watch a lot of TV, mostly local news in the morning and at night and then some shows like CSI, Survivor and after thinking aboout my TV watching habits, probably 90% of what I like to watch I can still watch but now for free.

I do want to add though that any like every antenna, it depends on YOUR area. You might not get 28 channels like I do and it might not make much of a difference like it did for me here in NJ. I am about 40 miles from Phila and 60-80 from NY. Also fool with the bipole rod adjustment, it can make a huge difference. Don't just pull them out and thats it. Pull them out, look at the TV, shorten them, look at the TV, position them horiizontally, look at the TV, and so on. Without spending the time doing this, I would probably be posting a review this didnt make much of a difference from my old antenna.e like it did for me here in NJ. I am about 40 miles from Phila and 60-80 from NY. Also fool with the bipole rod adjustment, it can make a huge difference. Don't just pull them out and thats it. product_title: TechCraft Wide Flat Panel TV Stand - Black
review_body: I confess that this stand really doesn't go with our home's colonial styling but, then again, neither does our 52\\" Sony Bravia XBR. The stand does however suit the flatscreen beautifully in style. I went oversize on the stand (60\\" stand for a 52\\" flatscreen) because I wanted a little 'margin of error' around the television so we'd be more likely to bump into the stand than the television and thus reduce the chance of knocking the television over.     The stand is pretty darn heavy. The frame isn't at all heavy, it's the three thick glass shelves (with the topmost shelf being especially thick) that add all the weight. I used the thin styrofoam type packing wrap to handle the shelves, which helped my grip as well as keep the glass fingerprint-free. Assembly might have been tedious but I worked while watching television so I didn't notice the passing of time. Everything lined up nicely and went together without even a single muttered curse. Knowing my husband's proclivity for spontaneously rearranging furniture, I stuck some heavy duty felt pads onto the bottom of the feet before I loaded the stand with the glass shelves. The 1\\" felt pads fit nicely into the bottom of the feet and allowed me to shift the stand on the hardwood floor even after it was weighted down. (Obviously, only do small, careful 'tweaks' to the positioning of the stand while the television is on it, otherwise remove the television before moving the stand! I know that should be obvious but...)    As others have mentioned, the shelves are not actually anchored onto the stand but the little rubbery adhesive nubs included do add plenty of friction as well as protection and the weight of the glass, even unladen with equipment, keeps the shelves pretty firmly in place -- unless perhaps you live in earthquake territory and, if you do, you probably should consider something that doesn't contain huge glass shelves, even if the glass is tempered.    I have to disagree with other reviewers about the lack of doors. Doors would only slow the accumulation of dust, not stop it, and the doors would actually make it a harder to clean, harder to assemble, etc. The simplicity of style and smoothness of the glass makes it quite easy to clean. (Cord management by bundling, wrapping, etc. will go a long way to making things easier on the eye as well as contributing to the ease of cleaning.) For the 'complaint' about the lack of doors making the equipment too accessible to children, I'd have to point out that a low object with very large spans of glass supported by 'I' shape framework is probably not the best choice for households with children. I wouldn't be worried about the tempered glass hurting the kids (unless they fell onto the edge because, even blunted, it's still a hard, narrow edge) but I'd be concerned about a sharp, concentrated force shattering the glass and causing the television to fall -- possibly on the rambunctious child.    I do love the smooth, sleek simplicity of this stand, even if it doesn't fit the rest of our decor. All the equipment blends into the shelves nicely because everything is black... except my Wii, which sticks out like a pale sore thumb. lol  So, excellent price, ease of assembly, and sleek styling make this stand an excellent choice if you don't have rambunctious children or teens, or live in earthquake-prone areas. Also, if by circumstance or positioning you need to anchor your television, this probably isn't the stand for you because there's no practical way of anchoring the television to the stand. Other than that, this stand is easy on the eye as well as the wallet and does a great job of combining simplicity, style, and functionality in one affordable -- though heavy -- package.

product_title: Sangean Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio
review_body: Update August 2010.  I have had this radio over a year and still am very pleased with it.  I reviewed all the Sangean PR-D7 product reviews and want to buy another one.    I have two edits to offer.    In my application, I drive a bus and want the radio to lie flat on it's back in front of me in a little home made box I made for it. If the base popped up and out, I can swing the antenna in a full radius.    My second opinion regards the sound quality.  Again, I drive a bus and it can get quite noisy in the background.  I cannot hear the radio with the buzz of the background  passenger noise.  Seems the speaker lacks the ability to drive the sound a few feet where I am sitting in the bus driver's seat with the background noise.    But when it is quiet, I love the sound quality this radio emits.  When my bus is empty or I am on my break, this radio does it all for me.    I dropped the radio, it broke and need to buy another one.  I want this one.  The Sangean PR-D7.  Best portable radio I have ever owned in my 50+ years.  Can't adequately describe how much enjoyment I get from this radio.    Oh, one more thing.  I bought the Eneloop batteries and I get over 25 hours of listening time using the charger these batteries come with.  Use the battery charger and don't depend on the radio to charge them.  You get a deeper charge from the Eneloop charger and longer play time.      Original Rewiew  _____________________________________  I too was tired of buying $30 \\"name brand\\" radios only to toss them in the trash out of sheer disappointment with their performance.  So I scoured Amazon for portable radios and was happy to find this radio.  What struck me instantly was the hundreds of 4 and 5 star reviews for this radio.  I read them all.... well almost all of them.  Based on these hundreds of 5 star reviews, I decided to give this radio a chance and have been very happy with it.     I can use this radio without the antenna raised and pull in great reception.  This is a great radio.  Sangean has perfected AM-FM radio reception.  I get over 30 hours of play time using Duracell batteries.  I have this radio playing at work all day long and I work 6 days a week.  I have proudly shown off this radio to fellow co-workers.    If you are looking for a dependable, quality radio that does a great job of pulling in and holding onto your favorite stations, this is the radio for you.  It is worth every dollar of the $60 I paid for this item.    I cannot say enough for this radio....
