product_title: Coby USB-Stick MP3 Player with LCD and FM Radio MP305 (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
MAY BE INCONVENIENT FOR AUDIOBOOKS
The Coby has the same "1 folder deep" file system of most MP3 players, which greatly limits taking full advantage of the 4G capacity. Tracks are played in alpha-numeric order, like most other MP3 players. HOWEVER, folders are played in the order loaded, NOT in alpha-numeric order. Higher level folders (i.e., those containing subfolders) are copied but are ignored as far as navigation or play-order is concerned. Nominally, it is possible to select the folders to play, but the folder name is not displayed. If you have several audiobooks with all the tracts of each book in a single folder (i.e., commercial downloads), you can load multiple audiobooks, but it will be difficult to select between them.

In my case, using Windows Media Player, I rip audiobooks from CD versions, which means I have a folder for each CD (named 01, 02, 03, etc. all in higher level folder such as "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince"). Note that if you drag and drop a folder such as my "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince" folder, which contains subfolders, that (for some bizarre reason) Windows copies the tracts and folders in random order, which means that on the COBY the folders will play in that same random order. In contrast, with my Zen Nano, Samsung YP, and even a crappy little Phillips MP3 player, I could load a whole book at one time (by just dragging and dropping, for example, my "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince" folder), and the (Nano, Samsung, or Philips) player would play the whole book in the correct order. Loading each folder one-at-a-time, in order, on the COBY is a major pain, exacerbated by the excruciatingly slow upload times---it can take 15 minutes or more to upload a typical audiobook.

To load more than one audiobook (containing subfolders for each CD) on the COBY would be even more difficult, I would have to rename the subfolders (e.g. A01, A02, A03, and B01, B02, B03 etc.) and also load them individually in the correct order.

While other MP3 players I've used reset the "bookmark" to zero when an audiobook is deleted, it is necessarily to reset the Coby to zero each time a new book is loaded. "Reseting to zero" requires backspacing through the tracts one track at a time---a real pain, particularly considering that some audiobooks have more than 1000 tracks.

The Coby offers two USB modes MSC and MTP, but will default to MTP if you have Window XP and Media Player 10 (or higher), in which case you cannot use Windows Explorer to copy files to the Coby or delete files---because the files themselves are "hidden". You have to push the menu button to change to "MSC mode" in order to be able to use the Coby like an ordinary thumb drive or normal MP3 player---i.e., to see the directories and contents, and to be able to copy files to and from the Coby (or delete the files). I suppose there may be advantages to messing with playlists and "syncing" them with your computer using Media Player---but not for me. Since I have two computers, I've intentionally not upgraded to MP10 on the one I use to load/unload the Coby

OTHER CAVEATS
To start or resume play, you have to press and hold the "play" button for ca 5 seconds, wait for the system to book up, and then press it 2 more times. On other MP3 players I've had, I only had to press "play" once to resume play.

All controls are 6 identical unlit buttons in a row, which means that you cannot easily operate the unit just by touch, e.g., to pause when someone is speaking to you, or to adjust the volume in a dark room.

Claims to be USB-2 for fast downloads, but in my experience loading an audiobook is agonizingly slow, much slower than other MP3 players I've used, such as a Zen Nano or Samsung YP.

Non-attached cap and battery cover are potentially loosable.

Cheap plastic. Not necessarily a problem, except for the attachment loop, to attach the player to a lanyard etc. (I use a small "cable tie" to attach the player to a D-ring which I clip to my belt loop).

No easy way to carry (except as I've described above, or with a lanyard, not supplied). No belt clip, or armband is included, and the unit would not be secure in an armband meant for other brands of mp3 players. You could carry it in a pants pocket, if free of keys, change, etc.

Front of box claims that it holds 2000 songs, back of box claims 1000 songs. Of course that depends on the sampling rate and song length--but it is evidence of poor design that the info on the box is self-contradictory

CUDOS
Good price, even for just a 4G thumb drive.

Relatively small, sleek.

Sound is very crisp, although I did not even try the included headphones (nasty uncomfortable airline/I-pod type headphones). It could be simply that the presets perfectly match my preferred headphones.

Uses AAA battery. It is important to me to have the player continuously available (with the change of battery, as needed), and not have to wait until I can charge an internal battery. Even so, I would have greatly preferred an AA-powered unit, like my Samsung YP--but it seems that no-one makes such MP3 players anymore.

The full size male USB plug nominally makes it possible to plug the unit into a computer without a cable---but in my case, the USB ports of my computer are recessed, so I have to use a short USB cable anyway.

OTHER
If the included AAA battery doesn't work, take off the nearly invisible plastic wrapping.

VERDICT
A great value for the price. Does the job, but may not be the best choice for audiobooks.

product_title: Ultra High Performance HDMI Switcher, 3to1 Switch
review_body: I don't know what there is to say about this device except that it provides great value for the price.  I have not had any problems with this product.  It simply works.  I really like the IR remote because I can hide the switch in my entertainment center.  The remote works really well to switch between either #1, #2, or #3 input.  There are more expensive switches out there, but why buy them if this product works great and costs much less.      In a general sense, a product like this is great for early adopters of HDTV's, which were equipped with only 2 HDMI inputs.  If you had only 2 HDMI inputs before, this product can double that up to four.  This prevents a person from having to buy a new TV just to get more HDMI inputs, probably to the chagrin of the TV industry.

review_body: These speakers were purchased for use in an office so we could listen to XM online.  They work great.  They were a great solution for us because our built-ins were not working properly. I also love that you can plug them in for a power source as well as use the batteries.  The only negative we've experienced was on a very cloudy, windy day, the reception wasn't great at times.  But my Satellite TV acts the same way so maybe to be expected.  I would recommend them!!

product_title: Onkyo TX-8255 Stereo Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This summer, the 20+ year old AM/FM receiver in my Maine vacation cottage died. It was a remarkablly reliable and  sophisticated Technics receiver whose power supply gave out. After searching for a replacement, I selected the Onkyo TX-8255 Stereo Receiver based on its simplicity (I wanted a good FM tuner plus inputs for a CD and audio tape), apparent power plus reliability, and of course cost. Amazon's price was the best, though at other times I could have found it for less. I ordered regular shiping but it arrived in two days!!!     The unit is as advertized: a basic receiver. No real bells and whistles. The sound is good to my elderly ears and controls are intuitive. I set it up in about five minutes, turned on the power and my problem was solved. Just what the doctor ordered.    Complaints? Nothing I didn't expect based on reviews and descriptions I'd read. Still, I am disappointed it doesn't have a loudness button and its tuning interval is .1 mhz (not .05 the Technics had), so it can't pull in distant stations as well as I'd like - i.e like the Technics.     Would I recommend it? Yes.

product_title: TDK 16X DVD+R 100PK Spindle
review_headline: Only compatible with some drives, at low speeds.
review_body: Although the box says TDK, as someody else mentioned, the manufacturer is Ritek. First 2 discs in the Pioneer drive from my laptop produced coasters. The maximum write speed accepted was 2.4x, although the drive itself is much faster and works very well with other brands. The resulting discs would not play in any DVD drive I tried.   I then tried to write a third disc on an external Toshiba drive, which routinely writes other discs at 8x, and I got a whopping 4x write speed with the \\"TDK\\". At least the Toshiba produced a disc that was readable in other drives.  If you are lucky and your drive is compatible with these discs, fine, if not, you get coasters.

review_body: Not at all happy with MP305. Earbuds on original unit chinchy .  Started having problems from start. Player would shut down for no reason. Tried deleting all music to fix problem but now player will not even turn on.    At this point i wiil trash unit and buy a MP3 player that works. Will not be a COLBY !!!

product_title: Sennheiser Sport Series II Twist to Fit Earbuds
review_body: I have used Sennheiser MX75 twist in ear style for two years running about 20 miles per week.  They got worn out, due to wire insulation fraying away. I upgraded to MX85's for same in ear style, but better sound quality.     The sound quality is noticeably better with MX85's, you can really tell on songs with some beat.  Still definitely not the best sound, but I would prioritize comfort and the fact that these headphones always stay in while running higher.    Definitely will keep buying the twist in ear style as the old ones wear out.

product_title: Bose 3·2·1 GSX Series III DVD Home Entertainment System
review_body: We have had our system for about a week.  Overall we are very happy.  It is perfect for the size room we have.  I am sure it is not as the same as true surround sound, but it sounds good to us.  It was easy to set up.  Has a helpful DVD for set up instructions and a manual that is easy to read.  Comes with most of the connection cords that you will need (real plus!)  We have not used the music storage system yet, but will try that soon.  Music CD's sound great and it will play my CD-R's that I record on my computer.  DVD player works great.  The remote also works our TV and Satellite too (two less remotes laying around!)  The best thing I can say is they have great customer service.  When I called with a question I was quickly put through to a knowledgeable rep who immediately solved my problem (which by the way was a loose speaker connection on my satellite box!)  No transfers from one department to the other and no overseas reps who you can barely understand.  Thanks BOSE!

product_title: JVC HAFX34B Marshmallow Headphones
review_body: These are, by FAR, the best earbuds I have ever owned.  Granted, I don't often invest in earbuds, but these should NOT be overlooked when considering new ones.    I use a standard Philips MP3/MP4 player for my music.  I previously owned the JVC \\"Gumi\\"s, which seemed to get excessively loud when an \\"ee\\" sound was played through them.  I also had difficulties hearing bass instruments with the \\"Gumi\\"s.  When I first listened to the same songs on the same device through the Marshmallows, I quickly noticed the amplified bass and lack of fluctuating volume.    These earbuds are very good for listening to a personal audio device in loud environments.  The comfortable mini-cushions block out all but a modicum of noise not being put through the earbuds.    I highly recommend these earbuds--especially when considering the low price (currently about $10).

product_title: eneloop Starter Kit in Blue Case (Power Pack 1st Gen)
review_body: Bought these batteries first time 2 years ago in Europe and was stunned by the capacity of the batteries (AA). Have used Duracell and other \\"brand\\" rechargeable batteries with higher marked capacity, but they are all outlasted by these.  Highly recommended batteries (carrying case is some how useless - takes too much space).

product_title: Sony MDR-W08L Vertical In-The-Ear Headphones
review_body: Great little headset. Goes everywhere with me! It is very light, you hardly feel it, and very comfortable.

product_title: Monster Small Diameter Cableit Wire Management System
review_body: A bit of \\"wrangling\\" is needed to get the cords\cables inside, but once completed, those cords\cables are not going anywhere!  Very useful product!

product_title: Altec Lansing Snugfit Earbuds w/ Silicone Ear Pads
review_body:
These are more comfortable (for me) than regular earbuds and better fit and better sound than most sound-isolating buds i have tried. ( I'll admit it seems hard to believe everyone's ear cavity will be the same shape, so perhaps that was a problem for other reviewers... )
I've used the smallest size of the three sizes of silicone pads they included. They fit well and are secure enough for a vigorous workout. No pressure points so i can wear them for a long time, unlike regular buds. I did not have to keep re-adjusting them into my ears, unlike regular buds.
The sound is better than the Skullcandy Full Metal earbuds i had previously used and is comparable to headphones for range and isolation.
The cord seems very good ( instead of plastic, it's woven/fabric sheathed)...
The carry pouch is convenient for preventing damage when tossed in my bag, and is a nice bonus you don't always get with an earbud.
The in-line volume control is sketchy. Sound quality is great at the max anywhere else is compromised... I have had better V controls on headphones, but it's definitely better than not having it at all. This is the weak link in this design.
Placement of the V control is reasonable ( at waist level, or about 40cm from the buds) compared to some others that put it too close or too far from the buds.

For $20CAD, I'm satisfied.

product_title: MAXIMO Enhanced Definition Isolation Earphones
review_headline: Well balanced sound that I was looking for.
review_body: I enjoy my music with these. They have good fit and stay comfortably for a long period of time. Also they point out all the flaws in the music, meaning you would need to listen to something in FLAC or at least in 320 kbps mp3's. You HAVE to give them time to break-in because out of the box the don't sound as good as when they reach 8-10 hours of playback. Also try all of the ear fittings till you find the right one because it has to do a lot with how they will eventually sound.   Once you've done all of that you are ready :)  About earbuds :   Sound: Is so well balanced. I'm sure I found what I was looking for. Everything I tried in the past either had overpowering bass or highs. But these are just in the right spot. Bass is rich and full yet does not overpower or mix up with mids, highs are crisp and clear. They give the atmosphere to music you listening to ( of course if it's high quality) they do not sound boring and give the enjoyment of listening.   Fit: As you can see these are kind of curved to give you comfort and prolong life of the buds. They have nice and soft silicone fittings and stay in my ears comfortably enough that I don't feel them after a little while.  Extras : Once you open up the box and see all the extras you know that everything's been taken care of.   Overall I love these and would recommend them and btw I'm buying another pair for the future.

product_title: Sony SA-W2500 Performance Line 100 Watt Subwoofer (Old Version)
review_body: I am coming in at the tail end of putting together my in home recording studio. I recently purchase a pair of the Samson MediaOne 4A and a pair of the MediaOne 3A studio monitors. While the speakers provide excellent sound quality for their price (total $250) they lacked low end frequencies like many small to medium studio monitors do. Not wanting to drop a ton of money into a solution I came across this sub.     Appearance: Let's be honest... this speaker is ugly. There is no way around it. Once out of the box it looks more like an old television than a subwoofer. I realize that many people hide their subs so this may not be an issue. I would have preferred more of a sleek design but if place in a corner with the back facing the walls it's not so much of an eyesore. It is small enough that it can be hidden rather easily, under a desk or behind a plant. It seems to be solid wood and not particle board with a \\"wood\\" covering and the constructions seems to be pretty solid. While running cables I was able to push myself off the floor using it as leverage with no structural give.     Ease of Installation: It's a mono subwoofer.. there is nothing complicated about it. You run a single RCA cable to your audio source, plug in the electrical cord, and turn it on.    Sound: We have to keep in mind that we are talking about a $100 subwoofer here. Most quality subs run upwards of $400. That being said if you are expecting a $100 sub worth of sound you will not be disappointed but maybe even slightly impressed. You also have to keep in mind that this is a 100 watt PEAK speaker. I'm not sure what the rms is ratted at but I'm sure it's considerably lower. This will not shatter walls and will not shake the earth. If you're looking for a sub that will make your house sound like one of those cars with thousands of dollars worth of stereo upgrades you're looking in the wrong price range. What this sub will do is adequately add the low end frequencies to a set up that perhaps lacks those low ends. I listen to death metal and it seems to handle this style of music considerably well.    Overall this is a good sub for under $100 but I don't know that it's worth much more than $100. Once you get closer to the $200 range then you can start looking at some of Polk Audio's lower end models which not only look better but sound better overall. I would recommend this sub to anyone looking at a cheap way to introduce low ends to their current setup. I'm not sure how this would standup as a means to provide sound for big explosions and what not for movie viewing but for music in a small room it's a good choice.

product_title: Sonic Alloy Metal-Body Noise Isolation Earbuds with Gold-Plated Stereo Connector and 3 Piece Custom Size Ear Gels
review_body: Man, is it ever unfortunate that some users give 5 star reviews for a horrible sounding product.  This doesn't help other purchasers on Amazon.  How anyone could give these earbuds 5 stars is beyond me.  My other great sounding earbuds couldn't hold up to the use at the gym and the cord ended up getting damaged. I purchased these for use at the gym, due in part to their metal construction, seemingly durable cord, etc...hoping that they'd sound pretty good and last longer.  Referring to the two users that gave these 5 stars, I bought these hoping they'd sound acceptable.  I should have listened to the 3 star reviewer who summarized it well:  \\"The lows are a bit overwhelming and mushy, the highs tinny and the mid-range seems non-existent.\\"  I'll add to this in my technical terms and say they simply sound like crap. IMO, no bass, no midrange, mushy and tinny.  Horrible.  I've had many sets of headphones...no changing of the ear gels or break in will make these earbuds sound good.  The cheap earphones that came with my HP laptop sound WAY better than these do.  If only they'd stay in my ears when I'm running on the treadmill.  These \\"INTENSE Sound\\" earbuds are mislabeled...the only thing that is INTENSE is realizing I just wasted my money.  Not recommended.  2 stars for the seemingly durable/quality construction.

product_title: Dvi To HDmi Over CAT5E Mini Extender
review_headline: DVI To HDMI Over CAT5E Mini Extender SIIG
review_body:
I have finished trying out the DVI extender I bought. What I have is Windows 7 running on a Nvidia GeForce 9400 GT video card. The 9400 has a DVI output as well as VGA to my Dell SP2208WFP monitor. The monitor's native res. is 1680 x 1050 which I use. I bought fifty feet of CAT6 wire to use and I already had a DVI to HDMI 25' cable as my standard.
Using the 25' cable, my nvidia control panel see my TV set as a Zoran HDMI TV and set the res. to 1080i or 1920 x 1080 @ 30Hz. Picture is solid with good color. Looks just like my dell monitor. When I switch to the DVI extender using the CAT6 50' wire, the nvidia control panel see the DVI extender as a DVI extender. The control panel shows the max res. at 720i. I can manually load more resolutions along with their frequencies (refresh rates) but they don't work. Nothing shows on the TV with the other rates and resolutions. They range from 29Hz to 60hz at different resolutions. I have tried them all. And really the 720i does not work because there are color sparkles on the screen, so the picture is unusable and unwatchable. To get true solid color I have to switch to 480i.
I do realize that to be real fair to the DVI extender I should have used a 25' cat 6 cable but the box does say it will work at a range to 130' or 80'. I will try to sell it but I can't list it as the company did because as far as I can tell the extender does not work at its printed specifications.
[[ASIN:B001QTW9LW HDmi To Dvi Over CAT5E Mini-extender]]
[[ASIN:B0021AEZH6 Dvi To HDmi Over CAT5E Mini Extender]]
So that is my report. Thanks for asking about my experience with the SIIG DVI to HDMI cat6 extender. I don't recommend it for High Def. pictures.
Aloha.

product_title: TriTrix MTM TL Speaker Kit Components Only Pair
review_headline: Incredible value -- but check out the kit with pre-cut cabinets
review_body: After selling a pair of well-loved Linn Katans, (sad story, don't ask, short version is: don't sell a set of speakers you love, especially if they're as portable as the Katans were.  Snif.) I found myself in a situation where I needed some hi-fi but didn't want to shell out too much cash.  I had seen some parts-express kits in the past, and had been interested in building my own speakers for awhile.  I had been imagining building a bookshelf kit, but when I saw this one, I couldn't help but get interested.  When I saw the matching pre-cut cabinets (Here is a kit with the cabinets included: [[ASIN:B002W7GSCS TriTrix MTM TL Speaker Package: Cabinet Kit and Components]]) I was sold.      OK, I did spend a significant amount of money on clamps, tools, and veneer, but the end product was still about half of what I paid for my Katans, and they sound excellent.  While they lack the incredible upper-end detail of the Katans, the bass is excellent, owing to the transmission-line speaker design.  It's a bass-boosting design, like the more common ported \\"bass reflex\\" design which dominates the market, but the bass does sound noticeably different: it's less boomy and more realistic, especially with string bass for jazz.  But there's still plenty there if you're listening to hip-hop or electronica.    Since the other item includes the cabinets, this item is probably more for people interested in designing and building their own enclosures.  If that's the case, you can disregard my comments above, but you've still probably found the best product on the market that purpose, as long as you want an MTM (Mid, Treble, Mid) design.  These parts sounds spectacular for the money.

product_title: APC BACK-UPS RS BR1500LCD 1500VA/865W UPS System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I live in a rural area of eastern Colorado where snow, thunderstorms and wind can knock our power out from seconds to hours on a pretty regular basis. As a photographer and graphic designer I spend a lot of time on my 24\\" iMac. The power outages are not only hard on the computer and external drives but my nerves as well. The power always seems to go out when I've forgotten to save a file that I've been working on for hours. I'm sure that I have over sized for my system with this back-up but it's pretty cheap insurance. I have another APC this size on my corn-burner stove as well. I'm sure that they were not designed or recommended for that, but it seems to work fine. I will be getting another soon for the T.V. and satellite system. My wife will be getting one for her computer at work as well.    If you haven't gathered, we love our APC.

product_title: C&E 3D High Speed and Ethernet 6

product_title: RCA ANT1400M Multi-Directional Digital Flat Passive HDTV Antenna (White)
review_body: Pros: can be moved without clipping a \\"rabbit ear\\" or worrying about something coming loose or breaking - one big flat slab o' plastic, durable; isn't picky about how it \\"lays\\" - flat, on the wall, on its side, propped up, stacked on books and so on; haven't found reception affected by the way it is \\"positioned\\".  Cons:  indeed, as another reviewer noted, this is not a \\"plug 'n play\\" antenna, instead plug it in, scan for channels, if you find too many missing channels, unplug, clear and start over - sure it's a minor \\"hassle\\", but in the end, after several different autoscans, my Proscan came up with all of the channels I expected and some I didn't know existed.      I do find there are days when the signal is just too problematic (lost signals and/or lots of freezing), regardless of the channel - but I've yet to find it was due to the antenna (e.g., knowing it hasn't moved and/or I haven't placed something to block it/affect it or similar), instead it must be weather, obstructions, the originating signal etc - frustrating at times, but that's what the DVD player is for - the \\"back up\\" viewing option, at least for me :)    Of note - I just moved this antenna to a new 42\\" Magnavox TV this weekend - I'm not a Magnavox fan (it was one of those \\"can't beat it TV deals\\"), but I have to admit, the antenna found even more channels on this TV than the Proscan - without the \\"unplug, clear, rescan\\" effort - perhaps just a coincidence.  In the end, I supposed I could spend two or three times the money for something that may indeed be \\"easier\\" to set up and/or achieve a few more channels - but I don't miss what I don't know I don't have - at least not at this writing :)    Prime shipping is, of course, a bonus in my book as I'm here to order a second antenna and know I can get it by Saturday morning!

Just make sure you set your expectations. These are not high-end speakers. They do not support heavy base very well and not mean t be blasted (though do support a decent volume), they are not a primary sound source if you are an audiophile.

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Radio
review_headline: Great idea, poor wireless, BUGGY ALARM CLOCK, missing features
review_body: UPDATE 2011-02-15:  I put the Radio elsewhere in my house due to the alarm problems (described below). The wireless connection seems unreliable -- it connected fine to my music collection for several weeks, and now can't find the network. I'm going to replace the Radio with a Boom (I have 3 and they're great).    UPDATE 2011-01-11:  The clock alarm feature is too unreliable, ringing when it isn't supposed to. This is INEXCUSABLE in an alarm clock! I'm probably getting rid of the Radio. Even when you disable off all alarms, sometimes it still rings, even with the latest 7.5.2 software. (See bugs 16210 and 16679 on [...].) It wakes me up on my day off. Logitech hasn't responded to my bug report about this in nearly 2 months. I am going back to an ordinary, reliable alarm clock, and reducing my rating to 1 star.    ORIGINAL REVIEW:  I *love* Squeezeboxes. I own ten of them. Unfortunately, the Radio is extremely disapppointing and I would not recommend it.    Out of the box, the Radio setup is more difficult than its predecessors.  Previously, the setup program located my home SqueezeCenter server automatically, and that was about it.  With the Radio, however, you must enter your MySqueezebox username and password, which is a pain with the little Radio dial. Why is this necessary? My home server ALREADY HAS my username and password. This is quite annoying, especially if you have a long, secure password with lots of nonalphabetic characters. I had to enter mine 3 times. My setup took 30 minutes (including the wireless problems below), and I'm a computer engineer!    Next, the Radio's wireless networking is of poor quality. From one room in my house, I managed to connect wirelessly.  When I unplugged the Radio and moved it to a different room, RIGHT NEXT TO a wireless Squeezebox Boom, the Radio said it could no longer find my network, while the Boom could. When I moved back to the original room (where it had worked before), it still insisted it could not find my network.After several attempts, I gave up and connected an ethernet cable.    Next, I wanted to set a static IP address, since all my other Squeezeboxes have one. And... it seems impossible. I look under \\"Networking\\" in the Radio settings, and all I can do is choose a wired or wireless network. Sigh. So I hit Google and find out that you can set a static IP address only if you DISABLE DHCP IN YOUR ROUTER during initial setup.  (Some Logitech documents say you can change this under Settings, but sorry, it's not there.) Since I'm not going hamstring my whole network while I set up an MP3 player, I gave up on the static IP address.  Why is this complexity necessary?  My other 9 Squeezeboxes make this easy.  Argh...    So anyway, now the Radio is up and running, so I visit SqueezeCenter to change its settings.  I visit the Player tab and look for the Menus settings... and it's gone! In fact, the Radio is missing a bunch of Player settings in SqueezeCenter.  Eventually I discover a way to change the Home menu using the Radio itself.    Now the Radio is set up the way I like it, so I try using my favorite three plugins that work on my other 9 Squeezeboxes: The Synchronizer, LazySearch2, and Bookmarks.  Only The Synchronizer works: the others won't even show up on the Radio.  Since LazySearch2 is the most valuable plugin I've ever seen (it reduces search time by maybe 80%), and I use it for nearly every song I play, this is a big disappointment.    OK, the Radio is a pain to set up.  How is the sound?  Quite good actually, considering it's mono. I'm satisfied with the sound.  The Boom is better, but it's also $100 more expensive. Also the Radio size is convenient for a bedside table.    Oh... did I mention there is no remote control?  The Classic remote works fine, but you can't buy them from Logitech anymore.  Logitech really seems to be getting it wrong with remotes: the Boom's remote omits all the useful buttons from the Classic.    And now, a final word... HELLO LOGITECH, this is your loyal customer base speaking. Enough with the useless features like \\"Buy from Amazon\\" and \\"Connect to Facebook.\\"  Give us reliable networking, bring back the missing settings, keep compatibility with plugins... in other words, get the basics right before you add whizzy & pointless features like wallpaper and album artwork display.  If the upcoming Squeezebox Touch is limited like the Radio, I will give up on your new \\"color touchscreen\\" models, go to eBay, and buy up used Squeezebox Classics before they become impossible to find. You have a great product. Please keep it great by getting the basics right.

This is really no problem for me since I simply use the buttons on the front of the switch to select my source. review_body: I was torn between this product and the Next Gen product [[ASIN:B000C1Z0HA Next Generation Remote Control Extender]]    I chose this one since it is wired and not wireless. product_title: Jacob Jensen Indoor Thermometer
review_headline: Looks good, but I can't read it
review_body:
I have owned this thermometer for three years. I enjoy its simple modular forms and its clearly-marked and easy-to-use function-buttons (Max, Min, °C/°F, Reset), and I am pleased with its accuracy. Yet Jensen's design has continually annoyed me. Here's why:

1. The thermometer appears (it is impossible to infer the designer's intent) to be designed to sit either perpendicularly or at an angle to a level surface. Bumping or touching it, due to its light weight, usually results in its falling over.

2. It is difficult to read at other than one particular angle of sight. Positioning the thermometer to be read when sitting hinders its being read when standing. And vice versa.

3. The contrast between temperature-display and its black background varies, and there is no light feature. Once precisely positioned and lit directly by bright, natural or artificial light, it is easy to read; otherwise its display area becomes a rectangular black hole.

In the design of this object, function seems to have been overlooked in the pursuit of form.

product_title: Atlantic 38435617 Oskar 1080 CD, Espresso Media Storage (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Great storage, little space, EASY setup!!! My first review.
review_body: This has been by far the best $120 I have spent. I have been looking for a bookshelf/media storage shelf for at least 6 months, looking at dozens of online retailers such as eBay, Staples, and Amazon. I have finally caved in on this particular shelf, and it's been the best thing I have purchased online!    First, the package was a little heavy and was kinda hard to put it upstairs by myself(I'm 17 years old btw :D). I was really excited though haha. :D The setup was extremely easy. Did it by myself - only took an hour! I'll tell you step by step what I did to set it up so you can get an idea.    The first step in the procedure would be to carefully take out ALL boards from the package and separate each board. Next step would be to find the middle board(all boards have a letter on them to easily identify which board is which). Then, you screw in 4 boards into the middle shelf on each side. Wasn't too hard, but took time to screw. Just remember that you aren't screwing the boards on BACKWARDS. After, would be the top end and the bottom end of the bookshelf. And guess what? You're close to finish! Rest of the steps is EASY.     The longest part would be hammering the nails for the backboard. The backboard isn't too thin, and isn't too heavy either. :) Just be sure to hammer ALL the nails so when you put some of your DVD's/games/CDs on the shelf, it doesn't push the nail back(as one review said). Oh, and remember to make sure to use a flat surface with the bottom end of the shelf sticking out. That way, it doesn't snap in half as another reviewer said. I used my bed which worked perfectly. :) The nails weren't too hard to hammer, so just be careful and diligent.     Well, I hope this review helps as it is my first! I hope this review helps in your thoughts of buying this product. I highly recommend it!

product_title: Woods Industries 509884  Do it Best Surge Tap
review_headline: Check the model # and protection level on this one.
review_body: This is my first negative review for anything I've ever purchased from Amazon.     The unit shipped did not match the unit ordered. Unit ordered was Woods Industries Model #556910 single outlet surge tap, rated at 810 joules of surge protection. [[ASIN:B000HJ97JO Woods Industries 556910 Do it Best Surge Tap]] Unit received was Woods Industries Model #509884, rated at 210 joules of surge protection. The price was great, the shipping time was great (less than two days), but at 75% LESS protection, the product was NOT what I expected. The unit ordered was \\"heavy duty,\\" while the unit received was definitely \\"lightweight.\\" ([...]) We live on the edge of a small town where power outages are almost a routine event in the Fall and Winter months, so we need the heavy duty protection for our washer, refrigerator and freezer. (Computers, TVs, microwave and DVDs are all covered already.) Built-in computers in appliances are great for reducing energy usage, but they don't deal well with transient voltage spikes.    Amazon customer service was great. They attempted to pull a replacement order immediately, but were unable to fulfill the order with the unit requested. They arranged for a full refund and sent me a shipping-paid return label to ship the parts back literally within minutes.    Now, I'll have to find another vendor . . .

product_title: Sony MDR-V500DJ Monitor Series Headphones with Swivel Earcups
review_headline: A bit uncomfortable, but OK sound quality, loud
review_body: I'm going to start with the GOOD: The sound is OK.  Highs and mids are decent while bass lacks a bit.  Construction is really durable, I like how there's no exposed cable other than where it runs to the player.  If you fall asleep with headphones on like the Panasonic RP-HTX7-W1 that have an exposed cable above the earcup you'll likely form a break in the cable from sleeping on it.  Not so with these cans.  Also the cable is nice, thick, and it's coiled.    The BAD:  It's almost impossible to listen at an enjoyable volume and be polite.  Even at just 50% volume on my Zune people across the room can hear what I'm listening to.  This is a big reason I don't like these.  If you don't care if you annoy people I guess it's ok.    They can get uncomfortable in long listening sessions (like after 45 min or so), sometimes near the end of an album I have to take a break.  The headband or whatever that holds the cups to your ears is just too strong/tight for an adult head.  It's fine for short sessions.    I actually had a pair of Panasonic RP-HTX7-W1 before these.  I fell asleep in them too often and the problem I described earlier with the cable happened so I got these to replace them.  I liked the Panasonic RP-HTX7-W1 better than these even though they have that bit of exposed cable by the earcups making them vulnerable to break if you fall asleep in them.  They were about the same price, but they were much more comfortable and sound was better ten-fold.

product_title: Sennheiser In-Ear Stereo Headphone
review_body: For basic listening at moderate to high volumes, such as riding the train or walking around, these are great headphones. I've got a couple problems with them, though. The first is that the cord is designed so that every time you touch it or it bumps against something, you can hear it basically amplified in your ears. Also, (and this isn't really the fault of the headphones) don't wear a fleece jacket with these, because you will get static electricity in your ears, which is real weird and potentially dangerous. My biggest complaint is that there is a fairly high level of white background noise, and this covers up large parts of the music at low volumes, and sometimes even distorts it a bit. This makes classical and jazz listening very difficult. If you're mostly listening to rock and pop, though, they're alright.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts APDAM2B Dual Articulating Arm (20” Extension) TV Wall Mount Bracket for 32-65” TVs (many up to 75” or more) up to VESA 600 and 165lbs, including a Twisted Veins 10’ HDMI Cable and a 6” 3-Axis Magnetic Bubble Level
review_headline: Heavy Duty Mount; Cheap Hardware; Great Price
review_body:
I looked at a lot of mounts and found most of them over priced for what they do (just hang there..). Even after reading the reviews that weren't so favorable for this mount because of the cheap hardware and poor instructions, I decided to buy it and give it a try. The price is just too good. Similar mounts at Best Buy or Sears were almost $200.

The box arrived pretty quickly and everything was there but one of the plastic knobs used to tighten the tilt angle was broken. It also looked like they sent two of the same brackets that mount directly to the TV. I had to take one apart and put it back together backwards so that the broken, plastic knob faced out and was accessible. I also krazy glued the knob back together. That was frustrating.

Like other reviews mention, the instructions are pretty sparse. Be prepared to measure (twice!) and figure out how to mount this thing on your own.

Other hardware issues:
-Anchors are bolts, not screws. You better have a ratchet set or a bit for your drill if you're buying this mount.
-The wing nuts that help control the tilt angle broke as I was hand tightening them. I'm not Superman, they're just garbage type cheap. I've never seen the wings fall off of these before. It was kind of funny.
-Mounting bolts to the TV were soft and the screw heads began to soften up after I took my power drill to them.

Even with all those issue, I LOVE this mount. It provides for a ton of movement and all the angles are easily adjustable. I would buy this again, even with all the hardware issues. It's super sturdy and should last a long time. I can replace the wing nuts for eighty cents.

Cheetah, if you're reading this, spend a few bucks more on better hardware. The mount is reasonably priced as is and a dollar or two more for better hardware is nothing.

product_title: H2O Audio Amphibx Waterproof Armband for iPod nano
review_body:
You will see this case reviewed very positively elsewhere, and the idea behind it (that you buy a case that will roughly fit an MP3 player of an approximate size, and be able to use it with multiple players, new generations of the Nano, etc) is intriguing. But it's not as great as I was led to believe.

The quality of the construction is really good. There's a neoprene and rubber arm-band, which seems very well-made. Tucked inside is a separate, heavy clear plastic waterproof envelope that is connected to an airtight gasket. You slip your MP3 player through the gasket, connect a short headphone cord, and IN THEORY slide the MP3 player in place. No problem, right?

Well, for the Nano 5G, there seem to be several issues (and based on the fact that the 5G is the same length as the 4G, these issues should occur there, too). First, the narrow rectangular gasket opening: Too short to slide the nano through sideways, you have to slide it through at an angle. Given that the waterproof envelope is none to big, and you have all that neoprene behind it, sliding it in and out is an adventure every time, and NOT the good kind of adventure. Feels like there's a serious risk of applying too much pressure to the Nano's screen, or scratching it, or whatever.

I have attempted putting my 5G Nano in there five or six times, and I have yet to be successful at getting it all the way in and positioned correctly in the window. Even if I had, the \\"hold\\" switch on the top of the Nano would not be accessible in any way -- so good luck if you have problems with \\"shake to shuffle\\" or if the plastic window accidentally depresses any of the controls. I have to believe that unless there's some trick I'm missing here, putting the Nano in and out of the case to sync or charge it will be a tremendous pain.

I really WANT this thing to work, but I'm on the verge of returning it.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 670 Universal Remote (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: So far, just a few days, the remote seems fairly easy to use.  My 6 year old(and my wife) already know how to work it!  The software on the other hand needs some improvement.  I don't like having to log into a web site to configure this.  It would have been better if the program worked offline, and only went online to download new devices etc.  While in the middle of configuring, the software would also lose the connection to the web site, and I would lose the changes I made.  This has happened a few times.  Also, even though my devices were in the database, I still had to learn the commands from my original remote, and in some cases, I had to learn the commands as RAW.  Also, a few of the commands that were in the database were actually sending out the wrong signal to the device.    For basic setup of the most common controls, the software and remote setup rather quickly, I would say under a half hour.  However, I am still configuring all the soft buttons for each activity to make it work the way I want(this will probably take a few weeks to get it \\"just right\\").  Also, it takes 3-5 minutes to upload the settings into the remote.  It seems as if it is uploading everything every time, instead of just the changes I make.  That's not too bad, but if you make lots of little tweaks, upload, test, make more tweaks, upload, test, etc. this takes up the better part of the day.    All in all, I like this remote.  The layout is fairly intuitive, wish the transport buttons (play,stop,etc) were arranged in the more traditional manor, i.e two rows instead of circular, but that is minor.  My biggest issue is the software.  The software brought this remote down to 3 stars instead of 4.

product_title: DVI-HDMI 2 Meter (6 Feet) Super High Resolution Cable
review_headline: Just as good as the more expensive cables
review_body: Don't waste your money buying a Monster cable or even a Belkin cable.  HDMI and DVI use digital signals to send the data from one end to the other.  The data either gets there or it doesn't. If the cable doesn't work right, it is because one of the wires is broken or has a bad connection to the pin in the connector.  Making sure the cable works properly is all about quality control.  But it sure doesn't cost Monster an extra $80 to test the cable before they ship it out.  So when you spend $99 for a Monster cable, you are just getting ripped off for a cable that costs them no more to make than this one.

review_headline: For those who want a Rolls Royce....
review_body: ...don't buy this and then trash it. You get what you pay for. Don't review it like you expect it to be a DJ quality direct drive 1200 series.  Good grief. It's a belt drive, and despite what some people say - the belt drive comes with the system. You have to put in on yourself. If you can't do that and do not understand the included instructions then seek help. Set up is relatively easy.    I would recommend a slightly better quality p mount cartridge which you can buy separately. Other than that, I'm playing everything from the Beatles and Led Zeppelin to The Jam and The Style Council as well as the Minutemen and Bad Brains. Coltrane's Blue Train sounds great on this system as well.    This is the perfect system for the casual listener, well built, easy to use and a sleek design.    You can adjust the tone arm if you so desire, but it was set up at the factory and runs just fine.

product_title: PARENT ASIN for Philips SHE2643/27 In Ear Headphone (Teal)
review_body:
I got these as a cheap replacement for the earbuds that came with my iPod and am quite disappointed. The sound quality is horrible, it's very fuzzy, not crisp and clear as it was with the iPod headphones.

The buds themselves are larger than on the iPod headphones. They have a rubber edge which makes them somewhat comfortable while wearing. Because they're so large, though, they often fall out because they don't fit right.

The cord is noticeably shorter than on the iPod headphones, I measured and it was about 6 inches shorter which makes a difference if you want to keep your device in your bag while wearing the headphones.

They're only $10 so it's not a huge loss but I wish I had spent a little more and gotten a better quality set of earbuds. Other earbuds in the $10-20 range (particularly those made by Sony) are of a much higher quality. Just because they say Philips doesn't mean that they're good!

Update 9/3/10: I've had these headphones for about a year and they still work! Granted, I don't use them daily, they are my backup headphones, but I'm really surprised that they have held up so well for a year! Not bad for 10 bucks!

product_title: ifrogz EarPollution Luxe Micro Bud Earbuds with Mic (Orange)
review_body:
I've always been a big fan of iFrogz products, so naturally I was expecting great things from this product. I was sold by the brand name and the styling to match my iFrogz Luxe iPhone case. I can't fault iFrogz on the look & design of the ear-buds, which are very aesthetically pleasing, and the control button is very sturdy & responsive (this was always an issue for me on the original supplied iPhone ear-buds, as the button would always go bad after about 3 months of use).

My main complaint is in the low sound quality of this product. A decent bass end is always an issue with ear-buds, but this product wasn't even on a par with Apple's proprietary buds. The sound was very thin, tinny, and seriously lacking in any warmth or richness of tone. I spent much time playing with the EQ settings on my iPhone but to no avail. I eventually went back to my old headset just to give my ears a break!

Another issue I noticed was the terrible wind & ambient noise being constantly picked up by the microphone while listening to music. I would have thought that the mic would only have been active when on a call, and there's nothing more annoying than hearing the mic rubbing against your body while walking!

I don't want to sound mean but I was almost relieved when I lost the ear-buds a few weeks later - at least I could buy something else new a clear conscience!

C'mon iFrogz, you're so much better than this!

product_title: Panasonic SC-PT770 1000W 5DVD 5.1 Channel Home Theater System with Built-in iPod dock and front-to-rear-Wireless Rear Speakers (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: HONEY turn it DOWN PLEASE!!!!! CLEAR SOUND..BIG BASS.. Follow the DIRECTIONS!!
review_body: Good day folks, just  read the one sheet that has the surround sound system speaker layout on it and you can pretty much expect to get most of the install correct the first time around. I enjoy the sub, right front and left front tower/satellite speakers, and the small rear speakers as well. The \\"WIRELESS\\" speakers ARE NOT \\"WIRE-LESS\\"...more like \\"TOTALLY WIRED\\" so don't be fooled by some idea that you are gonna just hang two wireless speakers up ...to good to be true as far as this feature is concerned. All my speakers do work and work well. The DVD player is a 5 disc holder and yes all CD's work and they LOOK like HD (not true HD 1080p) but they look better than they would on just a DVD player that does not have the picture upgrade feature. The connection in the rear of the receiver are only for connecting the DVD player to your Television and the other connection is the one that comes from your TV's AUDIO-out and to the rear of the Panasonic receiver. NOTE: the following is the best set up for maximum use of this system, which I have set up in my place: turn your TV on, Turn your Panasonic receiver on and go through the automatic setup if you have a Panasonic compatible tv or go through the manual setup as I had to since I have a Vizio 32\\" best in its class, select 16:9 as your tv ratio..REMEMBER 16:9...ok...16:9, after your receiver is happy with your setup, On your Panasonic remote select DVD (wait for about 2 min. or until the \\"Reading Disc\\" message is no longer on your Tv and your receiver will say 0:0). Now select  the setup/ ch select button at the bottom left of the remote. Select AUDIO.  you want all your audio to say bit and not PCM (bit should already be selected as it will be highlighted in a blue color). Now go to DYNAMIC..this is not set but will allow you to maximize your overall sound on your surround sound...so go to DYNAMIC MODE and use your remote and touch the \\"right\\" Arrow to select ON as dynamic is OFF by default....between you directional arrows on your remote hit \\"OK\\" to select the \\"ON\\" next Left arrow over and you will notice the \\"ON\\" is now highlight in blue...your Dynamic Mode is now \\"ON\\"..:)..Hook an optical cable from the back of your TV to your receiver for audio for all of your devices that you currently have connected to your TV...ex..I have xbox 360, xbox Hd DVD player, PS 2, and now the Panasonic Receiver/Dvd Player with an HDMI...My Xbox 360 is connected to my tv in the HDMI 2 and my Panasonic Receiver/Dvd player is connected to my HDMI 1 and my xbox 360 HD DVD player is connected to my xbox 360..I have the layout my Panasonic Surround sound system just about as exact as the diagram layout shows us. RECOMMENDATION: The speaker wires are all color coded and have labeling stickers in the plastic bag with the equipment manual. Ok, so I recommend taking the speakers one by one and attach the proper colored wire to its appropriate speaker..now look at the surround sound diagram and put your speakers flat on the floor near to where they will likely be setup. now take one wire at a time and run that one wire through the back of your tv stand and now plug that one wire into the back of your panasonic receiver and label the wire with the appropriate sticker. If you can use a piece of duck tape or a zip tie that is designed for lableling, I would label that one wire at the back of your tv stand also..since you will have a bunch of wires at the back of the tv stand, you will want to identify what wire is what in all that mess. Next do the same for the next speaker wire...last...WATCH the movie TWISTER on a sound of about 28 to 30 (it goes to 50) and you will probably have someone watching the movie with you to please LOWER THE VOLUME..LOL...\\"OK...I'd be more than happy to have to lower this BEAST!!\\" oh yeah..make sure your tv AUDIO is set on DOLBY Digital...and on your receiver you will have to press...EXT IN and select either AUX or D-IN TV(digital in tv)..If your audio out on your tv says AUX then you will likely need your Panasonic receiver on AUX...if the audio out on your TV does not say aux then you will likely set your receiver to D-IN...Remember OPTICAL OUT will have a red laser light at the none connected end of the optical cord if it the device is on..if you do not see a red light then maybe the connection came loose or the cord may be damaged...HDMI out of the Receiver is only for your Panasonic DVD player...but you can use any of the receiver/DVD players connections that is labeled as \\"OUT\\" to your tv for playing a lower quality DVD picture...OPTICAL for AUDIO and HDMI for Video...SET up the AUDIO from the Panansonic remote and Set up Dolby Digital from your TV remote...ou will likely need your Panasonic receiver on AUX...if the audio out on your TV does not say aux then you will likely set your receiver to D-IN...Remember OPTICAL OUT will have a red laser light at the none connected end of the optical cord if it the device is on..if you do not see a red light then maybe the connection came loose or the cord may be damaged...HDMI out of the Receiver is only for your Panasonic DVD player...but you can use any of the receiver/DVD players connections that is labeled as \\"OUT\\" to your tv for playing a lower quality DVD picture...OPTICAL for AUDIO and HDMI for Video...SET up the AUDIO from the Panansonic remote and Set up Dolby Digital from your TV remote...

product_title: Sony Earbud with iPod Remote Control
review_body:
I bought these headphones about 2 months ago and have been using them everyday since. I commute an hour each way on the train to work and listen to a lot of audiobooks and podcasts. I used to use my [[ASIN:B000MPNUE6 Sony Mdrnc22]] ear buds because they have noise canceling. Although since I got these I haven't used them at all.

Good Stuff
These headphones are much simpler and don't need a battery. They do a decent job of preventing some noise, nowhere near the other ones, but good enough.
These are small. The nc22s are long heavy and tangle like crazy.
The remote is very useful for pausing, volume and phone calls on the iPhone 3Gs.
The cord winder prevents most tangles.
Worth my $40.

Bad Stuff
Sound is decent but not great. Since I mostly listen to spoken word it doesn't matter so much.
The fit isn't as good as the older ones. Maybe I'm just used to them but they seem to be less secure and less comfortable. Still 100x better than the apple ones and still comfortable enough.

All in all they are really good headphones. For me the remote/mic make them worth using over any other headphones. I use it all the time. I really like being able to use voice command to call my girlfriend without having to take my phone out when its snowing. The apple headphones don't stay in my ears, sound terrible, and block 0 outside noise.

For people who are upset that they are not sweat proof, nowhere on there does it say they should be. You should check out the [[ASIN:B001GT185K Sennheiser PMX80]] or [[ASIN:B001GSX7R8 Sennheiser CX380 ]] My coworker has them and really likes them. Also they are sweat resistant, come with a guarantee, and are around the same price.

Compared to the Altec Lansing powered speakers I had before, these are much better.  I don't have any problems with interference as I did with the old speakers, so the shielding on these must be decent.  The one feature I wish these speakers had is auto-on; not a big deal turning them on & off though.    For the money, you can get better-sounding powered speakers that are just a bit larger than these.  If you really want a remote, however, I have not been able to find a better set.

product_title: Sennheiser Lightweight Collapsible Headphones
review_body: First of all, I have some headphones (Sony MDRG58V Street Style) that satisfy me in every way except they could use a little more bass. They have become the headphones to which I compare all others, and most headphones don't measure up. However, I know someday they won't be around anymore, and I also am to the point where I would like some more bass. I started a somewhat exhaustive search and decided to give these a try based on reviews about bass and thinking a pair of Sennheiser earphones I have are the best earphones I've heard.    They do have good bass for what they are, especially if you're listening to a device on which you can adjust your EQ settings. The bass might not sound that great without adjusting the EQ, and on my iPod Touch the EQ needs to be on some setting such as R&B or hip hop for the bass to really be anything special. Bass booster usually provides too much bass, but with R&B it sounds just right, for me. Other than that, I don't see how anyone can say the bass is \\"tinny\\" or overpowering. It might be overpowering if you're used to pretty much any kind of earphones or headphones that tend to sound very flat like Coby.     It is the case, as some other reviews in various places mention, sound clarity and crispness is an issue. I've seen the word \\"muddled\\" in descriptions. People also have mentioned that an adjustment period is necessary. I find there is some truth to that. Within the first 30 mins of listening, the sound did come across quite muddled and, as another reviewer mentioned, I seriously considered selling these headphones. After about 30 mins, I had basically adjusted to these headphones, and all that was left was to keep trying different genres to see how each sounded, as well as tinkering with the EQ a little more. At that point, any problems I had were not just the result of needing to adjust.     Basically, the only problem left was the sound clarity. The bass was there, and mids/highs were fine. But what I noticed is that in songsthat have a lot of sounds/instruments, many times some of the sounds either seemed to blur together in a very indistinguishable fashion, almost completely go absent or become less audible than with other headphones. A lot of the time, it's sounds that if you hadn't heard them with other headphones and/or aren't a very careful listener you wouldn't even know they were missing or lighter in volume. But for me, especially on songs I really love, it was too noticeable and it's the one thing I really dislike about these headphones. This tends to affect genres that have guitars most of all, i.e. pop/rock, alternative and other rock, country. I notice it most in pop/rock-type songs. Urban music, particularly rap, tends to sound incredible with these headphones just because of the bass and because that music, especially old school rap, isn't filled with sounds and instruments. I cannot express how great playing my old school rap playlist on my iPod Touch was, either, and this is one area where these headphones absolutely whipped the Sony headphones I love. I felt like I was at a party and almost felt like I was in an SUV with a decent-to-good sound system. Unfortunately, I do love a lot of sound-filled music, as well, and I wish I could enjoy the full range of sounds in all my music. Sound just isn't balanced with these headphones, and it's not because of \\"overpowering bass,\\" either--you can change the EQ settings to cut down the bass, and clarity/missing sounds is still an issue. It's a little surprising, given their earphones--or at least the ones I have--have very clear sound. I have just ordered the PX200s because I've read they have more clarity, and I will review those once I receive/try them.    The only other issues I had with these are in some songs the bass doesn't seem to respond no matter what EQ setting you use, or at least not as much as you'd like (again, most noticeable in pop, pop/rock-type stuff, which it seems a lot of people don't need/want much bass inthat kind of music anyway. I love bass in all my music, though); depending on the natural volume of the tracks you're listening to, some will satisfy you if you like loud music and others won't sound loud enough--and the iPod Touch is the loudest mp3 player I've ever heard, so if this is the case with the Touch then it certainly will be the case with other players; along the lines of sounds going missing, there are some songs in which I can barely hear the bass drum clearly; I would like to see volume control included with these headphones. Other than that, I find them comfortable and don't mind the open-air design. Being that I like loud music, I turn my music up enough so that outside sounds don't really bother me. And I have found that even with closed-ear designs--well, if you're like me, anyway--sound is going to leak out.  --  Conclusion: Pretty good bass if you can adjust your EQ settings, but clarity is a little lacking, especially if you're a very careful listener. These headphones are perfectly fine for most people and will probably sound excellent to the average listener, though, especially if used more for traveling or any other time when you're not going to be listening very carefully. I wouldn't necessarily spend $40 for them, especially with cheaper headphones that balance the sounds out more and have more clarity with acceptable bass after EQ changes--like the Sony headphones I mentioned (I have never spent more than about $22 on them). But these are certainly now #2 on my list of headphones as far as balancing sound quality with cost if you can find a deal where these are about $30 or less (like I did), especially if you like bass, and they are definitely better than some of the more expensive headphones I've tried (i.e. Skullcandy Skullcrusher headphones, for one).

review_headline: Excellent but could use better foam tips
review_body: I have had my HF2s for almost a year and love them.  Great sound, good noise isolation and the microphone works well with my iPhone.  I have not had problems with wind or cable noise.  My only complaint is that the foam ear tips are not that comfortable and are fragile.  The foam retracts from the harder core and loses its sound-isolating ability rather quickly.  My solution has been to replace the foam tips with the tapered foam tips that Shure provides for the SE-210, which I also own.  These are more comfortable, last longer, and fit easily on the HF2 nozzle.  I also have an iPod nano.  Users should be aware that the HF2 plug (and any earphone/mike plug)will cause problems with the nano.  When the plug rotates, it can pause playback or switch the nano to another song.  I would recommend an adapter plug or cable if you go back and forth between an iPhone and a nano.

product_title: Sennheiser In-Ear Stereo Headphone
review_body: I read the reviews and took the bait at under $20.  Wow, what a disappointment.    Let's start with the sound quality: it is worse that the stock Blackberry headphones that I replaced it with!  Treble is tinny and base is non-existent.  I was fatigued from using them after only 10 minutes.  Positioning them in the ear is critical and think I did get them where they needed to be.  The Apple headphones that seem to be the reference for the CX300 must be horrible.  Those of you with audiophile tendencies like me should stay away from this set.    Now for the cord.  It's too noisy (unless you are completely motionless), too short and the asymmetrical design causes the headset to pull awkwardly when you turn your head (especially given the short cord which takes out any slack).  I read others reviews of these issues and thought the negative ones were being overly critical given how many positive comments there were.  The negatives were right!  Again, none of these issues existed with the Blackberries.  Even the wire gauge was as thin as the Blackberries.  If you are rough on headphones then these won't last for you.    I need to point out that I have an excellent over the ear set of wireless headphones for my home system from Sennheiser that are excellent so I was expecting something good to arrive in the package especially given the high user ratings.  For me, I wouldn't use the CX300 even if they were free.  I'm still in shock that the Blackberries are better!

product_title: Philips Behind The Head Headphone
review_body: I paid very little for these at WalMart. I was looking for an inexpensive set of headphones for all-around use (at home, on a walk, etc) and I was looking for a pair that were small and subtle, but at the same time had decent bass response and decent clarity. These fit the bill perfectly. I'm not a fan of earbuds so those were out of the question, so these slim, light-weight, comfortable headphones were the perfect choice.     With the great bass response, and strong mid-range, music of any kind is great, and movies sound great as well. At-home listening on the PC while playing a DVD or listening to FLAC music files is great. I had never considered buying a pair for this cheap, and was unsure about the sound quality but after using them, I was blown away. I have used Senheisser, Audio Technica, and Sony, so I am used to paying no less than fitty bucks for a set of headphones. The price/performance ratio for this pair is phenomenal.     Great bass for on-the-ear design, and great clarity. Not bad for a cheap pair.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 880 Advanced Universal Remote Control (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Have AV equipment with no manual or remote, This remote is your new best friend
review_body: This remote has saved me millions, not really, but in stress probably.  I buy many audio components off of eBay.  Many of the best deals do not have manuals or remotes.  This Single remote has saved my life, in some respects.  All be it any Harmony remote could do the trick.      I've owned this remote for a couple of years now.  The initial setup takes a little bit of time, but its a fairly easy walk-through.  The features you get to use on this remote, leaves other universal remotes in the dust.   I recently bought a New LCD Toshiba and a Yamaha 7.1 channel receiver I bought off of eBay.  To swap out my old Samsung TV and my old Pioneer receiver took less than 10 minutes.  I was even able to have more features on my Harmony remote than the factory OEM remotes for either of the other two.  This remote even controls My Media Center PC, everything from movies and music to DVDs even iTunes and some feature of the internet. Support for this remote is also easy to find and updates for new equipment is often.    The only feature I wish this remote had, which are available in the more expensive, Harmony 890, 900, and 1100 models is the RF feature that could control the fireplace, ceiling fan, lights, and shades.     In my opinion I will probably never use another brand of remote for the foreseeable future. I was going to say for the rest of my life, but the amount of technology that has changed over the past ten years, it's hard to say what will be available 20 years from now.  It might all be wetware(mind controlled).   I purchased my Harmony Remote from Woot! For $69.99

product_title: Antennas Direct 42XG Antenna
review_body: The reviews on this antenna were spot on! Easy assembly, all hardware needed for mounting to a shaft was included. Assembly and installation couldn't have been simpler. I needed to install an inline amplifier though (radio shack #15-1170) [...]  to get a strong signal to the TV. The signal from the antenna directly to just one TV was fine, but once I split the antenna cable to feed 3 TVs the signal was very poor. A radio shack inline amplifier installed on the main feed line from the antenna (before the splitters) fixed up the signal nicely. Clear as a bell HD quality on all TV's...     I roughly aimed the antenna in the general direction of the Sutro TV TransmissionTower here in the SF Bay Area (~ 30 miles away). No tweaking needed for a good picture... AWSOME product. It will pay for itself in 1 month now that I have cancelled my cable TV suscription (~$63/mo for COMCAST basic cable here in the SF bay Area)

But overall, if you are looking for reliability and ease of use, this is an outstanding remote.

product_title: Speakercraft Aim 7 Two In-Ceiling pivoting Speaker (EACH)
review_body: Speakers are like cars, TV's, etc. You really need to test them out in person, compare them side by side with the competition and then make an informed choice.    I would not choose these speakers, especially considering they are to be installed in the ceiling or the wall and this would probably require hiring someone to do the work, unless you have the tools, knowledge, time, and ability to flush mount them yourself.    The sound quality is decent. It gives off acceptable low end bass, while the high end is also fairly clean and the sound level is also acceptable.    I'm far from being an audiophile, but I do have my own HT setup and even have surround setups for my computer systems, and when compared to what I already own I saw no reason to install these speakers to replace what is already there. The time, expense, and little to no improvement in sound quality just didn't justify a change.    This model is also the 'budget conscious,' model and there are higher end and higher price options from Speakercraft that could be a consideration for someone who is set on mounting speakers into their ceiling, but once again, it would be a good idea to test and compare in person.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16 GB 5th Generation
review_body: I purchased this iPod after my beloved 60GB iPod video was stolen. It has a nice design and it is very portable. The video camera and radio are nice features, although I haven't used either extensively. I mainly use it to listen to music which is why I gave it four out of five stars. Unlike my previous iPod, wakeup time when in powersaver mode is extremely slow. I will press the next or center button after I have been listening to music for a while and it will take about three seconds to either show me what song is playing or change the song. My older iPod did these things almost instantaneously. Secondly! My least favorite part about this new iPod is the battery life!! It says on the website that it is 24 hours but mine will only play for about nine. I have the brightness turned all the way down and the energy saver is on. Neither of these boost my battery life to 24 hours. As I mentioned above I mainly use this to listen to songs so there should not be that much strain on the battery. I have researched and this seems to be a problem for most people with these iPods. This is a good music player with good sound quality. The video camera also records very well (except in low light) and the radio is nice too. If you are a patient person you will not mind the slow wakeups and song changes but if you're used to the older videos they are much faster. Also battery life is horrible and definitely not 24 hours like it says on the website.

product_title: Apple iPod touch 8 GB 2nd Generation

product_title: Sennheiser Sport Earbud Line Stereo Neckband Headphone
review_body: I've just recently switch to wrap-around type headphones and love these.  There are some threads here that indicate the pressure created on the ears for these are too much, but I did not find that at all.  The phones created a perfect fit that eliminated most of the wind/road noise.  I use these for running and there is no movement at all once they're in place.  The single cord on the left is very nice, heavy and has enough length to do what you need...attach at the waist if you like.  I personally use an arm band and prefer shorted cord lengths, so I have excess to deal with.    The color is great!      The only downside that I can come up with is already identified in the threads.  Sweat buildup around the earbud.  The angle of the bud is perfect for channeling music to the ear, but this also allows for sweat to channel into the earbud as well.  I run for hours at a time and even in the northern climates you sweat.  The PMX70s are not waterproof and therefore while running I remove them, wipe and put them back in place.  For the price, with a little care, you could have a great set of headphones last for quite a while.    If you want waterproof, you'll have to more than double your price and get the PMX80.

product_title: Sony SS-B1000 5-1/4-Inch Bookshelf Speakers (Pair)
review_body: Got these with an Onkyo Receiver and Ipod dock.  Thought they might be a little small, but they sound great. For the money, I am satisfied.

product_title: Emerson ES769 Micro Stereo System
review_headline: CD works well' Radio needs work
review_body: Got as a gift for my mother for Christmas, so she can listen to her opera CD's.  The CD player seems fine, and it is pretty easy to operate.    However, it lacks a decent antenna for the FM radio, and getting a good station in can be frustrating.    I would recommend this as a small unit for a den or something, but it won't stand up as a main household system-the power just isn't there.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-919AH-K 120 Watts A/V Receiver with Full Color GUI/OSD, Advanced MCACC and Analog to HDMI Up-Conversion (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Probably the best receiver in it's price range
review_body: You'll be hard pressed to find a receiver with more features in this price range. I spent ALOT of time researching receivers and for the money the VSX-919-AH-K was it.I am extremely pleased with it. For the price, you get lots of features, some not available on units 3 or 4 times the price. Sound, the sound is excellent, very clean, match it with quality speakers and people will think you spent alot more than you did. The on screen programming is really cool, and the MACC (auto calibration), which will configure speaker level and to some extent the sound parameters is really helpful as it allows you to get it up and running right away. As you learn more about the functionality you may want to tweak the auto settings, but you wont have to. It was nice being able to run 3 HDMI and,or Composite devices through it eliminating some cables. It has a clean look to it, and the remote can be programmed to operate multiple devices. The manual could use some work. The informaiton is in there, it's just not well written. Sometimes the auto select for the surround mode does not choose what you would expect, but you can change it. The setup was not all that difficult. If this is your first surround receiver (or in my case first reveiver that also controlled the video), it can be a little tricky. Remember whatever format you put into the receiver, HDMI, Composite, etc, you have to have that same format going out to the TV. You can't plug all your devices into the recevier and then just have the HDMI or Composite, etc going to the TV. All in all a good receiver at a great price. I am using Klipsch Quintet speakers and a Klipsch 10\\" powered sub, and as for the rated power of 90w @ 8ohms or 120w @ 6ohms, I cannot turn it all the way up and stay in the room, at least not comfortably.

product_title: Altec Lansing BackBeat Titanium noise-isolating earphones
review_body: I picked up the [[ASIN:B001GUPEMW Altec Lansing UHP326 Backbeat Series In Ear Headphone with Ultimate Ears technology]] earlier this month as a Gold Box item at a fraction of their regular Amazon price.  These are my first IEMs and I am very pleased with their comfort and sound. Comfort for me is really important and I am finding that I can wear these for much longer than I can on ear headphones or the Apple ear buds that came with my ipod.  In addition to the clean mids and highs they deliver, I am really surprised at how much bass these put out. These come with a padded, soft storage pouch which I have found to be very convenient. Otherwise, the earphones and extra tips would be just laying around.    The bottom line for me is that these IEMs are very comfortable with enjoyable sound quality.

product_title: Skullcandy
review_body:
I've had a pair of Hesh headphones for less than a year, and two days ago they cracked. The portion of the band that retracts inside the main band when you extend them simply cracked on one side, and you can see where it's getting weak on the other side as well.

I'm really disappointed because they sound just as good, but don't sit right now, as the right ear cup tries to bend out away from my ear when I try to wear them, diminishing the sound quality only because that side doesn't hug my ear as it should.

All in all, they sound great, but I'm a stationary headphone user (sitting at home, working in the computer lab at school, etc.), so I can only assume they'd break more quickly under more strenuous use.
