product_title: URC WR7 Universal Remote Control for up to 7 A/V Components with 4 Favorite Channel Buttons
review_headline: Macro and learning functions of a $100+ remote for 1/5 the cost
review_body: Logitech Harmony 520 vs. new URC WR7 - URC WR7 wins!    Got my girlfriend's dad a nice Denon receiver, DVD player, and we went out on black Friday and picked up a Samsung plasma display and hi-def cable box. Brought everything home, set it up, and everything works great but the remote situation was too complicated for others to operate. So I did a bunch of research, compared features of modestly-priced universal remotes, and decided on the URC WR7. Got it for him for Christmas and even went through and pre-programmed it for him. It was such a breeze to program, including macros, and I only had to learn one missing IR command. I liked it so much I recommended it to my mom to replace her Harmony 520 that just recently flaked out. Same thing for her - breeze to program, including macros, and is able to operate every one of her components without issue now. With the easy of programming and versatility of the WR7 I would even consider it as an alternative to my much more expensive PC-programmable URC MX-850! I actually plan on picking up a WR7 as a secondary remote.    Programming:  - 3 methods - 3 digit code by make, auto search, and learning.  - Most components can be programmed via the 3 digit code entry by make. If that fails, try auto search by pressing the component button and then arrow up/down on the remote until the component turns off which indicates you have found the correct codes. As a last resort you can always learn the commands directly from the component's factory remote.  - The WR7 includes an extensive and very complete built-in IR database that included every single device in two different installs except for a specific model Kenwood receiver (learned commands for that).  - Learning IR commands from a factory remote is a breeze compared the Logitech's web-based software. Simply place the two remotes face-to-face, press the button to be programmed on the WR7, then press & hold the corresponding button on the factory remote until the component LED flashes. Continue on until you have learned all necessary commands. It really can't be any easier. Compare this to Logitech's web-based programming software which sounds nice a first but ends up being confusing, overly-complicated, and unorganized.  - Programming macros is also simple. Simply press the button you want to assign the macro to, then mimic the commands right on the remote. The remote will record and save this command sequence and repeat it back when this button is pressed. This includes the ability to power all components on/off with one button.    Quality:  - WR7 has a comfortable, ergonomic feel with soft easy-to-press buttons, and solid construction that doesn't make you worry about dropping and damaging it.  - The Harmony 520 had \\"clicky\\", hard-to-press keys with a hollow, cheap, plasticy feel.

product_title: Pioneer VSX-9040TXH 7-Channel Direct Energy Amplification Home Theater Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Let me start by saying that I don't consider myself an audiophile or any kind of A/V system devotee. I'm technically adept enough to have no problems hooking up multiple components and programming devices, but other than that I wouldn't describe myself as any kind of \\"power user\\" when it comes to home theater equipment. I just enjoy watching TV and movies with good, immersive sound.

I recently upgraded from a cheap old Sony \\"home theater in a box\\" receiver (STR-SE501) that we've had for about 10 years. The Sony served us well, but since we're accumulating components with HDMI outputs (the Sony had no HDMI) we needed to get a better receiver. I looked around for a while and considered a variety of receivers, looking mainly at the Yamaha models ranging from $400 to $1000. When it came time to finally pull the trigger on the purchase, I stumbled on this Pioneer unit on Amazon and was intrigued. I quickly checked reviews on AVSForum and based on those reviews and the price, I was sold. I added guaranteed Saturday delivery for $6.99 (placing the order around 11:30 on a Thursday night) with my Prime membership, and it arrived at my door just before noon on Saturday.

Hookup was straightforward, except for a little confusion (my fault) in which speakers to hook up for a 5.1 configuration. Overall, I prefer the screw-down connections to the spring-clip kind my old receiver had, it makes for a much more secure connection. Works fine with the cheap Sony HTIB 5.1 speakers, which I don't have the resources to upgrade right now... in fact, I was surprised to find that the sound quality is even better. Setup was pretty easy - the MCACC program walks you through the level test and tells you if your speakers are in phase or not, so you can swap the wires if necessary.

The unit has a reassuring weight to it (35 pounds shipping weight) that makes it feel like a serious piece of equipment, but one minor unexpected issue was that it's considerably deeper than the previous receiver, so I had to scoot the entertainment center another inch or two away from the wall to allow some room for the cables hanging out of the back.

Copious inputs on the back ensure that you can run pretty much any kind of components... 4 HDMI inputs is more than most people will need. Was easy to program with my Harmony 880 remote and has been working well for a couple of weeks now. Don't think I could have gotten a better receiver for the money ($540 including shipping).ious receiver, so I had to scoot the entertainment center another inch or two away from the wall to allow some room for the cables hanging out of the back. product_title: AKG K 242 HD High-Definition Headphones
review_body: Comfy, light, form-fitting, and stunning audio fidelity. I admit that I've never bothered to spend more than 20 to 50 bucks on a pair of headphones, but after 30 years of discomfort and lifeless response from cheap cans, I decided to splurge. I'm a composer and musician, and do all my recording in my apartment. In order to preserve the peace with my neighbors, I use headphones most of the time.  Right out of the box, I plugged these into my stereo and put on the David Byrne/Brian Eno cd 'My Life in the Bush of Ghosts' - my litmus for most new gear since I know it very well. It was like listening to it the first time. I heard things in the music I never noticed before, and the experience was quite moving. The sound detail was mind-blowing. It's hard to describe, but it was like I could feel the percussion instruments' density and materials - something I've never experienced in consumer-grade audio gear. And I know these headphones aren't top-of-the-line audiophile by a long shot, but what a profound difference from all my previous experiences.  I can wear these 'phones for hours with extreme comfort (though they did take a little getting used to), and they've only improved with use. I don't get the usual ear-sweat or fatigue from the semi-open design, and even listening to mp3's on my computer has taken on a whole new life.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player
review_body: I had done a lot of research and I finally settled on this player for its small form factor, expandable memory, cool design, and brand name respectability.    I really like the size of this player.  It's not quite iPod Nano thin, but it's good enough.  It fits really nicely in my shirt pocket and I keep it in there a lot.  I've even started keeping it in an Altoids tin (yes, it fits nicely in them).  The screen is a good size and so are the buttons.    I haven't used the video capabilities on it yet so I can't comment on that.  All I will say is that you need to download a big converter program to make them compatible for the Fuze.  They say they're working on making video transfers easier but it hasn't happened yet.  They've released two firmware updates since I've had it so they aren't just sitting around, dealing with complaints and making lame excuses.    So right off the bat I don't really care for the main interface.  It has nice icons and all but I don't like the way it's a circular list.  I would prefer a normal vertical list or an icon grid.    On the music menu they have typical categories like Artists, Albums, and such, but I really like that Audiobooks, Podcasts, and Recordings are under their own sub-menu.  With the latest firmware they even added a Folder view.  Scrolling through the lists is pretty easy, I like how it's an actual wheel that turns and not a virtual touch wheel.  It's not too easy to feel, but it's also kind of nice how you can feel an actual click going up and down lists.  Speaking of which, I'm terribly disappointed that there's no audible click while scrolling.  There's not even an option to turn on such a feature.  I don't know if a firmware upgrade would change this though, if there's no kind of mini speaker to make the noise.  I also might have been happier if the text was a bit smaller.  It couldn't get much smaller and still be legible, but if an Artist or Song is over 14 characters it gets cut off (it will scroll to show you the rest).    One big plus that made me choose this over another brand is that the expandable/flash memory integrates with the internal memory.  Because of this it does take some time to build the library [depending on how many songs you have].  Sometimes it's a good idea to unplug the player and go take a shower while it's refreshing.  This only happens if you add or remove songs on a PC though.  Just charging a player, reading it's contents, or deleting a song through the player menu doesn't cause a refresh.    I love that it uses microSDHC, not just microSD.  According to the SDHC standard it could go up to 32GB.  With the internal and expandable memory I don't see myself filling it up without putting on a bunch of stuff I'd never watch or listen to.    One gripe I have about the player is connecting it to the PC.  You can't have it just charge.  It's either connected or it's not.  That makes me wonder if the player would charge itself if I hooked it into a USB car charger or wall charger.    Another gripe I have (that they are aware of and working on) is the playlist changing.  If I'm playing a specific artist when I turn off the player it might play every song when I turn it back on.  The same thing could also happen when I delete a song.  Similarly, the ratings you are able to give to songs means nothing.  I could rate every song, turn off the player, then turn it back on and they'd all be gone.    One last tiny little thing I wish this player had was a Mono mode.  Sometimes I just leave in one earbud to hear what's going on around me and I end up losing half the song in Stereo mode.    This player isn't perfect, no player is, but at least they're continually working to make it better.  If you want the extra capacity and better video functionality go with the similar [[ASIN:B000MQJ19S SanDisk Sansa View]].  If you prefer a small player that's mainly for music then I'd highly recommend the Sansa Fuze.    One last thing.  GET A CASE FOR THIS THING BEFORE YOU USE IT!  The screen scratches way easier than you'd expect.

product_title: Sony STR-DH800 7.1-Channel Audio Video Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I searched for several months before pulling the trigger & buying the STR-DH800. Despite Sony bashing by many, I am very satisfied with my purchase. All of my other toys are HDMI equipped & up conversion was not a consideration. It has a decent amount of power & plenty of connections for virtually any device the average consumer will own. My suggestion would be to invest in banana plugs & save yourself a headache when connecting speaker wires, they saved me quite a bit of time. [....] has them pretty cheap.

The auto cal. does a great job at setting up speaker levels & distances. Night mode is also nice. The manual & menu may not be friendly to a newbie. An onscreen menu function would have been nice. If your seat is more than 10 ft. away, as mine is, you will end up standing or straining your eyes to make small adjustments. The receiver is relatively tall, but it is not very deep. It has a nice & simple layout. The buttons & knobs have smooth action & the display is not distracting while watching movies. It does not generate very much heat.

It has been a long time since I purchased home theater equipment & I am very satisfied with my purchase. My system includes: a Sony STR-DH800, Samsung BD-P1600, Sony DVPNS710H, Xbox 360 Elite (Resident Evil LE), Dayton HTS 1200 surrounds, Sony bookshelves, Logitech Harmony 550 remote, Dayton SUB-80, & Vizio 47XVT. Been busy since Christmas.

At it's current price, this receiver is definitely worth a look. I am sure you will not be disappointed. It has helped me save over [...] based on the HTIB I was considering.

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Clip 4 GB MP3 Player
review_body: Don't buy this for audio books unless you only plan to listen (and pay for) [...]audio books. After researching, reading forums and consulting others for almost 6 months, I finally took the plunge and purchased one of these primarily for listening to audio books since it was recommended as having a good bookmarking function, something missing from many other MP3 players. Unfortunately, no one mentioned that this function only works effortlessly with books downloaded from [...] and doesn't work at all with books downloaded from other sources, including those thousands of books offered free in my state from the public library. After searching on the web and reading hundreds of techie posts, I've found instructions on how to get the bookmarking function to work with non-audio books [...]; unfortunately, they involve downloading shareware to change metatags and other things a non-geek like me should never have to think about.  It's interesting to note that Sansa, on a posting on their forum in 2007, said they were working on a fix for this problem. My guess is they have an agreement with Audible.com not to try too hard, since they haven't come up with a solution yet.

review_body: Update as of 24Sept09:  It has started make popping sounds and can quit in the middle of a song.  I would not buy this speaker again.      Got this little speaker for work. product_title: MICROSOFT B4F00014 Xbox 360® Wireless Controller
review_body:
If you've got an XBox 360, you really should buy a couple of these These controllers are GREAT and clutter up your gaming area. To start with, the controller is much smaller than the standard XBox controller was.

For control items, you start with the standard blue X, yellow Y, red B and green A buttons. There are two thumbsticks, one on the upper left and one in the center right. There is also a directional (d-pad) in the lower left.

Next, you have a pair of shoulder buttons at the \\"top\\" of the unit, up above the other buttons. You also have a pair of triggers below those shoulder buttons.

Finally, you have a center X button that can be used to turn the console on and off, plus a \\"start\\" and \\"back\\" tiny white buttons on either side of it.

The buttons work great and they last a long time. defanently a great buy.

product_title: Philips Color Match In-Ear Headphone
review_headline: Fantastic Quality at a Low Price
review_body: When I purchased these a year ago two things drew me to them: the low price and the simplicity. I honestly was not expecting much out of them. What I got, however, is a whole different story.     The frequency range is an impressive 12-22,000 Hz (the average audible range for humans is 20-20,000 Hz, which is the typical range for cheap earphones). I listen to everything, from classical music to death metal, and these earphones produce excellent sound quality for the entire range of music. The sound was crisp, clear, and refreshing when listening to classical music; loud, full of bass, and with no distortion when listening to death metal. I liked them so much I even bought and extra pair to keep in case something happens to my current pair.    All in all, I would definitely recommend these. They may not be the Bose quality earphones that audiophiles are looking for, but they also don't come with the $250 Bose price tag.

product_title: Zune HD Video MP3 Player
review_body:
I have spent 2 days working with the Zune HD 16gig unit. Here is my impressions. This unit is a good starting point. There is a lot to love about the unit and some things that make you think why? The feel of the unit is amazing it is very thin and light it makes you wonder is this really going to play everything I throw at it? Well truning it on for the first time you look at it and go \\"WOW\\" what a screen. I have owed a long list of mp3 players including Zen vision W Ipood touch (1G) Iphone (1g) and the Archos 5 tablet. Until this point the Archos had the best looking screen. Now the Zune HD takes first place.

Touch response was great at times I felt is was a bit too touchy but I am getting use to it. To me the touch is read faster then on apple players not saying everything launches faster. Apps do take a long load time and they almost feel like an after thought they just do not seem to blend in as well as on the touch. Music play back is great. I am a bit disapointed with the ear buds included I think MS could have steped it up and give a better classyer pair they seem like a let down compared to the player. And why no cleaning cloth? This should have been included in the packageing.

Video playback is where I spent a lot of time here was a mixed bag of success and failure. Having owned several other players 1 being the Zen Vision W I have a nice collection of video's. Must of these came from Amazon Unbox and I have yet to get them on to the unit. This I feel is hurting the ZUNE Hd compared to the video offerings from apple I would think being able to use Amazon Unbox right away would be a very impotant thing. MS market place has a very poor offering of videos both movies and TV Shows and MS can use the Amazon site to show off thier units. Along with the weak video offerings I am wondering why on the Zune HD can you not make a video playlist this hurts big time. Now you can not do it on the Zen Vision W and it took an upgrade to do it on the Touch but now it is something expected out of the box why wait for an update this makes no sense.

Continue with video problems it is known that Apple has removed DRM from a lot of the music videos on thier site and since I owned a touch I wanted to watch these on my Zune HD. Now they will play in the Zune HD Software on your computer but try to transfer them to the unit and you hit a wall. I had to come up with a work around that required me to convert all my DRM free videos with the use of my Creative Zen software this took time and there is no reason as to why. Once converted they do look great.

Ok now let's look at the browser. It is a bit weak could be alot better. I am not sure if it is my home network or the unit but it kept loosing connection when loading pages. This adds to the load time which is slower then on the Touch. I still plan on doing more work with the browser right now I would say it is ok.

My review title says it all this is a good starting point for MS some things I think should have been done before it was shipped (Amazon Unbox, Video playlist) and a better use of the App store. It is great everything is free but there is no killer app in the store yet. I would like to see MS quickly add a few things one being a PIM app after all they are the makers outlook so I would like to carry my contacts and stuff right on my Zune HD.

Should you buy it that is a tough call if you want to get in on the ground floor of a new hot product and can accept that growth may or may not come quickly then you will love playing with it. If you want a more finshed product that has a base in placed then you must go to Apple just be warned you are tradeing in tommrow tech for yesterdays tech if you do so.

Update (09-25-2009)
I did some more video work on the Zune HD and for everyone that has Tivo I was able to transfer some of my Tivo recording to my zune for watching on the go. Again I had to use the Creative Zen software to covert the file and then added it to me Zune HD.e HD.

product_title: Onkyo HT-RC160 7.2-Channel A/V Surround Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I spent over an hour wiring my home stereo system with my tv, speakers, dvd player, and other components to the receiver.  Once all the equipment was hooked up to the receiver, I plugged in the unit and  pressed the power button.  It turned on and immediately went into standy mode.  I assumed it was normal that the receiver would go straight into standy. For some reason the unit would not turn on after I pressed the power button on the unit and on the remote control. I unplugged the unit and plugged it back in and it would still jump right into standy mode.  I spent another 20 minutes trying to turn on the unit and just got so frustrated that I decided to call Onkyo's customer support.  I explained to the service rep the situation and the first thing he said was that the unit is defective and that I immediately return the unit to Amazon.  I hope my replacement unit will work or I will seek a refund.

product_title: Sony STR-DH800 7.1-Channel Audio Video Receiver (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought this specifically so I would be able to access the DTS Master Audio  and Dolby True HD  available on many of the new Blu-Ray discs and I am not at all disappointed.  It was not yet in stock at Amazon so I paid what turned out to be a 65$ premium by ordering it from Vanns (so watch out for that -I could have lasted 2 weeks for 65$- d'oh).  If you have had previous STR series Sony receivers it's the same set up. Screws instead of clamps for speaker inputs are the only annoyance.   There are seemingly infinite manual adjustments which can be made and it takes time to get the hang of it- but it is laid out in the manual,  not exactly at \\"dummy\\" level, but it is there.  Four HDMI inputs allow for multiple decks of which I'm using 3 and they switch back and forth flawlessly.  The sound is extraordinary.  I'm in a 500 square foot rectangular room with a 15 foot ceiling, 7 speaker set up at the corners/ back / sides  and though there are  more expensive units,  many both from Sony and others, in my room as great as it sounds now  I could not justify spending more.

review_body: Like many others I like the product but have experienced quality problems.  The first unit I purchased declined pretty rapidly (display and backlight issues) and I was able to return it.  The other unit hung in their longer but now several display segments are out.  The unit will occasionally reboot which is not a good feature in an alarm clock.    Features are great and sound is OK. I think the optional remote is a must have item and wish that it was included with the product.      If iHome can sort out the quality problems this is a 4 star item.

product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_body: My son broke his earphone and wanted to buy a new one, after reading some rave review of this earphone on CNET and many positive reviews from Amazon, I convince him to buy Klipsch Image S4 instead of the Monster Turbine.     He doesn't like this due to lack of body on the upper range, the treble can sound thin, he prefers big bass and full body throughout frequency spectrum. I try out the Image S4, it provides nice bass, detailed  and musical midrange (5-10 khz.)  It is detailed enough that I hear the flaw of recording on my Sony HD5 MP3 player which I don't hear before. Overall, it is musical and balance headphone with thin upper range (> 13 Mhz) And the thin upper frequency allow more details, thus you will hear recording flaws.     The construction is okay, thin wires, not exudes quality.     Compare the S4 to my old sony headphone that costs less that [...], it is better but not that different as day and night. The S4 bass is a bit loose not punchy.     I don't have the Shure SE530 to compare with as CNET claims it sounds as good as HP three times as much, and they compare the S4 to the very expensive ones.     It is difficult to review subjectively on headphone, because each people has different ear canal, people with curved ear canal or improper fit, the earphone music can lost a lot of energy before it reaches the eardrum. And you have to rely on other reviews since you can't try them out due to health reason. It's difficult to describe sound quality and everyone has personal taste of audio quality. Best Buy won't accept return of earphone so buying earphone is a risky business.     With 8x the price from the stock Sony earphone and some increase in audio quality, I give the Klipsch Image S4 a better than average score of 3 1/2 stars. I will update my finding few weeks later after it is fully broken-in

product_title: ASUS Eee PC 1000 10-Inch Netbook Deluxe Netbook Carrying Case
review_body: We bought the laptop for our daughter and so we needed a way for her to store it. The fact that the bag is pink of course is just icing on the cake, but she was excited about it. The bag has more pockets than we need and it's just the right size, so it's working out perfectly for us.

We pull it way out when we're cooking in the kitchen, point it to the table if you want to check out the news during lunch, and in the evening it's pointing at the sofa.  It's child proof, earthquake proof, and looks great with the tv on the wall.  We actually have two of these, one in our main living area and the double armed one in our bonus room, we were so happy with the first that we bought the second one.

review_body: This reciever is not for the timid, or tech-impaired. With any decent speakers,(I'm using Polk towers and Bose surround) this unit will make any room acoustically beautiful. The Sc-07 has a self-calibrating set up with speaker phase control that brings any music to vivid reality. With all the bells and whistles you can imagine, Media sharing with LAN networking and internet connectivity, plus IPOD control; there is no need to look further. PLEASE forego the big-box stores and spend a little extra! THe raw power and awesome sound I still cannot get over. You need to experience sound processing like this once in you life. review_body: I bought these speakers on 4/17/09 and chose super saver (free) shipping to save 40 bucks.  They shipped on 4/20/09, fedex overnight and I got them 4/21/09.  That's fantastic!  The speakers themselves were just the right hight for me and they sound fantastic, but also important to me was that I owned a 5.1 surround sound system with all black Sony speakers exactly like these - so everything matches perfectly. I would highly recommend these to anyone, even the price is right - two speakers for the price of one of some other brands.

product_title: Sennheiser On-Ear 926MHz Wireless RF Headphones with Charging Cradle
review_body:
Everything has been said in 922 previous reviews . I found a headphone jack 3.5 mm jack for the computer and a set of RCA audio jacks in my package . I have Fibro and severe chronic pain . Zero quality of life until I put these on WOW . I own a acre and a third with a house at one far end . I walked to every point on my property after closing the door to the house and setting these up on the wall 3 feet above my computer and had no problems until I ducked behind a old Wells cargo trailor 400 feet away . Otherwise I did get some crackle but it was no worse then old vinyl scratches . My garage is behind the house I walked in with closed the doors and there was a van between me and the house and I heard everyting fine . The charging cradle is fine . Its easy to change the batteries and it came with rechargeables . Bottom line it works well . Sounds were crisp within reason for the crackles and pops . It scared me to think the radio waves were everywhere . I thought the bass was great . I like the position of the dials its not confusing . There is a adjustment on the base that helped me lock in a signal everywhere . Now the bad .

These headphones are for people sitting or walking easy . When I tried to bend over with them they fell off . I didnt get on my lawn mower but it would be about as far as I would push activity with them . They feel clumsy and akward for me and I imagine most people . I wore them as small as they would go and I am a 7 5/8 hat size . Maybe my ears are high on my head I dont know . Compared to the technology I knew these are a 6 but take two off for a 4 on a 5 point scale . Definitely worth the money but dont expect to do work in them you will have to find another model . I would love to hear what people are using for that . The range for me was unbelievable compared to what I expected . I never believed the claims . Now you do have to tune them in and adjust a little . My base was hung on a simple paneling nail on the wall above the computer with a light switch a foot away , air conditioner running , monitors , tv and a wireless phone system . No problems . The volume turns up just high enough to be pleasant yet safe . A very good purchase . These replaced a nice set of RCA's which sadly were lost before the package was even openned . product_title: JENSEN SRWS1000 AM/FM Weather Radio with Marine Forecast
review_body:
This radio works well enough, although setup for alerts is very poorly explained in the manual.

But it has a strangely poor design for a unit designed for emergencies. If you power it from AC, and count on the internal batteries for backup, you're looking for trouble. If there's a power failure, the internal batteries will NOT take over operation of the radio. (You have to physically unplug the external power to use batteries.)

Worse, when power returns, the radio will stay in Power Off mode, so it will not be alerting anything, and you will not be any the wiser. When you notice, and power it back on, you'll also have to reset the county code, or you'll get ALL alerts. (You don't have to reprogram the code memories, but you have to choose which one you want.

For a radio designed for use in emergency weather conditions, this sort of bad behavior during a power failure should earn it an \\"Unacceptable\\" rating.

If you're not relying on it for emergency alerts, you might live with this flaw.

Another negative is if you have guests, you have to provide them with a PIN in order to watch your TV. That is not real convenient. I don't know any way around this.     Like I said, overall a good product, but could use some improvements. Like a place for a battery backup for when the power goes out and the ability to add earned time on the fly.    Donna

product_title: Dared SL-2000A
review_body: The Dared SL2000A has gotten plenty of positive reviews, and I can see why.     It is solidly well-built, physically attractive, and -- most importantly -- it sounds really good.     The latest version has two inputs and two outputs, as well as a wooden remote volume control.    This compact, versatile unit is a great way to add some tube warmth and liquidity to your system at a reasonable price. It is often available on the used market for about $300, which is what I paid for mine.    My only minor quibble with the unit is a minor aesthetic one: there's a large unsightly engraving of the Dared logo, model number and -- bizarrely -- a toy-like line drawing of tube etched into one side of the chrome body. IMHO, it is an unfortunate aesthetic blunder on an otherwise classy chassis.     That tiny gripe aside, this little preamp has quickly become one of my favorite pieces of audio gear. I find myself listening to the budget system in which I have it more frequently than some of my more pricey systems.     In short, this little Dared is highly recommended -- especially with some nice NOS tube substitutions!    PS - When I first wrote this review, the retail price was in the low to mid 400's. Now I see it has gone up again to 519. At that price, I'm not sure that it is such a bargain. My advice would be to keep an eye out for a used one in good condition.

product_title: Sansa Shaker 1GB
review_headline: Fantastic for kids or adults that hate ear buds! Has survived through many knocks and drops.
review_body:
Oh my goodness! I love these little things. When my son was 5 he was fascinated by my Ipod. Of course there are some songs in my music collection that I would rather not let him hear so I started looking for a small mp3 player for him that wasn't like the junk from China that they sell on Ebay. He originally had the red Sansa Shaker (512mb.) He just turned 8 and we had to buy him a new blue one (512mb from Toys R Us for $19.99) because he lost his original Shaker. I couldn't tell you how many times that thing was dropped or stepped on, etc...It can take *a lot* of abuse.

Our 3 and 1/2 year old daughter wanted one in pink so I started looking. I'm guessing they've been discontinued in that color, considering the high prices I found for them. Eventually I found a 1GB pink Shaker on Ebay for $23.99, including shipping. Both of my children thoroughly enjoy having their own mp3 players and loading the music is SO easy. I just pop the memory card into the reader on my computer and drag and drop the songs I want to put on theirs.

I think the biggest plus of all is the built in speaker. My daughter's ears are too small for ear buds so she loves to hold her Shaker in one hand and dance around the house. While pressing the power button down you can shake the MP3 player and the song will skip to the next one, hence the name \\"Shaker.\\" The kids love that!

If you have trouble with the bottom cover staying on, just remember to turn it until it clicks. It takes one AAA battery that is included along with the cable to connect to the computer and a handy belt clip that you can put on if you choose to. This is great for kids but I love it too. If it only had a screen where I could see the artists and songs so I could choose what I wanted to hear, I would buy a couple of these for different genres of music and my Ipod would be replaced!

product_title: Powerful External Remote Amplified GPS Antenna Receiver for Garmin Nuvi
review_headline: cheap and effective antenna, fixed my Garmin
review_body:
This antenna performs as advertised. My Garmin Nuvi GPS was suffering increasingly intermittent connections with satellites. Eventually, it would only rarely locate my car, and several times I had to resort to my phone's GPS to get where I was going. Apparently, from browsing the web, this is a fairly common problem for Garmin units.

I was procrastinating before spending hundreds of dollars on yet another GPS, when I spotted a claim of this solution on a random web page, and then found it on Amazon and saw favorable reviews.

It still might take up to 30 seconds to locate the car when starting, but then the connection is rock solid. At about $20, it is a tiny fraction of the cost of a new GPS unit. The cable is longer than necessary, about 6 feet rather than the necessary 1 or 2 feet, but the antenna itself is compact. It makes putting the unit out of sight slightly more cumbersome, with the extra wire emanating from the GPS, a minor hassle.

[a few days later - after looking at the extra cable for a while, I wrapped it around, out the door, and used the magnet under the antenna to stick it on my car roof - the extra cable is actually a good thing.]

Instructions were minimal. The user simply plugs the cable into the little connection on the GPS antenna flap that lifts up from the back of the unit.

It worked for me, thanks Amazon and its diligent and accurate reviewers.

review_body: I bought this product primarily to receive a 40+ mile distant VHF HD ABC station (rated blue for my location by antennaweb.org) that I could not get with my old antenna (a very small, outdoor, omni-directional, UHF antenna) but also to hopefully receive other stations in the blue rating.  The antenna picks up the VHF ABC HD signal well.  The ABC station has about a 30 degree separation from the other stations in my area and the antenna still picks it up in a compromise direction about 25 degrees from optimal for the ABC signal.  All my other signals stayed about the same in signal strength but became more stable than the results I had with my old antenna.  I also liked the ease of mounting the antenna.    I only have one caveat in that it does not pick up any of the other \\"blue\\" rated signals at my location even when aimed directly at the stations, otherwise I would have given it a five star rating.    I had to leave the on/off switch on the power supply in the off position for best reception.  However, it must do something even in the off position because when I removed it from the system and hooked the antenna up directly, I got no useful signal.

It does have an odor from manufacturing, although this goes away pretty quickly if you leave the screen down for awhile rather than rolled up (an eye sore, I know). It provides a much better image than some other discount screen I've seen. Another option to consider are recessed installed screens, which are much less of an eyesore, but probably require a professional install. Projectors use much more energy than operating your TV and replacement lamps are expensive, so chances are you won't want to use it all the time.

Installation
The mounting hardware that comes with it is a little bizarre, so you may want use something else. I bought $1.00 worth of chain at home depot and a set of eye hooks, spray painted both to match the ceiling which attached to the two rings on the screen. For a wall mount you could probably use lag bolts or eyehooks. Either way you will want to use a 1/8\\" drill bit or similar to pre-drill the holes into the studs. With two people and at least one ladder, the install wasn't bad.

Pros:
+Inexpensive!
+Much better image than not having a screen.

Cons:
-Initial bad smell from manufacturing.
-Can be a bit of an eyesore when not in use.

review_headline: Great Antenna Works Great In the IE!!!!
review_body: With the digital change over we decided to keep our antenna which was old and falling apart instead of paying for service.  The digital reception on our old antenna was not good at all so we decided to get a new antenna.  This multi directional antenna we get 59 perfect channels when we used to get 16 ok channels (with old antenna non digital).  There is very minor interference not really worth mentioning.  We live in the inland empire where we have lots of tv station antennas within 20 or 30 miles so I know this antenna works great within that distance but can not comment on longer distances.  I am really impressed with the reception with this antenna I get channels from the OC, LA and IE areas perfectly.  It works great but surprisingly it is a little big and showy on your roof.    I read lots of reviews before purchasing this one and tried two antennas a directional and a multi directional (Antennas Direct DB4 Multi Directional HDTV Antenna).  Per notes on these two types of antennas you will be able to receive more channels with the multi-directional but may get more interference than with the directional.   I do not notice much interference with the Antennas Direct DB4 but I do notice all the channels this antenna picks up.  But this is something to consider when purchasing one depending on your area.      As noted in another review if you are not getting great reception with this antenna keep in mind obstacles such as buildings, hills, poor connections, splitters, long cable runs, low elevation or faulty tuners will cause problems.  Two of these were a huge issue when we went digital with this antenna.  We had to remove an electric splitter which was causing major interference and also add quad shield cabling.  I now get perfect digital reception.  It was a lot of work by well worth it as it is a lot cheaper than cable or satellite.      PS:  Antenna Web suggested in that I get a large directional.  I went ahead and got the large multi-directional because I wanted more channels that the directional was not able to pick up.  Where I am located I don't get really any interference with the multi-directional and I get all the channels I wanted.

product_title: Denon High Performance Over-Ear Headphones
review_body: Over the last few years, I have been slowly working my way up the mountain of diminishing returns that is high-end audio equipment. I've had my eye on a $300-$400 set of headphones for a while now, and when I finally went to take the plunge, I planned to get the Sennheiser 600 or 650's, but I did my homework first. These Denons popped up on the radar, a fairly new option, and I was intrigued.  Luckily, I have a high-end audio store near me, and I went in with the intention of picking up a pair of something directly from them (supporting local businesses!) but after listening for a while to a couple different Grado's and a set of AKG K601's, I left empty-handed because they were all just a bit too aggressive for me. (They don't carry Denon.)  I have pretty good hearing and I'm a bit sensitive to the higher frequencies so I think that's why those others headphones did not impress me. After a lot of thought, I decided that I'd drop the $200 on these Denon phones and hope that they worked for me - they are a good bit cheaper than the Senn 650s and I figure that I could resell them if necessary. Well, I'm keeping them because they are everything I was hoping for. Comfy, solid, fairly efficient, and they sound absolutely wonderful for me.  That being said, these definitely emphasize the lower frequencies. These are not \\"reference\\" headphones, but they are very enjoyable and fun to listen to. I find them detailed and precise, no muddy or mushy bass, and the mids/highs are clear. This is what I want music to sound like. I'm by no means a bass-head, but I like the richer sound of a little more emphasis in the low end, mainly so I can keep the higher-end from giving me a headache after a while. These do just that. Based on what I have read, and had I had the money, I would probably have gone for the 7000s (sometimes available for about $450) but would not have gone for the mid-level model. However, I am not disappointed in these whatsoever.   Unless you need a true referenceset of headphones, or you really detest any emphasis on the low end, these are about the best bang for your buck you're likely to find.

product_title: Sony Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones
review_headline: A lot of things to like, and a couple things not to.
review_body: One thing that you'll notice immediately when you put these on is that a large amount of the noise around you is cut out simply by the design. No fancy circuitry, just good, old-fashioned vinyl and foam. It might even be enough \\"cancelling\\" if not for the fact that, yes, these headphones do sound pretty bad without the noise-cancelling circuitry engaged. There just doesn't seem to be much bottom or mid-range unless you switch them on.    The good news is that they sound very good with the circuit engaged. Don't sit there and play \\"on again, off again\\" games with the switch and try to decide how much additional noise the circuitry is cancelling...just switch it on and listen to the sound quality you get, then decide if you like what you're hearing.    I think, for a relatively inexpensive set of headphones, these deliver remarkably well: the high end is crisp and the low is solid. There's enough noise cancelling to hear a broad dynamic range without having to turn the volume up.    I ride the bus to work every day and have even sat in the very back--the \\"business\\" end of things--and found that most of what I'm \\"hearing\\" from the engine revving is actually bass vibrations that I'm feeling. Ultimately, that's something no noise-cancelling headphone can eliminate...unless it also short-circuits your nervous system.    So I'd recommend these based on the sound alone, but with a few caveats: this whole \\"DJ-style\\" design that allows you to easily hold one earpiece up to your head also makes the earpieces flop around in clumsy ways...flipping over, turning backwards...ways that almost make me wish I was untangling ear bud wires. They're also pretty much impossible to put on your head one-handed (as in: you're standing at the bus stop with books in your hands and want to put them on), which tends to be a common problem with on-ear designs.

product_title: Sennheiser Closed Circumaural Hi-Fi Headphone
review_body:
I bought these headphones after returning the Bose Triports [[ASIN:B000MMWT9Q Bose® around-ear headphones, for personal and portable listening]], which have good sound but are flimsy. Even out of the box, without time for break-in, they are stunning. The sound is precise, clear, and natural. Listening to Mozart's Clarinet Quintet, I hear each instrument beautifully and in surprising detail.

You can buy these with great confidence. An audiophile vendor not associated with Amazon gives these headphones 5/5, and that company has ears trained on equipment costing thousands of dollars. Of course, if you are prepared to buy Sennheiser HD 600 [[ASIN:B00004SY4H Sennheiser HD600 Over-Ear Open Dynamic Hi-Fi Professional Stereo Headphones (Black)]] or HD 650 [[ASIN:B00018MSNI Sennheiser HD650 Audiophile Open Dynamic Stereo Headphone]], you will hear something else again, a magical liquidity - but only if you couple them with a dedicated headphone amplifier. If you use headphones to listen to music, rather than music to listen to headphones, you will be very happy with the 448 for portables and home listening.

PS: It's a year since I posted this review, and I have just made a surprising discovery (surprising to me, at any rate). I knew these were good headphones without an amplifier. What I did not realize is that with a headphone amplifier, they are in another league. I have a small headphone amplifier, and I was getting only fair results with my high impedance headphones (which are outstanding on my other, larger amplifier). So just as an experiment, when frankly I was ready to buy a better amplifier, I asked myself what would happen if I took out the Sennheiser HD 530 (300 ohm impedance) and tried the HD 448. They're stunning. I thought it wouldn't be necessary, because the HD 448 has just a 32 ohm impedance. And it isn't necessary, but it certainly makes a huge difference. Put the HD 448 together with -- say -- a Headroom Airhead or Bithead and you have an excellent little rig.ave an excellent little rig.

product_title: BlueAnt Supertooth 3 Bluetooth Handsfree (Black) + DB ROTH Microfiber Cleaning Cloth
review_headline: Very good handsfree speakerphone - no FM transmitter.
review_body: I bought this set after trying out the Jabra SP700, Motorola T505 and Parrot PMK5800.     I have a Treo 755P and had no problem mating the phone to the Supertooth and downloading my contacts to it. The Treo phone does not support voice dialing from any Bluetooth device, and I could not test the voice dialing feature. However, the Supertooth announces the caller on incoming calls and allows me to accept a call by saying OK after the beep.    The BlueAnt Supertooth is the best of the lot in terms of bluetooth connectivity, and did not loose connectivity with the phone once mated. This was a major problem with the Motorola which kept dropping the connection and announcing it every few minutes.    It was very easy to connect with the Supertooth, and it has nicely placed controls, which both the Jabra and the Motorola did not have.    In a device like this, where all programming is done through voice menus, it is very important to have clear voice menus which are easy to navigate. The Supertooth excels in this, unlike the Parrot device which I could not understand at all.    The main downside is that it does not have an FM transmitter to transfer calls to the car stereo, but since all the other devices drop the FM connection after ~10 minutes of idle time, it wasn't very useful to have this feature.

product_title: Coby 4GB Flash MP3 Player with FM and Color Display (Black) (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body:
When I considered an MP3/FM player for purchase, I was looking for the cheapest, halfways decent unit I could afford, and after research, chose this, and have not been disappointed.

This small, inexpensive device that features an equalizable Mp3 player, with a capacity of up to about 4 GIGS of songs/music, depending on what else you might throw onto it file-wise, along with a good FM radio receiver (with the ability to set pre-sets), was something I thoroughly did my research on, before parting with my bread. And I cannot say I was/am disappointed too much, except for the cheap earbud headphones included, but this is easily solved by using a better set of headphones. In fact, in some ways, it has and does exceed what I expected for the money. Besides a good Mp3 & FM radio player/receiver, other things I looked at before buying such a unit was whether it had some sort of rechargeable energy source (besides non-rechargeable batteries), as well as something which could perhaps exhibit photos, videos, text, and so forth. Ease of setup and use were also primary. According to expectations, this was and is, a nice purchase. Again however, I have been using it with a set of better headphones than what is included here.

While I can't say this product is totally five star, it does almost everything, almost perfectly, for which I bought it, and so I have to give it at least five stars, though it's closer to a four and a half rating than five. The GIG limits level may be well below requirements of some, or they may be looking for something a bit more substantial with a larger view screen, but I think for most casual users, and for the price, this is a pretty fantastic buy. My only real complaint overall is that the cheap and short-in-length earbud headphones included, are really crap, as almost all \\"earbud\\" types are to me, and if you buy this, I hope you have a much better non-earbud set of headphones, whether over or against the ear type. While the included short-sized earbuds may be tolerable, and useful where on-the-go use is concerned, one really should use something better than the earbuds set included with this for best effect.

While I primarily suggest one needs to use better headphones with this than those inexpensive earbuds supplied to get the full value here, that nitpick is minor compared to what this product actually does overall, which I find amazing, again for the cost. This includes being able to basically use it out-of-the-packaging, without reading too much initial instruction. I say this mainly because of my fading eyesight, but what was a pleasure and continues to remain so in my enjoyment of this was that it all really is highly intuitive, from initial charging of the included rechargeable lithium cell battery to the very simple button/wheel operations to get from uploaded Mp3 to FM to pictures, text, etc. While the nice color display is small, too small for this blind bat to get much out of reading text or looking at pictures and/or videos, I'm sure it would be fine for those with basically normal eyesight. What it does best however, is why I got it, and why I really like it, and that is the ability to easily upload tons of saved Mp3's to it for listening, as well as the ability to listen to local FM radio, both functions which it does wonderfully.

Please, all possible buyers, note that this unit REQUIRES one have a computer. One with a free USB connection slot. Whether one has an older USB 1 connection (like my computer dinosaur) or better yet a (faster) 2.0 USB hook-up, to recharge the battery here, you need to plug it in to a computer to use this. That is how you recharge the battery, period. A small USB to COBY cable is included. A computer (with folders/directories of saved Mp3's) is also required because if you have no saved computer Mp3's upon which to upload to this device, what's the point?

Fortunately for me, and why I bought this, isthat over about a decade of downloading Mp3's and in addition to ripping Mp3 versions of already owned music CD albums and tracks, I easily filled nearly 4 gigs right away and only dented my overall Mp3/CD music collection actually. This is an important point however that I can't emphasize strongly enough. If you have a computer, you are half-way there, a substantial collection of Mp3's (or ripped ones from already owned CD's), the other half. If you don't own a lot of computer Mp3 files, but a lot of CD's from which you want to rip from and save as Mp3 files (included is such a program but there are many programs to do this with, a few freeware), it's rather easy. Other audio formats can be played as well. As for pictures, it primarily likes JPEG's, but that's the most commonly worked with picture application for most digital cameras, and this will also accept BMP files for visual media. AVI movie files are the fave here, but it accepts other video app types as well. I mention the visual aspects only for the better-sighted than I, but since the menus on the screen allow for easy Mp3 and FM playback, I have no real beefs there. Besides, really, if one wants to look at pictures and watch videos, there are better ways to do it than on the tiny screen here.

The basics however? This wise, imho for me, purchase, does almost everything as well as I had hoped for. I find that the larger text visible in the main menus, with my bad eyes, even I can see okay. And once one learns to get the hang of it all button pushing wise, and again, with a better set of headphones, why carp? It has great sound, an equalizer of sorts, plays for a long time on a single charge, is pretty simple to use, and plays Mp3's really well in addition to offering a great FM radio feature.

If one is at least semi-computer literate, and knows their way around \\"windows explorer,\\" it's very easy to just drag and drop here, which I found helpful. Anyone looking for an Mp3 player would know a lot of the basics I've mentioned however and have a good collection to upload to this, so all in all, this does just what it should do really, plays Mp3's great, as well as offering a pretty good FM radio receiver. Along with the ability to view pictures and video. For the cost, this is probably more than anyone desiring an Mp3 player/FM radio receiver really needs. Just get or use a better set of headphones than supplied, that's all. I'm amazed at the full rich sound quality overall.

This is a really nice, inexpensive toy which will do the job for almost all users, without the added expense of going with overrated alternatives. Just be sure to ask yourself what you really want and really need, but for the basics of ease of use, rechargeability, and excellent Mp3/FM sound playback, you can't really go wrong here.

If you have a lot of music CD's you'd like to rip to MP3 with the included program, as well as a general knowledge of Windows and Explorer and how to connect simple USB from computer to this unit, for uploads of music, pictures, video, text, and more, you can't go wrong here. While a bit quirky, once one gets used to how to use it all properly (which I did without really reading any manuals or instructions, it's THAT intuitive), this was much more than I expected for the price, and there really is no need to spend anything more than to buy this gem.

I'm using a pair of $15 over-ear Panasonic RP-HT227 with this (reviewed elsewhere on Amazon), and I couldn't be more pleased. product_title: Verizon - Verizon DECT 6.0 2 Line
review_headline: Needs a lot of QA and design rework
review_body: After bearing with the interference and stuttering of 5.8Ghz phones for a few years, I was looking forward to upgrading to a DECT 2-line system.  Unfortunately, this DECT system is virtually unusable and cannot be recommended at all.  (And looking at the reviews of other DECT phones here on Amazon, it seems that they all have been rushed to market without proper QA.)    Pros:  * The sound is clear and without interference (when it works -- see the cons).    Cons:  There are so many.  Where do I start?  * When you pick up a ringing handset, frequently (>50% of the time) the caller hears a very loud screeching/electromechanical noise before the phone \\"settles down\\" and actually lets you talk.  * During many calls, the handset will spontaneously start beeping.  It will emit 3 short, loud beeps; pause; and then repeat. Your caller can hear the beeps to, and it's so annoying that you have to end the call.  Is it warning about a low battery?  Maybe...but the battery is fully charged, according to the phone itself (and it's been sitting in the charger for days...)  This happened sporadically with several different handsets (not all).  Tech support could not offer any explanation or solution.  * This is a 2-line phone system.  I give out ONLY my line 1 number to callers; I use line 2 for fax and for outgoing calls.  So no one calling me ever calls line 2.  Yet, on many occasions the system \\"confuses\\" the two lines; callers to line 1 will get the fax, and vice versa.  This is not due to a wiring problem in the house, as nothing has changed in the house for many years and my previous 2-line phone systems did not have this problem.  * If you hang up line 1 and then attempt to place another call on line 1, you'll have to wait.  The system refuses to release line 1 for a long time, sometimes up to 15 seconds.  It somehow \\"thinks\\" line 1 is still busy and repeatedly gives me line 2.  If I try to select line manually, the handset beeps at me reproachfully and refuses to give me line 1.  * 25% of the handsets I tried to use would never register with the base.  I returned/exchanged many handsets during the course of two months trying to get this system to work.  About 25% of them are just unusable...period.  So much for Verizon quality control.  When I called tech support about an unregisterable handset, they instructed me to \\"reboot\\" the handset by holding down certain keys simultaneously while turning the power on.  These instructions failed to do anything -- the handset did not respond to it at all, and did not reboot.  Tech support finally gave up on me, and basically implied \\"user brain damage.\\"  Note:  I am not technically challenged -- I design technology device software for a living.  * The documentation says the system supports up to 6 handsets, but I do not believe this is true.  I could never get the system to register more than 5 at a time.  I had 7 viable handsets at one point, but the base would refuse to register any more than 5 at one time.  * Handset buttons:  There is a longish delay between the time you press a button and the handset recognizes it.  You cannot dial a number quickly; the handset will drop half the digits.  (This problem does not occur with the buttons on the base system, however.)    * The button presses on the handset are spongy and do not give tactile feedback.  You cannot be sure you have actually pressed the button unless you look at the display.  * Handset volume is very low, ever at its highest setting.  If you are hard of hearing or are phoning from a room that has background noise, you will not be able to use these handsets.    There is more, but I'm depressed just thinking about it all.      Question:  Did the designers & programmers of these phones actually ever USE them before they were foisted on the public?

product_title: Harman Kardon AVR-354 7x75W 7.1 Channel Home Theater Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: For the price that you can get the AVR354, it offers significantly more bang for the buck than other receivers in the price range. You get support for all of the latest sound formats (except Dolby Pro Logic IIz), Great sound (very high quality and 75W is a very conservative rating), excellent video processing (upsampling to 1080p and overlays/OSDs even on high def outputs, which is rare in this price range), and included iPod dock.    The only caveats I would mention are a comparatively low number of HDMI inputs at 3, the inability to simply pass through video (everything is upscaled), and quirky firmware. The last issue is something that is supposedly getting fixed soon. Most of the \\"quirky firmware\\" issues have to do with HDMI compatibility. I've personally experienced losing all audio from my HD tivo and video corruption when moving from one resolution to another (switching inputs then back fixes it), but others have experienced numerous audio problems with the PS3 and compatibility issues using HDMI->DVI converters. According to HK tech support (as of 07/09), there is a firmware update coming within a few weeks that will remedy the majority of outstanding HDMI issues.    I'm very happy with the receiver, but my recommendation would be to wait for the next firmware before making a purchase on this receiver. Though the AVR354 usually operates very well, the HDMI bugs can be annoying. Wait until the new version of the firmware hits (current is 95.1.1 in the U.S.), then check online message boards to see if the big issues have been corrected. I rate this receiver a four based on an average. If the next firmware does not fix the HDMI issues, it should be a three, but if the new firmware does fix the issues, it's a five.

A quick comparison with Sennheiser PXC 250 Active Noise Canceling Headphone reveals that the two seem to have equal active noise cancellation capability, maybe slightly better. However, the ATH-ANC7 benefits from much better passive sealing. The end result is a very satisfactory noise isolation device.    The sound quality is also very good. product_title: Bose 3·2·1 GS Series III DVD Home Entertainment System
review_body: Being skeptical of such an expensive purchase, I really worked this thing over once I got it to make sure I was going to keep it. It did not take long to find out that it can't be beat. For such a simple system I was amazed at the performance. Let's start with the good: Very stylish, compact, and super easy to set up. The set-up I did was not your standard set-up either. I took advantage of running optical audio from my cable box (good idea) and I use the HDMI output to a 37inch LCD. I did not want all of my sound to always have to go through the unit so I had to use a few more wires. The sound is absolutely unbeatable for the size of system. If you are a sound junkie like myself you will appreciate the clarity and reality of the reproduction. Music is concert-like, DVD's play like you are in a mini-theater. People that do not like the sound of Bose generally like a lot of unnatural bass and Bose refuses to give in to that fake noise. I replaced a high end Sony 5.1 system with this for aesthetics and am kicking myself for not doing it sooner. The sound is now simply way better at all volume levels. Even 2.0 sound sounds better through these tiny speakers than they did with my old system. Now for the not so good: You need a fairly recent and not so cheap universal remote if you want to control this thing. Unless you don't mind the remote it comes with which claims to be universal but I found otherwise. The aqua display of text on the front of the unit can detour your focus when watching the TV screen. There is no equalizer if you wanted to create a different sound other than the Bose standard. Sometimes I want that cheesy bass although it pumps out plenty. Lastly, you almost need to use the optical audio connection to ensure full volume control. Without it you have to turn up the volume for different applications. I use the optical so I have no complaints. Before I go, I just want to let you know that if you want a small system that can fill your room with rich authentic sound then you are on the right track with this system. You can put a pretty nice system together for the price of this thing but what for??? 3 wires and you are done and have the best sound money can buy.

Choosing a subwoofer, or any home theater or stereo equipment can be a daunting task. There are so many options out there, most of them way beyond my budget. I did a lot of research and listening to different units. I checked out some of the audiophile forums and asked questions on an Amazon forum. I believe now that I made the best choice within my budget and the amount of space we have for the unit itself.

The first night I hooked up all the parts of the home theater system, I realized that I bought the wrong Y connector to connect this subwoofer to my receiver so we had to watch a movie without it. The sound was good, but the next day, with all the right connectors, this sub made it sound just amazing. You could feel the sounds in the sofa and on the floor. product_title: 4 Port Cable TV/HDTV/Digital Amplifier Internet Modem Signal Booster Internet AMP
review_headline: Does exactly what it is designed to do
review_body:
I'm very happy with this device. Looking at the reviews, I think those who are unhappy with it do not understand what it does:

An amplifier like this is not a magic box that will convert an unusable signal (say from a digital TV antenna) into a usable signal; rather it solves a very specific problem.
Suppose you have an signal that is usable at the point of the antenna, but is NOT usable at the point where you want to use it. This might be because you have a long run of coax cable between the antenna and your TV/converter box/tuner/whatever; or it might be because you want to split the signal to feed it into multiple TV/tuner boxes/etc.
If this is your situation, the device works very well.

If your problem is that your signal is too weak to be useful directly at the point it comes out the antenna, even before it goes through any long runs of coax or splitters, then no amplifier in the world is going to help you out. What you need is to acquire a better signal. Depending on your circumstances, this might be done by
- changing the angle/orientation of your antenna
- moving it around the room (so it's nearer windows or away from metal or whatever)
- moving it higher (if necessary going outside the house and onto the roof)
- or getting a larger antenna with a larger collecting area.

product_title: Ultimate Ears Super.fi 3 Studio Earphones
review_body: I have always been into music a lot, always carrying my CD or tape player around with me since I was probably 5 and now it is an iPod. I've always used over the ear headphones, mostly cheap Sony's (MDRV-100 and MDRv-150), but once I got my Creative NOMAD (RIP) I began solely using earbuds, the default Creative's that came with the NOMAD lasted me quite awhile and I loved them, nothing I got after them was able to compare. I began buying a pair of Philip's from Wal-Mart and after losing the silicon tips and the first two pairs blowing out I decided to maybe start researching higher end earphones.    I was going to Japan for a little bit so I decided on finding something that can really isolate outside noise well. I spent about a week doing research and it pretty much boiled down to the Super.fi 3's, Shure SE100's, or the Eytomic Research Er6i's. I noticed a lot of people enjoyed these, so that probably pushed me towards settling with these. The other bit I liked was that they had a replaceable cord, which is really nice because after about a month and half the left monitor blew out and luckily it was the cord, so a quick call to UE and still being under manufacturer warranty they sent me a replacement free of charge and received it about two days later.    Long intro, yes, so I'll say what I have to say about the sound quality: I honestly can't go back to anything else. Yes, those Philip's earphones I have sound similar but I get amazing isolation and a bit more clarity. Now, I am no audiophile (trying to get more and more into it) so I can't throw out technical jargon like \\"highs\\" and \\"lows\\" but I can say that treble is perfect and the bass is perfect, neither clash with the other.    I listen to a wide variety of music, mostly black metal, classical, and crust punk, and indie. So, the only problem I could say with these (which is probably true for other IEM's) is that there is a slight lack in space, what I mean is that you lose some of the atmosphere those genrescan produce when using these. I've tried my brother's SkullCandy (I believe they were the Ink'd) and his Sony MDRs (I forget the model, but they're from Circuit City, when they were opened) I also gave the Sony MDR-EX55's which broke on my roommate a week after he got them. All three of those had way too much bass for me, which made me feel that having too much bass in IEMs will kill the sound. Isolation on these things are amazing and I think only the Eytomic Research IEMs can rival them, fit is everything (if you didn't already read that ;)) and once you get the right fit these things really do shine. Speaking of fit, I ended up losing one of my silicon tips, so after 30 minutes of searching I decided to check to see if by some miracle my brother's SkullCandy tips could fit these, and they did. So instead of paying $10 for replacement tips, you can go out and buy a set of SkullCandy's for $10 give them to your bass head younger sibling or child and keep the silicon tips you need. The UE tips are better, though.    I have not tried these with an amplifier, so I can't say anything on that matter... I will hopefully get around to making myself a cMoy amp. If anythign that will boost my love of these.    Wrap up...  PROS: - Sound great, a great intro to IEMs.        - Everything in my music is much more clear than ever before.        - If isolation is needed, these will do the trick.        - Replaceable cords.        - You can use SkullCandy tips.        - Cheaper and better than the Bose in ear earbuds.        -iPod has longer battery life because I don't have to turn it up               nearly as loud as before.    CONS: - If you do like bass, these may not be for you.        - Until you get use to it, the cord length may be too short.        - It is pretty hard to sleep with these (the reason for me to be                thinking of getting the ER6is eventually)        - Not getting these before spending $100 on multiple pairs of          inferior earbuds.        -Like other IEMs, will not work if you want to use these while           being active (as in exercise).

product_title: SanDisk Sansa Clip 1 GB MP3 Player
review_body: I've only had this player for a few days, but am very impressed. I am a former iPod Shuffle (v2) user, and was not thrilled about that players durability.    The sound quality on the Sansa Clip is fantastic. I love the fact that you can see the Album/Artist/Song on the display, and can also sort this way. It is slightly larger than the iPod Shuffle, but not so much so that it is a burden. In fact, it is a very nice size, with no worries about clip slippage (if that is a word - LOL). product_title: Sony MDR-XB500 40mm XB Diaphragm Driver Extra Bass Headphones
review_headline: Fantastic headphones, just need an equalizer
review_body: I recently bought these headphones and have nothing but good things to say about them.  I am a hobbyist with a home studio, and I am familiar with a wide range of headphones including more expensive Sony headphones, AKG K99s, and Audio Technica ATHm20s.  It is my opinion that the xb500s are actually more capable than ANY of these headphones, but there is a catch.  What some of the other reviews say is true.  If you just plug them in and start listening, the bass does overwhelm the higher treble frequencies.  But all you need to do this is use a simple graphic equalizer.  Raise the treble frequencies, and these headphones, in my opinion, sound better than any in their price range.  They even sound better than some more expensive headphones.  I also find them to be very stylish and comfortable.  I have a large head with large ears, and these headphones do not hurt my head even after an album's worth of listening.  The large soft pillow like pads do make my ears a little warm, but not unbearably hot.  They do about as good a job as other closed back headphones at isolating audio from outside ambient noise.  In conclusion, I think these are fantastic headphones if you'll just take a second to play around with the EQ to get things balanced out right.  Once optimized, they perform as good or better than any in their class.

review_headline: 3.5 Stars - Great Earphones But They Lack Bass

While this may be good for protecting your hearing, it certainly is not ideal for audiophiles or for anyone trying to appreciate the full range of their music. Nonetheless music does sound crisp with these earphones and if you can live with only mild bass then you will be pleased.    *** Positive Points Include: ***    - Comfortable fit that allows for extended listening    - Very good noise isolation (this is passive noise isolation which means they act like ear plugs not active noise cancelling that some other models have)    - Comes with a nice case and plenty of different size earpieces so you can get a perfect fit    - Great high frequency and mid frequency response.    - Good sound separation.      *** Negative Points Include: ***    - Lacks deep low freqency (bass) response    - Price is a bit high      Overall:  I compared these earphones with a few cheaper alternatives that I have in my collection.  They outperformed nearly all of them in terms of sound clarity but they definitely did not have the bass response expected for today's music styles.  For this price you would want it all.

The sound is great, the station selection virtually unlimited, and the potential seems to be there for future updates via software downloads (for example, there's an intriguing \\"mode\\" button on the remote that's not currently used, but the instructions suggest that it may be activated in the future).  The Myein people are very nice and very responsive, too (send them an e-mail and they may even offer you a discount).  All in all a great value and loads of fun. product_title: Klipsch IMAGE S4 -Ear Enhanced Bass Noise-Isolating Headphones
review_headline: A Superlative Headphone Design at a Reasonable Price
review_body:
This superb set of headphones is quite astonishing considering the price for which they are now available. With an outstanding range that covers everything from the most spectacular highs all the way down to the lowest of lows, the headphones provide a realism to musical reproduction that forces us to reconsider how we listen to music. When paired with a high-quality MP3 player using a high bit rate for the ripped recordings, the Klispch S4's can rival the experience of the most expensive home systems, and in terms of sonic dimensions, can probably exceed them.
The quality of the S4 reproduction is so good that all those recordings you have been listening to with other headphones at 160kbps now sound dreadful when we plug the S4's in. This is because, with the wonderful characteristics of the S4's, we can now realize for the first time that our older headphones were not capable of reproducing the same level of sonic clarity, and the lower bit rate of recordings was not an issue. But now, we find that (for better or for worse, you be the judge) when we use a higher bit rate with the S4's (and assuming a good quality electronic player) we have a completely renovated musical experience: sparkling clarity, extremely wide dynamic range, and powerful lower sonics (without boominess), and then we understand why most reviews compare these headphones to models many times its price. The reviews are right.

There is one extremely important item to remember with these headphones, and one that was brought to my attention by another reviewer before I purchased my first set, which bears repeating. You may have the experience that, when you put the headphones in your ear for the first time and try them out, that they actually sound quite dreadful. This is an odd experience, considering all the superlative reviews (including this one). Indeed, I had this same experience. But what is happening is this: these headphones, which use a unique polymer/synthetic resin \\"bud,\\" greatly depend on the proper seating within the ear canal. In fact, if you look carefully at the buds, they are not round, as are most all other brands, but are, in fact, slightly oval in shape. In order to achieve the proper seating of the headphone, ensure that the buds are rotated on the axis of the headphone to fit the shape of your ear canal, and second, make sure you have attached the proper SIZE bud (the headphones come with three interchangeable sizes, as if the practice with many manufacturers) to the headphones. In my case, I needed to switch the largest of the three supplied sizes, and then, when I properly inserted the headphones into my ears, the sound transformed into something incredible.

I can easily recommend these headphones to anyone looking for high quality sound reproduction for a reasonable price. review_headline: Where's the Bass?  Hard to find, but worth the effort.
review_body:
I have very mixed feelings on these. These are clearly quality headphones. The sound of the mids and highs are great. MUCH better than the stock iPhone earbuds they replaced. My problem is the bass is missing unless I fiddle with them and find that perfect spot, where it quickly moves and the bass is gone. I would have rated them a 4 or 5 star if the bass wasn't an issue. 5 star if there was a call end/skip button. So lose one for that, and the bass drops it down to a 3. Odd method of wearing, but works.
Summary:
Phone calls are clear for both parties. Great!
When in the right spot, makes the .mp3's sound very good. Far superior to the iPhone stock earbuds.
When in wrong spot, bass is gone. Not so great.
The wires go up and over the ear, so a bit strange at first, but don't feel them after a minute or 2.

** UPDATE ** ** Five Months of Use **
When I first got these, I was a bit disappointed. First, I didn't realize you wrap the wires over the tops and behind your ears. Not a big deal, but kinda odd. Second, I was unable to get good bass response consistently. After I tried all the various gels, I settled on the 2nd to smallest pair and have found them to keep the bass flowing uninterrupted for the most part. But you really need to shove them deep into yours ears, something I was initially reluctant to do.

These excel in noise isolation. You really block out lots of sound with these, and can hear the music that much clearer. I used these on a round trip to Japan, and they saved my ears. Much less hearing fatigue on both flights.

The down side is finding the right way to wear them and getting the bass to work correctly. That, and the need to keep cleaning them or face ear wax buildup - e[...] Another downer is the lack of an end call/next song button for the iphone. That feature didn't seem so important when I ordered them, but not having it causes extra work.

After finding a fairly constant way to wear these and keep the bass flowing, I'll raise my rating to 4 stars.
